jobs.title: Associate Director, Cost-effectiveness Funder Analysis
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Application deadline:** December 7, 2026, at 11:59 PM PST.

**Job Overview**

Please note:

- Candidates must already have the legal right to work in the country of employment.
- US candidates must be based in an Eastern Time Zone location or the San Francisco Bay Area. For candidates in the San Francisco Bay Area, they must be willing to have at least two workdays per week with at least two hours of overlap with East Africa working hours.

This is one of two Associate Director positions established for this effort, split by function. This post is the technical-leaning role, accountable for the analysis that underpins cost-evidence-based funder engagement. This position sits within the Best Use of Resources (BUR) team and reports to the Senior Director, Cost-effectiveness. This role works alongside the Associate Director, Cost-Effectiveness Funder Engagement, who holds the more public- and funder-facing half of the same remit.

The IRC engages a rapidly growing pool of cost-evidence-based funders, whose allocation decisions are primarily based on rigorous impact-per-dollar analysis. Historically, humanitarian programming has not been a focus of this funder community. However, in recent years, the IRC has increasingly received cost-evidence-based funder support for a wide range of initiatives, from [conducting exploratory research](https://www.givewell.org/research/grants/International-Rescue-Committee-IRC-Desk-Based-Scoping-of-Programs-to-Increase-Vaccination-Coverage-September-2024%29) to [scaling malnutrition treatment](https://www.dioptratool.org/news/new-partnership-with-weiss-asset-management-foundation-to-advance-cost-efficiency-in-malnutrition-treatment) to [influencing foreign aid](https://www.dioptratool.org/news/open-philanthropy-support-for-cost-evidence-generation). As the “Solutions NGO” dedicated to scaling cost-effective programming, cost-evidence-based funders represent a values- and results-aligned opportunity to increase the reach and cost-effectiveness of IRC’s programming.

Working closely with the BUR team and in deep collaboration with External Relations (ER), this role will use BUR's cost-effectiveness research and IRC’s programming to build cost-effective donor-facing funding opportunities, ultimately allowing cost-evidence-based funders and the IRC to scale increasingly cost-effective programming.

**Major Responsibilities**

**Drive IRC’s strategy**

- Own the analytical component of an ambitious cost-evidence-based funder strategy, in collaboration with ER.
- Develop, track, and report progress against workplans and OKRs for the analytical workstream.

**Build the analysis that underpins funder engagement**

- In collaboration with BUR technical staff, build back-of-the-envelope calculations (BOTECs), absorptive capacity estimates, value of information analyses, and other analyses to inform public-facing materials and funder engagement.
- Work backwards from funders’ cost-effectiveness bars to identify ready-to-go IRC funding opportunities (e.g., malnutrition treatment) and consider new funding opportunities (e.g., AI-enabled improved immunization program targeting).

**Identify and secure highly cost-effective funding opportunities**

- Lead on the technical content for specific bilateral engagement materials and proposals for cost-evidence-based funders.
- Maintain up-to-date knowledge of BUR’s research and IRC’s programming to independently answer funders’ technical questions, such as how a CEA estimated years lived with disability (YLD).

**Support the wider team’s analytical capability**

- Develop and contribute to guidance, templates, and AI-enabled tools to support others to produce funder-ready analysis and associated collateral.
- For ongoing funding, coordinate with BUR, ER, and other IRC teams to support any ongoing cost analysis reported to funders.

**Steward Diversity, Equality and Inclusion both in the culture of IRC, as well as in our research and partnerships**

**Job Requirements**

- 8+ years of experience in cost-effectiveness analysis of multi-year $5M+ funding opportunities, including analysis produced for or used by funders. Strong preference for 3+ years of work experience in low- or middle-income countries.
- Excellent quantitative skills, including the ability to build BOTECs, cost-effectiveness analyses, value of information analyses, absorptive capacity analyses, and other analyses to quantify funding opportunities. Strong preference for candidates with experience (a) analyzing humanitarian programming in fragile and conflict-affected situations and (b) building and using AI tools to support analysis.
- Strong communication skills, including ability to write for both technical and lay audiences, fluency in cost-evidence-based funder terminology (e.g., tractability, room for more funding, fungibility), and adherence to cost-evidence-based funder values of high reasoning transparency, truth-seeking, humility, etc.
- Demonstrated ability to work as a strategic, proactive thinker who can design and prioritize their own workplan.
- High attention to detail, including for project and knowledge management.
- Demonstrated ability to manage complex projects and multiple stakeholders in a large organization to efficiently drive progress.
- The ability to be flexible and work well under pressure, dealing with competing priorities, in a fast-paced team environment.
- Fluent in English; French a plus.

**Compensation:** (USA: $105,282 - $140,000 annually) (UK: £65,263- £77,499 annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**US Benefits effective Jan 1, 2027:** IRC offers a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-30 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $187 per month, dental starting at $7.70 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare, dependent care, and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: HR SPECIALIST/ HOMERE REFERENT
jobs.description:
**Médecins Sans Frontières,** founded in 1971, is an international medical humanitarian organization that provides emergency medical assistance to people affected by conflict, epidemics, disasters or exclusion from health care. Our teams are made up of tens of thousands of medical professionals, logistics, administrative and various other professions, all guided by our medical ethics and our principles of impartiality, independence and neutrality.

**MSF WaCA,** created in 2019, is the first MSF headquarters in Africa, and responds to the desire to reinvent the MSF movement after 50 years of humanitarian actions in the world, for more access to care, more reactivity and proactivity for greater medical coverage of affected populations in the world.

**Why join us?**

You are preparing to become a member of the MSF family, with over 50 years of emergency medical action that earned the Nobel Peace Prize in 1999.

We are an inclusive organization that considers social and professional well-being a right for all and provides an environment that considers the diversity of each member.

**MSF WaCA** claims an African anchorage that considers the local expertise with which it contributes to the implementation of its activities and makes each member, a key actor of the new dynamics of the humanitarian action in the world.

**Diversity, Inclusion & Safe Recruitment**

MSF offers equal recruitment and development opportunities without any form of discrimination based on gender, religion, sexual orientation, ethnicity, geographical origin, physical disability or any other discriminatory ground.

**Female candidates who meet the requirements are strongly encouraged to apply.**

***Persons with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply, and reasonable accommodations are available upon request.***

**MSF is committed to applying Safe Recruitment principles, ensuring transparent, fair, and respectful recruitment processes that protect candidates, the organization, and its beneficiaries.**

**We Are Looking for: HR SPECIALIST/ HOMERE REFERENT**

**Department: Operations**

**Direct Manager: Head of HR Operations**

**Functional Manager: Head of HR Operations**

**Working %: 100%**

**Position Based in: Abidjan, HQ**

**Mobility: All MSF – WaCA’s Intervention Zones**

**Type of Contract: Fixed-Term Contract under Ivorian law; Renewable**

**Position to be filled: As Soon As Possible**

**Objectives**

The HR Specialist/ Homere Referent is responsible for overseeing the human resources information system in the field and at head office, as well as the HR forecasting tool to be selected by MSF WaCA.

**Main responsibilities**

1. **Processes and procedures**

• Establish standard reporting formats for projects, coordination and field visits.

• Work closely with the IT department to facilitate the digitisation of HR tools.

• Lead the overall strategy for HR information systems in the field, as well as data management and reporting within WaCA HR.

• Act as the point of contact for all technical issues relating to HR administration (Homère, HR Forecasting tool, compliance with the legal framework, remuneration, etc.)

• Analyse the needs of the HR department and develop HRIS strategies to meet these needs.

• Manage, maintain and troubleshoot the HRIS to ensure it runs smoothly.

• Carry out regular system audits and data validation exercises to ensure data integrity.

• Develop and implement training programmes for HR staff and other employees on the use of the HRIS.

• Work closely with the HR and IT departments to implement and update the HRIS software

• Produce reports and present data analyses to support HR decisions

• Assist with the development and improvement of HRIS procedures and documentation

• Recommend and implement updates or new HRIS systems where necessary.

**2. Capacity building**

• Supervision and point of contact for discussing training opportunities on Homère with HR teams in the field.

• Briefing field HR teams on new features in Homère, Odoo or the future HRIS.

• Design and delivering HR modules for various MSF training courses as required.

**3. Others**

• Actively contribute to any cross-functional projects at the request of the Head of HR Operations.

• May represent WaCA’s HR operations in working groups and HR platforms.

• May support the field team in the event of an emergency mission deployment or to fill a temporary vacancy.

## **Job requirements**

**Education**

• Bachelor’s degree in human resources management, IT or a relevant field

**Competencies**

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

• Self-motivated; you are recognised for your creativity, your ability to synthesise information, your proactivity and your strong analytical skills. You are also an excellent communicator.

• Ability to work independently, a professional approach and the ability to manage stress

• Good knowledge of human resources tools, policies and guidelines

• Attention to detail, strong analytical and summarising skills

• Strong organisational skills and experience in managing multiple tasks

• Commitment to the organisation and humanitarian work

• Flexibility and cultural sensitivity

• Ability to communicate effectively with others

• Proactive and solution-oriented

• Ability to think outside the box and demonstrate creativity

**Professional experience required**

• Proven experience in managing HR information systems and HR forecasting tools

• A minimum of three (3) years’ experience in a human resources role (in the field and/or at MSF headquarters) is an advantage

• Good technical knowledge of Homere & Odoo.

• Knowledge of HR processes and employment legislation

• Proven experience as an HRIS specialist (Homere & Odoo) or in a similar role

**Languages Skills**

· Working proficiency in English and French (Required)

**Computer Skills**

· MS Office suite (mainly MS Word, Excel and Powerpoint)

· In-depth knowledge of MSF’s human resources information systems (Homère) and the human resources forecasting tool.

· Familiarity with e-learning platforms.

\-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*N.B.: This job description provides a framework for the main responsibilities and primary activities of the position. It is not exhaustive. Therefore, the responsibilities and activities of the position may differ from those described in this job description due to organizational and operational needs.*

**Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.**

jobs.title: Manager, Major Giving Southwest
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Application deadline:** Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

## **Job Overview/Summary:**

The Manager, Major Giving Southwest will play a meaningful role in supporting the USA Philanthropy West/Southwest team, helping to handle distinct portfolios of high-net-worth donors and prospects and acting in very close collaboration with Officers and leadership to supervise progress on and implement the strategy for some of our most significant donor relationships. They will support the cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of a defined portfolio of IRC prospects and donors for assigned Officers. They will also coordinate stewardship reporting requirements, ongoing communications, information management, and donor database updates. The Manager will closely collaborate across ER to coordinate donor engagement, stewardship, and recognition consistent with donor stewardship plans and to maintain up-to-date portfolios for assigned Officers. This position offers a wide-ranging growth opportunity for someone eager to advance to front-line fundraising.

## **Highlights of Major Responsibilities:**

- Collaborate with assigned Officers to carry out strategies for high-net-worth individuals within each Officer's portfolio, bringing in critical revenue for the organization.
- Draft correspondence that supports the Officer’s interactions with the portfolio, including general and targeted communications such as letters and contact reports.
- Support the payments for bank transactions. Ensure completeness of payment documents in compliance with IRC and Donor policies and procedures.
- Assist in creating materials, agendas, and briefings for external prospect and donor meetings and for internal strategy meetings.
- With the Officer(s), supervise and manage expectations and objectives for each donor and prospect within the portfolio, including adhering to stewardship reporting requirements and timeframes.
- Alongside the Officer(s), act as the liaison between donors or prospects and field staff, ensuring both parties receive the most critical information and that it is communicated clearly and strategically reflective of its audience.
- Collaborate with other teams, including Prospect Research and Management, Analytics, and Operations, to supervise the entire donor cycle for Major Giving Southwest.
- Update the donor database (Salesforce) to maintain portfolio assignments, build and update giving proposals, request prospect research, review report requirements and submissions, supervise ongoing donor communication and activity, as well as additional relationship management duties.
- Manage information flows between donors and prospects, program staff, and Officer(s).
- Supervise internal drafting and approval processes vital for proposals, reports, and budgets.
- Develop and maintain excellent working relationships with colleagues and IRC program/support staff globally.
- Undertake special projects and administrative tasks as advised.

## **Minimum Job Requirements:**

**Work Experience:** Minimum 2-3 years previous work experience, preferably gained in a development or fundraising team, non-profit, marketing, or sales team.

## **Proven Skills and Proficiencies:**

- Ability to meet deadlines with quality products.
- Strong interpersonal skills; oral, written and presentation skills.
- Experience with and knowledge of relevant technologies and tools with excellent analytical skills combined with the substantiated ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and handle time effectively.
- Understanding of the role of written communications in building and maintaining individual and institutional relationships.
- Ability to identify, build, and implement processes vital to support effective donor relationships.
- Strong ability to establish and maintain lasting professional relationships both internally and externally.
- Highly computer literate, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, as well as familiarity with CRM databases, including Salesforce.
- Ability to respond quickly to changes in short-term work priorities.
- Ability to analyze and interpret financial data.
- Dedication to fundraising for international development, humanitarian, human rights, social justice, and US immigrant communities.
- Understanding of the US fundraising marketplace.

**Working Environment:** This role requires working remotely full-time (i.e., telecommuting). Applicants must have a home or alternate workspace where they can effectively complete their work during regularly scheduled hours.

**Compensation:** ($70,000-$80,000 - annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**US Benefits effective Jan 1, 2027:** IRC offers a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-30 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $187 per month, dental starting at $7.70 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare, dependent care, and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Programme Officer - Inclusive Education
jobs.description:
Sightsavers implements projects in over 30 countries in Africa and South Asia working to eliminate avoidable blindness and promote the rights of people with disabilities.

**Position Title**: Programme Officer – Inclusive Education

**Location**: Homa Bay, with quarterly travel to the Sightsavers Country office in Nairobi

**Contract**: Two-year fixed-term contract

**Salary**: Local Terms and Conditions apply

**Responsibilities**

- Support the effective planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of inclusive education activities, working closely with the Country Programme Manager, project partners and Sightsavers technical specialists.
- Support partners throughout the project cycle, including work planning, reporting, financial and resource management, monitoring and documentation.
- Work with schools, education authorities, organisations of persons with disabilities and communities to strengthen inclusive education practices and remove barriers to learners' participation and learning.
- Support teacher development, inclusive teaching approaches, accessible learning materials and learning environments, and appropriate support and referral pathways for learners.
- Contribute to monitoring, evaluation and learning activities, including school visits, accessible feedback from learners and caregivers, and the collection and analysis of appropriately disaggregated data.
- Support project partners with budgets, forecasts, expenditure monitoring and the timely submission of accurate financial returns.
- Build effective relationships with partners and other education and disability inclusion stakeholders, supporting capacity development, shared learning and local ownership.
- Contribute to communication, advocacy and reporting activities, including case studies and learning materials, while ensuring appropriate consent, safeguarding and data protection requirements are followed.

This is a varied and involved role, and the responsibilities outlined above are not exhaustive. The Job Description is currently being finalised and some details may therefore be subject to change. Any updates to the [Job Description](https://sightsavershh.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/HRExternal/IQDNmogb-ROxR4xDkUV61iYlAWv5lPs-ES2cUGy-pVeyeFs?e=LAToY6) will be shared with candidates before interview.

**Job Requirements**

**Essential:**

- Demonstrable experience in inclusive education, including supporting learners with disabilities and working with schools and teachers.
- A Bachelor's degree or above in education, special needs education, inclusive education, social sciences, development studies or a related relevant field.
- Significant experience of implementing complex programmes, with an understanding of disability inclusion, gender mainstreaming, child safeguarding and equitable participation in education.
- Experience of delivering education interventions with government departments, education authorities, schools and community-based stakeholders.
- Experience of providing technical assistance and capacity development support to partner organisations.
- Experience of advocacy relating to inclusive education and disability inclusion, including working with organisations of persons with disabilities, learners and caregivers.
- Familiarity with relevant national legislation and policies relating to education, inclusive education, disability inclusion, child protection and human rights.
- Knowledge of inclusive education approaches, including Universal Design for Learning, reasonable accommodation and accessible learning materials.
- Ability to travel to programme implementation sites within Homa Bay and occasionally to Nairobi as required.

**Desirable:**

- Familiarity with the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD) and Sustainable Development Goal 4.
- Experience of accessible data collection, monitoring education outcomes and analysing data using Microsoft Excel.
- Experience of working with devolved County Government departments.
- Experience of supporting teacher development or capacity-building activities relating to inclusive education.
- Experience of developing case studies, learning briefs or other programme communications for advocacy, learning or donor reporting.

jobs.title: Responsable des activités épidémiologiques F/H - Pool d'Urgence MSF OCP
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organization created in 1971 that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters.

Your main mission is assessing, implementing and maintaining the epidemiological surveillance systems/monitoring (if needed) according to MSF protocols, standards and procedures in order to contribute to appropriate evidence-based decision making using well managed health data in outbreak and emergency MSF programmes.

**Main responsabilites**

- Carrying out key epidemiological activities in outbreak investigation (description including time, place, people with emphasis on mapping when it is needed in collaboration with the GIS team) and advising on the operational response
- Implementing and maintaining a surveillance system to monitor epidemiological trends of relevant outbreak-prone diseases, working with health promotion and community engagement team as relevant. Guiding activities of medical staff for surveillance and/or active case finding, including ensuring understanding of the need for consistent case definitions and data recording (briefing of all new staff)
- Monitoring and Implementing initial assessment (for emergency situation), rapid health assessments and (baseline or follow-up) surveys. Where standard protocols are not available or appropriate, developing a protocol seeking extensive feedback and pilot testing of tools to ensure the objectives will be met robustly with support of HQ epidemiologist
- Planning and supervising the associated HR processes of the staff under his/her responsibility (recruitment, training/induction, evaluation, potential detection, development and communication) and ensuring that staff exhibits required skills after training and pilot test
- Supervise data encoding procedures, ensuring with the medical team that the data collection circuit is appropriate and epidemiology software tools are accurate and timely, analysing results and preparing regular written reports on progress and findings.
- Providing training sessions to medical teams on relevant aspects of epidemiology to enhance team response capacity
- Advising the MSF medical team on epidemiological matters that arise in the course of their activity research, and when necessary, designing and implementing epidemiological tools and data collection to meet new epidemiological needs.
- Work in tandem with other MSF sections present to ensure the harmonization of tools as relevant.
- Participating in operational monthly reports and organizing and/or assisting medical staff in preparing epidemiological reports related to health facilities and to researched areas
- Document lessons learned and capitalized on experiences, including handover, end of mission and capitalization reports
- Ensure regular collaboration with other supervisors / managers (HP, GIS, Medical activity managers, Logistics, Supply, Water and Sanitation, Admin).

**Profile required**

**Experience and Education:**

- Essential: Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in similar position and at least one year of MSF experience in similar position and working experience in in emergency interventions and assessments.
- Previous experience implementing a survey and/or outbreak investigation.
- Diploma: University degree in epidemiology or public health with specialization in epidemiology and/or biostatistics. Desirable: Master’s degree in epidemiology.
- Asset: previous experience in other medical NGOs.

**Competencies:**

- Demonstrated ability to identify priorities and to put in place relevant action plans in direct accordance with the operational/medical strategy.
- Leadership and organizational skills.
- Communication and reporting skills.
- Flexibility and ability to work under pressure.
- Ability to train, mobilize, and manage teams.
- Quality and Results-based orientation.
- Analytical and planning skills.
- Strategic Vision
- Service Orientation, teamwork and Cooperation.

**Computer knowledge:**

- Use of epidemiology related analytical software (R, excel, Epi-info, STATA and/or SPSS)

**Languages:**

- French & English working capacity (minimum B2)
- Knowledge in other MSF working languages such as Spanish or Arabic is an asset.

**Terms of Employment**

- Field-based position with (longer) visits to HQ in Paris.
- Fixed term and full-time contract (12 months, 100%) with possible extension.
- Ideal starting date: **January 2027**
- Gross monthly salary: According to MSF salary grid, L10
- Specific Emergency package including completion bonus and extra paid leaves.
- Social Benefits: Health insurance and living costs in the countries of intervention and in HQ, paid according to internal regulations.

jobs.title: Chargé de projet médical Kabo (F/H) - République Centrafricaine
jobs.description:
Vous souhaitez intégrer une association militante et agir concrètement pour plus de justice sociale ?

Médecins du Monde agit depuis plus de 40 ans pour soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, dénoncer les entraves à l’accès aux soins et faire évoluer durablement les politiques de santé.

En France et dans près de 30 pays, nos actions s’articulent autour de six combats politiques :

- droits et santé sexuels et reproductifs (dont le droit à l’avortement)
- migration, exil, droits et santé
- réduction des risques
- santé environnement
- droits et système de santé
- espaces humanitaires

## Médecins du Monde en RCA

Présent en République Centrafricaine (RCA) depuis juillet 2013, Médecins du Monde France (MdM-FR) a d’abord déployé des cliniques mobiles dans la ville de Bangui et dans l’Ombella Mpoko, afin de garantir l’accès aux soins de santé primaires aux populations déplacées en réponse à la crise sécuritaire. Les premières actions d’urgence ciblaient quatre sites de déplacés à Bangui.

Entre 2019 et 2022, dans le cadre du mécanisme de réponse rapide (RRM), les équipes d’urgence de MdM-FR ont mené huit interventions d’urgence rapide, notamment à Bossangoa-Benzambé et Ippy, avec le soutien d’ECHO et du Fonds Humanitaire RCA.

Durant cette période, des cliniques mobiles ont été déployées de manière réactive dans différentes régions du pays pour répondre aux alertes sanitaires et humanitaires.

Depuis 2019, MdM-FR intervient également dans la préfecture de l’Ouham à travers divers projets.

En septembre 2020, l’organisation a lancé le projet Bouca dans la sous-préfecture du même nom, dans la région de Yadé, avec l’objectif d’améliorer l’accès à des soins de santé de base de qualité pour les populations affectées par les crises.

Ce projet comprend le soutien aux formations sanitaires (FOSA) locales, passant de 5 FOSA en 2020 à 9 en juillet 2023, y compris l’hôpital de district de Bouca. Le soutien apporté couvre les soins ambulatoires et secondaires, la prise en charge des maladies courantes, les soins maternels et infantiles, la vaccination, la planification familiale, la prise en charge des violences basées sur le genre (VBG), ainsi que le référencement des cas nécessitant des soins spécialisés.

En novembre 2024, avec le soutien du Fonds Humanitaire RCA, MdM-FR a lancé un nouveau projet à Batangafo, axé sur la prise en charge des enfants souffrant de malnutrition aiguë sévère (MAS) et des survivant·e·s de violences basées sur le genre. Ce projet a connu une seconde phase qui se terminera en fin octobre.

Enfin en Mars 2026 grâce à une financement de la DG ECHO, MdM a ouvert une nouvelle base dans la sous-préfecture de Kabo couvrant 6 formations sanitaires dont l’hôpital secondaire pour une durée seize mois.

Pour renforcer l’impact et la cohérence des interventions, MdM collabore également avec d’autres ONGi françaises actives dans la région, telles que Première Urgence et Solidarités International.

Cette synergie favorise une meilleure coordination humanitaire, un partage d’informations sur les parties prenantes, et une mutualisation des efforts pour plus d’efficience

La stratégie d’intervention pour la période à venir prévoit une augmentation du volume opérationnel et financier, ainsi que de la couverture géographique.

Le repositionnement de Médecins du Monde comme acteur central de santé sur la thématique des VBG est également en cours de développement.

## Pourquoi nous avons besoin de vous

Sous la supervision du coordinateur terrain/site vous êtes responsable de la planification, de la coordination, de la mise en œuvre, du suivi et de l'évaluation de l'ensemble des activités médicales du projet.

Vous garantissez la qualité et la continuité des prestations de soins, assurez le renforcement des capacités des équipes médicales nationales et contribuez à la réhabilitation fonctionnelle et organisationnelle des formations sanitaires ciblées.

Vous veillez également à l'adaptation des interventions médicales à l'évolution du contexte épidémiologique, humanitaire, sécuritaire et opérationnel.

Plus spécifiquement, vos missions seront, en résumé, les suivantes:

**1. Pilotage et coordination du projet médical**

- Planifier, coordonner et superviser l’ensemble des activités médicales du projet
- Définir les priorités d’intervention, assurer le suivi des objectifs et proposer des ajustements si nécessaire
- Contribuer à la gestion des ressources, au budget et au reporting auprès de la coordination

**2. Renforcement du système de santé et qualité des soins**

- Accompagner la réhabilitation et le bon fonctionnement des structures de santé soutenues par le projet
- Garantir l’application des protocoles médicaux, des normes de qualité et des mesures de prévention des infections
- Améliorer l’organisation des services, les mécanismes de référence et la qualité de la prise en charge des patient.e.s

**3. Encadrement des équipes et développement des compétences**

- Superviser et accompagner techniquement les équipes médicales nationales
- Identifier les besoins en formation et mettre en œuvre des plans de renforcement des capacités
- Développer l’autonomie, le leadership et les pratiques professionnelles des responsables de santé

**4. Gestion des ressources médicales et surveillance sanitaire**

- Assurer la disponibilité des médicaments, consommables et équipements médicaux, et prévenir les ruptures de stock
- Suivre et analyser les données médicales, les indicateurs de performance et les tendances épidémiologiques
- Préparer et coordonner la réponse aux urgences sanitaires, épidémies et afflux de patients

**5. Représentation et gestion du contexte opérationnel**

- Assurer la coordination avec les autorités sanitaires, les partenaires et les autres acteurs de santé
- Représenter le projet dans les instances techniques et contribuer à l’appropriation locale des activités
- Adapter les interventions médicales aux évolutions du contexte sécuritaire et garantir la continuité des soins

**Vos collègues**

Sous la supervision hiérarchique du Coordinateur Terrain/Site et fonctionnelle du Coordinateur Médical, vous managerez l'équipe technique projet basée à Kabo. Vous interagirez avec les autres fonctions de la mission au niveau projet et coordination (logistique, admin et grants notamment) ainsi qu'avec l’équipe AFJC et le Médecin Chef de l’Hôpital Secondaire de Kabo

## PROFIL

**Vous êtes la bonne personne si…**

- Vous avez un diplôme de Docteur en Médecine, Sage-femme, Infirmier
- Vous avez une spécialisation ou une formation complémentaire en santé publique, médecine tropicale, ou gestion des projets de santé (cela constituera un atout certain)
- Vous avez une expérience confirmée dans la gestion ou la coordination de projets médicaux en contexte humanitaire
- Vous avez prouvé vos compétences en supervision, encadrement et développement de compétences d'équipes médicales pluridisciplinaires
- Vous avez une expérience réussie dans la mise en place, la réorganisation ou la relance de structures sanitaires
- Vous êtes reconnu.e pour vos capacités d'analyse, de synthèse et de rédaction de rapports techniques
- Vous êtes capable d'élaborer et suivre des indicateurs de performance sanitaire
- Vous avez une bonne connaissance des protocoles de prise en charge des principales pathologies tropicales
- Vous disposez d'une expérience en gestion des ressources médicales et en approvisionnement en intrants de santé
- Vous avez une expérience dans des contextes fragiles, isolés ou présentant des contraintes sécuritaires
- Vous avez, idéalement, une expérience préalable en Afrique centrale ou dans un environnement similaire
- Vous avez des compétences démontrées en organisation, gestion des priorités et travail en équipe
- Vous maitrisez le Pack Office
- Vous parlez français couramment. Si vous maîtrisez également l’anglais, ce sera un avantage

**Ce poste n’est pas pour vous si...**

- Vous craignez ne pas vous retrouver dans les valeurs et le positionnement militant de Médecins du Monde
- Vous ne préférez pas vivre sur une base aux conditions spartiates
- Vous n'êtes pas capable de travailler à un rythme soutenu et dans le respect des échéances imposées

**Les prochaines étapes**

Si votre candidature est sélectionnée, nous vous contacterons rapidement pour vous proposer un entretien RH avec un.e chargé.e de recrutement. Les entretiens techniques et managériaux, auxquels des cas pratiques pourront éventuellement être intégrés auront lieu par la suite.

Dans le cadre de notre processus de recrutement, une prise de références est systématiquement réalisée par l'équipe recrutement auprès de contacts professionnels fournis par les candidat·e·s.

Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, des vérifications d’antécédents sur listes internationales pourront être effectuées. Les données sont traitées de façon confidentielle et sécurisée. Plus d’infos :

Un extrait de casier judiciaire (B3) sera demandé à toute personne recrutée.

**Nous attendons votre candidature**

Nous n’avons besoin que de votre CV et de votre lettre de motivation.

Si vous pensez correspondre à ce poste, postulez !

## VOS CONDITIONS D'EMPLOI

**Contrat & statut :**

- Salaire brut mensuel 3 392 €
- CDD à pourvoir dès que possible jusqu'au 31 mai 2027
- Départ seul

**Cadre de travail :**

- Poste basé à Kabo, RCA
- Déplacements à prévoir dans la zone du Projet
- R&R tous les trois mois

**Les avantages :**

- 13e mois (pour les salarié.e.s ayant plus de 6 mois d’ancienneté)
- Prime d’expatriation de 10% du salaire brut par mois
- Prise en charge du transport (domicile – mission), des visas, des vaccins
- Hébergement: vous serez hébergé.e dans un logement individuel
- Assurance santé (participation à 50% de MdM et 50% du salarié)
- Assurance rapatriement
- MdM favorise la formation et la mobilité interne

**Les indispensables :**

- 5 semaines de congés + 22,5 RTT par an
- Plus d’infos : https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/nous-rejoindre/travail-humanitaire/travailler-a-linternational/

**Diversité et inclusion**

MdM s’engage pour l’insertion des personnes en situation de handicap et lutte contre toutes les discriminations.

Si vous bénéficiez d’une reconnaissance de la qualité de travailleur.se handicapé.e et/ou si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement de poste, n’hésitez pas à nous en faire part.

jobs.title: Climate & Environment Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Join MSF OCG as a Climate & Environment Coordinator !**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

## Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

## Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

We are looking for a Climate & Environment Coordinator to join MSF OCG.

Reporting to the Deputy General Director, the Climate and Environment Coordinator is responsible for leading and coordinating OCG’s strategic approach to reducing the environmental impact of its activities, while strengthening the integration of the health and humanitarian consequences of climate change into operational planning. The position works closely with the Logistics, Medical, Communication and Operations departments, supporting field missions and contributing to more relevant, responsible and effective humanitarian operations.

## Tasks & Responsibilities

- Develop and implement OCG’s strategy to address climate change and environmental issues across its activities.
- Support the integration of climate risks and evolving patterns of climate-sensitive diseases into operational planning to strengthen the relevance of operational responses.
- Promote the reduction of environmental impacts across OCG’s activities to enhance the environmental responsibility of MSF operations.
- Coordinate cross-functional initiatives on climate and environmental issues to ensure alignment and consistency across OCG.
- Develop frameworks, guidelines, and tools to support teams in effectively addressing climate risks and environmental impacts.
- Monitor progress towards climate and environmental objectives to ensure accountability and continuous improvement, including overseeing the organisation’s annual carbon accounting process.
- Represent OCG in intersectional and external meetings on climate and environment, and health.

## Your profile

*Education*

- Essential: Advanced university degree in environmental health, climate change, sustainability, environmental engineering, or a related field.
- Desired: Certification in carbon accounting.

*Experience*

- Essential: Experience in a similar role or in leading cross-functional initiatives involving multiple stakeholders without direct hierarchical authority.
- Field experience with MSF or another humanitarian organization is an asset.

*Languages*

- Fluency in English and French is mandatory.
- Additional languages are an asset.

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- Carbon accounting.
- Environmental sustainability and climate change.
- Health and humanitarian impacts of climate change.
- Strategic planning and change management.
- Data analytics, monitoring, reporting, and performance tracking.

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Strategic thinking.
- Influencing and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Coordination and facilitation skills.
- Communication and presentation skills.
- Project and change management skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment and demonstrate commitment to diversity, gender-responsive, inclusive, and non-discriminatory behaviours and attitudes.

## Terms of employment

- Full-time position 100%
- Open-ended contract
- **Working place: Amman, Dakar or Kampala**, subject to the selected candidate's eligibility to obtain the required work permit.
- Ideal start date: beginning of February 2027
- Terms of contract depending on the duty station.

jobs.title: P&O Partner Team Lead
jobs.description:
**What we’re looking for:**

Are you an experienced People and Organisation (P&O) leader with a passion for developing people, strengthening organisational effectiveness, and driving impactful HR solutions in complex humanitarian environments? NRC is looking for a **People and Organisation Partner Lead** to provide leadership and strategic P&O support across the **MENA and ESA regions**.

As part of NRC’s Global Team, you will play a key role in ensuring the delivery of responsive, consistent, and high-quality P&O services across the organisation. Working within a global matrix structure, you will lead a pooled P&O Operations team, providing strategic direction, remote team management, and effective resource allocation in response to evolving organisational needs and priorities. You will work closely with other section leads to ensure a coordinated approach, flexibility, and effective use of expertise across the global team.

Beyond team leadership, you will act as a trusted strategic partner and adviser to Country Offices, supporting the implementation of effective P&O strategies, policies, systems, and tools. You will also contribute to the contextualisation and development of policies and procedures, balancing global standards with local regulatory requirements and operational realities. The role requires both strategic oversight and hands-on engagement across critical P&O functions, including recruitment, Duty of Care, employee relations, and reward.

**To succeed in this role, you will bring:**

- A good appreciation of the humanitarian operating environment and the unique people management challenges within international organisations.
- A bachelor’s degree in human resources management, Business Administration, or another relevant discipline.
- At least 8 years of progressive experience in Human Resources Management.
- Demonstrated experience working in complex, volatile, and multicultural environments, ideally within an international humanitarian organisation.
- A strong understanding of complex, geographically dispersed matrix organisations and the ability to navigate diverse regional contexts and stakeholder expectations.
- Demonstrated experience leading remote, multicultural teams, building capability, and driving performance across different locations.
- Sound knowledge and practical experience navigating diverse and complex labour laws and employment regulations.
- A strong understanding of fundamental People and Organisation (P&O) principles.
- The ability to navigate complex employee relations matters, provide sound advice, and support effective resolution of sensitive people-related issues.
- The ability to manage competing priorities, make sound decisions, and allocate resources effectively in a fast-changing operational environment.
- Proven ability to lead and support organisational change, build buy-in, and guide teams and stakeholders through transitions.
- Strong relationship-building skills, personal influence, and the ability to establish trust, communicate convincingly, and influence decisions across different levels of the organisation.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Proximity to a selection of NRC Country and Regional Offices across the MENA and ESA regions to support effective collaboration, complementarity, and broad coverage across the Global P&O Partner pool.
- A strong understanding of the MENA and ESA regional contexts, including their operational and people management dynamics, will be an added advantage.

Please download a more detailed[**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQBhcRqkuLgQSZ3NBXNWotT_AfPFgZJVXqs5zr9QrVYisI0?e=GEPjFF) for more specific and generic duties and responsibilities.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: The position can be based at NRC Head Office in Norway, the Representation Offices in Germany or the UK, under an Employer of Records (EoR) listed countries, or a hosted contract arrangement in one of NRC’s Regional or Country Offices, provided the selected duty station is within ±3 hours of the MENA and ESA time zones.
- Contract: Permanent.
- Travel: Up to 25%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 10 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process
