jobs.title: Global Investigations Lead
jobs.description:
Do you want to be a driving force fostering ethical accountability in a global humanitarian setting? Step into a pivotal role where you'll serve as the technical lead for investigations—shaping standards, mentoring others, and ensuring that every case is handled with rigor, fairness, and impartiality

**Who are we?**
DRC’s work is guided by the values of Humanitarian Principles, Honesty & Transparency, Inclusion, Respect and Independence & Neutrality. It is essential that in all our work we uphold the highest standard of conduct and safeguarding standards for the communities where we work, our staff, interns, volunteers and contractors, partners, and other stakeholders. We have a duty of care to protect anyone who comes to contact with our work, particularly our vulnerable groups of beneficiaries and affected populations.
The Danish Refugee Council has a Code of Conduct (CoC) since 2007, and a Code of Conduct Reporting Mechanism (CoCRM) for International Operations since 2012. Together, they form a cornerstone of DRC’s commitment to accountability and integrity. As Global Investigations Lead, you will join a team of currently 6 colleagues (expanding further in early 2026) and support the Code of Conduct Reporting Mechanism in over 30 Country Operations.

**About the job**
As Global Investigations Lead, you will be responsible for the overall strategic direction, operational oversight, and quality assurance of the investigations function within DRC’s Safeguarding & Code of Conduct. This includes direct technical supervision of global investigations & investigators, technical guidance to Hub-based Global Safeguarding & Code of Conduct Advisors, collaboration with Country Operations, and ensuring alignment with organizational standards, Code of Conduct obligations, and donor requirements.

Strategic Oversight

- Participate, along with the Safeguarding and Triage & Intake (Global Registrar) Leads, to the overall team coordination, ensuring objectives, process and priorities alignments.
- Lead the development and implementation of the global investigations framework and methodology.
- Lead case meetings, quarterly reviews and contribute to Ethics Learning Reports and risk analysis products.
- Represent DRC in Investigators-dedicated external working groups and clusters.

Case Management and Quality Assurance

- Assign investigations in collaboration with the Head of Safeguarding & Code of Conduct and Triage & Intake Lead (Global Registrar).
- Supervise and review investigation plans, timelines, and outputs led by investigators and Authorizing Officers.
- Directly manage a caseload of high/very high-sensitivity cases, particularly those involving SEAH, retaliation, or high reputational risk.
- Ensure proper review and investigation reports’ quality for accountability and compliance with Standard Operating Procedures (SOP’s).
- Ensure fair, safe, and survivor-centered approach handling of investigations.
Lead peer review and improvement plans based on quality trends.
- Ensure, in collaboration with the Prevention/Safeguarding Lead, of the proper delivery and filling of post-case Management Action Plans.

Capacity Strengthening, Training and Reporting Obligations

- Support the recruitment, onboarding, mentoring and professional development of investigators.
- Design and support the delivery of investigations training, maintaining and updating a pool of investigators.
- Ensure systematic and confidential documentation of cases using approved systems.
- Collaborate with the relevant stakeholders on donor reporting obligations.
- Contribute to external reports when required, ensuring legal and ethical safeguards.
- Contribute to the analysis of findings across investigations to identify systemic issues, recurring trends, and lessons learned.

**About you**
To be successful in this role we expect you to bring sharp investigative instincts, sound judgment, and a principled approach to managing sensitive and high-risk cases. Success will rely on your ability to lead with clarity across geographies, mentor investigators, and provide strong technical supervision to uphold the highest investigative standards. You will need to champion quality assurance, ensuring that all outputs meet global benchmarks for integrity, impartiality & fairness, due process and a clear survivor-centered approach.

**Required**

- Minimum 7 years of experience leading or supervising investigations in humanitarian or complex organisational environments.
- A minimum of 5 years of management experience in the Ethics, Risk or Compliance areas, is considered a significant advantage.
- Master’s degree in law, human resources law, criminal law, human rights, gender or gender-based violence, international affairs, or any other directly relevant social science field.
- CHS Alliance-type certificate on PSEAH workplace investigations and fraud/corruption investigations certificates.
- Demonstrated expertise in SEAH and corruption-related investigations.
- Familiarity with trauma-informed practices, survivor-centered approaches, and duty of care.
- Demonstrated counter-fraud and anti-corruption experience and investigations
- Strong communication, judgment, discretion, and cross-cultural awareness.
- Commitment to upholding and modelling DRC’s values and Code of Conduct.
- Fluency in English.

Desirable

- Demonstrated counter-fraud and anti-corruption experience/certificates (e.g. CFE).
- Professionally qualified lawyers are encouraged to apply.
- Demonstrated understanding/experience of Internal Audit practices.
- Proficiency in French or Arabic.
- Field-related experiences (being based in a humanitarian setting/operation).
- Experience as manager or team leader supervising investigators or ethics officers.
- Experience and relevant certificates demonstrating experience as a Trainer of Investigators.

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

Work location: We will consider basing this role in the following locations – Copenhagen, London, Tunis or Dakar. This is a national position for which local terms and conditions apply. For roles based in our Copenhagen HQ, Salary and conditions will be in accordance with the agreement between DRC and AC.

We welcome all nationalities to apply for the role. If you do not have the existing right to work in Denmark, DRC will support with applying and paying for a work permit.

Please refer to [**our website**](https://drc.ngo/about-us/work-with-us/working-at-drc/salary-package-and-benefits/) for more details. For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Nathanael Monier-Dana, via **nathanael.monierdana@drc.ngo**

jobs.title: COORDINATEUR.TRICE PROJET RECHERCHE – EBOLA Nord Kivu - H/F
jobs.description:
**PRÉSENTATION ALIMA EN RDC**

Le 15 mai 2026, les autorités de la République démocratique du Congo ont déclaré une nouvelle flambée de maladie à virus Ebola dans la province de l’Ituri. Le virus identifié appartient à l’espèce Bundibugyo ebolavirus, pour laquelle aucun vaccin ni traitement spécifique n’a démontré d’efficacité à ce jour. Cette situation souligne l'importance de la recherche clinique afin d'évaluer rapidement des stratégies de prévention et de prise en charge adaptées à ce variant. La génération de données scientifiques robustes est essentielle pour orienter la réponse de santé publique et améliorer la protection des populations exposées. L’essai EBO-PEP est un essai clinique conçu pour évaluer l’efficacité, la sécurité et la faisabilité de stratégies de prophylaxie post-exposition chez les personnes exposées au virus Ebola. Il vise à produire des données probantes susceptibles d’éclairer les recommandations internationales et de renforcer les outils de contrôle des flambées de maladie à virus Ebola.

PROTECTION DES BÉNÉFICIAIRES ET DES MEMBRES DE LA COMMUNAUTÉ

Niveau 3 : Dans le cadre de ses fonctions, le ou la titulaire du poste sera amené·e à visiter les programmes et être en contact avec des enfants ou/et des adultes vulnérables. Par conséquent, la vérification du casier judiciaire ou la présentation d'un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs sera nécessaire. Dans les situations où l’impossibilité de fournir un casier judiciaire ou un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs est constatée, une déclaration sur l’honneur sera demandée.

LIENS FONCTIONNELS ET HIERARCHIQUES

Il/elle rend compte au Coordinateur Recherche Consortium EBO-PEP

Il/Elle est amené à travailler étroitement​ avec l’INRB, partenaire central de l’implémentation du projet.

**MISSION ET ACTIVITES PRINCIPALES**

Le/la Coordinateur(trice) projet de Recherche est responsable de la supervision de la mise en œuvre et du suivi des sites d’inclusion ALIMA pour le projet EBO-PEP; En étroite collaboration avec les équipes de terrain et les départements de support (médical, logistique, ressources humaines, finances, approvisionnement),, il/elle veille au bon déroulement des opérations conformément au protocole de recherche et aux Bonnes Pratiques Cliniques (BPC).

1. Définir et suivre le projet sur les sites d’inclusion

- Mettre en place la stratégie et le plan d’action établi en collaboration avec les instances coordinatrices de l’essai
- Applique le chronogramme des activités élaboré en collaboration avec le coordinateur de consortium de l’essai.
- Coordonner l'ensemble des activités de recherche sur les centres PEP, intégré aux différents piliers de la riposte, en collaboration avec l’équipe d’investigation
- Identifier et mobiliser les ressources nécessaires à la conduite de l'essai (ressources humaines, matériel médical et logistique), en collaboration avec l'équipe de coordination de la mission RDC.
- Collaborer avec INRB et UCAD pour le suivi des activités communautaires (suivi des contacts et stratégie d’engagement communautaire), intégré à la riposte, en veillant à leur bonne planification et mise en œuvre avant les périodes de forte inclusion des participants.
- Rédiger des rapports réguliers d'avancement destinés au reporting technique, et proposer des stratégies adaptées à l’évolution du projet.

2\. Veiller au respect du protocole de recherche ainsi qu'à la conformité aux lignes directrices des Bonnes Pratiques Cliniques (BPC) ICH E6 (R2) sur les sites dont il a la charge.

La qualité des données et le respect des GCP relèvent de l’équipe de monitorage et de gestion des données de l’essai (CTD, partenaires dans l’essai). Le coordinateur recherche s’assure que cette équipe dispose des ressources, procédures, outils et compétences nécessaires, et que les dispositifs prévus sont effectivement mis en œuvre. Il collabore avec le CTD pour :

- Accompagne le CTD dans la mise en œuvre des actions correctives et alerte les responsables appropriés lorsque cela est nécessaire.
- Organise les visites de monitoring avec le CTD, en assure la logistique
- Contribue au maintien d’un environnement de recherche conforme aux exigences réglementaires, éthiques, protocolaires et aux GCP, sans se substituer aux responsabilités propres du CTD.

3\. Encadrer les équipes d’investigation

Le coordinateur recherche anime l’équipe dont il a la charge, en collaboration avec le Co-RH et le coordinateur de consortium et l’administrateur.

- Participer à la composition des équipes et rédiger les profils de poste, identifier les besoins en formation.
- Organiser les plannings, planifier les remplacements du personnel en collaboration avec le Co-RH et l’administrateur.
- Assurer le suivi individuel de chaque membre de l’équipe : encadrement, coaching, soutien, conseil et évaluation. Organise l’accueil et le briefing des nouveaux arrivants.
- Réalise les POP (plan des objectifs de performance) des membres de l’équipe sous sa responsabilité directe.
- Transmettre aux équipes les informations et directives données par la coordination et/ou le siège ALIMA et s’assurer que les procédures de l’étude sont bien appliquées.
- Assure la prévention et la résolution des conflits au sein de son équipe.
- S’assure que les contraintes liées à la sécurité et à la santé sont comprises par tous.
- Planifie et anime les réunions de travail avec l’équipe et les partenaires : avancement des projets, sécurité, réunions d’équipe.
- Responsable du suivi de l’implémentation de la politique de protection contre les abus de pouvoir et les violences sexistes et sexuelles.

4\. Gérer les moyens matériels et financiers

- Supervise la bonne utilisation des moyens mis à la disposition pour la réalisation du projet, de l’ensemble des commandes (médicales et logistiques).
- Organiser le suivi des stocks de matériel (médical et logistique) et des médicaments d’investigation avec le logisticien du projet, ainsi que les commandes nécessaires.
- Assure le suivi mensuel de l’état des dépenses et des engagements du projet et analyse des données financières avec l’administrateur de la mission.
- Veille au respect des standards dans la gestion administrative et logistique du projet.

5\. Reporting et gestion de l'information

- Coordonne la production des SitReps, tableaux de bord et rapports de situation.
- Garantit la qualité, la fiabilité et la diffusion des informations opérationnelles.
- Produit les analyses nécessaires à la prise de décision du siège et des partenaires.

6\. Mise en œuvre des mesures de prévention contre les abus de pouvoir, les violences sexistes et sexuelles :

- Participe aux formations et aux séances de sensibilisation,
- Applique les standards relatifs à la prévention des abus,
- Assure, le cas échéant, que les membres de son équipe suivent les formations et les séances de sensibilisation et appliquent les règles de prévention des abus,
- Contribue à créer et maintenir un environnement épanouissant et protecteur.

## EXPRIENCES ET COMPETENCES

- Diplômes de médecin, infirmier, pharmacien ou de laboratoire.
- Master ou thèse en santé publique/épidémiologie.
- Expérience de coordination/ chef de projet d’au moins 2 ans
- Expérience du terrain, et de la coordination d’essai clinique obligatoire.
- Forte aptitude à la gestion de projets complexes
- Expérience préalable dans la coordination d'essais cliniques d’au moins 2 ans.
- Connaissances des bonnes pratiques liées à la recherche clinique obligatoire : Aspects réglementaires, éthique et vigilance.
- Des déplacements réguliers sur les sites d’inclusion sont à prévoir.
- Langues parlées du candidat
- La maîtrise du français et de l’anglais, à l'oral et à l’écrit est indispensable.

## CONDITIONS

- Durée et type de contrat : CDD de droit français de 6 à 12mois renouvelables.
- Prise de poste : asap
- Salaire : Selon grille salariale ALIMA + valorisation de l’expérience + Perdiem
- ALIMA prend en charge :
- Les frais de déplacements entre le pays d’origine de l’expatrié et le lieu de mission
- Les frais d’hébergement
- La couverture médicale du premier jour de contrat à un mois après la date de départ du pays de
- Mission pour l’employé et ses ayants droits
- L’évacuation pour l’employé et ses ayants droits

jobs.title: Country Director - Jordan CP
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**BACKGROUND**

In 2007, the IRC began providing humanitarian assistance to vulnerable and crisis-affected people in Jordan in response to an influx of Iraqi refugees and the strain on host communities. Following the eruption of the Syrian war in 2011, hundreds of thousands of refugees crossed into Jordan. The ongoing insecurity in Syria and the growing needs of refugees have strained Jordan’s resources and infrastructure and exacerbated pre-existing issues like water scarcity and high unemployment.

As resources become more limited, refugees and host communities have fewer economic opportunities and become more vulnerable. The IRC’s strategy for Jordan shows our commitment to improving the safety, health, education, and economic well-being of people affected by conflict, in camp-based refugees and urban-based refugees as well as vulnerable Jordanian host community, in coordination with the humanitarian community and the Government of Jordan. Simultaneously, IRC in Jordan is pivoting to a more long-term resilience/development programming responding to the context in Jordan and the worsening vulnerabilities faced by refugees and vulnerable Jordanians.

**SCOPE OF WORK:**

The Country Director (CD) is responsible for the overall strategic leadership and management of IRC's country program in Jordan, including programs, operations, finance, staff safety and security, program quality and accountability, stewardship of resources, and performance management. As the leader of the Senior Management Team (SMT), the CD ensures effective leadership and accountability across the country program and serves as IRC's principal representative to the Government of Jordan, donors, international organizations, civil society, partners, and other NGOs and the media.

The CD provides strategic direction and oversight of a portfolio of high-quality, cost-effective humanitarian and development programs, implemented directly and through local partners, in line with IRC's Strategy for Jordan. The role leads the transition towards stronger development-oriented programming while ensuring continued responsiveness to the evolving needs of refugees, vulnerable Jordanians, and other crisis-affected populations.

Success in this position requires exemplary leadership, strong communication and interpersonal skills, and the ability to translate geopolitical developments and evolving humanitarian, economic, and development conditions into strategic priorities and effective responses. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong contextual analysis, strategy development, and risk management skills, alongside the ability to build strategic partnerships, diversify program resources, and ensure readiness to respond to emerging needs while maintaining critical services. The CD provides strategic oversight and coaching for directly supervised senior managers, leads country program teams to identify, design and deliver responsive, high-quality programs; ensuring efficient management of public grants and private funds for results, compliance, and focused, timely reporting; and oversight of financial management and support systems.

**Specific Responsibilities:**

***Leadership and Representation***

- Lead the country program by establishing and maintaining open and professional relations with colleagues, promoting a strong team spirit throughout the country program, and providing guidance, oversight and resources to enable staff to perform successfully.
- Lead strategic representation and positioning with Jordan Government authorities at various levels; donors (including institutional, non-institutional and private), European Union; UN and other international organizations; international and local NGOs; and networks such as INGO coordination mechanisms and appropriate working groups. Develop and maintain a high level of understanding of donor priorities and planned funding.
- Play a leadership role in efforts to improve stakeholder coordination in Jordan.
- Provide leadership for strong, mutually beneficial, and effective partnerships with Jordanian organizations.
- Seek out and pursue respectful and safe opportunities to raise the profile of the work of IRC and its partners in Jordan, as well as the lives and the needs of the people IRC seeks to serve.
- Lead country program collaboration with colleagues in IRC’s MENAU Region to deliver regional programming and advocacy.
- Ensure leadership and management processes enable the IRC to effectively adapt to contextual changes and fully leverage opportunities to expand humanitarian access and assistance.
- Collaborate closely with regional leadership and neighboring country programs to address cross-border and regional issues coherently and effectively.

***Strategic Direction, Program Quality and Growth***

- Set the strategic vision and direction of the country program is aligned with IRC’s strategy to serve people with responsive and highest quality programming possible and secure the resources necessary to do so.
- Ensure the strategy action plan is of quality, implemented and guides decision making, to achieve IRC’s ambitions in Jordan and contribute to IRC’s strategic objectives globally.
- Ensure program quality through consistent use throughout the country program of rigorous assessment, design, and proposal development and review processes; comprehensive monitoring & evaluation, accountability and learning systems; staff development investments; and partner organization capacity strengthening.
- Actively seek out and pursue opportunities to expand, in line with the IRC’s mission, humanitarian, resilience and development programming in Jordan, in terms of populations and areas served.
- Develop a deep understanding of the geopolitical landscape and remain current on context analysis and develop responsive strategies to ensure the IRC mission can be carried out appropriately in case of contextual changes.
- Ensure timely submission of competitive, responsive, and high-quality proposals, and support colleagues in negotiations with donors.
- Lead implementation of IRC’s objective of expanding partnerships with Jordanian civil society organizations, and ensuring strong collaborative, principled partnerships that deliver effective and efficient program outcomes.
- Remain current on national and regional issues impacting the country program and partners and develop responsive strategies to changing contexts.
- Ensure the SMT delivers the leadership, management structures, staffing skills and approaches, and operational systems required to ensure a coherent “one IRC” approach to achieve Jordan and regional objectives. Identify opportunities for appropriate expansion and growth of programs, supported by the acquisition and investment of human resources.

***Emergency Response Management***

- Take primary responsibility for overall strategic and operational emergency response readiness and action for the country program.
- Lead Country Context Analysis, Emergency Response Planning and Strategy Development as well as In-Country Emergency Response Teams
- Ensure the country program maintains robust emergency preparedness and response capacity, including crisis management structures, clear decision-making protocols, and surge readiness to enable rapid operational scale-up or adaptation in volatile contexts.
- Lead and oversee the management timely, well-coordinated, and principled responses to emergencies, including conflict escalation, displacements, critical incidents, and program disruptions.
- Engage with Regional and Global Emergency Response Teams prior to, during and post emergency response, in line with organizational Emergency Guidelines.
- Represent IRC with peer organizations, and other emergency response agencies operating in Jordan.
- Ensure coordinated emergency response in the event of cross-border/regional emergencies.

***Safety and Security Management***

- Take primary responsibility for overall management of safety and security for the country program.
- Lead and oversee the management of all security risks and incidents, ensure timely, well-coordinated, and ensure primacy of the wellbeing and security of our clients, staff and partners. Create and maintain a culture of safety and security awareness throughout the country program, including training and briefings that prepare all country program staff for security incident prevention and response.
- Keep security, evacuation and contingency plans current and accessible to country program staff.
- Maintain close coordination and communication with the Regional Safety and Security Director on safety and security concerns and evolving issues that could adversely affect IRC staff or operations.Liaise with the regional office, with peer agencies and use the tools and information portals available to keep abreast of all security-related matters; In case of necessity, ensure adequate roll-out of emergency procedures.

***Staff Performance Management and Development***

- Supervise and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting performance objectives, providing regular and timely performance feedback, and leading documented semi-annual performance reviews.
- Provide direct oversight and guidance to multi-disciplinary teams across cross-cultural settings, ensuring performance excellence and alignment with strategic objectives.
- Effectively manage staff across various functions and locations, including setting clear expectations, performance monitoring, and accountability frameworks.
- Lead sensitive and complex staff-related conversations (e.g., performance issues, conflict resolution) with professionalism, empathy, and respect.
- Mentor and coach high-potential staff to support career progression and leadership development within the organization.
- Promote a culture of continuous learning and knowledge sharing across teams and departments.
- Promote and monitor staff care and well-being. Support appropriate interventions in response to identified staff care needs of staff.

***Stewardship and Operational Management***

- Drive operational excellence to achieve optimal efficiency and cost-effectiveness in all functions and operations of the country program.
- Oversee the development, deployment and utilization of financial and operational policies, procedures, and systems to deliver compliance with IRC and donor requirements.
- Ensure responsiveness and appropriate levels of in-person and remote support to all offices, especially in the areas of People and Culture, finance and supply chain.
- Provide timely and effective management and oversight of the Jordan country program’s financial position.
- Maintain effective and coordinated budget monitoring processes for grant funds and discretionary funds.
- Ensure a country-wide culture of safeguarding, grounded in accountability, transparency, and survivor-centered response. Provide strategic leadership to mainstream safeguarding across all country program operations and partnerships, in line with IRC’s Safeguarding Policy.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position reports to:** Regional Vice President - MENAU
- **Position directly supervises:** A senior management team responsible for Programs, Operations, Finance, People and Culture, and Grants.
- **Key Internal Contacts:** Country Program: All staff, Region: MENAU Regional Team, Head Office: Crisis Response and Recovery Department (CRRD), Awards Management, Ethics & Compliance, Operations and Strategy, Finance, Global Philanthropy & Partnerships, Program Quality, Technical Excellence, Advocacy and Communications, and General Counsel.
- **Key External Contacts:** Partner organizations, host country government officials, public and private donor agencies, international and national NGOs, UN agencies and Foreign governments and their diplomatic missions in Jordan.

**PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS**

Strong leadership abilities and interpersonal skills, and ability to deploy strong communications effectively, both internally and externally, and in humanatrian operational contexts. Ability to build networks, partnerships and diversify program resources.

- Graduate degree in a relevant field preferred.
- At least 12 years of dynamically responsible international work experience, including leadership at the Country Director level of multi-site, multi-sectoral operations in a complex operating environment, with demonstrated responsibility for emergency preparedness, crisis management, and operational response. Preference for experience in the MENAU Region.
- Prior experience working within organizational structures in transition and in humanitarian-development nexus.
- Experience working in conflict/post-conflict or disaster response situations is desirable.
- Fluency in English and Arabic is required. Fluency in Ukrainian an asset.

**Demonstrated Technical Skills:**

- Superior communications skills, verbal and written, in English. Arabic is desirable.
- Experience in managing security in a complex and rapidly changing security context.
- Proven ability to negotiate and work with partner organizations. Experience with organizational capacity strengthening and partnership building helpful.
- Strong budget and fiscal oversight capacities.
- Extensive representation experience and fundraising success, including prior experience with institutional and private donors.
- Established capacity to handle stressful situations in a healthy, constructive manner.
- Ability to respond to multiple priorities in a timely manner, producing high-quality outcomes.
- Prior work experience and a keen understanding of political complexities in the Middle East region.
- Proven experience in managing high-quality programming that meets the needs of clients.

**Ability to Travel:** Approximately 30% within Jordan and other IRC offices for workshops, representation and conferences**.**

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the country where this position is based and are currently residing outside of your home country, you may be eligible for an attractive relocation package. Eligibility is determined based on IRC's operational needs and specific role requirements. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to Clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its (CR) Client Responsiveness Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and giving them greater influence over program design and delivery.

**Diversity and Inclusion:** at IRC MENAU, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Senior Peace Finance Advisor, Peace and Security Investment Hub
jobs.description:
## About Interpeace

Interpeace is an international organisation for peacebuilding that strengthens the ability of societies to manage conflict themselves in sustainable and non-violent ways. Interpeace designs and delivers its work tailored to each situation in partnership with local partners and communities, based on extensive consultation and research. Interpeace also ensures that the processes of conflict management and change that it supports are integrated at all levels of society including local communities, civil society, government and the international community (we call it a ‘Track 6’ approach).

Interpeace was originally established by the United Nations and remains a strategic partner. Beyond field-based peacebuilding, Interpeace also assists the international community – particularly the UN – to be more effective in supporting peacebuilding efforts worldwide. This includes contributing innovative thought leadership on peacebuilding policies and practices. Interpeace is headquartered in Geneva and has offices around the world.

For more information about Interpeace, please visit [www.interpeace.org](https://www.interpeace.org).

## Background of the Assignment

The Peace and Security Investment Hub (PSIH) is anchored within the Agency for the Integrated Development of the North (ADIN) and financed by the African Development Bank’s (AfDB) Transition Support Facility (TSF) Pillar III. The PSIH initiative is connected to a larger AfDB investment: the Resilient Investment for Socio-Economic Empowerment – Peace and Security (RISE-PS) project, which is implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). The PSIH aims to catalyse peace-positive, locally grounded investments in Niassa, Nampula and Cabo Delgado.

With a mandate to bridge peacebuilding, development and economic recovery, the Hub is a strategic mechanism to address socio-economic exclusion, fragility and inequalities through inclusive and conflict-sensitive investment design. The PSIH aims to strengthen the ability of development finance and private sector investors to identify high-impact, peace-positive bankable opportunities in Northern Mozambique’s frontline markets. Currently, the business entry costs of scoping, developing local and community buy-in, and political engagement in sometimes contested and fragile environments are high and prohibitive for individual businesses and companies, despite the numerous opportunities that exist across various sectors – including agribusiness, aquaculture, forestry and infrastructure. The PSIH aims to stimulate private sector activity by leveraging an innovative toolkit to attract financing and investment in the North and, as such, accelerate the implementation of government plans, particularly the Programme for Resilience and Integrated Development of the North (PREDIN).

To achieve this, ADIN is partnering with Interpeace, an international peacebuilding organisation with a proven track record in operationalising peace-responsive development, to provide embedded technical support, capacity building and advisory services. Interpeace will draw on its Peace Finance expertise, participatory methodologies and the Finance for Peace Impact Framework to help establish the PSIH as a locally driven platform for community-validated, high-impact investments that enhance resilience and inclusive growth.

The PSIH will be piloted over an initial period of three years, with Interpeace support focused on three key pillars:

1. Embedded Technical Advisory and Institutional Capacity Strengthening;
2. Peace-Positive Investment Pipeline Origination and Research;
3. Support to Convening, Coordination and Advocacy Functions.

## Description of the Assignment

To support ADIN in developing a spectrum of locally informed, peace-positive bankable and concessional investment opportunities, with local buy-in, rigorous impact methodology and peace impact approaches built into the investment approach.

The PSIH will connect the private sector, development finance institutions, wider political, diplomatic and peacebuilding actors, as well as communities in the provinces of Niassa, Nampula and Cabo Delgado, to coordinate financing and catalyse implementation of shared peace and stability strategies. As such, it will provide a platform for local communities, civil society networks, peacebuilding experts, development finance partners and private sector actors to jointly ideate locally grounded, context-sensitive investment concepts that address community needs and can be scaled by public and private investors.

The Hub is situated within ADIN and will generate integrated participatory research, convening, consultations and technical support to develop a pipeline of locally informed and nationally owned peace-positive investment proposals that can be executed by development finance and private sector partners. Embedded community engagement will enable DFIs and MDBs operating in Mozambique to bring early-phase investment concepts to execution and accelerate the advancement of projects to later-stage proposal development for peace impact.

The Senior Peace Finance Advisor (SPFA) will be key to supporting ADIN in establishing a fully operational PSIH by embedding technical expertise, strengthening institutional capacity, and enabling inclusive, peace-positive investment design and coordination. In addition to managing the overall programme, the SPFA will ensure the Hub engages effectively with the private sector and with initiatives seeking to support the sector’s growth.

## Scope of Work

The SPFA will also function as the PSIH Programme Coordinator and work in close liaison with ADIN to ensure programme delivery. The SPFA will be technically responsible for the development of the pipeline of conflict-sensitive and peace-responsive investment proposals, aligned with national and international peace and stability strategies. The pipeline, which must be investor-ready, will cover a variety of economic sectors and industries that can increase livelihoods, productivity and diversification in key value chains, and improve the business environment – including agribusiness, aquaculture, forestry, infrastructure and manufacturing.

The SPFA will provide overall leadership for the PSIH, under the guidance of ADIN. The Advisor will serve as Interpeace’s representative to the RISE-PS programme and ensure that Interpeace’s Peace Finance approaches, tools and standards are embedded in ADIN and Programme Implementation Unit (PIU) programme documents, investment origination processes and implementation systems, in full alignment with the ADIN–Interpeace Terms of Reference and Programme of Work.

The assignment will ultimately support the development of ADIN’s institutional capacity to catalyse private sector and DFI activities in Northern Mozambique, the improvement of the investment climate, the creation of fair benefit-sharing and distribution mechanisms for communities, and the advancement of socio-economic opportunities.

The SPFA will be able to draw on the technical support and expertise of the wider Interpeace team on peace finance and the associated criteria and frameworks.

## Tasks

Under the guidance of ADIN and the Interpeace Peacebuilding Programmes Coordinator, the Senior Peace Finance Advisor will provide advisory services to advance the implementation of the Hub through:

### Strategic leadership and technical oversight

- Act as Interpeace’s senior presence and represent the organisation as the primary technical counterpart to ADIN, RISE-PS and AfDB, as well as to external stakeholders such as government, the private sector, development partners and civil society.
- Provide overall strategic and technical leadership for PSIH start-up and delivery in Mozambique, including shaping PSIH workplans, sequencing of outputs and management of risks, in line with the ADIN–Interpeace Programme of Work and donor commitments.
- Quality assure Interpeace technical advisory inputs, including the application of peace-positive investment standards, economic analysis and conflict-economy considerations in the origination and structuring of PSIH investment proposals.
- Ensure that capacity strengthening of ADIN forms a core approach to all PSIH programme activity.

### Stakeholder management

- Ensure continuous coordination and relationship management with ADIN, AfDB, UNDP and other PIU partners, including preparation of relevant meetings and technical briefings.
- Maintain regular stakeholder mapping and remain aware of and engaged with relevant initiatives and actors across the private sector, development finance initiatives and peacebuilding.
- Ensure engagement and coordination with relevant initiatives and programmes across Cabo Delgado, Nampula and Niassa.

### Pipeline development

- Coordinate the origination support for peace-positive investment pipeline development, including technical supervision of concept notes, theories of change, readiness criteria, first-stage peace/business diligence and partner engagement required for investment structuring.
- Contribute to the development of strategic guidance outlining peace-positive principles for foundations, CSR initiatives and blended finance actors, in alignment with national development goals and the Peace Finance Standards.
- Develop a pipeline sourcing strategy through field visits and enterprise diagnostics, screening opportunities against impact potential, commercial viability, risk profile and conflict sensitivity.
- Support investment proposals by overseeing:
- Preparation of pre-development feasibility studies for a spectrum of investment proposals, from small, impact-oriented, concessional sub-market-return ideas to large-scale, highly bankable, market-investor-based investments across sectors, scales, financing approaches and geographies;
- Provision of indicative financial structuring guidance and recommendations;
- Identification of risk mitigation measures and potential development and peace impacts, advising on de-risking tools and mechanisms;
- Development of investment-level peace-centred approaches and theories of change[1](https://reliefweb.int/#fn1), with key KPIs aligned with the Peace Finance Impact Framework and the Peace Taxonomy developed by Interpeace through the Finance for Peace initiative.[2](https://reliefweb.int/#fn2)

### Coordination of delivery systems

- Embed PSIH operational systems and governance routines, including maintenance of the PSIH Implementation Manual.
- Oversee the work of the Peace and Development Expert and interns, and ensure effective communication and collaboration with Interpeace HQ teams.
- Support the recruitment process for PSIH staff and consultants, including drafting TORs, supporting shortlisting, interviewing, selection recommendations and onboarding.
- Coordinate, supervise and quality assure the work of all PSIH consultants and short-term experts financed under the project budget, ensuring clear tasking, timely delivery, quality control and integration across outputs.

### Resource mobilisation

- Lead donor engagement and resource mobilisation to scale up the PSIH, including donor/DFI mapping, relationship cultivation, proposal/concept development and coordination of joint outreach with ADIN and Interpeace.
- Contribute to communications, visibility, knowledge management and evidence generation for the PSIH, including drafting strategic updates, learning products and inputs to high-level events and stakeholder engagements.
- Scope and cultivate partnerships with potential international and national actors to strengthen pipeline financing opportunities and investment uptake.

## Deliverables

- At least five sector and thematic opportunity scans per year, including value chain mapping and priority subsectors;
- Oversight of the development, maintenance and dissemination of an annual investment pipeline of at least five high-impact investment proposals that can be taken to execution phase by DFI/private sector partners. These would encompass the following key components:
- Intentional peace strategy connected to the investment concept;
- Theory of change with key KPIs based on the Peace Finance Impact Framework and Peace Taxonomy;
- Indicative financial structuring guidance and recommendations;
- First-stage business diligence based on external expert consultations;
- First-stage peace diligence based on participatory local engagement;
- Review of investment concept notes with basic financial models, risk and mitigation plans, and impact projections;
- Review of investor target list and support to the development of pitch decks ready for dissemination to target stakeholders;
- Recommendations for concessional financing approach(es), validated with key actors.

## Required Qualifications and Experience

- Advanced university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in economics, business development, public policy, international development or a related field;
- Minimum 10 years of directly relevant professional experience, including senior advisory/management roles that include technical support to government;
- Proven leadership experience in programme management, including supervision of multidisciplinary teams and management of multiple consultants;
- Strong negotiation, diplomacy and partnership-building skills; ability to represent Interpeace at senior level and to operate effectively in complex political environments;
- Demonstrated expertise in development finance/private sector development; familiarity with impact investment and peace-positive investment approaches is desirable;
- Strong track record of stakeholder engagement with government institutions, DFIs, MDBs, UN agencies and other donor/development partners;
- Demonstrated knowledge of and experience engaging with the Mozambican private sector;
- An existing right to work in Mozambique;
- Fluency in Portuguese and English required.

jobs.title: (2) Responsable de Programmes Desk - Siège Dakar - H/F / (2) Programs Manager, Desk - Dakar Headquarters - M/F
jobs.description:
## ALIMA recrute deux Responsables de Programmes Desk (H/F)

Siège Dakar, Sénégal · CDI de droit sénégalais · Déplacements terrain fréquents (30 %) · Prise de poste : 2027

Vous souhaitez mettre votre expertise opérationnelle au service de projets humanitaires à fort impact et contribuer aux orientations stratégiques d’une organisation médicale internationale ? Rejoignez-nous !

Au sein de la Direction des opérations, ALIMA ouvre deux postes de Responsable de Programmes, chacun à la tête d’un Desk couvrant quatre pays d’intervention.

Vous serez le lien entre le siège, les équipes de coordination pays et les équipes opérationnelles sur le terrain, avec une mission claire : garantir que chaque mission de votre Desk dispose d’une stratégie opérationnelle pertinente, évolutive et bien mise en œuvre.

Une belle opportunité de conjuguer leadership, vision stratégique et engagement humanitaire, au service des populations les plus vulnérables.

### Deux postes, deux périmètres

Desk 2

Desk 3

Pays couverts

Mali, République centrafricaine, Burkina Faso, Mauritanie

Soudan, Éthiopie, Nigeria, Guinée

Zone

Sahel central et Afrique centrale

Corne de l'Afrique, Afrique de l'Ouest anglophone et côtière

Enjeux marquants

Contextes sécuritaires très volatils, accès humanitaire contraint, crises prolongées et forte exigence de gestion des risques

Crises de grande ampleur et déplacements massifs de populations, environnements multilingues, coordination avec de nombreux partenaires et bailleurs

Langue de travail

Français prédominant, anglais professionnel requis

Anglais courant indispensable (à l’oral comme à l’écrit), cette langue étant largement utilisée au quotidien. Excellente maîtrise du français également requise.

Les deux postes partagent les mêmes missions et le même niveau de responsabilité. Merci d'indiquer dans votre candidature le Desk visé (Desk 2, Desk 3, ou les deux).

### Votre rôle

Rattaché·e au Directeur des opérations et membre de l'équipe de direction des opérations, vous définissez, pilotez, supervisez et évaluez les interventions humanitaires d'ALIMA dans les pays de votre Desk.

Vous animez une équipe de 5 référents (finance, RH, logistique, médical, bailleurs), encadrez et accompagnez les Représentant·es Pays et Chef·fes de Mission, et travaillez étroitement avec les ONG locales partenaires et l'ensemble des partenaires d'ALIMA.

### Vos principales responsabilités

- Analyse de contexte : assurer une veille permanente (politique, sécuritaire, économique, sociale, sanitaire), identifier les besoins prioritaires et les populations vulnérables, anticiper les risques et repérer les opportunités de nouvelles interventions.
- Stratégie opérationnelle : encadrer l'élaboration de la stratégie annuelle de chaque mission, en suivre la mise en œuvre, proposer les ajustements nécessaires et soumettre à la Direction des opérations de nouvelles réponses, y compris sur de nouveaux pays.
- Sécurité : évaluer en continu, avec les chef·fes de mission et les référents sécurité, l'exposition des équipes et des projets, et veiller à la mise en place des outils et moyens de gestion sécuritaire.
- Pilotage des programmes : superviser la planification, la mise en œuvre et l'évaluation ; valider les propositions de projets et réorientations ; suivre les indicateurs et accompagner les coordinations dans la résolution des difficultés.
- Partenariats : évaluer les partenariats existants (nationaux, internationaux) et identifier ceux à développer au service des objectifs du Desk.
- Management : constituer et encadrer une équipe Desk et des équipes de coordination engagées et compétentes, garantir le respect des politiques ALIMA (finances, logistique, RH), prévenir et arbitrer les conflits, conduire les recrutements de CP et CDM.
- Ressources et redevabilité : assurer la visibilité financière globale du Desk, faciliter la mobilisation des ressources et arbitrer leur allocation.
- Prévention des abus : appliquer et faire appliquer les standards de prévention des abus, et contribuer à un environnement de travail protecteur.
- Suivi, évaluation et capitalisation : organiser des revues périodiques, analyser l'impact, capitaliser les bonnes pratiques et nourrir l'apprentissage organisationnel.
- Vie associative : contribuer au plan opérationnel d'ALIMA, aux débats internes et aux échanges avec l'exécutif et les CA des ONG partenaires.

## ALIMA is recruiting two Desk Programme Managers (M/F)

Headquarters in Dakar, Senegal · Permanent contract under Senegalese law · Frequent field visits (30%) · Start date: 2027

Would you like to put your operational expertise to work on high-impact humanitarian programmes and help shape the strategic direction of an international medical humanitarian organisation? Join us!

Within its Operations Department, ALIMA is recruiting two Programme Managers, each leading a Desk covering four countries of intervention.

You will act as the key link between headquarters, country coordination teams and field operations teams, with a clear mission: to ensure that each country mission within your Desk has a relevant, adaptable and effectively implemented operational strategy.

An exciting opportunity to combine leadership, strategic vision and humanitarian commitment to serve the most vulnerable populations.

### Two positions, two scopes

Desk 2

Desk 3

Countries covered

Mali, Central African Republic, Burkina Faso, Mauritania

Sudan, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Guinea

Region

Central Sahel and Central Africa

Horn of Africa, anglophone and coastal West Africa

Key challenges

Highly volatile security contexts, constrained humanitarian access, protracted crises and demanding risk management

Large-scale crises and massive population displacement, multilingual environments, coordination with many partners and donors

Working language

Mainly French, professional English required

Fluency in English (both written and spoken) is essential, as it is extensively used in day-to-day work. An excellent command of French is also required.

Both positions share the same responsibilities and level of seniority. Please state in your application which Desk you are applying for (Desk 2, Desk 3, or both).

### Your role

Reporting to the Director of Operations and a member of the operations management team, you define, steer, supervise and evaluate ALIMA's humanitarian interventions in the countries of your Desk.

You lead a team of 5 advisors (finance, HR, logistics, medical, donors), manage and support the Country Representatives and Heads of Mission, and work closely with local partner NGOs and all of ALIMA's partners.

### Main responsibilities

- Context analysis: maintain continuous monitoring (political, security, economic, social, health), identify priority needs and vulnerable populations, anticipate risks and spot opportunities for new interventions.
- Operational strategy: oversee the development of each mission's annual strategy, follow its implementation, propose adjustments and submit new responses to the Operations Department, including in new countries.
- Security: continuously assess, with Heads of Mission and security advisors, the exposure of teams and projects, and ensure security management tools and resources are in place.
- Programme management: supervise planning, implementation and evaluation; approve project proposals and strategic reorientations; track indicators and support coordination teams in solving operational problems.
- Partnerships: assess existing partnerships (national and international) and identify new ones that serve the Desk's objectives.
- Team management: build and lead committed, competent Desk and coordination teams; ensure compliance with ALIMA policies (finance, logistics, HR); prevent and arbitrate conflicts; lead recruitment of Project Coordinators and Heads of Mission.
- Resources and accountability: ensure overall financial visibility of the Desk, facilitate resource mobilisation and arbitrate allocation.
- Abuse prevention: apply and enforce abuse prevention standards and help maintain a safe, supportive working environment.
- Monitoring, evaluation and learning: organise periodic reviews, analyse impact, capture good practices and foster organisational learning.
- Associative life: contribute to ALIMA's operational plan, internal debates and exchanges with the executive and boards of partner NGOs.

#### ​EXPERIENCES ET COMPETENCES / EXPERIENCES & SKILLS

**Votre profil :**

- **Formation :** diplôme supérieur en relations internationales, sciences politiques, santé publique, médecine, gestion de projets humanitaires ou équivalent. Une formation complémentaire en management, gestion de crise ou action humanitaire est un atout.
- **Expérience :**
- Expérience significative dans l'humanitaire international, dont une expérience préalable comme Chef·fe de mission, coordinateur·rice médical·e, coordinateur·rice de projet ou responsable de programmes.
- Expérience confirmée du management d'équipes multiculturelles.
- Expérience en contextes complexes, instables ou de crise.
- Maîtrise de la planification stratégique, de la gestion budgétaire et du suivi de programmes.
- Une bonne connaissance des enjeux opérationnels, des modes de fonctionnement et des politiques des organisations humanitaires médicales internationales constitue un atout.
- **Compétences :** gestion du cycle de projet, analyse géopolitique et humanitaire, gestion financière, gestion des risques et des urgences, suivi-évaluation, connaissance des principes humanitaires et du DIH, excellentes capacités rédactionnelles et de synthèse.
- **Langues :** français excellent à l'oral et à l'écrit ; anglais professionnel indispensable (particulièrement sollicité sur le Desk 3).
- **Qualités :** leadership affirmé et participatif, sens de l'analyse et de la décision, capacité d'anticipation et d'adaptation, éthique et sens des responsabilités, gestion du stress, talent de négociation et de diplomatie, ouverture interculturelle, esprit critique, grande disponibilité et forte mobilité.

**Your profile :**

- Education: advanced degree in international relations, political science, public health, medicine, humanitarian project management or equivalent. Additional training in management, crisis management or humanitarian action is an asset.
- Experience
- Significant experience in international humanitarian work, including previous experience as Head of Mission, Medical Coordinator, Project Coordinator or Programme Manager.
- Proven experience managing multicultural teams.
- Experience in complex, unstable or crisis contexts.
- Strong skills in strategic planning, budget management and programme monitoring.
- A good understanding of the operational challenges, working practices and policies of international humanitarian organisations would be an asset.
- Skills: project cycle management, geopolitical and humanitarian analysis, financial management, risk and emergency management, monitoring and evaluation, knowledge of humanitarian principles and IHL, excellent writing and synthesis skills.
- Languages: excellent written and spoken French; professional English essential (used extensively on Desk 3).
- Personal qualities: strong, participative leadership; sound analysis and decision-making; anticipation and adaptability; ethics and sense of responsibility; stress management; negotiation and diplomacy; intercultural openness; critical thinking; high availability and mobility.

#### CONDITIONS / TERMS AND CONDITIONS

**Ce que nous offrons**

- CDI de droit sénégalais, période d'essai de 3 mois renouvelable une fois.
- Salaire selon la grille en vigueur.
- Congés : 2 jours/mois + 0,75 jour/mois selon la politique ALIMA.
- Assurance médicale Allianz pour vous et vos ayants droit, et assurance rapatriement lors des déplacements terrain.
- Participation aux frais de scolarité des enfants de 2 à 18 ans présents à Dakar, selon conditions et plafonds en vigueur.
- Pour les candidat·es recruté·es à l'international, en plus :
- Frais de déplacements entre le pays d’origine et le pays de base (Sénégal) ;
- Un aller-retour par an dans le pays de résidence pris en charge pour l’employé et ses ayants droit et un second aller-retour par an pour l’employé ;
- Prime d’installation à Dakar en fonction de la composition familiale (3.000 à 5.000 €);

**What we offer**

- Permanent contract under Senegalese law, 3-month probation period renewable once.
- Salary according to ALIMA's salary scale.
- Paid leave: 2 days/month + 0.75 day/month under ALIMA policy.
- Allianz health insurance for you and your dependants, plus repatriation insurance during field travel.
- Contribution to school fees for children aged 2 to 18 living in Dakar, under current conditions and caps.
- For internationally recruited candidates, in addition:
- Travel expenses between the country of origin and the country of assignment (Senegal);
- One annual round trip to the country of residence covered for the employee and their eligible dependants, and a second annual round trip for the employee;
- A relocation allowance in Dakar, ranging from €3,000 to €5,000, depending on family composition;

jobs.title: Deputy Country Director, Partnerships
jobs.description:
**ABOUT SPARK MICROGRANTS**

Spark MicroGrants believes in a world where everyone lives with dignity and determines their own positive future. Spark has worked in 1000+ villages in 6 countries and has pioneered a community-driven development model in sub-Saharan Africa. Spark works with NGO and Government partners to scale the model's adoption and impact on rural communities - on their own terms. Our model combines facilitated community meetings with a small, discretionary grant to catalyze local action and institution building. Read more about our [Approach](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/the-spark-process), [Impact ](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/impact)and [Values ](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/about-spark#about-our-values)on our [website](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/).

Building on the success of the Advancing Citizen Engagement (ACE) Project, the Government of Rwanda, through the Ministry of Local Government (MINALOC) and the Local Administrative Entities Development Agency (LODA), has developed the National Framework for Participatory Village Planning (NFPVP). The framework aims to strengthen citizen participation and inclusive development planning at the village level as part of Rwanda’s decentralization agenda.

Spark MicroGrants, in collaboration with MINALOC and LODA, will support the national rollout of the NFPVP beginning in 2026, alongside direct implementation in selected sectors to generate learning for national scale-up.

**ABOUT YOUR TEAM**

The Rwanda program team works closely with MINALOC and LODA, including through embedded technical advisors in these institutions, Furthermore the team works with local governments in selected districts and sectors, where we have district coordinators and program facilitators respectively providing implementation support to the village planning process and village projects implementation. As the government has launched a national roll out of the village planning process, Spark Microgrants continues to support skills training for quality facilitation and joint resource mobilizations for villages to access financing for their identified priorities. The program team closely collaborates with other internal teams such as the monitoring, evaluation and learning; design and operations.

**WHO YOU ARE**

The Deputy Country Director, Partnerships is a senior leadership position responsible for strengthening Spark's country-level leadership, strategic partnerships, government engagement, and resource mobilization in Rwanda.Working in close partnership with the Country Director, this role helps drive Spark's overall country strategy, organizational growth, and external positioning. The Deputy Country Director plays a critical role in advancing Spark's partnership with the Government of Rwanda, particularly supporting the national operationalization and rollout of the National Framework for Participatory Village Planning (NFPVP).The position serves as a key strategic counterpart to the Country Director, taking ownership of major external relationships, leading donor engagement and fundraising efforts, and providing leadership and direction to the Partnerships and Resource Mobilization function. The role also contributes to broader country management, organizational decision-making, and cross-functional coordination, ensuring that external partnerships and funding opportunities translate into sustainable country-level growth and impact. As Deputy to the Country Director, the position will provide leadership and represent Spark in the Country Director's absence or when delegated, including in senior government, donor, and institutional engagements.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Country Leadership Support and Strategic Management**

- Serve as a key member of Spark Rwanda's country leadership team, working closely with the Country Director to drive the country's overall strategy, priorities, and organizational performance.
- Act as Deputy to the Country Director, providing leadership and representing Spark in internal and external engagements when delegated or in the Country Director's absence.
- Support the Country Director in translating organizational strategy into country-level priorities, annual plans, and measurable objectives.
- Provide strategic oversight and guidance across key organizational functions, ensuring alignment between programmatic priorities, partnerships, resource mobilization, and organizational growth.
- Contribute to country-level decision-making, risk management, organizational development, and operational effectiveness.
- Strengthen coordination and collaboration across teams, ensuring that external commitments and strategic priorities are effectively supported by internal functions.

**Government Relations and Strategic Partnerships**

- Lead Spark's senior-level government engagement and strategic partnership development, working closely with the Country Director to strengthen institutional relationships and advance Spark's country strategy.
- Serve as a senior representative of Spark with MINALOC, LODA, MINECOFIN, and other relevant government institutions, development partners, and strategic stakeholders.
- Drive the strategic partnership with MINALOC and LODA to support the operationalization and nationwide rollout of the National Framework for Participatory Village Planning (NFPVP).
- Identify opportunities to strengthen government ownership, institutional alignment, and long-term sustainability of Spark's approach within national development priorities.
- Build and maintain high-level relationships with government leaders, development partners, civil society organizations, and other influential stakeholders.
- Represent Spark in senior-level coordination platforms, policy discussions, strategic forums, and high-level convenings, strengthening the organization's credibility and influence.
- Oversee the development and strategic management of partnership agreements, MoUs, and institutional relationships, ensuring alignment with Spark's objectives and long-term ambitions.

**Resource Mobilization and Donor Relations**

- Lead the development and execution of Spark Rwanda's resource mobilization and donor engagement strategy, in close collaboration with the Country Director and global Growth team.
- Drive the identification, cultivation, and securing of new funding opportunities to support the national rollout of the NFPVP and Spark's broader country growth strategy.
- Build and steward senior-level relationships with institutional donors, bilateral and multilateral agencies, foundations, and strategic funding partners.
- Lead high-level donor negotiations, partnership discussions, and strategic funding conversations.
- Provide strategic oversight of proposal development and donor submissions, ensuring strong positioning, quality, and alignment with donor priorities and organizational strategy.
- Work closely with technical and program teams to translate programmatic priorities, results, and learning into compelling funding opportunities.
- Monitor donor trends, funding landscapes, and development financing opportunities, identifying opportunities for new partnerships and diversified funding.
- Ensure effective donor stewardship through strategic updates, high-level briefings, donor visits, and ongoing relationship management.

**External Relations, Communications and Organizational Positioning**

- Lead Spark's external positioning and institutional relationship strategy in Rwanda, ensuring a strong and consistent organizational presence among government, donors, and development partners.
- Provide strategic direction and oversight to external communications, donor-facing materials, presentations, policy briefs, and organizational messaging.
- Ensure Spark's work, results, and contribution to Rwanda's decentralization agenda are effectively communicated to key stakeholders.
- Oversee high-level donor and government visits, external events, strategic convenings, and visibility initiatives.
- Work with the Communications Officer and relevant global teams to strengthen Spark's reputation, visibility, and influence.
- Identify opportunities to position Spark as a thought leader and strategic partner in community-driven development and participatory village planning.

**Team Leadership and Functional Management**

- Provide leadership, direction, and mentorship to the Partnerships and External Relations team, including the Program Development Manager and Communications Officer.
- Set clear priorities, objectives, and performance expectations, ensuring strong coordination and accountability across the function.
- Build the team's capacity to deliver high-quality donor engagement, resource mobilization, partnership management, and external communications.
- Ensure effective collaboration between the Partnerships and External Relations team, program teams, and global functions.
- Contribute to talent development, organizational culture, and the development of a strong country leadership team.

**What You Bring**

- Master's degree in International Development, Public Administration, Business Administration, Public Relations, Political Science, or a related field.
- At least 8–10 years of progressively senior experience in international development, government relations, strategic partnerships, donor engagement, fundraising, or country-level leadership.
- Demonstrated experience working with senior government officials and national-level institutions, ideally within Rwanda or a comparable development context.
- Proven track record of building and managing high-level institutional partnerships with government, bilateral and multilateral donors, foundations, and development organizations.
- Demonstrated success in resource mobilization, donor negotiations, and securing significant institutional funding.
- Experience contributing to country strategy, organizational leadership, and senior-level management decision-making.
- Previous experience managing teams and leading cross-functional initiatives.
- Strong understanding of development financing, donor priorities, government systems, and the international development landscape.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to represent an organization confidently at senior-level meetings and forums.
- Fluency in English required; knowledge of Kinyarwanda and/or French is an advantage.

**OTHER INFORMATION**

Job Location: Kigali,Rwanda

Reporting to: Country Director

Start date: As soon as possible

Salary: Salary is based on geographic location and commensurate with experience

Probation period: Three months probation period with learning and performance objectives

Time commitment: Full time.

How to Apply: Follow the link to apply: [https://sparkmicrogrants.bamboohr.com/careers/186](https://sparkmicrogrants.bamboohr.com/careers/186)

**SAFEGUARDING**

Our safeguarding follows a do no harm principle. All Spark staff are expected to respect and uphold the safeguarding procedures and principles to minimize harm to stakeholders, program participants, and the environment, in compliance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework and national legislation in the countries where we operate.

**EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER**

Spark Microgrants provides equal employment and advancement opportunities to all individuals. Employment decisions at Spark are based on merit, qualifications, and abilities. Spark does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, gender identity, age, disability, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by the law. Spark will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities unless doing so would result in undue hardship to daily operations.

jobs.title: Country Protection Manager
jobs.description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified Country Protection Manager for DRC Sudan. This role has a country focus and ensures compliance to DRC procedures and guidelines within the country. The role contributes to the development of country strategies, which are translated into action plans and day-to-day tasks. The role provides technical support and guidance to field staff. This role is based in Khartoum

**About the job**

The Country Protection Manager has the overall responsibility for providing technical and programmatic support for DRC protection activities in the DRC areas of operations in Sudan. The role will include development and harmonisation of protection SOPs, tools, and training to protection staff in the field to ensure DRC has a consistent and clear approach to protection across all sites. The Country Protection Manager will lead in the development and roll out of DRC Sudan protection strategy including development of protection related advocacy messages using evidence. The position has strong focus on program development and identification of strategic areas through coordination mechanisms and donor engagement.

**Your main duties and responsibilities will be:**

- Protection Sector Technical Leadership
- Technical and Direct Line Management of Area protection managers
- Protection programme development, quality assurance and oversight
- Coordination and Advocacy
- Represent DRC in national and sub-national coordination fora (Protection Sector/sub-sectors and technical groups), providing high-quality technical inputs and promoting DRC’s evidence-based positions.
- Project development
- Contribute to and coordinate the design, implementation and evaluation of Protection related programming

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to lead ongoing protection analysis efforts, coordinating with Senior Management Team, Area Managers, and Clusters to identify protection trends and risks. In addition, you will guide the development and roll-out of country protection strategy in consultation with Head of Programme and other technical/area teams, ensuring alignment with regional/HQ priorities.

**Qualifications and experience required**

- Bachelor’s degree in Humanitarian Studies, Law, Social Sciences or relevant academic field is required. A Master’s degree relevant to humanitarian work is preferred.
- Minimum 5 years’ experience implementing and developing protection programs in displacement contexts
- Experience of preparing a protection programming strategies and advocacy strategies for a complex programme covering multiple sites.
- Experience in coordinating and standardizing approaches across a multi-site programme.
- Experience of integrating protection within a multisector portfolio.
- Experience providing remote technical guidance and developing training to suit a variety of audiences.
- Demonstrative ability to conduct trainings *on protection and human rights topics, including staff training*
- Full professional proficiency in English

***Desirable***

- Arabic is desirable

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

*Contract length***:** One-year contract with possibility of extension, subject to funding and performance.

*Band:* M.F

*Work location:* Khartoum

*Designation of Duty Station:* Unaccompanied/Non-family duty station

*Start date:* January 2027

Salary and conditions in accordance with the Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for International staff; please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-us/work-with-us/working-at-drc/salary-package-and-benefits/) for more details.
