jobs.title: Senior Digital Marketing Specialist
jobs.description:
Job Title: Senior Digital Marketing Specialist

Organization: Greenpeace Middle East and North Africa (MENA)
Department: Engagement
Reports to: Digital Marketing Manager

Location: The job is remote (based in the MENA region).

**OVERALL PURPOSE**

The overall purpose of this role is to contribute to the development and implementation of Greenpeace MENA’s digital marketing and channel strategies, strengthening the organization’s digital presence, audience growth, supporter engagement, and campaign impact.

The Senior Digital Marketing Specialist combines hands-on digital marketing expertise, analytical capabilities, and innovative approaches to translate strategic priorities into effective and measurable digital marketing activities.

**SCOPE**

The postholder is responsible for planning, implementing, managing, and optimizing assigned digital marketing initiatives across paid and organic channels, in alignment with Greenpeace MENA’s campaign, engagement, and fundraising objectives.

Working under the direction of the Digital Marketing Manager, the postholder contributes to strategic planning, ensures effective campaign delivery, and proactively identifies opportunities to improve digital marketing performance, audience engagement, and supporter acquisition.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**DIGITAL MARKETING AND CHANNEL STRATEGY:** Contribute to the development and refinement of Greenpeace MENA’s digital marketing and channel strategies, recommending approaches, priorities, and tactics informed by audience insights, performance data, and platform developments. Translate agreed strategies into actionable digital marketing plans.

**CAMPAIGN MANAGEMENT AND DELIVERY:** Lead the planning, coordination, and implementation of assigned digital marketing campaigns across paid and organic channels. Ensure timely and effective delivery through cross-functional coordination, content and asset readiness, publishing, campaign tracking, and quality assurance across relevant digital platforms.

**DIGITAL ADVERTISING AND MEDIA BUYING:** Plan, execute, manage, and optimize digital advertising campaigns across relevant platforms, including Meta and Google Ads. Manage assigned campaign budgets, targeting, placements, and testing to maximize campaign effectiveness and cost efficiency within approved strategies and budgets.

**AUDIENCE GROWTH AND ENGAGEMENT:** Apply audience insights, segmentation, and testing methodologies to refine targeting, messaging, and digital experiences. Work with the digital team to drive assigned initiatives to grow and engage priority audiences, strengthen supporter acquisition, and increase meaningful participation and conversion.

**CRM AND SUPPORTER JOURNEYS:** Utilize CRM and digital marketing platforms, including HubSpot, to implement relevant supporter communications and engagement initiatives. Contribute to the implementation and improvement of supporter journeys through audience insights, segmentation, and digital marketing expertise.

**INNOVATION AND RESEARCH:** Identify emerging digital trends, technologies, and platforms, evaluate their potential, and lead the testing and adoption of relevant innovations in alignment with Greenpeace MENA’s digital marketing strategy.

**REPORTING AND EVALUATION:** Work with the digital marketing manager on the analysis of digital marketing and channel performance. Support implementing actionable insights and recommendations, ensuring that lessons learned inform ongoing optimization and future digital marketing initiatives.

**CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION:** Work closely with Engagement, Campaigns, Fundraising, Data and Technology, and other relevant teams to ensure cohesive and integrated digital marketing activities that contribute to Greenpeace MENA’s organizational priorities.

**ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES:** Perform any other duties as appropriate to the post and as delegated by the line manager.

**QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, AND EXPERIENCE**

**Educational Qualifications**

- Graduate or postgraduate degree in marketing, communications, business, or a related field.

**Experience & Skills**

- 5–7 years of relevant experience in digital marketing, with demonstrated success in managing multi-channel campaigns and improving performance.
- Strong hands-on expertise in digital advertising, media buying, audience development, and campaign optimization.
- Proficiency in digital marketing and analytics platforms, including Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads, Google Analytics, and CRM platforms such as HubSpot.
- Strong analytical skills and understanding of emerging digital marketing trends and technologies.
- Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and collaborate effectively across teams.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in Arabic and English.
- Experience in the nonprofit, advocacy, or environmental sector is an advantage.

**Commitment**

Commitment to Greenpeace’s core values in response to environmental and peace issues through non-violent direct action-led campaigning in line with its mission.

**Disclaimer**

Greenpeace MENA is committed to achieving diversity within its workforce, irrespective of gender, nationality, disability, sexual orientation, culture, religion, and ethnic background. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

jobs.title: Regional Communications Coordinator - Middle East (50%)
jobs.description:
Malteser International (MI) is the international humanitarian relief agency of the Sovereign Order of Malta. For over 60 years we provide relief and recovery for people during and following conflicts and disasters around the world. Christian values and humanitarian principles form the foundations of our work. In over 30 countries in Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe and the Middle East, we support people in need – regardless of their religion, origin or political convictions.

At MI Regional Hubs are newly designed to contribute to increased funding, reduced risks and improved efficiency through regional coordination and shared capacities. Regional teams accelerate localisation by bringing expertise, partnerships and decision-making closer to local and regional actors. In close coordination with HQ and partner countries they facilitate capacity development and organizational learning.

**For the Regional Hub Middle East in Jordan we are looking for a Regional Communications Coordinator.**

The Regional Communications Coordinator is responsible for strengthening MI’s visibility, brand and strategic positioning across the region. He/she wil ensure high-quality and relevant regional communications that support MI’s and partners’ communication and fundraising objectives. Furthermore he/she will strengthen regional and partner communication capacities and networks to enable effective and locally anchored communications.

## **Your responsibilities:**

- Develop and implement MI’s regional communications strategy and annual communications plan in alignment with global and HQ Communications strategies
- Manage and monitor regional communications channels, media coverage and outreach to strengthen MI’s visibility and communication impact.
- Develop communication approaches that reflect localization, organizational transition and appropriate partner visibility.
- Coordinate regional crisis communications in close collaboration with country, regional and HQ teams, considering safety and reputational risks.
- Coordinate the production of regional communications materials, including stories, articles, photos and videos, ensuring compliance with MI guidelines and relevant donor and partner requirements.
- Maintain relationships with local and international media and serve as a key contact for HQ Communications and implementing partners.
- Contribute to MI’s Global Communications Network and strengthen communications capacities through knowledge exchange and collaboration with partners.

## **Your profile:**

jobs.description:
**JOB PURPOSE**

The Roving ICT Officer responsible for the daily operation, maintenance, and improvement of ICT systems, user support, and training. Acts as focal point for ICT matters, ensuring compliance with INTERSOS policies and alignment with HQ ICT strategies.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

• Monitor, maintain, and manage ICT equipment, tools, and services within the Mission.
• Plan and report field visits to monitor ICT activities and infrastructures.
• Provide ICT technical support and liaise with HQ ICT Unit and providers.
• Deliver training and guidance to staff and advanced training for ICT-responsible staff
• Produce reports, update and archive ICT documentation, and propose improvements to HQ.
• Ensure asset registration, tagging, and management as per INTERSOS standards.
• Provide technical input in local ICT procurement processes.
• Perform additional ICT-related tasks as assigned.

**Education & Professional Requirements:**

**Education**

- **Essential:** Advanced university degree in Computer Science or related field.
- **Desirable:** A master’s degree in one of these fields, ICT-related certifications are an asset.

## **Professional Experience**

- Minimum 3 years in ICT or technical functions, preferably in humanitarian or international contexts.

### **Professional Requirements (Technical Competencies)**

- Ability to use Google Workspace and provide support and troubleshooting (Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Meet, Forms, Calendar).
- Installation, configuration, and troubleshooting of hardware and operating systems (computers, printers, smartphones, Microsoft OS);
- Ability to provide technical expertise in the procurement of ICT equipment and services, ensuring compliance with HQ guidelines.
- Application of IT security practices: backups, password management, user access control, patching, endpoint protection, and basic security configuration.
- ICT asset management: registration, tagging, inventory tracking, and compliance with organizational policies.
- Practical application of IT security and IT service management practices.
- Configuration and troubleshooting of network infrastructure: LAN, WAN, Wi-Fi, routers, switches, access points; protocols (TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP).
- Use of Support Ticketing System.

**Added Value / Assets**

- Experience with Google Admin Panel.
- Experience with RMM tools (e.g., NinjaOne) and endpoint protection (e.g., SentinelOne).
- Experience with networking systems (Zyxel, Ubiquiti).

## **Personal requirements**

- Strong technical problem-solving skills.
- Communication skills, able to explain technical issues and solutions clearly.
- Ability to work independently and under pressure.
- Organizational and time management skills, ability to prioritize.
- Flexibility and adaptability.
- Result and quality orientation.
- Teamwork and cooperation.
- Commitment to INTERSOS principles and humanitarian values.

## **Languages**

- **Essential:** Fluent in written and spoken English; good spoken Hausa.
- Knowledge and fluency in local languages (Hausa and Kanuri) will be an asset.

jobs.title: Office Administrator
jobs.description:
**Background:**

GROOTS Kenya is a national movement of grassroots, women-led, community-based organizations and self-help groups in Kenya. We were founded in 1995, after the fourth UN Conference on Women in Beijing, China. We aim to address the lack of visibility of grassroots women in development processes and decision-making forums that affect them and their communities. We operate using a unique model, the “champions’ model”, which involves grassroots, community-led development process: Grassroots, women-led organizations, and groups take charge of their development by defining the problem, conceptualizing the solutions, designing and implementing interventions, and tracking change. We understand that no one can truly understand the needs of grassroots women better than they can. In this bottom-up model, an intentional effort is made to promote women’s voices and their personal and collective agency. The champions’ model challenges institutions and structures that disempower grassroots communities as agents of change.

**Purpose of Position:**

GROOTS Kenya seeks to recruit an office administrator responsible for coordinating and managing day-to-day administrative and operational support to ensure the efficient functioning of the organization. The position is responsible for promoting operational efficiency, ensuring proper utilization and accountability of organizational resources, maintaining compliance with organizational policies and procedures, and facilitating the smooth and effective running of the organization.

**Job Responsibilities:**

1. **Administration and Office Management**

- Serve as first point of contact for staff, grassroots women or external members and provide relative information as required
- Manage calls and correspondences, respond to enquiries or direct them to the appropriate person, and maintain records of communications where necessary.
- Maintain office environment, monitor stocks of office supplies, maintain inventory records and initiate replenishment requests in a timely manner.
- Coordinate the timely submission and processing of office utility bills, including. telephone bill, rental fee, internet fee and ensure that staff have access to essential office facilities and resources. Orient & induct new staff into the general office environment
- Prepare routine correspondences & provide document and records management support including scanning, printing, photocopying, filing and ensuring proper storage, accessibility and confidentiality of organizational administrative records
- Coordinate allocation and booking meeting rooms, shared facilities and office equipment to ensure their efficient and appropriate use.
- Coordinate and oversee compliance with established office opening and closing procedures in collaboration with the Office Assistant.
- Ensure office premises, common areas and shared facilities are clean, secure and properly maintained.
- Manage and maintain petty cash register, process approved routine administrative expenditures, ensure all transactions are supported by appropriate documentation and prepare timely accountability reports in accordance with the organization's finance policy.

**2.Asset and Inventory Management**

- Maintain an accurate record of all organizational assets, including their location, condition, assigned users and movement, and coordinate their servicing, repair and maintenance in accordance with organizational procedures. Coordinate the issuance, transfer and return of organizational assets, ensuring that all movements are appropriately documented in the asset register and asset issuance records. Maintain an up-to-date fixed asset register
- Ensure all organizational assets are insured, properly tagged and recorded.
- Coordinate periodic physical asset verification and promptly report discrepancies.

**3.Fleet Management**

- Coordinate vehicle booking and allocation for approved official assignments.
- Maintain vehicle movement schedules, logbooks and transport records.
- Coordinate vehicle servicing and maintenance schedules to ensure timely completion.
- Coordinate approved fuel requests and maintain fuel consumption records.
- Ensure drivers maintain accurate vehicle movement and mileage records.
- Maintain records of vehicle maintenance, repair costs and servicing history.
- Monitor vehicle insurance, inspections, licenses and other compliance requirements, and coordinate timely renewal.

**4. Travel and Logistics Management**

- Coordinate and support domestic and international travel arrangements for staff and grassroots women, including preparation of travel itineraries and schedules, flight bookings and ticketing, visa applications and travel documentation, accommodation, airport transfers and ground transportation, ensuring arrangements are made in a timely manner and in accordance with organizational procedures.
- Coordinate logistical arrangements for organizational meetings, workshops, trainings, conferences and other activities, including booking of venues,accommodation, transport, catering, equipment and other related requirements.

**5.Procurement Management**

- Coordinate procurement of goods and services in accordance with the organization's procurement policies, procedures, approved budgets and delegated authority framework.
- Identify potential suppliers, obtain quotations, conduct market assessments, undertake supplier due diligence and facilitate sanctions screening against applicable national and international sanctions lists and donor-restricted party lists. Maintain an updated supplier database in line with the organization's procurement procedures.
- Liaise with suppliers and service providers to confirm availability, pricing, bookings, delivery timelines and service requirements.
- Monitor and follow up on the timely delivery of goods and provision of services, ensuring they meet the agreed specifications and requirements in coordination with the requesting departments.
- Coordinate receipt and inspection of goods and services against approved orders and specifications, in collaboration with the requesting departments, and document and report any discrepancies. Maintain complete and accurate procurement and logistics records, including quotations, Local Purchase Orders (LPOs), procurement approvals, evaluation records, supplier due diligence documentation (where applicable), delivery notes, eTIMS-compliant invoices, booking confirmations and service completion records.
- Track supplier invoices and coordinate with the Finance Department to facilitate timely payment processing.
- Coordinate with relevant staff and suppliers to resolve logistical challenges, delivery delays, booking changes and other service-related issues.

## Qualifications

- A Bachelor’s degree in Administration, Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or a related field from a recognized university
- At least 3 – 5 years’ relevant experience in administration, logistics, procurement, or office support in a Not for profit organization
- Experience in asset management, procurement procedures, travel arrangements, and administrative documentation.
- Strong communication, interpersonal, coordination, negotiation skills & good market knowledge
- Excellent organizational, record-keeping and documentation skills, with high attention to detail.
- Demonstrated integrity, professionalism, discretion and commitment to accountability.
- Ability to prioritize competing demands, work under pressure, meet deadlines and work with minimal supervision.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite particularly, Excel, Word, and Outlook.

jobs.title: Chargé(e) de l’Administration et des Finances, Projet Wu’n Sina Sinru
jobs.description:
**A propos CIVIC**

Le Center for Civilians in Conflict (CIVIC) est une organisation internationale à but non lucratif, présente dans le monde entier, qui œuvre pour améliorer la protection des civils pris dans des zones de conflit. CIVIC aspire à un monde où aucun civil ne subit de préjudice du fait d'un conflit. Notre mission consiste à soutenir les communautés touchées par les conflits dans leur quête de protection, ainsi qu'à renforcer la volonté et les capacités des acteurs armés pour prévenir les atteintes aux civils et y réagir. Nous défendons l'idée qu'aucun civil pris dans un conflit ne doit être ignoré et nous agissons en tant que conseillers, proposant des solutions concrètes pour prévenir et traiter les préjudices subis par les civils. Pour en savoir plus, rendez-vous sur [civiliansinconflict.org](https://civiliansinconflict.org/).

**Resumé du poste**

Le/La Chargé(e) de l’Administration et des Finances assure la gestion financière, administrative et logistique du projet Wu’n Sina Sinru, financé par l’Union européenne et mis en œuvre par CIVIC, chef de file, avec ses codemandeurs Catholic Relief Services (CRS) et DEDRAS dans quatre communes frontalières de l’Alibori et du Borgou (Ségbana, Kalalé, Nikki et Pèrèrè). Basé(e) au bureau de CIVIC à Parakou, il/elle veille au respect des règles de l’Union européenne et des procédures de CIVIC, au suivi budgétaire du projet et des sous-subventions des partenaires, ainsi qu’au bon fonctionnement administratif du bureau de Parakou. Ce poste requiert de l’indépendance, de solides compétences organisationnelles et interpersonnelles, ainsi que la capacité d’anticiper les besoins de l’équipe de terrain.

• Ville, pays : Parakou, Bénin.

• Durée : 12 mois (renouvelable)

• Déplacements requis : 15 %

• Durée du contrat : 12 mois

• Supérieur hiérarchique : Directeur national (Togo et Bénin)

• Type de contrat : à durée déterminée

• Modalités de travail : sur place

**Responsabilités clés**

**1. Fonctions principales**

• Soutenir la gestion financière et budgétaire du projet Wu’n Sina Sinru ;

• Soutenir la gestion administrative, logistique et des ressources humaines du bureau de Parakou ;

• Soutenir la préparation des rapports financiers du projet pour CIVIC et l’Union européenne, y compris la consolidation des rapports des partenaires CRS et DEDRAS.

**2.Gestion et redevabilité financière**

• Enregistrer et traiter les dépenses du projet dans le système comptable de CIVIC, avec des pièces justificatives complètes et conformes aux règles de l’Union européenne et de CIVIC.

• Gérer la caisse et les opérations bancaires du bureau de Parakou et réaliser les rapprochements bancaires et de caisse mensuels.

• Gérer les avances liées aux activités de terrain (formations, ateliers, dialogues) et leur justification dans les délais, en privilégiant les paiements par mobile money ou virement.

• Vérifier les factures (factures normalisées), opérer les retenues fiscales applicables et préparer leur reversement dans les délais.

• Appuyer le suivi budgétaire mensuel du projet (budget, dépenses réelles, projections et analyse des écarts) et le partager avec le Chargé principal de programme et le Responsable Finances, RH et Administration.

• Appuyer la gestion du Fonds pour les initiatives locales (FIL) : vérification des dossiers (budget, plan de travail, plan d’approvisionnement), versements par tranches selon les étapes convenues, paiements directs le cas échéant, et contrôle des pièces justificatives.

• Appuyer les sous-subventions accordées à CRS et DEDRAS : revue des rapports financiers, contrôle des pièces justificatives, suivi des avances et appui au renforcement de leurs capacités financières.

• Appuyer la préparation des rapports financiers intermédiaires et finaux du projet pour l’Union européenne, en coordination avec le Responsable Finances, RH et Administration et l’équipe de gestion des subventions du siège.

• Appuyer la préparation et les vérifications des dépenses et les audits du projet, et assurer le suivi des recommandations.

• Appuyer l’inventaire des actifs et équipements du projet, et assurer l’archivage physique et électronique des pièces justificatives conformément aux procédures du bailleur et de CIVIC.

• Être flexible et disponible pour toute autre tâche.

**3. Ressources humaines**

• Soutenir le suivi rigoureux des feuilles de temps (timesheets) et de l’imputation du temps du personnel sur le projet, conformément aux exigences de l’Union européenne et de CIVIC.

• Veiller à ce que les ordres de mission soient signés avant chaque déplacement.

• Appuyer la préparation des contrats et autres documents des consultants et prestataires, et suivre leur exécution pour assurer le paiement des taxes et autres frais.

• Appuyer l’application rigoureuse du code de conduite de CIVIC, y compris en matière de protection contre l’exploitation et les abus sexuels (PEAS) et de sauvegarde.

**4. Administration, logistique et achats du bureau de Parakou**

• Soutenir les achats du projet conformément à la politique d’achats de CIVIC et aux règles de l’Union européenne applicables aux bénéficiaires de subventions (mise en concurrence, comités d’évaluation, dossiers d’achat complets).

• Soutenir la gestion administrative et logistique du bureau de Parakou (bail, véhicules, carburant, équipements, fournisseurs).

• Soutenir l’organisation de la logistique des activités (formations, ateliers, dialogues) dans les communes ciblées, en lien avec l’équipe programme.

• Appuyer l’application des mesures de sécurité du bureau.

**Qualifications & Expériences**

***Éducation***

Être titulaire d’une licence en finance, comptabilité ou gestion (un Master serait un atout).

***Expérience***

• Avoir entre 3 et 5 années d’expérience en gestion financière et administrative de projets financés par des bailleurs internationaux, idéalement l’Union européenne.

• Avoir une bonne connaissance des règles de l’Union européenne en matière de subventions (éligibilité des coûts, achats, rapports financiers, vérification des dépenses).

• Avoir une expérience dans le suivi de sous-subventions ou d’aides financières à des tiers.

• Avoir une expérience de travail pour des organisations à but non lucratif, idéalement au nord du Bénin ou en Afrique de l’Ouest.

• Avoir une expérience dans des environnements de conflit/post-conflit et/ou à haut risque (un atout).

***Compétences techniques***

• Maîtrise pratique des logiciels Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

• Oversee the design, contextualization, and delivery of trainings on civilian harm mitigation (CHM) and community engagement for security and defence forces pre- and awareness sessions for local initiative security and community self-protection measures.

• Lead technical workshops with the Beninese armed forces and the high command on civilian harm mitigation and protection of civilians.

• Ensure the integration of the community protection approach into civil-military committees and civil-security dialogues, and the quality of the protection risk analyses conducted with community peace and security spaces.

• Lead the conflict sensitivity and protection risk analysis during the start-up phase, and ensure it is updated before each activity bringing together civilians and security actors.

**2. Project Delivery and Consortium Coordination**

• Lead day-to-day implementation of the Wu’n Sina Sinru project in line with the work plan, the EU grant agreement, and CIVIC’s country strategy.

• Coordinate the consortium through regular technical coordination meetings, joint monitoring missions, and quarterly review cycles, ensuring coherence across the three specific objectives.

• Supervise the four community liaison officers based in Ségbana, Kalalé, Nikki, and Pèrèrè, and work closely with the Military Engagement Officer, the Community Engagement Officer, the Advocacy Officer, the Admin and Finance Officer, the MEAL Officer, and the leads of CIVIC’s other projects implemented in northern Benin.

• Ensure coordination with the cross-border action implemented in Nigeria by DRC, Search for Common Ground, and CIVIC (Bagudo, Borgu, and Baruten LGAs), including a common timeline and joint cross-border activities.

• Ensure the safe conduct of field activities in coordination with the security focal point.

**3. Budget Management and Financial Oversight**

• Collaborate with the Country Director, the Country Finance, HR & Admin Manager, and the Admin and Finance Officer to plan, monitor, and forecast the Wu’n Sina Sinru budget, including partners’ sub-grants.

• Oversee the Local Initiatives Fund (FIL): selection of community initiatives, disbursement by tranches against agreed milestones and supporting documents, or direct payment where needed, in compliance with EU rules on financial support to third parties.

• Ensure responsible use of funds and compliance with the EU grant contract, CIVIC internal policies, and procurement procedures.

• Track budget performance and provide regular updates, forecasts, and variance analyses; contribute to interim and final financial reports to the EU.

• Ensure cost-effectiveness and accountability across all operational and programmatic expenditures.

**4. Capacity Building and Institutional Strengthening**

• Mentor and build the capacity of CIVIC staff, community liaison officers, and partners (CRS, DEDRAS) in civilian protection, civilian harm mitigation, and community-based protection.

• Support Beninese institutions (EMG-FAB, ACM cell, ABeGIEF, ABPC) to integrate protection of civilians into their practices, training, and coordination mechanisms, including the replication of trainings by trained commanders.

• Support community peace and security spaces, including women, youth, and displaced people, to conduct protection analyses and carry advocacy messages to authorities and security forces.

**5. Business Development and Fundraising**

• Identify opportunities to consolidate and scale up Wu’n Sina Sinru results in northern Benin, in coordination with the Country Director and global programs team.

• Contribute to concept notes, full proposals, and engagement with donor representatives, including for follow-on funding.

• Provide technical inputs to logframes, theories of change, and narratives for protection-related opportunities.

**6. Stakeholder Engagement and Policy Influence**

• Represent CIVIC and the consortium with local authorities (mayors, prefects), FDS commands, ABeGIEF, ABPC, and humanitarian actors in northern Benin (UNHCR, UNICEF, WFP, ICRC, and the protection working group).

• Support ABeGIEF in organizing cross-border workshops on the protection of civilians in the Boo, Baatonou, and Fulani linguistic areas, and lead roadmap follow-up and advocacy meetings in Ségbana, Kalalé, Nikki, Pèrèrè, Kandi, Parakou, and Cotonou.

• Maintain regular communication with the EU Delegation and implement the project’s visibility strategy in line with EU guidelines and Do No Harm principles.

**7. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning**

• Ensure data are disaggregated by sex, age, and disability, that post-training evaluations take place three to four months after trainings, and that the register of dialogue commitments and the feedback and complaints mechanism are kept up to date.

jobs.title: Risk-informed Early Action Partnership (REAP) - Consultant Roster
jobs.company: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
jobs.description:
## **Organizational Context**

The [Risk-informed Early Action Partnership](https://www.early-action-reap.org/) (REAP, also ‘the Partnership’) brings together stakeholders across the climate, humanitarian, and development communities with the aim of making 1 billion people safer from disasters by 2025, by embedding early action at scale. REAP was launched at the UN Climate Action Summit in 2019, with [four targets](https://www.early-action-reap.org/who-we-are) designed to drive a systemic shift towards acting earlier, to reduce the impacts of disasters. REAP has also identified three drivers of change which inform its approach towards the 4 Targets, as set out in the [REAP Strategic Vision](https://www.early-action-reap.org/reap-strategic-vision) and [REAP Framework for Action](https://www.early-action-reap.org/reap-framework-action). The REAP Secretariat is hosted by the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

REAP is now looking toward its next strategic phase, 2026-2030. A 2030 strategy has been co-developed by Partners in order to continue REAP’s work while adapting to the new landscape and refreshing the value proposition of the Partnership. In REAP’s 2030 vision, people are resilient to the climate crisis because risk-informed early action is taken wherever and whenever needed, which REAP will achieve by “uniting governments and organisations working across all aspects of early warnings and early action, actively connecting diverse actors and initiatives to make sense of the complex ecosystems that enable early action, build coherence and complementarity of efforts, and enable partners to collectively scale resilient systems for risk-informed early action.” REAP will continue to push for systemic changes in finance for early action and for policy integration at all levels, while delivering the critical partnership functions—convening, community building, knowledge exchange and advocacy—that Partners have come to value. REAP’s next strategic phase will also include a more explicit focus in two important areas: (1) Being led by the needs of climate-vulnerable governments, using regional intergovernmental organisations as a way to achieve impact at scale and thus make best use of limited resources, and (2) Putting Partners in the driving seat so they take greater ownership over REAP’s work and build long-term sustainability of its efforts.

## **Background**

Launched at the UN Climate Action Summit (UNCAS) in September 2019, the Risk-informed Early Action Partnership (REAP) brings together an unprecedented range of stakeholders across the climate, humanitarian and development communities with the aim of scaling risk-informed early action. REAP is guided by its [2030 strategy](https://www.early-action-reap.org/strategic-vision).

## **Purpose**

You are applying for the REAP consultant roster. The purpose of the application is to provide information about your qualifications, experience, and expertise related to early warning early action (EWEA), including anticipatory action and pre-arranged financing. Your responses will help us update a consultant pool that we will draw on for specific activities that support the achievement of the REAP Strategy 2030.

## **Application process**

Please apply through the IFRC system using the link at the bottom of the page. Following this, you will have an opportunity to provide the information requested below.

Please note that in applying for this consultant roster, you consent to the use of your responses for the purpose of consultant selection and collaboration.

## **Important: application instructions**

Please provide your CV when prompted by the system.

In place of a cover letter, please provide a document of no more than two A4 pages that addresses all of the following:

### **Areas of expertise**

1. Areas of expertise on EWEA Pillars: Please prioritize from 1 (primary area of expertise) to 4:
- Disaster risk knowledge for EWEA
- Detection, observations, monitoring, analysis and forecasting of hazards
- Warning dissemination and communication
- Preparedness to respond to warnings / anticipatory action
2. Areas of expertise on EWEA foundational elements: Please prioritize from 1 (primary area of expertise) to 4:
- EWEA policy and institutional arrangements
- Community engagement and /or public awareness around EWEA
- Finance for early / anticipatory action
- EWEA M&E systems
- Other (please provide detail)
3. Relevant technical skills aligned with your areas of expertise
4. Key projects or initiatives: Briefly describe any major projects or initiatives you have contributed to in the field of early warning and early action.

### **Publications and research**

1. Please list your last 5 (max) publications on early warning early action, including anticipatory action and pre-arranged financing.
2. Please list your last 5 (max) consultancies / research activities you have undertaken in this field.

### **Additional Information**

1. Languages spoken.
2. Are you available for short-term or long-term consulting? Please specify your preferences.
3. Is there anything else you would like to share regarding your qualifications or experience?

Rather than following the traditional “people, process, technology” approach, this hub is built on a foundation of systems, people, and principles, recognizing that strong infrastructure and resilience must be values-led and people-centered to support our mission. It exists to enable and care for the wider organisation, upholding integrity, facilitating delivery, fostering culture, and ensuring our systems support not just what we do, but also how we do it, within the parameters of our decolonial and feminist values.

***Enabling with Care, Acting with Integrity***

**TEAM PURPOSE**: The Integrity Team exists to uphold the highest standards of ethical conduct, safety, and accountability across our organisation. We strive to prevent harm, mitigate threats, and ensure compliance with legal and moral obligations. We act as a trusted partner to protect people, preserve organisational credibility, and enable courageous and principled decision-making in pursuit of our mission

**JOB PURPOSE**: The Humanitarian Safeguarding Advisor provides specialist safeguarding expertise across humanitarian, fragile and high-risk contexts. The role strengthens Oxfam's ability to identify, assess and mitigate safeguarding risks in humanitarian responses by supporting the practical application of safeguarding standards during preparedness, response and recovery. The post-holder serves as the Secretariat focal point for humanitarian safeguarding preparedness, operational application and learning, ensuring that operational learning, emerging risks and sector developments inform preparedness, guidance and practice improvement across the Confederation. Working closely with Regional Safeguarding Advisors, humanitarian colleagues, affiliate safeguarding leads and other safeguarding stakeholders, the role supports greater consistency, preparedness and organisational learning in relation to safeguarding in humanitarian settings. This is a Secretariat-based, non-operational role that works through technical expertise, influence, coordination and advisory support.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES (Technical, Leadership, People, and Resource management)**

**1.Humanitarian Safeguarding Risk and Response Support**

- Monitor humanitarian contexts to identify emerging safeguarding risks, trends and vulnerabilities.
- Provide safeguarding risk analysis, technical advice and briefing products to support preparedness and response decision-making.
- Support humanitarian teams to identify, assess and mitigate safeguarding risks within programmes and operations.
- Promote practical, risk-informed approaches that balance safeguarding standards with operational realities.

**2. Humanitarian Preparedness and Operational Support**

- Support integration of safeguarding into emergency preparedness, contingency planning and response design.
- Develop and maintain humanitarian safeguarding preparedness resources, operational support materials, advisory products and context-specific implementation guidance that support application of existing safeguarding standards in emergency settings
- Support the operational application of safeguarding policies and standards through context-specific humanitarian guidance, tools, and advisory support.
- Advise regions, affiliates and humanitarian teams on adapting safeguarding approaches to humanitarian contexts while maintaining alignment with confederation standards.
- Coordinate the identification, mobilisation and technical support of safeguarding capacity required for humanitarian responses, providing specialist oversight and guidance while working through established deployment and management mechanisms.
- Coordinate humanitarian safeguarding inputs into relevant audits, certifications, assurance processes and organisational reviews to strengthen preparedness and operational effectiveness.

**3. Humanitarian Learning, Capacity Strengthening and Continuous Improvement**

- Translate learning into practical guidance, advisory products and implementation resources for humanitarian contexts.
- Provide humanitarian safeguarding subject-matter expertise and content to learning, onboarding and capability-strengthening initiatives led by relevant functions.
- Promote accessible safeguarding knowledge and learning that reflects humanitarian operating realities.
- Analyse learning from safeguarding incidents, audits, assurance activities, certifications, reviews and humanitarian operations to identify themes, systemic issues, emerging risks and opportunities for organisational improvement.

**4. Partnership, Coordination and Organisational Support**

- Work with Regional Safeguarding Advisors, affiliates and humanitarian teams to strengthen understanding and application of safeguarding approaches within humanitarian contexts.
- Facilitate exchange of learning, good practice and emerging approaches between regions and humanitarian responses.
- Support risk-based safeguarding approaches for partner-led and locally led humanitarian responses.
- Provide humanitarian safeguarding analysis and specialist input into organisational planning, preparedness, risk discussions, donor assurance processes, funding opportunities, audits and organisational reviews, as requested. Identify recurring humanitarian safeguarding challenges and opportunities for confederation-wide learning and improvement.
- Serve as the Secretariat focal point for humanitarian safeguarding coordination, including safeguarding inputs to humanitarian-related audits, certifications, assurance processes and organisational reviews, and facilitate the application of resulting learning to strengthen preparedness, response and continuous improvement efforts.

**5. External Engagement and Sector Awareness**

- Represent Oxfam in relevant safeguarding, PSEA and humanitarian protection forums as agreed.
- Monitor sector developments and emerging good practice in humanitarian safeguarding.
- Build networks and relationships that strengthen organisational learning and awareness of evolving risks and approaches.
- Contribute humanitarian safeguarding expertise to sector discussions and knowledge exchange initiatives.

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

**Most importantly, everyindividual at OxfamInternational Secretariat needsto be able to:**

- **Live our values of INCLUSION, ACCOUNTABILITY, EMPOWERMENT, COURAGE, SOLIDARITY and EQUALITY (read more about these** [**here**](https://oxfam.box.com/s/yfy4iyac8ulvoc01rkdg51awssv7ie1x)**)**
- **Ensure you commit to our ORGANIZATIONAL ATTRIBUTES (including adhering to the Code of Conduct):**

**Essential Requirements**

- Advanced degree in Humanities, Social Sciences, or any other relevant field.
- Significant experience in safeguarding, PSEA, protection or accountability within humanitarian contexts.
- Experience supporting responses in complex, fragile or high-risk operating environments including working with humanitarian coordination systems, partner led responses or with international NGO/UN environments.
- Experience conducting safeguarding risk analysis and developing mitigation strategies in humanitarian responses
- Experience developing practical guidance, tools and resources for operational teams.

jobs.title: Communications Advisor (Consultant)
jobs.description:
**Programme:** ASEAN-UK Health Security Partnership (HSP)

**Contracting organisation:** FHI 360 UK

**Type of engagement:** Individual consultant, call-down contract. Work is assigned on an as-needed basis through task requests; no minimum number of days is guaranteed.

**Duration:** Start date: as soon as possible to 31 March 2027, with probable extension subject to programme need, performance and funding.

**Level of effort:** Up to 50 days over the contract period, drawn down by task.

**Reporting to:** Robert Rosenthal, Senior Programme Leader, FHI 360 UK

**Location:** Home-based, Bangkok or Jakarta strongly preferred. Occasional in-person work in Bangkok and Jakarta and travel within ASEAN Member States for events or project site visits.

## 1. Background

The ASEAN-UK Health Security Partnership (HSP) is a five-year (2024–2029), £25 million programme funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO). HSP works with the ASEAN Secretariat, ASEAN sectoral bodies and partners across 11 ASEAN Member States to strengthen regional health security. Through collaboration with UK diplomatic missions in the region, ASEAN health institutions and national stakeholders, HSP supports capacity building, and implementation of national and regional health priorities. The programme is implemented by FHI 360 UK with the Pandemic Institute and Itad, and provides grant funding to a portfolio of regional and national organisations working on priorities aligned with ACPHEED and the wider ASEAN health security agenda.

HSP was launched at the ASEAN Senior Officials Meeting on Health Development (SOMHD) in July 2025. Now in full implementation after several rounds of grant making, the HSP stakeholder engagement and communications strategy is shifting from introducing the programme to stewarding partnerships, supporting grantee delivery, and demonstrating results. We work in close coordination on communications with the UK Mission to ASEAN (UKMis) and the ASEAN Secretariat Community Relations Division (ASEC CRD).

## 2. Purpose

HSP is engaging a Communications Advisor to provide flexible, hands-on communications support to the HSP team. The Advisor will write, edit and produce content in a range of formats (written, visual, video and event-based) that makes HSP results visible, supports grantees to communicate their work, and positions the UK as a trusted partner working alongside ASEAN. The Advisor will be part of the HSP Technical Assistance Hub (TA Hub).

### The Advisor will:

- Produce stories of grantee impact and other content that shows HSP results to ASEAN, UK and global audiences.
- Keep HSP communications products current, accurate and on-brand.
- Support HSP events and the HSP team’s engagement with FCDO, UKMis, ASEAN counterparts and grantees.

## 3. Scope of Work

Tasks will be drawn from the areas below and assigned as needed (see Section 4).

### 3.1. Impact stories, reports, and case studies

- Produce stories of grantee impact in collaboration with the HSP team and FCDO, from identifying stories through interviews, drafting, review and approval.
- Contribute to, review, and fact-check project reports for accuracy and professionalism.
- Apply relevant FHI 360 UK communications policies including informed consent, safeguarding and giving featured people the chance to review their own story.
- Work with HSP technical staff to ensure health security content is accurate and accessible.

### 3.2. Brand and communications materials

- Revise and update communications materials as needed, including fact sheets, country briefs, posters and presentations.
- Maintain and apply design templates, working with designers where needed.
- Keep HSP’s photo library and content archive organised, captioned and consent-checked.
- Collaborate with FHI 360 UK and FH 360 (US) communications team members to ensure brand consistently and compliance.

### 3.3. Digital, social media and newsletter

- Write and edit content for blogs and social media (primarily LinkedIn and Facebook), including adapting HSP technical papers and reports for general audiences.
- Write and edit content for the HSP newsletter, which reaches more than 2,000 contacts across ASEAN and beyond.
- Support updates to the HSP website and online presence.
- Coordinate approvals with FCDO, UKMis and ASEAN counterparts as needed, in line with the HSP editorial calendar and clearance process.

### 3.4. Video and multimedia

- Produce videos as needed, including script writing and storyboarding, arranging and conducting interviews, and capturing and editing footage directly or managing a videographer to do so.
- Capture photography at events and field visits, with captions and consent records.
- Produce short-form assets for social media (e.g. quote cards, short clips, simple infographics).

### 3.5. Events

- Join the FHI 360 UK team to produce events (e.g. launches, learning forums and side events at ASEAN meetings), including venue set-up and coordination, organising participation, writing remarks and talking points, and documenting events in written and photo formats.
- Prepare post-event summaries and reporting products.

### 3.6. Grantee communications support

- Support grantees to understand and implement FCDO, HSP and ASEAN branding and acknowledgement guidelines.
- Help grantees coordinate with the HSP grants team and the donor on communications activities and identify grantee stories and content for HSP channels.

### 3.7. Other tasks

- Other communications tasks within the Advisor’s expertise, as assigned by the Senior Programme Leader.

## 4. Expected Outputs

Outputs will vary by task. Typical outputs may include:

- **Impact stories and case studies (FCDO-approved):** Word/PDF documents and web-ready text, accompanied by photos and captions.
- **Fact sheets, country briefs, and posters:** Updated materials provided in editable source-file formats as well as print-ready/PDF versions.
- **Blog articles, social media posts, and newsletter content:** Ready-to-publish copy and visual assets.
- **Videos:** MP4 files optimized for web and social media use, including scripts, subtitles (where required), and an archive of raw footage.
- **Event documentation:** High-resolution photographs (JPEG) and a brief written summary or event report.
- **Monthly timesheets and activity summaries:** Completed timesheets and concise activity reports in Word and/or Excel format.

All outputs must meet FCDO, FHI 360 and HSP branding and acknowledgement requirements. Products using the ASEAN logo require ASEC approval, coordinated through HSP.

## 5. Required Qualifications and Experience

### Essential

- At least 5 years of communications experience, ideally in international development, global health or a related field.
- Excellent written and spoken English, with strong writing and editing skills and the ability to turn technical content into clear, engaging stories.
- Proven ability to create and manage media in a variety of formats: written content, case studies, photography, video (scripting, interviewing, filming and editing) and basic graphic design.
- Experience producing content for LinkedIn, Facebook, newsletters and websites.
- Experience supporting or producing events.
- Ability to work independently, manage several tasks at once and meet deadlines with minimal supervision.
- Based in Bangkok or Jakarta (strongly preferred), and able to travel within ASEAN Member States.

### Desirable

- Experience with FCDO or other donor branding, approvals and communications requirements.
- Familiarity with ASEAN and the regional health security context.
- Thai, Bahasa Indonesia or another ASEAN language.
- Own laptop and camera/audio equipment, and proficiency with editing and design tools.
- Experience managing videographers, designers or other creative suppliers.

## 6. Management and Reporting

- The Advisor will report to the Senior Programme Leader and work closely with the HSP core team, grantee focal points and, where relevant, FHI 360 UK country offices.
- Regular check-ins (proposed fortnightly, or more often during busy periods) to review the task pipeline and priorities.
- All FCDO-, UKMis- and ASEAN-facing communications and approval requests are coordinated through HSP unless otherwise agreed.

jobs.title: Senior Statistics Adviser (Innovation and Methods)
jobs.description:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Statistics for Development Division (SDD)’s** goal is to help the Pacific Island Countries and Territories achieve “highly competent and sustainable national statistics systems that meet national and international statistics needs for evidence-based policy, planning and monitoring.” SDD has a regional statistical system leadership and coordination role; and also supports the region directly in data infrastructure, collection, statistical methodology, analysis and dissemination.

The role – **Senior Statistics Adviser (Innovation and Methods)** will provide technical leadership on large change projects to support Pacific Island Countries and Territories in innovations in statistics collection and processes. Lead the technical agenda for the Pacific Statistics Methods Board and develop and improve statistical processes, methods and systems in SPC and member countries.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Technical Leadership for Regional Statistical Innovation Projects**

- Ensure relevant projects have a coherent approach to innovation that will lead to increased efficiency and effectiveness of official statistics in the Pacific.
- Ensure project technical approaches are evidence-based, appropriate to Pacific operating environments, subject to appropriate peer review and quality assurance, and incorporate innovations with a credible pathway to improved efficiency, quality or sustainability.
- Ensure project documentation (annual plans, operations manuals, reports, etc) are completed as needed, incorporate what is needed for strategic project success, and are of high quality in technical aspects.

**Development and Improvement of Statistical Processes, Methods and Systems including Survey Census and Administrative Data**

- Adopt improved methods and practices within SPC and/or member countries and contribute to improved quality, efficiency, timeliness or sustainability.
- Ensure a tangible contribution is being made to those improvements by this role in official statistical methods
- SPC is recognised as a successful leader promoting good practice in the Pacific with regard to official statistics.
- Ensure documentation and dissemination of improved methods through commissioned works, guidance notes and other publications that are well researched and founded in evidence and duly consulted on, quality assured and approved e.g. by the Pacific Statistics Methods Board.

**Support the Pacific Statistics Methods Board**

- The agenda of the Board is managed proactively and strategically, topics are identified well in advance, multiple parties are submitting papers, and the Board is recognised as leading consensus-building for statistical standards in the Pacific.
- Ensure advice to the Board is consistent, appropriately filtered, well presented, backed by best practice evidence, on time, and useful for the Board in taking decisions.
- Guide SPC staff and other authors to develop methodological advice effectively including consultation and testing with stakeholders and effective advice to the PSMB.
- Ensure meetings, logistical and administrative matters are well managed with support of the Finance and Administration Team.

**Technical Assistance, Training, and Support**

- Staff from SPC, national statistics offices and relevant staff in line ministries are trained and visibly developing skills in survey, census and administrative data most relevant to the projects this Adviser is working on
- Ensure positive relationships with key stakeholders – in member countries, donors, implementation partners and universities.
- A tangible contribution is made to progress in the countries and territories SPC is working with towards strengthened capacity to deliver surveys and censuses, through including methods capability, statistical skills, software skills (Stata, R, CSPro, etc.).

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- Master’s degree in statistics, data science or other academic discipline related to the role or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 12 years of relevant experience including 5+ years in a senior role (management, or influential technical leadership) in official statistics or related areas.
- Demonstrated experience as a technical innovator and leader, communicating a vision, and influencing a wide range of stakeholders
- In-depth knowledge and experience in at least one of complex surveys or administrative data for official statistics, and solid working knowledge of the other.
- Experience in designing and delivering training for professionals.
- A good understanding of the challenges developing countries (particularly small island states) face, in the collection, production and use of official statistics.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** – **3 years** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **Senior Statistics Adviser (Innovation and Methods)** is a band 12 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 3,743‒4,679 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 11,566–14,458 (USD 5,016–6,270; EUR 4,526–5,658). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: MG 129 – Consultant international : formation de l’ANFA à la modélisation MINIMOD
jobs.description:
Helen Keller Intl recrute un consultant international pour environ 10 jours de travail répartis sur environ 3 mois, afin de former le comité directeur de l'Alliance nationale pour la fortification alimentaire (ANFA) à l'outil de modélisation MINIMOD. La mission combine une préparation à distance et une mission de 4 jours à Antananarivo pour la formation.

À l'issue de la formation, les membres de l'ANFA doivent pouvoir utiliser MINIMOD pour comparer des options de fortification de l'huile, du bouillon et de la farine de blé, et disposer d'un premier rapport de modélisation pour appuyer leurs décisions.

**Introduction et contexte**

Helen Keller Intl met en œuvre la composante Madagascar du Global Programme Modular Nutrition Actions (MoNA), axée sur la fortification alimentaire à grande échelle (LSFF), avec la GIZ, sur financement du BMZ et de la Fondation Gates. La subvention de Helen Keller Intl court du 15 septembre 2026 au 15 mai 2028.

L'ANFA coordonne l'agenda national de fortification alimentaire, mais manque encore de moyens et d'outils d'aide à la décision. Le passage de la fortification volontaire à la fortification obligatoire, notamment pour l'huile et la farine de blé, demande de comparer les options possibles : véhicules alimentaires, niveaux de fortification, couverture, coûts et effets attendus sur les apports en micronutriments.

MINIMOD (Micronutrient Intervention Modeling) est un outil développé par l'Université de Californie à Davis pour estimer l'efficacité et le coût de différentes combinaisons d'interventions en micronutriments. Helen Keller Intl prévoit d'y former environ 15 membres du comité directeur de l'ANFA. Les 2 notes politiques prévues dans la même activité sont suivies directement par Helen Keller Intl et ne font pas partie de cette mission.

**Objectifs**

**Objectif général :** renforcer la capacité de l'ANFA à utiliser la modélisation pour orienter les décisions en matière de fortification alimentaire.

Les objectifs spécifiques sont les suivants :

1. Paramétrer MINIMOD pour Madagascar à partir des données nationales disponibles.
2. Former environ 15 membres du comité directeur de l'ANFA à l'utilisation de MINIMOD.
3. Produire avec les participants au moins un scénario de modélisation comparant des options de fortification.
4. Proposer un plan de suivi pour que l'ANFA puisse mettre à jour les modèles sans appui extérieur.

jobs.title: Sr. Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant
jobs.description:
Under the overall and direct supervision of the Head of Sub-Office (HoSO) in Cotabato and the technical supervision of the National Monitoring and Evaluation Officer, the successful candidate will provide operational and technical support for information management, monitoring, evaluation and learning activities for programmes in Mindanao, with a focus on projects related to peacebuilding, community stabilization, durable solutions, climate mobility, and migration management and protection. Based in the Cotabato Sub-Office, the incumbent will support the implementation and coordination of M&E activities in Mindanao and, in close coordination with the National M&E Officer, provide technical support to M&E staff based in the Marawi and Zamboanga Satellite Offices.

## **Responsibilities**

1. Coordinate with the National M&E Officer and M&E staff in satellite offices to support the implementation of M&E activities for projects in Mindanao, in line with approved M&E plans, and provide technical guidance and support to M&E staff in satellite offices.
2. Contribute to the development and usage of M&E tools and plans for qualitative and quantitative data collection, data quality monitoring, analysis and regular reporting on project indicators;
3. Create and manage internal project databases, ensuring that all relevant data on the implementation of projects are captured and organized;
4. Contribute to the preparation of donor reports, project progress updates, and institutional reports, as required and in coordination with the National M&E Officer, by providing accurate and verified data and information on project outputs, outcomes, and results for internal and external reporting and communication purposes.
5. Conduct field monitoring and evaluation visits in coordination with the project teams to monitor technical compliance against approved Results Framework and plans;
6. Coordinate and provide technical guidance to enumerators during data collection for monitoring and evaluation purposes, as needed;
7. Consolidate, clean and analyze data on programme implementation and indicators and report any issues to the supervisor and project team;
8. Support the final evaluation of projects, as required, in coordination with the project team and other relevant stakeholders;
9. Serve as the Community Feedback Mechanism (CFM) focal point for Mindanao, providing timely coordination and documentation support for community feedback and contributing to the implementation and strengthening of CFM mechanisms in line with the approved framework.
10. Support the implementation of PSEA-related initiatives, including the integration of relevant PSEA considerations into M&E activities, as appropriate.
11. Perform other duties, as may be assigned.

## **Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in Social or Political Science, Development Studies, Statistics, or any related field from an accredited academic institution with four (4) years of relevant professional experience in monitoring and evaluation; or
- Completed High School degree from an accredited academic institution with six (6) years of relevant professional experience.

**Experience**

- Experience in project development, project management, monitoring and evaluation, and information management required.
- Experience in data analysis and report writing required.
- Proven ability to consolidate and validate information from multiple sources.
- Working experience with UN agencies, NGOs and/or other humanitarian and development agencies, a distinctive asset.

**Skills**

- Proven ability to consolidate and validate information from multiple sources.
- Proven ability to work with basic presentation software, especially Microsoft PowerPoint and Excel.
- Knowledge of ACCESS and statistical analysis, preferred.
- Knowledge on project management in a peacebuilding and development context ideal.

**Languages**

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written). Proficiency in Tagalog and/or other languages commonly spoken in Mindanao is desirable.

**Required Competencies**
