jobs.title: Oficial de Enlace
jobs.description:
**DATOS GENERALES**

- *Sede de Trabajo: Caracas, Venezuela*
- *Mes de inicio: Enero 2027*
- *Plazas Disponibles: 1*
- *Reportará a : Director del Proyecto*
- *Unidad a la que pertenecerá: Programas*

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL PROGRAMA:**

AFGHS-FHI 360, un proyecto global financiado por el Departamento de Estado (DOS), tiene como objetivo: garantizar la continuidad y la cobertura de los servicios sanitarios; aumentar la capacidad de los sistemas sanitarios nacionales para integrar y mantener de forma eficaz los servicios y las innovaciones técnicas; garantizar que las amenazas de enfermedades infecciosas se detecten a tiempo, se contengan y se evite que crucen las fronteras; aumentar la capacidad de los gobiernos nacionales y subnacionales para alcanzar la autosuficiencia programática y financiera; y mitigar el riesgo de transición.

Años de crisis económica, social y política han aumentado la vulnerabilidad de América Latina y el Caribe (ALC)2 ante las enfermedades y han mermado su capacidad de respuesta. Durante el último año, el cambio de liderazgo en el país y dos terremotos devastadores han supuesto un reto adicional para la nación. El VIH sigue siendo una prioridad de salud pública, pero el contexto y las limitaciones de recursos frenan los avances. La falta de coherencia en las políticas entre regiones afecta al rendimiento a lo largo de la cascada del VIH, ya que el sistema nacional aún no tiene la capacidad de implementar y garantizar una atención y un tratamiento del VIH coherentes en todas las regiones. La imprevisibilidad de los contextos sociales, políticos y operativos crea obstáculos únicos para la implementación de un modelo comunitario de lucha contra el VIH.

El fortalecimiento de la capacidad de los socios comunitarios para implementar intervenciones de calidad contra el VIH, alineadas con las normas globales y las políticas y protocolos del gobierno anfitrión, es fundamental para el éxito de esta actividad. En colaboración con FHI 360, VENGOAL facilitará la formación y el asesoramiento en materia de información técnica y estratégica (SI) a los socios comunitarios, además de realizar la supervisión en el terreno y las evaluaciones de la calidad de los datos (DQA), de modo que se apoye a los socios comunitarios para que establezcan colaboraciones de alta calidad con las partes interesadas locales y los clientes.

**OBJETIVO DE LA POSICIÓN:**

Apoyar al Director del Proyecto en la coordinación operativa y administrativa de la respuesta a emergencias actuales o futuras, asegurando la ejecución oportuna de las actividades dentro del alcance, cronograma y presupuesto establecidos. La posición facilita la articulación entre el equipo de gestión, las oficinas de VENGOAL, el donante y las organizaciones socias locales; acompaña la selección, incorporación y fortalecimiento de capacidades de los socios; y da seguimiento a la implementación, el desempeño, los reportes y el cumplimiento de las políticas y estándares institucionales y del donante.

Asimismo, contribuye al monitoreo de riesgos y a la rendición de cuentas, apoya la preparación de informes y el análisis de datos, y representa al proyecto en los espacios de coordinación que le sean asignados, promoviendo relaciones sólidas y eficientes con los socios y otros actores del sector salud.

**RESPONSABILIDADES/FUNCIONES PRINCIPALES**

1. Apoyar al Director de Proyecto en la gestión administrativa de la respuesta a la emergencia, actual o futura, desde el punto de vista operativo.
2. Coordinar con los socios locales lo necesario para la implementación del proyecto de respuesta en alcance, tiempo y presupuesto.
3. Coordinar eventos y actividades para la respuesta.
4. Mantener el control semanal de los reportes, de acuerdo con el acuerdo para la respuesta a emergencias actuales o futuras.
5. Apoyar al Director de proyecto en el seguimiento de las tareas asignadas a las diferentes áreas y/o socios, garantizando el cumplimiento de las metas dentro del plazo establecido.
6. Apoya en la elaboración de informes, la captura y el análisis de datos, así́ como en la revisión de TDR e informes de misión cuando se le solicite.
7. Coordinar con otras oficinas de VENGOAL para responder a emergencias o desastres cuando se requiera.
8. Mantener el estricto cumplimiento del cronograma de actividades de *AFGHS.*
9. Participar en las reuniones técnicas con el donante cuando se le solicite.
10. Elaborar el informe mensual de *AFGHS* con base en los reportes de los socios.
11. Responder a emergencias y desastres.
12. Mantener al día los reportes de seguridad solicitados por el donante, en coordinación con el punto focal regional de seguridad.
13. Representar al Proyecto *AFGHS* ante el equipo de Partnership Regional y Global.
14. Coordinar, representar y brindar orientación general entre las ONG locales asociadas y el equipo de gestión del proyecto, asegurando el desarrollo de relaciones eficientes, sólidas y a largo plazo.
15. Orientar el proceso de selección de las ONG locales asociadas y dirigir los procesos de debida diligencia y evaluación de la capacidad de los socios antes de su selección final e incorporación, de acuerdo con las políticas y procedimientos establecidos.
16. Dirigir, recomendar y coordinar la incorporación de socios locales conforme a los procedimientos establecidos por VENGOAL.
17. Planificar, orientar y supervisar la implementación de las evaluaciones de capacidad de los socios, así́ como la estrategia y los planes de capacitación para los socios locales, conforme a las herramientas y procesos establecidos y a las instrucciones del Director de Proyecto.
18. Orientar a los socios locales en la creación de redes y en la participación en redes y actores del sector salud.
19. Coordinar y brindar soporte en el monitoreo del desempeño de los socios, el seguimiento del progreso de la implementación de los proyectos ejecutados por los socios y los planes de capacitación para el fortalecimiento de capacidades, de acuerdo con los planes de trabajo y los planes MEAL.
20. Asegurarse de que los socios completen los informes requeridos, tanto narrativos como financieros, de manera oportuna y conforme a los estándares establecidos, incluida la provisión de toda la documentación de verificación financiera requerida.
21. Coordinar estrechamente con el equipo de gestión del proyecto para apoyar la adecuada implementación del programa por parte de los socios locales y el cumplimiento de las políticas, procedimientos, normas y reglamentos establecidos, incluida la gestión de riesgos, la protección y los protocolos y políticas de PSEA.
22. En coordinación con el personal pertinente del proyecto, apoyar a los socios locales en el desarrollo e incorporación de mecanismos de rendición de cuentas y retroalimentación comunitaria, de acuerdo con los estándares establecidos.
23. Detectar e informar a la dirección del proyecto, según corresponda, cualquier uso indebido de los fondos, así́ como los desafíos o problemas de implementación enfrentados por las organizaciones asociadas.
24. Monitorear continuamente las capacidades de los socios e identificar acciones esenciales para su fortalecimiento, en coordinación con el equipo de gestión del proyecto y los asesores técnicos.
25. Orientar el desarrollo de planes de trabajo anuales, la actualización de las actividades del proyecto y otros materiales de comunicación e informes relacionados con los proyectos implementados por los socios locales.
26. En representación de VENGOAL, identificar, relacionarse y establecer vínculos con nuevos socios potenciales.
27. Orientar y brindar soporte en cualquier proceso de investigación, de conformidad con las políticas institucionales, con el fin de prevenir irregularidades y garantizar el cumplimiento de las políticas antifraude y de protección.
28. Otras funciones que le sean asignadas por el Director de Proyecto, en el marco de los objetivos y necesidades del programa.

**PERFIL MÍNIMO REQUERIDO**

***Estudios Profesionales:***

- Licenciatura en Relaciones Internacionales y/o Política Internacional.
- Maestría en Relaciones Internacionales y Seguridad.

***Experiencia Profesional:***

- Mínimo tres (3) años de experiencia en respuesta humanitaria.

***Experiencia específica:***

- Experiencia profesional en coordinación de proyectos
- Gestión de asociaciones (*partnerships*)
- Negociación de acuerdos y soporte ejecutivo en organizaciones humanitarias e internacionales
- Gestión integral de asociaciones, dirección de procesos de debida diligencia y evaluación de capacidad de socios locales e internacionales.
- Negociación, redacción y procesamiento de acuerdos, contratos y subvenciones con socios estratégicos.
- Monitoreo del cumplimiento de proyectos y gestión de documentación en conformidad con los más altos estándares normativos de donantes internacionales (como USAID y OFDA).
- Coordinación y participación en respuestas a emergencias humanitarias (incluyendo logística de despliegue de delegados, manejo de equipos de comunicación y operaciones en terreno).
- Funciones de enlace diplomático e institucional con embajadas, agencias de la ONU y Sociedades Nacionales.
- Elaboración, revisión y traducción (inglés-español) de informes técnicos, reportes narrativos y financieros, así como correspondencia general.
- Organización logística de eventos regionales y gestión de agendas para visitas diplomáticas de alto nivel.

***Conocimientos***

- Conocimiento en manejo de fondos del departamento de estado y cumplimiento.
- Conocimiento de la red pública sanitaria local

***Competencias y Habilidades:***

- Excelente capacidad de negociación y manejo de relaciones con socios clave.
- Enfoque de derechos humanos y manejo confidencial de datos.
- Excelentes capacidades de comunicación oral y escrita.
- Dominio del idioma inglés hablado y escrito
- Comunicación multilingüe e interpretación (español e inglés, idiomas adicionales son un plus).
- Desarrollo de asociaciones estratégicas, diplomacia y compromiso efectivo con las partes interesadas (*stakeholder engagement*).
- Negociación de acuerdos y contratos, investigación rigurosa, análisis de políticas y análisis de datos.
- Logística de eventos regionales, coordinación de viajes y soporte ejecutivo avanzado.
- Análisis crítico y atención al detalle para la identificación de riesgos, gestión de información confidencial y control de cumplimiento.
- Habilidad para planificar, organizar y priorizar múltiples actividades y proyectos transfronterizos.
- Comunicación efectiva y asertiva con equipos técnicos, administrativos y contrapartes externas.
- Dominio de herramientas digitales y MS Office.

**SALVAGUARDIA**

Los niños, niñas y los adultos en situación de vulnerabilidad deben estar protegidos en la mayor medida posible de acciones deliberadas o inadvertidas y fallas que los ponen en riesgo de abuso, explotación sexual, lesiones y cualquier otro daño. Una de las formas en que VENGOAL muestra este compromiso continuo con la protección es incluir rigurosos antecedentes y verificaciones de referencia en el proceso de selección para todos los candidatos.

**RESPONSABILIDAD DENTRO DE VENGOAL**

VENGOAL es un empleador que ofrece igualdad de oportunidades y tiene un conjunto de políticas de integridad. Se espera que cualquier candidato que ofrezca un trabajo con VENGOAL se adhiera a las siguientes áreas clave de responsabilidad:

- Cumplir con las políticas y procedimientos de VENGOAL con respecto a la protección, el Código de Conducta, la salud y la seguridad, la protección de datos y la confidencialidad, los principios de no dañar y los protocolos de comportamiento inaceptables.
- Informar cualquier inquietud sobre el bienestar de un niño o adulto en situación de vulnerabilidad, o cualquier irregularidad dentro de nuestra área de programación.
- Informar cualquier inquietud sobre el comportamiento inapropiado de un personal o socio de VENGOAL.

jobs.title: MEAL Team Leader - Data & Digitalisation
jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **MEAL Team Leader - Data & Digitalisation**, you will lead the monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning of programme results across all levels, ensuring reliable data and performance information support accountability, informed decision-making and continued Global Fund programme performance. You will strengthen MEAL systems, data management and evaluations, support World Vision International CAR and Sub-Recipients in improving programme quality and promote a learning culture through evidence-based insights shared with the Global Fund, Ministry of Health disease programmes and other stakeholders.

**KEY JOB RESPONSIBILITIES**

**(a) Establish and Operationalize a Robust Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning System**

You will develop and manage costed M&E work plans, establish indicator measurement and data collection systems, and strengthen data management and reporting across disease programmes. You will lead the rollout of CommCare, promote data sharing and interoperability, establish accountability and feedback mechanisms, and coordinate learning activities with the Ministry of Health, partners and Sub-Recipients.

**(b) Data Quality Assurance**

You will develop and implement data quality protocols and mechanisms to ensure accurate, complete and timely data collection, reporting, analysis and storage. You will conduct routine data quality assessments, address reporting gaps and integrity risks, and strengthen data security, confidentiality and access controls.

**(c) Capacity Building**

You will assess the MEAL capacity of grant staff, Sub-Recipients and implementing partners, develop and deliver training plans, and provide coaching, mentoring and supervision to strengthen monitoring systems and address implementation challenges.

**(d) Program Review, Evaluation, and Surveys**

You will oversee programme performance, cost-effectiveness and impact through reviews, evaluations and surveys. You will coordinate national HIV, TB and malaria studies, consolidate population estimates, lead analysis of disaggregated data, and support resource mapping and intervention planning while ensuring ethical data collection and protection.

**(e) Reporting**

You will lead the preparation, review and submission of accurate and timely Global Fund reports across Malaria, HIV, TB and RSSH components. You will strengthen reporting capacity among staff and partners, prepare MMRs for the Chief of Party, integrate World Vision and Ministry of Health data systems, and monitor Sub-Recipient performance, reporting timeliness, data quality and corrective actions.

**Requirements include:**

- Must have 5 -7 years of progressive relevant experience in monitoring and evaluation in the public health sector, epidemiological literacy, and surveillance.
- 5 years of progressive relevant experience in program management.
- Experience developing monitoring and evaluation frameworks for public health programs (designing questionnaires, conducting surveys/research).
- University degree in Public Health, Epidemiology, Monitoring and Evaluation, Statistics, International Development and Rural Development
- Certification in monitoring and evaluation will be an added advantage
- Demonstrated experience with Global Fund performance frameworks, reporting requirements, data quality and grant performance monitoring, plus
- Practical experience with DHIS2 and/or comparable digital health/MEAL platforms, with CommCare experience desirable. Accountability: Ensure partners and communities can safely provide feedback and complaints, and that these are properly recorded, addressed, followed up, and used to improve program quality.
- Learning: experience with documenting lessons and best practices and facilitating learning reviews, translating findings into program adaptations, and tracking implementation of agreed actions.
- Experience working in developing countries and maintaining good relations with government and international organizations.
- Proficiency in both FRENCH and ENGLISH is required

**Travel, Language and/or Work Environment Requirement**

- French proficiency is required due to the context
- Work environment: Office-based with frequent travel to the field
- Travel: 30% Domestic/international travel is required.
- On call: As required

**Applicant Types Accepted:** Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted

jobs.title: Oficial de Ayuda Legal - Caracas (Personal Nacional)
jobs.description:
Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, en el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto, DRC está buscando un/a **Oficial de Ayuda Legal** altamente calificado/a con sede en Caracas, Venezuela.

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC administra sus operaciones en Venezuela bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela implementa actividades de monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para personas con necesidades específicas (PWSN), sesiones informativas para personas de interés (PoC), prevención de la trata de personas y seguridad alimentaria.

En el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto ocurrido en el mes de junio 2026, DRC está abriendo una nueva oficina de implementación en Caracas, independiente de la oficina de país, para atender las necesidades de las poblaciones afectadas. Para ello, busca incorporar un/a Oficial de Recuperación Económica – Medios de Vida será responsable de implementar de manera efectiva y oportuna las actividades de los programas de Recuperación Económica de DRC en Venezuela.

**Objetivo general del puesto**

El objetivo principal del Oficial de Ayuda Legal es implementar las actividades legales en el marco del programa de Protección de DRC. Bajo la supervisión del Gerente de Protección implementará las actividades de ayuda legal y es responsable de brindar asesoría legal y gestión de casos para restablecer los derechos de las personas de interés en materia civil, administrativa y constitucional. Es también responsable de la implementación de sesiones informativas sobre temas legales en estrecha colaboración con el equipo de protección.

**Principales Responsabilidades**

- Este rol tiene un enfoque de área y garantiza el cumplimiento de los objetivos de asistencia/asesoría legal bajo los procedimientos y las pautas de DRC dentro del área. El rol contribuye al desempeño de los planes de acción y proporciona apoyo y orientación técnica para operaciones legales en el terreno.
- Trabajar en estrecha cooperación con el equipo de protección de DRC y responder a las necesidades legales documentadas;
- Implementar las actividades de asesoría y servicios legales conforme a los objetivos meta de los proyectos;
- Elaborar documentos de asesoría y servicios legales, determinando la mejor estrategia para los casos de beneficiarios bajo la supervisión del Gerente de Protección.
- Implementar asesoría y servicios legales en las zonas de intervención seleccionadas por el programa según el plan mensual establecido;
- Planear y proporcionar citas individuales para el asesoramiento jurídico a las personas de interés, según sea necesario.
- Recopilar información de los beneficiarios gestionando archivos de manera confidencial y completa; trasferir diariamente las informaciones relevantes en la base de datos legales para permitir el seguimiento de los casos legales identificados o remitidos.
- Proporcionar asesoramiento individual en temas de protección incluyendo protección internacional, reunificación familiar, registro civil y nacionalidad, afiliación en el sistema de seguridad social, acceso a salud, educación y vivienda y otros casos de derecho civil y administrativo que requieran asistencia jurídica.
- Acompañar a los beneficiarios a instituciones públicas según sea necesario.
- Apoyar a la Gerencia de Protección en la elaboración de estrategias y procedimientos estándares para facilitar la implementación de las actividades legales.
- Mantener buenas relaciones con las entidades e instituciones públicas pertinentes para que la coordinación y la articulación sea fortalecida.
- Proporcionar información para informes semanales según sea requerido.
- Participar activamente a las reuniones de equipo proporcionando insumos, desafíos y lecciones aprendidas.

**Programación y Operaciones**

- Asegurar la implementación eficiente y efectiva de las actividades legales en terreno.
- Abordar las necesidades de asesoría y servicios legales de las personas de interés.

**Experiencia y competencias:**

- Mínimo 2 años de experiencia relevante como abogado/a
- Pregrado en Derecho, con experiencia en derecho constitucional/derecho de los refugiados/derechos humanos.
- Experiencia demostrable en definición de estrategia legal y seguimiento de casos.
- Optimas habilidades de escritura informes.
- Optimas habilidades para trabajar con tabletas y computadores.
- Optimas habilidades en MS Word y Excel.
- Voluntad y habilidad de aprender.
- Experiencia con los procedimientos y directrices estándar.
- Alta ética profesional.

**Educación:**

Pregrado en Derecho, con experiencia en derecho constitucional/derecho de los refugiados/derechos humanos. Experiencia demostrable en definición de estrategia legal, seguimiento de casos y litigio.

**Idioma:**

- Ingles (A2 Deseable)
- Español

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: 3 meses con disponibilidad de extensión según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda H.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.
- Contratación nacional.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC.

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Domingo 06 de noviembre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

**Fecha de inicio:** Diciembre 2026

jobs.title: Global Fund Contract and Supply Chain Manager
jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Global Fund Contract and Supply Chain Manager**, you will provide technical leadership and management of the Global Fund Supply Chain Team, covering procurement, logistics, warehousing and asset management. You will ensure effective systems, policies, procedures, controls and staff capabilities to deliver timely, professional and cost-effective services while achieving value for money across supply chain activities.

**KEY JOB RESPONSIBILITIES**

**(a) Leadership and Management**

You will lead the Global Fund Supply Chain function, coordinate technical support from regional and global teams, manage relevant agreements and contracts, and develop procurement policies and standards. You will strengthen coordination with other business units and external stakeholders, oversee annual business and procurement plans, and ensure supply chain input is included in project design and strategic planning.

**(b) Procurement Management, Process, Procedure and Policy**

You will oversee procurement planning, supplier prequalification and screening, supplier performance and strategic sourcing. You will lead contract and supplier negotiations, develop sourcing strategies, support budgeting, and ensure procurement processes comply with WVI and donor requirements. You will also review and improve procurement policies, systems and guidelines, and advise National Offices on logistics providers and INCOTERMS.

**(c) Contract Management**

You will review and finalise standard and supplier contracts, ensure performance indicators are included in strategically sourced contracts, resolve contractual issues, and establish effective supplier onboarding and relationship management processes.

**(d) Managing Provision Processes and Metrics**

You will oversee procurement requests and team assignments, maintain supply chain documentation and reporting, and monitor procurement performance through metrics and KPI dashboards. You will address process gaps, support user training, collaborate with Shared Services and Provision teams, ensure transformation and optimisation targets are met, and supervise the Global Fund Procurement Team.

**(e) Risk and Audit Management**

You will identify and assess supply chain risks, develop mitigation plans and strengthen internal controls and policy compliance. You will investigate reported breaches, fraud and misuse of funds or assets, address audit findings, prepare for audits and monitor the implementation of recommendations. You will also strengthen partner and sub-grantee controls and implement anti-corruption and fraud prevention strategies.

**(f) Reporting**

You will prepare and submit monthly, semi-annual and annual supply chain reports, including procurement, logistics, asset and warehouse reports. You will monitor action plans for identified challenges, submit procurement plans on time, and maintain accurate asset registers and disposal records.

**(g) People Management, Training and Capacity Building**

You will lead the Supply Chain Department, align its work with the Our Promise strategy, and manage staff performance through regular feedback, coaching and development. You will train staff, sub-recipients and partners on Global Fund and WVI procurement policies and systems, and develop and monitor partner capacity assessment and improvement plans.

**(h) Learning and Innovation**

You will identify opportunities to improve business processes and achieve value for money, and lead the implementation and rollout of new initiatives.

**Requirements include:**

- University Degree in Supply Chain Management, Procurement, Engineering, or Business Administration, or equivalent professional qualification (advanced CIPS).
- Minimum of 7 years’ experience in contract management, Supply Chain Management, or Logistics and Procurement
- MUST have at least 5 years of relevant experience with the Global Fund.
- At least 5 years of experience in managing staff
- Experience managing statutory and donor audits
- Substantive experience working in the INGO sector dealing with multiple donor funds and meeting different donor requirements
- Proven experience in supervising staff with different expertise
- Demonstrated high proficiency levels of electronic systems related to procurement management, administration, security systems, as well as fleet and safety management
- Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills
- Ability to present information clearly and concisely in writing or verbally, with excellent written and spoken English
- Ability to negotiate and influence, challenge and question
- Ability to create and maintain procurement, asset management, logistics, and Warehousing.
- Able to prioritize own and others' work to tight work deadlines.
- Proactive with a positive outlook and willingness to embrace change
- Ability to work using own initiative but knowing when to consult.
- Proficiency in both FRENCH and ENGLISH is required

**Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

- The position requires the ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally up to 35% of the time.

*Applicant Types Accepted:* Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted

jobs.title: Driver - Marsabit
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Driver

**Reports to:** Area Manager

**Job Location:** Marsabit

**Contract Details:** Fixed Term

**Salary Range:** Kes 75,024 per month

**Requirements:** Travel within programme areas of Marsabit, and other Concern Offices

**About Concern:** Established in 1968, Concern is a non-profit, non-governmental humanitarian organisation, dedicated to the reduction of suffering and the ultimate elimination of extreme poverty in the world’s poorest countries.

Concern’s vision, our mission and our work are all defined by one goal – ending extreme poverty, whatever it takes. Concern strives for a world free from poverty, fear and oppression.

Our culture is values driven and we believe that our people are central to all that we do and are key to delivering on our goal of Reaching the Furthest Behind First. We are committed to ensuring a workplace where everybody feels valued and are enabled to succeed in their work and contribute to delivering on our mission.

**Job Purpose:**

The incumbent will drive Concern vehicles as directed by the Officer Logistics, Procurement & Transport and in compliance with Concern’s transport policy and procedures and the Kenyan Law while making sure that all the passengers and goods are safe and secure during the journey. S/he is also responsible for accident and incident reporting, reporting repair, maintenance and service needs and all vehicle documentation required.

**Responsibilities:**

- Adhere to the country Traffic ACT, rules and regulations, Concern’s Transport and Fleet Management Manual, standard operating procedures and best practices
- Conduct daily pre-driving checks (fuel, lubricants, water, tool kit, two spare wheels, jack, winch, wheel spanner, fire extinguisher, life savers, valid insurance and driving license, communication equipment/satellite phone, sanitiser etc.) to ensure that all vehicle legal and safety requirements are present in the vehicle, and functioning, before embarking on any journey
- Operate all functions of the vehicle in a way to maximize its operating lifespan and to the highest safety & security standards
- Make daily recommendations regarding vehicles functionality in relation to health and safety of passengers and goods including reporting all technical faults by filling the daily and weekly vehicle check lists
- Immediately report to the Line Manager, Head of Field Office and Security Focal Point any incidents and accidents and submit the completed incident and accident reporting form to the Line Manager within 24hours
- Effective record keeping including completing log sheets, job cards, daily and weekly vehicle check lists and battery and tyre records promptly and accurately as per Concern’s transport policy and procedures
- Load and offload items into and from vehicles
- When transporting goods, ensure safe delivery and submit delivery notes and/or reports and to confirm the status and quantity of goods with the recipient and the sender
- Ensure that s/he carries only authorised passengers or goods
- Ensure that all safety belts are in good working condition and that all passengers including him/her fasten their seat belts before embarking on the journey
- Ensure the vehicle is clean at all times
- Liaise as necessary with the Line Manager, Head of Field Office and Security Focal Point for security updates and take necessary security measures to minimise exposure to threats.
- The driver must put the safety of passengers and him/herself first at all times.

**Role Holder Essential Requirements:**

- Minimum O level certificate
- Valid driving license class BCE. Motor bike riding license is an added advantage
- Minimum five (5) years’ driving experience working in operations in remote locations preferably with an NGO. Three (3) years accident-free experience
- Good spoken language in English and Kiswahili. Ability to speak one or more of the local languages an added advantage
- Relevant basic qualifications or related extensive experience in mechanical fault diagnosis and repairs preferably in Land Cruisers
- Practical driving skills and knowledge of 4x4 driving
- A certificate of good conduct
- Excellent physical and health condition
- Must be familiar with the geographical location of the programme areas/Excellent road knowledge
- Commitment to adhere to the standards of conduct outlined in the Code of Conduct and Associated Policies

**Preference will be given to candidates who have:**

- High integrity and demonstrated ability to follow standards and policies
- Commitment to humanitarian principles and values
- A proven history of accountability and integrity
- Ability to join immediately

**Important information:**

Concern has an organisational **Code of Conduct** supported by three Associated Policies: The **Programme Participant Protection Policy, the Child Safeguarding Policy, and the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Policy** accessible [here](https://www.concern.net/accountability/codes-and-policies/safeguarding). These have been designed to ensure the highest level of protection for everyone the organization engages through its work.

The policies set out the behaviours and responsibilities that Concern staff, and all its representatives (including consultants, contractors, sub-contractors, suppliers, partners, visitors, ambassadors and Board members) are expected to uphold. They also articulate Concern’s commitment to safeguarding and protecting adults and children from harm in all aspects of our work. We will therefore do everything possible to ensure that only those who are suitable to work or volunteer with adults and children are recruited by us for such roles. Consequently, working or volunteering with Concern may be subject to a range of vetting checks, including criminal background checking.

In this context, all staff and representatives of Concern have a responsibility to uphold the highest standards in their work, in accordance with Concern’s core values and mission. Any candidate offered a job with Concern Worldwide will be expected to sign the Concern Staff Code of Conduct and Associated Policies as an appendix to their contract of employment. By signing the Concern Code of Conduct, candidates acknowledge that they have understood the content of both the Concern Code of Conduct and the Associated Policies and agree to conduct themselves in accordance with the provisions of these policies.

jobs.title: SAFETY & SECURITY OFFICER _ BORNO STATE
jobs.description:
**JOB PURPOSE**

Under the supervision of the Security Manager **Support the risk management, in all locations**. Ensure an adequate level of situational awareness to support and perform risk **analysis** of the local security situation. Analyze main security threat at field level and provide advice. Ensure that Safety and Security equipment are available and ensure support in establishment of risk treatment measure and access issues are followed up.

Support in ensuring that structures and systems for safety and security management are in place and respected.

.

**RESPONSIBILITIES/ TASKS**

- In close cooperation with the Field Coordinator, conduct security risk assessments in new areas/routes, and advise them on security measures to be implemented.
- Establish and maintain an active information network with other NGOs, UN, formal and informal community leaders, and national and international security actors operating in the area to obtain credible and relevant safety information.
- Coordinate and liaise with police, security forces and relevant authorities to effectively communicate INTERSOS operations and modus operandi in order to build reliable levels of acceptance and enhance accessibility to the areas of operations.
- Support the Field Coordinator in the establishment of security plans and procedures in the areas of operations, providing inputs on existing documents, updating information on tools and identifying procedures to revise and suggest new ones. Support Field Coordinator and the Security manager in decision making and coordination with other third parties when needed.
- Support the sharing of information about the security tools in place and different measures in coordination with the Field Coordinator. In coordination with the Field Coordinator Conduct induction sessions to field staffs whenever necessary.
- Provide Safety, Security and Risk Management training when needed. If not possible in person identify possible providers or remote-on-line solution.
- Report to the line manager the progress of on-going procedures and alert in case of change of legislation in government procedures if impacting on the safety and security of the operations.
- Identify the applied safety and security need and coordinate with logistic for their establishment.
- Daily check on security and safety road conditions and inform the Field Coordinator. If needed also the Security Coordinator.
- Track the staff’s movements
- Regularly collect data on security incidents. Provide assistance in the management and follow up of incidents affecting INTERSOS project staffs and offices, sharing reliable reporting with the line manager
- Conduct basic training to drivers, guards and staffs on topics identified by the line manager (alert system, tracking, access control, etc.)
- Guarantee the proper set up of safety equipment and measures in place in vehicles and premises. Contribute to the proper set up and monitoring of the safe rooms
- Represent INTERSOS at security meetings or fora, and in meetings with communities and government and non-government stakeholders and administrative and security services to obtain documents and relevant information and to negotiate access to the field, and prepare regular reports
- Perform other security-related tasks assigned by the Security Manager

Education

- University Degree in relevant field (Social Sciences, Psychology, Social Work, Human Rights, International Humanitarian Law or other fields related to social development and humanitarian work)
- Master’s degree in human Rights, International Humanitarian Law or other fields related desirable
- .

## Experience

Professional experience

- Minimum 3 years of working experience as Security Officer in a humanitarian/recovery context or relevant working experience in safety, security and risk analysis

Professional requirements

- Good understanding of humanitarian safety practices, procedures and principles and their application
- Experience, based on evidence, of humanitarian negotiation (with national authorities, local authorities, non-state actors, military forces) and humanitarian access in complex emergencies
- Experience in reporting and emergency response planning

Personal requirements

- Moral integrity
- Teamwork and communication skills
- Networking skills
.

**Languages**

- Proficiency in English (written and spoken)
- Knowledge and fluency in English and local languages (Hausa and Kanuri) will be an asset.

jobs.title: Deputy Programme Manager
jobs.description:
**JOB PURPOSE**

The Deputy Programme Manager ensures constant engagement by/with different support departments and technical sectors to ensure timely support to the project team.

The Deputy Programme Manager, supports the Programme Manager to and supervises/monitor closely the staff planning, procurement planning, financial planning, liquidity planning and budget utilization/burn rate monitoring for the supported projects.

The Deputy Programme Manager works closely with the technical sector lead to monitor implementation, complete progress reports, ensuring that they align with the project log frame and work plan and project activity tracking tools.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Ensures the planning, implementation and monitoring/evaluation and sets targets as included in the project description. Flag significant deviation from the program implementation plan and estimated expenditures; alert relevant staff.
- Guarantee an efficient financial management as main budget holder for the project in compliance with INTERSOS’ model and donor regulations.
- Team/HR management (staff and volunteers)
- Deliver quality project activities reporting, including the findings in terms of impact/changes at the level of beneficiaries achieved through the project, compliant and consistent reporting per INTERSOS and donor requirements, in collaboration with the HQ Grants Unit
- Develop clear understanding of INTERSOS program and country strategy among project team – ensure also timely input/feedback by team on strategic issues.
- Support the Program Coordinator in program/project development.
- Ensure that program delivery matches INTERSOS and donor technical minimum standards and seek technical section and MEAL department guidance and tools.
- Ensure clear overview of actors and services in area of intervention, permitting development and implementation of partnerships and referral pathways.
- Administrative and office support activities (agreement, amendments, signed reports, communications, etc.), ensuring documentation cycle is up to date, and ensure all departments’ requirements are aligned and addressed.
- **Detailed responsibilities and tasks:**
- Ensure the full and timely implementation of the project proposal as approved, pro-actively respecting deadlines for reporting:
- Project kick-off and presentation/sharing of project with teams
- Review and prepare a detailed activity plan with team
- Verification on the targeting of beneficiaries
- **Financial management and procurement:**
- Prepare, monitor and implement financial and procurement plan
- Prepare financial plan
- Approval of all purchases/contracting and budget line allocations
- Verify the bookkeeping entries in the INTERSOS accounting spread sheets (JOURNAL): verify budget line allocations, budget expenditure status against actual delivery and the financial plan for the remainder project implementation period
- Ensure for all purchases/contracting of goods/services/supplies the correct INTERSOS procurement guidelines are applied and properly documented, in coordination with the Finance and Logistics departments.
- Verify the list of expenditures prior to finalizing the interim and final financial reports
- Holds final responsibility for verification of all support documents’ completeness and correctness.
- **People management:**
- Agree and establish clear reporting and communication lines
- Team recruitment, liaise with HR Department to secure up to date HR files.
- Permanent on-job coaching of teams to work on quality in delivery.
- Manages and evaluates the performance of the project staff.
- Conduct weekly and monthly meetings with the team to review the planning and discuss the main concerns to focus on for the upcoming period.
- Continuous/fast verification of data quality collected and received from field staff.
- Ensure teams respect INTERSOS rules and guidelines to the mission and adhere to INTERSOS Code of Conduct and Charter of Values.
- **Monitoring & evaluation:**
- Ensure monitoring and verification for the targeting of beneficiaries.
- Applying a result-based management approach, monitor the project outcomes, in addition to the outputs and activities, including changes at the household and community level achieved through the project.
- Undertake (if security situation allows) field visits to provide technical guidance and supervision to the team and to monitor the progress and quality of the different project activities.
- **Reporting:**
- Ensure quality reporting on achievements through daily short briefings, monthly and weekly planning presented against weekly and monthly performance reports containing clear quantitative and qualitative information related to the activities.
- Secure regular reporting per team and compile, review and analyses reports on monthly bases to be reflected in INTERSOS Project Appraisal Tool.
- Prepare ad hoc progress reporting for the donor and official required interim and final project reports; prepare interim and final narrative reports for the donor in a timely and qualitative manner, looking into achievements against outcomes and output and reflect lessons learnt clearly into recommendations for future programming.
- Holds final responsibility for all support documents (means of verification) and general project documents.
- Delivers regular communication products (including pictures) on the project to be used by the INTERSOS communication department in different outlet.
- **Coordination and representation:**
- Support the Program Coordinator / Technical Coordinators in attending cluster meetings and ensure timely reporting of highlights and relevant information for intervention area.
- Participate in regular meetings with the donor representatives and facilitates field visits by donor missions (when security allows for), in coordination with the Program Coordinator.
- Ensure systematic information and update sharing with the program coordinator
- Perform any other related duties as required

**Education & Professional Requirements:**

**Education**

- **Essential:** Advanced university degree in Social Sciences, Political Sciences, International Relations, Humanitarian and International Cooperation or related field.
- **Desirable:** a master’s degree in one of these fields.

## Professional experience

- Minimum 3 years of professional experience in management of humanitarian project/program, including financial management and logistics responsibilities.
- Minimum 1 year experience in the implementation of multi-sector humanitarian programming and in security context analysis.
- Experience in complex emergency setting and insecure countries
- Administration, finance and budget management skills
- Essential computer literacy (word, excel and internet)
- Analytical thinking, analysis capacity and strategic program development skills
- Experience working with State and LGA government counterparts and traditional institutions in North-East Nigeria.

## Personal requirements

- Experience in establishing and maintaining collaborative relationships with donors and government counterparts, and with donors compliance and reporting
- Strong representation and negotiation skills
- Ability to ensure quick quality delivery in stressful environment
- Ability to adhere to deadlines and respect line management
- Strong interpersonal skills: communication, diplomatic skills and problem-solver
- Leadership, people management and development
- Organization and problem solving Commitment to INTERSOS principles

## Languages

- **Essential:** Fluent in written and spoken English; good spoken Hausa.
- Knowledge and fluency in local languages (Hausa and Kanuri) will be an asset.

jobs.title: Country Director - Yemen
jobs.description:
**Place:** Sana’a with regular travel to Aden, Mokha, Hajjah & Hodeidah - Yemen
**Starting date:** 1st of March 2027 (1 month VISA process)
**Duration of contract:** 18-24 months

Humanity & Inclusion is an independent and impartial aid organisation working in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. The organisation works alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations, taking action and bearing witness in order to respond to their essential needs, improve their living conditions and promote respect for their dignity and fundamental rights.

Since its creation in 1982, HI has run development & humanitarian projects in more than 55 countries and responded to numerous emergencies. Today, we have a budget of approximately 200 million euros, with 4,000 employees worldwide

At Handicap International-Humanity & Inclusion, we truly believe in the importance of inclusion and diversity within our organisation. This is why we are engaged to a disability policy to encourage the inclusion and integration of people with disabilities.

Please indicate if you require any special accommodation, even at the first interview. For more information about the organisation:

**JOB CONTEXT:**

Yemen has been for long the poorest country in the Arab world.

In January 2015, the Houthis overthrew the President Hadi government. Since the end of March of the same year, an international coalition of countries led by Saudi Arabia allied with the President temporarily exiled in Saudi Arabia, launched a military campaign against the advances of the Houthis in the country. At the end of 2017 the alliance between the GPC of the former president Saleh and the Houthis broke out in Sana’a and Saleh was killed. In January 2018 the alliance in the south as well broke out: the Southern Transitional Council, in favor of an independent state in the south took over Aden from the hands of Hadis’ supporters, Hadi being still in exile in Saudi-Arabia.

Following the UN brokered truce between the Houthis and the Government of Yemen in 2022, there has been an informal truce (calm period) since then, and a new escalation started in July 2026. Houthis has gained new territorial controls mainly in the West Coast of the country with the fighting still ongoing. Following the new escalation, there is an increasing concern about the security situation in Aden where most of the organizations including UN agencies have their country offices.

As a result of such violence and instability, it is more than 22 million of Yemenis out of 30 million in need of any kind of aid. Malnutrition, cholera, diphtheria hit most of the families and a failed health system, with no salaries paid for several years, cannot cope.

UN agencies and several international organizations have closed their operation in North Yemen (areas under Houthis control) in 2025, while over 70% of people in need are in the North and few organizations have remained operating under Houthis control. The Humanitarian situation in the North is worsening and there is growing concern about the humanitarian situation in 2027 following the ongoing escalation. The international organizations working in the North have formed a coordination platform (Joint Humanitarian Partnership-JHP), and they collectively engage the donors, UN leadership and the local authorities. HI is a member of the JHP group.

**Base:** Sana’a, Yemen.

Under the responsibility of the Geographic Director Middle East, the Yemen Country Director is responsible for implementing the Operational Strategy (2026-27 strategy currently being designed), in line with the HI Global Strategy. He/she ensures optimal quality and impact of the activities in the Program, through a delegation system with appropriate control mechanisms. He/she shares with all HI managers the responsibility of sound management and successful functioning of the global organization, through paradigm changes.

**YOUR MISSION:**

The Country Director is the **legal representative** in the country of the overall HI organization internally and externally and promotes a high reputation and positive image of HI.

He/she **deploys HI’s full mandate** and 2026-27 Strategy in his/her geographical area, with operational partners, institutions and/or donors, and steers **organizational transformation** in line with HI global standards. In case of emergency, he/she takes responsibilities in accordance with the response framework defined.

He/sheensures **compliance** with his/her budget framework (including unrestricted funds) and HI policies and frameworks (safeguarding, commitment thresholds, security, human resources, risk management, etc.)

He/sheactively **monitors and analyses context developments** in his/her geographical area, in order to identify risks and opportunities.

**Responsibility 1: Management**

- Set up team spirit and a functioning team, guaranteeing synergies and exchanges of good practices between the different actors in the Program and with head office colleagues.
- Based on the Human resources strategy of the Program (in the StratOp), size and plan annually human resources needs of the Program.
- Recruit and contribute to the professional development, autonomy and well-being at work of his/her direct managers: in link with the corresponding professional channels, set formalized individual objectives, ensure coherence between HI’s needs and competencies and motivation of his/her teams, develop and monitor competence development plan, evaluate individual performance, contribute to career evolution.
- Acknowledge individual and collective efforts and performance.
- Embody and transmit HI values, ensure compliance with code of conduct and institutional policies, ensure the expected mind set and individual and collective behaviors, and disciplinary measures when necessary.
- Conduct a Program Steering Committee with his/her direct managers: Operations Manager, Area Managers, Technical Unit Manager & Shared (support) Services managers.
- Steer organization transformation, in particular through managerial and work practice change and continuous improvement of working processes.

**Responsibility 2: Deployment of HI Strategy and HI frameworks and regulations in the program**

- Conduct the development of the Program’s Operational Strategy (StratOp), and its implementation and annual monitoring, taking into account context and external constraints, HI’s mandate and global strategy, the Technical Strategies and the Development plans of Emergency, Atlas and Impact-Innovation-Information Divisions.
- The Operational Strategy includes a fundraising strategy aligned with HI’s ethical principles and the Institutional Funding Development Plan.
- Develop regular contact with donors at field level and liaise regularly with Institutional Funding Division.
- Ensure the best allocation of resources to match Program’s ambitions, and plan accordingly (including support missions).
- Ensure the deployment of and compliance with HI global frameworks, institutional policies and standards.
- Ensure financial control and monitoring of operations are effective in the Program
- Ensure technical quality standards are applied in the projects of the Program, and monitor the implementation of evaluations and donor audit recommendations.
- Facilitate internal audits (operational, financial and organizational) and ensure the implementation of their recommendations.
- Be responsible for security management: in link with the Security advisor, develop a culture of safety & security at Program level; ensure that security documents are up-to-date and that all necessary measures are put in place; ensure incident management and reporting according to HI frameworks.
- With both potential opportunities and risks in mind, ensure continuous monitoring and analysis of current developments in his/her geographical context

**Responsibility 3: Legal representative**

- Employer’s representative responsibilities and compliance with local working regulations.
- Communications on behalf of HI.
- Representation of HI vis-à-vis local, national, traditional, political, military and diplomatic authorities and bodies.
- Representation of HI vis-à-vis international organizations and coordination mechanisms & system.
- Negotiation and signature of operational partnerships, and monitoring of operational partnerships signed in affiliated countries.

**Responsibility 4: Influence and leadership**

- Take on the messages of HI global advocacy to all relevant external parties.
- Develop a specific local advocacy activity in accordance with the Operational Strategy of the Program.
- Develop communication and information activities, in accordance with the Operational Strategy
- Contribute to the conception, promotion and evolution of HI strategy and policies.

**CHARACTERISTICS OF THE POSITION:**

The position is based in Sanaa – Yemen with regular travel to Aden for representation with local authorities.

The expatriate is expected to travel between HI bases (Aden, Mokha and Hajjah, Hodeidah) and all the project sites. In the four locations, shared guesthouses well equipped with a safe-room, most of the work is done at the office but there are some possibilities to go out for work purposes. Outside movements are possible for some extra-professional activities in Sanaa and Aden. All movements are done by car. HI has set up a curfew. Regional conflict escalation has a direct impact on Yemen. The Conflicts between the Houthis and the Internationally recognized government of Yemen has escalated in 2026, with increased fighting in the coastal region, Bab El Mandeb and other frontlines. The Yemen conflicts have resulted over 300,000 people internally displacement as of October 2026, and the number is likely to increase in the coming period. The Government of Yemen allied forces have carried out air strikes in the Houthis strong holds, frontline areas. Yemen situation has been fragile even before the current escalation, with Houthis engaged in strikes on shipping in the Red Sea and on Israel territory in 2025, they have faced air-strikes from Israel and the US. Infrastructures (Al Hudaydah port and power plants) have been targeted. This leads to major supply disruptions and exacerbates acute humanitarian risks. The situation in the South of Yemen is increasingly becoming high risks following the Houthis attacks in several areas including Aden. The mission has put in place adequate security rules and processes to allow teams to work in a safe environment.

Local medical capacity remains a concern for the person with fragile health, ongoing treatment and that needs close medical follow up. Dress code: Men will be required to wear long pants and at least a short-sleeved shirt. Women are required to wear the abaya and hijab (headscarf) outside of the compound. For female staff in the office, appropriate attire includes long pants and long sleeve shirts.

## **Requirements**

- You have proven experience as Country Director in complicated contexts
- You share HI’s vision, mandate, values and strategy
- You have proven experience in implementing emergency, development and armed violence reduction actions.
- You understand the geopolitical issues linked to Yemen and have experience in risk management

- You have leadership, you are responsible and you can take decisions (including taking risks)
- You know how to simplify and prioritize
- You have proven experience in managing multi-cultural and multi-sector teams
- You are fluent in English

## **Benefits**

At HI, the conditions offered are up to your commitment and adapted to the context of your mission.

18-24 months International contract starting from 1st , March 2027;

The international contract provides social cover adapted to your situation:

- Unemployment insurance benefits for EU nationals;
- Pension scheme;
- Medical coverage with 50% of employee contribution;
- Repatriation insurance paid by HI;

Salary from 3232€ gross/month upon experience;

Perdiem: 619€ net/month - paid in the field

Hardship: 500 € net/month paid with your salary;

Paid leaves: 25 days per year;

R&R: according to the level of the mission 5 days every 8 weeks

Position:

Unaccompanied:

- Payment for travel costs (air ticket & visa) and transport of your personal effects;
- a child allowance of 100€ per month, per child (from the second child) paid in the field;

Housing: Collective taken in charge by HI

jobs.title: Logistics Coordinator - UKRAINE (H/F/X)
jobs.description:
**Working environment:**

The humanitarian situation in Ukraine remains critical amid ongoing international conflict. Since the escalation of the armed conflict on 24 February 2022, the destruction of vital civilian infrastructure continues to rise, leading to the destruction of homes across the country and cutting off access to critical services for millions of people. In 2025 in Ukraine, the UN estimates approximately 12.7 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance. Ukrainian refugee numbers abroad stand at about 6,9 million, while 3,7 million people are internally displaced (IDPs) within Ukraine.

Generally, the severe damage to critical infrastructure such as hospitals, schools, and water treatment plants has compromised access to clean water, sanitation, and essential healthcare services. Constant and long-lasting disruptions to the power grid have plunged entire regions into darkness, hindering communication and hampering daily life.

With the humanitarian situation in Ukraine being a challenge and may deteriorate further, the International Red Cross & Red Crescent Movement has mobilised all its emergency response mechanisms. Together, ICRC, IFRC, Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) and National Societies are undertaking a coordinated response. As the conflict entered into protracted mode, Movement partners are pursuing their collaboration to answer the evolving needs, all over the country.

**General mission of the DMI:**

The purpose of the position is to ensure logistical technical assistance & coordination of all URCS projects supported by the French Red Cross; and to support, coach & guide the Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) in specific logistics capacity strengthening areas agreed with the URCS and as per the HNS strategic plans.

**KEY ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

In the context of the continuous support to URCS operations in Ukraine, and under the supervision of the Head of Delegation, the logistics coordinator will be in charge especially of the following activities (non-exhaustive list):

- **Objective# 1:** Logistics Coordination of the FRC delegation and of all FRC supported projects with URCS
- **Objective# 2 :** Manage, supervise and monitor all purchases of supplies, goods, services and works; as per projects and delegation needs
- **Objective# 3 :** Stocks and IT management
- **Objective# 4 :** Partnership relationship, specifically with the URCS Logistic Department and other relevant counterparts.
- **Objective# 5:** day-to-day logistics Capacity Building and Strengthening for the URCS partner
- **Objective# 6:** Security and Safety Monitoring & Management

**HIERARCHICAL AND FUNCTIONAL LINKS**

**Managing lines:**

- Incumbent reporting line: Reporting to Head of Delegation
- Incumbent operational links: HQ Logistic Advisor - purchasing department
- Incumbent will manage: 1 resident staff

**Collaborates internally with:**

- All relevant FRC HQ Support and technical departments.
- FRC program, admin and finance team-members in Ukraine

**Collaborates externally with:**

- URCS Logistics/procurement
- URCS program teams as required.
- Counterparts and colleagues within the RCRC Movement and INSO

**PROFILE**

**Qualifications and experience**

Education :

- Generalist educational background: master in logistics, supply chain management, Logistics training (Bioforce type or bachelor's degree in logistics), or relevant field and experience in a similar position or at least 3 years in a field logistics position

Experiences:

- Minimum 5 years of experience in complex emergency humanitarian context
- Minimum 3 years of experience in team management
- Minimum 3 years experience working in the supply chain management
- Experience in building and strengthening capacities of national/local/civil society organisations
- Experience of working for the RC/RC Movement is an asset

**Skills**

Mandatory job requirements

- driving licence (manual gear)
- Prior experience and knowledge in contracts, purchasing and supply chain management is highly desirable
- High flexibility
- Ability to adapt to different cultures and to listen
- Ability to cope with various pressures
- Good synthesis and analytical skills
- Excellent teamwork skills. At ease and flexible in human relations.
- Rigor, flexibility and adaptability

Valued skills

- Proficiency in the Office pack (Word, Excel, Powerpoint), networking (G-Suite/Google Workspace)
- Proper knowledge of FRC and RCRC Movement would be an asset

Skills related to the specific environment of the mission:

- Ability to work in complex environments including the active conflict context.
- driving licence (manual gear) is mandatory

Languages

- English fluency mandatory (oral and written);
- French and other language of the region would be an asset

**Conditions of employment:**

- Type of status: expatriate
- Type of contract: Fixed-term contract under French law
- Salary: According to the classification of the position on the CRf grid and the experience of the candidate
- Per diem: daily per diem which varies according to the country
- Leave: 10 to 15 days minimum every 6 months - Airfare paid at 100% by CRF for home travel
- Health coverage: CFE + Mutuelle MSH (covered 100%) - covered at 75% by the CRF
- MedEvac/repatriation insurance: YES
- Other insurances: Provident insurance (death and disability)

**SUMMARY**

- Location: Kyiv - UKRAINE
- Duration: 12 months (renewable)
- Starting date : as soon as possible

jobs.title: Logistics Coordinator - LEBANON (H/F/X)
jobs.description:
The **French Red Cross (FRC)** is part of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, providing assistance to people affected by conflicts, disasters and social or health-related crises, in accordance with its seven Fundamental Principles. FRC supports emergency response, health programmes and capacity-building initiatives, primarily in partnership with sister National Societies.

Following the outbreak of the Syrian crisis in 2011, FRC established a permanent presence in Lebanon in 2013 to support the Lebanese Red Cross (LRC) in responding to the needs of Syrian refugees and vulnerable Lebanese communities. Its engagement has progressively evolved towards strengthening LRC's institutional and operational capacities, particularly in Health and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), in line with its national strategy.

Lebanon continues to face a complex humanitarian, economic and security environment, resulting from the prolonged economic and financial crisis, weakened public institutions and recurrent regional instability. The renewed escalation of hostilities in March 2026 triggered large-scale displacement, significant damage to infrastructure and further pressure on essential public services, particularly in southern Lebanon, Nabatieh and the Bekaa. Despite subsequent de-escalation efforts, the security situation remains volatile, while displaced and returning populations continue to face significant challenges in accessing healthcare, housing and basic services. These developments have further strained an already fragile health system and increased the operational demands on humanitarian organisations, particularly the LRC. At the same time, Lebanon remains highly exposed to natural hazards, including earthquakes, floods, wildfires and extreme weather events, whose impacts are compounded by climate change, uncontrolled urbanisation and socio-economic vulnerabilities.

**General mission of the DMI:**

The purpose of the position is to ensure logistical technical assistance & coordination of all LRC and SARC projects supported by the French Red Cross; and to support, coach & guide the FRC logistic department at delegation level as well as LRC and SARC teams when requested by the HNS.

In the context of the continuous support to LRC operations in Lebanon, and under the supervision of the Head of Delegation, the logistics coordinator will be in charge especially of the following activities (non-exhaustive list):

- **Objective# 1:** Ensure the coordination and the supervision of the FRC delegation logistics department and activities
- **Objective# 2 :** Day-to-day logistics/procurement Capacity Building and Strengthening of FRC delegation logistic team
- **Objective# 3 :** Partnership relationship, specifically with the implementing partners
- **Objective# 4:** Security and Safety Monitoring & Management

**HIERARCHICAL AND FUNCTIONAL LINKS**

**Managing lines:**

- **Incumbent operational links:** HQ Logistic Advisor - purchasing department
- **Incumbent will manage:** 3 resident staff (1 in direct management)

**Collaborates internally with:**

- All relevant FRC HQ Support and technical departments.
- FRC program, admin and finance team-members at delegation level

**Collaborates externally with:**

- LRC/SARC (+ PRCS branches in Lebanon and Syria) Logistics/procurement
- LRC/SARC (+ PRCS branches in Lebanon and Syria) program teams as required.
- Counterparts and colleagues within the RCRC Movement and HULO

**Qualifications and experience**

Education :

- Generalist educational background: master in logistics, supply chain management, Logistics training (Bioforce type or bachelor's degree in logistics), or relevant field and experience in a similar position or at least 3 years in a field logistics position

Experiences:

- Minimum 5 years of experience in complex emergency humanitarian context
- Minimum 3 years of experience in team management
- Minimum 3 years experience working in the supply chain management
- Experience in building and strengthening capacities of national/local teams and civil society organisations
- Experience of working for the RC/RC Movement is an asset

**Skills**

Mandatory job requirements

- Prior experience and knowledge in contracts, purchasing and supply chain management is highly desirable
- Prior experience in leading a team and particularly in building and strengthening team capacities and responsibilities
- Excellent teamwork skills. At ease and flexible in human relations.
- Ability to adapt to different cultures and to listen
- High flexibility
- Ability to cope with various pressures
- Good synthesis and analytical skills
- Rigor and adaptability

Valued skills

- Proper knowledge of FRC and RCRC Movement would be an asset

Skills related to the specific environment of the mission:

- Ability to work in complex environments including the active conflict context.

Languages

- English fluency mandatory (oral and written);
- Arabic would be an asset

**Conditions of employment:**

- Type of contract: Fixed-term contract under French law
