jobs.title: Consultant - Operationalising human rights and gender justice in the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD)
Community and membership assistant (M/F)
jobs.description:
**Date de début de contrat :** Février 2027

**Type de contrat** : Contrat à durée déterminée jusqu’au 31/10/2027

**Localisation** : Montreuil (93) / France (télétravail possible en France métropolitaine)

**QUI SOMMES-NOUS ET QUE FAISONS-NOUS…**

La Société Coopérative Européenne d’Intérêt Collectif « Humanitarian Logistics Cooperative », aussi La Société Coopérative Européenne d’Intérêt Collectif « Humanitarian Logistics Cooperative », aussi connue sous l’appellation « hulo », est la première coopérative humanitaire fondée en juin 2021. Dirigée par des organisations humanitaires et intégrant de nouveaux membres régulièrement, hulo a pour objectif d'améliorer l'impact de l'aide humanitaire en renforçant la collaboration et la mise en place de projets communs dans ses pays d’intervention. Chez hulo nous sommes convaincus que le partage et la mise en commun de ressources et d’expertises entre organisations contribue à augmenter la performance de la logistique humanitaire et de la chaine d’approvisionnement

Notre action s’appuie sur une approche collaborative et participative, l’intelligence collective et l’animation d’une communauté de pratiques. Toutes nos activités sont structurées autour d’un objectif commun, impliquant plusieurs parties prenantes autonomes et interdépendantes, qui coopèrent de manière horizontale. Le pilotage y est distribué, fondée sur la concertation, la co-responsabilité et l’engagement volontaire.

Dans nos 7 pays d’intervention répartis dans 3 régions nous mettons en place des initiatives mutualisées dans les domaines des achats, des ressources humaines et de l’environnement. En support aux organisations humanitaires nous coordonnons des initiatives de transport international humanitaire mutualisées à destination des crises humanitaires les plus graves. Enfin nous développons constamment des solutions digitales au service de la communauté humanitaire.

Pour en savoir plus, vous pouvez consultez le rapport annuel 2026 en cliquant sur le lien [https://hulo.coop/january-2026-annual-impact-report/](https://hulo.coop/january-2026-annual-impact-report/)

**DESCRIPTIF DU POSTE**

Le rôle principal du ou de la Community and Membership assistant au sein de la Coopérative hulo est de contribuer à la mise en œuvre opérationnelle du Community Membership Model de hulo et à la qualité de l’expérience des organisations membres.

Sous la supervision de la Community and Membership Manager, il/elle assure le suivi du cycle de vie du membership, facilite la coordination des actions de suivi et accompagne les équipes dans l’application des processus et outils communs.

Il/elle contribue également au déploiement du CRM et à l’accompagnement au changement, puis à son utilisation quotidienne, afin de disposer de données fiables, d’améliorer la continuité du suivi des membres et de faciliter le pilotage de l’engagement.

**MISSIONS PRINCIPALES**

**\#1 : Assurer le suivi opérationnel du membership et du parcours membre**

- Assurer le suivi des différentes étapes du parcours membre
- Vérifier la complétude des informations et documents nécessaires, tenir à jour les statuts et coordonner les relances avec les interlocuteurs concernés.
- Organiser et suivre les étapes d’onboarding
- Tenir à jour le calendrier des adhésions, renouvellements et échéances de contribution.
- Assurer, en coordination avec la Finance, le suivi administratif des contributions et de la facturation

**\#2 : Contribuer au déploiement du CRM et accompagner son adoption**

- Participer aux tests utilisateurs et vérifier que les parcours et fonctionnalités répondent aux besoins opérationnels.
- Centraliser les anomalies, demandes d’ajustement et retours des utilisateurs, et en assurer le suivi avec les interlocuteurs concernés.
- Préparer et actualiser des supports pratiques : guides utilisateurs, tutoriels, FAQ et règles de saisie.
- Après le déploiement, assurer un support fonctionnel de premier niveau et contribuer aux évolutions de l’outil

**\#3 : Contribuer au reporting et à la coordination des activités autour de la communauté**

- Veiller à la complétude, à la cohérence et à l’actualisation des données relatives aux organisations, contacts, adhésions et interactions.
- Préparer les tableaux de bord et extractions nécessaires au suivi du membership et de l’engagement
- Consolider les éléments opérationnels utiles aux rapports internes et aux présentations destinées à la gouvernance.
- Contribuer au suivi de la mise en œuvre du Community Playbook avec les représentants pays
- Contribuer à la préparation et au suivi des réunions avec les référents des organisations membres de la gouvernance

**VOTRE PROFIL**

**Expérience et formation :**

- Formation niveau Bac+5 en coordination de projets, administration publique, gestion des associations, gestion de l'information ou un domaine connexe.
- Une formation supplémentaire en système CRM, gestion des données ou gestion du changement est un atout.
- Au moins 2 ans d’expérience professionnelle en gestion de membres, coordination de réseaux ou de partenaires, soutien opérationnel et administratif aux projets.
- Expérience humanitaire appréciée mais pas obligatoire.

**Compétences techniques :**

- Suivi opérationnel des processus d'adhésion, incluant l'intégration, les renouvellements, la documentation et le suivi des actions
- Utilisation pratique d'un CRM pour tenir des enregistrements, suivre les interactions et les actions
- Capacité à préparer des tableurs, des tableaux de bord et des rapports
- Capacité à contribuer aux tests utilisateurs, documenter les problèmes et assurer le suivi des actions correctives
- Capacité à développer des procédures claires, des guides d'utilisation et des supports de formation
- Capacité à accompagner les utilisateurs dans l'adoption de nouveaux outils et modes de travail
- Maîtrise du Pack Office complet, particulièrement d’Excel et des outils collaboratifs.
- Expérience pratique avec un CRM ou une base de données comparable, une connaissance d'un CRM spécifique n'est pas requise
- Familiarité avec les outils de visualisation de données ou de reporting est un atout

**Compétences transversales :**

- Excellente communication écrite et orale, avec une capacité à vulgariser les sujets techniques
- Rigueur, polyvalence, planification, gestion des priorités et organisation du travail
- Excellent relationnel interpersonnel et approche collaborative
- Force de proposition et capacité à prendre des initiatives, proposer des solutions.
- Capacité à travailler de façon autonome et indépendante.
- Capacité à travailler avec des équipes à distance.
- Connaissance du fonctionnement coopératif est un atout.
- Français et Anglais indispensables

**HULO VOUS OFFRIRA LES CONDITIONS SUIVANTES :**

Un poste salarié temps plein

- Basé à Montreuil avec possibilité de travailler à distance en France métropolitaine.
- Contrat de travail de droit français à durée déterminée de 9 mois (jusqu’au 31/10/2027).
- Statut cadre au forfait annuel sur base de 1607 heures par an.
- Conditions salariales :
- Salaire brut annuel : 29 620€ sur 13 mois
- 22 jours de RTT par an
- Mutuelle et Prévoyance AXA (prise en charge à 100% par hulo)
- Tickets restaurants : valeur faciale de 8€, pris en charge à 60% par hulo
- Conditions et aptitudes spécifiques : station assise prolongée, expression orale, travail sur écran, contacts téléphoniques.

jobs.title: Consultoría Veterinaria para apoyar en Acciones Anticipatorias de El Niño en la Guajira, estado Zulia
jobs.description:
DRC Venezuela busca una persona consultora en servicios veterinarios que pueda liderar el proceso de apoyo preventivo a la salud animal para proteger el ganado ante los impactos de la sequía.

**1. Antecedentes**

El Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una organización humanitaria internacional que trabaja en más de 40 países. Brinda protección y asistencia a personas refugiadas, desplazadas internas, retornadas, migrantes y comunidades de acogida, siguiendo los principios humanitarios de humanidad, neutralidad, imparcialidad e independencia.

DRC Venezuela opera desde Caracas y cinco bases: Maracaibo, Guasdualito, Carúpano y Sur del Lago. En el estado Zulia, DRC implementa acciones de preparación frente a los efectos del fenómeno de El Niño en los municipios de Colón, Catatumbo y La Guajira, donde la agricultura y la ganadería constituyen medios de vida fundamentales. Los análisis climáticos y las consultas comunitarias realizadas en 2026 evidencian una disminución de las fuentes de agua, el deterioro

de los pastizales, el aumento de la salinidad (Guajira) y mayores dificultades para mantener la producción agropecuaria, generando riesgos para la seguridad alimentaria y los ingresos de los hogares rurales.

Las comunidades identificaron una afectación creciente sobre los rebaños bovinos, ovinos y caprinos, reflejada en pérdida de condición corporal, reducción de la producción y mayor vulnerabilidad a enfermedades asociadas al estrés hídrico y nutricional. En respuesta, DRC desarrollará acciones anticipatorias para fortalecer la salud animal mediante campañas de vacunación y desparasitación, suplementación vitamínica y mineral, evaluación sanitaria de rebaños y capacitación para reducir los efectos negativos del niño sobre sus ganados y animales traspatio, con el fin de proteger los activos productivos y la resiliencia de las familias más expuestas a los efectos de la sequía.

**2. Objetivos**

**Objetivo general:**

Fortalecer las capacidades de los hogares productores del municipio Indígena Bolivariano Guajira para la protección y manejo adecuado de sus activos pecuarios, mediante acciones de asistencia técnica, formación e implementación de medidas preventivas de sanidad animal que contribuyan a la sostenibilidad de sus medios de vida frente a los efectos de la sequía.

**Objetivos específicos:**

1. **Realizar la evaluación y selección técnica de los potenciales beneficiarios del componente pecuario**, mediante diagnósticos de campo que permitan determinar la elegibilidad de los hogares y el estado sanitario de sus animales, de acuerdo con los criterios establecidos por DRC.
2. **Diseñar e impartir un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva**, dirigido a pequeños productores u hogares que poseen cría de animales para la subsistencia (auto-consumo), abordando temas relacionados con alimentación animal en condiciones de sequía, suplementación nutricional, vacunación, desparasitación, bioseguridad y otras medidas para la protección de los medios de vida pecuarios.
3. **Implementar jornadas veterinarias preventivas para bovinos, caprinos, porcinos y aves** de traspatio, incluyendo actividades de evaluación sanitaria, vacunación, desparasitación y orientación técnica a productores, contribuyendo a mejorar la salud animal y la capacidad de recuperación de los hogares frente a los impactos de la sequía.
4. **Desarrollar una evaluación final de los beneficiarios y elaborar un informe técnico de resultados**, que documente la implementación de las actividades, los principales logros alcanzados, las mejoras observadas en las capacidades de los hogares participantes y las recomendaciones para el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia de los medios de vida pecuarios frente a eventos climáticos adversos

**3. Alcance del trabajo**

La consultoría cubre los siguientes componentes:

1. Realizar la evaluación y selección técnica de los potenciales beneficiarios del componente pecuario. Meta: Evaluar al menos a 80 hogares, para seleccionar 60 hogares que cumplan con los criterios (línea de base). Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del municipio Indígena Bolivariano Guajira
2. Diseñar e impartir un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva. Meta: 1. Diseñar un programa formativo de 4 sesiones, para un total de 16 horas formativas por cada grupo. 2. Brindar formación a al menos 2 grupos de 30 personas, para un total de 60 personas formadas. Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del municipio Indígena Bolivariano Guajira: Espacios comunitarios ubicados por DRC para realizar la formación
3. Implementar jornadas veterinarias preventivas para bovinos, caprinos, porcinos y aves de traspatio. Meta: Brindar jornadas veterinarias a los 90 participantes seleccionados en el programa. Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del municipio Indígena Bolivariano Guajira: Espacio puede ser mediante visitas domiciliarias o acordando con la comunidad un espacio céntrico para los participantes
4. Desarrollar una evaluación final de los beneficiarios y elaborar un informe técnico de resultados. Meta: 1. Aplicar una línea de salida a los participantes (53 encuestas) 2. Elaborar 1 informe técnico de resultados. Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del municipio Indígena Bolivariano Guajira: Espacio para realizar línea de salida puede ser mediante visitas domiciliarias o acordando con la comunidad un espacio céntrico para los participantes.

**Nota:** la persona consultora no tendrá que cubrir los costos de traslados a las comunidades ni la adquisición de materiales formativos, toda vez que serán cubiertos por DRC.

A su vez, la lista de personas pre-identificadas a diagnosticar será proporcionada por el equipo de Recuperación Económica de DRC.

**4. Productos esperados**

Los productos se entregan de forma progresiva durante el contrato, según las prioridades que fije el Líder de recuperación económica con el Gerente de base. Los plazos y productos son indicativos y se cuentan desde la firma del contrato.

1. Diagnóstico inicial y plan de trabajo con estimación de horas por componente. Semana 1
2. Realizar la evaluación y selección técnica de los potenciales beneficiarios del componente pecuario. Semanas 2-4
3. Diseñar un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva. Semanas 5-6
4. Implementar jornadas veterinarias preventivas para bovinos, caprinos, porcinos y aves de traspatio. Semanas 6-8
5. Impartir un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva. Semanas 9-12
6. Desarrollar una evaluación final de los beneficiarios y elaborar un informe técnico de resultados. Semanas 13-16

Cada mes la persona consultora entrega, junto con su factura, un timesheet con las horas trabajadas por componente y un breve reporte de avance.

**5. Dedicación, modalidad y supervisión**

- **Período:** desde la firma del contrato, prevista para noviembre de 2026, hasta febrero de 2027. Puede extenderse por enmienda según necesidades y presupuesto.
- **Dedicación:** por horas, según las necesidades del Gerente de base y Líder de Recuperación Económica. El total no puede superar **640 horas**, DRC no garantiza un mínimo de horas.
- **Modalidad:** Presencial. El consultor deberá trasladarse con el equipo de DRC a las comunidades de intervención del proyecto, en el cronograma acordado con la oficina de la base de DRC.
- **Supervisión:** Gerente de base. La coordinación diaria es con la Líder de equipo de Recuperación Económica. También habrá coordinación con Supply cuando aplique.
- **Recursos que aporta DRC:** acceso a la documentación interna necesaria, costos de traslado a comunidades y material didáctico requerido. La persona consultora usa su propio equipo y conexión, así como la propiedad intelectual del desarrollo de las formaciones.

**6. Perfil requerido**

**Requisitos obligatorios**

- Profesional universitario en Medicina Veterinaria, Zootecnia, Ingeniería en Producción Animal, Biología o carreras afines relacionadas con la producción pecuaria y la sanidad animal.
- Mínimo dos (2) años de experiencia profesional comprobable en el diseño, implementación o acompañamiento de proyectos vinculados a la sanidad animal, producción pecuaria, extensión rural o fortalecimiento de medios de vida agropecuarios.
- Experiencia en la ejecución de jornadas veterinarias preventivas, incluyendo vacunación, desparasitación, evaluación sanitaria y manejo de especies pecuarias como bovinos, caprinos, porcinos, ovinos y aves de traspatio.
- Experiencia en el desarrollo e implementación de procesos de formación y asistencia técnica dirigidos a productores agropecuarios, organizaciones comunitarias o promotores locales.
- Conocimiento y experiencia en enfoques de adaptación al cambio climático y gestión de riesgos en sistemas productivos agropecuarios, incluyendo medidas orientadas a fortalecer la resiliencia de los medios de vida rurales frente a eventos climáticos extremos.
- Experiencia de trabajo de campo con comunidades rurales, poblaciones vulnerables, personas desplazadas, migrantes, refugiadas y/o comunidades de acogida.
- Capacidad demostrada para facilitar procesos participativos, relacionarse con diversos actores comunitarios e institucionales, coordinar actividades en terreno y trabajar de manera efectiva con equipos multidisciplinarios.
- Habilidades para la elaboración de informes técnicos, sistematización de resultados y presentación de recomendaciones derivadas de procesos de diagnóstico, capacitación y asistencia técnica.
- Disponibilidad para iniciar en noviembre de 2026 y trasladarse a las comunidades de los municipios indicados, de preferencia en horarios de la mañana.

**Requisitos deseables**

- Experiencia previa de trabajo con organizaciones humanitarias, agencias de cooperación internacional o programas de recuperación temprana y resiliencia.
- Conocimiento de los sistemas productivos pecuarios predominantes en el estado Zulia o en otras zonas rurales de Venezuela.

**7. Contenido y presentación de la oferta**

Las ofertas deben incluir:

1. **CV** de la persona consultora, con tres referencias profesionales verificables.
2. Propuesta de contenido formativo (preliminar), detallando la siguiente información: - Número de módulo - Nombre de la sesión - Contenido a abordar propuesto - Horas requeridas - Material didáctico requerido - Total horas.
3. **Oferta financiera:** tarifa diaria en USD, **todo incluido** (honorarios, impuestos, equipo, conexión y cualquier otro costo), por una jornada de 8 horas. La tarifa horaria se calcula como la tarifa diaria dividida entre 8.
4. **Documentos administrativos**: RIF vigente, documento de identidad o registro mercantil, y formulario de registro de proveedor de DRC.
5. Declaración firmada de ausencia de conflicto de interés y aceptación del Código de Conducta de Proveedores de DRC.

No se solicita propuesta técnica.

**8. Criterios de evaluación**

Las ofertas que cumplan los requisitos administrativos y obligatorios se evalúan con una ponderación de 70 % técnica y 30 % financiera. La evaluación técnica se basa en el CV y las referencias. Solo pasan a la evaluación financiera las ofertas con al menos 49 de 70 puntos técnicos. DRC puede entrevistar a las personas mejor puntuadas.

- Formación académica en Medicina Veterinaria, Zootecnia, Ingeniería de Producción Animal o áreas afines. *20 puntos*.
- Experiencia en sanidad animal, producción pecuaria y ejecución de campañas de vacunación, desparasitación o atención veterinaria preventiva. *20 puntos*.
- Experiencia demostrable en el diseño e implementación de intervenciones para el fortalecimiento de medios de vida pecuarios, incluyendo diagnósticos técnicos, capacitación de productores, asistencia veterinaria preventiva y acciones de resiliencia frente a riesgos climáticos en comunidades rurales. *15 puntos*.
- Calidad de la propuesta metodológica para la ejecución de la consultoría *15 puntos*.
- **Total técnico 70** ***puntos.***
- Oferta financiera: tarifa diaria más baja / tarifa evaluada × 30 30
- **Total 100** ***puntos.***

**9. Condiciones contractuales**

- **Contrato:** Contrato de Servicios de Consultoría de DRC, con las Condiciones Generales de Contrato y el Código de Conducta de Proveedores de DRC como anexos obligatorios.
- **Pagos:** mensuales, por transferencia, según las horas efectivamente trabajadas, a la tarifa horaria derivada de la tarifa diaria ofertada. Cada pago requiere factura válida y timesheet aprobado por el Gerente de base. Se aplican las retenciones de ley. El monto total no puede superar el equivalente a 640 horas.
- **Confidencialidad:** toda la información de DRC, de sus donantes, de su personal y de las personas participantes es confidencial. Los productos de la consultoría son propiedad de DRC.
- **Protección de datos:** el tratamiento de datos personales, incluidos los de personas beneficiarias de CVA, sigue las políticas de protección de datos de DRC.
- **Conducta:** la persona consultora firma y cumple el Código de Conducta de DRC, incluida la tolerancia cero frente a la explotación y el abuso sexual, el fraude y la corrupción.
- **Conflicto de interés:** no pueden participar personas de DRC Venezuela ni que tengan vínculos con personal involucrado en esta contratación.
- **Derecho de DRC:** DRC puede aceptar o rechazar cualquier oferta, total o parcialmente, sin obligación de justificar su decisión.

jobs.title: Programme Manager Mine Action & Disarmament
jobs.description:
Do you have senior management experience from humanitarian mine action and strong skills in programme leadership, donor engagement and capacity development? Are you motivated by a role where you will contribute to the clearance of explosive ordnance, strengthen national mine action capacity and support the safety and livelihoods of affected communities in Lebanon? Then you might be the candidate that we are looking for!

**What we offer:**

- The opportunity to lead and further develop NPA’s Mine Action and Disarmament programme in Lebanon.
- The opportunity to develop and implement a mentorship strategy that strengthens national mine action management capacity and supports localisation.
- A meaningful role contributing directly to the clearance of explosive ordnance and improved safety and livelihoods for affected communities.
- A one-year expatriate contract.
- Comprehensive salary package including country-specific allowances.
- A robust insurance scheme.
- Five weeks’ annual holiday plus one additional week off for expats.
- Three international flights home per contract year.
- R&R scheme.

**Requirements:**

- Minimum five years’ experience at senior management level in a humanitarian mine action programme.
- Relevant higher education and work experience and/or relevant military experience and education.
- Experience with programme strategy, large-scale project management, monitoring and evaluation, risk management and donor compliance.
- Strong people management experience and proven ability to lead multidisciplinary and multicultural teams, including remotely.
- Experience engaging with donors, governmental authorities, national stakeholders and local partners.
- Experience of managing finance, administrative and human resource systems to ensure programme efficiency.
- Knowledge and understanding of relevant institutional donors (NMFA, USDoS, GFFO, EU, FCDO, etc.).

As a person, you identify with NPA’s leadership principles and demonstrate strong cultural awareness, communication skills, integrity and the ability to motivate and support others in a calm and professional manner. This role requires strategic leadership, sound judgement and the ability to work independently in a complex and volatile context. Therefore, it is particularly important that you enjoy building relationships, mentoring colleagues, and leading teams through operational and organizational change.

**Responsibilities:**

- Provide strategic, financial and operational leadership for the Mine Action and Disarmament programme in Lebanon, ensuring safe, effective and donor-compliant implementation.
- Lead programme planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting in line with NPA strategies, donor-approved plans and relevant standards.
- Develop funding proposals, donor reports and resource mobilisation initiatives in close coordination with the Country Director and Head Office advisors.
- Build and maintain constructive relationships with Lebanese authorities, donors, UN agencies, local communities, partners and other humanitarian actors.
- Line manage, mentor and support programme staff, including developing and implementing a mine action mentorship strategy to strengthen localisation and nationalisation.
- Ensure compliance with NPA policies, donor requirements, national standards, IMAS/NMAS, financial procedures, safeguarding obligations and safety and security systems.

\*Validity of the offer and contract depends on satisfactory medical certificate, full vaccination, valid travel visa and necessary permits for service and residency in the country of service. The offer and contract also depend on donor funding and might be subject to donor approval.

jobs.title: SAFETY & SECURITY MANAGER _ BORNO STATE
jobs.description:
**JOB PURPOSE**

Under the supervision of the Security Coordinator / Head of Mission the Safety and Security Manager will Develop and implement security policies, protocols and procedures to guarantee security standards are respected. He/ She will Plan and monitor all security related activities in the mission, he or she will support

To Recruit, train and supervise security personnel. The Safety and Security Manager is responsible for protecting personnel, premises, assets, and programmatic operations across assigned areas. The role combines continuous risk analysis, access negotiation, policy enforcement, emergency response readiness, and staff capacity building to enable safe and principled humanitarian delivery in a dynamic security environment.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

- **1. Context Monitoring, Threat & Risk Assessment**
- Monitor, verify, and analyze local political, socio-economic, and security developments affecting staff, communities, and operations.
- Produce concise, timely security advisories, incident trend analyses, and weekly/monthly context updates for leadership and operational teams.
- Conduct security risk assessments (SRAs) for offices, guest houses, field sites, travel routes, and new project locations prior to deployment.
- **2. Security Management Plans, Policies & Compliance**
- Maintain and localize Base/Field Security Management Plans, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and contingency plans (hibernation, relocation, evacuation).
- Ensure staff compliance with organizational safety and security rules, movement protocols, communications tracking, and humanitarian principles.
- Audit physical security measures across offices and residences (perimeter access, lighting, communications equipment, guard protocols) and recommend upgrades.
- **3. Humanitarian Access & Stakeholder Networking**
- Build and maintain constructive, principled relationships with local authorities, community leaders, humanitarian peers, security focal points, and relevant actors to support safe access.
- Represent the organization in relevant security/access coordination forums and information-sharing networks as mandated.
- Support acceptance strategies that align with organizational mandates and local cultural norms.
- **4. Training, Briefings & Team Supervision**
- Deliver mandatory security briefings and contextual orientations to new staff, visitors, and consultants, plus pre-mission and post-incident debriefings.
- Organize and deliver practical trainings (e.g., incident reporting, travel safety, communications protocols, crisis awareness) and supervise/coach security personnel and contracted guards.
- **5. Incident & Crisis Management**
- Act as a key operational advisor during security incidents or emergencies, supporting rapid information verification, reporting, and crisis response coordination.
- Help coordinate contingency actions—such as movement freezes, relocations, evacuations, or medical evacuation logistics—alongside management and external providers.
- Maintain accurate, confidential incident logs and support post-incident reviews and lessons learned.

Education

- University Degree in relevant field (Social Sciences, Psychology, Social Work, Human Rights, International Humanitarian Law or other fields related to social development and humanitarian work)
- Master’s degree in human Rights, International Humanitarian Law or other fields related desirable
- .

## Experience

Professional experience

- Minimum 4 years of working experience as Security Manager in a humanitarian/recovery context or relevant working experience in safety, security and risk analysis

Professional requirements

- Good understanding of humanitarian safety practices, procedures and principles and their application
- Experience, based on evidence, of humanitarian negotiation (with national authorities, local authorities, non-state actors, military forces) and humanitarian access in complex emergencies
- Experience in reporting and emergency response planning

Personal requirements

- Moral integrity
- Teamwork and communication skills
- Networking skills
.

jobs.title: Chargé.e de projet Orientation scolaire (Offre nationale)
jobs.description:
**Le projet**

Bibliothèques Sans Frontières (BSF) lance au Tchad un projet d'appui à l'orientation scolaire, financé par la Fondation Mastercard via le HCR et mis en œuvre avec le Jesuit Refugee Service (JRS). L'objectif est de réduire le décrochage scolaire et de faciliter la transition vers le secondaire des élèves réfugiés et des communautés hôtes, grâce à l'orientation scolaire et professionnelle et à des ressources pédagogiques hors ligne (Ideas Cube).

**Vos missions**

Le/La Chargé.e de projet est responsable de la planification opérationnelle, de la coordination, du suivi technique et budgétaire et de l’assurance qualité des activités dont BSF a la charge dans le projet, en lien avec JRS, qui pilote le projet et son suivi-évaluation, et avec le HCR.

Il/Elle garantit l’atteinte des résultats attendus de BSF, conformément au protocole d’accord avec JRS, aux exigences du HCR et de la Fondation Mastercard ainsi qu’aux standards techniques et de médiation de BSF.

La grande majorité des activités du projet se déroulera à l’Est du Tchad. Toutefois, certaines activités prendront place au Sud et au Lac et feront partie du périmètre de suivi du/de la Chargé.e de projet.

Le/La Chargé.e de projet est sous la supervision directe de la Responsable des Programmes Tchad de BSF.

Plus spécifiquement, ses responsabilités sont les suivantes :

- la planification, la coordination et le suivi des activités de BSF dans le projet ;
- le déploiement et le suivi des espaces documentaires numériques (installation, maintenance, analyse des données d'utilisation) ;
- la formation et l'accompagnement technique des superviseurs et conseillers d'orientation recrutés par JRS ;
- le suivi-évaluation, le reporting et le suivi budgétaire des lignes déléguées
- la représentation de BSF auprès des partenaires et des autorités éducatives.

**CONDITIONS**

- Type de contrat : Contrat à durée déterminé de 6 mois
- Date de démarrage : 18/12/2026
- Statut : poste national
- Rémunération : 600 000 XAF
- **Lieu de travail :** Abéché ou Farchana (bureaux de JRS), avec déplacements réguliers dans les établissements des camps et sites de réfugiés de l’Est (Ouaddaï, Wadi Fira, Sila et Ennedi Est) et ponctuels à N’Djamena, au Lac et dans le Sud selon les besoins du projet

**Profil recherché**

- Bac +3 minimum (Bac +5 apprécié) en sciences de l'éducation, gestion de projet, sciences sociales ou domaine équivalent

- Connaissance du système éducatif tchadien, de l'orientation scolaire et des principes de protection (sauvegarde de l'enfant, PSEA) appréciée
- Bonne maîtrise d'Excel, des outils numériques et de Kobo

jobs.title: Chargé.e de projet Jeunesse et Education (offre nationale)
jobs.description:
**Le contexte**

Dans l’Est du Tchad (Ouaddaï et Wadi Fira), BSF travaille en partenariat avec le Conseil norvégien pour les réfugiés (NRC) pour renforcer la résilience et l’autonomie des jeunes réfugiés et des communautés d’accueil. BSF y apporte son savoir-faire en éducation, numérique et médiation culturelle. Le partenariat comprend les projets RESIST et SDC (Ideas Box dans les centres de formation professionnelle des camps, avec trois nouvelles Ideas Box en 2026-2027), ainsi que le projet CDCS Metché, qui installera bientôt des Digital Learning Hubs dans quatre écoles.

**Votre mission**

Le/La Chargé.e de projet Jeunesse et Education est responsable de la planification opérationnelle, de la coordination, du suivi technique et budgétaire et de l'assurance qualité de l'ensemble des activités de BSF mises en œuvre en partenariat avec NRC dans l'Est du Tchad.

Il/Elle garantit l'atteinte des résultats de chaque projet, conformément aux exigences des bailleurs ainsi qu'aux standards techniques et de médiation de BSF, et veille à une distinction rigoureuse entre les projets, en particulier entre RESIST et SDC qui se cofinancent.

Plus spécifiquement, ses responsabilités sont les suivantes :

- Planifier, coordonner et suivre la mise en œuvre des projets, en assurant un suivi distinct des activités, indicateurs et dépenses de chaque financement.
- Superviser le déploiement, l’inventaire et la maintenance des Ideas Box et des Digital Learning Hubs, et gérer les contenus éducatifs.
- Encadrer et former les facilitateurs bénévoles des Ideas Box, avec 2 à 3 jours de visite terrain par semaine, en les accompagnant vers l’autonomie.
- Assurer le suivi-évaluation et le reporting (collecte de données, outils de suivi, rapports internes et pour NRC).
- Suivre le budget délégué et les démarches logistiques, et veiller au respect des procédures BSF, NRC et bailleurs.
- Représenter BSF auprès de NRC, des gestionnaires de camps, des autorités locales et des acteurs éducatifs.

**Conditions**

- CDD, statut employé
- Rémunération : 600 000 XAF / mois
- Lieu : Adré, avec déplacements réguliers dans les camps d’Arkoum, Alacha, Metché et Aboutengé, et ponctuels à Iriba (Wadi Fira)

**Profil recherché**

**Votre profil**

- Bac +3 minimum (Bac +5 apprécié) en gestion de projet, éducation, sciences sociales, développement, médiation numérique ou domaine équivalent.
- Au moins 3 ans d’expérience en gestion de projets humanitaires ou de développement (éducation, médiation, formation professionnelle, inclusion des jeunes), idéalement avec plusieurs financements en parallèle.
- Une expérience auprès des réfugiés et communautés hôtes, et dans l’Est du Tchad, est fortement souhaitée.
- Connaissance des exigences des bailleurs institutionnels ; une expérience en partenariat avec une grande ONG internationale est un atout.
- Expérience en formation et coaching d’équipes (bénévoles, jeunes), en pédagogie et en animation éducative.
- À l’aise avec le numérique (maintenance de premier niveau), Excel et Kobo.
- **Français et arabe courants indispensables** ; l’anglais est un atout.
- Rigueur, autonomie, bonne gestion du stress dans un contexte sécuritaire évolutif, et adhésion aux valeurs de protection et d’inclusion.

jobs.title: Country Director - Niger
jobs.description:
**About MSI**

MSI Reproductive Choices is one of the world’s leading providers of sexual and reproductive healthcare. We believe that everyone should have the right to choose. From contraception to safe abortion and life-saving post-abortion care, we are committed to delivering compassionate, affordable, high-quality services for all.

Today, our organisation has around 10,000 team members working in 36 countries across the world. Our success lies in the fact that MSI teams are locally led, entrepreneurial and results-driven, and are passionate about delivering high quality, client-centred care in their own communities. As a social business, we focus on sustainable delivery, efficiency, and funding models that are built to last, so that the women and girls we serve today will have a choice in the future too.

We know that access to reproductive choice is life changing. For some, it can mean the ability to complete an education or start a career. For others, it means being able to look after the family they already have. For everyone, it means the freedom to decide their own future, creating a fairer, more equal world.

**About the programme**

Since 2014, MSI Niger, a branch of MSI Reproductive Choices, has been a key contributor to Niger’s national family planning and reproductive health response. Operating across 6 of the country’s 8 regions, the programme delivers high-quality, voluntary and client-centred services, with a strong focus on expanding contraceptive access and reaching underserved populations.

Over the past five years, MSI Niger has reached more than 1.5 million women, men, adolescents and young people. In 2025 alone, the programme served over 549,000 family planning clients, generating approximately 811,000 couple-years of protection and contributing to an estimated 640 maternal deaths averted.

MSI Niger delivers services through a diversified model comprising 14 mobile outreach teams, 14 MS Ladies and a network of 221 public-sector sites, aligning with national maternal health priorities and working in close partnership with national, regional and district health authorities. The programme combines direct service delivery with public-sector strengthening, including provider capacity building, clinical quality improvement, data strengthening and support for sustainable national ownership.

A strong focus is placed on reaching people who face the greatest barriers to care, including rural women, adolescents and young people, internally displaced people, people living with disabilities and survivors of gender-based violence. Community-based approaches, including community liaisons, community-based distribution, help address socio-cultural barriers.

These channels are complemented by MSI Niger’s toll-free “488” client hotline, which provides reproductive health information and facilitates referrals to appropriate service delivery points.

**About the Role**

The Country Director, Niger, is responsible for delivering results for women and their families, driving programmatic excellence, and implementing best practice at scale in Niger. They provide high-quality services where they are needed the most, and their work directly contributes to preventing maternal deaths and making a sustainable impact on the lives of thousands of people every year. The CD is also responsible for ensuring Niger’s social business model has a strong footing on both the social and business side. The Country Director, Niger, is a key leadership position. The CD represents the organisation in Niger and is responsible for the overall strategy, management (programmatic, financial, and administrative), and development of MSI Niger’s national family planning and reproductive health programmes. CD is leading skilled, professional country teams to deliver life-saving services through clinical centre, mobile outreach teams, MS Ladies, public sector support, and social marketing. In addition, CD is responsible for preparing and executing annual budgets, marketing plans and work plans; developing new business opportunities; overseeing financial, administrative, and logistical resources; ensuring adherence to MSI minimum standards; and assuring quality operations in line with annual and long-term strategic goals and objectives. The Country Director manages results, valuing and rewarding high performance, accountability, speed and efficiency and innovation, while keeping the client at the heart of everything we do. The Country Director is MSI Niger’s senior representative in the country of assignment. Reporting to Africa Regional Office of MSI, MSI Niger is an implementing partner of the MoH, with whom MSI Niger works closely and aligns its projects and service delivery channels with national priorities, partnering at national, regional, district and facility level. They work closely with government to overcome barriers that prevent women and men from accessing safe, affordable, reliable family planning and other reproductive health services.

**About You**

For us, it’s vital that every MSI team member believes in and is committed to our organisational mission, vision and values.

**This means that we will only accept applications from candidates who are unequivocally pro-choice.**

Our values act as guiding principles, providing us with a clear direction. They set the tone for how we approach our work, interact with others and align ourselves as ‘One MSI’. It’s important that our team members truly resonate with our values and demonstrate them consistently, in all that they do.

We recruit talented, dynamic individuals with diverse backgrounds who share our mission and are focused on delivering measurable results. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can participate and contribute meaningfully. We value open-mindedness, curiosity, resilience, and a solutions-oriented mindset, alongside a commitment to promoting equality and safeguarding the welfare of both team members and clients.

We seek exceptional communicators who are self-motivated, solutions-driven, and aligned with MSI’s mission and entrepreneurial mindset. You should be dedicated to driving social change in an environment focused on sustainable impact, both locally and globally, and comfortable working with diverse teams in an ambiguous setting.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following skills:**

- Proven experience of driving impact, quality and sustainability in programmes and improving operational standards
- Effective interpersonal skills, with the ability to lead, motivate and guide Country Programmes and teams.
- Proven ability to effectively communicate ideas, proposals, issues, and implications at senior level.
- Excellent project management skills related to organisational development projects and international, cross-functional teams with a proven history of delivering results.
- Highly developed problem solving, diplomatic, networking and negotiation skills.
- Demonstration of ‘making things happen’, operating at pace and delivering effectively through others.
- High capability on change management within fast-paced environment

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following experience:**

- Experience of developing and successfully implementing business plans and growth strategies, with a track record of aligning resources with key priorities, keeping management teams focused on critical milestones and consistently achieving results.
- Experience of communicating a range of complex issues with the ability to convey an inspiring vision and purpose both within operations and where appropriate across other business functions.
- Experience leading, managing and mentoring teams and individuals ; able to clearly articulate strategies that support a team to deliver results
- An understanding of major policies/ issues of large bilateral/multilateral donors strong working knowledge of business practices
- An international mindset, with an understanding of, and empathy for, the development sector, together with an appreciation for cultural differences
- Experience of formulating and controlling budgets to ensure effective monitoring takes place.
- Understanding of the issues surrounding provision of reproductive health care services internationally
- A reputation for ‘making things happen’, operating at pace and delivering effectively throughothers.
- Fluent in French and capacity to communicate in English language (written and oral) is preferable for this role.

Please see the job description in English [**here**](https://www.msichoices.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/202611-Job-Framework-Country-Director-Niger-002.pdf)**.**

Please see the job description in French [**here**](https://www.msichoices.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/202611-Description-de-Poste-Directeur-Pays-MSI-Niger.pdf)**.**

**Location:** Niger.

**Contract type: 2 year fixed term contract**

**Salary**: The salary will be strictly banded within the local national context.

**Salary band: BG 12C**

**Closing date: 26th December 2026 (midnight GMT**). Interviews may take place before this date for exceptional candidates.

***For internal employees applying from an MSI country programme, the role will be benchmarked to the local labour market of that country. Local terms and conditions of the country will apply.***

jobs.title: Asistente de Recursos Humanos

El Consejo Danés para Refugiados (DRC por sus siglas en inglés) es una de las principales ONG humanitarias del mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para proporcionar asistencia adecuada con un enfoque basado en derechos para los refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, los desplazados internos, repatriados y migrantes. Actualmente DRC Colombia implementa una respuesta humanitaria centrada protección para refugiados y migrantes venezolanos y colombianos retornados en ciudades de Colombia como Riohacha, Barranquilla y Bogotá, actualmente también incorpora actividades en Nariño y en Norte de Santander.El Consejo Danés para Refugiados (DRC por sus siglas en inglés) es una de las principales ONG humanitarias del mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para proporcionar asistencia adecuada con un enfoque basado en derechos para los refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, los desplazados internos, repatriados y migrantes. DRC ha estado presente en Colombia desde 2011, pero 2018 amplía sus operaciones en respuesta a la crisis venezolana. Actualmente DRC Colombia implementa una respuesta humanitaria centrada protección para refugiados y migrantes venezolanos y colombianos retornados en ciudades de Colombia como Riohacha, actualmente también incorpora actividades en Nariño y en Norte de Santander.

Responsabilidades:
Reclutamiento y selección

- Citar a los candidatos para la realización de pruebas técnicas, garantizando el envío y la recepción de estas y consolidando la información de los resultados.
- Citar a los candidatos a entrevistas.
- Actualizar las bases de datos del proceso de selección.
- Salvaguardar la documentación del proceso, garantizando el adecuado archivo del proceso

- Realizar las entrevistas que resulten de los procesos de selección.
- Realizar la verificación de referencias correspondientes para los procesos de selección.

Contratación

- Solicitar y verificar referencias laborales.
- Programar exámenes médicos de ingreso y/o periódicos.
- Realizar los procesos de afiliación a medicina prepagada y al sistema de seguridad social.
- Crear perfiles de nuevos colaboradores en el ERP Dynamics.
- Efectuar la solicitud de contratos y otrosí.

- Enviar la documentación de contratación y garantizar la creación del expediente del empleado.

Bienestar

Desarrollo

Facturación y Viajes

Otras actividades

Experiencia y Competencias Técnicas:

- Conocimientos técnicos básicos de Recursos Humanos y Legislación laboral
- Sensibilidad cultural y capacidad para trabajar en un entorno intercultural

- Manejo básico de ERP de nómina y administración de personal
- Atención al detalle, organización y orientación al resultado

Educación

Idiomas:

- Lograr la excelencia: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes
- Colaboración: involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación
- Tomar la iniciativa: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación
- Comunicar: escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad
- Demostración de integridad: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC

**Ofrecemos:**

**¡Queremos que hagas parte de nuestro equipo!**

Por ello, invitamos especialmente a personas con movilidad reducida que cumplan con el perfil del cargo a postularse y participar en nuestros procesos de selección.**

Si durante el proceso de selección requieres algún ajuste razonable o apoyo para participar en igualdad de condiciones, te invitamos a informárnoslo. Estaremos encantados de brindarte el acompañamiento necesario para que puedas participar plenamente.**

Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un(a) candidato(a) adecuado(a). DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo. Se recomienda hacer la aplicación a esta vacante lo más pronto posible, si esta es de su interés.***

jobs.title: MERL Director - USDA Food for Peace Non-Emergency Program - El Salvador
jobs.description:
**The Organization**

***About Corus:*** Corus International is the parent of a family of world-class social impact organizations that collaborate in the world's most vulnerable communities to deliver holistic and sustainable solutions to the interconnected challenges of poverty, access to healthcare, and climate change. Corus combines more than 150 years of experience from its nonprofit and for-profit affiliates - IMA World Health, Lutheran World Relief, CGA Technologies, Ground Up Investing, and LWR Farmers Market - to develop rural economies, eliminate extreme poverty, expand access to quality healthcare, and respond to urgent humanitarian needs in fragile contexts.

Further details about the organization can be found at: [https://corusinternational.org](https://corusinternational.org/)

***About Lutheran World Relief:*** Founded in 1945, Lutheran World Relief (LWR) partners with local governments, farmer organizations, private-sector actors, and communities to build sustainable, inclusive, market-based rural economies. LWR brings deep experience in agricultural market systems, food security, resilience, financial inclusion, value-chain development, producer organization strengthening, and private-sector engagement, including longstanding programming in El Salvador and across Latin America.

**Position Summary**

Lutheran World Relief is seeking a Monitoring, Evaluation, Research, and Learning (MERL) Director to lead the MERL function for an anticipated USDA Foreign Agricultural Service Food for Peace Non-Emergency multi-year program in El Salvador. USDA has identified El Salvador as a priority country and announced that this programming will target people and places experiencing recurrent food crises through a Graduation through Agriculture-led Development Approach that combines the Graduation model, U.S. agricultural commodities, and targeted market systems strengthening focused on agricultural value chains. The program is intended to build resilience, improve food security, and reduce dependence on emergency food assistance.

The MERL Director will provide strategic and technical leadership for the program's monitoring, evaluation, research, learning, and accountability systems. The position will ensure that the program generates timely, reliable, and actionable evidence to measure participant progress, assess the effectiveness of graduation pathways, understand changes in agricultural market systems, track resilience and food-security outcomes, and inform continuous improvement and adaptive management.

The MERL Director will design and oversee an integrated MERL system capable of measuring both household-level and system-level change. Particular emphasis will be placed on tracking participant trajectories toward evidence-based graduation criteria and understanding whether agricultural markets, services, financial systems, and other local actors are becoming more inclusive, resilient, and capable of sustainably serving vulnerable households beyond the period of direct project assistance.

The MERL Director will work closely with the Chief of Party, Deputy Chief of Party, technical leads, consortium partners, and Corus technical experts to ensure that evidence and learning directly inform program decisions. The position will supervise MERL staff, strengthen partner MERL capacity, oversee data quality and analysis, coordinate research and evaluations, and support high-quality donor reporting and learning products.

The position will be based in El Salvador and will report to the Chief of Party. Regular travel to project areas is required. Actual hiring is contingent upon signed agreement and USDA approval. Salvadoran nationals are highly encouraged to apply.

The scope aligns with Corus Director | Grade 90, reflecting leadership of a major technical function, direct oversight of technical quality and staff, and 8-10 years of relevant experience.

**Responsibilities**

- Provide strategic and technical leadership for the program's monitoring, evaluation, research, learning, and accountability functions, ensuring that MERL systems are aligned with the program's theory of change, USDA requirements, approved indicators, and learning priorities.
- Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the program's comprehensive MERL plan, including results frameworks, indicators, targets, data sources, collection methodologies, reporting processes, learning questions, evaluation activities, and data-quality procedures. Ensure that MERL systems appropriately measure food security, resilience, agricultural livelihoods, nutrition-sensitive outcomes, economic inclusion, climate adaptation, and other priority outcomes established under the award.
- Develop and oversee systems for tracking participant progress through the graduation pathway, including baseline status, receipt and sequencing of interventions, household milestones, resilience and food-security outcomes, livelihood performance, economic resilience, access to financial and market services, and achievement and sustainability of established graduation criteria. Establish mechanisms to identify households that are progressing at different rates and generate evidence that enables technical teams to adapt the intensity and sequencing of support.
- Develop approaches for measuring market-systems and agricultural value-chain change, including changes in market relationships, access to inputs and services, financial inclusion, buyer-seller relationships, private-sector behavior and investment, producer organization performance, market access, and the continuation or replication of improved practices and services beyond direct project support.
- Lead or oversee the design and implementation of mixed-methods research and learning activities for baseline, midline, endline, and other quantitative and qualitative studies, assessments, evaluations, and operational research required by the program or donor to explain not only whether program outcomes are being achieved, but how, for whom, under what conditions, and why.
- Work with program leadership and technical teams to develop a focused learning agenda addressing critical questions related to graduation, agriculture-led development, market systems, resilience, food security, U.S. agricultural commodity integration, inclusion, and sustainability.
- Establish regular processes for translating monitoring, research, and evaluation findings into program decisions, including dashboards, reflection sessions, pause-and-reflect exercises, learning reviews, and other adaptive-management mechanisms. Analyze participant and implementation data to identify patterns, bottlenecks, unintended effects, differential outcomes, and emerging risks.
- Design and maintain robust systems for data collection, storage, management, visualization, and analysis that provide program teams and leadership with timely access to accurate and decision-relevant information.
- Establish and oversee rigorous data-quality assurance processes, including routine data-quality assessments, verification, validation, spot checks, documentation standards, and corrective-action processes across LWR and consortium partners.
- Ensure appropriate disaggregation and analysis of results by sex, age, geography, vulnerability status, disability, and other relevant characteristics to understand differential participation, access, progression, and outcomes and to support inclusive programming.
- Work closely with technical teams to integrate participant accountability and feedback mechanisms into program monitoring and learning systems and ensure feedback from participants and communities informs program decisions.

jobs.title: Chief of Party - USDA Food for Peace Non-Emergency Program - El Salvador
jobs.description:
**The Organization**

***About Corus:*** Corus International is the parent of a family of world-class social impact organizations that collaborate in the world's most vulnerable communities to deliver holistic and sustainable solutions to the interconnected challenges of poverty, access to healthcare, and climate change. Corus combines more than 150 years of experience from its nonprofit and for-profit affiliates - IMA World Health, Lutheran World Relief, CGA Technologies, Ground Up Investing, and LWR Farmers Market - to develop rural economies, eliminate extreme poverty, expand access to quality healthcare, and respond to urgent humanitarian needs in fragile contexts.

Further details about the organization can be found at: [https://corusinternational.org](https://corusinternational.org/)

***About Lutheran World Relief:*** Founded in 1945, Lutheran World Relief (LWR) partners with local governments, farmer organizations, private-sector actors, and communities to build sustainable, inclusive, market-based rural economies. LWR brings deep experience in agricultural market systems, food security, resilience, financial inclusion, value-chain development, producer organization strengthening, and private-sector engagement, including longstanding programming in El Salvador and across Latin America.

**Position Summary**

Lutheran World Relief is seeking a Chief of Party (COP) to provide overall vision, technical direction, and executive management for an anticipated USDA Foreign Agricultural Service Food for Peace Non-Emergency multi-year program in El Salvador. USDA has identified El Salvador as a priority country and announced that this programming will target people and places experiencing recurrent food crises through a Graduation through Agriculture-led Development Approach that combines the Graduation model, U.S. agricultural commodities, and targeted market systems strengthening focused on agricultural value chains. The program is intended to build resilience, improve food security, and reduce dependence on emergency food assistance.

The COP will be accountable for the integrated design and delivery of a sequenced graduation and market systems strategy. The role will ensure that household-level support - including consumption support, coaching, financial inclusion, skills development, productive assets, and links to services - is deliberately connected to commercially viable agricultural opportunities, inclusive value chains, private-sector incentives, and durable local systems. The COP will lead the project team and consortium, serve as LWR's primary representative to USDA and senior Salvadoran stakeholders, and ensure high-quality, compliant, adaptive, and results-focused implementation.

The position will be based in El Salvador and will report to the Managing Director for Latin America and the Caribbean. Regular travel to project areas is required. Actual hiring is contingent upon signed agreement and USDA approval. Salvadoran nationals are highly encouraged to apply.

The scope aligns with Corus Senior Director | Grade 100, which covers full responsibility for all aspects of complex program implementation and senior external representation.

**Responsibilities**

**Strategic and Technical Leadership**

- Provide strategic, technical, and managerial leadership for the full program, ensuring a coherent theory of change and implementation strategy that integrates graduation, agriculture-led development, market systems strengthening, resilience, food security, nutrition-sensitive programming, and the use of U.S. agricultural commodities.

**Household and Graduation approach**

- Lead contextualization and sequencing of the graduation approach, including transparent participant targeting, time-bound consumption support, household coaching and mentoring, savings and financial inclusion, technical and business skills development, productive asset transfer, and linkages to government, financial, social, and market services. Ensure that household graduation strategies are based on clear criteria and realistic opportunities for sustainable livelihoods.

**Agricultural value chains and market systems development**

- Provide senior technical leadership for market systems development, including agricultural value-chain analysis, market actor and incentive mapping, private-sector engagement, access to inputs and services, finance, producer organization and MSME development, buyer-seller relationships, value addition, post-harvest systems, and enabling-environment constraints.
- Balance targeted support to highly vulnerable households with facilitative market systems approaches that avoid long-term distortion or dependency; use adaptive management to adjust sequencing, intensity, and partnerships based on participant trajectories and market performance.

**Program Management and Administration**

- Lead annual work planning, budgeting, implementation, risk management, and performance reviews; ensure that technical, operational, financial, commodity, subaward, security, safeguarding, and human-resources functions operate as one integrated program.
- Ensure full compliance with the award, applicable USDA and U.S. Government regulations, LWR/Corus policies, Salvadoran law, safeguarding requirements, and donor branding, marking, reporting, and recordkeeping requirements; maintain strong controls to prevent waste, fraud, abuse, exploitation, and diversion.
- Build and manage a high-performing multidisciplinary team and consortium; define roles and decision rights, supervise senior staff, manage partner performance, resolve implementation bottlenecks, and foster an inclusive culture of accountability, learning, collaboration, and staff development.
- Ensure robust monitoring, evaluation, accountability, research, and learning systems that disaggregate results, track household graduation and market-system change, assess resilience and food-security outcomes, document unintended effects, and support timely course correction.
- Ensure timely, accurate, and high-quality submission of work plans, financial and program reports, indicator data, evaluations, learning products, and other deliverables; communicate implementation risks, decisions, and corrective actions clearly to USDA and Corus leadership.
- Oversee all aspects of U.S. agricultural commodity planning and integration relevant to the award, coordinating with qualified commodity, logistics, warehousing, distribution, and compliance staff to ensure commodities support program objectives and participant safety without undermining local markets.

**Supervisory**

- Directly supervises the Deputy Chief of Party, MERL Director, and other senior project leadership positions established in the approved staffing structure.

**Education & Experience**

- Master's degree in agricultural economics, economics, agribusiness, international development, food security, business administration, public policy, or a closely related field; a bachelor's degree with substantial additional relevant experience may be considered.
- Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible experience leading large, complex, multi-year international development or food-security programs, including substantial senior management responsibility for technical quality, personnel, budgets, partnerships, compliance, and results.
- Prior experience as Chief of Party, Project Director, Deputy Chief of Party, or equivalent senior leader on a large U.S. Government-funded agriculture, livelihoods, resilience, food assistance, or economic-growth program is required; USDA/FAS or legacy USAID Food for Peace DFSA/RFSA experience is strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated technical expertise in the Graduation Approach or closely related economic-inclusion programming, including participant targeting, consumption support, coaching, savings and financial inclusion, livelihood skills, productive assets, service linkages, and graduation measurement.
- Demonstrated expertise in market systems development and agricultural value-chain programming, including private-sector engagement, market analysis, business and financial services, producer organizations, MSMEs, market linkages, and strategies to address systemic constraints without creating dependency.
- Proven ability to integrate household-level graduation interventions with market systems facilitation in fragile, shock-prone, or food-insecure settings, and to manage the trade-offs between short-term stabilization and long-term commercial sustainability.
- Demonstrated experience managing food-security, resilience, and agriculture-led development programs that apply adaptive management and evidence to adjust implementation in response to shocks, participant progress, and market dynamics.
- Experience leading complex consortia and managing subrecipients, grants, contractors, and technical partners; demonstrated ability to align diverse organizations around shared results, quality standards, timelines, budgets, and compliance requirements.
- Strong financial, operational, and award-management skills, including experience overseeing large budgets, internal controls, procurement, subaward management, audit readiness, and donor reporting under U.S. Government rules and regulations.
- Experience with U.S. in-kind food assistance, commodity management, supply-chain logistics, warehousing, distribution, or market-impact monitoring is strongly preferred; the candidate must be able to supervise specialized teams responsible for these functions.
- Demonstrated ability to engage effectively with senior government officials, USDA and other U.S. Government representatives, private-sector leaders, financial institutions, producer organizations, local partners, and community stakeholders.
- Experience working in El Salvador or the Northern Central America region is strongly preferred, with a strong understanding of rural livelihoods, agricultural value chains, recurrent food insecurity, climate and economic shocks, migration dynamics, and public-private coordination in the Salvadoran context.
- Excellent leadership, negotiation, communication, analytical, problem-solving, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to lead multidisciplinary and multicultural teams and make timely decisions under complex operating conditions.
- Professional fluency in Spanish and English, including the ability to conduct high-level negotiations and produce clear technical and management documents in both languages, is required.
- Ability to travel regularly within El Salvador and internationally, as required, and authorization to work in El Salvador at the time of hire or ability to obtain such authorization.

jobs.title: ICLA Project Manager Tripoli Libya
jobs.description:
**What we are looking for**

The **Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)** is looking for an experienced and motivated **ICLA Project Manager** to lead our Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) programme across **West Libya**.

This is a unique opportunity to manage a high-impact legal protection portfolio that supports internally displaced people, returnees, refugees, migrants and vulnerable host communities to understand, claim and exercise their rights. Working in a complex humanitarian environment, you will lead a diverse team, oversee multi-donor projects, engage with authorities and partners, and help shape solutions that improve access to justice, legal documentation, housing, employment and essential services.

**We are looking for an experienced project manager within the humanitarian sector with a strong leadership profile, results driven and with a passion for empowering people affected by displacement. You are a skilled project manager who can balance strategic leadership with day-to-day operational delivery in a challenging context.**

**Experience and background in legal or protection work is an added advantage.**

***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Libya, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***

**What you will do**

As ICLA Project Manager, you will lead NRC's legal protection and Individual Protection Assistance, Protection from Violence (PfV) portfolio across Tripoli, Misrata, Tawergha and other locations in West Libya.

Key responsibilities include:

- Managing a team of legal, protection and information management professionals.
- Leading project design, implementation, monitoring, reporting and budget management.
- Ensuring high-quality legal assistance, counselling and case management services.
- Overseeing legal protection interventions covering: Housing, Land and Property (HLP) rights, legal identity and civil documentation, employment rights and procedures, legal stay and residency issues and access to essential services.
- Contribute to the development of Country, Area and ICLA and PfV strategies; initiate and participate in the development of relevant ICLA and PfV projects, proposals and budgets.
- Provide technical support to the teams, training and coaching teams to ensure implementation is aligned to the technical direction provided by the ICLA Specialist and ensure high technical quality of ICLA and PfV projects and also coach and train team members on technical
- Provide regular progress reports to the Area Manager and the ICLA Specialist, highlighting achievements, challenges and risks.
- Building and maintaining relationships with government authorities, civil society organizations, legal actors, partners and donors
- Driving evidence-based advocacy to promote the rights of displacement-affected communities
- Ensuring compliance with donor requirements, NRC standards, safeguarding principles and data protection protocols

**What you will bring**

- Master’s degree in law or social science or bachelor’s degree in law or social science (minimum); human rights or a related field is an asset.
- Project management Professional course and minimum 4 years of experience in a senior project management position in Libya.
- Experience in Protection and legal programming is an asset.
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities, including excelent project planning, team management and budget management (spending plans, budget monitoring, procurement planning).
- Experience in donor reporting and proposal development.
- Experience from working in complex and volatile contexts.
- Fluency in English and Arabic, both written and verbal; excellent drafting skills in both languages.
- Strong computer skills.

**Context-Specific Skills & Experience**

- Excellent knowledge of Libyan laws, regulations and administrative practices relevant to ICLA and PfV thematic areas.
- Knowledge of the context in West Libya, including displacement dynamics and the situation of refugees and migrants.
- Experience negotiating access and working with authorities and duty bearers in a restrictive operating environment.
- Experience in leadership roles and team management.
- Experience in protection programming, including Safe and Inclusive Programming, gender and protection mainstreaming; experience with integrated protection/PfV programming is an asset.
- Experience with M&E and outcome monitoring, and with handling sensitive personal and case data in line with data protection standards.
- Strong legal research and analytical skills; experience producing legal fact sheets, research or advocacy outputs.
- Experience with donor-funded projects and their compliance requirements.
- Strong training, facilitation and presentation skills, and experience creating team spirit and a peer-learning environment.
- Experience with digital legal information tools or platforms is an asset.

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAl6bfkFmEMSbDu6n-vybDeARUFC7Wa2BjYArYwJwVdmck?e=dFJHHY) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Libya (Tripoli or Misrata), covering operations in all West Libya.
- Contract: Fixed term, 12 months, renewable subject to funding and performance
- Travel: 30 to 40% within West Libya (Tripoli, Misrata, Tawergha and other mobile locations in West Libya), Tunisia where Country Office is established, and other location depending on programme needs and security clearance.
- Salary/benefits: Grade 8 on NRC's national grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- We invite applications from all qualified candidates matching the profile. ***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Libya, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV and cover letter.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

[Learn more about NRC Libya](https://www.nrc.no/countries/africa/libya)
