jobs.title: 23915 Protection Officer (Assisted Voluntary Return (AVR)) (P)
jobs.description:
IOM’s Approach to Protection promotes a coherent and accountable organizational role in safeguarding the rights of individuals across operational contexts. The IOM Mission in the Central African Republic (CAR) provides protection and assisted voluntary return support to vulnerable migrants, including third-country nationals, migrants in transit, and persons requiring post-arrival or return assistance.

Under the overall supervision of the Migration Protection Officer (P3) and the direct supervision of the Migration Protection Officer (P2), the Protection Officer (Assisted Voluntary Return (AVR)) will coordinate the day-to-day implementation of protection, case-management, and assisted voluntary return activities. The Protection Officer (AVR) will supervise a team of AVR/Protection Caseworkers and provide technical guidance to support safe, dignified, and needs-based assistance in accordance with IOM policies, informed consent, confidentiality, data-protection requirements, and the do-no-harm principle.

**Responsibilities**

1. Conduct and coordinate individual protection screenings and vulnerability assessments using IOM-approved tools; document needs and refer complex or high-risk cases to the supervisor.
2. Coordinate the day-to-day implementation of assisted voluntary return, post-arrival, and protection activities, including beneficiary information, informed consent, case follow-up, and pre-departure arrangements.
3. Supervise and guide AVR/Protection Caseworkers, distribute daily tasks, review case files for completeness, and escalate protection concerns or operational gaps to the supervisor.
4. Monitor accuracy and timeliness of case records in IOM-approved systems, including Migrant Management Operational System Application (MiMOSA) where applicable, in line with confidentiality, data-protection and information-sharing requirements.
5. Coordinate referrals to legal, health, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), child-protection, Gender-Based Violence (GBV), family-tracing, accommodation and other specialized services, and follow up on the continuity of assistance.
6. Assist with documentation and coordination with competent Central African authorities, diplomatic and consular representations, relevant IOM missions, immigration services, and service providers.
7. Maintain updated service mapping and referral pathways for protection and assisted voluntary return activities in CAR, identifying gaps in available services and suggesting corrective measures to the supervisor.
8. Provide clear, culturally sensitive, age-appropriate, and linguistically accessible information to beneficiaries regarding available assistance, procedures, rights, responsibilities, and feedback mechanisms.
9. Compile, analyse and provide operational updates, case summaries, statistics and periodic reports while protecting personally identifiable information.
10. Monitor implementation of activities against agreed workplans, indicators and service standards, and report implementation gaps to the supervisor.
11. Participate in local coordination activities, technical discussions and stakeholder meetings when requested by the supervisor.
12. Coordinate closely with protection, health, MHPSS, movements, logistics, accommodation and finance colleagues to facilitate timely assistance and resolve routine operational issues.
13. Undertake duty travel as required for field visits, airport movements, service monitoring, and liaison with counterparts.
14. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Social Sciences, International Relations/Affairs, Migration Studies, Research, Law, Human Rights, Psychology, Social Work, or a related field from an accredited academic institution; or,
- University degree in the above fields with two years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience supporting migrant protection, case management, assisted voluntary return, or related humanitarian or migration activities;
- Experience working with migrants in vulnerable situations and communicating with persons who have complex needs;
- Experience providing day-to-day guidance to support staff or case workers is desirable;
- Experience coordinating referrals with government services, UN agencies, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), diplomatic or consular representations and service providers;
- Experience with documentation, protection information management, monitoring or reporting is an advantage; and,
- Experience with IOM or another United Nations agency is desirable.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of basic IOM and inter-agency protection standards and case-management principles;
- Good organizational, coordination and problem-solving skills;
- Ability to supervise support staff, allocate tasks and review routine case documentation;
- Good written and verbal communication skills and ability to prepare clear case notes and operational updates;
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and digital case-management or reporting tools; knowledge of MiMOSA is an advantage;
- Demonstrated judgment, discretion and respect for confidentiality; and,
- Ability to work effectively with people from diverse cultural and professional backgrounds.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of Sango and other official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) or any relevant language in the Central African Region is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Consultance – Gestionnaire Technique de Projets d’Abri – Shelter Research Unit (SRU) – Afrique de l’Est (AE)
Head of Mission - Syria
jobs.description:
INTERSOS is an independent humanitarian organisation that assists the victims of natural disasters, armed conflicts and exclusion. Its activities are based on the principles of solidarity, justice, human dignity, equality of rights and opportunities, respect for diversity and coexistence, paying special attention to the most vulnerable people.

## **TERMS OF REFERENCE**

**Job Title:** Head of Mission

**Code:** SR-53-10265

**Duty station:** Damascus, Syria (with regular visits to field locations)

**Starting date:** 23/12/2026

**Contract duration:** 12 months

**Reporting to:** Regional Director

**Functional Supervisor:**

**Supervision of:** Mission SMT

**Type of Duty Station:** Non-family duty station

## **GENERAL DESCRIPTION OF THE CONTEXT**

Following the major political transition and the fall of the Assad regime in late 2024, Syria's humanitarian landscape in 2026 is characterized by massive returns of refugees and internally displaced persons. The international focus is shifting towards long-term recovery – albeit funds to support this recovery are slow to come. At the same time, the impact of over a decade of conflict, damaged economy, crippled infrastructure, and severe climate shocks makes Syria still one of the most complex humanitarian crises. This is coupled by a critical funding crisis with the humanitarian appeal only 20% funded.

Since 2019, INTERSOS has maintained a strategic presence across high-need areas in Syria, focusing on regions where infrastructure damage and displacement have severed civilian access to essential services. Currently, operations are centered in Rural Damascus, Hama, and Idlib governorates, with strategic plans underway to expand the response into southern areas. With established operational offices in Damascus and Hama, INTERSOS is well-positioned to address the massive influx of returnees, support the transition for local communities through integrated programming and fostering social cohesion, and reach underserved communities and the most vulnerable groups.

INTERSOS is currently implementing multi-sectoral programs funded by international donors such as ECHO, AICS, and Stichting Vluchteling (SV). The intervention strategy prioritizes Community-Based Mechanisms and an increased focus on localization. These interventions are designed to bridge the gap between emergency relief and early recovery across three primary sectors:

- Health: Supporting Primary Health Care Centers (PHCCs) through the provision of essential free medications, medical equipment, clinical staffing, and the rehabilitation of damaged clinics. This component includes operating Mobile Medical Teams (MMTs) and Mobile Health Units (MHUs) to extend integrated healthcare - including pediatric care, reproductive health, and chronic disease management - to remote and hard-to-reach communities.
- Protection: Running integrated protection programming across static centers and mobile teams. This includes specialized case management, psychosocial support (MHPSS), Gender-Based Violence (GBV) prevention, disability inclusion, comprehensive child protection programmes and cash for protection.
- Livelihoods: Integrating economic support by conducting labor market and socio-economic assessments to provide vocational training and small start-up grants to beneficiaries referred directly from the protection activities.

## **GENERAL PURPOSE OF THE POSITION**

The Head of Mission represents INTERSOS in the country and acts on behalf of the Director General, leading the organization’s response, including strategy design, planning resources, management and implementation of programs.

## **MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES AND TASKS**

**Strategy and vision**

- Is responsible for monitoring and analysing the political and humanitarian situation across the country and surrounding countries through established contacts and carrying out exploratory missions to identify potential fields of intervention. Design, propose, elaborate and develop new strategy of interventions in line with INTERSOS values and principles.
- Explore and present funding opportunities that integrate initiatives and leverage impact for the communities; support and direct fund-raising activities with institutional and private donors.
- Monitor donor’s priorities and intervention strategies in the country. Guarantee the strict observance and adherence to INTERSOS and donors’ procedures.
- Overview the development and implementation of projects and programs and through periodic visits to the areas of intervention, evaluate their evolution and quality as per internal and external standards and requirements, final results and achievements to ensure that organization’s technical and ethical standards are respected and objectives are achieved.
- Greenlight project proposals and response to emergencies to be submitted to HQ for approval. Evaluate potential emergency responses in the country and lead on developing additional programs in line with review and assessment results.
- Lead the detailed country strategy planning process and prioritising of actions and resources to achieve program objectives.

**Representation and advocacy**

- Represent the organisation and manage relations with the authorities ensuring smooth and timely implementation of planned interventions and safeguarding impartiality and independence.
- Follow up, guarantee and monitor government recognition procedures for the organisation in compliance with the host country formalities.
- Maintain a productive communication with donors and ensure that the assessed needs are communicated to impact on donors’ priorities.
- Represent INTERSOS in relevant fora.

**People management**

- Ensure that the senior management team is effective, mutually supporting and sufficiently involved in key decision-making processes.
- In coordination with the HR Coordinator, guide and supervise the staff performance process for international and national staff.
- Ensure the respect organisational values, Code of Ethics, Organization Management and Control Model, and INTERSOS procedures.
- Maintain high ethical standards and promote teamwork and ensure a productive working environment.
- Empower staff to meet organizational goals and work as a highly functioning and cooperative team.

**Finance, logistics and supply**

- Together with the Finance Coordinator, define and oversee the overall financial management of the mission, striving towards financial sustainability and assume responsibility for the mission funds management (NGO budget).
- Ensure that allocated resources are managed effectively and transparently.
- Together with the Logistics and Supply Coordinator, ensure that required and efficient supply services and processes are in place.

**Safety and security**

- Hold final accountability for security, including development and validation of country security plan and ensuring adherence to procedures, monitoring of the context development, analysis and provision of recommendations.
- Regularly interact with the Regional Office and the Security & Access Advisor on security issues (if available).
- Hold final responsibility for any decision concerning security in the country.

**Accountability and quality control**

- In collaboration with the SMT is responsible to produce and submit the mission monthly activity reports.
- Continuously assess, analyse and evaluate the impact of the country program and operations, also through periodic visits to the areas of intervention, in collaboration with the SMT.
- Ensure all the policies within INTERSOS Safeguarding Framework are respected by the staff
- Together with MEAL Department, supervise the effectiveness of a complaint feedback mechanism
- Oversee program quality and impact in line with established strategic objectives and related indicators.
- Oversee program reporting, ensuring compliance with INTERSOS policies and procedures, donor regulations and national requirements.

## **REQUIRED PROFILE AND EXPERIENCE**

### **Education**

- University degree Project management, International Affairs, Development, International Political Economy or other relevant field

### **Professional experience**

- Eight years experience in management positions in humanitarian contexts

### **Professional requirements**

- Experience with NGOs in humanitarian settings
- Experience with major humanitarian grants and international donors
- Experience of working within an insecure environment with responsibility for security planning, monitoring and management
- Essential computer literacy (MS office or equivalent, et alia)

### **Languages**

- English proficiency is essential
- Arabic knowledge is considered an advantage

### **Personal requirements**

- Strategic vision
- Good organizational and planning skills
- Leadership, team management and cooperation
- Behavioral flexibility
- Networking, negotiation skills and decision-making skills
- Diplomatic, interpersonal and good communication skills
- Ability to take initiative and work independently
- Strong analytical and practical problem-solving skills
- Commitment to INTERSOS principles

## **GENERAL CONDITIONS AND BENEFITS**

- **Salary range: 14 - 4.505€ - 5.182€ monthly gross**
- **Accommodation: Shared Guesthouse**
- **R&R:** 7 days of psycho-physical recovery every 12 weeks + 1000€ allowance.
- **Remuneration:** The monthly remuneration is defined, for each position, according to the standard salary grid and function grid, taking into account the experience of the selected candidate. It is communicated during the HR interview, or at any rate during the first stage of the selection process.
- **Transportation:** Round-trip flights for the humanitarian. For any mission lasting at least 9 months, an additional flight ticket to the Country of residence and return to the mission is covered by the Organisation for the humanitarian worker.
- **Medical insurance:** Injuries and death insurance; civil liability insurance; reimbursement for vaccines, medical certificate and PCR test for deployment; psychosocial support on request for the humanitarian worker.
- **Visa:** INTERSOS covers the costs and visa support for the humanitarian worker.
- **Annual Leave:** 2.5 days per month
- **Induction:** Online orientation course: each new staff member receives preparatory training before departure, adequate to provide the necessary information related to the structure of INTERSOS and the main decision-making processes and working tools, in order to facilitate entry into the Organisation.
- **Note 1:** INTERSOS applies a “Learning & Development Policy” which includes the possibility to receive capacitation and participate in internal and external training. Priority will be given to the staff working for INTERSOS for over two years.
- **Note 2:** The categorisation of Accompanied, RnR, and Unaccompanied Duty stations is subject to security criteria, access to health and education services, and is non-negotiable.

jobs.title: 24266 Regional Human Resources Business Partner (P)
jobs.description:
Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director (RD) and direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director (Management), and secondary reporting line to the Chief, Human Resources Business Partnering & Culture Division, and in coordination with relevant Units in Headquarters (HQ) and Administrative Centres, the Regional Human Resources Business Partner will be responsible and accountable for supporting, advising, guiding, and monitoring Human Resources (HR) related functions of the Country Offices (COs) within the Region. In addition, the Regional Human Resources Business Partner will also be responsible for the implementation of key HR processes in the Region and strengthening the HR Team's ability in the Region.

**Responsibilities**

1\. Policy Advice

- Advise staff and managers on HR policies, guidelines, and practices.
- Provide quality advice to develop innovative HR approaches and solutions to complex problems.
- Propose business cases and provide justifications for revising or drafting policies, as well as contribute to institutional policy reviews.
- Ensure the implementation of HR policies and practices by managers, HR Focal Points, and other non-HR staff involved in the implementation of HR policies and processes at the CO and RO level, providing timely advice, guidance, and ensuring follow-up as appropriate.

2\. Performance Management and Staff Development

- Manage the implementation of all corporate talent management programmes, while ensuring local relevance (performance appraisal system (PAS), succession planning, global mobility, staff development, etc.) and initiatives in the Region, working closely with other actors in the DHR, HQ and Administrative Centres.
- In collaboration with relevant managers, support leadership in strengthening the links between individual performance and delivery of strategic priorities, and effective management of underperformance.
- Advise staff on career development, and support managers in continuous capacity building and developing staff management capabilities.
- In collaboration with DHR/Occupational Health Unit/Staff Welfare, provide support on identifying and managing complex cases (e.g., performance, health, medevac and separations).
- Work directly with staff members in Regions and Country Offices on skill/learning needs assessments, and contribute to the design and implementation of customized learning interventions.
- Advise and support in the design and implementation of interventions to support organizational effectiveness and high-performing teams.
- Participate as a team member in HR projects, working groups, task forces, etc. within and outside the Region.
- Under the guidance of the Deputy Regional Director (Management) and Chief, HR Business Partnering & Culture Division, act as an integral member of the Regional Office Leadership Team, providing input on workforce planning, staffing trends and needs, implementation of HR initiatives/programs and current people issues/solutions.

3\. Planning and Analytics, and Workforce Management

- Use HR analytics proactively to understand the staffing trends in the Region.
- Advise and assist managers in analyzing staffing needs, taking into account existing and anticipated work requirements and institutional goals/objectives.
- Contribute to the development and implementation of the Annual Regional Plan (e.g., workforce analysis, recruitment, staff performance, staff development, career development and succession) in consultation with key stakeholders to support the delivery of IOM’s People Strategy.

4\. Organizational Design and Structures

- Advise and guide the Region’s managers to set up organizational structures to address the operational needs of and account for the complexity involved in accomplishing business objectives.
- Ensure and promote the use of Generic Position Descriptions to maintain consistency within and outside the region.
- Review classification requests before submission to HQ for evaluation and liaise with the Classification Team to assess the need for desk audit and to facilitate the process.

5\. Recruitment and Staffing

- Guide all recruitment activities of national and international staff, including high-level national posts at Country and Regional level, and provide advisory services as required.
- Guide Country Offices, as needed, on staffing matters.
- Advise on recruitment and administration of national and international Individual Consultants.
- Work with regional bodies, academic institutions, and Non-Governmental Organizations to identify sources of talent.
- Provide guidance and facilitate the induction, orientation, and integration of new staff members in the Region as needed; ensure staff exit interviews are conducted.
- Facilitate knowledge building and knowledge sharing in the Region through active participation in the HR community of practice.
- Contribute to building awareness and understanding of HR policies through knowledge sharing across the Region.
- Provide oversight and guidance to staff/team members on HR matters.

7\. Undertake Travel on Duty as necessary.

8\. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Business Administration, Human Resources, Law, Organizational Design, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience at International level managing complex human resources (HR) issues, in a multicultural setting; extensive operational and field experience in HR in the multilateral, hardship and international humanitarian and development context;
- Experience working in transformational HR projects with specialization in one or more HR disciplines, including recruitment, performance management, career development, administrative law, succession planning, training and staff development, or workforce analytics; and,
- Knowledge and experience in the Region with international organizations is advantageous.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of HR management concepts and practices in the various HR disciplines;
- Knowledge of UN HR rules, regulations and policies is an asset;
- Ability to position HR as a strategic business partner with multiple stakeholders; and,
- Ability to interpret and apply HR policy in a consistent and transparent manner.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Project Officer (Nationals Only)
jobs.description:
## Mission description

Expertise France is the French public agency for international technical cooperation and a subsidiary of the French Development Agency (AFD Group). It designs and implements projects that strengthen public policies in developing and emerging countries, in sectors such as governance, sustainable development, security, health and education.

The EU funds the “Green and Circular Economy (GCE) in the Southern Neighbourhood” programme, which promotes GCE as a driver of jobs and economic opportunity and supports the external dimension of the European Green Deal in the Mediterranean. It works at three levels: policy (macro), institutions (meso) and enterprises (micro).

Expertise France implements the policy (macro) component, GREEN FORWARD: a four-year project (January 2024 – December 2027) that supports sound, enforceable GCE policies and legislation in the Southern Neighbourhood through advocacy, peer exchange and stronger stakeholder collaboration. The project also promotes policy convergence on GCE with the EU framework and across the region.

The project aims to achieve two outcomes:

- Outcome 1: Regional public authorities share a common vision of inclusive GCE inspired by EU best practices.
- Outcome 2: Inclusive GCE principles, inspired by EU best practices, are mainstreamed in national policy and regulatory frameworks in the Southern Neighbourhood countries.

## Project or context description

The Green Forward Policy team is based in Amman, Jordan, and coordinates implementation across the region. The team includes the Project Manager, the Deputy Project Manager (Implementing Expert), Project Officers, a Project Assistant, a Communication Officer and a Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Coordinator, supported by country experts. Government engagement is organised through designated focal points and nationally established task forces and/or committees.

Based in Amman, the Project Officer coordinates project activities in Libya, Morocco, Egypt and Tunisia. The post reports to the line manager and works under the guidance of the Project Manager and the Deputy Project Manager (Implementing Expert).

The role combines operational coordination (work plans, expert contracts, events, reporting) with technical review of expert outputs. You will work with the Middle East Project Officer, the Project Assistant and Expertise France’s (USP).

The current country portfolio covers the following countries and focus areas:

- Libya: development and follow-up of a system for monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) of industrial greenhouse-gas emissions, focusing on the iron and steel sector.
- Morocco: policy and regulatory support for implementing the circular economy roadmap for the automotive sector
- Egypt: policy and regulatory support for the green transition of the automotive and electrical/electronics industries, including carbon accounting, MRV and readiness for EU market requirements.
- Tunisia: policy and regulatory support for food-waste prevention and organic-waste recovery in the hospitality sector, including technical, legal and green-financing recommendations.

I.Key Responsibilities

The main responsibilities of the Project Officer are as follows:

1\. Expert Coordination & Deliverable Management

- Liaise with government focal points and national task forces or committees to obtain feedback, organise consultations and follow up on validation steps agreed with project management.
- Act as day-to-day focal point for country experts: hold regular coordination meetings (typically weekly), record agreed actions, keep work plans and deliverable trackers up to date, and flag delays and risks early with proposed solutions.
- Track expert deliverables against ToRs and work plans; check completeness, consistency and relevance; give first-level technical feedback; and coordinate specialist review before validation by the Project Manager and the Deputy Project Manager (Implementing Expert).

2\. Activity Implementation & Logistics

- Plan and deliver capacity-building activities and workshops in the assigned countries (concept notes, agendas, participants, venues, travel), coordinating expert inputs, government participation and logistics, with the Project Assistant and USP.
- Collect and verify attendance records and financial supporting documents after each activity, and follow up reimbursements through to financial closure with the finance team.

3\. Contracts, Procurement & Payments

- Prepare procurement files (ToRs, specifications, budget estimates) and expert contract requests with USP, and plan lead times from the country work plans.
- Check that payment requests carry the required documents and the written approval of deliverables before submission to finance.
- Track commitments, expenditure and payment status for country activities and expert contracts, check that files are complete, and flag bottlenecks.

4\. Monitoring, Reporting & Communication

- Support the MEAL Coordinator in collecting quantitative and qualitative data (surveys, feedback forms, pre/post assessments) during and after activities for the indicator tracking table.
- Support the MEAL Coordinator in updating project indicators and results in OPSYS (the EU’s monitoring and reporting platform), twice a year or as requested.
- Prepare country updates and contribute to quarterly, semi-annual and annual reports, including the EU annual review.
- Provide technical inputs and expert availability for communication activities led by the Communication Officer.

5\. Team & Cross-Cutting Support

- Work with the Middle East Project Officer to keep tools and practices consistent and cover each other’s portfolios when needed.
- Apply donor rules and Expertise France procedures and keep complete project records (work plans, approvals, procurement and payment files).
- Contribute to other tasks aligned with project objectives, including support to other countries in the portfolio.

II.Expected Results

Success in this role means:

- Country work plans and deliverable trackers are up to date.
- Expert deliverables are validated on schedule.
- Payment requests are complete at first submission.
- Planned activities are delivered with closed financial files.
- Indicators are entered in OPSYS on time.
- Country inputs are delivered for each quarterly, semi-annual and annual report.

## Required profile

1\. Qualifications and Skills

- Bachelor’s degree (Master’s degree is an asset) in environmental sciences, sustainability, public policy, economics, engineering, international relations or a related field.
- Advanced Excel and MS Office skills for work plans, trackers and expenditure follow-up.
- Fluent English and Arabic (written and spoken) (C1 or equivalent). French (B2 or higher) is highly desirable.
- Understanding of green and circular economy, climate or environmental policy sufficient to review technical reports and turn findings into follow-up actions.

2\. Specific Professional Experience

- At least 5 years’ experience in project coordination or management in international development or technical cooperation.
- Demonstrated experience coordinating consultants or experts and tracking deliverables, including follow-up with government counterparts.
- Experience organising workshops or capacity-building activities, including logistics and financial follow-up.
- Practical experience preparing procurement documentation, following up contracts and compiling payment files.
- Working knowledge of donor-funded project rules, ideally EU-funded (procurement, eligibility, reporting).

3\. Desirable Qualifications

- Familiarity with MEAL tracking systems, online survey tools (e.g., KoboToolbox, SurveyMonkey), or EU reporting platforms (e.g., OPSYS).
- Professional experience in circular economy, MRV/carbon accounting or industrial policy.
- Experience organising activities across several countries.

4\. Interpersonal and Soft Skills

- Organised and accurate; able to manage several country work plans at once.
- Clear written and spoken communication, diplomacy with experts, government focal points and senior stakeholders.
- Comfortable in a multicultural, multi-country setting.

## Additional information

I.Practical Information

Application Documents

- Resume
- Cover letter, in English
- Contact details of three professional references will be requested only from shortlisted candidates

.

Additional Information

- Salary: according to the Expertise France salary scale, based on profile
- Work modality: on site
- Application opening date: 24th of November 2026
- Application deadline: 3rd of December 2026, 23:59

Selection Process

- Applications will be screened against the criteria above. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an interview.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

**Deadline for application : 2026/12/03 23:55**

jobs.title: Procurement Team Leader
jobs.description:
## **MSF Eastern Africa is looking for a Procurement Team Leader**

*Do your skills and experience not precisely match the requirements? At MSF EA, we strive to create a safe, diverse and inclusive workplace, recognising the need to increase access to professional opportunities for historically underrepresented groups. If you're interested in this position but your experience doesn't align perfectly with the selection criteria, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the ideal candidate for this or other positions.*

*Firmly committed to safeguarding patients, community members, staff, and all those in contact with the organisation from all forms of abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), we will take all necessary steps, through rigorous vetting processes, to ensure that confirmed perpetrators of abuse do not join the organization.*

*For this position, contact level with patients and children is categorized as **Low** risk and will be monitored with this in regard.*

## ***Introduction***

Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) is an international independent medical humanitarian organisation that provides assistance to people affected by conflicts, epidemics, and natural or human-made disasters and excluded from healthcare. We provide this assistance without discrimination, irrespective of race, religion, creed or political affiliation.

## ***About MSF Eastern Africa***

MSF Eastern Africa (MSF EA) is the regional institutional office of MSF. It focuses on representation and networking, recruiting and supporting staff from the region, communications and fundraising, as well as working on other dossiers of importance to MSF such as Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI), Data Protection, mutualization, training, medical operational support and environmental health.

## ***Rationale/Objective for Position***

The Procurement Team Leader is responsible for strengthening and overseeing procurement systems, governance, and performance within MSF Eastern Africa (MSF EA), ensuring efficient, transparent, compliant, and value-driven procurement practices aligned with operational needs and organizational priorities. The job holder also plays a key role in structuring procurement practices through the development of policies, SOPs, tools, performance monitoring systems, and stakeholder coordination mechanisms; contributing to procurement compliance, audit readiness, strategic sourcing, supplier management, and continuous improvement initiatives, including ERP-related procurement processes. The position leads procurement planning, sourcing pipelines, spend management, tender governance, and contract and supplier lifecycles within delegated authority and defined decision rights; manages risks, business continuity, performance, stakeholder services and team development; and strengthens digital procurement, data quality and responsible sourcing to deliver value, compliance, accountability and support across MSF Eastern Africa.

This position will be **hierarchically** and **functionally** accountable to **Head of Logistics.**

## ***Tasks & Responsibilities***

**Strategic Responsibilities**

- Develop and implement procurement strategies aligned with the MSF EA strategic plan and SPARC priorities (SP 2026–2031) and Annual Plans.
- Oversee compliance of the procurement unit with implementation of the SP 2026–2031.
- Oversee compliance and implementation of the procurement unit’s commitments under SP 2026–2031 and approved Annual/multi-year Plans aligning resources and delivery with organisational priorities.
- Oversee planned deliverables, procurement planning, spending visibility, tender compliance, contract renewals, supplier performance, service standards and corrective-action closure.

**Technical and Operational Responsibilities**

***Procurement Management***

- Oversee quality end-to-end procurement and purchasing processes, from requisition through delivery and contract closure, ensuring activities are implemented in line with approved procedures and delegated authorities.
- Lead procurement planning and develop a roadmap in coordination with different departments.
- Lead the annual/multi-year procurement planning cycle, consolidate departmental demand, maintain the sourcing pipeline and procurement roadmap, and align team capacity with business priorities and required lead times.
- Ensure timely procurement of quality goods and services aligned with entity needs and priorities.
- Ensure fair, transparent and well-documented competitive tendering and management, including appropriate committee composition, conflict-of-interest declarations, integrity of technical and financial evaluations, award documentation and audit trail.
- Review procurement requests and documentation quality; identify delays, risks, overdue contracts, and supplier management issues, and provide findings, recommendations, and corrective measures for improvement and risk mitigation.
- Provide strategic sourcing oversight and escalation handling for complex or high-risk procurement cases.
- Own the procurement KPI framework, tools and management dashboard.
- Conduct regular procurement performance reviews, tools, and reporting management and track corrective actions closure.
- Contract drafting in collaboration with the Legal department, renewals, and performance tracking.
- Establish contract lifecycle governance from sourcing strategy and negotiation, approval and validation requirements.
- Draft supplier contract or framework agreements and in collaboration with the Legal department, process, performance monitoring, and tracking renewal or extension/modifications and closure.
- Develop and implement mutualization efforts of MSF entities in Nairobi.

***Supplier & Market Management***

- Ensure market analysis, supplier mapping, and database management to support informed sourcing decisions.
- Promote framework agreements and long-term supplier relationships.
- Where aligned with MSF policies, integrate responsible sourcing, environmental considerations, supplier ethics and proportionate local-market development into sourcing decisions.
- Govern supplier onboarding, prequalification, due diligence, segmentation, performance reviews and corrective actions; manage strategic supplier relationships and ensure suspension or exit decisions follow approved procedures and delegated authority.

***Compliance & Risk Management***

- Ensure adherence to organizational policies, applicable donor requirements, and procurement threshold standards. Own the implementation and monitoring of the approved procurement Delegation of Authority; ensure sourcing methods, approvals, award decisions, exceptions and contract commitments follow authorized thresholds and segregation-of-duties requirements.
- Strengthen procurement internal controls, learning, documentation standards, and compliance practices.
- Maintain the procurement risk register and document lessons learned and good practice.
- Assess supply-market, supplier concentration, fraud, corruption, compliance and business continuity risks.
- Maintain alternative source strategies for critical categories and escalate risks requiring management decisions.
- Lead audit preparations and oversee implementation of audit recommendations, including tracking systems for regular monitoring of audit findings and corrective actions.

***Policy, Systems & Process Improvement***

- Develop, review/update, and enforce procurement policies, SOPs, and governance frameworks to reflect operational realities, needs, and complexities; act as custodian of policy, thresholds, and governance.
- Conduct an annual rapid assessment of procurement workflows, staffing, controls, backlog, and service bottlenecks, and provide strategic recommendations.
- Act as procurement process owner for ERP and e-procurement workflows, procurement master data, analytics and controls in coordination with ICT and Finance.
- Lead user acceptance testing, including test criteria and procurement sign-off, system optimization and user adoption. and address workflow gaps and end-user challenges.
- Continuously improve and standardize procurement processes to enhance efficiency, consistency, and service delivery.

***Leadership and Advisory***

- Provide strategic procurement advice to senior management through spend analysis, category strategies and executive reporting.
- Maintain visibility over spend/under spend management, identifying savings and cost-avoidance opportunities and report realized value using methodologies agreed with Finance.
- Define procurement service standards, requester responsibilities, escalation pathways and periodic stakeholder feedback mechanisms; ensure effective coordination across departments.
- Drive mutualization and collaboration initiatives across MSF EA, Ubuntu, and MSF entities in Nairobi, where relevant.

**Other Responsibilities**

- Lead procurement team planning, including structure, staffing needs, workload allocation, capability development and succession planning.
- Supervise and mentor staff and provide training on procurement standards, procedures and tools.
- Set team and individual objectives, monitor procurement staff performance and conduct timely performance reviews; recognize & motivate strong performance, address gaps and follow up agreed development actions.
- Integrate EDI & Safeguarding aspects in area of work responsibility, including policies and practices.
- Recognize, respond, and document any form of abuse or inappropriate behavior and alert the safeguarding unit of any suspected potential abuse.
- Proactively participate in the individual performance management process including objective setting, performance monitoring and performance evaluation.
- Recognize and reinforce strong performance in supervisees; identify and encourage improvement where needed; and ensure quality and timely performance management process is carried out for supervisees.

***Qualifications***

**Education**

- A bachelor’s degree in Procurement, supply or related field from a recognized institution.
- Fluency in English is required, and knowledge of French and a third language is an added advantage.

**Experience**

- A minimum of seven (7) years of progressively responsible procurement or supply chain experience, including at least 3–5 years in a procurement leadership or management role with direct responsibility for staff and procurement performance.
- Experience with ERP and e-procurement workflows, procurement analytics, database tools and data-driven performance management.
- Demonstrated experience in market analysis, strategic sourcing, supplier management and negotiations, framework agreements and contract lifecycle management.
- Demonstrated experience applying procurement policies, thresholds and internal controls, maintaining audit readiness and following up corrective actions.
- Experience with supplier due diligence, supplier performance management and procurement risk management.
- Strong experience in spend analysis, category strategy, sourcing pipeline management and executive reporting, including procurement advice to senior management.
- Experience in an INGO, humanitarian, regional, and ability to drive mutualization and collaboration across MSF Entities or multi-entity environment is desirable (including shared procurement services and collaboration).

**Competencies**

- **Technical**
- Advanced knowledge of procurement governance, sourcing, contracting, supplier management, risk and controls
- **Behavioral/General Competencies**
- Detail-oriented with a high level of accuracy.
- Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills.
- Acts as a team player and facilitates teamwork.
- Articulate, with good communication skills.
- Ability to communicate and problem-solve effectively across diverse cultures with sensitivity.
- Commitment to MSF's Principles.
- Service orientation.
- Ethics: High ethical standards and a commitment to protecting the data of individuals and furthering MSF mandate.

***Conditions and Benefits:***

- **Job Location**: MSF Eastern Africa office in Nairobi (Kenya),
- **Contract**: Full time, 3-year contract, renewable.
- **Start date**: As Soon As Possible.
- **Salary:** An annual salary of **EUR 27,145 at HQ Grade 8** based on a full-time appointment with an annual increment of 2% every year up to a maximum of 10 years.
- **Work-life balance financial benefit;** ranging between **EUR 620 to 1,159/month** based on individual & administrative status. This amount may be used to cover accommodation and utilities, transportation, etc.
- **Other benefits include;**
- **Annual Leave:** 25 days of annual leave per year.
- **Other Holidays:** sick leave, circumstantial leave, maternity leave (21 weeks), paternity leave (4 weeks), own affairs days off, etc.
- **Employer Pension contribution**: 10% of basic salary:
- **International insurance** for both medical and disability.
- **Relocation support**; based on MSF EA terms/conditions.
- **Work-life balance**: Daily flexi-hours and 2 days working from home possible.
- **School fees benefits**: for eligible dependents, based on individual & administrative status.
- **Diverse team composition**; Collaborate with a global network of talented professionals, bringing diverse perspectives and expertise from around the world.
- **Career Development**: MSF provides many learning resources (online learning resources, regular trainings – including language, Peer to peer learning.
- **Mobility**: You will have opportunities to travel abroad for work, meetings, trainings and workshops; giving you a chance to experience different cultures and broaden your professional network.
- **Annual home leave ticket**: To be taken once every year for both staff and eligible dependents back to their home country for vacation. Only applicable to non-Kenyans and based on individual & administrative status.

jobs.title: Protection from Violence (PFV) Project Manager North-East Syria
jobs.description:
**Background**

As the Syrian crisis has entered its 15th year, a record-level 16.7 million people, over 71% of the population, is in need of humanitarian assistance. Almost half are children. The fall of the former government, in December 2024, has sparked hope for the country’s future and those in need of aid. However, ongoing conflict, economic collapse and record-high humanitarian needs persist throughout the country, coinciding with unprecedented cuts to humanitarian aid globally at a time where aid resources for Syria were already stretched thin.

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has been a leading humanitarian actor in the response to the Syria crisis, in Syria and across the region, since 2012. Against a backdrop of conflict, socioeconomic and environmental deterioration, climate change and natural disasters, we provide emergency, transitional, early recovery and resilience programmes to people in need. We lead advocacy to promote unimpeded and sustained access to assistance for people across Syria and we call for increased humanitarian funding, resilience and early recovery support to alleviate the hardships of the Syrian people.

**What we are looking for**

A dynamic, motivated **Protection from Violence Project Manager** who will be tasked with implementing Protection programming in **Northeast Syria** ensuring high-quality, accountable and timely delivery of protection assistance.

The PfV programme encompasses Individual Response Services (IRS), including general protection case management and Individual Protection Assistance (IPA), Civilian Self-Protection (CSP), and Protection Monitoring and Analysis.

If you are a passionate, seasoned professional with extensive experience in humanitarian project management, budget management, protection case management & monitoring, staff supervision and operational coordination, this is the role for you!

**\*\*\*\*\*Please note for this role, applicants must be legally eligible to work in Syria. We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position. \*\***

**What you will do**

**The role will have some of the following specific responsibilities:**

- Project Management & Reporting.
- Individual Response Services (IRS).
- Civilian Self-Protection.
- Protection Monitoring & Analysis.
- Coordination & Advocacy.

Please download the [detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAtNVVe61OLQ4aqADdJ66nmAbXC0a3tEYUlW3GWWpeLRDg?e=84QbMV) to learn more about the position.

**What you will bring**

- **Minimum 3 years of experience** in a senior-level project implementation position in a humanitarian/recovery context.
- Experience from working in **complex and volatile contexts.**

jobs.title: Donor Relations Manager "Climate Resilience"
jobs.description:
The position is to be filled as soon as possible, with a contract duration until December 31, 2027. There are prospects for a contract extension. Employment location will be Bonn, Germany.

As Donor Relations Manager “Climate Resilience” you will be part of the Institutional Donor Relations Unit contributing to secure and expand institutional funding in the field of climate resilience. You will be the key contact of Welthungerhilfe for institutional donors in the field of climate resilience developing strategic cooperations and partnerships. Through your work, you will enhance Welthungerhilfe's profile and visibility as a key player in humanitarian aid and development cooperation.

## Your responsibilities

- Develop and implement a strategy on respective donors with a focus on climate resilience within the institutional donor strategy framework
- Coordinate the application process and ensure that applications and reports are submitted to the respective donor with high quality and in accordance with donor guidelines
- Assist in the development of climate resilience funding at Unit- and Country Office level
- Participate in donor conferences and in relevant networks of the respective donor in the field of climate resilience
- Prepare, support and conduct (high-level) donor visits relevant for climate resilience
- Analyze, interpret and process information and relevant policies and trends of the respective donor
- Identify new funding opportunities in the area of climate resilience
- Advocate for optimizing donor terms and conditions

## Your profile

- A university or college degree in the field of social sciences, development policy, international relations or a comparable degree
- At least 5 years of relevant professional experience in international development cooperation
- Experience in planning and implementing development cooperation initiatives
- Proven experience in acquisition of project funds for NGO led projects for climate resilience and adaptation to and mitigation of climate change
- Extensive knowledge about institutional donors in the field of climate resilience, e.g. IKI, Darwin Initiative, multilateral climatefonds (Green Climate Fund, Adaptation Fund), development banks
- Strong negotiation and cooperation skills, ability to work in a team, strong communication skills and stress resistance
- Strong text production and report writing skills
- Awareness of the growing importance of data in your field and willingness to apply your skills to incorporate data-informed approaches into your work
- Very good ability to work in an intercultural environment and willingness to travel outside of Europe
- Very good written and spoken English skills; German and/or French language skills are an advantage

## Our offer

We offer you the opportunity to work in a responsible and interesting field as part of an extremely dedicated team. Welthungerhilfe attaches great importance to the personal and professional development of its employees and the balance of their work and private life. This includes flexible working hours as well as working from home. Remuneration is based on our gender-independent salary scale. In addition, Welthungerhilfe offers numerous other benefits, which are listed under ["Our benefits"](https://www.welthungerhilfe.org/benefits-for-employees-in-germany/).

*\*Welthungerhilfe values diversity and ensures an inclusive, non-discriminatory working environment. We welcome applications from suitably qualified people from all sections of the community.*

jobs.title: Consultant - Inception Review and Strategic Retreat, Gulf of Guinea Program
jobs.company: Geneva Centre for Security Sector Governance
jobs.description:
At DCAF, we envision a world where democratic sector governance advances sustainable peace and development and human dignity for all.

Our mission is to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices.

DCAF contributes to making peace and development more sustainable by assisting partner states and international actors supporting these states, to improve the governance of their security sector through inclusive and participatory reforms. It creates innovative knowledge products, promotes norms and good practices, provides legal and policy advice and supports capacity‐building of both state and non‐state security sector stakeholders.

**External Consultant – Inception Review and Strategic Retreat, Gulf of Guinea Program**

**Workplace: Geneva, Switzerland**

**Contract type: Freelance / Consultancy**

**Expected start date: December 2026 / January 2027 (TBC)**

**Estimated level of effort: 10 working days**

**Duration: December 2026 – January 2027**

**The role**

DCAF’s Africa and Americas Entity is seeking an external consultant to review the strategic direction and coherence of its Gulf of Guinea regional security sector governance program and facilitate strategic working sessions in Geneva. The assignment will help clarify priorities, identify feasible adjustments to the 2027 workplan and develop a strategic roadmap, learning agenda and recommendations on delivery arrangements. It is not an external evaluation or a new program design exercise.

**Your profile**

- Strong experience in strategic planning, program review and design in international cooperation.
- Proven ability to facilitate participatory, decision-oriented discussions, challenge assumptions constructively and translate strategic choices into practical plans.
- Understanding of politically informed programming, adaptive management and donor-funded implementation constraints.
- Excellent facilitation and drafting skills in English; ability to work with English- and French-speaking participants.

Strong assets

- Experience in security sector governance and reform (SSG/R) and knowledge of West Africa and the Gulf of Guinea.

Applications from individual consultants or small teams combining complementary expertise are welcome.

For further information on the scope of work, deliverables and timeline, **please refer to the** [**Terms of Reference**](https://ats.johdisuite.ch/storage/offers/1ovdMfUIX9MkQUZ4A9Fwp7AKAs0p7e0DZl0innXc.pdf) available here.

jobs.title: WASH Portfolio Manager
jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As WASH Portfolio Manager, you will provide overall leadership, technical direction and management of World Vision PNG’s WASH Technical Program. You will serve as the primary contact for the donor and key WASH stakeholders, lead senior staff in delivering grant activities and ensure effective implementation, risk management and sustainable outcomes that improve child well-being.

You will set the strategic direction of the WASH program, oversee grant implementation and quality assurance, align activities with the World Vision PNG Strategic Framework, develop a sustainable strategy that attracts donor funding, and address grant management issues promptly.

You will work with the Program Quality Manager to maintain effective monitoring and evaluation systems, collect and analyse performance data, report against standard indicators, and use evidence to guide programme decisions and improvements.

You will supervise senior national and international staff, strengthen their capacity to manage complex donor-funded projects, oversee grant staff and consultants, and provide WASH technical training as required.

You will manage the grant budget within approved limits, ensure accurate and timely financial reporting, and monitor expenditure for proper allocation and compliance with donor requirements, financial standards and audit requirements.

You will manage donor relationships with the Operations Director, build partnerships with government, NGOs, UN agencies and other stakeholders, represent World Vision in key meetings and technical cluster forums, and lead the management of the WASH Cluster.

**Requirements include:**

- A Master’s degree in Water Engineering or Civil Engineering.
- At least eight years of experience in international development, including five years at management level on medium- to large-scale grant-funded projects.
- Demonstrated experience leading WASH programs.
- Strong knowledge of WASH issues and challenges in Papua New Guinea.
- Proven ability to manage programs in complex political and cultural settings.
- Experience coordinating teams across multiple locations.
- A current driver’s licence and the ability to drive.
- A demonstrated track record of leading technical teams and building trust within diverse teams.
- Knowledge of donor policies and requirements, particularly those of DFAT, UNICEF and the World Bank.
- Willingness to travel to implementation sites and within the region as required.
- Willingness to work in challenging security environments in accordance with World Vision’s security policies and procedures.

jobs.description:

The HR Manager will provide generalist and operational HR support, ensuring the development of a highly effective recruitment function within the Syria Country Office. This role is responsible for ensuring that the organization attracts, retains, and develops the right talent to achieve program goals and effectively serve beneficiaries. The HR Manager will oversee the implementation of key HR services, policies, and infrastructure in alignment with the SCI Syria Country Office Well-being Action Plan.
Additionally, the HR Manager will lead efforts to enhance employee relations, manage safeguarding-related incidents, and support a positive and compliant work environment. This role will also track training initiatives, monitor HR scorecards, and drive performance management to optimize staffing, improve work efficiency, and mitigate institutional risks.

jobs.title: Senior Project Officer (MEAL), Syria
jobs.description:
**"This is a domestic hire, expected to be based in Syria, and we will only hire nationals or candidates who have the independent legal right to work in this country."**

**About CRS:**

CRS is an international humanitarian and development agency working to *save, protect, and transform* lives in need in more than 100 countries, without regard to race, religion or nationality. CRS’ relief and development work is accomplished through programs of emergency response, health, agriculture, education, microfinance and peacebuilding.

**Job summary**

Lead the design and implementation MEAL activities in conjunction with the program team and MEAL manager including system design, tools development, timely collection of quality data, regular monitoring of project interventions using CRS standards for results measurement, and facilitation of participatory reflection on monitoring results and preparation of progress reports. Generate evidence through relevant quantitative/qualitative studies to measure effectiveness of projects. Maintain responsibility of accountability to the affected population, donors/partners and CRS.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities:**

- Lead coordination and implementation of all assigned project activities as outlined in the detailed implementation plan in line with CRS program quality principles and standards, MEAL Procedures and Policy, donor requirements, and good practices.
- Liaise with various community stakeholders and mobilize them to ensure full involvement of community members and leaders in the overall implementation and improvement of project MEAL activities.
- Lead the design of the project’s MEAL system to jointly establish a monitoring framework aligned with the project’s theory of change, that incorporates both formal and informal monitoring methods.
- Develop routine monitoring of interventions to track output level achievements and behavior change at the intermediate result level using qualitative and quantitative approaches.
- Monitor and report any challenges and/or gaps identified to inform adjustments to plans and implementation schedules. Assist partners in their efforts to reflect on project experiences.
- Coordinate and support capacity-strengthening and technical assistance activities to ensure assigned project activities are implemented in accordance with established guidelines and quality standards.
- Support partners to maintain a simple but robust database for quantitative monitoring data and develop systems for strategically capturing qualitative changes
- Organize quarterly reflection sessions with CRS and partner staff to joint review of monitoring findings and rapid learning to guide adaptive management.
- Conduct Annual Data Quality Assessments (DQAs) to verify data accuracy, reliability, and timeliness and strengthen partner capacity.
- Identify key learning questions related to key program areas including but not limited to protection, livelihoods, social cohesion, climate resilience, and disaster risk reduction, and develop a project learning agenda in collaboration with project team
- Ensure learning properly accompanies project activities throughout the project cycle. Support the development of learning products such as briefs, case studies, and success stories, that can be used in reports, donor briefings, external coordination structures
- Coordinate the implementation of monitoring and accountability activities and processes (including ICT4MEAL) according to the Detailed Implementation Plan and MEAL systems of each project. Ensure the quality of monitoring data through annual data quality assessments. Support active seeking and responding to feedback from all members of targeted communities and other stakeholders.

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor's Degree required. Degree in public health, Statistics, Data Sciences, or a similar field would be a plus.
- Minimum of 5 years of relevant work experience in MEAL, ideally with an international NGO.
- Experience designing MEAL frameworks and tools for emergency, recovery and/or development projects
- Experience using DCED standards for private sector development an advantage
- Experience using KoBoToolbox, CommCare, and Power BI.
- Experience analyzing quantitative and qualitative data.
- Experience using MS Windows and MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, OneDrive, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams (including Microsoft Forms).

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Experience in participatory action planning and community engagement.

jobs.description:
Tearfund is looking for a Regional **Proposal Development Officer** for its East & Central Africa (ECA) Region to play a vital role in our mission of following Jesus where the need is greatest, responding to crises, and partnering with local churches to bring restoration to those living in poverty.

The Regional **Proposal Development Officer** is responsible for providing hands-on capacity to six Country Programmes—Burundi, Rwanda, DRC, CAR, South Sudan, and Ethiopia—to develop high-quality, competitive proposals for institutional donors, foundations, and private companies, as well as multi-country proposals. Based in any of the six ECA countries, the post holder works closely with country and regional teams to ensure countries' funding plans are fulfilled. They are accountable for devising effective donor engagement mechanisms to attract potential donors, enhancing the visibility of Tearfund's work, and independently writing winning proposals that translate field insights into evidence-based, innovative interventions.

**Key accountabilities, among others, include:**

- Lead the end-to-end development, drafting, and submission of high-quality, competitive proposals and unsolicited concept notes for institutional donors, trusts, and foundations in close collaboration with country and regional teams.
- Facilitate and coordinate the proposal design process across the entire proposal writing lifecycle, managing timelines and embedding past project learnings and emerging sector trends into narratives.
- Support the development and implementation of agreed strategies for securing and managing institutional funding, ensuring funding streams are identified and pursued to satisfy Country Funding Plans.
- Support the development of Country and Regional donor funding pipelines aligned to strategic priorities, working closely with DMEAL and communications teams to build strong pitches for potential donors.
- Network with other grant-receiving agencies to share learning, understand donor intelligence, and identify potential areas of collaboration.
- Provide capacity-building training, support, and practical coaching to Tearfund regional and country staff, fundraising leads, and partners on proposal preparation, programme delivery, and compliance.

**To be successful, you'll need the following:**

- Degree and/or equivalent qualification in a humanitarian, development, or management-related discipline (a relevant post-graduate qualification is desirable).
- Proven ability in securing funding and managing relationships with major institutional donors (such as USG, FCDO, UN entities, or the European Commission).
- Extensive experience in needs assessment, project design, **proposal development**, reporting, and writing winning multi-year proposals for development and emergency grants.
- Experience identifying, setting up, and managing consortia, as well as collaborating with finance teams to develop aligned, competitive budgets and budget narratives.
- Familiarity with major donor grant portals (e.g., UN Partner Portal, Grants.gov, European Commission's PROSPECT/SEDIA, FCDO systems).
- Fluent in written and spoken English, with excellent analytical, verbal, and written communication skills.
- Experience working in sectors relevant to Tearfund's strategy (such as Food Security, WASH, peacebuilding, climate action, or livelihoods) and managing US government funding is desirable.
- Willingness and ability to travel regularly across the regional countries.

If the above describes you, we would love to hear from you. Please find the Job Description attached.

**Note:**

Tearfund is committed to promoting gender equality and encourages applications from qualified women and men, including those with disabilities. Tearfund is committed to promoting gender equality and ensuring the protection of all individuals, particularly the most vulnerable. We actively encourage applications from qualified women and men, including those with disabilities, and strive to create a work environment where everyone feels safe, respected, and empowered to contribute.

Applicants must be committed to Tearfund's Christian beliefs. The recruitment process will include specific checks related to safeguarding issues (including a DBS/Police check and screening under the SCHR Misconduct Disclosure Scheme). In addition, personal identification information will be submitted to a watchlist database to check against criminal convictions as a counter-terrorism measure.

jobs.title: Annual Audit Assasuni Upazila, Bangladesh
jobs.description:
**Organisation**

Hoffnungszeichen | Sign of Hope e.V.

[www.hoffnungszeichen.de](http://www.hoffnungszeichen.de), [www.sign-of-hope.org](http://www.sign-of-hope.org)

**Position**

Auditor

**Type of Contract**

Short-term consultancy

**Type of Audit**

In depth

**Location**

Home-based with field mission travel to Assasuni Upazila, Bangladesh

**Languages Required**

English, Bengali

**Application Deadline**

10.12.2026

**Starting Date**

11.01.2027

**Auditing Period**

From 01.08.2026 to 31.12.2026

**Project Title**

Increasing resilience through climate change adaptation and sustainable livelihoods in Assasuni Upazila, Satkhira, Bangladesh.

**Total Project Budget**

464,000 EURO

**Annual Project Budget**

109,500 EURO

Hoffnungszeichen | Sign of Hope e.V. (SoH) is announcing **an open tender procedure for external independent financial audit services in Bangladesh.**

**Background and Organisational Setting**

SoH is a Christian motivated organisation for Human Rights, Humanitarian Assistance and Development Cooperation. Based in Constance, Germany, SoH is dedicated to helping those in distress and exploited people worldwide.

An audit is commissioned under the German Federal Ministry of Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) funding guidelines for development projects run by private German executing agencies.

SoH will be the private German executing agency and the contracting party, with Bangladesh Nazarene Mission (BNM)being the local implementing agency.

Strengthening livelihoods and supporting sustainable socio-economic development in highly disaster-prone and vulnerable communities in southern Bangladesh. By revitalizing disaster management committees and providing targeted training to community members for emergency situations, their vulnerability is reduced, and faster recovery from shocks is enabled. The establishment of self-help and farmer groups forms a central component of the project, aimed at enhancing local skills and promoting community initiative. Capacity building is achieved through climate-resilient adaptation of existing livelihoods, strengthening resilience against natural hazards, increasing agricultural productivity through modern technology, and diversifying income- generating activities. In addition, awareness-raising activities on hygiene and health are implemented, alongside training on balanced nutrition, to reduce the communities' susceptibility to disease. Furthermore, communities are supported in environmental protection measures that aim to make their surroundings more climate-resilient and overall safer.

**Audit Objectives**

The purpose of the in-depth audit is to provide SoH with a sound basis for its accountability, transparency and accuracy in the financial disclosure towards the funding agency BMZ. The tasks of this recruitment relate to:

- An annual audit, with a detailed examination of all the supporting documents for the period of 01.08.2026 – 31.12.2026;

This in-depth audit will verify the compliance with standards of the funding agency BMZ, SoH, national regulations and the international accounting standards (ISA).

The auditor will review all of the project’s financial documents, receipts lists, records of transactions, all vouchers and receipts disbursed, and relevant project documents in order to come up with a professional, independent opinion on the financial accounting of the project “Increasing resilience through climate change adaptation and sustainable livelihoods in Assasuni Upazila, Satkhira, Bangladesh” for all funds received and expended by BNM from 1st August 2026 to 31st December 2026.

Additionally, the audit shall give recommendations on strengths, weaknesses, and required improvement in the project-related financial and human resources management systems of BNM.

The audit will support the project quality assurance measures implemented by SoH and contribute to the decision-making process with regard to the project management and monitoring of finances by SoH and BNM.

**Expected Deliverables**

The auditor is expected to produce an audit report, an audit certificate and a management letter, which will comprise the following:

1. Presentation of the scope and mandate of the audit, as well as the list of documents that formed the evidence for the audit,
2. An opinion whether financial statements (statement of accounts broken down for each year being audited) are issued in accordance with the financial reporting framework of the project, BMZ requirements and an internationally recognized accounting standard,
3. A checked, signed and stamped list of all (100%) project costs receipts, sorted by BMZ budget lines (list is provided by the local implementing partner).
4. Recommendations on identified shortcomings, and, if applicable, comments on the follow-up of audit observations and recommendations from previous years.
5. FD-4 Report according to Bangladeshi Law.

Audit documents can be issued in English or German.

**Scope of the Audit**

The audit should focus on the following:

- The correctness and completeness of the accounting records,
- The financial report, showing all project related income and expenditure structured by budget lines,
- Deviations of expenditure by budget lines. The expenditure, which exceeds or falls below the budget appropriations by more than 20 %, shall be explained separately, if the approval of the BMZ has not previously been obtained,
- That receipts and relevant supporting documents are available for all project related income and expenditures (100% verification),
- The management of the funds made available, which includes the transfer of project funds, all interest earned from the project funds during the reporting period and further income generated by the project,
- Reviewing the appropriate use of funds according to the project objectives,
- Evaluation of the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of the usage of funds,
- Budget adherence through the comparison between budgeted and actual costs in the currency in which the expenditure was incurred. The audit report will not convert the examined amounts into the Euro amounts,
- Reviewing if personnel costs and social security contributions conform to the regulations in the project country and are locally comparable,
- The economical use of the project equipment and assets,
- The inventory and the use of capital items, their whereabouts and their purposive usage,
- Compliance with the legal framework of the project (project agreements and annexes, contracts, etc.) and the donor requirements,
- Compliance with the policies of the local implementing partner regarding procurement, financial administration, human resources management and travel.

**Procedures and Communication**

The auditor will be given access to all necessary documents in the project offices through the local implementing partner BNM as well as relevant donor documents through SoH.

The auditor will be responsible to set up a schedule in agreement with the local implementing partner BNM. Any expenses for field trips, postal and translation services and other expenses shall be included in the auditor’s proposed budget. BNM will support the auditor with logistics and arrangements, however, all payments of the contract will be made directly by SoH.

**Qualifications and Experience**

- Necessary qualification to serve as a recognized independent auditing authority,
- Minimum of five (5) years of experience conducting external independent audits of projects funded by international institutional donors in Bangladesh,
- Experience in conducting audits for BMZ-funded projects is desirable.
