[https://drive.google.com/file/d/17VtPxzsYzK48eZFvjPFsOnPm0TmTUapT/view?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/file/d/17VtPxzsYzK48eZFvjPFsOnPm0TmTUapT/view?usp=sharing)

**PROJECT TITLE**

Establishment of and Support to Public Diplomacy Think Tank, Prince Sultan University (PSU), (Project Number: 01004920).

**PROJECT DESCRIPTION**

Through the partnership between the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and Prince Sultan University (PSU), this project supports the establishment and operationalisation of the Public Diplomacy Think Tank in Saudi Arabia. The initiative represents Phase II of a multi-phase cooperation, building on the successful completion of Phase I, which defined the strategic foundation and institutional design of the Think Tank. The Think Tank operates as Athar.

The Think Tank will strengthen Saudi Arabia’s capacity for public diplomacy by advancing research, innovation, and capacity development aligned with Vision 2030. It will serve as a centre of excellence to promote thought leadership, knowledge exchange, and cross-sector partnerships, positioning PSU as a national and regional leader in public diplomacy.

UNDP provides technical and operational support to ensure the Think Tank’s establishment adheres to international standards, integrates sustainable governance systems, and strengthens PSU’s institutional capacity. PSU will lead in developing research, training, and outreach programmes to enhance Saudi Arabia’s influence, promote global dialogue, and develop local expertise in digital diplomacy and soft power strategies.

The project contributes to the UNSDCF Outcome 4: fostering peaceful, just, and inclusive societies and mobilizing means required for the implementation of Agenda 2030. It aligns with UNDP Strategic Plan Output 3.1 (economic diversification through research, innovation, and digital transformation) and CPD Output 4.3 (strengthening institutional and technical capacities of civil society and academic partners).

**SCOPE OF WORK**

Athar needs in-house design capacity to produce its visual material in Arabic and English, using the brand guidelines from its creative agency, so its research, events and channels look consistent.

Under the direct supervision of the Director of Operations/Project Manager and the Head of Pillar 3, the Digital Media Specialist will:

**Key Responsibilities**

- **Visual identity:** apply Athar's visual identity consistently across all outputs and maintain brand consistency.
- **Template library:** build and maintain Athar's template library, including social media formats, presentations, publication layouts (policy briefs, working papers, reports), newsletter and event materials.
- **Design production:** produce graphics, including infographics, data visualisations for research outputs, banners, event backdrops, and short motion or video edits.
- **Publication layout:** lay out research publications for digital release in Arabic and English, including right-to-left formats.
- **Asset management:** set up and maintain Athar's digital asset library on SharePoint (logos, photography, approved visuals, templates) with consistent naming and version control.
- **Design tools:** set up and maintain the team's design tools and shared design files.
- **Agency coordination:** act as counterpart to the creative agency engaged by Athar on visual identity, and convert its brand guidelines into working templates.

**QUALIFICATIONS OF THE SUCCESSFUL INDIVIDUAL CONTRACTOR**

**Min. Education requirements**

Bachelor's degree in graphic design, visual communication, multimedia design or a related field.

**Min. years of relevant work experience**

At least 3 years of professional graphic design experience, with a portfolio showing template systems, publication layout and social media design.

**Required skills**

- Visual consistency and attention to detail.
- Ability to build templates and systems that others can use.
- Ability to manage several requests and deadlines at once.
- Discretion with unpublished material.
- Designing in Arabic and English, including right-to-left typography.
- Adobe Creative Cloud (InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop) and Canva.
- Motion graphics and short video editing.

**Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section**

- Data visualisation and infographics for research or policy content.
- Working from an external agency’s brand guidelines.
- Think tank, academic, public sector or international organisation settings.
- Microsoft 365 and SharePoint.

**Required Languages**

Arabic and English, fluent written and spoken (required).

jobs.title: Media and Communications Officer
jobs.description:
**Media and Communications Officer**

**(Madagascar)**

**Position Overview**

This is an exciting opportunity for a skilled Media and Communications Officer to play a central role in delivering the communications strategy of an international NGO in the heart of Madagascar.

Based in the coastal town of Fort Dauphin, the Officer will oversee the daily running of SEED’s social media and content development, manage a junior team member, and strengthen collaboration between the Communications and Programmes teams. The role includes supporting with major fundraising appeals, producing engaging donor updates, and developing innovative content across all platforms, including expanding SEED’s presence on TikTok.

The successful candidate will work closely with both national and international staff, contributing to impactful campaigns that showcase SEED’s work in sustainable development and conservation. Predominantly office-based with occasional travel to rural project sites, the role offers a diverse range of responsibilities for a communications professional looking to develop their leadership skills while contributing to meaningful, community-driven development.

*Location:* Fort Dauphin, Anosy Region, Madagascar
*Commitment:* 24 months, extendable, 40 hours a week
*Salary:* Local salary, up to £1,200 contribution for a return flight and up to £650 contribution towards insurance

**Duties and responsibilities**

- Lead the daily management of SEED’s social media platforms, including developing and scheduling content across all channels, with a particular focus on expanding SEED’s TikTok presence.
- Produce, edit, and publish engaging written, visual, and multimedia content for social media, website, newsletters, and PR, ensuring alignment with SEED’s brand and communications goals.
- Gather stories, photos, and videos from field sites to highlight SEED’s work, ensuring safeguarding, consent, and data protection policies are upheld.
- Develop and edit donor updates in collaboration with programme teams to showcase project impact.
- Oversee the production of blogs and articles, editing contributions from staff and volunteers for external publication.
- Line-manage the Junior Officer or intern, providing day-to-day guidance, feedback, and professional development opportunities.
- Support the development of the Communications team STAGE interns, remote international interns and volunteers, ensuring learning and capacity building within the team.
- Deliver media, consent, and storytelling training to international staff, strengthening best practice across the organisation.
- Manage the relationship between Communications and Programmes teams to deliver major fundraising appeals, from concept to promotion; from storyboarding and gathering updates to shape engaging communication content that highlight SEED’s impact.
- Work with the Coordinator and International Operations Manager to ensure consistent and impactful messaging for appeals and campaigns.
- Contribute ideas for innovative fundraising content and approaches to broaden SEED’s donor base.
- Support the review and evaluation of communications platforms against agreed marketing KPIs.
- Contribute to quarterly communications reports for trustees, providing insights and analysis on content performance and audience engagement.
- Ensure SEED’s brand identity is consistently reflected across all outputs, with oversight from the Coordinator.
- Uphold SEED’s safeguarding, whistleblowing, and anti-corruption policies, ensuring best practice in all communications.
- Work flexibly, including outside standard office hours when necessary, to meet tight deadlines (e.g., donor reports, funding documents).
- Ensure all of SEED’s policies and procedures are evident throughout the work of the department, including those for safeguarding, whistleblowing and anti-corruption, and undertake continual training to ensure these are promoted at all times.
- Complete other ad-hoc tasks as required by the International Operations Manager, or Director of Programmes and Operations to further the aims and work of the organisation.

**Person specification**

- A degree-level qualification in Communications, International Development, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
- At least 1–2 years’ professional experience in communications, marketing, or fundraising, ideally within the non-profit sector.
- Some prior experience in line management, supervision, or project coordination.
- Experience creating and managing social media content and marketing campaigns.
- Demonstrate a working knowledge of producing and managing high-quality photo and video content.
- Confident in editing visual content with software such as Canva (experience with CapCut, GetResponse, or similar tools desirable).
- Excellent writing and editing skills, with proven ability to tailor messaging for different audiences and platforms.
- Ability to communicate an organisation’s ethos and mission to diverse national and international audiences through photography, videography, and writing.
- Strong verbal and written communication skills with a keen eye for detail.
- Demonstrated interest in conservation and community development, with an understanding of international development challenges in the global south desirable.
- Knowledge of PPC, content strategy development, or other advanced communications tools desirable but not essential.
- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to work to tight deadlines and manage multiple priorities.
- Proven problem-solving skills and the ability to deal appropriately with challenging situations.
- Passion, curiosity, and motivation for the role, with the ability to enthuse and inspire others.
- Capacity to build skills and share knowledge across cultures, working with people from diverse economic and cultural backgrounds and across multiple language barriers.
- Awareness of and comfort with increased social and professional responsibility, always working with cultural sensitivity and respect.
- Confident and socially skilled, able to provide guidance and support to junior staff and volunteers.
- Flexible and patient, with the ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
- Commitment to SEED’s ethos, values, and safeguarding approach, acting as a positive ambassador at all times.
- Willingness to adapt to living and working in a low-income country with sometimes basic living conditions.
- Fluent English to a high standard (both spoken and written).
- Basic working knowledge of French is desirable though not essential.

**About the organisation**

SEED Madagascar is a British Charity working in partnership with communities in the south east of Madagascar. We integrate high quality community health, rural livelihoods, education infrastructure and conservation programmes to support long term, sustainable change and add to international best practice through research and publication across all of our programmatic areas. We are now looking for entry level officers to work alongside national staff and expand our team.

More information on the work of SEED can be found at [www.madagascar.co.uk](http://www.madagascar.co.uk)

jobs.description:
Vacancy announcement

**Position**

Regional finance Officer

**Starting date**

ASAP

**Location**

Kampala

**Type of contract**

Fixed term

**About ACTED**

Since 1993, as an international non-governmental organization, ACTED has been committed to immediate

humanitarian relief to support those in urgent need and protect people’s dignity, while co-creating longer term opportunities for sustainable growth and fulfilling people’s potential. ACTED endeavours to respond to humanitarian crises and build resilience; promote inclusive and sustainable growth; co-construct effective governance and support the building of civil society worldwide by investing in people and their potential. We go the last mile: ACTED’s mission is to save lives and support people in meeting their needs in hard-to-reach areas. With a team of 4,800 national staff, 450 international staff, ACTED is active in 38 countries and implements more than 505 projects a year reaching over 20 million beneficiaries. ACTED has been operating in Uganda since 2004.

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. Historically, the two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support on its fields of intervention as part of the REACH Initiative.

Since 2017 Acted has been hosting IMPACT Initiatives in Uganda, under their REACH Initiative partnership. REACH was born in 2010 as a joint initiative of two International NGOs ([IMPACT Initiatives](http://www.impact-initiatives.org/) and [ACTED](http://www.acted.org/)) and the United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR) Operational Satellite Applications Programme ([UNOSAT](http://www.unitar.org/unosat/)). In Uganda, IMPACT, via the REACH, has provided supports to response actors, line ministries and the Office of Prime Minister that includes the development and sharing of information products to enhance the decision making and planning capacity for refugee response. This has included dedicated assessments on cash and markets; multi-sectoral needs in refugee settlements; community vulnerability and resilience; and access to basic services.

**Assignment**

*In East Africa, IMPACT has country missions in Somalia, Kenya, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Sudan, Uganda and Mozambique. These missions are hosted by sister-organisation Acted, who provide operational hosting and support. These missions are also supported by an IMPACT Regional Finance Manager, based in Kampala, who provides financial control and management across all IMPACT missions. To support this Regional Finance Manager, IMPACT is seeking an experienced candidate with prior experience in financial planning, managing financial transactions, budgeting, forecasting, and donor reporting.*

## OBJECTIVES

## Ensures sound accounting and finance management for IMPACT missions in East Africa, according to the procedures defined for each mission.

## FUNCTIONS

## Under the supervision of the IMPACT Regional Finance Manager, the Finance Officer’s tasks will be defined and allocated based on workflows for countries across the region. These tasks might include:

**Manage Finance Transactions**

- Record accounts payable and accounts receivable in Excel and SAGE + SAGA
- Support in updating/uploading SAGA/SAGE
- Check and update the daily payments file on a regular basis.
- Draft budget proposals for IMPACT projects in collaboration with relevant staff at IMPACT and ACTED
- Prepare and update the Financial Sheets (FS) for IMPACT projects
- Prepare donor financial reports
- Prepare and check BoQs and forward inputs into budget template
- Assist in forecasting expenses, and support on control and analysis of the costs of IMPACT/REACH dedicated costs to improve budgeting and increase financial visibility.
- Support with reallocations (check payments\\allocations, etc.)
- Support in updating the Allocation table on a monthly basis, for IMPACT international and IMPACT-dedicated national staff in the allocation table
- Support on the mid-year and annual closure by cross-checking between ACTED and IMPACT accountancy
- Under the guidance of the Regional Finance Manager, streamline, improve and implement any processes related to finances and finance management that are currently inefficient or absent.

**Participate in quarterly and annual audits**

- At the end of the contract or annually, assist the Regional Finance Manager in preparation of files to be sent to headquarters (final checking of invoices and their presence, complete the risk file if necessary)
- Assist the Regional Finance Manager in preparation of the document base on external/ internal Auditors query
- Assist the Regional Finance Manag to finalize the dispatch of files by adding labels and adequate packaging

**Internal Communication Processes**

- ### As requested by the Regional Finance Manager, liaise closely with Acted and IMPACT team members across East Africa to guarantee support to all IMPACT activities.
- Regularly communicate with both the IMPACT and ACTED HQ finance teams as required for the review and validation of reports and budgets.

**TECHNICAL SKILLS**

- Good knowledge of accounting and bookkeeping procedures
- Advanced MS Excel skills (creating spreadsheets and using financial functions)
- Familiarity with accounting software (e.g. SAGE, SAGA)
- Extreme attention to detail, with an ability to spot numerical errors
- Highly proactive, with good self-organisation skills and the ability to work with a minimum level of supervision

jobs.title: Communications Adviser
jobs.description:
**Program Background**

Pacific Australia Skills is a significant Australian investment which stands to make a major contribution to supporting social and economic growth in the region through strengthening the skills and training sector across the Pacific and Timor-Leste. Pacific Australia Skills builds on the achievements of 17 years of Australian Government support for skills and training in the Pacific.

**About DT Global Asia Pacific**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [www.dt-global.com](http://www.dt-global.com/)

**The Role**

The Communications Adviser will provide critical strategic communications support to the Pacific Australia Skills Solomon Islands Country Office, including the SIRIS program. This role will serve as key country-level communications support for Pacific Australia Skills in Solomon Islands, integrating activity planning, preparation, and implementation with the program-wide Pacific Australia Skills Communications Strategy and the Australian High Commission’s public diplomacy strategy. In this role, the Communications Adviser will be responsible for managing the Solomon Islands Communications Coordinator and liaising closely with the Pacific Australia Skills Regional Communications Team and Australian High Commission.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

**Strategic communications**

- Develop, implement and regularly review the SIRIS communications strategy, ensuring alignment with the program-wide Pacific Australia Skills Communications Strategy, program goals, DFAT requirements and stakeholder priorities.
- Provide strategic communications advice to program leadership, partners and stakeholders on reputation management, messaging, stakeholder engagement and communications risks.
- Identify opportunities to enhance program visibility, promote achievements and strengthen the profile of the Australian High Commission, Pacific Australia Skills, SIRIS and program partners.

**Communications capability development and mentoring**

- Provide leadership, supervision and mentoring to communications personnel and relevant program staff.
- Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement and high performance.
- Support communications capability strengthening initiatives with program partners and stakeholders.
- Actively contribute to the fortnightly Pacific Australia Skills Communications Community of Practice.

**Stakeholder engagement and relationship management**

- Establish and maintain effective working relationships with government representatives, national regulatory authorities, development partners, donors, civil society organisations, implementing partners and other key stakeholders.
- Support stakeholder engagement activities and ensure communications initiatives contribute to productive partnerships and collaborative outcomes.
- Liaise with donor representatives and partner organisations to ensure communications activities are coordinated, timely and responsive to stakeholder needs.
- Support the development of Pacific Australia Skills and SIRIS communications materials for technical meetings, working groups and sector consultations as required.

**Communications products and content development**

- Lead the development, review and quality assurance of a wide range of communications materials, including media releases, speeches, talking points, briefing notes, newsletters, social media content, reports, case studies, success stories and other promotional materials.
- Ensure all communication products are clear, accurate, evidence-based and tailored to relevant audiences.
- Maintain high editorial standards and ensure communications outputs comply with branding, accessibility and DFAT requirements.
- Coordinate with the Regional Communications Team for messaging, graphic design, branding and approvals.

**Event managemen**t

- Lead the planning, coordination and delivery of program events, including high-level meetings, workshops, skills competitions, conferences and stakeholder engagement activities.
- Ensure event planning and implementation appropriately considers protocol requirements, stakeholder expectations and donor visibility requirements.
- Oversee event communications, promotional activities and post-event reporting.

**Program management and coordination**

- Manage communications workplans, budgets and delivery schedules to ensure activities are completed on time and to a high standard.
- Coordinate communications activities across program teams and workstreams, ensuring consistency of messaging and approach.
- Monitor and report on communications activities, outcomes and performance, and identify opportunities for improvement.
- Other tasks and duties, as required, to ensure the smooth and effective delivery of Pacific Australia Skills.
- This ToR may vary and change in future.

**Selection Criteria**

**Essential Experience and Knowledge**

- At least five years of experience in communications roles, working on DFAT-funded projects is a strong advantage. Experience working in Solomon Islands and the wider Pacific region is also highly regarded.
- Demonstrated experience developing and implementing communications strategies that support program objectives, strengthen stakeholder engagement, and enhance organisational visibility and reputation.
- Proven experience planning and delivering complex events, including high-level meetings, conferences, and others which involve attention to governmental protocol requirements.
- Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain productive relationships and work collaboratively with clients, donors, government representatives, development partners, civil society organisations and others.
- Proven ability to lead, supervise, mentor, and develop communications staff or multidisciplinary teams, fostering high performance, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Experience engaging with partners and stakeholders for communications capability development is also highly regarded.
- Strong ability to research, synthesize, and edit a broad range of communications products including media releases, talking points, social media content, success stories and others.
- Exceptional attention to detail and ability to ensure high-quality communication products, including compliance with branding and accessibility guidelines.
- Program management skills, including excellent time management skills, the ability to manage multiple priorities and lead high-quality delivery of outputs in a fast-paced environment.
- Experience providing strategic communications advice to senior leaders, donors and other partners.
- Willingness to travel throughout Solomon Islands to support program implementation and communications, including staying overnight in rural and remote locations.

**Desirable**

- Experience with developing and managing the creation of visual communications, particularly the production of video content.
- Understanding of and commitment to Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI), Child Protection, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), prevention of human trafficking, environmental protection, anti-corruption and other DFAT safeguarding policies.
- DT Global strongly encourages applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds including first nations, diverse SOGIESC and people with disabilities.
- People with lived experience of the regions in which Pacific Australia Skills operate are strongly encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Deputy Country Director - Operations
jobs.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Under the supervision of the Country Director, the Deputy Country Director for Operations will lead on the strategic direction and coordination of the field operations of ACF across Northern and Southern Yemen, being accountable for ensuring that the ACF humanitarian response implementation is effective and efficient.

The main responsibilities and challenges of the position will be as follows:
Provide leadership in strategic vision, context analysis and operational direction of the country officeContribute to the development, implementation and annual review of the country office strategy
Ensure continuous analysis of humanitarian needs and context dynamics across Yemen, to assess their possible implications for programme delivery, access and operational risks
Ensure quality and effective programme deliveryProvide leadership and oversight to ensure efficient, timely, accountable, and principled implementation of ACF programmes across all areas of intervention
Ensure programme implementation aligns with ACF's standards, donors' requirements, humanitarian principles, and relevant international standards
Lead operational coordination, and external representationSupport the Country Director in maintaining and strengthening strategic relationships with relevant authorities, donors, UN agencies, national and international NGOs, and other relevant stakeholders
Promote and strengthen partnerships with local and international organizations
Support ACF advocacy efforts through evidence-based operational analysis and engagement
Ensure tge development and direction of the mission field coordination structureProvide guidance and support in resolving operational, partnership, access, and stakeholder-related challenges
Support risk management and business continuity.

Profile :

You hold a Master's Degree in International Relations, Humanitarian Assistance, Political or Social Sciences, Economics, Business Administration or any related field.
You have at least 10 years of professional experience in the humanitarian sector, with a minimum of 5 years in management role and leading field operations. A previous experience coordinating implementation of multi-sectoral programs is considered an asset.
You demonstrate a strong leadership and decision-making abilities at strategic levels, good communication, representation, and influencing skills. You are recognised for your ability to work effectively under pressure, to adapt to changing circumstances, establish priorities and meet deadlines.
You master English (written and spoken) and have strong report writing, monitoring and evaluation skills and experience.
Additional language skills in Arabic, previous experience in the Middle-East and familiarity with the regional context are considered an asset.

Conditions d'emploi

Fixed term contract under French legislation: 6 months
Monthly gross salary from 2899 to 3376euros upon experience, including 13th month
Reimbursement of the pension insurance for non-French citizens: 16% of the gross monthly salary
Annual salary increase: 6% increase after and each 12 months of continuous contract
Monthly per diem and living allowance: 730 USD net, field paid
Monthly country allowance: 450euros
Child allowance: 1500euros per year per child present in the country of origin (maximum 6000euros/year)
Transportation and accommodation: Coverage of transportation costs and guest house
Medical coverage: ACF covers 100% of the health and repatriation insurance agreement fees, for your medical expenses (as well as your dependents if you have a family post), and up to 1 month after the end of your contract
Salary sustainment measures (sickness, paternity, maternity)
Leaves and RnR: 25 days of paid leaves per year, 20 RnR per year, airfare reimbursement with a ceiling to get to the chosen break destination, and 215 euros for each RnR period
Accompaniment and trainings:Follow-up and support for career development
Free and unlimited access to the e-learning platform Talentsoft
ACF is committed to people with disabilities and actively fights against all forms of discrimination.

jobs.title: Communications, Advocacy and Fundraising Coordinator
Field Logistics Officer
jobs.description:
Location Tshopo Province with travel within or to other provinces as necessary and visit to Kisangani Office

Position Type: Consultant

Length of contract: 3 months

**Background**

Global Outbreak Response Support (GORS) delivered by Global Emergency Group, Inc. (GEG), under a cooperative agreement with the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy (GHSD), provides rapid activation, surge response, and transition support enabling countries to detect, contain, and recover from infectious disease outbreaks. GEG leads GORS as the prime recipient, building on its ongoing role as Field Programs Support lead for Team Credence on the Humanitarian Assistance Support Contract (HASC). Founded in 2007, GEG delivers GORS through a global network of regional response hubs, a pre-vetted surge roster, and embedded in-country teams that mobilize within hours of an authorized outbreak response.

**Reporting/Communication Lines**

Under the supervision of the GORS Logistics and Supply Chain Lead for work planning, execution, and performance.

**Scope of Work**

**Position Description**

Field Logistics Officer (FLO) will be deployed to work in a Health Zone (HZ) and/or Health Area (HA) to support the Ebola Response at that/those location(s). The Field Logistics Officer will support the GDRC Zone Health Logistics and GDRC Area Health counter parts. The FLO will assess the logistics situation locally, report to the Logistics Lead on the findings and propose recommendation with the GORS program activities and pillars. Once the plan is approved, the FLO will support plan implementation, providing support and training in the HZ and HA.

*The Field Logistics Officer will:*

Needs assessment

- Assess the logistics capacity and needs of the health zone or health areas at the field location.
- Draft a proposed logistics plan of action with the local counterpart and submit it to the Logistics Lead for review, comment and approval by the Leads at the Kisangani Office.
- Coordinate with the local structure, to identify a counterpart when no logistics counterpart is available.

Logistics implementation

- Implement the approved plan of action while actively involving the local counterpart at every step, gradually shifting from demonstrating (doing and showing) to supervising (letting them do and observing).
- Repeat the needs assessment several times during implementation and submit any changes to the Logistics Lead for inclusion in the approved plan.

Vehicle(s) and fuel management

- Manage its own vehicle following fleet and safety and security procedure and processes, with reporting to Fleet Officer and or the Safety and security Coordinator for incidents.
- As necessary, support the Fuel Monitoring Assistant in monitoring fuel and vehicle rental to local partners
- Report immediately any wrongdoing on fleet and fuel usage to the fleet officer for action.

Requisition

- Support writing of all requisitions from the quality of the documents and local approval before they are sent the GDRC Logistics coordinator
- Route possible requisition that supports GEG GORS pillars to Logistics team in Kisangani for approval and action.

Safety and Security

- Follow and ensure full implementation of Safety and security protocols, processes and guidelines
- Report any safety and security issues to the Safety and Security Coordinator immediately following communication procedure

Access and Stock management

- With Counterpart, review the access to local facilities from Kisangani and Nai Nai Logistics Hub, includes the last mile delivery plan in the logistics implementation plan
- At field level with counterpart, review storage and stock management, present, introduce and train on stock management best practice according to the type of goods and location.

**Required Position Qualifications**

- At least 2 years of Logistics field experience, in humanitarian program or private sector with at least 1 year of medical logistics.
- Demonstrate the management of field logistics at a regional level or higher
- Demonstrate knowledge on how to work with a fleet of ambulances in outbreak or emergency settings.
- Strong understanding of field logistics, quality assurance, and chain of custody.
- Ability to work in a difficult environment and work under pressure.
- Fluent communication in French, English is an asset.
- Ability to use Excel and word as an advance user, using complex excel sheet
- ICT knowledge is an asset

**Competencies/Performance Criteria**

- Adherence to and promotion of the GEG Way.

**Travel**

The Field Logistics Officer (FLO) will mostly work at the HZ and HA level of Tshopo Province and may travel to Haut Uele and other provinces according to operational needs.

**Working Conditions**

Emergency support will follow agreed activation and backup arrangements. The Field Logistics Officer (FLO) adheres to GEG security management directives and policies.

**About Global Emergency Group**

Founded in 2007, GEG is a benefit corporation that supports vulnerable people affected by crisis in more than 52 countries by providing a broad range of humanitarian support services to a wide range of organizations, including the United Nations, the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, donor governments, companies, major international and national NGO’s and local communities. Every day, these organizations and communities rely on GEG’s emergency response expertise, and on the combined capabilities and dedication of its people to implement strategies, find solutions and seize opportunities to assist the world’s most vulnerable people.

Global Emergency Group is committed to being an equal opportunity employer and recruiting people of diverse backgrounds and experiences. GEG does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion or belief, color, gender, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, family structure, age, medical condition, disability, ancestry, national origin or ethnic group. All recruitment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications, merit and business need.

Localisation : Province de Tshopo avec déplacements à l'intérieur ou vers d'autres provinces selon les besoins et visite au bureau de Kisangani

Type de poste : Consultat

Durée du contrat : 3 mois

**Contexte**

Le programme **Programme mondial d’appui à la réponse aux épidémies (Global Outbreak Response Support - GORS)**, mis en œuvre par Global Emergency Group, Inc. (GEG) dans le cadre d’un accord de coopération avec le Bureau de la sécurité sanitaire mondiale et de la diplomatie (Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy – GHSD) du Département d’État américain, fournit un appui à la mobilisation rapide, à la réponse d’urgence et à la transition, permettant aux pays de détecter, de contenir et de se relever des épidémies de maladies infectieuses.

GEG assure la direction du programme GORS en tant que bénéficiaire principal, en s’appuyant sur son rôle actuel de responsable de l’appui aux programmes de terrain (Field Programs Support Lead) au sein de Team Credence, dans le cadre du contrat d’appui à l’assistance humanitaire (Humanitarian Assistance Support Contract – HASC).

Fondée en 2007, GEG met en œuvre le programme GORS grâce à un réseau mondial de centres régionaux de réponse, à un vivier de personnel d’urgence préalablement sélectionné et qualifié, ainsi qu’à des équipes déployées directement dans les pays. Ces équipes peuvent être mobilisées dans les heures suivant l’autorisation officielle d’une intervention en réponse à une épidémie.

**Rapport hiérarchique/communication**

Sous la supervision du responsable logistique GORS pour la planification, l'exécution et la performance du travail.

**Étendue des responsabilités (Scope of Work)**

**Description du poste**

Le Responsable de la Logistique sur le Terrain (Field Logistics Officer – FLO) sera déployé dans une zone de santé et/ou une aire de santé afin d’appuyer la réponse à l’épidémie d’Ebola dans la ou les localités concernées.

Il apportera un appui aux responsables logistiques des Zones de Santé et aux équipes de santé des Aires de Santé de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC). Le FLO évaluera la situation logistique au niveau local, présentera ses constats au Responsable de la Logistique et formulera des recommandations en lien avec les activités et les piliers du programme GORS.

Une fois le plan d’action approuvé, le FLO appuiera sa mise en œuvre, tout en assurant l’accompagnement, le renforcement des capacités et la formation des équipes des Zones et Aires de Santé concernées.

***Le Responsable de la Logistique sur le Terrain (FLO) sera chargé de :***

**1. Évaluation des besoins**

- Évaluer les capacités logistiques et les besoins de la Zone de Santé ou des Aires de Santé au niveau du site d’intervention.
- Élaborer, en collaboration avec les interlocuteurs locaux, un projet de plan d’action logistique et le soumettre au Responsable de la Logistique pour examen, commentaires et approbation par les responsables du bureau de Kisangani.
- Coordonner avec les structures locales afin d’identifier un interlocuteur logistique (contrepartie locale) lorsqu’aucun responsable logistique n’est disponible.

**2. Mise en œuvre des activités logistiques**

- Mettre en œuvre le plan d’action approuvé en impliquant activement la contrepartie locale à chaque étape, en passant progressivement d’une approche de démonstration (faire et montrer) à une approche de supervision (laisser faire et observer).
- Réaliser plusieurs évaluations des besoins au cours de la mise en œuvre et soumettre toute modification au Responsable de la Logistique afin qu’elle soit intégrée au plan d’action approuvé.

**3. Gestion des véhicules et du carburant**

- Gérer son véhicule conformément aux procédures et processus de gestion de flotte, de sûreté et de sécurité, et signaler tout incident au Responsable de la Flotte et/ou au Coordonnateur de la Sûreté et de la Sécurité.
- Si nécessaire, appuyer l’Assistant chargé du suivi du carburant dans le contrôle de la consommation de carburant et de la location des véhicules mis à la disposition des partenaires locaux.
- Signaler immédiatement au Responsable de la Flotte toute irrégularité ou mauvaise utilisation des véhicules ou du carburant, afin que les mesures appropriées soient prises.

**4. Gestion des demandes d’approvisionnement (Requisitions)**

- Appuyer la préparation de toutes les demandes d’approvisionnement, en veillant à la qualité et à la conformité des documents ainsi qu’à l’obtention des approbations locales requises, avant leur transmission au Coordonnateur Logistique du Gouvernement de la RDC (GDRC).
- Transmettre à l’équipe logistique du bureau de Kisangani, pour approbation et traitement, toute demande d’approvisionnement susceptible de contribuer à la mise en œuvre des piliers du programme GEG-GORS.

**5. Sûreté et sécurité**

- Respecter et veiller à la mise en œuvre intégrale des protocoles, procédures, processus et directives en matière de sûreté et de sécurité.
- Signaler immédiatement tout problème relatif à la sûreté ou à la sécurité au Coordonnateur de la Sûreté et de la Sécurité, conformément aux procédures de communication établies.

**6. Accès et gestion des stocks**

- En collaboration avec la contrepartie locale, examiner les modalités d’accès aux installations et aux ressources logistiques depuis Kisangani et le hub logistique de Nai Nai, notamment le plan de livraison du dernier kilomètre (*last-mile delivery*), et intégrer ces éléments dans le plan de mise en œuvre logistique.
- Au niveau du terrain, examiner avec la contrepartie locale les conditions de stockage et les pratiques de gestion des stocks, présenter et introduire les bonnes pratiques de gestion des stocks, puis assurer la formation correspondante en fonction de la nature des biens et du contexte du site d’intervention.

**Qualifications requises pour le poste**

- Avoir au moins deux (2) ans d’expérience en logistique sur le terrain, dans le cadre de programmes humanitaires ou dans le secteur privé, dont au moins un (1) an d’expérience en logistique médicale.
- Démontrer une expérience dans la gestion de la logistique opérationnelle sur le terrain à l’échelle régionale ou à un niveau supérieur.
- Démontrer une connaissance de la gestion d’une flotte d’ambulances dans des contextes d’épidémies ou d’urgence.
- Avoir une solide compréhension de la logistique de terrain, de l’assurance qualité et de la chaîne de traçabilité (*chain of custody*).
- Être capable de travailler dans un environnement difficile et sous pression.
- Maîtriser le français à l’oral et à l’écrit ; la maîtrise de l’anglais constitue un atout.
- Maîtriser Microsoft Excel et Word à un niveau avancé, notamment l’utilisation de feuilles de calcul Excel complexes.
- Avoir des connaissances en technologies de l’information et de la communication (TIC) constitue un atout.

**Compétences et critères de performance**

- Respecter et promouvoir les valeurs, principes et méthodes de travail de GEG (*The GEG Way*).

**Déplacements professionnels**

Le Responsable de la Logistique sur le Terrain exercera principalement ses fonctions dans la province de la Tshopo. Il pourra également être amené à se déplacer dans le Haut-Uele et dans d’autres provinces de l’Est de la RDC, pour des périodes convenues, en fonction des besoins opérationnels et lorsque cela sera nécessaire.

**Conditions de travail**

Le soutien d'urgence suivra les modalités d'activation et de sauvegarde convenues. L'officier de flotte respecte les directives et politiques de gestion de la sécurité du GEG.

**À propos de Global Emergency Group (GEG)**

Fondée en 2007, Global Emergency Group (GEG) est une entreprise à mission sociale qui apporte un soutien aux personnes vulnérables touchées par des crises dans plus de 52 pays. Elle fournit une large gamme de services d’assistance humanitaire à diverses organisations, notamment les Nations Unies, le Mouvement international de la Croix-Rouge et du Croissant-Rouge, les gouvernements donateurs, les entreprises, les grandes ONG internationales et nationales, ainsi que les communautés locales.

Chaque jour, ces organisations et communautés comptent sur l’expertise de GEG en matière de réponse aux urgences, ainsi que sur les compétences, l’engagement et la complémentarité de ses équipes pour mettre en œuvre des stratégies, trouver des solutions et saisir les opportunités permettant de venir en aide aux populations les plus vulnérables dans le monde.

Global Emergency Group s’engage à promouvoir l’égalité des chances en matière d’emploi et à recruter des personnes issues d’horizons divers et ayant des expériences variées. GEG ne pratique aucune discrimination fondée sur la race, la religion ou les convictions, la couleur, le genre, le sexe, l’orientation sexuelle, l’état matrimonial, la situation familiale, l’âge, l’état de santé, le handicap, l’ascendance, l’origine nationale ou l’appartenance ethnique.

Toutes les décisions de recrutement sont prises sur la base des qualifications, du mérite et des besoins de l’organisation.

jobs.description:
**Terms of Reference (TOR) for**

***Baseline Consultancy for GBV consortium project in Sudan***

Who is the Danish Refugee Council?

Founded in 1956, the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is a leading international NGO and one of the few with a specific expertise in forced displacement. Active in 40 countries with 9,000 employees and supported by 7,500 volunteers, DRC protects, advocates, and builds sustainable futures for refugees and other displacement-affected people and communities. DRC works during displacement at all stages: In the acute crisis, in displacement, when settling and integrating in a new place, or upon return. DRC provides protection and life-saving humanitarian assistance; supports displaced persons in becoming self-reliant and included into hosting societies; and works with civil society and responsible authorities to promote protection of rights and peaceful coexistence.

DRC has been operating in Sudan since 1994, working in collaboration with a number of partners on protection, GBV, shelter, WASH, CCCM, food security/economic recovery, peacebuilding and humanitarian mine action and clearance. More specifically, DRC is leading a consortium with Trocaire, Norwegian Church Aid, and nine Sudanese Women-led-organisations to respond to gender-based violence (GBV) and conflict sexual related violence (SCRV) in Sudan.

## Purpose of the consultancy

The Danish Refugee Council based in Sudan seeks proposals from Consultant(s)/consultancy firm that will work in collaboration with the consortium management unit, the wider consortium agencies, and FCDO and is responsible for leading and carrying out the baseline assessment for this project. This includes developing the methodology and execution of the baseline assessment and providing recommendations to fully establish the set-up of the project. All work should be aligned with project priorities and protection/do no harm principles. The ideal candidate(s) would preferably have experience working on previous baselines/evaluation, ideally have worked on projects related to the prevention and response to sexual and gender-based violence and have experience collecting data safely and ethically on GBV-related topics with women, girls and other at-risk groups.

## Background

Sudan is in the midst of one of the world’s worst protection crises. An estimated 12.4 to 12.7 million people—predominantly women and girls—are at risk of gender-based violence (GBV) in Sudan, a figure that has quadrupled since the conflict erupted in April 2023. According to [UN Women](https://www.unwomen.org/sites/default/files/2024-12/sudan-gender-alert-2_en_2024.pdf) and the [United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)](https://www.unfpa.org/resources/unfpa-situation-report-sudan-january-february-2026), women and girls account for 98% of documented conflict-related sexual violence survivors, facing systematic abuses including rape, gang rape, abduction, sexual slavery, intimate partner violence, and forced child marriage. Assessments reported by [UN News](https://news.un.org/en/story/2026/04/1167330) further reveal that 76% of women aged 25 to 49 feel unsafe in public spaces and displacement camps. While hundreds of formal cases are verified annually, humanitarian agencies emphasize that severe underreporting—driven by social stigma, fear of retaliation, and the collapse of healthcare and legal systems—means documented incidents represent only a small fraction of the actual crisis. Additionally, access to survivor-centred sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) services remains extremely limited. Many survivors have never received basic medical and psychological care, and they struggle to access justice and socioeconomic rehabilitation. Prior to the conflict, Sudan had made modest progress on women’s rights, including repealing the restrictive Public Order Act and criminalizing Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) and child marriage. The current conflict has reversed these fragile gains. Sexual violence is being used as a tactic of war, causing severe physical and psychological harm and social exclusion. Socially, the conflict has shattered community structures and support systems, amplifying vulnerabilities. Survivors now remain increasingly stigmatised and isolated, facing multiple forms of discrimination and increased vulnerability, escalating the risk of exploitation and violence. All this makes urgent protection and accountability measures critical. In a context where populations are not effectively supported by law enforcement, there is a lack of access to and functionality of formal justice mechanisms, leading to large-scale protection threats. The lack of a political solution in Sudan, alongside the lack of solutions for the millions of Sudanese affected by displacement affect national and local-level stability, both in regard to ongoing conflict and competition over resources, as well as rising rates of criminality and food insecurity in response to increasing poverty and vulnerability. Cultures of impunity and stigmatisation are perpetuating and reinforcing violence against women and girls -with sexual violence normalised and seen as inevitable.

Launched in 2026, HOPE-S (Healing, Outreach, Protection, Empowerment) is a five-year, £19.95 million programme funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) to tackle GBV and conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV) across conflict-affected regions of Sudan. Following a call for proposals, the Danish Refugee Council in Sudan has successfully been awarded the annual grant agreement (AGA), leading a consortium with Trocaire, Norwegian Church Aid, and nine Sudanese Women-led-organisations. The programme has three outcomes:

- **Risk Mitigation:** strengthen WLO/community structures for community-led prevention
- **Response:** improve access to essential GBV/SGBV response services for survivors
- **Social norms:** Harmful social norms/behaviours that perpetuate GBV/CRSV are transformed, and protective community norms are strengthened

The programme design explicitly references **localization** - support the leadership of Sudanese WLOs, working in high-risk locations- and, in turn, has inclusive, participatory delivery informed by a Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) analysis & safeguarding.

## Objective of the consultancy

The baseline study aimed to be participatory and will serve to define indicators to capture both quantitative and qualitative data throughout the 5-year project to update the Project’s M&E framework with initial data, to build further on the evidence and indicators used in other projects supporting survivor-led networks, allowing an analysis of the impact and effects cumulatively and to lead an intersectional needs analysis.

**The assignment has the following key objectives:**

- Provide quality baseline data (quantitative and qualitative) to respond to the already designed indicators in the Project's logical framework/M&E framework, including ethical considerations for data collection
- Define methods and tools to evaluate some of the indicators in the Project's logical framework/M&E framework drawing on relevant interagency GBV guidance, minimum standards, and survivor-centred ethical principles.
- Provide inputs into the M&E framework – including baseline targets;
- Provide an analysis of key forms of marginalisation, exclusion and barriers faced by groups at risk of GBV/CRSV, and inform DRC and consortium partners' programming, engagement and strategic priorities.
- Provide recommendations to Project stakeholders in order to strengthen the Project’s impact and effectiveness.
- Identify the locally relevant harmful norm through a participatory social norms exploration

*Preparation*

- Review project proposal documents, resources, and standards, including a desk review of the context
- Develop a baseline methodology, for both beneficiaries and humanitarian stakeholders. The scope of the baseline assessment covers locations across 5 states (Central Darfur, North Darfur, South and North Kordofan and Khartoum)
- Develop data collection tools
- Share draft tools, sampling frame and analysis plan with CMU
- Develop an interview and data collection schedule, with support from Consortium MEAL Co as necessary. This should include proposed ethical guidance throughout the process
- Train, support and supervise data collectors on data collection tools and techniques (in Arabic)
- Identify key stakeholders and conduct field interviews
- Analyse data into an initial set of findings disaggregated by age, gender, and inclusion.

*Data collection, analysis and report*

- Train consortium staff/partners on data collection tools and techniques, as required.
- Supervise data collection timeline and quality, consolidating findings on an ongoing basis.
- Analyse data collection into an initial set of findings (disaggregated by age, gender, and disability inclusion), supporting additional data collection as identified.
- Validation meeting (with presentation) and final report

**Other key information:** An independent midline and endline study is planned by FCDO, which will be contracting an independent evaluation company. Additionally, FCDO is also contracting a third-party monitoring entity. The midline and endline study will utilise as much as possible the same methodology as the baseline in order to ensure the comparability of the findings. The objectives of this assignment (full report, data collection tools and presentation of findings) is expected to be completed in English and Arabic.

1. ## Scope of work and Methodology

**Proposed Scope (to be confirmed during onboarding) :** The assessment will focus on understanding safety and security concerns, available support systems, and social dynamics influencing the safety of women and girls in crisis-affected areas. The study will use secondary data, community mapping, a survey, and primary qualitative data to gather information on safety perceptions, responses to violence, and community-driven initiatives for GBV prevention and support. The consultant will be responsible for developing a full assessment protocol based on this TOR, including refining the methodology and finalizing the data collection tools tailored to each target group, conducting data analysis and writing report. The consultant will also ensure that the data collection methods and tools are adapted to the cultural and social context of the selected locations. In addition, the consultant will ensure that all enumerators receive training prior to data collection on the code of conduct, safeguarding, and basic protection principles. The consultant will be responsible for ensuring that strict safe and ethical approaches procedures are adhered to at all stages of the assessment. The geographical scope includes Central Darfur (Zalengi, Nertiti, Um Dukhn Golo locality), North Darfur (Tawila locality), South Kordofan (Dellemi, Thobo, Dilling, Kadugli, Abyssia and Abu Jabayha localities), North Kordofan (El Obeid and Rehad localities Khartoum (East Nile, Ombduram- Umbadda, Omdurman- Khariri, Bahri and Khartoum localities). It will target key populations, including women, adolescent girls, men, community structures, service providers, and both government and non-government actors. All participant data will be anonymized, and confidentiality will be maintained at all stages. The assessment will follow strict ethical standards to minimize harm to both participants and researchers.

**Methodology :** The baseline assessment will utilize a mixed-methods approach, combining secondary data from desk-based document review and primary quantitative and qualitative data collection.

- **Survey (quantitative):** one survey with modules on perceived safety and wellbeing, access to services, and social norms, with the Washington Group Short Set on functioning.
- **Qualitative Methods: Key Informant Interviews (KIIs):** Interviews with relevant stakeholders, including service providers, WLOs and local partners, religious and traditional leaders, community leaders, and local authorities (if appropriate)
- **Focus Group Discussions (FGDs):** Discussions with different community groups (women, girls, men, boys, and marginalized groups) to capture diverse experiences and concerns. Please refer to the geographic scope
- **A review of secondary data** to assess drivers of GBV and types of GBV in the proposed implementation areas, barriers to accessing GBV services, and existing practices of WLOs and local national NGOs regarding safe and ethical data management, referral pathways, and SOP. This will include data from local actors, government sources, and other agencies
- Validation meeting: the consultant will facilitate a validation meeting to share/ verify initial findings and recommendations, with a remit to how they can be integrated into the context in Sudan.
- **Presentation:** of findings to consortium unit and to FCDO. CMU will logistically organise but expect the consultant to present the findings.
- \*\*Final report (\*\*no more than 20 pages). The final report should also include (raw analysis, data tools, analysis and secondary sources used), including a short 2-3 pages max summary as well as recommendations & proposed targets
- **Tentative Indicators to be baselined** (see below). This will be confirmed, and the logframe shared during onboarding, after confirmation with FCDO, DRC and Tier 2 & Tier 3 partners).

**Indicator**

**Method**

**Impact 1:** % of women, girls and other at-risk groups in targeted areas reporting improved perceptions of safety and psychosocial wellbeing.

Individuals

**Impact 2:** Average self-reported impact of WLOs and/or women and adolescent girls in decision-making structures

Women’s Reported Impact Questionnaire

**Impact 3:** % of women and girls, including those at risk of GBV/CRSV, who report being able to access service they need, including health, psychosocial and protection services.

Individuals

**Outcome 1:** % of supported WLOs/women representatives reporting increased ability to influence decisions in identified formal and informal structures.KII

**Outcome 2:** % of supported service delivery points meeting agreed minimum quality standards for survivor-centred GBV

KII

**Outcome 3:** % of women, men, girls and boys in target population who report that they disagree or strongly disagree with locally relevant harmful norms related to GBV/CRSV.

SNET

## Deliverables

The Consultant will submit the following deliverables as mentioned below:

Throughout the phases, the Consultants/consultancy firm will be supported by the Chief of Party and the Consortium MEAL Coordinator (the latter acting as the primary focal point) who will facilitate access to the wider consortium for field data collection activities, and ensure they are conducted in a sensitive, safe and harmonized manner.

**DRC's responsibilities**

DRC is responsible for providing a briefing and will facilitate meetings with consortium stakeholders and share background information/documents (with support from the wider consortium). The wider consortium will support in providing secondary documentation information, list of locations, agreed list of KIIs and WLOs identification and will be responsible for data collection. The consortium members will either hire the data collectors or make their staff available during this time period. Each of the 12 consortium agencies will identify and make available a focal point - who will also engage in briefing, validation meetings, and act as a primary focal point in coordinating the data collectors, sharing information on locations, KIIs, WLOs, etc. Output documents will be reviewed for quality, and final payments will be made upon submission of all agreed deliverables.

**Consultancy firm/consultants’ responsibility**

The consultant will be responsible for all aspects of the deliverables and other responsibilities stipulated in the ToR. It is expected that the Consultant will be able to conduct work remotely. The consultant(s) is/are responsible for providing the following deliverables:

- **Inception Report:** Share detailed methodology, assessment tools, and a work plan outlining activities, timelines, and milestones
- **Data collection tools:** Develop and share questionnaires, interview guides, etc as applicable
- **Training** – train data collectors, keep track of information, and brief/debrief focal points
- **Clean raw data & data analysis –** clean and analyse data collected during the assignment
- **Update M&E framework** (site- and theme-specific) baseline, midline targets on planned results and indicators
- **Validation meeting** – Conduct a validation meeting with key consortium members & FCDO to validate the findings
- **Draft Assessment Report:** A preliminary report summarizing key findings and gaps.
- **Final Assessment Report:** A comprehensive report with findings, analyses, and actionable recommendations.
- **Presentation:** A PowerPoint summary of key findings and recommendations - at least two PPTs (1) with consortium (2) with FCDO (&/or other external stakeholders - to be confirmed)

The Consultant(s)/consultancy firm can work flexibly over a period of a maximum of 40 days, ideally starting in mid-December 2026- mid-February 2027. While the exact dates and number of working hours will be flexible and adapted to operational requirements (including Christmas/end of year break), it is expected to be finalized in the application process. A suggested indicative breakdown of the work schedule is as follows:

- Onboarding and Desk review 5 days
- Baseline methodology, tool development and training 7-10 days
- Data collection, cleaning and analysis 7-14- days
- Report drafting 6 days
- Presentation and validation meeting (consortium and FCDO) 2 days
- Report revision and finalization (post DRC review) 3 days

In advance of each phase of work, the Consultant will be expected to confirm with the DRC Chief of Party/MEAL Coordinator that the number of days outlined above remains appropriate; maximum figures can be reduced or increased as required, at the discretion of DRC. Accordingly, deadlines for all deliverables will be finalized based on consultation with DRC CMU with the final report package delivered by **15th February 2027.** Tentative early findings to be provided by 17th January 2027 (aligned with donor reporting

## Duration, timeline, and payment

The Consultant(s) will be expected to work full-time over the course of a **maximum of 40 days** (period of **mid-December 2026 –mid-February 2027)**. While the exact number of days, dates, and number of working hours will be flexible and adapted to operational requirements and the holiday period, this will be finalized in the application process. Accordingly, deadlines for all deliverables; which will be synchronized with two possible payment tranches

1. 30% upon submission of inception report and validated Data collection tools, along with invoice
2. 70% upon submission of validated final report (with validated PPT, raw data, updated M&E framework) along with invoice

The consultant shall be prepared to complete the assignment no later than ***15th February 2027.***

Proposed Composition of Team

Evaluation team – consisting of Lead Evaluator (with GBV and evaluation skills) – in both Arabic and english

## Eligibility, qualification, and experience required

**Consultant(s) profile and technical competencies**

### Essential:

- At least 5 years’ experience in conducting baseline studies and/or evaluations, using mixed methods evaluation skills and having flexibility in using non-traditional and innovative methods, including participatory and inclusive methods of data collection;
- Experience in the implementation of and monitoring/evaluation of humanitarian, and development Gender-based violence or women empowerment projects in fragile contexts with expertise in gender and human-rights based approaches
- Specific data collection experiences in the areas of ending violence against women and girls, in particular experience engaging with and conducting or guiding interviews with survivors;
- Able to work independently as well as collaboratively in diverse teams with multiple stakeholders across the delivery chain with varying capacities
- Ability to produce timely and high-quality written reports
- Ability to work remotely- training and guiding data collection and analysis process remotely
- The candidate/s must read, speak and write English and Arabic fluently;

### It is expected that the Consultant will be able to conduct the assignment remotely. As the consultant is expected to train, engage and support the data collectors in Sudan - at a minimum the consultant(s) are expected to work in same time-zone as Sudan.

### Desirable:

- Professional experience in Sudan is preferred.

Bidders must meet the Essential Criteria below for this tender. Failure to comply with the criteria will result in the disqualification of the bid. Submitted offers will be reviewed on “Pass” or “Fail” basis to determine compliance with the below formal criteria/ requirement:

**Essential**

**Requirements**

1- The consultant must possess authorization to work in Sudan and/or have the necessary permissions for travel and data collection within Sudan and/or have access to an authorized third party with permission to collect data and operate in Sudan.

Please note that bids shall respond to all criteria, or their bid may be disqualified.

Bidders who pass the technical evaluation will be invited for an online panel interview. The interview will be evaluated per the following criteria:

**Technical criteria #**

**Panel Interview criteria**

**Weighting in technical evaluation \[Total 50%**

1- Previous experience in similar data collection, analysis, and research projects 5%

2- Clarity of proposed process 20%

3- Demonstration of understanding of challenges and best practices across various contexts 20%

4- Spoken fluency in English 5%

Please note that bids shall respond to all criteria, or their bid may be disqualified.

### It is expected that the Consultant will be able to conduct the assignment remotely. As the consultant is expected to train, engage, and support the data collectors in Sudan, at a minimum, the consultant(s) are expected to work in the same time zone as Sudan.

### Desirable:

- Professional experience in Sudan is preferred.

## Technical supervision

The selected consultant will work under the supervision of the SALAMA project Chief of Party [(Muhammet.Kalei@drc.ngo](https://reliefweb.int/%28Muhammet.Kalei@drc.ngo) ) with day-to-day engagement with the Consortium MEAL Coordinator [(Christian.Eboh@drc.ngo](https://reliefweb.int/%28Christian.Eboh@drc.ngo) )

## Location and support

The assignment can be carried out remotely with working hours preferably in the same time zone as Sudan.The Consultant will provide her/his own computer and mobile phone

## Travel

N/A

## Submission process

**Application process:** Interested applicants/consultancy who meet the required qualifications and experience are invited to submit their expression of interest, which includes the following documents as per the RFP letter invitation, including:

- CV(s) with details of qualifications and experience, indicating documentation of relevant assignments undertaken and full correct details of three professional referees
- The envisioned work plan (maximum 5 pages) that summarizes
- An understanding of the objective of the baseline
- A proposed methodology and envisaged work plan which contains a well-informed approach to the participation of survivors in the study and approaches to ethics, "Do no harm" and gender sensitivity;
- A proposed timeline for completing the assignment;
- Financial proposal providing cost estimates of daily consultancy fees - only financial offers (inclusive of VAT and all relevant taxes will be accepted).
- Supplier profile and registration form
- Registered Certificate of firm

Deadline to submit the expression of interest is **Wed 9th December 2026.** The final deliverables of the assignment are expected by 15th February 2027 (exact date to be determined with the consultant(s))/consultancy firm.

## Evaluation of bids

DRC will evaluate the proposals and award the assignment based on technical and financial feasibility. DRC reserves the right to accept or reject any proposal received without giving reasons and is not bound to accept the lowest or the highest bidder. Only those shortlisted will be contacted. Any subcontracting of the consultancy will not be accepted.

jobs.title: Deputy Country Director - Operations
jobs.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Under the supervision of the Country Director, the Deputy Country Director for Operations will lead on the strategic direction and coordination of the field operations of ACF across Northern and Southern Yemen, being accountable for ensuring that the ACF humanitarian response implementation is effective and efficient.

The main responsibilities and challenges of the position will be as follows:
Provide leadership in strategic vision, context analysis and operational direction of the country officeContribute to the development, implementation and annual review of the country office strategy
Ensure continuous analysis of humanitarian needs and context dynamics across Yemen, to assess their possible implications for programme delivery, access and operational risks
Ensure quality and effective programme deliveryProvide leadership and oversight to ensure efficient, timely, accountable, and principled implementation of ACF programmes across all areas of intervention
Ensure programme implementation aligns with ACF's standards, donors' requirements, humanitarian principles, and relevant international standards
Lead operational coordination, and external representationSupport the Country Director in maintaining and strengthening strategic relationships with relevant authorities, donors, UN agencies, national and international NGOs, and other relevant stakeholders
Promote and strengthen partnerships with local and international organizations
Support ACF advocacy efforts through evidence-based operational analysis and engagement
Ensure tge development and direction of the mission field coordination structureProvide guidance and support in resolving operational, partnership, access, and stakeholder-related challenges
Support risk management and business continuity.

Profile :

You hold a Master's Degree in International Relations, Humanitarian Assistance, Political or Social Sciences, Economics, Business Administration or any related field.
You have at least 10 years of professional experience in the humanitarian sector, with a minimum of 5 years in management role and leading field operations. A previous experience coordinating implementation of multi-sectoral programs is considered an asset.
You demonstrate a strong leadership and decision-making abilities at strategic levels, good communication, representation, and influencing skills. You are recognised for your ability to work effectively under pressure, to adapt to changing circumstances, establish priorities and meet deadlines.
You master English (written and spoken) and have strong report writing, monitoring and evaluation skills and experience.
Additional language skills in Arabic, previous experience in the Middle-East and familiarity with the regional context are considered an asset.

Conditions d'emploi

Fixed term contract under French legislation: 6 months
Monthly gross salary from 2899 to 3376euros upon experience, including 13th month
Reimbursement of the pension insurance for non-French citizens: 16% of the gross monthly salary
Annual salary increase: 6% increase after and each 12 months of continuous contract
Monthly per diem and living allowance: 730 USD net, field paid
Monthly country allowance: 450euros
Child allowance: 1500euros per year per child present in the country of origin (maximum 6000euros/year)
Transportation and accommodation: Coverage of transportation costs and guest house
Medical coverage: ACF covers 100% of the health and repatriation insurance agreement fees, for your medical expenses (as well as your dependents if you have a family post), and up to 1 month after the end of your contract
Salary sustainment measures (sickness, paternity, maternity)
Leaves and RnR: 25 days of paid leaves per year, 20 RnR per year, airfare reimbursement with a ceiling to get to the chosen break destination, and 215 euros for each RnR period
Accompaniment and trainings:Follow-up and support for career development
Free and unlimited access to the e-learning platform Talentsoft
ACF is committed to people with disabilities and actively fights against all forms of discrimination.

jobs.title: MISSION FRANCE - MÉDIATEUR.RICE EN SANTÉ – LITTORAL NORD
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e médiateur.rice en santé projet Littoral Nord

**CONTEXTE**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et l’Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution.

Dans un contexte de forte vulnérabilité des personnes exilées à la frontière franco-britannique, le projet Littoral Nord vise à améliorer l’accès aux soins et à la protection des publics les plus exposés, tout en documentant les impacts sanitaires, psychologiques et sociaux des politiques migratoires. Il constitue un axe stratégique de la Mission France, à l’interface entre opérations de secours et plaidoyer.

**MISSION**

Sous la responsabilité du·de la Responsable de la promotion et de la médiation en santé, vous jouerez un rôle essentiel de lien entre les personnes exilées et le système de santé français, afin de faciliter leur accès aux soins et aux droits en santé.

Au plus près des personnes, vous contribuerez à lever les obstacles aux soins, à renforcer leur autonomie et à développer des actions de prévention, de promotion de la santé et d'engagement communautaire.

Votre mission associera présence sur le terrain, accompagnement individuel, sensibilisation et travail en équipe pluridisciplinaire.

**Vos principales responsabilités**

**Faciliter l'accès aux soins et accompagner les personnes**

- Aller à la rencontre des personnes exilées sur leurs lieux de vie, instaurer une relation de confiance et identifier leurs besoins en santé.
- Informer, orienter et accompagner les personnes vers les structures de soins et les dispositifs d'accès aux droits.
- Assurer le suivi des parcours de soins, notamment des situations complexes, en collaboration avec les équipes médicales, psychologiques et sociales.
- Identifier les obstacles à l'accès aux soins et contribuer à leur résolution.

**Développer la prévention et la promotion de la santé**

- Organiser et animer des actions individuelles et collectives de sensibilisation, d'éducation à la santé et de prévention.
- Participer à la conception d'outils de médiation et d'information adaptés aux besoins des personnes accompagnées.
- Favoriser la participation des communautés et renforcer leur capacité à agir pour leur santé.

**Contribuer aux activités communautaires et au suivi des besoins**

- Participer aux évaluations des besoins, à la surveillance communautaire et à l'identification des personnes nécessitant une orientation vers les soins.
- Recueillir les préoccupations, les retours et les difficultés rencontrées par les personnes accompagnées.
- Contribuer au suivi des activités, à la collecte des données et à l'amélioration continue des interventions.
- Participer aux interventions d'urgence, notamment après les naufrages, et veiller au respect des règles de sécurité et de protection des personnes.

**Profil recherché**
