jobs.title: Chief of Party, USDA Food for Peace Non-Emergency Program
jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Chief of Party, USDA Food for Peace Non-Emergency Program**, you will lead the overall management, implementation and representation of a proposed 3- to 5-year, approximately $70 million USDA-funded programme. You will oversee efforts to improve and sustain food security among extremely poor and socially marginalised populations through a Graduation through Agriculture-led Development Approach, combining agricultural value chain development, market systems strengthening and U.S.-sourced agricultural commodities. You will build strategic partnerships, promote adaptive management and social inclusion, and lead staff development and programme and financial reporting.

You will direct and oversee grant implementation to achieve strategic objectives through effective programme design, staffing, implementation and quality assurance. You will build relationships with governments, donors, local organisations and partners; support consortium members in maintaining programme quality; and address implementation challenges through stakeholder coordination and regular learning events. You will supervise senior international and national staff, strengthen technical capacity, and manage grant staff and consultants. You will establish effective reporting, evaluation and communication systems and submit accurate, timely donor reports. You will also manage the grant budget, ensure expenses comply with approved budgets and donor requirements, address grant management issues promptly, and perform other duties as required.

**Requirements include:**

- A minimum of 15 years of progressively increasing management responsibility in complex, multi-sectoral international projects, and at least five years of experience in fragile or post-conflict states such as Ethiopia preferred.
- Demonstrated technical expertise in food security and livelihoods and experience in managing program implementation and financial reporting.
- Experience with graduation programming preferred.
- Proven success serving in a leadership role for a project addressing issues related to resilience, agriculture, natural resource management, agribusiness, or similar is required, preferably in Horn of Africa sub-region.
- Familiarity with Ethiopia’s social, political, economic, and cultural landscape, and demonstrated ability to build and maintain relationships with host governments, donors, other donor-funded projects and stakeholders, local organizations, and partners preferred.
- Demonstrated experience in adaptive management and learning techniques highly encouraged.
- Experience with large Title II grants with USG food commodities, including Resilience Food Security Activity (RFSA), Development Food Security Activity (DFSA), and Development Food Assistance Programs (DFAP)s.
- Experience with market strengthening grants like Feed the Future (FtF) and Food for Progress (FFPr) preferred.
- Demonstrated experience in developing and managing alliances with the private sector is desirable.
- Familiarity with and commitment to addressing social inclusion in project sectors is required, as demonstrated by at least two years of senior-level experience working on projects that addressed such constraints.
- Proven leadership skills managing projects of a similar size and scope in developing countries facing complex, volatile, and uncertain contexts involving Title II commodities and/or cash transfer mechanisms.
- Demonstrate experience in recruiting, developing, and managing large and diverse teams in remote contexts, including with multiple sub-awardees.

**Required Language(s):**

- Fluency in oral and written English is required.
- Fluency in a local language is advantageous.

**Required travel and/or work environment accommodations**:

- Mandatory travel to implementation sites and regional, global meetings as required.
- Travel to the United States World Vision Washington, DC Office to meet with donors and other stakeholders.

**Position’s physical requirements**:

- Ability to sit for prolonged periods and use standard office equipment like computers and phones.
- Strong speaking and hearing ability for high-level meetings and liaison with government officials and stakeholders.

*Applicant Types Accepted:* Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted

**Note: The CoP position is contingent upon funding and donor approval and will be based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia with 25% of the time spent in targeted regions of Ethiopia.**

jobs.title: Programme Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Overview and Purpose**

The purpose of this role is to lead the Shared Future: Economic and Social Connection for Ukraine’s Veterans programme in Kharkiv region.

The Programme Coordinator will work with a dedicated team including an Interventions Expert, MEAL Expert, Project Officer, Procurement Officer and Driver.

**Job Title:** Programme Coordinator – Shared Future

**Reports to:** Deputy Programme Director

**Terms:** *1 yearFixed Term, Full time, Fully office based, unaccompanied*

**Location:** Ukraine

**Salary:** GB6 (€46,821– €52,024)

**Requirements:** This role is based in Kharkiv, Ukraine, with regular travel within the regional.

**Responsibilities**

The Programme Coordinator will lead the Shared Future programme, which aims to support veterans' economic and social integration. The role will drive the strategic design, implementation, and portfolio management of market-based interventions to eliminate structural barriers to veterans’ employment and entrepreneurship. The role oversees project budgets, adaptive management, and results measurement to continuously refine strategies and drive impact in compliance with organizational and donor standards. The role will also oversee Shared Future’s social reintegration component.

**Market Systems Analysis and Strategic Intervention Design**

- Lead market systems analysis to identify opportunities and constraints affecting veterans' economic reintegration.
- Develop and regularly update market systems strategies, theories of change, and intervention portfolios based on evidence and market intelligence.
- Ensure interventions are designed around facilitation principles, sustainability, scale, and systemic change rather than direct service delivery.
- Integrate inclusion considerations throughout programme design, ensuring equitable participation of women veterans, veterans with disabilities, internally displaced veterans, and other vulnerable groups.

**Partnership Facilitation and Programme Delivery**

- Build and manage strategic partnerships with employers, private sector firms, business associations, financial institutions, training providers, government agencies, veteran organisations, and other market actors.
- Facilitate collaboration between market actors to strengthen pathways for veterans’ economic reintegration.
- Together with the Interventions Expert, support market actors to test, adapt, and adopt innovative models that improve opportunities for veterans’ economic reintegration.
- Support Interventions Expert to implement interventions portfolio, ensuring activities remain responsive to market dynamics and stakeholder incentives.
- Support Project Officer to implement the programme’s social reintegration component.
- Manage project budgets, workplans, contracts, and partner performance in line with Concern and JERU processes and donor requirements.
- Represent the programme with donors, government stakeholders, private sector partners, and technical working groups.

**Results Measurement, Learning and Adaptive Management**

- In collaboration with the MEAL Expert ensure the implementation of market systems development-aligned monitoring, evaluation, and learning systems that measure behavioural change, systemic change, sustainability, scale, and inclusion outcomes.
- Use evidence to inform adaptive management decisions and continuously improve intervention effectiveness, facilitating reviews, learning sessions, and assessments to test assumptions and refine strategies.
- Generate and communicate evidence of programme results, learning, and impact through reports, case studies, presentations, and knowledge products.
- Strengthen team and partner capacity in market systems thinking, facilitation, results measurement, and adaptive programming.

**Additional Responsibilities:**

- Support JERU’s security and risk management system, including staff training, monitoring and reporting.
- All managers are responsible for upholding and promoting Concern’s values, demonstrating leadership on workplace equality, diversity and inclusion, and role modelling a positive safeguarding ethos.
- All managers are required to actively participate in any emergency response as and when required.

**Role Holder Requirements**

- Master’s degree in Economics, Business, Public Policy, Labor Market Development, or related field (or equivalent practical experience).
- 5-7+ years managing economic development or livelihoods programs, including minimum 3 years in management or technical advisory roles within market systems development.
- Prior commercial/for-profit sector management experience.
- Experience with armed forces, veterans, or economic reintegration initiatives.
- Demonstrated focus on facilitating systemic change (rather than direct service delivery), applying market systems development minimum standards, DCED results measurement, and disability-inclusive development principles.
- Proven ability to engage with private sector actors, market intermediaries, legislators, and regulatory bodies.
- Strong background in monitoring, results measurement, learning, and adaptive programme management.
- Strong programme management skills including quality assurance, risk and security management, financial management, donor engagement and safe programming approaches, including trauma-informed care.
- Excellent team leadership, facilitation, and interpersonal skills with proven influence, negotiation, and relationship-building capabilities across internal and external audiences.
- Excellent written and spoken English, paired with strong proposal and report writing skills. Proficiency in Ukrainian (spoken and written) is a distinct advantage.
- Commitment to organizational ethos and values.
- Proficiency in standard digital tools.

**We would also like:**

- You to be flexible and reliable.
- You to be culturally sensitive and empathic to others.
- You to be able to work under pressure and to strict deadlines.
- You to travel frequently to remote and insecure locations.

jobs.title: Deputy Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
**ABOUT SPARK MICROGRANTS**

Spark MicroGrants believes in a world where everyone lives with dignity and determines their own positive future. Spark has worked in 1000+ villages in 6 countries and has pioneered a community-driven development model in sub-Saharan Africa. Spark works with NGO and Government partners to scale the model's adoption and impact on rural communities - on their own terms. Our model combines facilitated community meetings with a small, discretionary grant to catalyze local action and institution building. Read more about our [Approach](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/the-spark-process), [Impact ](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/impact)and [Values ](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/about-spark#about-our-values)on our [website](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/).

**ABOUT YOUR TEAM**

**Spark is growing and adding a key finance leader to our team.** This role offers an accomplished finance leader the opportunity to develop CFO-level skills as a strategic partner to senior leadership in a growing international non-profit.

The Deputy CFO will oversee global financial planning and enterprise risk management, while also leading operational excellence initiatives in partnership with the CFO. They will receive structured guidance, coaching and support from an experienced CFO who has helped other finance leaders ascend to the CFO role, and an opportunity to take the next step in their career.

This role will suit a senior leader working in international development, and may also suit a current senior finance executive working in for-profit finance, looking to transition to the non-profit sector. In all cases, the successful candidate will have already demonstrated the ability to develop and lead strong teams. They will have shown their ability to provide value-added guidance to internal and/or external partners, and have a desire to leverage this experience to support local communities and champion community driven development.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**OVERVIEW**

The Deputy CFO will initially oversee Global Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), Enterprise Risk, Compliance, and coordination of outsourced legal support. As part of a structured path to get to know the organization and its’ processes, they will also coordinate the finance team’s progress towards increasing operational excellence, and will coordinate closely with the Head of Finance and the CFO on Global Accounting and Consolidation, Program Finance, and Internal Audit, among other Operations functions.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Global Financial Planning & Analysis**

- Guide and mentor the Manager/Senior Manager of FP&A
- Ensure the effectiveness of the annual and multi-year budget process, quarterly forecasting and the consolidated Budget vs Actual (BVA) review.
- Oversee forecasts of quarterly, annual and long-term revenue and cash flows
- Ensure donor budgets and financial proposals are effective, timely, and meet the needs of the growth team and donors.
- Conduct scenario planning and financial modeling to assess the impact of strategic initiatives.
- Ensure sustainable finance planning and oversee financial reserves.

**2. Operations: Compliance, Procurement, Legal, Treasury & Risk Management**

- Ensure compliance with regulatory and donor requirements, support donor due diligence, and ensure effective management of enterprise risk. There is some opportunity to structure these responsibilities to best leverage the candidate’s strengths and address their development needs.
- Work with outsourced legal counsel to address current and potential legal risks and ensure contract structures and processes are appropriate and effective.
- Ensure compliance with financial regulations and reporting standards across all operating countries, including US state and federal requirements.
- Oversee the monitoring and action plans for a comprehensive risk management framework for global operations.
- Oversee insurance coverage and risk mitigation strategies across all countries.
- Oversee treasury policies and practices,, including cash forecasting, foreign exchange risk, and ensuring appropriate funds are available in each region.
- Manage organizational reserves and ensure adequate cash flow for operations.
- Implement robust anti-fraud measures and secure financial systems.
- Own key global policies and procedures, including those related to finance, risk management, treasury and legal.

**3. Strategic Finance**

- Partner with the CFO and executive team to develop multi-year financial scenarios and strategies that support Spark’s long-term vision and growth
- Work closely with the C-suite, Executive Committee, CFO, and Head of Finance, to implement financial strategy, communicate financial information and translate financial information to effective decision making across the organization.
- Design and create effective materials for communicating financial information and informing decisions, including materials for the CEO, donors, and Board of Directors.
- Working closely with the Head of Finance, designs and prepares materials for the Board Finance Committee meeting.
- Oversee financial reserves, and provide guidance and analysis during planning processes to ensure appropriate trade-offs between funding strategic objectives and ensuring long term sustainability.
- Establish strong business intelligence and track key financial and operational KPIs to monitor organizational financial performance.
- Participate, present and lead strategic and management meetings, and act on behalf of the CFO when needed.

**4. Finance and Operations Team Leadership**

- Lead, coach and develop the Manager/Senior Manager, FP&A and provide guidance and support to the wider finance team across multiple countries and time zones.
- Set clear performance objectives, provide regular feedback, and support the professional development of finance team members.
- Oversee tracking and monitoring of finance & operations OKRs, metrics and stakeholder deliverables and drive execution on behalf of the CFO.

**5. Other Finance & Operations**

- Oversee financial policy and compliance, including designing and improving policies, and collaborating with the Finance team and across the organization to implement streamlined, efficient policies and practices.
- Work closely with the Head of Finance and the CFO to lead strategic finance and operations projects and initiatives.
- Depending on the candidate’s skills and experience, they may also be involved with accounting, external and/or internal audit, payments, and program cost analysis, whether initially or at a future date.

**WHO YOU ARE**

**QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.
- Professional accounting certification (CPA, ACCA, or equivalent) and/or MBA is desirable though not required.

**Experience**

- Minimum 12+ years of progressively responsible leadership experience in finance and accounting, though likely significantly more, including senior leadership roles, preferably in an NGO or international development context.
- Candidates with significant experience managing finance staff is expected.
- Top candidates will have finance and/or accounting experience in multi-country financial operations, ideally including experience with consolidation, budgeting, and reporting.
- Knowledge of accounting principles, internal controls and compliance requirements.
- Strong background in FP&A, financial modeling and scenario analysis, preferably including donor budgets, is preferred.
- Experience in the preparation and effective presentation of financial information to executive leadership, funders and Board members is preferred.
- Demonstrated use of AI tools to improve analysis and efficiency.
- Experience leading internal and external audits, tax compliance, contracts and/or regulatory reporting is desirable.Experience implementing financial systems, controls and tools is strongly preferred and direct experience with NetSuite, Google Workspace, and business intelligence tools is helpful.

**Skills and Competencies**

- Ability to support, adapt to, and anticipate organizational growth and change.
- Proactivity and enjoys working in a fast-paced, multi-country environment.
- Strong leadership, coaching and team management skills.

jobs.title: Program Design Director
jobs.description:
**ABOUT SPARK MICROGRANTS**

Spark MicroGrants believes in a world where everyone lives with dignity and determines their own positive future. Spark has worked in 1000+ villages in 6 countries and has pioneered a community-driven development model in sub-Saharan Africa. Spark works with NGO and Government partners to scale the model's adoption and impact on rural communities - on their own terms. Our model combines facilitated community meetings with a small, discretionary grant to catalyze local action and institution building. Read more about our [Approach](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/the-spark-process), [Impact ](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/impact)and [Values ](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/about-spark#about-our-values)on our [website](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/).

**WHO YOU ARE**

We are seeking an experienced Program Design Director to lead Spark’s curriculum design and training functions across our global portfolio. The role will provide strategic direction and quality assurance for program designs, training, and facilitation, ensuring approaches are grounded in co-design principles, adapted to local contexts, and aligned with program and organizational goals and processes. The Program Design Director will manage and develop the design team, strengthen Spark’s systems, tools, and standards, and guide the thoughtful adoption of innovations that strengthen design quality and delivery.

The Program Design Director will report to the Senior Program Design Director and oversee a team of managers responsible for training and curriculum development across Spark’s countries of operation. They will work closely with other units within the Program Design Department to deliver consistent, high-quality design across the organization. The team will support Programs and Innovation teams to design quality programs, pilots, and technical assistance in line with organizational goals.

The role is ideal for someone with strong experience in program design and team leadership, passionate about community-driven development and human-centered design, and skilled in coordinating across teams, communicating clearly, and empowering others to do their best work. You are passionate about designing programs, pilots, and systems that are effective, scalable, and center the communities we serve. You bring technical experience in designing large scale training programs, curriculum and facilitation materials, and community-driven development.

RESPONSIBILITIES

**Responsibility: Strategic Leadership and Team Management**

**Duties:**

1. Championing a culture of feedback, learning and iteration to ensure Spark’s curriculum design and training systems continue to adapt, improve, and lead program quality and innovation.
2. Drive team strategy including setting and achieving team and organizational goals. Manage, develop and retain the design team by setting clear responsibility domains and deliverables, leading through empowerment, and investing in their growth through coaching and support.
3. Manage design budgets to ensure consistency with strategic priorities and available funding and that activities make cost-effective use of resources and optimize for program ROI.
4. Lead to day to day running of strategically important projects, ensuring that all projects are delivered on-time, within scope and within budget.
5. Oversee technical specialists or consultants to provide needed technical expertise or support
6. Serve as a coordinator across the portfolio, keeping teams, leadership, and external partners aligned on priorities, timelines, and decisions.

**Responsibility:** Develop and lead Spark’s curriculum design and training functions

**Duties:**

1. Quality assure curriculum design, training, and facilitation across all Spark projects, ensuring that approaches are in line with program and organizational goals and standards
2. Oversee end-to-end design of assigned programs and pilots, supervising relevant Program Design Leads and providing quality assurance of final products. This may include supporting design of Innovation pilots and technical assistance to external stakeholders, including the World Bank.
3. Develop and maintain templates, tools, examples, and standard operating procedures related to curriculum, training, and design team activities to support consistent and high-quality design processes. Integrate human-centered design and co-design best practices and innovations to co-create programs with the communities they serve.
4. Develop innovative technical and technological tools for design, training and implementation, based on program and partner needs. These include remote training tools, remote assessment and feedback systems, and facilitation guides. Guide teams in integrating new tools and technologies into their work, applying judgement about which tools add value.
5. Provide technical expertise to inform the design of internal and external program evaluations, research, and growth opportunities.

**Responsibility: Industry leading learning and quality assurance**

**Duties:**

1. Maintain and enhance learning platforms across our global portfolio, identifying shared lessons and trends, and helping Spark teams to re-embed learning into programming.
2. Stay abreast of industry evidence and learning, including emerging co-design and human-centered design practices, and translate lessons into practical program design and management tools.
3. Lead the development, validation, and updating of assigned "Design Standards" outlining minimum standards and guidance on core elements of the FCAP model
4. Manage cross-departmental collaboration to deliver high-quality program design outputs

**REQUIREMENTS:**

Qualifications, experience & skills:

- 8-10 years of relevant experience, such as in program design, delivering high quality research and technology tools, community-driven development, and human-centered design
- Masters Degree in the field of Economics, International Development, Product Design, or related fields
- Excellent track record in designing and managing rural development programs and/or community-driven development projects
- Proven track record of developing and deploying program design tools, such as training guides, workplans, and partnership agreements
- Demonstrated experience in team management and development
- Experience designing programs or initiatives at regional or national scale is a strength
- Experience working with the World Bank on designing or implementing operations is a strength
- Experience working with local or central government on design or implementation activities is a strength
- Ability to operate independently and strong in working as part of a larger team
- Strong project management skills and attention to detail are required
- Experience in strategy development is desirable
- Excellent English written and oral communication

jobs.title: Finance Manager
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Cash and Markets Project Manager Ukraine - open to internal candidates
jobs.description:
**What we are looking for**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is seeking an experienced and driven Cash & Markets Project Manager to lead the implementation of multi-sectoral cash assistance programming across Ukraine. This is a unique opportunity to join a high-impact operation that has supported hundreds of thousands of conflict-affected people through innovative, technology-enabled humanitarian assistance.

Working at the heart of NRC's Ukraine response, you will oversee complex cash programmes, manage high-performing teams, strengthen digital delivery systems, and ensure vulnerable households receive timely, safe, and dignified assistance.

**We are looking for candidates that are diplomatic, curious and solution driven, and keen on driving operational effectiveness. If you're ready to lead, innovate, and make a meaningful difference for people affected by conflict, we'd like to hear from you.**

**Applicants must be internal and legally eligible to work in Ukraine. We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.**

**What you will do**

- Lead the implementation and quality delivery of NRC's multi-sectoral cash assistance programmes.
- Manage project planning, budgets, workplans, reporting, and donor compliance.
- Supervise and develop a skilled cash programming team. Work closely with the Area Offices to deploy assets to support cash programming, find solutions for reaching vulnerable populations, and ensuring cash programming delivery aligns with standards and country-criteria.
- Drive the effective use and improvement of digital cash systems, including platforms such as RedRose, Salesforce, Twilio/WhatsApp, and related tools.
- Support rapid emergency cash responses for households affected by conflict and displacement while ensuring safe and equitable delivery of cash assistance to households most in need.
- Strengthen coordination with area offices, partners, and key stakeholders to expand reach and impact.
- Oversee data-driven targeting, reporting, analysis, and quality assurance processes.
- Champion accountability, information security, and protection of participant data.
- Contribute to programme innovation, systems enhancement, and evidence-based decision-making.

**What you will bring**

- Minimum 5 years of programme or project management experience, Knowledge and experience in cash and market systems programming ideally within humanitarian or emergency response settings.
- Demonstrated experience managing teams, budgets, and complex projects.
- Experience working in challenging and rapidly changing contexts.
- Strong analytical skills and experience using data to inform programming decisions.
- Familiarity with participant management systems, CRMs, digital platforms, or humanitarian data systems.
- Outstanding communication, stakeholder engagement, and coordination skills.
- Fluency in English and working knowledge of Ukrainian or Russian.

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAATFzd8BQnRrrgDV_DLwBfAcweuUTlv_QeN_6ylFuS1zY?e=CpCQNV) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- This is an Hybrid position.
- Duty station: Kyiv, Ukraine, with possibility to be hosted from other NRC Ukraine offices
- Fixed term contract: 12 months national contract.
- Travel: Up to 30%
- Salary/benefits: Grade 8 on NRC's national grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

**Important information about the application process**

- We invite applications from qualified internal candidates matching the profile. **Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Ukraine, we are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.**
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV and a cover letter.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

- The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.
- [Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.
- We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:
- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

[Learn more about NRC Ukraine](https://www.nrc.no/countries/europe/ukraine/)

**JOB TITLE:**

Program coordinator - Pro 0001

**DEPARTEMENT:**

Program

**BASE LOCATION:**

IR Syria Office - Damascus

**REPORTING TO:**

Head of Programs

**THE ORGANISATION:**

Since 2012, Islamic Relief Syria, part of Islamic Relief Worldwide, has provided humanitarian and development assistance across Syria, reaching millions of people affected by conflict and displacement through emergency relief, food security and livelihoods, WASH, health, education, shelter and non-food assistance. As the context in Syria has evolved, Islamic Relief has adapted its programming from predominantly emergency response towards early recovery, resilience and rehabilitation, supporting the restoration of essential services and infrastructure, livelihoods and economic recovery, while continuing to address humanitarian needs and promote protection, inclusion and social cohesion.

**PURPOSE OF DEPARTMENT:** The department reinforces IRW’s implementing structure to enable these people and their communities to develop themselves sustainable and ensures that the organization is prepared to respond promptly and effectively to humanitarian crises. The department increases the organisation’s ability to tackle poverty by developing and fostering partnerships and institutional relationships effectively and proactively, and by ensuring transparent and timely reporting to the organisation’s donors.

**JOB PURPOSE:** The Program coordinator supports the Head of Programmes in ensuring effective programme planning, quality implementation, grant management, proposal development, reporting and documentation. The position coordinates programme information across teams and ensures that projects remain aligned with approved plans, donor requirements and IRW standards.

**KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

- Reports to: HoP/Deputy CD
- Work closely with: Project teams and all other departments

**ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:**

- Prepare and submit quality reports monthly, quarterly, and annual to donors.
- Prepare and submit quality CN and proposals
- Prepare weekly, monthly, and annual Work plans in Coordination with relevant staff members.
- Ensure Archiving of all documents related to the conducted activities; hard and soft

**SCOPE AND AUTHORITY**

**Scope of the Role:**

The Program coordinator under the supervision of the HoP is responsible to improve the program quality and results by:

- Guaranteeing quality, efficiency, and effectiveness of reports and proposals
- Coordinate and fully implement projects in close coordination with Program team
- Follow up with the program team to ensure archiving of all the projects

**KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:**

**A. Programme Planning and Coordination**

- Coordinate the preparation and regular review of weekly, monthly and annual programme workplans.
- Follow up with project teams on implementation progress, planned activities, targets and timelines.
- Consolidate programme updates and highlight delays, challenges and implementation gaps to the Head of Programmes.
- Facilitate programme coordination and review meetings and follow up on agreed actions.
- Support programme teams in ensuring implementation is aligned with approved proposals, budgets and workplans.
- Contribute to the development and review of the Country Strategy and Annual Business Plan.

**B. Proposal Development and Business Development**

- Coordinate the preparation of concept notes and project proposals in collaboration with relevant programme and support departments.
- Monitor funding opportunities and maintain an updated donor and funding opportunity database.
- Coordinate the preparation of logframes, indicators, activity plans and budget inputs.
- Ensure proposals are aligned with IRW strategic priorities, community needs and donor requirements.
- Follow up on proposal development timelines and ensure timely submission.

**C. Reporting and Grant Follow-up**

- Coordinate the preparation and submission of monthly, quarterly, annual and donor-specific reports.
- Maintain an updated reporting calendar and ensure timely collection of inputs from project teams.
- Review and consolidate project reports to ensure consistency, accuracy and quality.
- Coordinate with MEAL to ensure that reported achievements are supported by reliable data and evidence.
- Consolidate project OnTrack updates and share them with the Head of Programmes and MEAL team.
- Follow up on donor requirements, reporting deadlines and outstanding grant deliverables.
- Maintain an overview of project progress against approved targets, indicators and timelines.

**D. MEAL, Learning and Documentation**

- Coordinate with MEAL to ensure that assessments, monitoring findings, evaluations, case studies and lessons learned are documented and reflected in programme reports.
- Facilitate the documentation and sharing of programme achievements, good practices and lessons learned.
- Follow up with project teams to ensure proper archiving of project documents, both electronically and in hard copy.
- Ensure project files are regularly updated and complete throughout the project cycle, including at project closure.

**E. External Coordination and Representation**

- Coordinate IRW participation in relevant cluster and sector working group meetings.
- Follow up on the timely submission of 4Ws/5Ws and other required coordination information.
- Maintain constructive working relationships with relevant NGOs, UN agencies, local authorities and other stakeholders.
- Attend coordination meetings, workshops and forums as delegated by the line manager.
- Share relevant coordination updates and information with programme teams.

**F. Other Responsibilities**

- Undertake other duties assigned by the line manager.
- Support other departments as required and agreed with the line manager.
- Ensure compliance with IRW policies, procedures, Code of Conduct and donor requirements.
- Promote the integration of gender, protection, safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, disability inclusion, accountability to affected populations and Do No Harm principles across programme activities.

**4. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

- Bachelor's degree in Development Studies, Social Sciences, International Relations, Management or another relevant field.
- Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in programme coordination, project management, grants management or reporting.
- Previous experience working with an NGO/INGO is required.
- Demonstrated experience in proposal development, donor reporting and programme coordination.
- Good understanding of Results-Based Management (RBM) and the project cycle.
- Experience coordinating with MEAL and other support departments.
- Good understanding of donor requirements and budget management principles.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in Arabic and English; French is an advantage.
- Good computer skills, particularly Microsoft Office.

**5. COMPETENCY PROFILE**

- Strong coordination, planning and organisational skills.
- Good proposal writing and reporting skills.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
- Ability to coordinate multiple tasks and meet deadlines.
- Good interpersonal and communication skills.
- Ability to work effectively with multidisciplinary teams.
- Attention to detail and commitment to quality.
- Ability to work independently and take initiative.
- Understanding of gender, diversity, inclusion and accountability.
- Knowledge of humanitarian standards, including Sphere, CHS, Do No Harm and safeguarding principles.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

- Bachelor’s degree in development studies, Social Sciences, International Relations, Law, Management or a relevant field.
- Minimum **3 years of relevant experience** in programme/project management, grants management, reporting or proposal development.
- Previous experience with an NGO/INGO is required.
- Proven experience in proposal development, donor reporting and programme coordination.
- Good understanding of Results-Based Management and the programme cycle.
- Experience working with MEAL teams and using quantitative and qualitative programme data.
- Good understanding of budgeting and donor compliance requirements.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills in **Arabic and English**;
- Good knowledge of Microsoft Office and programme/grants management systems.

**Languages:**

A high level of spoken and written Arabic and English is essential.

All staff are required to contribute to the achievement of this framework.

**Background and Organisational Setting**

SoH is a Christian motivated organisation for Human Rights, Humanitarian Assistance and Development Cooperation. Based in Constance, Germany, SoH is dedicated to helping those in distress and exploited people worldwide.

An audit is commissioned under the German Federal Ministry of Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) funding guidelines for development projects run by private German executing agencies.

SoH will be the private German executing agency and the contracting party, with Koinoniabeing the local implementing agency.

This project aims to improve the living conditions of 2,500 people in five vulnerable villages located in the Saghata Upazila (Gaibandha District, Rangpur Division), Bangladesh significantly. These communities face recurring challenges due difficult weather conditions (floods, drought, etc.). They lack adequate coping mechanisms, which result in severe food insecurity and malnutrition, especially amongst children. The project's primary focus is to bolster their resilience to cope with the changing climate conditions. To achieve this, a range of diverse activities will be introduced. The proposed initiatives include providing comprehensive training on innovative agricultural techniques, fostering income-generating activities and establishing self-help groups to advocate for their civil rights, among others.

**Audit Objectives**

The purpose of the in-depth audit is to provide SoH with a sound basis for its accountability, transparency and accuracy in the financial disclosure towards the funding agency BMZ. The tasks of this recruitment relate to:

- An annual audit, with a detailed examination of all the supporting documents for the period of 01.01.2026 – 31.12.2026;

This in-depth audit will verify the compliance with standards of the funding agency BMZ, SoH, national regulations and the international accounting standards (ISA).

The auditor will review all of the project’s financial documents, receipts lists, records of transactions, all vouchers and receipts disbursed, and relevant project documents in order to come up with a professional, independent opinion on the financial accounting of the project “Promoting sustainable livelihoods and food security initiative in Saghata Upazila, Bangladesh” for all funds received and expended by Koinonia from 1st January 2026 to 31st December 2026.

Additionally, the audit shall give recommendations on strengths, weaknesses, and required improvement in the project-related financial and human resources management systems of Koinonia.

The audit will support the project quality assurance measures implemented by SoH and contribute to the decision-making process with regard to the project management and monitoring of finances by SoH and Koinonia.

**Expected Deliverables**

The auditor is expected to produce an audit report, an audit certificate and a management letter, which will comprise the following:

1. Presentation of the scope and mandate of the audit, as well as the list of documents that formed the evidence for the audit,
2. An opinion whether financial statements (statement of accounts broken down for each year being audited) are issued in accordance with the financial reporting framework of the project, BMZ requirements and an internationally recognized accounting standard,
3. A checked, signed and stamped list of all (100%) project costs receipts, sorted by BMZ budget lines (list is provided by the local implementing partner).
4. Recommendations on identified shortcomings, and, if applicable, comments on the follow-up of audit observations and recommendations from previous years.
5. FD-4 Report according to Bangladeshi Law.

Audit documents can be issued in English or German.

**Scope of the Audit**

The audit should focus on the following:

- The correctness and completeness of the accounting records,
- The financial report, showing all project related income and expenditure structured by budget lines,
- Deviations of expenditure by budget lines. The expenditure, which exceeds or falls below the budget appropriations by more than 30 %, shall be explained separately, if the approval of the BMZ has not previously been obtained,
- That receipts and relevant supporting documents are available for all project related income and expenditures (100% verification),
- The management of the funds made available, which includes the transfer of project funds, all interest earned from the project funds during the reporting period and further income generated by the project,
- Reviewing the appropriate use of funds according to the project objectives,
- Evaluation of the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of the usage of funds,
- Budget adherence through the comparison between budgeted and actual costs in the currency in which the expenditure was incurred. The audit report will not convert the examined amounts into the Euro amounts,
- Reviewing if personnel costs and social security contributions conform to the regulations in the project country and are locally comparable,
- The economical use of the project equipment and assets,
- The inventory and the use of capital items, their whereabouts and their purposive usage,
- Compliance with the legal framework of the project (project agreements and annexes, contracts, etc.) and the donor requirements,
- Compliance with the policies of the local implementing partner regarding procurement, financial administration, human resources management and travel.

**Procedures and Communication**

The auditor will be given access to all necessary documents in the project offices through the local implementing partner Koinonia as well as relevant donor documents through SoH.

The auditor will be responsible to set up a schedule in agreement with the local implementing partner Koinonia. Any expenses for field trips, postal and translation services and other expenses shall be included in the auditor’s proposed budget. Koinonia will support the auditor with logistics and arrangements, however, all payments of the contract will be made directly by SoH.

**Qualifications and Experience**

- Necessary qualification to serve as a recognized independent auditing authority,
- Minimum of five (5) years of experience conducting external independent audits of projects funded by international institutional donors in Bangladesh,
- Experience in conducting audits for BMZ-funded projects is desirable.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Major Giving (Southwest)
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview/ Summary:**

The External Relations (ER) department is comprised of three main but complementary functional areas: Private fundraising, Communications, and Advocacy. The main objective of the department is to enable this organization of more than 15,000 staff to have the resources needed to continue serving 18 million people worldwide in places affected by war and disaster. The Philanthropy unit, part of the ER department, leads on the organization’s work with High-Net-Worth Individuals.

Positioned within the USA Philanthropy department, the Major Giving West team has a goal of growing private individual support for the IRC by engaging, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding significant, multi-year commitments from high-net-worth individual supporters based in the Western United States (West of the Mississippi River).

The Associate Director of Major Giving, Southwest will be a dynamic seasoned fundraiser and relationship cultivator who will work closely with the Director of USA Philanthropy’s Major Giving West/Southwest team to build a strategy to support a growing portfolio of high-net-worth individuals. With a geographic focus on the Los Angeles and Southern California region, the Associate Director will serve as a relationship manager throughout the donor life cycle, working across fundraising teams and cross-functional teams with senior leadership to qualify, cultivate, solicit, and steward five, six, and seven-figure gifts, using donor-centric fundraising practices and deploying program and IRC leaders. They will also build a strong donor pipeline of major gift donor prospects and increase regional revenue.

**Priority will be given to candidates with existing work authorization in the location(s) where the position is advertised.**

The ideal candidate is an entrepreneurial professional who has demonstrated experience understanding the motivations of philanthropists and can assess the inclination of a donor or prospect’s willingness to make a significant gift to the IRC over a number of years.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Grow and manage a dynamic portfolio of high-net-worth individuals by moving the IRC's relationship with each through cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
- Participate in active prospect discovery through relationship and network mapping. Qualify prospects using research and discovery to unearth new donor relationships.
- Design creative and meaningful engagement opportunities for area donors to learn and connect with the IRC’s programs and leadership working across functions and teams, with participation from key existing donors and leadership volunteers.
- Co-create and deploy strategic correspondence, including solicitations, cultivation pieces, reports, and other stewardship materials, to engage donors and prospects.
- Design tactics and creative, long-term engagement strategy to deepen donor dedication and increase giving.
- Choreograph, prepare strategy, and briefing and debriefing materials for face-to-face meetings and solicitations with Major donors conducted personally and/or by senior staff and Board leadership.
- Collaborate with colleagues across the IRC, institutional fundraising colleagues, and field staff, to align donor and organizational priorities in a way that increases income for the IRC and builds multi-layered, deep engagement with the organization.
- Work collaboratively with Account Managers to strategize, actively track, and measure progress toward financial goals and movement of prospects and donors across the donor lifecycle.
- Undertake special projects as requested.

**Candidate Requirements:**

- 6-8 years of progressive fundraising experience and demonstrated expertise in private sector, major gifts, or major gifts fundraising; or sales, including direct solicitation of donors or clients.
- Knowledge of and experience working with the philanthropic community in the Los Angeles metro area

**Preferred Experience & Skills:**

- Proven track record of closing 5 and 6-figure gifts from a dynamic portfolio of donors and prospects, including qualifying prospects and upgrading donors;
- Consistent record of developing blended and multi-year funding opportunities;
- Outstanding communication skills, including writing, listening, verbal presentation, and speaking;
- Ability to develop creative and nuanced donor strategy often carried out in partnership with program staff or senior leadership;
- Adaptable to change in a fast-paced work environment while keeping donor priorities at the center of strategy and relationship building;
- Ability to diplomatically and sensitively collaborate across teams internally, regardless of distance, and garner support for and implement initiatives effectively;
- Ability to identify, build, and implement processes vital to supporting effective donor relationships;
- Ability to analyze and interpret financial data;
- Ability to navigate CRM systems;
- Dedication to fundraising for international development, humanitarian, human rights, gender and racial equality, social justice, and US immigrant communities.

**Working Environment*****:*** Requires remote/flex-time work.

**Commitment to Diversity and Inclusivity:**

IRC is committed to building a diverse organization and a climate of inclusivity. We strongly encourage applications from candidates who can demonstrate that they can contribute to this goal.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:**

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

**Compensation:** ($109,986 – $157,279 / annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Servicios Expertos en Manejo de Información con énfasis en Sistemas de Información Geográfica
jobs.description:
**Términos de Referencia-Servicios Expertos en Manejo de Información con énfasis en Sistemas de Información Geográfica**

**Organización:** 3iS

**Dirección de Oficina:** Calle 92 #15-78

**Denominación de los Servicios:** Experto en Manejo de Información con énfasis en Sistemas de Información Geográfica

**Domicilio Contractual:** Bogotá D.C.

**Tipo de Contrato:** Contrato de Prestación de Servicios

**Fecha esperada de Inicio:** Lo antes posible.

**Fecha de terminación del contrato:** 30 de abril de 2027

**Honorarios:** COP 6.000.000 – 8.000.000

## **Organización**

*3iS es una organización internacional sin fines de lucro cuya función es brindar servicios de gestión de información a organizaciones humanitarias y de desarrollo, permitiendo a los socios tomar decisiones informadas que, en última instancia, brindan asistencia específica de alta calidad a las poblaciones más vulnerables del mundo. 3iS convierte los datos en información y crea conocimiento para los tomadores de decisiones que operan en conflictos, desastres, entornos posteriores a desastres y recuperación, así como otras situaciones de emergencias complejas y contextos de desarrollo.*

**Contexto**

El proyecto tiene como objetivo fortalecer la capacidad de respuesta ante emergencias de organizaciones nacionales, organizaciones comunitarias, comunidades y autoridades locales en la Cuenca Amazónica, con el fin de mejorar la preparación, coordinación y respuesta frente a emergencias de origen natural y/o antropogénico.

La intervención surge en un contexto caracterizado por el aumento de riesgos asociados al cambio climático, la degradación ambiental, la expansión de economías ilícitas, la presencia de actores armados y las limitadas capacidades institucionales en amplias zonas de la Amazonía. Estos factores han incrementado la vulnerabilidad de comunidades indígenas, rurales y ribereñas frente a eventos como inundaciones, sequías, incendios forestales, desplazamientos forzados y otras crisis humanitarias.

El proyecto se implementa en zonas priorizadas de Bolivia, Brasil, Colombia, Ecuador, Perú y Venezuela, y combina el fortalecimiento de capacidades de organizaciones nacionales, comunitarias y autoridades, la coordinación regional a través de una red humanitaria y la generación de información y análisis que apoyen la toma de decisiones, incluido el monitoreo de la situación humanitaria y del desplazamiento interno.

La iniciativa incorpora de manera transversal los enfoques de género, edad, inclusión y protección, garantizando la participación activa de mujeres, jóvenes, pueblos indígenas y otros grupos en situación de vulnerabilidad en los procesos de preparación, respuesta y fortalecimiento de resiliencia comunitaria.

**Objetivo de la consultoría**

Generar, gestionar y analizar información geoespacial de calidad que permita a los actores humanitarios, organizaciones locales y autoridades de la cuenca amazónica contar con datos periódicos, análisis oportunos y un monitoreo continuo de la situación humanitaria —con énfasis en el desplazamiento interno y en los factores ambientales y de violencia que lo generan—, y que estos productos resulten útiles para comprender el contexto, facilitar la coordinación y fundamentar decisiones de preparación, priorización y respuesta.

Los análisis geoespaciales también apoyarán la gestión del riesgo y la acción anticipatoria, incluida la identificación y validación de variables e indicadores hidrometeorológicos y ambientales, así como criterios de seguimiento y umbrales de activación temprana, en articulación con fuentes oficiales, protocolos territoriales y el mecanismo digital de coordinación y comunicación

## **Descripción de los Servicios**

La persona contratada será responsable de diseñar, implementar y mantener el componente geoespacial del sistema de monitoreo de la situación humanitaria en la cuenca amazónica (Bolivia, Brasil, Colombia, Ecuador, Perú y Venezuela), integrando datos secundarios, información de teledetección y reportes de organizaciones locales y de la Red Humanitaria de la Cuenca Amazónica. A partir de ello, elaborará mapas, tableros y análisis espaciales que alimenten los productos de información periódicos (boletines, informes de situación, análisis temáticos e informe regional de análisis humanitario) y atenderá las solicitudes de productos geoespaciales recibidas a través de EVIDESK.

Adicionalmente, brindará soporte geoespacial a los demás componentes de la acción, asegurará la aplicación de estándares comunes de datos espaciales y de protección de datos a lo largo del ciclo de gestión de la información, y servirá de enlace con proveedores de imágenes satelitales y con otros actores técnicos para el intercambio de información geográfica.

**Actividades**

**A. Actividades específicas:**

**1. Monitoreo de la situación humanitaria y del desplazamiento interno**

- Diseñar e implementar, en coordinación con el equipo de gestión de información, el componente geoespacial del sistema de monitoreo de la situación humanitaria: variables, fuentes, unidades territoriales de análisis, frecuencia de actualización y criterios de alerta.
- Apoyar técnicamente la selección, análisis y validación de variables e indicadores hidrometeorológicos y ambientales que puedan utilizarse para construir umbrales de seguimiento y activación temprana por unidades territoriales pertinentes (por ejemplo, subcuencas), considerando series históricas, fuentes oficiales, resolución espacial y temporal, y la relación entre condiciones observadas e impactos registrados.
- En apoyo al analista de datos, compilar, depurar, integrar y actualizar periódicamente datos secundarios de fuentes oficiales, humanitarias, ambientales, científicas y de gestión del riesgo de los seis países
- Monitorear, mediante análisis espacial y teledetección, la deforestación y el cambio en el uso del suelo, las fuentes de contaminación (minería ilegal, derrames de petróleo y escorrentía de agroquímicos), los incendios forestales y los eventos hidrometeorológicos (inundaciones, sequías y niveles de los ríos) que actúan como multiplicadores de riesgo.
- Desarrollar y aplicar metodologías innovadoras y costo-eficientes para identificar, georreferenciar y analizar dinámicas de desplazamiento interno vinculadas a crisis climáticas, degradación ambiental y violencia, especialmente en zonas de difícil acceso donde las evaluaciones tradicionales son limitadas.
- Integrar espacialmente los reportes de organizaciones locales, puntos focales de la Red y alertas comunitarias canalizadas por el mecanismo digital de coordinación, aplicando procedimientos de verificación, triangulación y control de calidad.
- Incorporar, cuando sean pertinentes y hayan sido definidos o validados por las propias comunidades, señales comunitarias, bioindicadores e indicadores locales asociados a cambios ambientales o hidrometeorológicos, incluyendo conocimientos ancestrales de pueblos indígenas. Estos insumos deberán documentarse y contextualizarse territorialmente, respetando su origen y condiciones de uso, y triangularse con información técnica y fuentes oficiales, sin sustituir las competencias de las autoridades para la emisión de alertas oficiales.
- Incorporar datos desglosados por sexo, edad, discapacidad y pertenencia étnica cuando estén disponibles, para visibilizar riesgos y necesidades diferenciadas.

**2. Productos de información y análisis**

- Elaborar mapas, tableros geográficos, visores e infografías espaciales que alimenten los boletines, los informes de situación ante emergencias específicas (sequías, inundaciones, incendios, etc), los análisis temáticos y el informe regional de análisis humanitario, así como sus materiales de difusión (resúmenes ejecutivos, mapas y notas informativas).
- Contribuir a los productos de información y análisis temáticos que se difunden a nivel regional con socios humanitarios y de desarrollo, el donante y las organizaciones de redes en la Cuenca Amazónica, visibilizando tendencias, patrones de impacto, riesgos emergentes y brechas en la respuesta.
- Adaptar los productos a distintas audiencias, incluyendo formatos ligeros para contextos de baja conectividad y para públicos no especializados, en coordinación con el/la experto/a en comunicación y conforme a los lineamientos de visibilidad del donante y a la identidad visual común del programa.
- Presentar los productos de información en reuniones de coordinación, espacios de la Red y foros regionales de preparación, cuando así se requiera.

**3. Servicio de información bajo demanda (EVIDESK)**

- Atender las solicitudes de productos geoespaciales recibidas a través de EVIDESK de acuerdo con la priorización acordada según su relevancia para la respuesta y la disponibilidad de recursos, dando prioridad a los temas de interés común
- Registrar, dar seguimiento y cerrar oportunamente las solicitudes en EVIDESK, documentando tiempos de respuesta, productos entregados y usuarios atendidos.
- Promover el uso de EVIDESK y de los canales digitales de comunicación y coordinación entre las organizaciones de la Red, los socios del consorcio y las autoridades locales y nacionales.

**4. Soporte geoespacial a los demás componentes de la acción**

- **Organizaciones nacionales:** cuando se requiera, proveer cartografía base y capas de amenaza y riesgo ambiental para la elaboración de productos.
- **Preparación comunitaria:** apoyar, cuando se requiera procesos de cartografía participativa comunitaria y aportar información técnica (precipitación, niveles de los ríos, puntos de calor, contaminación) para la definición de umbrales de activación temprana.
- **Mecanismo digital y acción anticipatoria:** apoyar la construcción y documentación de matrices de variables, fuentes y umbrales por amenaza y territorio/subcuenca; relacionar los resultados técnicos con señales comunitarias, bioindicadores, protocolos y acciones tempranas; y facilitar su integración e interoperabilidad con el mecanismo digital de coordinación y comunicación (ANTICIPA u otra solución que adopte el proyecto), así como con otras plataformas y fuentes oficiales pertinentes
- **Coordinación con autoridades y otros actores:** elaborar productos cartográficos que apoyen la toma de decisiones y contribuir a la capacitación de los puntos focales en herramientas de reporte georreferenciado cuando así se requiera.
- **Respuesta a emergencias:** producir de manera rápida mapas y análisis de población expuesta cuando se requiera.

**5. Gestión de datos, calidad y protección**

- Aplicar principios de protección de datos en todo el ciclo: minimización, controles de acceso, anonimización y agregación de la información, y manejo especialmente cuidadoso de los datos de localización en zonas especiales, de conformidad con la evaluación de impacto en protección de datos de la acción, la normativa de la Unión Europea y las políticas de 3iS.
- Definir flujos de recolección e intercambio de información adaptados a la baja conectividad, en coordinación con el equipo técnico.
- Documentar las metodologías, fuentes y procesos utilizados (fichas metodológicas, metadatos y lecciones aprendidas), incluidas las metodologías de análisis de desplazamiento y de validación de la información.
- Servir de enlace en temas de información geográfica con proveedores de imágenes satelitales y con otros actores técnicos (observatorios, academia, organismos internacionales y plataformas de coordinación) para facilitar el intercambio de datos y la coherencia en la gestión de la información.

**6. Seguimiento, utilidad de los productos y reportes**

- Contribuir a medir la utilidad de los productos de información: incorporar mecanismos de retroalimentación en los productos difundidos, apoyar las encuestas de satisfacción a usuarios (actores humanitarios y organizaciones locales) y sistematizar sus resultados para ajustar los productos a las necesidades identificadas cuando así se requiera.
- Registrar la información necesaria para el seguimiento de los indicadores del componente de información (productos elaborados, solicitudes atendidas, usuarios alcanzados y valoraciones de utilidad) cuando sea solicitado por M&E.
- Preparar reportes mensuales de avance con el estado de los productos, las solicitudes atendidas, las dificultades encontradas y recomendaciones.

**B. Actividades transversales:**
- Elaborar el plan de trabajo en coordinación con la gerencia del proyecto, alineado con el plan de trabajo de la acción y con las solicitudes de información de los socios del consorcio y de otros actores clave, y comunicar oportunamente sus avances, dificultades y retos al referente de este contrato.
- Participar en las reuniones del equipo de gestión de información, del consorcio y de la organización, así como en espacios de coordinación humanitaria nacionales y regionales cuando se requiera, actuando como enlace para el intercambio de datos con socios humanitarios y organismos internacionales.
- Atender los espacios presenciales del proyecto y realizar misiones a terreno cuando se requiera.
- Garantizar la entrega oportuna y organizada de los productos acordados en el cronograma de trabajo.
- Participar en los grupos transversales y en los espacios de gestión del conocimiento de 3iS, contribuyendo al fortalecimiento del conocimiento interno sobre el uso de SIG, estadística e inteligencia artificial en la gestión de datos.
- Aplicar en todo su trabajo los enfoques de género, edad, diversidad y protección, el principio de «no causar daño» y consideraciones ambientales (soluciones digitales de bajo consumo).

**Productos esperados**

- Plan de trabajo aprobado y actualizado periódicamente.
- Geodatabase regional documentada (metadatos y diccionario de datos) y actualizada.
- Componente geoespacial del sistema de monitoreo de la situación humanitaria (visor o tablero) operativo y actualizado con la periodicidad acordada.
- Mapas y productos geoespaciales para boletines, informes de situación, análisis temáticos y el informe regional de análisis humanitario.
- Productos geoespaciales entregados a través de EVIDESK, con su registro de solicitudes y cierre.
- Productos cartográficos de apoyo a los demás componentes de la acción (planes de respuesta, cartografía comunitaria, mecanismo digital, mapeo de actores de la Red y emergencias).
- Documentación metodológica, incluida la metodología de identificación y análisis del desplazamiento interno.
- Documentación de metodologías y matrices de variables, fuentes, unidades de análisis y umbrales técnicos utilizados para el monitoreo de amenazas priorizadas, incluyendo su validación, trazabilidad y articulación con protocolos comunitarios, fuentes oficiales y el mecanismo digital de coordinación y comunicación, cuando corresponda al plan de trabajo.
- Reportes mensuales de avance.

## **CALIFICACIONES MÍNIMAS:**

**Educación**

Profesional acreditado en geografía, cartografía, arquitectura, urbanismo, ingeniería geológica o áreas afines. Se valorarán estudios de posgrado.

**Experiencia**

Para ser elegible, la persona que aplique a esta prestación de servicios deberá contar con al menos tres (3) años de experiencia comprobada en actividades similares a las descritas en estos Términos de Referencia. Se valorará de manera especial la experiencia en el sector humanitario y/o en gestión del riesgo de desastres; en monitoreo ambiental o de riesgos mediante teledetección; en análisis de desplazamiento y/o movilidad humana; y en contextos amazónicos, rurales o de difícil acceso (deseable). Se valorará también la participación en procesos de análisis y recolección de información primaria y secundaria, la experiencia previa en el uso de herramientas de inteligencia artificial, automatización de procesos o desarrollo de agentes inteligentes (deseable), y la elaboración de informes técnicos o productos analíticos dirigidos a públicos no especializados.

Se valorará adicionalmente la experiencia o conocimientos aplicados en hidro meteorología, gestión del riesgo de desastres, sistemas de alerta temprana y/o acción anticipatoria, incluyendo la interpretación de variables y la construcción o validación de criterios y umbrales para amenazas como inundaciones, sequías, incendios forestales y otros riesgos ambientales. Asimismo, será deseable experiencia en integración e interoperabilidad de sistemas de información mediante APIs, servicios web u otros mecanismos automatizados de intercambio de datos.

**Habilidades Técnicas**

- Conocimientos avanzados en ArcGIS Pro y ArcGIS Online; experiencia con ArcMap y QGIS.
- Dominio avanzado del análisis espacial y habilidades expertas en modelamiento y limpieza de geodatabases.
- Experiencia en teledetección y procesamiento de imágenes satelitales (por ejemplo, Google Earth Engine u otras plataformas similares) aplicada al monitoreo de deforestación, incendios, cuerpos de agua o inundaciones.
- Conocimientos deseables en análisis hidrometeorológico aplicado y gestión del riesgo, incluyendo interpretación de precipitación, caudales y niveles de río, índices de sequía, focos de calor y otros indicadores ambientales, así como su relación con protocolos de preparación, niveles de atención y criterios de activación temprana.
- Conocimientos deseables en interoperabilidad de sistemas y consumo/integración de datos mediante APIs, servicios geoespaciales y bases de datos, así como en automatización e inteligencia artificial aplicada a la integración, consulta, análisis y procesamiento de información proveniente de múltiples fuentes y plataformas.
- Conocimientos intermedios en Python, JavaScript o SQL, y en plataformas de visualización de datos, tales como Power BI, Tableau, Looker Studio u otras herramientas similares.
- Habilidad en la creación de tableros y visores de datos geográficos.
- Habilidades avanzadas en diseño cartográfico y conocimiento de plataformas y fuentes abiertas (por ejemplo, OpenStreetMap, Google Earth Pro, HDX).
- Comprensión de las prácticas de recolección de datos de campo mediante GPS y herramientas móviles (incluido el trabajo fuera de línea), así como del manejo de fuentes de información estadística oficiales.
- Conocimiento de principios de protección de datos y manejo responsable de información sensible en contextos humanitarios.
- Manejo avanzado de Office.

**Idiomas**

Se requiere dominio fluido de los idiomas español e inglés (hablado y escrito). Se valorará el conocimiento del portugués.

**Responsabilidad ante los beneficiarios**

Se espera que el personal respete los principios de rendición de cuentas a los beneficiarios de los programas de 3IS en línea con las normas internacionales, al tiempo que involucra activamente a las comunidades beneficiarias como socios iguales en el diseño, seguimiento y evaluación de los proyectos de 3IS.

## **PRINCIPIOS GUÍAS:**

Se espera que el personal respete la cultura local y las políticas, procedimientos y valores de 3IS en todo momento.

3IS tiene tolerancia cero con el acoso, la explotación y el abuso sexual, la trata de personas, el abuso y la explotación infantil. Cualquier violación de estos principios y políticas será tratada como falta grave.

3IS es un empleador que ofrece igualdad de oportunidades independientemente de los antecedentes. 3IS puede llevar a cabo comprobaciones de referencias con otras organizaciones sobre asuntos relacionados con el acoso sexual, la explotación y el abuso.
