jobs.title: Monitoring Evaluation Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Manager for DCA South Sudan (Nationals only)
jobs.description:
DanChurchAid (DCA) is an International Non-Governmental Organisation with headquarters in Copenhagen, Denmark. The organisation was founded in 1922, and have country offices in 19 countries across Africa, the Middle East, Ukraine, and Asia.

DCA is working with local partners in South Sudan to assist the poorest of the poor with a focus on protection, combating hunger, working for peace and conflict mitigation and the safe removal of explosive remnants of war (EWR).

In DCA we strive to secure high-quality standards for both our programme and support staff. The aim for our staff is to maintain a smooth running of the DCA Office with accountability, professionalism, and staff welfare as a priority, creating an efficient, open, and inspiring work environment for all.

Are you a visionary and passionate professional with experience in managing humanitarian projects? Have you got solid experience working as MEAL? Do you have experience in capacity strengthening of partners, high-quality MEAL systems designed and experience within cash and protection programming?

Then you might be our new MEAL Manager in DCA South Sudan!

DCA has been active in South Sudan since 2007 and works within the three Global Goals of DCA – Save Lives, Build Resilient Communities, and Fight Extreme Inequalities. We work across Upper Nile, Jonglei, GPAA, Central Equatoria, and Eastern Equatoria States primarily through national partners.

**The Role:**

The Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) Manager provides both operational oversight and technical leadership to ensure high-quality MEAL systems are designed, implemented, and continuously improved across South Sudan and South Sudan Cross-Border Programmes. The role ensures that evidence generated through MEAL informs programme design, adaptive management, strategic decision-making, and organizational learning.

The MEAL Manager will establish and strengthen a robust MEAL system aligned with organizational standards and effectively contribute to programme quality, accountability to affected populations, and impactful programming. Mentoring and coaching partners and staff alike.

He/she will also be responsible for strengthening the partner MEAL capacity to regularly monitor the project performance; ensuring monitoring, evaluation and reporting are used to maintain a culture of providing credible, reliable, timely and cost-effective information for management decisions, accountability and learning in alignment with the donor requirements.

The MEAL Manager is expected to spearhead the implementation of strategies to achieve measurable improvement in community engagement, information-sharing, community participation, feedback and complaints mechanisms. He/she will manage the project database and ensure timely integration with the DCA Country Office PowerBI platform, routinely analyze feedback trends, document the lessons learnt and best practices for internal and external learning as well as used in future project designs.

**Key responsibilities**

**MEAL systems strengthening and strategic leadership**

- Provide overall strategic direction and leadership for MEAL across the country programme, ensuring alignment with organizational strategy and global standards
- Drive evidence-based decision-making and adaptive management by generating, analyzing, and translating data into actionable insights for senior management and programme teams
- Establish and continuously strengthen a coherent, integrated MEAL system, harmonizing indicators, tools, methodologies, and reporting frameworks across projects and partners
- Provide technical leadership during programme design and proposal development, ensuring strong theories of change, logical frameworks, and measurable indicators.

**Evidence, analysis and strategic decision support**

- Lead the generation and use of high-quality evidence and analytics to inform programme design, adaptation, and strategic direction
- Translate complex data into clear insights, recommendations, and decision-making tools for senior leadership
- Oversee the production of dashboards, performance reports, and analytical briefs to track organisational impact and results
- Support organisational processes including annual planning, programme reviews, and strategic frameworks through evidence-driven inputs.

**Monitoring, evaluation, research, learning**

- Oversee the design and implementation of comprehensive monitoring, evaluation, and learning frameworks across the programme cycle
- Lead and supervise baseline, midline, endline studies, evaluations, reviews, and operational research initiatives
- Promote real-time monitoring and adaptive management approaches to enhance programme effectiveness
- Ensure systematic tracking of outputs, outcomes, impact, and programme quality benchmarks.

**Data governance, systems and digital innovations**

- Establish and oversee robust data management systems and architectures, including digital tools and databases
- Ensure strong data quality assurance (DQA) frameworks, data integrity, and compliance across all programmes
- Champion the use of digital, innovative, and cost-effective technologies for data collection, analysis, and reporting for all partners and teams
- Strengthen organizational and partnerships capacity in data literacy, analysis, and utilisation.
- Ensure systematic documentation and retention of programme evidence, monitoring reports and verification data to support donor reporting, audits and organisational compliance.

**Accountability and community engagement**

- Work with all teams to design and strengthening of accountability systems, including feedback and complaints response mechanisms (FCRM)
- Ensure feedback from communities is systematically captured, analysed, and acted upon to improve partner’s programmes and decision-making
- Promote meaningful participation and inclusion of communities, particularly vulnerable and marginalised groups, throughout the programme cycle with partners.
- Ensure transparent communication and safeguarding principles are embedded in all MEAL processes.
- Ensure accountability to affected populations (AAP) commitments are systematically integrated across programme design, implementation, monitoring, and reporting.

**Learning and knowledge management**

- Institutionalise structured learning processes (e.g., after-action reviews, reflection sessions, learning events)
- Develop systems for capturing, synthesising, and disseminating lessons learned, best practices, and innovations
- Ensure learning is embedded in programme adaptation, design, and organisational strategy
- Lead the development and dissemination of knowledge products and external visibility materials.

**Quality assurance and compliance**

- Oversee the design and implementation of quality assurance frameworks, tools, and audits.
- Ensure continuous improvement of MEAL systems and their contribution to programme effectiveness and accountability
- Provide technical oversight to ensure compliance with donor requirements, organisational standards, and regulatory frameworks.

**Leadership, coordination and capacity strengthening**

- Provide technical leadership and direction to the MEAL function and team across programmes and with partners
- Build and sustain a high-performing MEAL team through coaching, mentoring, and professional development
- Strengthen the capacity of programme staff and partners in MEAL systems, tools, and approaches
- Establish a structured partner monitoring framework to assess programme quality and implementation of agreed recommendations.
- Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, learning, and innovation across the organization and partners
- Represent DCA in external technical forums, coordination platforms, and sector working groups.

**Qualification required**

**Education:**

A minimum of a University Degree in Statistics, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Economics, Public Health, Information Management, or related field.

**Technical qualifications required:**

Analysis using qualitative and/quantitative methods including use of participatory methods and tools for planning, monitoring and evaluation, and data visualization.

**Professional technical skills desired:**

Knowledge of the SPHERE standards, Code of Conduct for Red Cross/Red Crescent, Humanitarian Accountability Partnerships (HAP); Core Humanitarian Standards (CHS) and other international humanitarian standards and other capacity-building skills.

**Working experience required:**

- Minimum of 7 years in humanitarian emergencies, monitoring and evaluation with reputable humanitarian organisation. At least 5 years of work experience must be focused on MEAL at various levels.
- Strategic thinking and systems leadership
- Data-driven decision-making and analytical excellence
- Programme quality and impact orientation
- Stakeholder engagement and influencing
- Leadership and team development able to engage meaningfully with HQ Advisors, Partners and in country teams

**Technical and language skills:**

- Excellent analytical skills
- Good team player, flexible and capable of working with a multinational country team, and capable of working under pressure
- Strong computer application skills, with good command of Kobo Toolbox and PowerBI
- Good organizational skills
- Fluency in English, and the local languages (E.g. Arabic)
The position will be reporting to the Head of Programmes.

The position will work closely together with colleagues in the programme team, the implementing partners, the consortium partners, other stakeholders.

**What we can offer you:**

The successful applicant will be offered **a contract up to One (1) year, with the possibility of extension** depending on both funding and performance.

The position is for **South Sudanese nationals**. Women and minorities are strongly encouraged to apply.

**Expected starting date:** December 15th, 2026, or at earliest possible date after this.

**Working hours:** 40 hours per week.

DCA is an equal employer, so, we encourage women to apply and only a South Sudanese will be preferred for the position.

**Interested candidates should apply through:** [https://dca-1.career.emply.com/ad/monitoring-evaluation-accountability-and-learning-meal-manager-for-dca-south-su/hqy4ro](https://dca-1.career.emply.com/ad/monitoring-evaluation-accountability-and-learning-meal-manager-for-dca-south-su/hqy4ro)

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, race, religion, sexual orientation, abilities, or ethnic affiliation are encouraged to apply for the vacancy. DCA conducts an anti-terror check as part of the recruitment process. It is a prerequisite that you can pass this check and maintain this status throughout your employment with us. Everyone applying for a job with DCA must be ready to comply with our Code of Conduct, Staff Policy on Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment and our Child Safeguarding Policy.

**Deadline for applications as described above are the December 7th, 2026. before 5:00 pm CAT**

For further information regarding DCA, please visit our website at: [https://www.danchurchaid.org/](https://www.danchurchaid.org/)

Only applications following the abovementioned procedures will be considered and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

jobs.description:
## **About ONSUR:**

The International Association for Relief and Development (ONSUR) is a non-governmental organization established in early 2012 and registered in Syria. ONSUR is dedicated to implementing relief and development projects that empower local communities and promote a dignified life for vulnerable populations. , the organization operates through a network of execution offices in Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Turkey, and Yemen. ONSUR delivers humanitarian assistance and sustainable development initiatives in conflict-affected regions, with a focus on transparency, community engagement, and long-term impact.

The MEAL Officer is responsible for planning and managing monitoring and evaluation streams to support in developing and rolling out of the overall MEAL strategy for collecting, aggregating, analysing, and using information and data to produce high-quality and consistent reports.

All employees are expected to uphold the highest standards of behavior to ensure the safety and well-being of children, and any breach of this policy will result in immediate disciplinary action.

ONSUR is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace for all. jobs.title: Head of Global Emergency Response Team (G-ERT)
jobs.description:
**Starting Date / Initial Contract Details**

Starting date to be agreed. Full-time position, with regular travel and deployment to emergency responses as required. Open-ended.

**Role Summary**

The Head of the Global Emergency Response Team (G-ERT) leads Medair’s organisational emergency response strategy, preparedness, and operational response to new crises. The role provides strategic and operational leadership to G-ERT, oversees the initiation and management of new emergency responses and strategic start-ups, and ensures Medair can deploy rapidly and deliver high-quality, principled humanitarian assistance. The Head of G-ERT leads and develops the G-ERT team (approx. 6-10 people), coordinates response decisions and resources across the organisation, represents Medair in key humanitarian networks, and drives learning and continuous improvement in emergency response practice. The role positions Medair in the sector as a leader in the implementation of high-quality responses to rapid-onset and complex humanitarian emergencies worldwide through rigorous program design, implementation, and monitoring of performance.

**Project Overview**

Medair’s G-ERT exists to save lives and alleviate suffering by responding rapidly to the needs of vulnerable populations through essential health, nutrition, MHPSS, shelter, NFIs and CVA, and WASH interventions. The G-ERT is a standing global emergency response team designed to deploy within 24 hours of new sudden-onset emergencies, conduct needs assessments within 72 hours, and begin delivering lifesaving assistance within one week. Historically, new G-ERT responses account for 5–10% of Medair’s annual budget, with an average of 1–3 responses each year, around 1/3rd of which transition into longer-term country programmes. The Head of G-ERT leads the team of emergency response specialists and coordinates closely with the International Programmes Department, GSO functions, country programmes, affiliates, donors, authorities, and humanitarian networks. The G-ERT will capture organisational best practice and learning on emergency response, develop tool kits and templates, provide training and advice to existing Country Programmes when they respond to new emergencies within their Country’s borders. The G-ERT will develop strategies for prepositioning emergency supplies and partnerships in higher risk locations around the world in anticipation of new emergencies.

**Workplace & Conditions**

GSO based position in Lausanne, Switzerland. Swiss or eligible EU citizens, or those with a valid work permit for Switzerland, can apply for the role based in Switzerland.

**Responsibilities**

- **Emergency Response Strategy & Leadership:** Develop, implement, monitor, and review Medair’s emergency response strategy and preparedness priorities; advise senior leadership on emerging crises and response options; initiate and chair organisational response decision-making processes; oversee response set-up plans; and provide strategic and operational direction for new emergency responses and strategic start-ups.
- **G-ERT Team Leadership & Development:** Lead, manage, and develop the G-ERT team; ensure effective workforce and deployment planning; set clear objectives and accountability; oversee recruitment, performance, staff care, coaching, and professional development; build a collaborative and resilient team culture; and ensure team members are prepared for rapid deployment and cross-cultural leadership. Ensure the emergency roster of alumni is maintained, engaged (with training and events) and kept informed of key Medair updates and opportunities.
- **Emergency Response Oversight & Organisational Coordination:** Oversee the initiation, implementation, and transition of emergency responses; ensure response strategies, structures, budgets, staffing, security arrangements, and operational systems are fit for purpose; coordinate GSO support and organisational resources; monitor response performance and risk; and intervene or deploy directly when senior leadership is required.
- **Financial, Risk & Security Accountability:** Develop and manage the annual G-ERT budget and oversee response budgets and grant performance; ensure compliance with donor, legal, and Medair requirements; maintain appropriate financial controls; oversee organisational risk and security management for G-ERT deployments; and ensure significant risks and incidents are escalated and managed effectively.
- **Preparedness, Policy, Learning & External Engagement:** Lead the development and maintenance of emergency response policies, procedures, SOPs, toolkits, contingency plans, training, and response standards; embed lessons learned and good practice; strengthen organisational emergency response capacity within the GER-T and in existing Country Programmes through training, advice and promotion of preparedness strategies; maintain strategic relationships with institutional donors, authorities, humanitarian networks, NGOs, partners, and Medair affiliates; and represent Medair in relevant external forums.

**Qualifications, Experience & Technical Competencies**

- Relevant advanced degree in humanitarian action, disaster management, international development, management, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- Minimum seven years of relevant humanitarian experience, including substantial field leadership experience and at least two years leading emergency responses or strategic start-ups. Demonstrated experience managing and developing cross-cultural teams is required; previous Medair experience is desirable.
- Excellent understanding of humanitarian principles, standards, current emergency response practice, and the operational requirements of rapid response. Strong experience in programme leadership, security and risk management, project cycle management, organisational coordination, and operational support functions.
- Proven strategic planning, change leadership, emergency coordination, donor engagement, proposal and grant management, budgeting, and external representation experience. Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and coordinate decisions across functions and locations.
- Fluent written and spoken English and proficient in Microsoft Office.
- Desirable: French and/or Arabic; professional training or facilitation experience; and familiarity with health, WASH, shelter, and cash programming.

**Behavioural Skills**

- Provides clear, strategic, and servant-hearted leadership, setting direction and accountability while empowering others to perform effectively.
- Makes timely, well-judged decisions and solves complex problems in uncertain, fast-moving, and high-pressure environments.
- Thinks and plans strategically, prioritises organisational resources, delegates effectively, and oversees multiple responses and workstreams.
- Builds trusted relationships, communicates and negotiates confidently, and represents Medair credibly with senior internal and external stakeholders.
- Leads change and continuous improvement, remains resilient under pressure, and creates a culture of learning, collaboration, and operational excellence.

**Team Spiritual Life**

Reflect the values of Medair with team members, local staff, people we serve, and external contacts. Work, live, and pray together in our Christian faith-based teams. Fully contribute to a rich spiritual team life, including team devotion, prayer, and words of encouragement.

jobs.title: Cash and Medical Assistance Benefits Specialist
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Application deadline:** Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

***This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.***

**SCOPE OF WORK:**

The Cash and Medical Assistance Benefits Specialist will provide comprehensive services and conduct activities related to Cash and Medical Assistance (CMA) programs that are funded by the Kansas Office for Refugees (KSOR). The CMA Benefits Specialist will implement Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA), Refugee Medical Screening (RMS), and/or Refugee Medical Assistance (RMA) programs as outlined in federal regulations, by KSOR, and the Medical Replacement Designee (MRD), as applicable. The CMA Benefits Specialist will represent the IRC and collaborate and coordinate closely with the donor, other implementing agencies, local stakeholders and service providers.

**Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Provide comprehensive and required services to IRC clients enrolling or enrolled in Refugee Cash Assistance, Refugee Medical Services, and/or Refuge Health Screening services;
- Review applications for accuracy and make eligibility determinations, ensuring non-duplication of services.
- Prepare all enrollment documents and conduct enrollment meetings, ensuring clients understand their rights and responsibilities;
- Conduct monthly redetermination meetings to track and plan participation in employment services for the purpose of determining continued eligibility.
- Prepare the enrollment package including Enrollment Letter and Insurance Card and any other items designated by the Kansas Office for Refugees (KSOR) or the Medical Replacement Designee (insurer) and conduct enrollment meetings to provide enrollment documents and ensure RMA recipients know their rights and responsibilities.
- Conduct RMA orientation, including in-depth orientation to benefits and local health systems.
- Provide support to recipients with billing issues and troubleshooting with providers who need verification of insurance coverage/benefits.
- Collaborate with KSOR and health clinic staff to ensure refugee health screenings are scheduled and coordinated with the direct service team, and to trouble-shoot any issues that arise.
- Prepare and disseminate case closure documentation according to policies.
- Maintain meticulous documentation and ensure that all deliverables are submitted to KSOR on time and in compliance with the policies and procedures.
- Attend all KSOR-scheduled meetings to coordinate with key stakeholders, Quarterly Forums, training events and collaboration meetings.
- Actively engage with donors and other stakeholders to develop policy and processes, identify ways to improve programs and provide feedback.
- Communicate resettlement trends, including spikes in scheduled arrivals, to donors and medical providers on a regular basis.
- Remain current on topics and the context in which CMA benefits are processed, accessed and used, including the Code of Federal Regulations that relate to each of the benefits available through the Kansas CMA Benefits Program.
- Ensure understanding of changes to TANF policies, SNAP Employment & Training, KanCare and/or Medicaid policies, employment programs and local and global medical issues, and how these changes impact clients and KSOR-funded programs.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s Degree strongly preferred, preferably in Social Work or related field.

**Work Experience:**

- Minimum one-year related work experience with human services programs and increasing levels of responsibility.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Proven ability to work under pressure with deadlines and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively and diplomatically in a multi-cultural setting and with limited- English proficiency speakers.
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluency in Dari, Pashto, or Afrikaans both spoken and written desired.
- International work or study experience a plus.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.
- Demonstrated ability to promote an organizational culture that reflects IRC’s core values of service, accountability, integrity, and equality. Working Environment:
- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $20.97/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**US Benefits effective Jan 1, 2027:** IRC offers a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-30 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $187 per month, dental starting at $7.70 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare, dependent care, and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Director, Innovation and Continuous Analytics & Assurance (Internal Audit)
jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Director, Innovation and Continuous Analytics & Assurance (Internal Audit)**, you will drive innovation and data-driven transformation in audit practices, leading the integration of continuous analytics to strengthen risk visibility and assurance delivery. You will coordinate and coach Regional Specialists, align initiatives with GAA priorities, and deliver timely, technology-enabled insights with high ethical standards.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Drive Innovation**

You will develop and implement innovative audit methodologies, tools and technologies, promote automation, AI and data science for continuous monitoring and risk detection, and collaborate with GAA work streams and global leaders to scale solutions. You will also mentor the team, identify process improvements and monitor emerging trends in internal audit and digital assurance.

**Promote and Ensure High Team Performance**

You will provide strategic direction, coaching and technical guidance to Regional Specialists, set clear performance objectives, encourage collaboration and knowledge sharing, address skill gaps through capability-building initiatives, and assess performance through regular feedback and recognition.

**Promote and Ensure High-Quality Standards**

You will uphold GAA's ethical and quality standards, supervise regional specialists, provide technical support during audit planning and fieldwork, ensure review notes are addressed and quality audit findings and reports are prepared, and oversee follow-up activities to confirm that audit findings are fully resolved.

**Professional Development**

You will maintain the required Continuing Professional Education (CPE).

**Requirements include:**

- Minimum 8 years of progressive experience in internal audit, data analytics, or risk assurance, with at least 5 years in roles that integrate technology and data-driven approaches into audit processes.
- Proven leadership experience in managing or coordinating multi-regional or global teams, including developing talent and driving high performance in a distributed analytics or audit function.
- Strategic experience in designing and implementing analytics frameworks, tools, or platforms to support continuous auditing, monitoring, and assurance at scale.
- Demonstrated success in leading innovation initiatives within an audit or risk context—e.g., deploying automation, advanced analytics, AI/ML, or real-time monitoring to enhance assurance capabilities.
- Strong track record of engaging senior stakeholders, including global function leaders, and aligning analytics initiatives with enterprise risk priorities and assurance objectives.

Ces dynamiques combinées affectent durablement les conditions de vie des populations déplacées, retournées et hôtes, en particulier dans les provinces de l’Est et certaines zones de l’Ouest du pays.

Dans ce contexte, Acted intervient principalement dans les provinces du Sud-Kivu, Nord-Kivu, Tanganyika, Nord-Ubangi et Sud-Ubangi, à travers des projets financés notamment par le Department of State / US, ECHO, FCDO, SDC, le Fonds Humanitaire, ainsi que le CDCS, afin de répondre aux besoins humanitaires immédiats et aux vulnérabilités persistantes des populations les plus affectées. Afin de renforcer la couverture et la complémentarité de ses interventions, Acted intervient en coordination avec plusieurs partenaires opérationnels, et est membre de consortiums humanitaires.

Cette coordination permet à Acted de mettre en œuvre des réponses d’urgence rapides et multisectorielles pour couvrir les besoins vitaux liés aux conflits, aux déplacements forcés, aux catastrophes naturelles et aux crises sanitaires. Colombia continues being affected by a complex humanitarian crisis, characterized by multidimensional factors such as protracted armed conflict, natural disasters, and mixed movement/displacement dynamics (both internal and external displacement). Moreover, the crisis is exacerbated by the limited presence of state actors in several zones of the country, especially in hard-to-reach and rural areas combined with high poverty rates (36.6%) and food insecurity levels (30%) resulting in approximately 9.1 million people estimated in need of humanitarian assistance.

In parallel, Venezuela continues facing a severe humanitarian crisis, with nearly 8 million people having migrated since 2014, marking the largest exodus in Latin America. 7.9 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance due to the deterioration of basic public services and a deep economic crisis characterized by high inflation rates and lack of purchase power, resulting in an estimated 56% of its population living in extreme poverty. Moreover, according to the OECD, Venezuela also ranks among the top 3 countries with the highest increase in human fragility, while 40% of the population experience moderate to severe food insecurity and 62% face restriction on access to drinking water. Highly vulnerable communities, living in rural and border areas are affected the most, and 1.4 million children are estimated in need of protections assistance.

- Expérience en management de projets, particulièrement avec une composante institutionnelle ;
- Expérience dans le domaine de la participation communautaire, le lien avec les autorités locales ;
- Compétences en gestion et administration ;
- Flexibilité, adaptation, résistance au stress ;
- Patience et esprit de négociation, excellentes capacités de communication écrite et oral..

## **Conditions**

- Salaire défini par la grille des salaires Acted en fonction du niveau d’études, de l’expertise, du niveau de sécurité et du niveau d’expérience : entre 3100 et 3200€ net mensuel (avant impôts sur le revenu)

- Transport vers la mission et billet retour totalement pris en charge tous les 6 mois (vers l’adresse spécifiée sur le contrat de travail)
- Frais de visa pris en charge par Acted
- R&R tous les 3 mois (billet d’avion pris en charge jusqu’à 500$ + indemnité supplémentaire de 200$)
