1. ### Undertake an appropriate risk assessment of the organization in country.
32. The audit should include site visits to sub offices, project areas and an assessment of these respective sub offices and projects.
33. ### Where the Islamic Relief Somalia is undertaking projects funded by institutional donors, the audit should include the verification of the expenditure incurred on the projects and the income received for the project, including the existence, ownership of any assets purchased for the project.
34. ### A report is required to be sent to Islamic Relief International Headquarters stating whether, in your opinion, the financial statements of the organization in country, which have been audited by your firm, give a true and fair view of the state of the organization affairs at the period end, and of its income and application of resources for the period then ended.

It is expected that Auditors maintained an open communication approach with Islamic Relief Somalia Finance Manager and Country Director and ensure that there is no surprises at the end of the audit.

1. ## IRW Consolidation
2. ### In order to consolidate and compare local country accounts, IRW finance has prepared a consolidation template.

The IRW consolidation template must be signed by the following to confirm its accuracy and consistency with the audited trail balance:

1\. Country Director

2\. Country Finance Manager

1. ## Reporting

The Audited Financial Statements and the Management should be sent as soon as possible on completion to:

**Head of International Finance & Services**

**Islamic Relief Worldwide**

**19 Rea Street South**

**Birmingham B5 6LB**

**United Kingdom**

A copy should be given to the Islamic Relief Somalia Finance Manager and Country Director and discussed with them before and during as well as on completion of the audit.

## **Section 2 Audit Tender**

1. ### Requirements for Proposals from prospective auditors

The prospective auditor is required to submit its understanding about the audit scope, methodology, client resource base and professional fee.

The attached Audit Tender document should be completed and sent to prospective auditors.

1. ### RED TEXT completed by IR Somalia
2. #### Introduction

Islamic Relief Somalia main objective is to promote sustainable social development by co-operating with local communities through relief and development programs. Islamic Relief has implemented a variety of relief and development programs, as well as launching several emergency responses since its inception, this includes; working with IDPs affected by floods and conflict through emergency and Relief programs. In the period to be audited, IR Somalia implemented projects funded by IR Partners, SIDA, DEC, IDB, Start Fund and WFP among others.

jobs.title: DG ECHO HIP 2027 Lebanon proposal writer consultancy
jobs.description:
**About Trócaire**

Trócaire is the official overseas development agency of the Catholic Church in Ireland. Trócaire was established to express the concern of the Irish Catholic Church for any form of human need, but particularly for the needs and problems of communities in the Global South. With our partners we work with some of the world’s poorest people, supporting women, men and communities for long-term change. In Ireland, we raise awareness about the causes of poverty through our outreach programmes in the education sector, through parish networks, and through our public campaigns and advocacy work. In Lebanon, Trócaire works in partnership with local civil society organisations to respond to humanitarian needs and promote the rights and resilience of vulnerable and conflict-affected communities. Its programming focuses on humanitarian response, protection, women's empowerment and strengthening locally led responses, with particular attention to women and girls, displaced populations and other marginalised groups. More information about Trócaire is available at [www.trocaire.org](http://www.trocaire.org/)

**Context of Work**

For the DG ECHO Humanitarian Implementation Plan (HIP) 2027, Trócaire Lebanon will lead a consortium comprising local implementing partners focusing on a protection-led humanitarian response. The response will leverage the consortium's complementary technical expertise, operational presence and local partnerships to address persistent humanitarian needs in underserved and conflict-affected communities.

**Scope of the Work**

**Purpose**: To produce a high-quality, competitive proposal package on behalf of Trócaire Lebanon and its consortium partners under the DG ECHO HIP 2027 for Lebanon.

**Roles and responsibilities**: The consultant will work closely with the Trócaire Lebanon country office its partners and global technical advisers. As part of this agreement, Trócaire Lebanon will lead coordination between consortium partners and ensure technical and operational adherence to Trócaire’s strategy, policies and procedures. The consultant will be responsible for completing and submitting to Trocaire the final offline version of the E-Single Form, as per the DG ECHO guidelines.

The consultant will lead development and writing of a high-quality, competitive, evidence-based proposal and ensure alignment with DG ECHO priorities and policies, including the HIP 2027 priorities and Technical Annex, relevant sectoral policies, protection mainstreaming, gender and age considerations, disability inclusion, accountability to affected populations, and Minimum Environmental Requirements.

The consultant will maintain timely communication with the Trócaire Lebanon focal point throughout the proposal development process. Building on the consortium's ongoing work, the consultant will support the refinement of the intervention strategy, including project objectives, geographical and beneficiary targeting, sectoral priorities, implementation modalities and consortium roles and responsibilities.

The consultant will support consensus-building, identify gaps requiring technical clarification and advise on complementarity across consortium members.

Particular attention will be given to localisation, protection mainstreaming and complementarity with existing humanitarian interventions.

The consultant will work closely with Trócaire's MEAL, finance and technical teams and consortium partners to ensure technical coherence across the proposal package. No travel will be funded. Any costs associated with completing this consultancy, including but not limited to commuting, IT equipment and insurance, are the responsibility of the consultant.

**Deliverables**

The expected deliverables include:

- **Contribution to strategic proposal positioning and intervention design:** Review and analyse the applicable DG ECHO HIP 2027 priorities, technical guidance, humanitarian needs and consortium capacities to support the consortium-led intervention design process. Provide strategic and technical recommendations to inform the refinement of the proposed intervention and strengthen its relevance, competitiveness, added value and comparative advantage.
- **Contribution to consortium project design and technical workshops:** Active participation in consortium-led project design and technical workshops where needed, providing technical inputs, constructive feedback and recommendations to support the refinement of the intervention design. Support the consolidation of the agreed intervention framework, Theory of Change, results framework, key decisions, workshop outcomes, action points and follow-up responsibilities.
- **Completed DG ECHO Single Form:** Development of a comprehensive, compelling, technically sound and submission-ready DG ECHO Single Form, aligned with the applicable HIP 2027 priorities, requirements and guidance. The proposal narrative should effectively integrate findings from needs assessments, secondary data reviews, protection and health gap analyses, relevant sector coordination data, lessons learned and consortium partners' technical inputs. It should clearly articulate the rationale for the intervention, consortium added value, complementarity, feasibility, cost-effectiveness and expected humanitarian outcomes.
- **Support to logical framework (logframe) development:** Support Trócaire's MEAL team, technical advisers and consortium partners in the development, refinement and consolidation of a robust, results-oriented logical framework. Provide technical inputs and recommendations on objectives, results, indicators, baselines where applicable, targets and means of verification, while supporting alignment with DG ECHO requirements, the proposal narrative, activities, beneficiary targets and budget.
- **Budget coherence and value for money:** Review the financial statement and project budget in coordination with Trócaire and consortium partners' finance and programme teams to ensure consistency with the proposal narrative, proposed activities, beneficiary targets, implementation modalities and expected results. Provide advice and recommendations to strengthen cost-effectiveness and value for money, while responsibility for budget development and finalisation remains with Trócaire and consortium partners' finance teams.
- **Project work plan:** Development and consolidation of a realistic and coherent project work plan using the applicable DG ECHO template, aligned with the intervention design, implementation arrangements, activities and budget.
- **Supporting annexes and technical documentation**: Development, consolidation and/or technical review of additional annexes as agreed with the consortium. These may include maps of project locations, a detailed communication plan, and technical inputs into the needs assessment report, Protection Risk Analysis, NEAT+ assessment and other relevant supporting documentation.
- **Proposal quality assurance and finalisation:** Conduct a comprehensive quality assurance review of the complete proposal package against applicable DG ECHO requirements, identifying and addressing weaknesses, inconsistencies, gaps and potential compliance risks. Incorporate feedback from Trócaire, consortium partners and technical advisers, ensuring the final submission package is coherent, competitive and submission-ready within the agreed timeframe.
- **After-action review:** Participation in an internal after-action review session (1–2 hours) with selected staff from Trócaire Lebanon, global advisers and consortium partners, to identify lessons learned and recommendations for future proposal development processes.

**Essential qualifications, experience and skills**

- Demonstrable track record of successfully leading the development and writing of DG ECHO HIP proposals that have secured funding, preferably involving large-scale or complex, multi-partner humanitarian interventions.
- Advanced knowledge of DG ECHO funding priorities, proposal assessment criteria, Single Form requirements, logical frameworks, technical guidance and humanitarian programming standards.
- Strong strategic and analytical skills, with the ability to translate humanitarian needs, contextual analysis, technical evidence and donor priorities into a compelling, competitive and coherent intervention design.
- Demonstrated ability to critically assess and strengthen programme design, identify gaps and weaknesses, and articulate the added value and comparative advantage of consortium-based humanitarian interventions.
- Extensive experience coordinating complex proposal development processes involving multiple consortium partners, local humanitarian organisations, technical advisers, MEAL specialists and finance teams.
- Strong understanding of DG ECHO's cross-cutting requirements, including protection mainstreaming, the Gender-Age Marker, disability inclusion, accountability to affected populations and environmental considerations.
- Experience designing evidence-based, results-oriented humanitarian interventions, including the development of robust logical frameworks, indicators and beneficiary targets, and ensuring coherence between programme design and financial resources.
- Experience working with organisations implementing humanitarian programmes through local partners, with a strong understanding of localisation, equitable partnerships and consortium coordination.
- Experience working in Lebanon or demonstrated in-depth knowledge of the Lebanese humanitarian context, sector coordination mechanisms, humanitarian needs and operational challenges.
- Excellent facilitation, communication and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to constructively challenge technical inputs, facilitate consensus and reconcile competing priorities.
- Exceptional written and spoken English, with demonstrated ability to produce persuasive, concise and technically rigorous donor proposals and consolidate complex technical inputs into a coherent narrative.
- Proven ability to independently manage demanding proposal development processes, respond effectively to feedback and deliver high-quality outputs within tight deadlines.

**Desirable qualifications and experience**

- Demonstrated experience leading successful DG ECHO HIP applications specifically in Lebanon.
- Experience developing successful integrated protection and health proposals for DG ECHO.
- Good understanding of humanitarian protection and health programming, particularly protection case management, GBV, psychosocial support and secondary healthcare.
- Familiarity with the Lebanese humanitarian funding landscape, existing humanitarian interventions and opportunities for complementarity across sectors and actors.

**Location and working arrangements**

The consultancy can be undertaken remotely. However, candidates based in Lebanon or the region, or able to participate in key in-person project design and technical workshops, are particularly encouraged to apply. Access to the Trócaire Lebanon office for meetings and collaborative working can be arranged.

**Duration and Level of Effort**

The DG ECHO Humanitarian Implementation Plan (HIP) 2027 for Lebanon is expected to be published in late November 2026 and will guide the development and submission of the consortium's proposal. The final submission deadline will be confirmed following the publication of the HIP and its accompanying guidance. We would therefore like the consultant to commence work in December 2026, following completion of the recruitment process, to ensure availability throughout the proposal development and submission period, expected to extend into January 2027, especially considering that some Trócaire Lebanon staff, global advisers, and consortium partners may have less availability over Christmas due to the holiday period.

We expect the consultant to be available for the equivalent of **25–30 working days**, distributed across the proposal development period according to the agreed work plan and key milestones. The consultant will be expected to coordinate exact availability with the Trócaire Lebanon country office focal point to ensure timely submission of documents, participation in key technical discussions and workshops, and sufficient availability for revisions and finalisation in the period immediately preceding submission.

jobs.title: Protection Coordinator
jobs.description:
INTERSOS is an independent humanitarian organization that assists the victims of natural disasters, armed conflicts and exclusion. Its activities are based on the principles of solidarity, justice, human dignity, equality of rights and opportunities, respect for diversity and coexistence, paying special attention to the most vulnerable people.

## **Terms of reference**

**Job Title:** Protection Coordinator

**Code**: SR-49-10316

**Duty station:** Maiduguri

**Starting date:** 06/01/2026

**Contract duration:** 7 months

**Reporting to:** Head of Mission

**Functional Supervisor:** Protection Advisor

**Supervision of:** Protection Manager and protection team

**Type of duty station:** Non-family duty station

## **General context of the project**

With over a decade of conflict, there have been devastating humanitarian consequences across North-East (Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe (BAY) states) and the North-West Nigeria. According to the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2025, an estimated 7.8 million women, men, and children need some form of humanitarian and protection assistance. 2.3 million people have been forced to flee their homes due to persistent violence and remain internally displaced. Food insecurity and malnutrition are exacerbated by inflation, poverty, and restricted access due to insecurity, which impedes livelihood opportunities. 5.1 million are projected to be acutely food insecure during the 2025 lean season, with 2.5 million children malnourished. Gender-based violence (GBV) has been a significant protection concern faced byIDP women and girls in the area. Numerous basic infrastructure like hospitals, clinics, water supplies are damaged,posing constraints on essential service provision. Epidemics like cholera arising from flooding and overcrowdedsetting put extra stress to the already vulnerable communities.

In support to the coordinated humanitarian response in Nigeria, INTERSOS has been delivering multi-sestoral interventions addressing critical gaps in protection, health and nutrition, WASH, food security & livelihoods, and Camp Coordination and Camp Management for the most vulnerable communities in both Northeast and Northwest Nigeria, with funding support from OCHA, ECHO, WFP, SV, etc.

## **General purpose of the position**

In collaboration with the HOM, define and coordinate the implementation of protection strategy and program of the mission.

Lead and provide technical guidance to protection staffs ensuring the different components of the protection programme are delivered according to internal guidelines and in line with international standards and principles, in order to ensure quality and achieve mission’s goals effectively, according to INTERSOS vision and values.

## **Main responsibilities and tasks**

**Coordination and support**

- Participate actively in the definition and update of annual project planning and budgets, defining strategies and providing advice to the Head of Mission in the translation of the identified logistics, supply, and ICT needs into objectives, priorities, and resources needed for the mission
- Is responsible for monitoring the implementation of logistics, supply, and ICT activities in the mission (construction and rehabilitation, stock and supply of non-medical and medical material, fleet management and transport, water and sanitation, vehicles and engines, equipment/installation and infrastructures, security rules (implementation and enforcement, ICT, assets, etc.)
- Ensure compliance with INTERSOS standards, protocols, and procedures, across the mission and according to donor requirements including procurement. Report to the Head of Mission on the development of the ongoing programs and propose reorientation strategies when needed
- Is responsible for ensuring technical reference and support for all logistics, supply, and ICT issues in the mission, providing coaching to logistics staff, and representing INTERSOS in meetings with authorities, other NGOs, and coordination networks for technical/logistics-related issues
- Ensure the production of mission-level SOPs (if needed) for the Logistics needs

**Logistics Information Management**

- Provide monthly reporting to the Head of Mission Regional Logistics and Supply Coordinator (through IMP) and related people on projects/mission evolution from the technical/logistics perspective and propose corrections if needed
- Ensure that data reported in INTERSOS Logistics software (Intersos Management Platform - IMP) is correctly used and accurate. Provide training to mission staff if required and support the implementation of INTERSOS Logistics software in missions

**Supply-Chain Management and Procurement**

- Monitoring overall procurement performance for the mission. Ensure effective and cost-efficient procurement planning by liaising with technical staff, Field Coordinator, and/or Project Managers. Ensure that online procurement plans are created on IMP and up to date while guaranteeing INTERSOS and donor procurement policies and procedures are being adhered to at all times. Research to ascertain the best products and suppliers in terms of best value, delivery schedules and quality
- Coordinate with the Administration and Finance Department to ensure that payment processes to suppliers are made on time and respecting the financial systems
- Plan and perform field audits to ensure consistency in process application and proper documentation and filing are maintained
- Develop and implement service contract management instructions, policies, and procedures. Examine and re-evaluate existing service contracts and oversee regular rent, utility payments (i.e., electricity, water, gas, etc.), office and guesthouse maintenance contracts, and running costs procedures. Ensure that they are properly handled by Logistics and Supply Officer and Assistants, Administration, and/or focal points
- Overview that the Supply Manager/Assistant and Field Coordinator Logistics and Supply Officer maintain and update a pre-qualified suppliers list per base
- Is responsible for ensuring the good storage of all projects materials within warehouse/stock, in respect of the INTERSOS Supply SOPs and regular inventory checks every quarter
- Check and coordinate with logistics staff that goods deliveries are done as planned and properly stored
- Prepare and launch tenders documents in coordination with the Supply team

**Transportation management**

- Ensure that INTERSOS Fleet Management model, movement security protocols, and Brand Identity Manual are applied in missions - the fleet is checked, and regularly maintained and that vehicles are insured and taxes are paid
- Follow-up on proper monitoring of fuel consumption and use of vehicle log-book, maintenance log, oil log, and other fleet formats and templates by Field Coordinator logistics staff. Ensure that proper documentation of vehicles (i.e. lease, insurance, mechanical inspection, etc.) is properly handled by logistics staff
- Contribute to the development of sustainable approaches to transport management by streamlining INTERSOS environmental policy and Regional Office suggestions

**Facilities and Communications management**

- Oversee the installation and maintenance of functional office space(s) and guesthouse facilities with adequate living conditions and in accordance with INTERSOS minimum standards and brand identity manual. Ensure the application of defined safety and security measures and make inspection visits to assess the rehabilitation needs of facilities
- Is responsible for ensuring that facilities have an appropriate IT and Communications infrastructure and equipment to sustain INTERSOS software platforms and in line with policies and procedures - allowing permanent communication between capital, projects, bases, and HQ and proper management of the bases. Guarantees that all staffs in the mission have proper training on how to use communications equipment available (e.g. satellite phones, HF/VHF radios, computers, etc.)
- Contribute to the development of sustainable approaches to facility management by streamlining INTERSOS environmental policy and Regional Office suggestions

**Assets management**

- Oversee the purchase, use, and maintenance of IT assets, office and project equipment, and communication tools, while ensuring that all mission assets registered in IMP are documented, issued with unique INTERSOS asset numbers, tagged, and logged according to asset management policies and procedures
- Report asset list at the end of the project and oversee asset rollover according to the defined destination with the Programs Department
- Oversee regular fixed assets check every quarter

**Human Resources management**

- Coordinate the Logistics team and participates in the HR processes (recruitment, training, briefing/debriefing, evaluation, potential, detection, staff development and internal communication) to ensure both the sizing and the amount of knowledge required for the activities he is accountable for

**Applied security**

- In collaboration with the Head of Mission and the Security Coordinator (if present) is responsible for co-defining and monitoring the technical aspects of the risk reduction policy, transport, communication, protection, identification and preparation of the technical aspects of the mission security policy and guidelines, evacuation plan and contingency plan, monitoring daily the security rules and reporting to the Head of Mission of any problem. For this purpose, in case of absence of a dedicated Security Focal Point, the Logistics Coordinator has to create an appropriate environment to facilitate the exchange of information on security situations. Is the security backup in the absence of the Head of Mission.

## **Required profile and experience**

**Education**

- BA in relevant field (Social Science, Psychology, Social Work, Human Rights, International Humanitarian Law or other fields related to social development and humanitarian work)
- Desirable Master degree (MA or LLM) in Human Rights, International Humanitarian Law or related subjects

**Professional Experience**

- Minimum 8 years of experience with NGOs in developing countries of which minimum 5 years should be in protection technical roles
- Experience in implementation of key protection interventions related to Case management, PSS and Community based Protection

**Professional Requirements**

- Essential computer literacy (word, excel and internet)
- Strong theoretical, technical and practical background in protection

**Languages**

- English (written and spoken) is required

**Personal requirements**

- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills and ability to work and integrate in a multicultural team
- Ability to work under pressure, flexibility
- Problem solver, dynamic, mature, proactive
- Diplomatic skills in networking with partners, authorities and donors
- Experience in complex emergency setting involving internal displacements
- Reporting skills, experience with monitoring tools and systems, data collection and analysis
- Stress management
- Commitment to INTERSOS principles

## **General conditions and benefits:**

- **Salary grid:** 12 - 3.690€ - 4.245€ monthly gross
- **Remuneration:** The monthly remuneration is defined, for each position, according to the standard salary grid and function grid, taking into account the experience of the selected candidate. It is communicated during the HR interview, or at any rate during the first stage of the selection process.
- **Accommodation:** Shared Guesthouse
- **R&R:** INTERSOS staff required to work for extended periods at duty stations under hazardous, stressful and difficult conditions are granted a regular and mandatory period of Rest and Recuperation (R&R). This is due to protecting their health and well-being and ensuring optimal work performance upon the resumption of their duties, while, at the same time, preserving the operational readiness of the Organisation. R&R benefits are not financial compensation for the degree of hardship and insecurity of a duty station. Eligibility: staff members recruited as international field staff whose contract states one R&R Duty Station as the main Duty Station and whose contract duration is equal to or longer than 4 calendar months. R&R: 7 days of psycho-physical recovery every 8 weeks + 1000€ allowance.
- **Annual Leave:** 2.5 days per month
- **Medical insurance:** Injuries and death insurance; civil liability insurance, reimbursement for vaccines, medical certificate and PCR test for deployment; psychosocial support on request for the humanitarian worker.
- **Transportation:** Round-trip flights for the humanitarian. For any mission lasting at least 9 months, an additional flight ticket to the Country of residence and return to the mission is covered by the Organisation for the humanitarian worker.
- **Visa:** INTERSOS covers the costs and visa support for the humanitarian worker.
- **Induction:** Online orientation course: each new staff member receives preparatory training before departure, adequate to provide the necessary information related to the structure of INTERSOS and the main decision-making processes and working tools, in order to facilitate entry into the Organisation.
- **Note 1:** INTERSOS applies a “Learning & Development Policy” which includes the possibility to receive capacitation and participate in internal and external training. Priority will be given to the staff working for INTERSOS for over two years.
- **Note 2:** The categorisation of Accompanied, RnR, and Unaccompanied Duty stations is subject to security criteria, access to health and education services, and is non-negotiable.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Donor Stewardship and Strategic Communications
jobs.description:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

The Senior Manager, Donor Stewardship & Strategic Communications is a key member of the individual giving team, responsible for creating compelling donor communications that strengthen relationships with principal, major, and planned giving donors. This role develops customized reports, proposals, impact updates, and stewardship materials that demonstrate the impact of philanthropy and inspire deeper engagement with Habitat for Humanity's mission.

Working collaboratively across fundraising, communications, donor relations, and program teams, the senior manager translates complex information into clear, donor-centered narratives. Success in this role requires strategic thinking, strong relationship management, exceptional writing skills, and the ability to manage multiple high-priority projects while delivering an outstanding donor experience.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Why This Role Matters**

Our principal, major, and planned giving donors make transformational investments in Habitat’s work. This role helps ensure those donors understand the impact of their support through customized stewardship, thoughtful engagement, and compelling stories that connect generosity to measurable outcomes.

**What You'll Do**

· Create donor reports, impact updates, proposals, case statements, briefing materials, and other stewardship communications.

· Develop compelling donor-centered stories that communicate Habitat's global impact and funding opportunities.

· Partner with major gift, principal gift, and planned giving professionals to support cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and renewal strategies.

· Conduct donor research and develop profiles, briefing materials, and strategic communications that support fundraising efforts.

· Translate complex programmatic, financial, and impact data into clear, engaging donor communications.

· Collaborate with communications, donor relations, finance, and program teams to gather data, stories, and outcomes for donor-facing materials.

· Manage multiple communication and stewardship projects from concept through completion while ensuring accuracy, quality, and timely delivery.

· Help identify new and innovative approaches to donor stewardship, impact storytelling, and donor engagement.

**What You'll Bring**

**Required Qualifications**

· Bachelor's degree in Communications, Journalism, Marketing, English, Nonprofit Management, International Development, Business, or a related field.

· 5+ years of experience in donor communications, philanthropy, fundraising, stewardship, proposal development, executive communications, or a related field.

· Experience working with principal gift, major gift, or foundation donors.

· Experience within a nonprofit, international development, humanitarian, healthcare, higher education, or other mission-driven organization.

· Demonstrated success developing donor reports, investment cases, proposals, and customized stewardship materials for sophisticated donor audiences.

· Exceptional writing, editing, storytelling, and communication skills.

· Strong analytical, research, and project management skills.

· Ability to build collaborative partnerships across teams and navigate multiple priorities.

**Preferred Qualifications**

· Knowledge of fundraising principles, donor stewardship practices, and philanthropy trends.

· Understanding of major gifts, principal gifts, and planned giving strategies.

· Experience conducting donor research and utilizing donor intelligence to inform engagement strategies.

· Ability to interpret and communicate programmatic impact data and outcomes.

· Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Canva, and donor database/CRM systems.

**What We Offer**

Join a global organization committed to building strength, stability, and self-reliance through shelter. You'll work alongside passionate colleagues and help deepen relationships with donors whose generosity advances Habitat's mission around the world.

**Culture and Values**
At Habitat for Humanity International, you join a community that believes in:
**\*Humility:** We are part of something bigger than ourselves.
**\*Courage:** We do what is right, even when it is difficult.
**\*Accountability:** We take personal responsibility for Habitat’s mission.
**\*Safeguarding:** We protect the rights, dignity, and safety of all people we serve and work alongside.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$84,600.00 USD

\-

$125,850 USD

/

Annual

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

**Habitat for Humanity International is an E-Verify employer.**

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
**Projects Manager**

**ABOUT VIDERE**

Videre is an award-winning, UK-registered NGO that exposes human rights abuses and holds perpetrators to account. We work directly with communities in stressed environments, equipping networks of activists and community leaders with the technology and training necessary to safely capture visual documentation of political violence, human rights violations, and other systemic abuses. Our aim is to ensure that the concerns and knowledge of affected communities drive advocacy, policy, and legal action.

**ABOUT THE ROLE**

Videre's partnerships work is growing, and we're looking for an experienced Project Manager to help us deliver an expanding portfolio of projects and grants. Working closely with partners, consultants and colleagues across the organisation, you'll play a key role in making sure partnership projects are well planned, properly resourced and delivered effectively from start to finish. You'll be responsible for keeping projects on track, managing donor and budget requirements, and helping build the systems and support needed as our partnerships portfolio continues to evolve and grow.

**KEY RESPOSIBILITIES**

**Project and Partnership Management**

- Manage a portfolio of partnership projects, ensuring delivery against agreed objectives, budgets, timelines and quality standards.
- Develop project plans, monitor progress, identify risks and adapt approaches as contexts and priorities change.
- Maintain strong, trusted relationships with partners, serving as their primary day-to-day point of contact.
- Support collaborative planning, problem-solving and decision-making with partners to maximise impact and sustainability.
- Ensure projects are delivered in line with organisational priorities and donor commitments.

**Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning**

- Lead project monitoring and reporting, ensuring progress and impact are effectively tracked.
- Develop and strengthen MEL approaches, frameworks and tools where needed.
- Analyse project results and learning to inform decision-making, adaptive management and future programme design.
- Coordinate partner and consultant contributions to monitoring, reporting and learning processes.

**Donor and Financial Management**

- Support day-to-day relationships with donors and respond to information requests.
- Coordinate high-quality donor reporting, ensuring compliance with contractual requirements.
- Monitor project budgets, expenditure and forecasts, working closely with finance colleagues and partners.
- Review financial and narrative reports and address any issues or risks that arise.

**Consultant and Resource Management**

- Manage a roster of trusted technical consultants and specialists.
- Scope, commission and oversee consultancy assignments, ensuring high-quality delivery and value for money.
- Coordinate consultant inputs alongside partner workplans and project objectives.

**Organisational Contribution**

- Contribute to the development and improvement of systems, processes and tools that support effective programme delivery.
- Work collaboratively across teams to strengthen organisational learning, efficiency and impact.

**SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE**

**Essential**

**Experience**

- At least five years' experience managing complex projects or programmes in the non-profit, international development, human rights, humanitarian or related sectors.
- Experience managing institutional donor-funded projects and grants from design and start-up through to delivery, reporting and close-out.
- Experience managing project budgets and financial reporting.
- Experience building and managing effective partnerships with diverse stakeholders.
- Experience managing partnerships remotely, including in complex, high-risk or rapidly changing environments.
- Experience coordinating consultants, technical specialists or external service providers.
- Experience developing or implementing monitoring, evaluation and learning approaches.

**Knowledge**

- Strong project and programme management skills, including planning, risk management and delivery oversight.
- Excellent relationship management, communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Strong financial management and budget monitoring capability.
- Ability to develop practical systems and processes where they do not already exist.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent written communication skills, including report writing and donor communications.
- Ability to work independently and effectively within a remote, internationally distributed team.

**Desirable**

- Experience working with civil society, community-based or grassroots organisations.
- Experience managing projects in conflict-affected, politically sensitive or fragile contexts.
- Experience managing multi-country programmes or partnership portfolios.
- Experience with subgrant management.
- Experience supporting organisational learning and adaptive programming.
- Knowledge of safeguarding, duty of care and risk management.
- Familiarity with participatory, qualitative or outcome-focused MEL approaches.
- Understanding of equitable partnership and localisation approaches.
- A recognised project management qualification (e.g. PMP, PRINCE2 or equivalent).
- Relevant additional language skills.

**Personal Attributes**

- Adaptable and proactive, comfortable navigating changing priorities, ambiguity and evolving circumstances.
- Collaborative and solutions-focused, with strong personal accountability.
- Culturally sensitive and able to work effectively across diverse contexts.
- Strong judgement and discretion when handling sensitive information.

**APPOINTMENT TERMS**

**Contract: 1-year fixed term** (with possibility of extension based on funding)

**Preferred Location**: Asia (Bangkok preferred); United Kingdom

**Compensation**: Salary is dependent on location. The equivalent of a UK annual salary of £40,000 - £45,000 plus pension contribution will be converted according to location using ICSC scales and paid in local currency.

**All staff receive:**

- A minimum of 28 days Annual leave
- Counselling and mental health support
- Annual wellbeing days

jobs.title: Head of Office - Based in Dakar
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte
une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de
conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore
d'exclusion des soins.

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is a non-profit medical humanitarian organisation that intervenes
in crisis and conflict situations. In accordance with its charter, MSF delivers aid to populations in
need, to victims of natural or man-made disasters and of armed conflicts, regardless of race,
religion or political beliefs. MSF’s work is based on humanitarian principles, operating
independently and impartially. More than 90 per cent of overall funding comes from nongovernmental
private sources. MSF is neutral and does not take sides in armed conflicts; providing
care on the basis of need alone. MSF medical teams often witness violence and neglect in the course
of their work, largely in regions that receive scant international attention. At times, MSF may
publicly speak out to draw attention to a forgotten crisis, to alert the public of obstacles and/or
abuses occurring beyond the headlines, to criticize the inadequacies of the humanitarian response,
or to challenge the diversion of humanitarian aid for political interests.

Context

The Dakar Intersectional and Regional Support to Operations (DIRSO) office aims to bring in
perspectives and expertise from the region, pool resources and identify synergies across MSF
operational centers (OC) and engage with the vibrant organizational ecosystem in Dakar in
support of MSF operations in west and central Africa. The Dakar Office groups together MSF
operational support teams (cells/desks), technical referents and back-office teams. The DIRSO
Strategic Plan (2024-2026) provides the overall framework and the detailed unit-specific objectifs.
As of June 2026, the DIRSO is composed of around 100 FTEs from 8 MSF entities. This team
includes a wide range of medical and operational skills, including, among others, specialists in
emergency management, epidemiology, pediatrics, mental health, community engagement, as well
as communication, advocacy, human resources, administration, and logistics teams.

The position is mandated to lead and manage the Dakar Support Office (DSU) and the Shared
Units (Med Platform, Regional HR Unit, Intersectional Communication) teams on behalf of the
Dakar Strategic Committee and is accountable to its members: the General Directors of OCP,
OCBA and OCG. The DSU provides back-office services such administration, local human
resources, finance, logistics, and IT support, to facilitate the work of all MSF teams present in
Dakar.

Scope of responsibilities – objectives of the position

The Head of Office (HoO)
is in charge of the management of the Dakar office that is hosting several MSF sections
leads and manages the Dakar Support Unit team
strategizes and contributes to the development and growth of the Dakar Office
collaborates with the Head of Desks and the other Desk members to adapt and ensure
continuous relevance of the Dakar Office strategy, activities and resources
coordinates with the other sections (in Senegal and in the region) to explore possibilities
for mutualization and develop synergies
is responsible for the external representation with senegalese authorites, the overall
functioning of the regional entity, and leadership of the team ensuring adherence to MSF
values and ethical standards.

Strategy, planning and resources management

The HoO is responsible for ensuring that all the resources needed to run the office and the teams
are in place, in particular by organising optimal and secure working conditions, for ensuring that
that internal and external working relationships are fluid, organised, documented and structured,
and that resources and funds are planned, used and anticipated in an appropriate manner:

• Lead and accompany the development of a coherent mid/long term strategic vision for the
Dakar office, reporting on a quarterly basis to the Strategic Committee.
• Chairs the Dakar Steering Committee on a 1-2 months basis.
• Ensure that the priorities of Dakar office are aligned with the Dakar Strategic Plan.
• Lead and plan processes related to the annual planning and reporting cycle in close
collaboration with the functional units present in Dakar and their respective HQs
• Develop, plan, and manage the resource requirements and budgets associated to the Dakar
Support Unit.
• Coordinate activities and establishe responsibilities and procedures for attaining the
objectives.
• Ensure the functioning of the Dakar Support Unit (DSU) ensuring smooth office and
facilities management for all.
• Take decisions within the scope of the position and in alignment with Strategic Committee
direction.
• Develop and structure the collaborative and administrative part of the internal work
organization, in particular the 6 Operational Entities partnership agreements.
• Effectively recruit, manage, lead and evaluate the staff in line with established
organizational policies, organizational culture, and effective contribution towards achieving
objectives.
• Ensure high-level financial accountability and transparency.
• Ensure that the office meets its legal and fiscal obligations and define the best legal and
administrative frame to support the development of its activities.
• Lead and accompany the development of a coherent mid/long term strategic vision for the
regional initiatives along with the Dakar DG Steering Committee.
Networking, representation and communication
The HoO is responsible for ensuring that that internal and external working relationships are fluid,
organised, documented and structured:
• Actively coordinate and facilitate networking between MSF teams and relevant civil society
networks in Senegal in ways that contribute meaningfully to the work of MSF in the region.
• Represent MSF with Senegalese authorities related to all registration, immigration, foreign
affairs and employment.
• Develop and maintain relationships with international organizations and the academic and
medical communities to further MSFs work and reputation.
• Actively advocate for MSF positions and interests; promote MSF to broad and specific
audiences through information and awareness raising events, widening the supporter base.
• Maintain and expand a network of regional analysts to (a) gain and outside-MSF perspective
of contextual development and (b) be ready to engage ad-hoc expertise for work requested by
mission.
• Support with the identification of potential collaboration opportunities with external
partners.

Thematic work

• Lead, in collaboration with the L&D, the development of various learning and experience
sharing events.
• Contribute to the development and implementation of a mid/long term strategy of the
intersectional Dakar HR unit.
• Strengthen the network of contacts with relevant institutions of higher education,
professional associations and other pertinent actors in the region.
• Participate upon request to special events linked to human resources unit.
Operational Support
Provide back office support to the operational cells and units such as hosting,
administration, domestic human resources and general services.

On request basis by operational cells the EO may represent MSF and the operational
programs within pre-identified platforms in Dakar level such as NGO, donor, or specific
thematic taskforces.
Is available to be deployed as a member of CIMT during critical incidents
Is available to support the ops teams in regular programs & emergency response in terms
of strategy definition, specific tools development, ops support, M&E, context analysis,
inductions, mentoring and training facilitation, etc.

Security management

In charge of the security management for the Dakar Office.
Is the final decision-maker when it comes to personal safety and security of Dakar staff.
Intersectional dynamics
Represent the Dakar Office in intersectional discussions and Hub meetings on the
evolution of the office and possibilities for intersectional collaboration.
Maintain and strengthen links with other MSF sections and offices in the region.
Develop a specific policy for the transfer of positions to Dakar and propose the resources
to be based in Dakar.
Support all efforts to ensure that the different teams and individuals from the different
sections are aligned, coordinated and that a proper working environment is maintained.
Continue and expand areas of joint work with other sections in Dakar and the region.
Hierarchical line management of
The Dakar Support Unit (DSU), the Human Resource Unit (HRU) and the International
Comms team.

Reports to:
The Dakar Office Steering Committee whose membership consists of DG of OCBA, OCG,
and OCP.
The Steering Committee has delegated the day to day management to the OCG Deputy
Director General.

Internal Relations:
The Dakar Office Steering Committee
Functional relationships with other MSF sections as guided by the strategic and annual
plans.
All office users: Operational cells, HR unit, Medop support, EPI/SIS team, the Dakar
Support Office (DSU)
Headquarters of participating OCs, mainly at director level

External Relations:
Represent MSF with Senegalese authorities related to all registration, immigration,
foreign affairs, employment and other issues that may impact MSF presence in Senegal.
Coordinate and align representation messages on operational issues targeting multilateral
UN agencies, NGOs, civil and military authorities, donors, researchers, and academics
within Senegal with MSF HRT and operational cells in Dakar.

jobs.title: MULTI - Responsables des initiatives mutualisées - HULO
jobs.description:
**Date de rédaction : 19/11/2026**

**Date de début de contrat : 01/02/2027**

**Type de contrat : CDD**

**Localisation : RCA, RDC, Cameroun**

**Conformément aux principes de fonctionnement propre à la Coopérative, ces 3 postes sont recrutés et contractualisés par Solidarités International, pour le compte de la Coopérative hulo.**

**QUE FAISONS-NOUS…**

La Société Coopérative Européenne d’Intérêt Collectif « Humanitarian Logistics Cooperative », aussi La Société Coopérative Européenne d’Intérêt Collectif « Humanitarian Logistics Cooperative », aussi connue sous l’appellation « hulo », est la première coopérative humanitaire fondée en juin 2021. Dirigée par des organisations humanitaires et intégrant de nouveaux membres régulièrement, hulo a pour objectif d'améliorer l'impact de l'aide humanitaire en renforçant la collaboration et la mise en place de projets communs dans ses pays d’intervention. Chez hulo nous sommes convaincus que le partage et la mise en commun de ressources et d’expertises entre organisations contribue à augmenter la performance de la logistique humanitaire et de la chaine d’approvisionnement

Notre action s’appuie sur une approche collaborative et participative, l’intelligence collective et l’animation d’une communauté de pratiques. Toutes nos activités sont structurées autour d’un objectif commun, impliquant plusieurs parties prenantes autonomes et interdépendantes, qui coopèrent de manière horizontale. Le pilotage y est distribué, fondée sur la concertation, la co-responsabilité et l’engagement volontaire.

Dans nos 7 pays d’intervention répartis dans 3 régions nous mettons en place des initiatives mutualisées dans les domaines des achats, des ressources humaines et de l’environnement. En support aux organisations humanitaires nous coordonnons des initiatives de transport international humanitaire mutualisées à destination des crises humanitaires les plus graves. Enfin nous développons constamment des solutions digitales au service de la communauté humanitaire.

Pour en savoir plus, vous pouvez consultez le rapport annuel 2026 en cliquant sur le lien [https://hulo.coop/january-2026-annual-impact-report/](https://hulo.coop/january-2026-annual-impact-report/)

Au sein d’une équipe d’une soixantaine de collaborateurs, le département des opérations est composé actuellement d’une dizaine de personnes au siège et d’une vingtaine sur le terrain.

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** est une association d’aide humanitaire internationale qui, depuis près de 40 ans, porte secours aux populations victimes de conflits armés et de catastrophes naturelles en répondant aux besoins vitaux, boire, manger, s’abriter. Particulièrement engagée dans le combat contre les maladies liées à l’eau insalubre, première cause de mortalité au monde, SI met en œuvre par ses interventions une expertise dans le domaine de l’accès à l’eau potable, l’assainissement et la promotion de l’hygiène mais également dans celui, essentiel, de la sécurité alimentaire et moyen d’existence. Présentes dans une vingtaine de pays environ, les équipes de SI - 2000 personnes au total composées d’expatriés, de staffs nationaux, de permanents au siège, de quelques bénévoles…- interviennent avec professionnalisme et engagement dans le respect des cultures.

**DESCRIPTIF DU POSTE**

**Objectif général :**

Le.la responsable des initiatives mutualisées a la charge de la gestion complète des initiatives de mutualisation (« Joint Initiatives » ou « JI ») prévues par la communauté hulo, notamment dans sa zone d’affectation.

Il.elle assure l’animation de sa communauté et organise des réunions relatives aux JI.

Il.elle coordonne avec la Communauté hulo l’évaluation des besoins, facilite l’avancement des dossiers mutualisés tout en renforçant la coordination inter-ONGs dans sa zone d’affectation

En lien avec les JI, il.elle assure la planification, la mise en œuvre et le suivi des différentes étapes des initiatives mutualisées tout en respectant les principes humanitaires, de transparence et de redevabilité.

**Principales missions :**

COORDINATION DES MEMBRES

- Déployer et maintenir une communication régulière avec les ONG dans sa zone d’intervention.
- Participer aux réunions des clusters et groupes de coordination pertinents dans sa zone d’intervention
- En fonction des besoins et des acteurs logistiques déjà présents dans la zone, positionner hulo dans cet écosystème en lien avec le Représentant Pays, le cas échéant.
- En lien avec la Communauté et les besoins communs identifiés, proposer des opportunités de mutualisation lors de la conception de la feuille de route Pays.

GESTION OPERATIONNELLE DES INITIATIVES MUTUALISEES (JI)

- Analyser les besoins consolidés des organisations humanitaires de la Communauté
- Animer les étapes clés de chaque processus d’initiatives mutualisés tout en s’assurant que les organisations soient engagées dans ce processus
- Suivre et piloter l’utilisation des JIs
- S’assurer que les objectifs prédéfinis pour chaque initiative sont atteints et que les JI soient largement diffusées à la Communauté.
- Documenter les bonnes pratiques et les leçons apprises
- Assurer le lien entre la coopérative et les prestaires locaux sélectionnés dans le cadre des JI

GESTION OPERATIONNELLE DES INITIATIVES D’ACHATS MUTUALISEES (JPI) – *(Poste au Cameroun uniquement)*

- Analyser les besoins consolidés des organisations et le marché sélectionné
- Proposer et valider avec les participants la stratégie d’approvisionnement
- Animer les étapes clés du processus d’achats mutualisés et assurer l’engagement de la communauté hulo à ces étapes
- Etablir une relation fiable avec les fournisseurs sélectionnés et faciliter la résolution des conflits entre les ONG’s et fournisseurs si nécessaire
- S’assurer que les objectifs prédéfinis pour chaque initiative sont atteints et évaluer la satisfaction de l’ensemble des parties prenantes

CONFORMITE, QUALITE ET REDEVABILITE

- S’assurer que les achats mutualisés respectent les procédures internes de hulo
- Participer avec le Représentant pays à la mise à jour du système de suivi / qualité incluant des indicateurs clés de performance sur les JPI, en lien avec la Business Analysis and Research Unit et le département environnement de hulo

INNOVATION ET AMELIORATION CONTINUE

- Identifier et proposer des solutions innovantes pour améliorer l’efficacité du dispositif hulo et sa contextualisation
- Piloter la capitalisation des initiatives mutualisées.
- Contribuer à la diffusion des bonnes pratiques sur les initiatives mutualisées

**Priorités 2-3 premiers mois**

Cameroun

Ouverture de mission en autonomie (avec le support du Coordinateur régional) :

- Implémenter hulo dans le paysage logistique à Yaoundé.
- Lancer une initiative de mutualisation à fort impact et ayant un résultat rapide.

RDC

Poste basé à Bunia pour appuyer la Communauté à la réponse Ebola :

- Livrer des JI prêt à l'emploi et ayant un impact sur la Communauté pour mieux répondre à l'épidémie Ebola.

RCA

Renforcement de l’équipe hulo à Bangui, avec un focus sur le déploiement en province :

- Dynamiser hulo en province
- Soutenir le processus de localisation en RCA à travers les activités et outils Hulo

**VOTRE PROFIL**

**Expériences /formation**

- Formation technique en logistique/supply chain : BAC+2 minimum, spécialisation humanitaire est un plus
- Expérience dans le secteur humanitaire : 3 ans minimum
- Expérience sur poste similaire souhaitée

**Compétences techniques et transverses**

- Compréhension des enjeux de la gestion de la chaine d'approvisionnement humanitaire et en matière d'appels d'offre
- Connaissances des procédures d'achats des organisations humanitaires
- Connaissances des standards humanitaires de redevabilité et de bonnes pratiques
- Connaissances de l'environnement logistique en RCA / RDC / Cameroun
- Connaissances en environnement : achats durables, critères ESG, gestion des déchets
- Bon sens rédactionnel et relationnel
- Animation d'ateliers
- Capacité d’analyse et d’organisation, de gestion des priorités
- Compétences en gestion de projets : savoir définir des priorités d'action et d'allocation de moyens / ressources / délais
- Capacité à développer et entretenir un réseau professionnel
- Maîtrise indispensable de l'informatique (Excel, Word, Outlook)
- Maitrise courante du français et de l'anglais (très bon niveau lu, écrit et parlé).
- Connaissance de langues locales est un atout

**SI VOUS OFFRIRA LES CONDITIONS SUIVANTES**

- 1 poste basé à Bunia (RDC) – CDD de 6 mois (jusqu’à fin juillet 2027)
- 1 poste basé à Bangui (RCA) – CDD de 8 mois (jusqu’à fin septembre 2027)
- 1 poste basé à Yaoundé (Cameroun) – CDD de 8 mois (jusqu’à fin septembre 2027)
- Salaire brut mensuel : à partir de 2365€ (2150+ 10% congés payés) en fonction de l’expérience du/de la candidat/e.
- Perdiem : selon la politique perdiem en vigueur
- Breaks : Pendant la mission, un système d’alternance entre travail et congés est mis en place à raison de 7 jours ouvrables tous les trois mois. A ces périodes de pause, s’ajoute un jour de repos supplémentaire par mois travaillé.
- Couverture sociale et médicale : Les expatriés bénéficient d’une assurance qui rembourse tous les frais de santé (y compris les frais médicaux et chirurgicaux, les soins dentaires et ophtalmologiques, le rapatriement) et d’un système de prévoyance incluant les risques de guerre. Les frais de vaccination et de traitement antipaludéen indispensables sont remboursés.

jobs.title: Case Worker - Administrative Support
jobs.description:
Overview of position

**The Mental Health and Psychosocial Support** **(MHPSS) Case Worker- Administrative Support** will provide dedicated administrative and operational support to the Migration Management Unit (MMU) to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of service delivery. Given the high volume of cases managed by the MMU, the position is intended to strengthen case tracking, documentation, coordination, reporting, and beneficiary follow-up processes.

While the position will be embedded within the MMU structure and primarily support MMU operations, the incumbent will also participate in relevant MHPSS activities, trainings, and capacity building initiatives to promote integrated programming and strengthen psychosocial support approaches for better service delivery. The position reports directly to MMU Programme Associate and has dotted reporting line to the Protection Coordinator

Role objectives

- Provide administrative support to the MMU team in planning and implementing activities.
- Maintain organized records of beneficiary files, referrals, case documentation, and service reports.
- Support scheduling and coordination of MMU activities, meetings, outreach missions, and follow-up appointments.
- Assist with data entry, filing, and archiving of case-related information in accordance with confidentiality and data protection standards.
- Support case registration, documentation, and tracking processes.
- Assist in monitoring referrals and ensuring appropriate follow-up of beneficiaries accessing services through the MMU.
- Support compilation and analysis of case management data for reporting purposes.
- Participate in MHPSS trainings, workshops, and technical learning opportunities relevant to the role.
- Promote basic psychosocial support principles during interactions with beneficiaries.
- Support implementation of integrated MHPSS activities where requested by the MMU and MHPSS teams.
- Assist in collecting information related to psychosocial needs and service gaps identified during field activities.
- Support awareness-raising and community engagement initiatives related to mental health and psychosocial wellbeing when required.
- Coordinate with MMU team members to ensure accurate and timely documentation of activities.
- Support preparation of weekly, monthly, and ad hoc reports.
- Contribute to monitoring and evaluation efforts through data compilation and reporting.
- Liaise with internal teams and external service providers as directed to facilitate coordinated responses.
- Coordinate appointments for clients' beneficiaries and provide them with management updates.
- Support with counselling of beneficiaries to enhance their mental health and make referral to relevant service provides.
- Identify needs of migrants with special needs and liaise internally to timely manage risks and identify opportunities.
- Perform any other tasks as maybe required

Project reporting

MHPSS Coordinator

Key competencies

- The staff assumes the duty of humanitarian care and ethical conduct that goes with the responsibilities. By signing a code of conduct, the staff thereby signals responsibilities to uphold its standards of behaviour accordingly.
- A staff must adhere to the guiding principles of Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and ensure all survivors as further protected from harm.
- Be friendly and welcoming
- Be careful in the words and actions you choose.
- Help create welcoming, inclusive, safe space for people from diverse against others because of their identity (race, gender, sexuality, age, class background. Ability, religion and more)
- Be present
- Have fun and be creative.
- Protect the integrity of the organization.
- Staff must protect Assets and items should be given to the right beneficiaries

Team management

This role has no team management responsibility

Further information

Qualified female candidates are encouraged to apply for this role

jobs.title: Humanitarian Advisor – Eastern Mediterranean Region
jobs.description:
## **About CBM**

CBM (registered as CBM Christoffel-Blindenmission Christian Blind Mission e.V.) is an international development organisation committed to improving the quality of life of persons with disabilities in the persons communities of the world. Based on our Christian values and more than 100 years of professional expertise, we address poverty as a cause and a consequence of disability. We work in partnership to create an inclusive society for all.

**About the role:**
As Humanitarian Advisor, you will serve as the primary humanitarian focal point for assigned Country Offices and partners across the Eastern Mediterranean Region. You will provide technical guidance, strengthen programme quality, support emergency preparedness and response, and contribute to Humanitarian-Development-Peace (HDP) Nexus programming and disability-inclusive humanitarian action.
**This is a fixed-term position for 15 months and will be filled locally in either Amman, Jordan, or Bensheim, Germany, under the contractual conditions of the respective country. Expatriation is not intended.**

## **You Will:**

- Serve as the primary humanitarian focal point for assigned Country Offices and partners, providing technical advice throughout the project cycle, from design and implementation to monitoring and review.
- Support the development of high-quality, disability-inclusive humanitarian programmes and partner portfolios, contributing to project reviews, donor compliance and portfolio monitoring.
- Provide technical guidance on emergency preparedness, sudden-onset responses and HDP Nexus programming in line with humanitarian principles and standards.
- Promote the meaningful participation of persons with disabilities and Organisations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) throughout humanitarian programming.
- Strengthen the capacities of CBM staff and partners through coaching, technical support, quality assurance and the promotion of inclusive humanitarian approaches.
- Facilitate effective coordination between Country Offices, Technical Advisors, Global Programme Teams, Fundraising, Finance and other internal stakeholders on humanitarian programmes and priorities.
- Contribute to knowledge management, organisational learning and continuous improvement across the humanitarian portfolio.
- Support CBM's engagement in relevant humanitarian networks and coordination mechanisms, in collaboration with Country Offices and other CBM teams, as appropriate.

**These are your qualifications**

- Advanced degree in Humanitarian Action, International Development, Public Health, Social Sciences or a related field.
- At least five years of experience in humanitarian programming in a technical or coordination role, preferably in conflict-affected or emergency contexts.
- Strong understanding of humanitarian principles, standards and coordination mechanisms, including disability-inclusive humanitarian action.
- Experience working with local partners and implementing humanitarian projects is an advantage.
Knowledge and understanding of the Eastern Mediterranean humanitarian context is a strong asset.
- Experience implementing projects funded by institutional donors, particularly the German Federal Foreign Office, BMZ or ECHO, is an advantage.
- Excellent communication, coordination and stakeholder management skills.
- Ability to work effectively under pressure and adapt to rapidly changing humanitarian contexts.
- Fluency in English; Arabic is a strong asset.
- Strong commitment to disability inclusion and localisation in humanitarian action.
- Willingness and ability to undertake international travel.
- Identification with the Christian values and mandate of CBM.

## **What we offer**

- A meaningful position with a lot of creative freedom in the world's leading organisation in the field of Disability Inclusive Development
- A fair salary and other social benefits based on the local conditions in the country you apply for
- An approachable, agile organisation with self-reliant people in a diverse and collegial team and great team spirit

jobs.title: Head of Satellite Office (Marawi)
jobs.description:
Position Title : **Head of Satellite Office (Marawi)**

Duty Station : IOM Philippines - Country Office (Marawi City)

Classification : National Officer, NO-B

Type of Appointment : Fixed-Term, one year with possibility of extension

Estimated Start Date : As soon as possible

Closing Date : 01 December 2026

Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) and direct supervision of the Head of Sub-Office (HSO) based in Cotabato, Philippines the incumbent will be responsible for providing overall administrative oversight of the satellite office in Marawi City, Philippines and contribute to the implementation, oversight and coordination of various IOM humanitarian, development and/or peacebuilding programmes in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) and its neighboring areas, more specifically in the provinces of Lanao del Norte and Lanao del Sur.

## **Responsibilities**

1. Provide strategic support, analysis, and technical input to the HSO and COM on the administration of the Satellite Office.
2. Provide, in close coordination with HSO and relevant Programme Coordinators, backdrop support to the implementation of the programme in line with IOM's policies and practices as well as donor requirements, being primarily responsible for the administrative managemet, coordination, and stakeholder engagement activities.
3. Establish partnerships and maintain working relationships with relevant interlocutors (including government line ministries, CSOs, UN agencies, donors, and other stakeholders) to promote institutional advocacies, facilitate information exchange, and strengthen strategic cooperation.
4. Monitor, support, and guide the satellite office staff in planning and executing operational, supply chain, financial, and administrative activities in line with IOM’s rules and procedures and in close coordination with the HSO, Programme Coordinators, and National Resource Management Officer.
5. Oversee and manage the performance of various units and teams, and provide guidance and feedback to ensure safe, effective, and coordinated programme planning and implementation.
6. Exercise quality control over office and staff management in line with IOM rules and procedures.
7. Lead the drafting of reports, presentations, talking points, and briefings, ensuring strategic messaging and visibility of programme activities of the Satellite Office.
8. Contribute to identifying challenges and opportunities in strengthening IOM’s presence and operations in the area and take part in project development efforts to complement or expand existing projects and/or for new project initiatives.
9. Represent IOM in events, initiatives, meetings, or other fora that are institutionally and/or programmatically relevant.
10. Provide regular feedback and bring to the attention of the HSO which are not meeting timelines or where quality standards are not being met and provide recommendations for improving the existing quality control system.
11. Regularly update the HSO, provide recommendations, and implement strategic measures to address emerging issues and challenges in management of the Satellite Office.
12. Ensure relevant reports on administrative activities of the Satellite Office is submitted to HSO in a timely and accurate manner.
13. Provide administrative support and guidance, in close coordination with HSO and line managers of each programme, to ensure compliance to IOM Standards of Conduct, policies and procedures for Preventing and Responding to Sexual Exploitation and Abuse, and frameworks on Accountability to Affected Population (AAP), Do-no-Harm and Conflict Sensitivity.
14. Undertake duty travels in support of the programme and perform other duties that may be assigned.
15. Perform other duties as may be assigned.

## **Qualifications**

EDUCATION

- **Master’s degree** in Political or Social Science, International Relations, International Development, Migration Studies, Peace and Conflict Studies, Public Administration, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with **minimum two years of relevant professional experience**; or
- **University degree** in the above fields with **minimum four years of relevant professional experience.**

EXPERIENCE

- Experience in managing humanitarian, development and/or peacebuilding programmes and capacity-building activities with the UN, Government and INGOs.
- Experience in liaising with governmental authorities as well as with national and international institutions.
- Experience in project development, reporting, management, planning and implementation,

## **Required Skills**

- Ability to lead and maintain effective operations in a changing environment, demonstrating flexibility, sound judgment, and responsiveness to emerging needs.
- Demonstrated ability to supervise, train and motivate staff in a multicultural team environment.
- Demonstrated cultural awareness and ability to foster respectful, inclusive, and productive relationships across multicultural teams and diverse stakeholder groups.
- In depth knowledge of the broad range of migration related subject areas dealt with by the Organization
- Knowledge of UN and bilateral donor programming.
- Proficiency in the responsible use of artificial intelligence and digital productivity tools to support work organization, information management, and operational efficiency.
