jobs.title: Migration Health Associate (GHS)
jobs.description:
Position Title : **Migration Health Associate (GHS)**

Duty Station : IOM Philippines Country Office (Zamboanga)

Classification: General Service, G-5

Type of Appointment: Fixed-Term

Estimated Start Date: ASAP

Closing Date : 08 December 2026

**Organizational Context and Scope**

Under the overall supervision of the Head of Sub-Office (HoSO) in Cotabato, and the direct supervision of the National Migration Health Officer (Maternal, Neonatal, and Child Health), the Migration Health Associate will be responsible for supporting the implementation of IOM health programming, including the delivery of basic health services and related activities to vulnerable mobile populations, under the technical and administrative guidance of the supervisor. To facilitate programme implementation and coordination, the incumbent may be deployed or co-located within partner government offices, health facilities, or points of entry for specified periods, as required by operational needs and in accordance with established agreements and organizational policies.

## **Responsibilities**

1. Assist in implementing and monitoring health programmes and initiatives tailored to the needs of the migrants and returnees population arriving at ports, transit centres, or referral facilities, as guided by the supervisor.
2. Provide support to migrants and returnees in accessing health services, including conducting basic health assessments such as vital signs monitoring, triage, diagnostic testing in accordance to established protocols, and documenting and referring identified health needs for appropriate care and follow-up.
3. Support regular communication and coordination with government partners, private sectors, and other development and humanitarian partners.
4. Support the delivery of orientations, briefings, counselling, and risk communication and community engagement activities for migrants and mobile populations, providing clear information on the migration health assessment process, required treatments, follow-up procedures, and specialised referrals, as appropriate.
5. Support the coordination and facilitation of referrals and admissions for migrants and mobile populations, including timely communication with receiving and referring health facilities, transmission of clinical documentation and endorsements prepared or approved by the responsible medical authority, documentation handover, and follow-up in accordance with established protocols.
6. Support the organisation and delivery of capacity building and mentoring sessions for health partners on migration health management, including follow-up with participants to support the application of technical guidance.
7. Monitor the utilisation of health kits and testing/screening equipment, record and report shortages or irregularities, and support compliance with established infection prevention and control, waste management, and other relevant protocols.
8. Support in collecting and maintaining up to date project data and records, including health assessments, activity outputs, referral information, and follow-up actions, and assist in preparing project reports and briefers.
9. Support organisation, implementation, and monitoring of community and stakeholder engagement activities, such as monitoring, consultations, focus group discussions, information campaigns, surveys, mapping, trainings, and other activities.
10. Perform various administrative and clerical tasks such as preparing the necessary activity logistic arrangements and requests such as documents, materials and resources for the smooth execution of activities and office functions in the province.
11. Assist in the implementation of IOM’s policies and protocols on PSEA and AAP, such as through dissemination of relevant messages and information.
12. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

## **Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in Nursing, Public Health or a related field from an accredited academic
institution with three years of relevant professional experience; or,
- High School diploma with five years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Relevant public health or clinical experience, preferably in high-volume settings, emergency
departments, or community health centers;
- Experience in programme support, implementation, monitoring and evaluation, and
coordination of public health activities;
- Experience in administrative and clerical management related to public health activities;
- Experience in humanitarian or development operations and/or Government Social or Health
Services; and,
- Experience in liaising with government counterparts, including those in the Local Government
Unit (LGU), Bureau of Quarantine (BOQ), Department of Health (DOH) and/or the ministries
of Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

**Skills**

- Good technical skills, including clinical assessment;
- Knowledge of migration health, communicable disease control, vaccination programmes, and
emergency and disaster response operations is an advantage;
- Computer literacy required: MS Office suite (Word, Excel, Access etc);
- Training in the areas of Tuberculosis management, mass immunisations, communicable diseases,
laboratory testing, or public health is an advantage;
- Ability to support orientations, mentoring, feedback, and community-engagement sessions using
approved technical materials;
- Ability to support community advocacy and engagement activities related to tuberculosis, hygiene,
mental health, nutrition, adolescent and reproductive health, and maternal health, using
established technical guidance and materials; and,
- Familiarity with the context of BARMM and surrounding areas; knowledge of the issues and
programmes related to returnees and mobile populations at the National and Local
(Mindanao) level is highly desirable.

**Languages**

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, English and Filipino is required (oral and written).

DESIRABLE
Working knowledge of any BARMM language (Ex. Tausug (Bahasa Sug), Sinama (Bajau), and Yakan).

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.

- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

jobs.description:
**About Trust Consultancy and Development**

Trust Consultancy and Development is an independent research and third-party monitoring and evaluation (M&E) consultancy based in Gaziantep, Turkey, with two branches in Syria and Palestine. Trust provides a range of services and works with partner companies and NGOs in the MENA region and beyond. Our work addresses the growing demand for high-quality research, third-party research, data collection, data analysis and capacity-building services. Our clients include international and national non-governmental organizations and donors, including UNICEF, UNFPA, OCHA, Expertise France, Global Communities, IRC, IMC, DCA, Save the Children, People in Need, World Vision, Norwegian Refugee Council, GIZ, USAID/BHA and ECHO. As a research and M&E company, we offer a unique perspective and can tap into a network of people working on the ground in real time on the issues we research. Currently, we are working in Syria, Turkey, Iraq, Yemen, Pakistan, and Afghanistan.

jobs.title: General Manager-SHOFCO SACCO
jobs.description:
**Department:** SACCO

**Location / Work station:** Kibera

**Working Hours:** Monday – Friday, 8:00am – 5:00pm and Saturday, 8:00am – 1:00pm

**Reporting Relationships**

**Reports to:** SHOFCO SACCO Board

**Direct reports:** Head of Operations & Sacco Accountant

## **About SHOFCO**

SHOFCO is a leading community-based organization mobilizing the largest network of social groups in Kenya to provide holistic, needs-driven services and redefine the potential of citizen-led change.

We partner across a range of sectors to provide programs ranging from health and education to economic and social empowerment. These services are informed by our community advocacy platforms. Originally founded in Kibera, SHOFCO is now reaching communities across Kenya, with more than 800 staff.

## **About SHOFCO SACCO**

SHOFCO Sacco Society Ltd is a Community Value Based Savings and Credit institution guided by ethical values and it is affiliated to SHOFCO – an NGO that has been in existence since 2008. The Sacco focuses on savings mobilization and credit initiatives in various locations where SHOFCO operates and beyond. The sole purpose is to address the needs of the economically vulnerable community members.

## **Job Purpose**

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the SACCO General Manager will be responsible for providing strategic and operational leadership to the SACCO, ensuring sustainable growth, excellent member service, financial stability, regulatory compliance, and effective implementation of the SACCO's strategic goals and objectives.

The role is responsible for translating the strategic direction of the Board into actionable business plans, leading the management team, safeguarding the SACCO's financial and operational interests, and ensuring that the SACCO remains competitive while delivering value to its members.

## **Key Responsibilities and Job Dimensions**

### **Responsibilities**

- Develop and implement the SACCO's strategic plan, annual business plans, and performance targets.
- Provide strategic direction and leadership to the Management team and technical advisory to the Board
- Formulate and implement t strategies, policies and procedures and in consultation with the Board, ensure they are followed and reviewed where necessary.
- Enforce compliance and implementation of policies and ensure the SACCO operates within applicable laws, regulations, policies and Board-approved frameworks.
- Facilitate the preparation and implementation of annual work plans, procurement plans, budgets, goals and objectives.
- Develop and provide high quality products and efficient services which are value-adding to clients so as to enhance market share and revenue command of the Sacco.
- Manage the Society’s resources within budgetary guidelines according to the institution’s policies and cooperative laws and regulations.
- Ensure maintenance of effective external/internal controls to safeguard the Society’s assets and oversee the annual/quarterly or ad hoc financial audit processes as required.
- Ensure the Society’s vision, mission, products and services are consistently presented in a strong, positive image to relevant stakeholders media, public and private sector as well as the membership.
- Promote management and technological innovations to enhance organizational efficiency, productivity and meet dynamic business requirements.
- Ensure funds due to the Society are promptly collected in accordance with existing procedures.
- Submit reports to the Board, concerning performance, plans and recommendations for action.
- Present the Society’s annual capital, audit reports and revenue budgets to the Board for adoption.
- Oversee financial management, risk management and investment undertakings by ensuring that sound policies and practices are adopted for optimal utilization and returns as well as ensuring adherence to Society’s budget.
- Oversee effective management of human resources for optimal productivity through policies and strategies that attract and retain qualified and competent staff.
- Provide strategic linkages with the corporate world, business community, government agencies and other social partners for the benefit of the Society’s growth.
- Ensure corporate compliance with all statutory, legal, social and regulatory requirements in the execution of its business strategies.
- Manage society’s corporate change through adopting policies and strategies that will ensure the effectiveness and business survival in delivery of services.
- Oversee execution of all business processes within the set policies, procedures, norms and standards.
- Identify opportunities for business growth, diversification, partnerships, and innovation.
- Maintain strong relationships with strategic partners and industry stakeholders(internal & external).
- Provide support to the Board of Directors by organizing all Board and Sub Committee meetings, Annual and Special Delegates Meetings and Supervisory meetings as and when required.
- Oversee development and implementation of corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiatives and ensure that the image is well projected and protected.
- Perform such other duties as may be assigned by the board and from time to time.

## Job Competencies (Knowledge, Experience and Attributes/Skills).

### Academic Qualifications

- Bachelors’ degree in business, finance or a related field from a recognized institution.
- Masters’ Degree in Finance/Strategic Management or equivalent will be an added advantage.
- Post-graduate qualifications will be an added advantage.

### Professional Qualifications

- Relevant professional qualifications such as CPA, ACCA, CFA, CPS or equivalent will be an added advantage.
- Membership to relevant professional bodies with good standing e.g. ICPAK, IHRM.

### Other required qualifications (unique/job specific)

- Minimum of 10 years’ relevant experience with at least 5 years in senior management position.
- Prior working experience in cooperative movements will be an added advantage.
- Experience working with a Board of Directors and Board committees.
- Working knowledge of banking and accounting systems.
- Experience in strategic planning, organisational leadership and change management.
- Knowledge of the Kenyan SACCO regulatory and operating environment.

### Technical Skills:

- Strategic Leadership & Governance
- Financial Management
- Credit & Risk Management
- SACCO Operations Management
- Regulatory Compliance
- Digital Transformation & Innovation
- Business Development & Growth
- Board procedures
- Member Experience & Stakeholder Management
- People & Performance Management
- Business Continuity & Risk Oversight
- Business acumen

### Behavioral Competencies/Attributes:

- Visionary
- Strategic thinking
- Problem-solving
- Integrity
- Effective communication
- Decision-making
- Leadership
- Assertive & Pro-active
- Diligent
- High standards of service delivery
- Influence

**Overall competency expectation:** Ability to provide strategic, financial and operational leadership that ensures the SACCO's financial sustainability, regulatory compliance, membership growth, sound governance and excellent member service.

jobs.title: Information Technology Specialist (Scientific Computing)
jobs.description:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community** (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Ecosystems (FAME)** division is composed of three programmes: the Coastal Fisheries and Aquaculture Programme (CFAP); the Oceanic Fisheries Programme (OFP); and the Marine Ecosystems Programme (MEP). The Director’s Office provides implementation support and strategic direction across the three programmes and cross-cutting projects. Working with all 22 PICTs, SPC FAME has strong partnerships with regional, sub-regional and national entities working in the marine sector. SPC FAME staff are based in New Caledonia, Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tonga, with most of the staff being based in New Caledonia.

The **Information Technology Specialist (Scientific Computing)** will provide specialist scientific computing expertise to support OFP’s scientific and modelling activities, ensuring reliable, efficient and fit-for-purpose high-performance and high-throughput computing systems. The position will provide technical advice, support and training to scientific staff, while working closely with SPC ICT to plan and implement evolving computing needs. The role will support software development, reproducible scientific workflows and the effective and secure use of emerging technologies, including cloud computing and AI.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Development, maintenance and support of scientific computing tools and systems**

- Manage the internal HTC Condor and HPC systems and software, including virtual machines (VMs) and related operating systems,
- Optimize system performance,
- Manage and monitor usage of compute resources, including planning for and scheduling critical work with scientists, and advanced communication of necessary downtimes for maintenance work,
- Administer the OFP Linux-based computer network in collaboration with the SPC ICT section,
- Identification and liaison with external cloud system providers where these are deemed suitable options for certain tasks,
- Keep tools, dependencies, and computing environments current, secure, and reliable,
- Focus on user-centred design, so tools and systems fit how scientists work.

**Provide technical support, advice and training to OFP scientists and contractors in the area of scientific computing and use of available systems**

- Respond to and troubleshoot issues raised by OFP scientists and contractors relating to computing systems, and work with ICT to solve complex and wider system problems where necessary.
- Provide constructive advice on appropriate tools, approaches, and computing resources for specific analytical work,
- Design and deliver training on scientific computing, reproducible workflows, workflow orchestration, version control and efficient use of computing resources,
- Maintain accessible documentation and examples to help scientists use and adapt these tools independently,
- Provide focussed induction training to new staff,
- Communicate with users on system changes, new capabilities, and common issues,
- Translating computing concepts, methods and technical language between scientists, managers and ICT staff.

**Work with the SPC ICT team and OFP scientists on strategic planning of scientific computing needs and solutions, including implementation**

- Ensure fit-for-purpose scientific computing systems and resources by working with the SPC ICT team and FAME scientists to identify current and future scientific computing needs, contribute to short (annual) and longer-term (5 year) strategic planning, priorities, and costing for computing infrastructure, tools, and capability.
- Explore alternative approaches and systems for continuous improvements that align with FAME research needs and SPC ICT standards, policies, data and security requirements,
- Collaborate with SPC ICT to cost, purchase and implement computing hardware and software.

**Software development, management, repeatable workflows, use of AI and public repositories**

- Support OFP’s Multifan-CL maintenance and development contractor, maintain the public GitHub repository for the opensource Multifan-CL project, with best practices, version and new version release control,
- Support internal and external collaborators on software development or joint project work requiring access to OFP computing resources and GitHub repositories
- Maintain compilation tools for Multifan-CL for Linux, Mac and Windows OS,
- Contribute to and support scientists with development and maintenance of dashboards and web tools (internal and public accessible), including R Shiny Apps and cloud hosting with Posit, and Azure,
- Work with scientists to design, implement, integrate and maintain shared scientific workflow orchestration systems that support reproducible and efficient analyses,
- Provide information and training to scientific staff on programming good practices for optimization and efficient memory use, particularly in R,
- Liaise with SPC ICT to ensure an organizational level understanding of AI use policies and advise staff on their AI use and risks,
- Ensure provision of relevant documents and files are available on relevant websites or public repositories as required by contractual agreements with donors.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- Postgraduate degree in Computer or Computational Science, Information Technology, or related subject or equivalent body of knowledge and experience

**Technical expertise**

- At least eight years’ experience in computational or computer science,
- At least three years’ experience developing and maintaining high-performance and/or high-throughput scientific computing environments (e.g., HTCondor, supercomputers, cloud computing, virtual computing environments),
- Client-side and server-side Java, C and C++ programming and compilations,
- Version / revision control experience, GitHub, Docker,
- Demonstrated practical experience in using AI-assisted tools for software development, code review, testing and scientific workflow automation, including the ability to critically evaluate and validate AI-generated outputs,
- Programming in R, Python, C++ other languages,
- Knowledge and experience of Linux and Microsoft Windows-based operating systems,
- Parallel computing (multiprocessing, GPU computing),
- Expertise in designing, implementing and maintaining reproducible scientific workflows and workflow orchestration systems.

**Language skills**

- Good written and spoken English skills,

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work as part of an interdisciplinary and multi-cultural team,

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This contract is budgeted for 3 years and is subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – the **Information Technology Specialist (Scientific Computing)** is a band 11 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of SDR (special drawing rights) 4,397-5,400 per month, which converts to approximately XPF 634,433-779,190 (USD 5,892-7,236; EUR 5,317-6,530). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea** – SPC provides housing support in Noumea. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will begiven to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

jobs.title: Climate Change and Health Consultant
jobs.description:
**Role Objectives.**

To lead the integration of climate resilience, adaptation and climate-informed humanitarian action, with a focus on SRH and SGBV, across IPPF Humanitarian's strategy, systems, tools and documentation (from strategic roadmaps and policies to operational guidance and procedures) and Member Affiliates programming, in alignment with the SPRINT V program, the IPPF Climate Crisis and SRHR Framework, the full disaster management cycle and external guidance, and to lead implementation of the strategy by providing hands-on technical support to selected Member Associations.

Specific objectives include;

- Ensure alignment with the full disaster management cycle (DMC) and with external guidance, such as the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP), Sphere, existing clear best practice documents and WHO climate-related frameworks.
- Review IPPF’s existing humanitarian strategic, policy, operational and procedural documents to identify where climate, sustainability, SRH and SGBV considerations are missing or weak, and ensure they are integrated across all SPRINT V outcomes.
- Translate the strategy into usable operational tools, such as checklists, guidance notes and procedures, for each phase of the disaster management cycle.
- Develop practical, scalable and locally led approaches that can be implemented within existing MA capacities and resources.
- Support selected MAs to apply the updated documents and implement the strategy in their own contexts, strengthening their capacity and generating learning.
- Document lessons and recommendations to inform scale-up across the Federation.

**Guiding Principles.**

The consultant will:

- Build on existing IPPF humanitarian systems, tools and guidance rather than creating parallel frameworks.
- Ensure all climate approaches are practical, proportional, and implementable by Member Affiliates.
- Apply a localisation approach, recognising Member Affiliates leadership and ensure ownership through contextual adaptation country by country.
- Strengthen the humanitarian-development-climate nexus using existing programme structures, including the SPRINT V.
- Integrate climate considerations across existing SPRINT V activities rather than proposing stand-alone workstreams.

**Key Deliverables.**

The work will commence in January 2027, upon signing. The consultant will share a detailed work plan, incorporating key deliverables and tasks. The consultant will report to the Humanitarian Head of Quality Services with close collaboration with the Head of Humanitarian Operations, SPRINT Programme Manager and other technical advisors, operation team and development teams located in different parts of the world. For technical guidance, content review and approval of key deliverables, including the following;

**1. Gap analysis and alignment report.** This covers the review of IPPF’s humanitarian documents, with the alignment matrix against SPRINT V, the Climate Crisis and SRHR Framework, the disaster management cycle, MISP, Sphere, , existing clear best practice documents and WHO frameworks. It will include the following suggested products:

- Inception report and workplan.
- Climate Resilience and Adaptation Strategy for IPPF Humanitarian.

**2. Revised and new climate-integrated documents and tools.** This covers the strategic, policy, operational and procedural content, the field-ready tools for each phase of the disaster management cycle, and the short integration guide for future documents. It will include the following suggested products:

- Climate and SRHR landscape review and MA mapping report.
- Climate and Health Vulnerability & Adaptation (V&A) Assessment Tool and Guidance Note.
- Climate-integrated Emergency Preparedness Plan template and supporting tools.

**3. Member Association implementation support, with final report.** This covers the support plans for the selected MAs, the training and learning sessions, and the final report with lessons and scale-up recommendations. It will include the following suggested products:

- Climate Technical Guidance package.
- Climate Technical Assistance Framework for MAs.
- Climate Integration Checklist for SPRINT V activities.
- Climate-SRHR stakeholder mapping and engagement plan.
- Climate and SRHR Evidence and Learning Agenda (2027-2030), and a draft MEL framework.
- Technical support to 2-3 pilot MAs.
- Document of lessons learnt and recommendations to inform scale-up across the Federation.

**Essential.**

- Advanced expertise in climate change adaptation and climate-resilient health systems.
- Demonstrated knowledge of, disaster risk reduction, the full disaster management cycle and WHO climate-related frameworks.
- Demonstrated experience undertaking climate and health vulnerability and adaptation assessments.
- Strong experience in humanitarian/fragile context settings.
- Demonstrated experience integrating climate considerations within humanitarian programming.
- Proven experience revising or developing strategies, policies, guidance and procedures for international organizations or NGOs.
- Experience working with national and local actors in disaster-prone contexts.
- Demonstrated experience developing practical tools and guidance for frontline humanitarian actors.
- Experience providing technical assistance and capacity strengthening to local or national organizations.
- Progressive direct experience in the areas of climate change and health. Academic credentials preferred.
- Proficiency in Microsoft applications.
- Ability to thrive in cross cultural environments, with respect to local knowledge and local experience in various context.

**Highly desirable.**

- SRHR expertise and/or SGBV expertise.
- Experience in the Indo-Pacific.
- Experience in compound crises.
- Experience working with WHO climate and health frameworks.
- Experience supporting localisation and locally led adaptation.

**Competencies, Skills and Experience.**

Core Competencies:

- Knowledge, experience and network in climate research, advocacy and/or programming combined with health expertise (e.g., public health, reproductive health).
- Ability to break down complex concepts into simple explanation for non-experts.
- Experience working with an INGO or NGO is highly desirable.

**Language Requirements and Proficiency Required.**

- Excellent command of English language, both written and oral.
- Proficiency in other IPPF languages (French, Spanish, Arabic) is desirable.

**Duration:** 60 working days spread across 6 months (January – July 2027)

jobs.title: AI Adoption Lead, CRRD
jobs.description:
**Application deadline:** Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world’s largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you’re a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people worldwide for a better future.

IRC’s AI Transformation Priorities set three aims: deploying new tools, reshaping workflows so that teams redesign how work gets done, and reinventing models so that services reach more people faster, at greater scale and at lower cost. The AI Policy is the responsible-use foundation under all three. The AI Learning Strategy is how IRC builds the skills, habits and shared practice behind those aims. This role contributes mainly to the second aim: helping Crisis Response, Recovery & Deliver (CRRD) teams redesign how work gets done. The CRRD Department implements our work, with staff on the frontlines of program delivery to provide high-quality programming with impactful results for the people we serve.

**Job Overview:**

We are hiring an AI Adoption Lead to help embed AI in the day-to-day work of CRRD teams. A primary part of this role is understanding how work actually gets done, deciding which tasks AI should perform and which should stay with people (with accountability always remaining human), and reconstructing workflows accordingly. You will work alongside teams as a standing resource, diagnosing workflows, co-designing AI-enabled solutions, and building the local capacity teams need to sustain adoption on their own.

The role has two connected parts. First, you will be an AI adoption partner for CRRD, supporting multiple teams at once rather than embedding with one team at a time: providing hands-on guidance, building reusable tools and templates, and cultivating superusers who become self-sustaining champions within their own teams. Second, you will play a key role in delivering the IRC’s AI Learning Strategy. That means partnering with Global Learning & Development (L&D), AI Learning and Change Management working groups, and CRRD colleagues to build experiential learning opportunities like workflow design workshops and master classes.

This is a limited-term role through September 2027. At the conclusion, success means that CRRD teams will work differently, not because of any single tool, but because redesigned workflows are in routine use, managers model their own AI use, and local champions sustain the practice without central support.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Capacity Building & Adoption in CRRD**

- Provide hands-on coaching, training, and feedback loops that build staff comfort and competence with AI tools.
- Facilitate Workflow Design Sprints (short, structured working sessions in which a team maps a real workflow and builds an AI-enabled version of it) with CRRD teams, helping them develop sophisticated, multi-step prompting workflows.
- Monitor adoption and usage patterns across CRRD, adjusting approach to ensure sustained uptake rather than one-off experiments.
- Work with L&D on ways to showcase what teams with AI users have created, show what they gained, and sustain AI-enabled practices after direct engagement ends.

**Workflow Diagnosis & AI Solution Design**

- Work alongside teams to map and diagnose existing workflows, identifying high-value opportunities for AI-enabled improvement and deciding which tasks AI should perform and which should stay with people.
- Build and scale reusable AI-enabled solutions (e.g., prompt & skill libraries, tools, and workflow templates) that can be deployed across teams.
- Ensure solutions are practical, sustainable, and designed for handoff, not dependent on ongoing central support.

**Delivering the AI Learning Strategy**

- In partnership with other AI Adoption Leads and Global Learning & Development, build, adapt and run learning for CRRD staff, including self-paced learning and live learning such as master classes.
- Run peer learning events that show people in the same role what AI has done for colleagues like them: Open Hours, live demos, learning segments in existing department or location meetings.
- Help teams apply the repository standard for shared workflows, so that what teams build is verified, curated and published in a form other teams can reuse.
- Contribute to CRRD AI adoption metrics in partnership with CRRD and AI program leadership. Track and report to leadership quarterly.

**Quality Assurance & Responsible AI Use**

- Make responsible use a practice, not a policy read once: help staff learn what must not be entered into AI tools, how to check the output, and how to own it, with particular care for beneficiary and other sensitive program data, safeguarding, and data protection.
- Contribute to organizational thinking about responsible AI use, ensuring practices reflect both ambition and rigor.
- Help teams apply “what good looks like” for AI-enabled solutions in CRRD (quality checks, human review expectations, evaluation approaches, and documentation), and make sure solutions meet that bar before broad rollout.
- Work with \[IRC’s AI governance team\] so that CRRD practice stays consistent with the AI Policy and the approval process for new AI tools and uses.

**AI Systems, Intake & Scalable Infrastructure**

- Maintain the playbooks, prompt libraries, and workflow templates (in partnership with programs staff) that allow AI-enabled practices to scale, sharing them with the other two AI Adoption Leads and Global L&D so that what is built for one area is reused in others.
- Document lessons learned, edge cases, and best practices in accessible formats that enable self-service adoption.
- Continuously update resources as AI capabilities evolve, staying current with frontier AI developments and proactively identifying new opportunities, ensuring the toolkit reflects what is currently possible.
- Feed insights, best practices, and emerging AI capabilities from your work into the AI Learning Working Group and IRC’s broader AI Transformation efforts.

**Job Requirements:**

- 4–7 years of relevant professional experience (e.g., process improvement, product management, solutions engineering, operations, learning and development, or change management), with increasing recent focus on applying AI tools to personal and/or team workflows.
- fluent in AI platforms, particularly Claude (IRC’s primary platform for this work; hands-on experience with other frontier AI platforms is also valued), and stays current as capabilities evolve. comfort executing sophisticated, multi-step prompting against real operational data / context and using AI to generate and iterate on functional tools (e.g., dashboards, automations, lightweight applications).
- equal parts analyst, builder, coach, and teacher: able to decompose complex workflows, prototype AI-enabled solutions quickly, and bring colleagues along with patience and pragmatism, including colleagues who are skeptical or have real concerns.
- bias for action, a high bar for what “good” looks like, and the judgment to know when AI adds genuine value and when it doesn’t
- Experience designing and facilitating learning for adults (e.g., workshops, training, peer learning, or communities of practice), with the ability to bring non-technical colleagues along and build their confidence with AI tools, including colleagues who are skeptical.
- Ability to influence managers and leaders without formal authority, and to manage several partners and priorities at once.
- Strong written communication skills, particularly the ability to create clear, usable documentation and instructional materials.
- Fluency in English. Proficiency in French, Spanish or Arabic preferred.
- Strongly preferred: Experience working across cultures and time zones.
- Strongly preferred: Familiarity or demonstrated interest with humanitarian program delivery, award management, or emergency response.

**Application Requirements:**

Along with your resume and cover letter, please submit two examples of AI tools, workflows, or applications you have personally built in the past 6 months. This could include:

- Links to custom GPTs or Claude Projects you have created
- Screenshots or documentation of automation workflows you have built
- Demos or code samples of agents you have configured
- Brief descriptions of AI implementations you have led, including the tools used and outcomes achieved

If your work is confidential or belongs to a current or former employer, describe your approach and the outcomes rather than sharing the work itself. Please do not submit any real personal, beneficiary, or other sensitive data.

Please also include an example of how you helped others learn to use AI (e.g., training materials, a workshop outline, a peer demo, or a how-to guide).

Please also briefly describe (up to 150 words) an AI solution or workflow you built that did not work as expected or was not adopted by its intended users, and what you learned from it.

We are specifically looking for evidence of recent hands-on building experience with current AI tools and platforms. The goal is to see how you approach solving problems with AI, not to evaluate you on years of experience in a field where many of these tools have only existed for months.

**Working Environment:** Standard office environment or remote work environment, depending on location.

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Kenya and Jordan.***

jobs.title: Senior Executive Director
jobs.description:
**Application deadline:** Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC is at work today in over 40 countries and 28 U.S. cities. The IRC’s Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) department creates opportunities for refugees and other vulnerable migrants to survive and thrive in the US and Europe. RAI serves more than 100,000 individuals each year in the US, including newly arrived refugees and asylum seekers as well as the broader immigrant community, through a diverse portfolio of programs aimed at five core outcomes: Health, Safety, Economic Wellbeing, Education and Power.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

The Senior Executive Director (SED) provides dynamic leadership for the delivery of high-quality programs within their assigned portfolio (“cluster”) of program offices. The SED directly leads the Atlanta, Miami, and Iowa City program offices and provides leadership, oversight, and support to additional offices within the cluster. They develop a vision for the assigned cluster to achieve impact, growth, operational compliance and excellence, and fiscal sustainability and effectively engage with IRC teams, partners, and external parties to bring the vision to life.

Most office clusters will comprise between six to eight program offices and a total annual operating budget of between $26 - $40 million.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Leadership**

- Lead the development and implementation of RAI’s Strategy100 and local Strategic Action Plan (SAP) initiatives, ensuring alignment with client aspirations and organizational goals.
- For primary office(s), set and communicate vision and strategy. Establish and maintain strong relationships with local leaders, including the State Refugee Coordinator, and communities to further IRC’s mission and act as a thought and operational leader. Foster cooperative working relationships with state and local agencies and service providers, donors, advocacy partners, and community organizations.
- Mentor, advise, and support Executive Directors (EDs) and Site Directors (SDs) as they lead program offices. Support EDs in designated cluster to improve local relationships as appropriate and always enabling the designated ED/SD to be lead in their communities.

**Program & Operational Oversight**

- Ensure efficiency of own primary program office, while also providing support and building high performance in other offices within the assigned portfolio.
- Coordinate cluster operations, ensuring high-quality service delivery in both union and non-union environments and under emergency conditions and/or drastically changing geopolitical landscapes.
- Empower local leadership to ensure that programs are developed collaboratively with strong programmatic cohesion across sectors, particularly between resettlement and non-resettlement programs.
- Provide strategic and operational support to EDs, reinforcing their leadership without assuming representational responsibilities on their behalf within their office and/or community.
- Lead goal setting, track work progress, and assess outcomes to meet departmental objectives and employee needs.
- Engage with RAI and Support Function leaders to drive systems solutions that improve organizational efficiency.
- Promote innovative programming within the cluster and work collaboratively to pilot new ideas.

**Financial & Grants Management**

- Ensure good stewardship of IRC and donor resources. Exercise oversight of operating budgets and cultivate a diligent approach to fiscal management, ensuring that the program offices within the cluster fully meet their obligations.

**Fundraising & Business Development**

- Develop and communicate strategic fundraising priorities which articulate IRC’s vision and ability to provide tangible solutions to specific societal problems.
- Drive vision for office resource development and provide strategic oversight and mentoring to leaders, business development, and grants management teams to meet targets.
- Ensure significant efforts are dedicated to locally sourced public funding, beyond ORR pass-through, in addition to private fundraising.

**Public Advocacy & Media Relations**

- Communicate the organization’s mission, impact, and client needs to various audiences. Advocate for humanitarian issues and promote policy changes at the local and national levels.
- Lead local advocacy efforts in home office and support cluster and national advocacy efforts; host Board, senior staff, and donor visits, and engage in and support community and policy outreach efforts.
- Manage IRC's public image; partner with local media; collaborate with IRC Communications team.
- Foster positive relationships with all collaborators, including client communities, local and regional employers, healthcare providers, school systems, and civil service. Work with partners to enable client success.

**Cultural Sensitivity and Supportive Supervision**

- Cultivate an inclusive, accountable culture rooted in IRC’s People Manager Standards and Guiding Principles.
- Lead a diverse team of staff, interns, and volunteers within the cluster, supporting high performance and well-being.
- Manage cluster functions per IRC policies and standards, encouraging a safe work environment for staff and clients.
- Engage on staff development, retention, and succession planning that fosters an engaging, diverse, and equitable environment.

**KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

**Position reports to:** Vice President, Program Delivery

**Position directly supervises** various positions including: the highest-ranking leader at each program office within their cluster, and the leadership team of the Sr. ED’s home offices.

**Key partners**: RAI HQ Units and IRC Shared Services Support functions groups including Operations, Finance, Strategy, Policy & Advocacy, and People & Culture.

**KEY COMPETENCIES & QUALIFICATIONS:**

**Critical personal characteristics**

- The ideal candidate is a strategist and thought partner who will see beyond their immediate team, role, and cluster and collaborate across functional groups to implement action plans that support broader organizational goals and a ‘One IRC culture.’
- As a manager, they will engage, rally, and inspire the team to the highest quality of work.
- As a leader, they will engage positively with counterparts and leadership at the headquarters level and work towards a constructive and progressive environment.

**Demonstrated Skills and Proficiencies**

- Ability to coordinate, plan, schedule, determine priorities and meet deadlines.
- Outstanding written and verbal communication skills are essential.
- Ability to anticipate and assess situations accurately and recommend/implement effective courses of action required.
- Ability to coordinate multiple meeting tasks and a myriad of complex details on a concurrent basis.
- Ability to communicate effectively with internal and external collaborators with tact and diplomacy, both orally and in writing, including working with all staff levels and diverse personalities.
- Ability to exercise discretion in dealing with sensitive material and maintain confidentiality.
- Ability to handle stress, function effectively under pressure and meet time parameters.
- Ability to expand on own initiative in performance of duties.
- Must have excellent discretion, judgment, tact, initiative, creativity, critical thinking, problem solving, organizational skills, and self-motivation.

**Education & Experience**

- Undergraduate degree or equivalent experience required. Graduate degree in a relevant area strongly preferred.
- Minimum of 10 years’ relevant experience, including 8+ years in senior leadership roles.
- Experience managing large, diverse teams and multi-million-dollar portfolios in humanitarian and/or nonprofit sectors. Experience managing multi-site budgets and teams strongly preferred.

**WORKING ENVIRONMENT**

- Occasional flexibility, after-hour demands and the ability to attend evening and weekend events, when needed.
- This position has been designated as ‘hybrid.’ It requires in-person work, including regular onsite presence within the assigned primary office(s) and periodic travel to additional office(s) within the cluster and other IRC sites. A private, secure, and distraction-free home workspace is required when not working onsite.

Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. jobs.title: Oficial de Seguridad y Acceso Humanitario - Maracaibo
jobs.description:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Seguridad y Acceso Humanitario** altamente calificado con sede en **Maracaibo, Edo. Zulia.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y cuatro oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure, La Guaira y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**Descripción general del cargo**: El/La Oficial de Seguridad y Acceso Humanitario es un miembro clave del equipo de gestión de la base Maracaibo en el Estado Zulia. Su objetivo principal es garantizar la ejecución segura y efectiva de los programas del Consejo Danés para Refugiados (DRC), asegurando el acceso humanitario continuo y fluido a las comunidades. Esta función es responsable de monitorear de cerca el contexto local, proponer e implementar medidas de mitigación de riesgos de seguridad, y mantener una red de contactos sólida con actores locales para facilitar las operaciones humanitarias de DRC en la región.

**Seguridad y acceso humanitario:**

- Participar activamente en las reuniones de planificación de los equipos de programa para integrar el análisis de riesgos y las estrategias de acceso desde el diseño de las actividades.
- Establecer y mantener una red de contactos con autoridades locales, líderes comunitarios, contrapartes y otras partes interesadas para facilitar el acceso seguro a las operaciones.
- Actuar como punto focal para negociar el acceso humanitario seguro a las comunidades vulnerables, en coordinación con los equipos de programa.
- Apoyar al Gerente de Base en la implementación, evaluación y actualización de todos los procedimientos y normas locales de seguridad.
- Proporcionar asesoramiento oportuno sobre la gestión de riesgos de seguridad y acceso en el desarrollo y ejecución de los programas.
- Identificar barreras de acceso y apoyar a los equipos del programa para desarrollar e implementar estrategias de participación comunitaria que promuevan la aceptación y el acceso de DRC.
- Participar activamente en la identificación de las mejores rutas terrestres y fluviales para distribución de canastas.
- Realizar la evaluación de transporte terrestre y fluvial, asegurando que cumplan con los requerimientos de seguridad necesarios para el resguardo de los colaboradores y las distribuciones planteadas.

**Monitoreo, informes y análisis**

- Monitorear y analizar continuamente los incidentes y las tendencias contextuales en materia de seguridad y acceso en los diferentes municipios del Estado Zulia.
- Responder ante incidentes de seguridad, manteniendo estrecha comunicación con el Gerente de Base y equipo de Seguridad de la Oficina Nacional.
- Informar inmediatamente al Gerente de Base sobre cualquier cambio repentino en el contexto que pueda afectar la seguridad del personal o el acceso a las áreas de operación.
- Realizar Evaluaciones de Riesgos de Seguridad (SRA) periódicas para las áreas de intervención y para misiones exploratorias en nuevas zonas.
- Apoyar en la preparación y entrega de Reportes de Incidentes de Seguridad (SIR) al Gerente de Base y al equipo de seguridad nacional.
- Proporcionar insumos contextuales para los informes de situación humanitaria.

**Enlace y coordinación:**

- Coordinar la comunicación con actores relevantes en todos los asuntos relacionados con la seguridad del personal y el acceso humanitario.
- Mantener y actualizar regularmente una lista de contactos de partes interesadas en el área operativa.
- Trabajar en estrecha colaboración con la Coordinación de Seguridad y Acceso Nacional para asegurar la coherencia en los procedimientos.

**Capacitación y desarrollo de capacidades**

- Apoyar al Gerente de Base en la realización de inducciones de seguridad a nuevos integrantes de la organización y visitantes.
- Impartir capacitaciones en procedimientos de seguridad y concienciación sobre el contexto para todo el personal de la base.
- Promover la sensibilización interna y el conocimiento de los documentos y estrategias de acceso de la organización.
- Apoyar el equipo de Ecrec en las actividades de registro y distribución de alimentos en las diferentes comunidades

**Experiencia y competencias técnicas:**

- Mínimo 3 años de experiencia en un puesto similar, preferiblemente en seguridad, acceso humanitario o logística con organizaciones humanitarias nacionales y/o internacionales.
- Conocimiento profundo del contexto social, político y de seguridad del Estado Sucre y capacidad para establecer redes de contacto en la zona.
- Capacidad para trabajar en un entorno de seguridad fluido, impredecible y complejo y disponibilidad para trabajar en horarios irregulares si la situación lo requiere.
- Excelentes habilidades de comunicación, negociación y diplomacia para interactuar con una amplia gama de actores.
- Fuertes capacidades analíticas y de resolución de problemas.
- Se requiere un alto nivel de alfabetización informática, con excelente manejo de MS Word, Excel y PowerPoint.

**Educación**:

- Título Universitario en áreas de ciencias sociales, relaciones internacionales, administración, logística o un campo afín.

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1.000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda H.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: **miércoles 2 de diciembre de 2026** a las 23:59 Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

**Fecha de inicio aproximada:** Diciembre 2026.

jobs.title: Security & Liaison Officer, Hasakah, Syria
jobs.description:
The Security & Liaison Officer supports the safe, informed, principled and sustained delivery of DCA’s humanitarian operations in the area of responsibility. The postholder contributes to security risk management, staff safety, movement and journey management, emergency preparedness, incident response, security information analysis, and the development and maintenance of constructive relationships with authorities, community stakeholders, humanitarian actors, and other relevant interlocutors. The role supports operational access while upholding humanitarian principles, duty of care, and DCA policies and procedures.

**Functional Responsibilities:**

• Contribute to the development and implementation of safety and security policies, procedures, and protocols.

• Conduct safety and security risk assessments to identify potential security threats and vulnerabilities.

• Collaborate with other departments to integrate security measures into overall business operations.

• Oversee the installation, maintenance, and monitoring of access and security systems.

• Respond to security incidents and emergencies promptly.

• Manage access control systems to regulate entry and exit from secured areas.

• Conduct periodic audits to ensure compliance with access control policies.

• Approve Journey Management Plans (JMP’S) for operational staff visits.

• Provide training to employees on safety and security protocols and procedures.

• Conduct drills and exercises to ensure that staff are prepared for emergency situations.

• Foster a culture of security awareness throughout the organization.

• Investigate security incidents, breaches, and violations as directed.

• Coordinate with law enforcement agencies as directed.

• Develop and implement corrective actions to prevent future incidents.

• Maintain communication with relevant stakeholders, including employees, management, and external authorities.

• Prepare and submit regular reports on security activities, incidents, and trends.

• Provide practical safety, security and access advice to programme, logistics, and field teams.

• Represent DCA at area level, in relevant safety and security forums (INSO, UNDSS) and maintain accurate records of engagements and follow-up actions.

• Support timely acquisition, renewal, and management of permissions, approvals, and other access-related requirements, within delegated authority.

• Work with external security service providers or vendors to ensure the effectiveness of security measures.

• Evaluate and select security technology, equipment, and services.

• Stay informed about relevant laws and regulations pertaining to security.

• Monitor and analyse developments affecting humanitarian access, including administrative barriers, movement restrictions, community dynamics, and changes in local authority arrangements.

• Ensure the organization's compliance with security-related legal requirements.

• Assist with the development and maintain emergency response plans.

**Minimum Required Knowledge & Experience:**

• University Degree or equivalent professional qualification in security risk management, international relations, humanitarian affairs, political science, law, public administration, or a related discipline.

• At least 3–5 years of relevant experience in humanitarian safety, security, access, or risk management.

• Experience supporting staff safety and movement, including journey management, field-mission planning, communications protocols, movement tracking, and emergency preparedness.

• Strong stakeholder-engagement and liaison skills, with the ability to build constructive, professional relationships with local authorities, community representatives, humanitarian actors, and security actors while maintaining appropriate boundaries.

• Demonstrated security risk-management capability, including context monitoring, security analysis, risk assessment, mitigation planning, contingency planning, and incident response.

• Excellent Arabic and professional working (verbal and written) English, including the ability to conduct liaison, produce clear written security reporting, and communicate effectively with diverse internal and external stakeholders.

• Formal training in security risk management, first aid, crisis management, humanitarian access, civil-military coordination, or explosive-ordnance risk.

• Experience engaging with INSO, UNDSS, OCHA, humanitarian clusters, or area security-management structures.

• Experience supporting mine-action, explosive-ordinance-risk, protection, livelihoods, or integrated humanitarian programmes.
