jobs.title: Coordinateur administratif (F/H) - République Démocratique du Congo
jobs.description:
Vous souhaitez intégrer une association militante et agir concrètement pour plus de justice sociale ?

Médecins du Monde agit depuis plus de 40 ans pour soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, dénoncer les entraves à l’accès aux soins et faire évoluer durablement les politiques de santé.

En France et dans près de 30 pays, nos actions s’articulent autour de six combats politiques :

- droits et santé sexuels et reproductifs (dont le droit à l’avortement)
- migration, exil, droits et santé
- réduction des risques
- santé environnement
- droits et système de santé
- espaces humanitaires

**MdM en République démocratique du Congo**

Dans le cadre de sa réponse d’urgence à l’épidémie d’Ebola, Médecins du Monde déploie une mission à Isiro, en République démocratique du Congo. Le contexte exige une organisation administrative, financière et RH réactive, fiable et adaptée à une intervention de courte durée, ainsi qu’un suivi rigoureux des exigences légales, internes et bailleurs.

**Pourquoi nous avons besoin de vous**

Vous prenez en charge la coordination administrative de la réponse d’urgence. Vous structurez et sécurisez les dispositifs RH, financiers et comptables de la mission, accompagnez les équipes opérationnelles et garantissez la conformité des pratiques de Médecins du Monde et de ses partenaires.

**Vos missions**

**Piloter la gestion des ressources humaines de la mission**

- Déployer et actualiser la stratégie, les politiques et les procédures RH dans le respect du droit national et des standards de MdM
- Suivre le budget RH, les effectifs, l’organigramme et la base de données du personnel
- Superviser la paie, le paiement des impôts, l’administration du personnel, les recrutements et le suivi des situations individuelles
- Former les équipes aux politiques fondamentales de MdM, notamment la PSEA, la lutte contre la fraude et la corruption et la protection de l’enfance
- Conseiller les responsables sur la gestion des équipes, des conflits et des procédures disciplinaires

**Garantir l’organisation financière et la conformité de la mission**

- Mettre en œuvre les procédures financières et les mécanismes de contrôle interne de MdM et des bailleurs
- Élaborer et suivre les budgets, analyser les écarts, proposer les réallocations nécessaires et produire les rapports financiers
- Veiller au respect des obligations fiscales, faciliter les audits et garantir l’archivage des pièces justificatives
- Organiser les réunions mensuelles de suivi budgétaire et fournir aux équipes les informations nécessaires au pilotage des programmes
- Suivre et contrôler la gestion financière des partenaires locaux

**Superviser la trésorerie et la comptabilité**

- Évaluer les besoins de trésorerie, consolider les demandes de fonds et sécuriser les paiements
- Superviser la comptabilité informatisée de l’ensemble des sites et l’imputation aux bailleurs
- Actualiser les protocoles de gestion de trésorerie et coordonner les clôtures comptables mensuelles et annuelles avec le siège
- Identifier des prestataires de services financiers fiables et adaptés au contexte

**Manager et accompagner l’équipe administrative**

- Recruter, intégrer, former et accompagner les personnes placées sous votre supervision directe ou technique
- Fixer les objectifs, organiser la charge de travail, suivre les plans d’action et conduire les évaluations professionnelles
- Organiser les réunions du département administratif et superviser la politique et les outils de signalement des alertes

**Contribuer à la coordination et à la représentation de la mission**

- Contribuer aux rapports internes et externes
- Entretenir les liens avec les départements administratifs des autres ONG internationales présentes dans le pays
- Superviser étroitement les activités administratives et financières des partenaires locaux

Cette liste d’activités n’est pas exhaustive et peut évoluer selon la situation.

**Vos collègues**

Vous travaillez sous la responsabilité hiérarchique du coordinateur urgence en lien fonctionnel avec les référent·es RH et finances au siège. Vous supervisez directement un.e chargé.e d’administration de droit national, en cours de recrutement, et apportez un appui technique aux équipes opérationnelles.

**Ce que vous pouvez attendre de nous**

- Renforcer votre capacité à piloter simultanément les dimensions RH, financières et administratives d’une réponse d’urgence
- Développer votre maîtrise du suivi budgétaire, de la conformité bailleurs et des mécanismes de contrôle interne en contexte humanitaire
- Consolider vos compétences de management, de formation et d’accompagnement d’équipes dans un environnement exigeant
- Approfondir votre capacité à conseiller les opérations et à travailler avec des partenaires locaux, des autorités et un réseau d’ONG internationales

## PROFIL

**Vous êtes la bonne personne si…**

- Vous êtes titulaire d’une formation supérieure en gestion de niveau bac + 3 minimum
- Vous justifiez d’au moins quatre ans d’expérience professionnelle, dont au moins deux ans au sein d’une ONG internationale dans une fonction administrative
- Vous maîtrisez la gestion budgétaire, la comptabilité, la trésorerie, les procédures bailleurs, la paie et l’administration du personnel
- Vous savez analyser les écarts entre prévisions et réalisations, identifier les risques et proposer des solutions opérationnelles
- Vous savez concevoir et adapter des procédures, conduire des recrutements et accompagner les responsables sur les sujets RH
- Vous avez une expérience du management, de la formation et du développement des compétences
- Vous faites preuve de réactivité, d’anticipation, d’autonomie, d’adaptabilité et d’un excellent sens des priorités
- Vous disposez de solides capacités de négociation, de communication et de travail en réseau
- Vous maîtrisez parfaitement le français à l’oral comme à l’écrit.
- Vous avez une excellente maîtrise de Microsoft Office, notamment Excel, ainsi qu’une connaissance des logiciels comptables et des bases de données RH
- Une expérience en contexte de conflit ou en environnement difficile, dans la négociation avec les autorités ou au sein de Médecins du Monde constitue un atout

**Ce poste n’est pas pour vous si…**

- Vous n’êtes pas disponible pour une mission courte, à temps plein, basée à Isiro et impliquant des déplacements réguliers sur les sites d’intervention
- Vous ne souhaitez pas travailler dans un contexte d’urgence évolutif, avec des priorités susceptibles de changer rapidement
- Vous préférez intervenir uniquement sur les sujets financiers ou uniquement sur les sujets RH, sans assurer une coordination administrative transversale
- Vous craignez ne pas vous retrouver dans les valeurs et le positionnement militant de Médecins du Monde

**Les prochaines étapes**

Si votre candidature est sélectionnée, nous vous contacterons rapidement pour vous proposer un entretien RH avec un·e chargé·e de recrutement. Des entretiens techniques et managériaux, auxquels un cas pratique pourra éventuellement être intégré, pourront ensuite être organisés.

Dans le cadre de notre processus de recrutement, une prise de références est systématiquement réalisée par l’équipe recrutement auprès de contacts professionnels fournis par les candidat·e·s.

Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, des vérifications d’antécédents sur listes internationales pourront être effectuées. Les données sont traitées de façon confidentielle et sécurisée. Plus d’informations : https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/nous-rejoindre/travail-humanitaire/travailler-a-linternational/

Un extrait de casier judiciaire (B3) sera demandé à toute personne recrutée.

**Nous attendons votre candidature**

Nous n’avons besoin que de votre CV et de votre lettre de motivation.

Si vous pensez correspondre à ce poste, postulez

## **VOS CONDITIONS D'EMPLOI**

**Contrat & statut :**

- Salaire brut mensuel 3 392 €
- Contrat à durée déterminée d’usage (CDDU) de 10 semaines, suivi de 21 jours de quarantaine ou de surveillance au retour (dans son pays d'origine) à pourvoir à compter du 21 décembre 2026
- Prise de poste au plus tard le 21 décembre 2026
- Statut agent de maîtrise
- Départ seul
- Temps plein

**Cadre de travail :**

- Poste basé à Isiro, en République Démocratique du Congo (RDC)

**Les avantages :**

- 13e mois (pour les salarié.e.s ayant plus de 6 mois d’ancienneté)
- Prime d’expatriation de 10% du salaire brut par mois
- Prise en charge du transport (domicile – mission), des visas, des vaccins
- Hébergement: vous serez hébergé.e à l'hôtel (pris en echarge par MdM)
- Assurance santé (participation à 50% de MdM et 50% du salarié)
- Assurance rapatriement
- MdM favorise la formation et la mobilité interne

**Les indispensables :**

- 5 semaines de congés + 22,5 RTT par an
- Plus d’infos : https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/nous-rejoindre/travail-humanitaire/travailler-a-linternational/

**Diversité et inclusion**

Médecins du Monde s’engage pour l’insertion des personnes en situation de handicap et lutte contre toutes les discriminations.

Si vous bénéficiez d’une reconnaissance de la qualité de travailleur·se handicapé·e et/ou si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement de poste, n’hésitez pas à nous en faire part

jobs.title: Oficial de Monitoreo Local (Estados Distrito Capital, La Guaira y Miranda-Venezuela)
jobs.description:
## **Antecedentes**

RET está comprometido a trabajar en emergencias, en crisis prolongadas y en contextos frágiles para aliviar los sufrimientos más profundos, construir la resiliencia de las personas y mejorar su autosuficiencia.

Somos una de las ONG líderes en ofrecer soluciones a medida y programas pertinentes para reducir las brechas y responder a las necesidades y retos reales de las comunidades.

Asumimos un papel catalizador decisivo en el desarrollo sostenible. Nuestro objetivo es provocar un cambio positivo significativo que permita a jóvenes y mujeres jóvenes especialmente vulnerables tomar las riendas de sus vidas y hacer realidad sus derechos sociales y económicos.

Acompañamos a las personas, a los refugiados, a los retornados, a los desplazados internos y a las comunidades de acogida, adoptando los principios fundamentales de humanidad, imparcialidad, neutralidad e independencia.

En el marco de los proyectos que RET International implementa en Venezuela, se publica la posición de Oficial de Monitoreo Local (Estados Distrito Capital, La Guaira y Miranda).

## **Descripción del puesto**

### **Objetivo del puesto**

El/la Oficial de Monitoreo Local será responsable de implementar en los territorios asignados las actividades de monitoreo, seguimiento, rendición de cuentas y gestión de información del proyecto, asegurando la recolección oportuna y de calidad de los datos generados por las intervenciones de RET, el adecuado registro y seguimiento de las personas participantes y la disponibilidad y trazabilidad de los Medios de Verificación requeridos por el proyecto.

Asimismo, realizará el seguimiento territorial de los indicadores, metas y actividades bajo responsabilidad de RET; implementará los procedimientos establecidos para el registro de participantes, control primario de duplicaciones, seguimiento de cohortes y rendición de cuentas a las poblaciones afectadas (AAP); y remitirá al Oficial MEAL – Proyecto de RET información completa, consistente y debidamente verificada para su validación y consolidación a nivel nacional.

### **Ubicación del puesto**

La posición está basada en la Oficina Local de RET con cobertura operacional directa sobre los municipios priorizados de la zona centro-occidente, en los estados Distrito Capital, La Guaira y Miranda. Requiere disponibilidad permanente para realizar desplazamientos y misiones de campo a los centros educativos de la zona.

### **Línea de Reporte y Coordinación**

1. ### Reporta al Oficial MEAL – Proyecto.
2. Coordina con el/la Coordinador/a Local de Proyecto, los Oficiales de Monitoreo Local de la otra zona del país y el equipo técnico de Educación en Emergencias, Infraestructura/WASH y Seguridad
3. Articula con Puntos Focales MEAL/M&E de socios implementadores en la región.

**Responsabilidades Específicas**

*1. Levantamiento, Calidad y Gestión de Datos en Terreno*
4. Implementar en los territorios asignados las herramientas, metodologías y procedimientos de recolección de información establecidos en el Plan MEAL del proyecto, asegurando su aplicación consistente en las intervenciones bajo responsabilidad de RET.
5. Recopilar y registrar oportunamente información cuantitativa y cualitativa en escuelas y Espacios Educativos y de Bienestar (EEB) de Distrito Capital, La Guaira y Miranda mediante dispositivos móviles y formularios digitalizados (KoboToolbox / ODK).
6. Garantizar que la captura de datos cumpla con los criterios de desagregación requeridos: sexo, edad, tipo de discapacidad (Set Breve de Washington), condición de movilidad humana y estado/municipio.
7. Realizar la verificación primaria de inconsistencias, duplicaciones o vacíos en las listas de beneficiarios e instrumentos de campo antes de su carga final en el sistema centralizado de la organización.
8. Apoyar la actualización y mantenimiento seguro de las bases de datos locales y los repositorios digitales en la nube de la zona asignada.
9. Asegurar la correcta aplicación de los mecanismos de consentimiento, confidencialidad y protección de datos durante los procesos de recolección y registro de información.

**2. Seguimiento a Indicadores (KPIs) y Alertas Tempranas**
10. Realizar el seguimiento periódico de los indicadores, actividades y metas correspondientes a las intervenciones de RET en los territorios asignados, de acuerdo con el Marco de Resultados y el Plan MEAL.
11. Mantener actualizadas las herramientas territoriales de seguimiento y proporcionar al Oficial MEAL – Proyecto información sobre avances, brechas y aspectos que requieran atención.
12. Monitorear los indicadores clave de desempeño (KPIs) correspondientes a su ámbito territorial e identificar oportunamente desviaciones respecto de las metas previstas.
13. Generar alertas tempranas sobre retrasos, brechas de cobertura, inconsistencias de información u otros factores que puedan afectar el cumplimiento de los resultados previstos, informando oportunamente al Oficial MEAL – Proyecto y a la Coordinación Local.
14. Participar en reuniones periódicas de seguimiento con los equipos técnicos y operativos de RET para revisar avances y apoyar la definición y seguimiento de acciones correctivas.

**3. Registro de participantes y control primario de duplicaciones**
15. Implementar en terreno los procedimientos establecidos por el proyecto para el registro único de participantes y control de duplicaciones.
16. Verificar la correcta identificación y registro de las personas participantes antes de incorporar la información a las bases correspondientes.
17. Realizar controles primarios para identificar posibles registros duplicados, inconsistencias o información incompleta, efectuando las verificaciones y correcciones correspondientes antes de remitir la información al Oficial MEAL – Proyecto.
18. Documentar e informar los casos de posibles duplicaciones que no puedan ser resueltos a nivel territorial para su revisión por el Oficial MEAL – Proyecto.
19. Garantizar la adecuada trazabilidad de los registros de participantes entre las diferentes actividades y servicios implementados por RET en los territorios asignados.

**4. Seguimiento de participantes y cohortes**
20. Implementar en terreno los mecanismos definidos para el seguimiento individual y longitudinal de las personas participantes y cohortes que requieran mediciones periódicas.
21. Dar seguimiento a la información necesaria para la medición de indicadores relacionados con acceso, asistencia, permanencia, continuidad, finalización y aprendizaje, según corresponda a las intervenciones implementadas por RET.
22. Verificar la actualización periódica de los registros requeridos para mantener la trazabilidad de los participantes durante el período de seguimiento.
23. Identificar casos con información incompleta, pérdida de seguimiento u otras inconsistencias y coordinar con los equipos correspondientes las acciones necesarias para actualizar los registros.
24. Remitir oportunamente al Oficial MEAL – Proyecto la información requerida para la medición y análisis de los indicadores de seguimiento de cohortes.

**5. Calidad y verificación de datos**
25. Realizar controles rutinarios de calidad de la información recopilada en terreno, verificando completitud, exactitud, consistencia y oportunidad.
26. Revisar periódicamente las bases y registros correspondientes a los territorios asignados e identificar errores, vacíos o inconsistencias antes de su remisión al nivel nacional.
27. Implementar las acciones correctivas requeridas y dar seguimiento a su resolución con los equipos responsables.
28. Apoyar los ejercicios de verificación y evaluación de calidad de datos (DQA) coordinados por el Oficial MEAL – Proyecto.
29. Mantener un adecuado registro de las verificaciones realizadas, hallazgos identificados y acciones correctivas implementadas.

*6. Medios de Verificación (MoV) y Soportes*
30. Recopilar, verificar, organizar y archivar de manera sistemática (en físico y digital) los Medios de Verificación (MoV) de las actividades locales: listas de asistencia firmadas, actas de entrega de kits educativos/higiene, fichas de infraestructura, fotos georreferenciadas y registros de talleres.
31. Garantizar que la documentación de soporte cumpla rigurosamente con los estándares institucionales de RET y las exigencias del donante para superar auditorías.
32. Asegurar su correcta identificación, organización y almacenamiento conforme a los procedimientos establecidos por el proyecto.
33. Identificar oportunamente MoV faltantes, incompletos o inconsistentes y coordinar con los equipos técnicos y operativos su subsanación.
34. Remitir los MoV requeridos al Oficial MEAL – Proyecto conforme a los calendarios y procedimientos establecidos.

**7. Monitoreo de campo**

1. Realizar visitas periódicas de monitoreo a escuelas, espacios educativos, comunidades y demás lugares de implementación de las actividades de RET en los territorios asignados.
2. Verificar en terreno el avance, cobertura y ejecución de las actividades y contrastar la información observada con los registros y resultados reportados.
3. Aplicar listas de verificación, herramientas de observación y otros instrumentos de monitoreo establecidos para el proyecto.
4. Documentar los principales hallazgos, brechas y recomendaciones derivados de las visitas y comunicarlos oportunamente al Oficial MEAL – Proyecto y a la Coordinación Local.
5. Dar seguimiento a las acciones de mejora acordadas como resultado de los ejercicios de monitoreo.

### **8. Rendición de Cuentas (AAP) y Marcadores Transversales**

1. Desplegar y supervisar el funcionamiento operativo de los mecanismos de Retroalimentación, Quejas y Reclamos (FCRM/AAP) en las escuelas y comunidades de Distrito Capital, La Guaira y Miranda.
2. Recoger, registrar y canalizar confidencialmente las peticiones, comentarios o denuncias recibidas de estudiantes, docentes y familias, aplicando los protocolos de referencia segura para casos sensibles de Protección/PSEAH.
3. Monitorear en terreno la aplicación del Marcador de Género y Edad (IASC GAM), los enfoques de inclusión para personas con discapacidad y las Normas Mínimas de la INEE en las entregas y talleres.
4. Asegurar que los mecanismos sean accesibles, seguros, confidenciales e inclusivos, considerando las características y necesidades de las diferentes poblaciones participantes.
5. Registrar y canalizar oportunamente la retroalimentación y las quejas recibidas hacia las instancias responsables, asegurando su adecuado seguimiento y cierre.
6. Identificar y derivar inmediatamente, conforme a los protocolos establecidos, cualquier queja o información sensible relacionada con protección, salvaguarda, PSEAH u otros riesgos, sin realizar investigaciones que excedan las responsabilidades del cargo.
7. Contribuir a la sistematización de la retroalimentación recibida en los territorios para identificar tendencias y oportunidades de mejora.

**9. Reporte y flujo de información**

- Preparar y remitir al Oficial MEAL – Proyecto los reportes, bases de datos, matrices, MoV y demás información territorial requerida, respetando los formatos y calendarios establecidos.
- Asegurar que la información remitida haya sido previamente revisada y cuente con los controles básicos de calidad correspondientes.
- Responder oportunamente a solicitudes de aclaración, corrección o complementación de información formuladas por el Oficial MEAL – Proyecto.
- Mantener comunicación permanente con el Oficial MEAL – Proyecto sobre avances, dificultades, riesgos y necesidades identificadas en los procesos de monitoreo territorial.
- Contribuir con información y evidencia territorial para la elaboración de informes, análisis y productos de seguimiento del proyecto.

**10. Apoyo a evaluaciones, estudios y ejercicios de medición**

- Apoyar la implementación territorial de líneas de base, evaluaciones, estudios, encuestas y otros ejercicios de medición previstos por el proyecto.
- Apoyar la organización logística y coordinación con comunidades, centros educativos y participantes para los procesos de recolección de información.
- Aplicar o apoyar la aplicación de herramientas de recolección conforme a los protocolos metodológicos establecidos.
- Contribuir a los procesos de seguimiento y verificación requeridos para garantizar la calidad de la información recopilada.
- Apoyar la documentación de lecciones aprendidas, buenas prácticas e historias de cambio significativo identificadas en los territorios.

### **11. Articulación Local y Fortalecimiento de Capacidades**

1. Orientar y brindar asistencia técnica a los docentes, personal de escuelas y organizaciones aliadas locales sobre el correcto llenado de formatos e instrumentos de recolección de datos.
2. Representar al equipo MEAL de RET, previa delegación, en las mesas locales de coordinación del Clúster de Educación y espacios interinstitucionales en Distrito Capital, La Guaira y Miranda.
3. Aportar información de contexto (socioeconómico, migratorio, de seguridad y dinámicas escolares) para los reportes situacionales y análisis de tendencias en su zona.

### **Responsabilidades Secundarias y Transversales**

1. Participar en ejercicios de evaluación de medio término, línea de base, evaluaciones finales o estudios cualitativos (grupos focales, entrevistas a informantes clave) que ordene el Oficial MEAL – Proyecto.
2. Apoyar la identificación y documentación de historias de éxito, testimonios y casos de estudio (Most Significant Change) en las escuelas atendidas para visibilizar el impacto del proyecto.
3. Velar por la protección estricta de la imagen institucional, el cumplimiento del uso de logos del donante/RET y el respeto a las políticas de consentimiento informado en la toma de fotografías o vídeos.
4. Cumplir con cualquier otra tarea técnica o de soporte operativo inherente a sus funciones que le sea asignada por el/la Oficial MEAL – Proyecto o la Coordinación de Proyecto.
5. Facilitar información técnica, programática y de resultados del proyecto, y apoyar el desarrollo de nuevas propuestas e iniciativas, aportando datos, evidencias, aprendizajes y otros insumos relevantes derivados de la implementación.

Adicionalmente, como todo el personal de RET
6. Trabajar con confianza e integridad y tener un claro compromiso con los valores fundamentales y los principios de RET, asegurando que las actividades y su desempeño cumplan con lo establecido en el Código de Conducta de RET, el PSEAH y otros Manuales y Políticas Internas;
7. Trabajar en equipo demostrando transparencia, habilidades de gestión y uso eficiente de los recursos asignados.
8. Comunicarse de manera clara, asertiva y sensible con las comunidades, organizaciones e instituciones vinculadas al proyecto.
9. Proponer, de manera constructiva, soluciones alternativas ante los desafíos que se presenten en el terreno.

## **Calificaciones y requisitos**

### **Formación y experiencia**

1. Título Universitario en Ciencias Sociales, Economía, Estadística, Educación, Trabajo Social o carreras afines.
2. Formación complementaria en Monitoreo y Evaluación, MEAL, gestión de información, análisis de datos, investigación social o áreas relacionadas, deseable.
3. Mínimo de tres (3) años de experiencia comprobable en funciones de monitoreo, recolección, levantamiento y sistematización de información en proyectos sociales o humanitarios.
4. Experiencia en recolección, registro, procesamiento, validación y control de calidad de datos, incluyendo trabajo directo en terreno.
5. Experiencia en trabajo de campo con comunidades vulnerables, escuelas, niños, niñas y adolescentes.
6. Experiencia en respuesta humanitaria o proyectos de Educación en Emergencias (EiE) o Protección (valorado muy positivamente).
7. Experiencia de trabajo en los estados Falcón, Carabobo y/o Aragua (deseable por conocimiento del contexto local).
8. Nacionalidad venezolana o permiso de trabajo legal en el país (indispensable).
9. Idiomas: Español fluido oral y escrito (indispensable).

**Competencias técnicas**

1. Conocimiento práctico de Monitoreo, Evaluación, Rendición de Cuentas y Aprendizaje (MEAL) y seguimiento basado en resultados.
2. Capacidad para aplicar correctamente definiciones de indicadores, criterios de medición, herramientas y protocolos de recolección de datos.
3. Experiencia en registro y seguimiento de participantes, controles primarios de duplicación y verificación de calidad de registros.
4. Capacidad para realizar seguimiento longitudinal de participantes y cohortes, manteniendo registros completos y actualizados.
5. Conocimiento y experiencia práctica en control de calidad de datos, identificación de inconsistencias y aplicación de acciones correctivas.
6. Capacidad para recopilar, revisar, organizar y verificar Medios de Verificación.
7. Dominio en el uso de herramientas digitales de recolección de data en terreno (KoboToolbox, ODK o similares).
8. Manejo intermedio/avanzado de Microsoft Excel (fórmulas, limpieza de datos, consolidación de bases) y paquete Office 365.
9. Familiaridad con el manejo de canales de atención comunitaria / AAP y mecanismos de quejas y reclamos.
10. Conocimiento básico de estándares humanitarios (Normas Mínimas INEE, enfoque de género e inclusión de discapacidad).
11. Alta rigurosidad, atención al detalle y compromiso con la precisión y veracidad de la información recopilada.
12. Excelentes habilidades interpersonales y de comunicación sensible para interactuar con comunidades, docentes y autoridades educativas.
13. Capacidad de organización autónoma del trabajo bajo presión, priorizando metas simultáneas en contextos dinámicos.
14. Disposición e idoneidad física para realizar traslados terrestres continuos a comunidades rurales y urbanas de los 9 municipios de cobertura.
15. Capacidad para realizar monitoreo de campo, observación estructurada, entrevistas y aplicación de herramientas cuantitativas y cualitativas

jobs.title: REGIONAL RISK ANALYST-AFRICA
jobs.description:
**1. Role Purpose**

Provide independent, evidence-based and forward-looking assessments of security and broader contextual risks across the Aga Khan Development Network’s (AKDN) African operating environments. The role is responsible for producing timely, analytically rigorous and operationally relevant assessments that identify emerging threats, anticipate potential developments and support informed decision-making by AKDN leadership and field teams.

**2. Key Responsibilities**

**Security Monitoring and Risk Analysis**

- Monitor security, political, economic, social and humanitarian developments in countries and sectors where AKDN operates in Africa, drawing on credible open, authorised non-public and social-media sources.
- Independently produce concise, high-quality country, regional, sectoral and incident-based assessments that explain underlying drivers, emerging risks, likely developments and their implications for AKDN personnel, assets and programmes.
- Apply structured analytical techniques, including hypothesis testing, scenario analysis and the identification of indicators and warnings, to challenge assumptions, assess alternative explanations and develop defensible analytical judgements.
- Critically evaluate information sources, distinguish verified facts from analytical assessments, identify information gaps and clearly communicate uncertainty and confidence levels.
- Translate analytical findings into practical operational implications, including personnel security, programme delivery, travel and movement planning, operational continuity and potential risk mitigation measures.
- Proactively identify emerging developments requiring Security Risk Advisories, analytical commentary, situation reports or other targeted analytical products.

**Reporting and Information Management**

- Independently manage assigned reporting responsibilities, ensuring the timely delivery of accurate, analytically robust and publication-ready products that meet departmental quality and presentation standards with minimal substantive revision.
- Maintain and analyse incident and risk datasets, producing maps, charts and other visualisations that identify trends, geographical concentrations, escalation indicators and changes in operational exposure.
- Manage competing reporting priorities and deadlines, proactively communicating potential delays or constraints and taking appropriate measures to maintain continuity of analytical outputs.
- Issue timely alerts and situation updates, respond to urgent information requests and provide analytical support during significant incidents, crises or surge events, as required.
- Apply appropriate professional judgement when using AI-assisted research and analytical tools, ensuring independent reasoning, verification of outputs, source integrity and compliance with organisational information security requirements.

**Briefings, Coordination and Operational Support**

- Deliver concise, decision-oriented security briefings to Security Coordination Cells (SCCs), Department of International Security (DIS) leadership and other AKDN agency staff, adapting content to specialist and non-specialist audiences.
- Clearly communicate and substantiate analytical judgements, including key assumptions, uncertainties, alternative scenarios and potential operational consequences.
- Maintain constructive relationships with AKDN field teams and relevant security, development and humanitarian counterparts to strengthen information sharing and contextual understanding.
- Undertake occasional field visits to strengthen situational awareness, validate analytical assessments and engage with relevant stakeholders.
- Contribute analytical input to departmental risk planning, preparedness, crisis management and strategic discussions.
- Protect sensitive information and sources through appropriate information security practices, confidentiality and need-to-know dissemination.
- Undertake other relevant analytical tasks assigned by the Senior Security Risk Analyst (SSRA) and Global Security Operations Adviser (GSOA).

**3. Reporting and Coordination**

The Regional Risk Analyst reports directly to the Senior Security Risk Analyst, with strategic oversight provided by the Global Security Operations Adviser.

The position works closely with DIS colleagues, AKDN Security Coordination Cells, agency security focal points and relevant field representatives to ensure analytical products remain aligned with organisational priorities and operational requirements.

**4. Job Specifications**

Essential Qualifications and Experience

- Bachelor's degree in international relations, security studies, political science, criminology, law, data analysis or a related discipline.
- Minimum three years of relevant experience in security, geopolitical or contextual risk analysis, including independent production of analytical reports. Five or more years preferred.
- Strong understanding of political, security and socioeconomic dynamics in Africa, with expertise in at least one of the Sahel, Central, East or Southern Africa regions.
- Proven ability to evaluate sources, synthesise complex information and produce independent, evidence-based and forward-looking analysis.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly present security risks, operational implications and recommendations to diverse audiences.
- Ability to analyse security-related datasets and produce relevant maps, charts and other visualisations.
- Working knowledge of open-source research, social-media monitoring, incident tracking and information management.
- Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and ability to independently manage competing priorities and deadlines.
- Sound judgement, discretion and professional integrity, with the ability to work effectively under pressure and during crises.
- Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate across multicultural and geographically dispersed teams.
- Willingness to undertake occasional field travel.

**Desirable Qualifications and Experience**

- Postgraduate qualification or professional certification in security studies, intelligence analysis, geopolitical risk, geospatial analysis or risk management.
- Advanced proficiency in geographic information systems (GIS) and data visualisation platforms, including ArcGIS, QGIS, Excel, Power BI or comparable applications.
- Experience in spatial analysis, multi-variable data visualisation and the integration of quantitative and qualitative information into analytical products.
- Working knowledge of Adobe Creative Cloud applications, particularly InDesign, for producing professional reports and visual analytical products.
- Experience supporting international, humanitarian, development or multi-country operations, preferably in complex or fragile environments.
- Experience delivering security briefings, supporting crisis management activities or providing analytical advice to senior decisionmakers.

**5. Core Competencies**

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

- **Analytical rigour:** Ability to move beyond descriptive reporting to identify underlying drivers, assess risks, anticipate developments and articulate operational implications.
- **Independent judgement:** Capacity to develop and defend well-reasoned analytical conclusions, recognise uncertainty and challenge assumptions constructively.
- **Initiative and accountability:** Proactive identification of emerging risks, independent ownership of assigned responsibilities and consistent delivery against agreed deadlines.
- **Technical proficiency:** Ability to use research, data analysis and visualisation tools to strengthen the quality, accuracy and usefulness of analytical products.
- **Communication:** Ability to present complex information clearly, concisely and persuasively in written reports and verbal briefings.
- **Adaptability:** Capacity to respond to rapidly changing security environments, shifting priorities and urgent operational requirements.
- **Professional integrity:** Commitment to objectivity, confidentiality, evidence-based analysis and responsible information management.

jobs.title: Deputy Director - Central African Republic
jobs.description:
**Organisation Background**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts.

INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. INSO provides daily support to more than 1,500 NGOs operating in 24 of the world’s most insecure countries. INSO is registered in the Netherlands, with its headquarters located in The Hague, a city renowned for its international focus on peace and justice.

**Overall Purpose of the Role**

As Deputy Director, you will lead the delivery of INSO’s core services, ensuring humanitarian partners receive timely, high-quality security and access support. You will oversee the programme team, drive context analysis and service excellence, contribute to country strategy, and act as Country Director when required.

**Main Duties & Responsibilities**

*Service Delivery & Analysis*

- Lead the delivery of INSO services to humanitarian partners, ensuring quality and compliance with organisational standards.
- Oversee key products and services, including analytical reports, incident reporting, the Conflict and Humanitarian Data Centre (CHDC), crisis support, training, and safety/access forums.
- Guide context and conflict analysis to ensure services remain relevant and responsive to partner needs.
- Engage with humanitarian coordination and access forums, representing INSO and strengthening stakeholder relationships.
- Translate partner challenges, trends, and operational needs into practical services and analysis.
- Uphold and promote INSO’s principles of independence, impartiality, and neutrality.

*Programme Leadership*

- Manage and develop the programme team, including recruitment, performance management, mentoring, and capacity building.
- Foster collaboration across programme, operations, and HQ functions to ensure coherent service delivery.
- Capture lessons learned, best practices, and programme achievements for internal learning and improvement.
- Ensure compliance with INSO’s Code of Conduct and Duty of Care commitments.

*Strategy & Representation*

- Support the Country Director in implementing and advancing INSO’s country strategy and mandate.
- Contribute to annual planning, programme development, donor engagement, and reporting processes.
- Maintain and update security management policies, SOPs, and operational guidelines.
- Support the application of INSO policies across HR, finance, security, and operations.
- Represent INSO with NGOs, UN agencies, donors, and other external stakeholders.
- Serve as Country Director in their absence.

**Knowledge, Skills and Experience**

*Essential*

- Extensive experience in complex and insecure operating environments, with demonstrated progression into leadership roles and at least one year of senior management experience.
- Proven writing, editing, and analytical skills and a keen eye for detail - the position entails substantial report editing and reviewing.
- Fluent in spoken and written French and working proficiency in English communication skills
- Good understanding of humanitarian safety practices and their application.
- Significant leadership and staff management experience in a diverse multicultural setting.
- Excellent networking, diplomatic, and representative communication skills.
- Graduate-level education in a relevant field.

*Nice to Have*

- One year (recent) experience working in CAR or a similar context with a humanitarian NGO and demonstrable understanding of the context.
- Experience in staff capacity development.
- Experience with the NGO project management cycle, including donor reporting and relations.
- First-hand experience of crisis management.
- Prior experience in an inter-agency role.
- Existing information networks and/or local language skills.
- Detailed understanding of INSO mandate & services.

**Core Competencies**

- Problem-Solving - identifies issues quickly, analyzes root causes, and develops practical solutions.
- Leadership - Communicates effectively, organizes resources, and manages teams to achieve objectives.
- Accountability - Works independently, takes ownership of decisions, and delivers results under pressure.
- Integrity - Maintains confidentiality, upholds ethical standards, and actively manages conflicts of interest.
- Cultural Awareness - Demonstrates respect, humility, and effectiveness when working in diverse and multicultural environments.

**INSO’s Safeguarding Policy**

INSO is fully committed to safe recruitment, selection and vetting of all potential new staff, trustees and volunteers. We ensure rigorous compliance with our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy throughout the recruitment process. INSO is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and the selected candidate will be required to undergo the relevant misconduct disclosure checks as part of the final hiring steps.

**Terms & Conditions**

12-month renewable contract. 5750 € per month salary. 4 calendar days of annual leave per month and 3 days of R&R every 3 months with 1 250€ allowance, global medical coverage (excluding USA) and AD&D insurance.

jobs.title: Statistician Officer
jobs.description:
**Job Rank/Seniority:** Officer

**Job Grade:** SH 5

**Department:** MEL

**Location / Work station:** Nairobi

**Working Hours:** Monday - Friday, 8am - 5pm

**Reporting Relationships**

**Reports to:** Analytics Manager

## **About SHOFCO**

SHOFCO is a leading community-based organization mobilizing the largest network of social groups in Kenya to provide holistic, needs-driven services and redefine the potential of citizen-led change.

We partner across a range of sectors to provide programs ranging from health and education to economic and social empowerment. These services are informed by our community advocacy platforms. Originally founded in Kibera, SHOFCO is now reaching communities across Kenya, with more than 800 staff in 20 offices.

## **Job Purpose:**

The Statistician is responsible for the design, execution, and quality assurance of statistical analyses across the organization’s program portfolio. Reporting to the Analytics Manager, the role provides the statistical backbone of SHOFCO's evaluation and research work — from designing robust sampling frameworks and running quasi-experimental analyses to validating data integrity and interpreting findings for funder and policy audiences.

## **Key Responsibilities and Job Dimensions**

### **Statistical Analysis & Modelling**

- Lead the quantitative analysis component of SHOFCO's program evaluations, impact studies, and research briefs, using appropriate statistical methods for each study design.
- Design and implement quasi-experimental analyses including difference-in-differences (DiD), propensity score matching (PSM), instrumental variables (IV), and regression discontinuity designs (RDD), in collaboration with the Snr Research & Evaluation Specialist.
- Conduct descriptive, inferential, and multivariate analyses on program data, producing outputs that are accurate, reproducible, and clearly interpreted.
- Develop and maintain analysis scripts in R, Python, or Stata — following reproducible research standards including version control, documentation, and peer review of code.
- Produce statistical annexes, technical notes, and methodology sections for funder reports, evaluation submissions, and research publications.

### **Study Design & Sampling**

- Support the design of evaluation and research studies from a statistical standpoint — including power calculations, sample size determination, and randomization protocols where applicable.
- Develop and review sampling frameworks for surveys, tracer studies, and field verification exercises, ensuring representativeness and statistical validity.
- Advise the MEL team and program Leads on appropriate study designs for specific research questions, balancing rigor with feasibility given field constraints.
- Review and quality-assure data collection instruments (questionnaires, Kobo Toolbox forms) to ensure the data they generate is analytically usable.

### **Data Validation & Quality Assurance**

- Conduct statistical validation of program datasets — including outlier detection, consistency checks, missing data analysis, and distributional testing — before data is used for reporting or analysis.
- Develop and apply statistical cleaning protocols for the MEL master database, working with the Data Analyst to maintain a clean, analysis-ready dataset at all times.
- Identify and flag data anomalies, collection errors, or systematic biases in field data, and work with program MEL Officers to resolve them at source.
- Maintain a statistical audit trail for all analyses — documenting data versions, transformations, analytical decisions, and assumptions to ensure reproducibility and transparency.

### **Funder-Facing Evidence & Verification**

- Provide the statistical analysis underpinning SHOFCO's employment outcome verification, including verification rate calculations, cohort tracking analysis, and dignified work indicator modelling.
- Support CIFF reporting by conducting statistical analysis of program outcome data across the IIVC and Integrated Schools portfolios, including cross-site comparisons and trend analysis.
- Contribute statistical rigor ensuring that impact estimates, confidence intervals, and attribution claims are methodologically sound and clearly communicated.
- Respond to funder queries on statistical methodology, data quality, and analytical findings, in collaboration with the Impact Director and Analytics Manager.

### **Research & Publications**

- Under the direction of the Impact director, contribute to the development of research papers, policy briefs, and evidence publications using SHOFCO program data, with the goal of building a peer-reviewed evidence base that supports prospecting and fundraising.
- Liaise with academic and research partners on collaborative studies, providing SHOFCO's statistical analysis contribution and ensuring methodological alignment.
- Stay current with advances in evaluation methodology, statistical computing, and development sector research standards, and bring relevant innovations back to the MEL team.

### **Capacity Building & Knowledge Transfer**

- Support the MEL leadership to build the statistical literacy of the wider MEL team through peer coaching, documentation of analytical approaches, and structured training sessions on key methods and tools.
- Develop reusable statistical templates, analysis guides, and code libraries that allow MEL Coordinators and Data Analysts to apply standard methods consistently across programs.
- Support the onboarding and supervision of research interns or consultants engaged on specific evaluation projects.

### **Job Competencies (Knowledge, Experience and Attributes / Skills).**

#### **Academic Qualifications**

- Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Biostatistics, Applied Mathematics, Quantitative Economics, or a closely related field.
- A Master's degree (MSc or equivalent) in Statistics, Applied Epidemiology, or Evaluation Methods is strongly preferred.

#### **Professional Qualifications**

- Minimum 2 years of professional experience in quantitative data analysis, with at least 1 year in an international development, social impact context.
- Demonstrated proficiency in at least two statistical computing environments: R (tidy verse, survey, lme4, Match It) and/or Stata; Python (pandas, SciPy, stats models) is an advantage.
- Demonstrated experience applying quasi-experimental evaluation methods — including DiD, PSM, or RDD — in real programme evaluation settings, not only in academic work.
- Strong experience in survey data analysis, including complex sampling designs, weighting, and the use of survey analysis packages.
- Experience producing methodological documentation — power calculations, sampling memos, analysis plans, statistical annexes — for institutional funder reporting.

#### **Other required qualifications (unique/job specific)**

- Experience with longitudinal panel data analysis and cohort tracking in livelihoods, economic inclusion, or youth employment programs.
- Familiarity with cost-effectiveness analysis and social return on investment (SROI) methodologies.
- Knowledge of Bayesian statistical methods and their application in evaluation contexts.
- Experience working with or contributing to peer-reviewed research publications.

### **Functional Skills:**

- Statistical rigor — holds a high standard for methodological soundness and does not overstate findings or confidence beyond what the data supports.
- Tech savvy- Familiarity with mobile data collection tools (ODK, Commcare, Kobo Toolbox) and the analytical challenges they present (missing data, skip logic, data cleaning).

### **Behavioral Competencies/Attributes:**

- Clarity of communication — able to explain complex statistical findings and their limitations to non-technical audiences clearly and without condescension.
- Intellectual curiosity — brings genuine interest in development sector research questions and a drive to generate insight that matters.
- Attention to detail — catches errors others miss; treats data cleaning and documentation as core professional responsibilities, not afterthoughts.
- Collaboration — works well across a team of MEL professionals with different technical backgrounds, adapting their communication accordingly.
- Integrity — handles beneficiary data with discretion; upholds ethical standards in research and data use.
- Ownership — takes responsibility for the quality of analytical outputs from start to finish, without waiting to be managed.

jobs.title: Readvertsiment-Food Security and Agriculture Program Coordinator
jobs.company: International Association for Relief and Development
jobs.description:
## **About ONSUR:**

The International Association for Relief and Development (ONSUR) is a non-governmental organization established in early 2012 and registered in Syria. ONSUR is dedicated to implementing relief and development projects that empower local communities and promote a dignified life for vulnerable populations. , the organization operates through a network of execution offices in Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Turkey, and Yemen. ONSUR delivers humanitarian assistance and sustainable development initiatives in conflict-affected regions, with a focus on transparency, community engagement, and long-term impact.

**Location:** **Damascus**

**POSITION SUMMARY:**

The Food Security and Agriculture Program Coordinator leads the technical design, delivery and quality assurance of ONSUR’s food security and agricultural programming .

The role supports crisis-affected households and communities to meet immediate food needs, restore and strengthen crop and livestock production, protect productive resources, and build resilient, sustainable local food systems. Programming is informed by food availability, access, utilization and stability, and adapted to seasonal, market, climate and conflict-related risks.

The Coordinator is accountable for food-security results and the technical quality of agricultural interventions from emergency food assistance, crop and livestock inputs, agricultural extension and irrigation to animal health, post-harvest practices and the resilience of farming systems.

In ONSUR’s integrated programming, agricultural commercialization, farmer-to-market linkages, producer-enterprise development, SME support, small grants and agribusiness financing are led by the Early Recovery and Livelihoods (ERL) Program Coordinator and requires high level of coordination between the FSA and ERL programs.

This position provides the agricultural and food-security technical inputs to such initiatives and ensures interventions are complementary and well-coordinated.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Program strategy, technical assessments and design**

**•** Lead food security and agriculture Program planning in line with ONSUR priorities, national and local context, humanitarian principles, area-based approaches and applicable donor and sector guidance.

**•** Oversee household food-security assessments, agricultural needs and capacity assessments, market and price analysis, seasonal calendars, crop and livestock production assessments, water-resource considerations and conflict-sensitivity reviews.

**•** Develop context-specific responses that address urgent food gaps while linking, where feasible, to recovery of agricultural production, natural resources and local food systems.

**•** Lead technical inputs to concept notes, proposals, theories of change, log frames, budgets, implementation plans and sector-specific SOPs, working closely with Program , Finance, Supply Chain and MEAL colleagues.

**2. Emergency food security and household access to food**

**•** Provide technical leadership for appropriately targeted food assistance, including in-kind food distributions, food vouchers and cash-based food assistance where needs, markets, donor rules and risk analysis support the modality.

**•** Guide selection of transfer or food-basket content, adequacy, frequency, distribution arrangements and monitoring in relation to household needs, local diets, food prices, market functionality and dignity of recipients.

**•** Ensure sound beneficiary targeting and verification, safe and accessible delivery, appropriate food quality and shelf-life controls, post-distribution monitoring and effective community feedback processes.

**•** Promote nutrition-sensitive food security, food safety, dietary diversity and practical links with WASH, Health and Protection services; identify referral needs without duplicating specialist nutrition or health functions.

**3. Crop production, seed systems and farmer support**

**•** Design and technically supervise agricultural recovery packages covering quality seeds and seedlings, tools, appropriate fertilizers, soil inputs, home gardens, field crops, horticulture and protected agriculture, based on agroecological suitability.

**•** Strengthen smallholder production through agricultural extension, demonstration plots, farmer field schools, crop calendars, soil management, integrated pest management and safe input handling.

**•** Ensure agricultural inputs meet agreed quality specifications, locally appropriate varieties and planting seasons; coordinate verification, transparent distribution and post-assistance technical follow-up.

**•** Assess and support rehabilitation of essential on-farm productive assets and community agricultural services where feasible, with due attention to safe land access, tenure, affordability and maintenance.

**4. Livestock production and animal-source food security**

**•** Lead technically appropriate support for small-scale livestock, poultry and other relevant animal production systems, focusing on household food supply, herd or flock productivity and resilience.

**•** Coordinate animal feed and fodder assistance, veterinary outreach, vaccination, animal-health services, husbandry training and disease-prevention measures through suitably qualified veterinary personnel and responsible authorities.

**•** Promote animal welfare, biosecurity, adequate water provision, safe handling of animal-source foods and environmentally responsible livestock management.

**•** Monitor seasonal feed availability, animal health risks, local service capacities and the practical sustainability of supported livestock assets.

**5. Irrigation, climate resilience and natural-resource stewardship**

**•** Provide technical direction for agricultural water access and irrigation rehabilitation, including water-efficient equipment and practices, in coordination with qualified engineers and relevant authorities.

**•** Integrate climate-smart and resource-efficient farming practices, drought preparedness, crop diversification, soil and water conservation and other locally suitable risk-reduction measures.

**•** Ensure proposals are grounded in water availability, environmental and social risk screening, feasibility, safe maintenance arrangements and avoidance of harm to other water users.

**•** Coordinate infrastructure interfaces with WASH, Shelter and other technical teams without duplicating engineering approval or sector-specific accountabilities.

**6. Agricultural services, post-harvest management and integrated technical support**

**•** Strengthen agricultural extension networks, community seed systems, farmer technical training and access to essential agricultural inputs, veterinary support and production-related services.

**•** Improve on-farm and post-harvest handling, safe storage, food safety, produce quality and loss reduction to protect agricultural output and food availability.

**•** Assess agricultural input availability, production constraints, crop and livestock service gaps, seasonal risks and food losses, and translate findings into technically sound food security and agricultural recovery interventions.

**•** Coordinate with the ERL Program Coordinator on initiatives involving agricultural commercialization, farmer-to-market linkages, producer organizations and enterprises, SME support, small grants, business incubation or agribusiness finance. The ERL Program Coordinator leads the economic empowerment components; this role provides technical oversight of agricultural production, livestock systems, input quality and food-security outcomes.

**7. Implementation quality, operations and risk management**

**•** Provide technical oversight to project teams on workplans, activity sequencing, procurement specifications, bills of quantities, distribution protocols, supplier quality and seasonal delivery timelines.

**•** Develop or review technical guidelines, SOPs, eligibility criteria, site assessments and inspection checklists for agricultural assistance, food commodities and productive-asset rehabilitation.

**•** Conduct regular field visits and technical reviews; track progress, expenditure implications, input performance and implementation risks; agree corrective actions with project teams and management.

**•** Coordinate with Supply Chain and Finance on due diligence, commodity and input traceability, transport, storage, distribution documentation and appropriate segregation of duties.

**•** Enforce ONSUR and donor requirements on safeguarding, PSEA, accountability, anti-fraud, data protection, conflict sensitivity, environmental responsibility and safe access for women and marginalized groups.

**8. MEAL, results measurement and reporting**

**•** Work with MEAL colleagues to establish baselines, outcome indicators, field verification, beneficiary feedback, seasonal follow-up and suitable post-distribution monitoring systems.

**•** Measure food-security changes using context-appropriate indicators (for example Food Consumption Score, reduced Coping Strategies Index and dietary diversity), alongside agricultural production, yields, asset functionality and adoption of improved practices.

**•** Analyze food prices, crop and livestock outcomes, access barriers, environmental risks and sustainability; adjust programming based on evidence and community feedback.

**•** Prepare accurate technical and narrative inputs for donor reports, proposals, learning notes and internal performance reviews, reconciled with MEAL and financial records.

**09. Team leadership, coordination and partnerships**

**•** Provide technical leadership, mentoring and quality assurance for food security and agriculture staff and implementing partners, including capacity-building plans and field coaching.

**•** Maintain effective working relationships with agriculture and veterinary directorates, local authorities, farmers and community agricultural structures, research and extension bodies, UN agencies, NGOs and relevant agricultural service providers.

**•** Represent ONSUR in appropriate Food Security and Agriculture coordination platforms and technical working groups, as delegated by the Programs Manager.

**•** Advance integrated and area-based programming with the ERL Program Coordinator and other relevant sector teams, ensuring complementary interventions, clear technical accountabilities and appropriate referral or coordination pathways.

**10. Safeguarding and Compliance**

• Ensure all interventions are designed and implemented with due consideration of **protection, gender, age, disability inclusion**, **housing-land-and-property rights**, conflict sensitivity, and the **do-no-harm principle**.
• Promote safe, accessible, and accountable programming and ensure staff, contractors, and communities understand feedback and reporting mechanisms for misconduct or abuse.
• Ensure compliance with **ONSUR's Code of Conduct**, Child Safeguarding Policy, **PSEA standards**, procurement rules, technical approvals, and donor requirements.
• Report safeguarding, fraud, safety, environmental, or compliance concerns through established organizational procedures and support timely corrective action.

**Note:**

The above responsibilities are illustrative and not exhaustive. Additional tasks may be assigned based on organizational needs and evolving program requirements.

## **Required Qualifications & Experience**

**Education:**

- Education: Bachelor’s degree in agriculture, Agronomy, Agricultural Engineering, Animal Science, Veterinary Medicine, Food Security, Rural Development or a closely related field. A relevant postgraduate qualification is an advantage.

**Experience:**

- Experience: At least 04 years of relevant experience in food security and/or agriculture Programs, including at least two years of program management, technical supervision or sector coordination.

**Technical Skills**

- Technical expertise: Practical knowledge of food assistance modalities, agricultural inputs and extension, crop or livestock production, seasonal planning, food-price and agricultural-input availability assessments, and rural community-based programming.
- Experience with agricultural irrigation, climate-smart practices, producer services, post-harvest systems or natural-resource management is highly desirable; specialists should demonstrate the ability to coordinate complementary disciplines.
- Strong capability in proposal and budget preparation, technical specifications, donor compliance, risk analysis, MEAL frameworks and constructive engagement with local institutions and communities.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint; experience with data collection, GIS or analytical dashboards is an asset.

**Core Competencies**

- Strong **coordination, communication, negotiation, leadership**, and decision-making skills.
• Ability and willingness to travel within Syria and to ONSUR's project locations as required.
• Commitment to upholding the highest standards of **safeguarding, accountability**, technical integrity, impartiality, and professional ethics

**Languages:**

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills in **Arabic and English**.

**Child Protection Policy**

ONSUR maintains a strict **zero-tolerance policy** toward all forms of child abuse and exploitation. The organization is fully committed to creating and maintaining a **child-safe environment** across all areas of its work. All employees are expected to uphold the highest standards of behavior to ensure the safety and well-being of children, and any breach of this policy will result in immediate disciplinary action.

**Anti-Discrimination, Harassment, and Abuse Policy**

ONSUR is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace for all. Discrimination, harassment, or abuse of any kind — whether based on race, ethnicity, religion, gender, age, disability, marital status, citizenship, or military status — is strictly prohibited and will not be tolerated.

All staff are expected to **promote a culture of respect** and integrity. Participation in any form of abuse, harassment (verbal, physical, or sexual), intimidation, or exploitation — whether inside or outside the workplace — is a violation of ONSUR’s core values and policies.

**Diversity & Inclusion**

ONSUR is strongly committed to gender equality and **encourages qualified female candidates** to apply for this position.
