Working under the supervision of the Human Resources Manager and in coordination with the HR & Administration Officer, the position supports recruitment administration, personnel documentation, onboarding and offboarding, timesheet and leave tracking, HR information systems, and routine HR processes. The role also supports immigration documentation and coordination with internal teams and external service providers, ensuring accurate, timely and confidential administrative support in line with NP procedures.

**KEY OBJECTIVES/RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Recruitment, Selection and Placement**

- Provide administrative support for recruitment, including posting vacancy announcements, monitoring applications and maintaining recruitment trackers.
- Schedule interviews, communicate logistical information to candidates and prepare interview documentation.
- Collect required recruitment, reference-check and pre-employment screening documents for review by the HR team.
- Assist with preparation of employment contracts, appointment letters and related documents under HR supervision.
- Organize onboarding schedules, induction meetings and required documentation for new employees.
- Support offboarding, including clearance documentation, collection of records and exit formalities.

**Payroll, Leave and Benefits Administration**

- Collect and track monthly timesheets, follow up on outstanding submissions and check completeness before HR review.
- Update leave records and internal trackers based on approved requests; flag discrepancies for review.
- Prepare and organize payroll-related inputs and supporting documents for the HR & Administration Officer.
- Maintain employee insurance and benefits records and assist with updated staff lists and routine queries.
- Provide administrative support for military registration and reservation documentation as instructed by the HR Manager.

**Personnel Documentation & Records Management**

- Maintain accurate and confidential electronic and hard-copy personnel files, including scanning, filing and archiving.
- Update employee records in the HRIS and relevant trackers and monitor contract, probation and other HR deadlines.
- Coordinate routine document exchange between the HR team, field offices and HR outsourcing provider.
- Prepare routine employment letters, certificates and confirmations for review and signature.
- Handle personal information in accordance with NP confidentiality and data protection requirements.

**Human Resource Management & HRIS**

- Provide routine administrative support to employees using NP HR information systems and refer complex issues to the relevant focal point.
- Track completion of mandatory staff training and provide regular status updates to the HR Manager.
- Monitor performance review deadlines and follow up on outstanding documentation as instructed.
- Prepare staff lists, HR trackers, basic reports and meeting or training logistics.
- Support HR team activities and staff well-being initiatives.

**Administration and Immigration Support**

- Assist with preparation, collection and processing of business travel requests and travel orders.
- Support visa, immigration and residency documentation for international staff and visitors, including appointments and follow-up under HR guidance.
- Coordinate preparation and distribution of employee identification cards.

**Compliance, Coordination and Team Support**

- Carry out assigned duties in accordance with NP policies, procedures and applicable Ukrainian legislation.
- Identify missing documents or potential administrative compliance issues and refer them promptly to the HR & Administration Officer or HR Manager.
- Communicate professionally and confidentially with colleagues, field teams and external service providers.
- Participate in team meetings and learning activities and perform other duties appropriate to the role as assigned.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND COMPETENCIES**

**Commitment to NP Principles**

- Demonstrate commitment to NP’s mandate and principles.
- Maintain a positive image of the organization and demonstrate integrity, confidentiality and professionalism.

**Education, Knowledge, and Experience**

- Secondary education required; a degree or ongoing studies in Human Resources, Business Administration, Management or a related field is an advantage.
- Previous administrative, HR support or office support experience is an advantage.
- Experience supporting recruitment, personnel documentation or administrative processes is desirable.
- Experience in an NGO or humanitarian organization is an advantage.
- Familiarity with HR information systems and electronic filing is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Strong organizational skills, accuracy and attention to detail.
- Ability to manage several tasks, meet deadlines and work independently and in a team.
- Professional communication skills and a service-oriented approach.
- Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information responsibly.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office 365, particularly Word, Excel and Outlook.
- Good written and spoken Ukrainian and English.
- Flexibility and ability to adapt to changing priorities and challenging working circumstances.

jobs.title: Communications and Branding Consultancy – Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP) Academy
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Communications and Branding Consultancy – Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP) Academy
**Department:** Programming
**Duty Station:** Remote
**Administrative Line Manager:** UCP Academy Manager
**Position Type:** Consultancy

**1. Background**

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) advances civilian-led, nonviolent approaches to the protection of civilians and the prevention and reduction of violence. The UCP Academy is an online learning initiative supporting accessible, high-quality learning on Unarmed Civilian Protection and related practice. As its digital platform is being strengthened, the Academy is preparing for its hard launch in the first half of 2027.

In parallel, the Academy is running a three-month pilot with Viamo that adapts NP’s Introduction to UCP course into an interactive, voice-based learning experience delivered by basic mobile phone in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The pilot tests a scalable way to reach people who face barriers to conventional online or in-person training, such as limited connectivity, no access to smartphones or computers, low digital literacy, geographic isolation or a preference for oral learning.

The Academy seeks a Communications and Branding Consultant to complement the work of its Web Design Consultant with a focus on five priorities: defining a branding strategy for the Academy that is rooted in NP’s brand while creating space for partnerships; documenting the Viamo voice-training pilot through case studies; designing a marketing strategy for the launch of the Academy’s online platform; developing the Academy’s social media strategy and branding; and establishing a consistent brand system across Academy products and publications.

**2. Objective**

The objective of this consultancy is to strengthen the UCP Academy’s brand, marketing and communications so that it can attract and engage learners, partners and supporters. Specifically, the Consultant will:

- **Branding strategy:** develop a branding strategy for the UCP Academy that is rooted in Nonviolent Peaceforce’s brand identity and values and that creates clear space for partners to be visible through co-branding and co-delivery;
- **Pilot case studies:** produce case studies on the Viamo voice-training pilot in the DRC for social media, the Academy website and partner and donor audiences;
- **Launch marketing strategy:** design a marketing strategy for the launch of the Academy’s online platform and produce the related promotional materials;
- **Social media strategy and branding:** develop a social media strategy and a branded social media presence for the Academy, aligned with NP’s channels;
- **Brand templates:** create brand templates for Academy products and publications, building on the branding strategy, visual identity, tone of voice and website content.

**3. Duration and Location**

- **Period:** 4 January 2027 to 28 February 2027
- **Level of effort:** Up to 20 working days in total
- **Fee:** up to USD 8,000 in total
- **Location:** Remote
- **Work planning:** Days may be used flexibly, based on a workplan agreed with the UCP Academy Manager.

**4. Reporting Line**

The Consultant will report directly to the UCP Academy Manager and will work in close collaboration with relevant NP consultants and communications staff. For pilot-related content, the Consultant will coordinate, through the UCP Academy Manager, with the NP DRC team and Viamo focal points.

**5. Scope of Work**

**5.1 Branding strategy rooted in Nonviolent Peaceforce’s brand**

- Review NP brand guidelines, existing Academy content and communications materials, and consult key stakeholders (NP communications staff, the Academy team, NP country programmes and selected partners) on target audiences, perceptions and key messages.
- Develop a branding strategy for the UCP Academy that positions it clearly as Nonviolent Peaceforce’s learning offer, defining its brand positioning, value proposition, core messages and brand personality, and drawing on NP’s identity, field credibility and UCP principles, including the primacy of civilians affected by conflict, nonviolence and nonpartisanship.
- Define the Academy’s brand architecture, setting out how it relates to the NP master brand (e.g. as an endorsed sub-brand), which NP brand elements it inherits and where it may have its own distinct visual and verbal expression.
- Create space for partnerships by developing a partnership and co-branding framework with tiered options (e.g. NP-led, co-delivered and partner-led adaptations), logo lock-ups and placement rules, attribution and visibility guidance, so that partners such as Viamo, local civil-society organisations, training institutions and humanitarian actors can be visible while NP retains responsibility for UCP content integrity, quality assurance and safeguarding standards.
- Refresh the Academy’s visual identity (logo usage, colour palette, typography, imagery and iconography) and develop a tone of voice, in English and French, that reflects NP’s values and speaks to practitioners, community actors, students, partners and donors, including audiences reached through oral and low-literacy formats.
- Redesign and rewrite website content (homepage, course and membership descriptions, calls to action) so that it is clear, accessible and search-friendly.
- Work with the Web Design Consultant to integrate content and branding coherently into the website, app and user journeys.

**5.2 Case studies on the Viamo voice-training pilot in the DRC**

- Develop a case-study format and editorial plan aligned with the final phase and close of the pilot (e.g. final weeks of delivery, learner feedback and end-of-pilot results).
- Write a series of short case studies for NP and Academy social media channels and the Academy website, covering: why voice-based learning on basic mobile phones makes foundational UCP learning accessible; the learner journey, from the voluntary screening and baseline survey through Lesson 1 (“When people feel unsafe, what do they do?”) and Lesson 2 (“Choosing safer, nonviolent protection actions”) and the knowledge checks; two-way participation by voice or keypad; the NP–Viamo partnership model; and results and insights on participation, completion, comprehension, confidence and learner preferences.
- Produce one longer-form case study or learning brief for partners and donors that presents the pilot’s results, lessons learned and potential for scale to further languages, modules, countries and partner-led adaptation.
- Produce accompanying visuals, captions and short-form adaptations (e.g. quote cards, carousels and, where appropriate, short audio clips), in English with French adaptations as needed, and Swahili excerpts where available from pilot content.
- Gather information remotely in coordination with the NP DRC team and Viamo, using only content and voices obtained with informed consent. Anonymise participants and exclude sensitive incident details or identifying information, in line with the pilot’s safeguarding and data-minimisation protocols.
- Provide a reusable case-study template so Academy staff can document future phases, new languages or other roll-outs of the voice-training model.

**5.3 Marketing strategy for the launch of the Academy’s online platform**

- Develop a marketing strategy for the launch of the Academy’s online platform, defining marketing objectives, target audience segments (e.g. UCP and protection practitioners, NP staff and country programmes, students, partner organisations and donors), the value proposition and key messages for each segment, and pathways from awareness to registration, course enrolment and membership.
- Set out a channel mix and phased plan covering the pre-launch, launch and post-launch phases, including the Academy website, NP and Academy social media, email and newsletters, NP country programmes and partner networks, sector platforms, webinars and events, with recommendations on low-cost organic options and, where relevant, targeted paid promotion.
- Integrate the Viamo pilot case studies and partner voices into the launch narrative as evidence of the Academy’s reach, accessibility and partnership model.
- Define key performance indicators and a simple monitoring framework (e.g. reach, engagement, website traffic, registrations, course enrolments and partner uptake), with indicative targets and recommended tracking tools.
- Produce launch promotional materials, such as teaser and announcement social media posts, email announcements and newsletter content, flyers, web banners and a short presentation.
- Prepare a partner toolkit with ready-to-share and co-branded content for NP country programmes, partners and networks, in line with the partnership and co-branding framework.
- Deliver all launch materials in advance of the hard launch date, following the timeline agreed in the inception workplan.

**5.4 Social media strategy and branding**

- Review the current social media presence, audiences and performance of NP and the Academy, and recommend which channels the Academy should prioritise (e.g. LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, WhatsApp) and whether it should use NP’s existing channels, dedicated Academy channels or a hybrid model.
- Develop a social media strategy setting out objectives, target audiences, content pillars (e.g. UCP learning, field stories and case studies, courses and the platform launch, partnerships and learner community), posting frequency, and engagement and community-management guidelines, aligned with the launch marketing strategy.
- Develop the Academy’s social media branding, including profile and cover visuals, branded post formats, hashtags, caption tone, co-branded post formats for partners, and accessibility standards (e.g. alt text, subtitles and plain language).
- Provide guidance on moderation, responding to sensitive or hostile comments and managing reputational and safety risks when communicating about conflict-affected contexts.
- Prepare a three-month social media content calendar covering the platform launch period.

**5.5 Brand templates for Academy products and publications**

- Design editable, branded templates for Academy products and publications, such as course and module covers, certificates of completion, learner guides and handouts, slide decks, reports and briefing notes, case-study and learning-brief layouts, social media and newsletter templates, and webinar and event materials, including co-branded formats for partnerships such as Viamo.
- Provide short usage guidance so Academy staff can apply the templates consistently and adapt them independently.

**5.6 Cross-cutting standards**

- Ensure all materials are inclusive, accessible, conflict-sensitive and consistent with do-no-harm principles, safeguarding, informed consent and NP and partner data-protection requirements.

**6. Deliverables**

- Inception note and workplan, within the first week, including a timeline aligned with the Academy hard launch date and pilot milestones.
- UCP Academy branding strategy and brand guide, rooted in NP’s brand, including brand positioning, brand architecture, visual identity, tone of voice, and a partnership and co-branding framework.
- Revised website content and visual assets, ready for upload.
- Series of case studies on the Viamo voice-training pilot, comprising short social media case studies with accompanying visuals and captions, one longer-form case study or learning brief for partners and donors, and a reusable case-study template.
- Marketing strategy for the launch of the Academy’s online platform, including audience segmentation, key messages, channel plan, phased content calendar and KPI framework.
- Hard-launch communications package: promotional materials and co-branded partner toolkit, delivered ahead of launch.
- Social media strategy and branding package: strategy and content pillars, community-management guidance, branded profile assets and post formats, and a three-month content calendar.
- Suite of editable brand templates for Academy products and publications, with brief usage guidance.
- Handover note and transfer of all editable source files, by 15 March, 2027.

**7. Required Qualifications and Experience**

- Proven experience in communications, branding and copywriting, ideally for NGOs or online learning, supported by a portfolio.
- Proven experience developing brand strategies, including brand architecture and co-branding or partnership frameworks for sub-brands within an established organisational brand.
- Demonstrated experience writing short-form case studies and human-interest stories for social media, ideally on humanitarian, development or digital-inclusion programmes.
- Experience designing and delivering marketing and launch strategies for a digital platform, product or organisation, with measurable KPIs.
- Experience developing social media strategies and managing branded social media channels, ideally for NGOs, online learning or advocacy campaigns.
- Experience developing brand identities, tone-of-voice guidelines and template systems for publications and digital products.
- Sound understanding of ethical storytelling, informed consent and safeguarding when communicating about conflict-affected communities.
- Proficiency in Canva, Adobe Creative Suite or Figma; familiarity with Wix is an asset.
- Excellent English writing skills; working knowledge of French is a strong asset. Familiarity with the humanitarian or peacebuilding sectors, or with mobile and voice-based learning, is an asset.

jobs.title: MENA Regional Director — Vacancy Announcement - Jordan
jobs.description:
**Position Start Date :** 1.02.2027

**Duration** : 24 months

**Location :** Amman, Jordan

**Department :** Operations

**Tdh :**

The Terre des hommes Foundation (Tdh), with headquarters in Lausanne and an office in Zurich, is the leading Swiss child rights organisation with more than 2000 employees worldwide. We stand together with children to uphold their rights, protect their lives and improve their well-being. We achieve this through innovative programmes focused on health, migration and access to justice, specially designed to have a positive and sustainable impact.

Terre des hommes Lausanne (Tdh) is seeking a strategic, values-driven senior leader to direct its operations across the Middle East and North Africa. Based in Amman and reporting to the Director of Operations, the Regional Director provides strategic and operational leadership across the region, translating Tdh’s global strategy into regional priorities and high-quality impact for children and communities.

Scope and accountability

As the senior accountable leader for the region, you will be responsible for strategic delivery, organisational performance, risk management, safeguarding, compliance, security and institutional representation. You will lead Deputy Regional Directors, Country Directors and the Regional Office team, ensuring that country operations have the direction, capacity and support to deliver Tdh’s mission and commitments to children, communities, partners and donors.

The role combines regional leadership with oversight of complex multi-country operations and stewardship of human and financial resources. You will balance programmatic ambition with operational feasibility, compliance obligations and risk considerations, ensuring that decisions remain within approved delegations, budgets, policies and Tdh’s risk appetite. Matters outside your authority, material deviations from approved plans and risks exceeding that appetite must be escalated to the Director of Operations or the relevant authorised decision-making body.

Your responsibilities

- **Shape regional strategy and lead people.** Contribute to Tdh’s global strategy, adapt priorities to regional realities and emerging trends, and ensure alignment across countries. Provide line management, performance oversight, coaching and accountability for country and regional leaders, with clear objectives, succession planning and talent development. Lead organisational change and ensure timely management intervention when significant performance, conduct or operational concerns arise.
- **Lead governance and organisational oversight.** Establish regional governance, assurance and decision-making mechanisms that enable transparency, clear accountability, escalation of critical issues and timely corrective action. Monitor strategic commitments and internal controls, participate in institutional leadership bodies, and strengthen cross-country collaboration and learning.
- **Direct programme delivery and financial stewardship.** Lead regional planning and budgeting, aligning programme priorities with available resources. Oversee consolidated financial performance, expenditure and forecasts, ensuring that material variances and funding gaps are identified, escalated and addressed. Hold managers accountable for programme quality, results and donor, legal and organisational requirements. Ensure that children, young people and communities can influence priorities and access safe, inclusive feedback and complaints mechanisms, with feedback informing decisions and responses communicated appropriately.
- **Oversee risk, compliance and integrity.** Ensure identification, assessment, monitoring and mitigation of strategic, operational, financial, safeguarding, legal and reputational risks, supported by regular regional risk reviews and reporting. Uphold fraud-prevention, anti-corruption and conflict-of-interest standards, support investigations and remediation, and ensure that audit findings and management actions are promptly addressed.
- **Champion safeguarding and child protection.** Keep safeguarding a strategic priority across all operations and promote prevention and zero tolerance for abuse, exploitation, harassment and misconduct. Ensure compliance with safeguarding and PSEAH requirements, with incidents reported, managed and escalated appropriately.
- **Lead security, crisis response and duty of care.** Oversee regional security management, preparedness and risk mitigation. Lead regional responses to critical incidents, safeguarding cases, security events, fraud allegations and organisational crises, ensuring rapid escalation and decision-making. Work with country leadership and people and culture teams to address staff wellbeing, psychosocial risks and excessive workloads, and ensure access to applicable support and incident-response arrangements.
- **Represent Tdh and build strategic partnerships.** Engage governments, donors, UN agencies, NGOs and strategic partners at senior level. Develop high-level institutional relationships, strengthen Tdh’s visibility, credibility and influence, and advance advocacy, partnerships and resource mobilisation across the region.
- **Lead the Regional Office and support country operations.** Provide strategic oversight of regional support functions, including finance, people and culture, operations and security. Ensure adequate capacities, structures and resources, compliance with local and internal requirements, and continuous improvement in systems and operational efficiency.

What you bring

- **Substantial senior leadership experience** within international organisations, including responsibility for organisational strategy, multidisciplinary teams, significant budgets and management accountability across complex multi-country operations.
- **Relevant operational experience** in humanitarian and development programming, child rights and protection, strategic planning, budget and resource management, donor engagement and partnership development, including organisational transformation and work in complex and volatile environments.
- **Strategic judgement and ethical leadership:** strong analytical and decision-making abilities, self-awareness, integrity and accountability, with the resilience to lead through crises and the ability to balance delivery, compliance and risk.
- **People leadership and influence:** the ability to develop teams, manage performance and change, listen and communicate effectively, negotiate, mediate and resolve conflict. Cultural sensitivity, adaptability and strong representation and stakeholder-engagement skills are central to the role.
- **Technical and institutional knowledge** of child rights and protection frameworks, international NGO management, risk management and internal controls, institutional donor relations, security management and the regional geopolitical context. Familiarity with Tdh’s policies, standards and procedures is expected of internal candidates.
- **An advanced university degree** in International Relations, International Development, Humanitarian Assistance, Public Policy, Management or another relevant discipline.
- **Languages and regional experience:** written and spoken English and French are mandatory. Arabic is an asset, and experience in the Middle East and North Africa region is a strong asset.
- **Digital and management tools:** proficiency with the Microsoft Office package, enterprise resource planning and management systems, budgeting and reporting tools, and collaboration and communication platforms.

**Your commitment:** Put Tdh’s values and principles into practice through exemplary behaviour and uphold the Code of Conduct and ethical policies, including safeguarding, anti-fraud and corruption, and conflict-of-interest requirements. Promote a culture of integrity, prevention, accountability and continuous improvement, systematically report violations through formal mechanisms, and ensure that concerns are addressed through established procedures.

Tdh Global Code of Conduct and Risk Management Policies :

- Fully complies with Tdh’s Global Code of Conduct and systematically reports any breach to the Code through the whistleblowing procedure: raises awareness within the Foundation on abuse and violence and the rights deriving therefrom, respecting the rights and dignity of children, members of the communities and our own Staff
- Commits to respecting Risk Management Policies including: Safeguarding Policies (Child Safeguarding Policy, Policy on the Protection against Sexual Exploitation and the Directive on Staff Misconduct at the Workplace), Safety and Security Policy and Anti-Fraud/Corruption and Prevention of the Financing of Criminal Activities Policies
- Commits to reducing the risk of abuse and harm by developing a culture of open and informed leadership within the organization and in our work with children and the communities in which we intervene in.

We offer an exciting and varied work, useful and meaningful, in a team that wants to make a difference for vulnerable children.

Are you interested? Do you want to face this challenge?

jobs.title: Deputy Director of Programs
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**ORGANIZATIONAL BACKGROUND**

The IRC began planning to reopen an occupied Palestinian territories (oPt) country program in mid-2022 and launched an emergency response in Gaza in October 2023. The organization is currently supporting a network of local partners in both Gaza and the West Bank to sustain critical health, protection, food security, cash, education, and early childhood development interventions. The IRC is also deploying emergency medical teams to provide surge clinical capacity in hospitals and other health facilities.

The IRC is working to scale its emergency response while building a longer-term oPt country program in parallel.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

The Deputy Director for Programs (DDP) provides strategic leadership, decision-making and coordination for program development and delivery, overseeing the effective implementation and technical quality of IRC’s programs in oPt. The DDP ensures that programs are evidence-based and needs-driven, monitored closely, and funded appropriately. The position reports to the Country Director (CD) and is a member of the Senior Management Team. The DDP directly supervises grants, partnerships, MEAL, and all technical coordinators, currently inclusive of health, protection, education and WASH, with potential to expand into additional technical areas.

This position has close working relationships with the MENA Deputy Regional Director and other members of the regional support teams.

**RESPONSIBILTIES**

**Strategic Leadership**

- Provide overall leadership and management of IRC Palestine programs, maintaining and enforcing strategic program direction and growth.
- Oversee the implementation of the country program Strategy Action Plan (SAP) and ensure it remains relevant and evidence-based.Drive IRC’s efforts towards a ‘partner first’ program approach and foster a network of local Palestinian partners, empowering those entities to lead key decision making and service delivery, and positioning IRC as a partner of choice.\] Build strategic partnerships with local actors, fostering collaboration on strategy, program design and development, and capacity sharing.
- Serve as a leader in building a culture of effective and respectful partnerships. Promote attitudes and values conducive to building and sustaining collaborative partnerships across the country program.
- Participate actively in country program management, coordination, and strategy meetings with other members of the senior management team.

**Program Quality**

- Ensure programming is aligned with the emergency response plan, SAP priorities, and IRC’s Outcomes and Evidence Framework (OEF), including program planning and project design.
- Liaise with regional technical advisors and ensure technical coordinators apply relevant guidance and best practices in new program design and implementation.
- Ensure high-quality and adaptive technical program support and guidance to partners.
- Support the development of measurement tools to assess program impact and involvement of client groups in program design. Ensure the alignment of the IRC oPt programs with the MEAL Handbook and the use of established stringent monitoring and evaluation systems.
- Champion an organizational culture where data and client input are routinely used for decision making and program adaptation. Promote systems which ensure that evidence is used to inform proposal design and theories of change.
- Identify and pursue opportunities to improve client feedback mechanisms to ensure responsive programming.

**Program Delivery**

- Maintain a sound understanding of IRC oPt’s programs and activity plans. Ensure continued oversight of both partner and direct delivery.
- Support and supervise implementation of strong Project Management Cycle processes and tools in accordance with standard IRC tools.
- Ensure program teams develop, implement, and regularly update detailed workplans, procurement plans, spending plans and staffing plans.
- Actively contribute to and/or chair project implementation meetings as required to review progress of programs, including but not limited, to progress indicators, workplans and spending. When required, lead the development of corrective measures to ensure projects finish on time and on target, ensure timely follow up on any agreed actions.
- Ensure the office consistently promotes and effectively uses IRC’s Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS) and that partnership decision-making and action is driven by IRC’s partnership principles.

**Business Development and Grants Management**

- Work with colleagues in the country program, region and HQ to identify funding opportunities and develop competitive, responsive proposals that are strategically aligned and donor compliant.
- Provide strategic direction for new program design in close coordination with the grants and technical coordinators.
- Ensure that strategic partnership considerations are incorporated in program design, including in Go / No-Go funding discussions.
- Ensure the proactive engagement of partners in program development and project design efforts.
- Review and assure the quality of concept notes and proposals.
- In collaboration with the Grants Coordinator, ensure program compliance with donor regulations, local government regulations and IRC internal control procedures.

**Representation and Coordination**

- Maintain a strong working relationship with donors. Lead external representation with donors as required.
- Actively, systematically, and regularly ensure ongoing communication with various partners in country.
- Ensure that IRC oPt’s program interventions are planned and coordinated within the broader humanitarian effort.
- Ensure IRC is represented at sector coordination groups, including the clusters.

**Staff Performance Management and Development**

- Supervise and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting performance objectives, and establishing a supportive environment while emphasizing accountability.
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions.
- Develop cohesive teams through regular department meetings, individual meetings, and the promotion of a collaborative working environment.
- Coordinate performance management within the department and ensure a culture of high performance through staff engagement and accountability.
- Promote and monitor staff care and well-being. Model healthy work-life balance practices.
- Work with P&C colleagues to identify and implement recruitment and retention strategies.
- Model and encourage active practice of the principles of the “IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct” throughout the Palestine country program.

**REQUIREMENTS**

- Excellent professional track record with at least 8 years of experience in conflict and humanitarian environments with significant program leadership responsibilities.
- Successful experience delivering programs in a complex and volatile security environment strongly preferred.
- Proven ability to think strategically, prioritize and meet deadlines in a challenging emergency setting.
- Demonstrated ability for rapid, accurate analysis of complex issues, strong decision-making, and translation of programmatic priorities into operational strategies.
- Familiarity with IRC oPt’s core programming areas including health, protection, WASH and education.
- Excellent leadership, people management, interpersonal and negotiation skills and a demonstrated ability to develop harmonious teams.
- Demonstrated ability in coordination, networking and relationship building with key partners including government, donors, INGOs, national and local organizations, UN agencies.
- Extensive representation and fundraising success, including prior experience with European, US and other international donors.
- Excellent oral and written English skills, including the ability to write and edit complex technical documents for external submission with minimal oversight. Knowledge of Arabic preferred.
- Excellent MS Office skills.
- Self-motivated, honest, highly responsible.
- Ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
- Willingness to travel at least 25% of time, including to complex security environments.

**Gender Equality**: IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances.

**IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer.** IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Regional Accountant - ECA
jobs.description:
We are seeking a qualified accountant with relevant post-qualification experience. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in financial reporting, financial accounting, and finance systems. Experience with institutional donors, capacity building, and working within an international organisation will be a distinct advantage.

The Regional Accountant ensures high-quality, customer-focused accounting support for Tearfund's operations across the East and Central Africa region. Working closely with Tearfund's Global Finance team, the role plays a key part in maintaining financial integrity and operational efficiency.

Do you have:

Relevant post-qualification finance experience?

Experience in finance capacity building and training?

Substantial experience working with accounting software and online systems?

Proven experience in budgeting and budget management?

Proven experience in donor financial reporting?

Exposure to organisational finance compliance?

Proven experience in supporting programme teams in project design and management?

Do you have the ability to:

Communicate complex financial data to non-finance professionals?

Work under your own initiative and make decisions within a clear systems framework?

Work cross-culturally and build effective relationships with colleagues across multiple locations?

Are you:

A fully qualified accountant holding a recognised professional accounting or auditing qualification (e.g., ACA, ACCA, CIMA, or equivalent)?

A committed Christian aligned with Tearfund's Mission, Values, and Beliefs?

Willing and able to travel approximately 35% of the time?

Do you have:

Excellent written and verbal English communication skills?

The ability to communicate in French?

Strong organisational and administrative skills?

A passion for Tearfund's vision to see all people freed from poverty, living transformed lives, and reaching their God-given potential?

Then we'd love to hear from you.

Note:

jobs.title: FSL Program Coordinator- Climate Specialist
jobs.description:
**Position Summary**

The Climate Specialist Coordinator provides technical leadership for integrating climate adaptation, environmental sustainability and climate-risk management across Food Security and Livelihoods programming within the assigned hubs.The coordinator leads the day-to-day delivery of assigned hub-level projects, implemented directly by CARE field teams or through local partners, consultants and vendors, and works closely with CARE’s support functions (finance, grants, procurement, risk management, MEAL, etc.). The role ensures that project design and implementation are informed by climate-risk and vulnerability analysis and incorporate appropriate adaptation measures, including climate-smart agriculture and livestock practices, sustainable natural-resource management, water and energy efficiency, ecosystem-based approaches, and disaster-risk reduction. Where staff are assigned, the coordinator provides direct supervision and strengthens the capacity of local partner organizations to deliver market-oriented, gender-responsive and climate-resilient FSL programmes.The role provides technical quality assurance for climate-related interventions, supports the development of climate adaptation strategies and technical standards, and monitors the effectiveness of adaptation measures using relevant climate and resilience indicators. The coordinator also supports the identification and testing of context-appropriate climate technologies, strengthens access to climate and early-warning information, and documents evidence and learning to inform programme adaptation and scale-up.The role represents CARE in hub-level and sub-national climate, environment, agriculture, FSL, Early Recovery and Livelihoods coordination mechanisms and technical working groups. It contributes technical and operational evidence to climate-risk and vulnerability assessments, feasibility studies, market and value-chain analyses, learning reviews, policy engagement and the development of climate-focused and climate-finance proposals.Cross-cutting priorities include gender equality and the empowerment of women and youth, gender-responsive and locally led climate adaptation, environmental and social safeguards, conflict-sensitive natural-resource management, accountability to affected populations, and strict adherence to donor and CARE policies.

**The employee is also required to:**

- Remain aware of and comply with safety and security regulations and procedures and bear responsibility for personal safety and security while under contract.
- Comply with CARE policies, including but not limited to the Safeguarding Policy, Code of Conduct, and other organizational and HR policies.CARE has a zero-tolerance approach towards sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, and child abuse towards any person, including our staff, representatives, partners, programme participants, and members of the communities where we work. We expect all staff, partners, and related personnel to share this commitment by understanding, abiding by, and working within the CARE International Safeguarding Policy and related framework at all times while representing CARE.
- Ensure that all direct team members are aware of their responsibilities under the CARE International Safeguarding Policy commitments, including signing the Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct and completing induction and refresher training.
- Depending on the specific role and responsibilities, the employee may be requested to comply with additional policies, guidelines, and related regulations, as necessary.

**Key Responsibilities**

1. **Program Implementation & Quality Assurance:**

- Lead the day-to-day delivery of all climate-focused and climate-resilient FSL activities, implemented either directly by CARE field teams or through partners, consultants and vendors, ensuring full compliance with approved proposals, work plans, budgets, donor rules, and CARE policies, climate and environmental safeguards, and technical standards.

Sector coordination and reporting:

- Serve as the national climate and climate-resilient FSL coordination focal point, with relavant local authorities and other coordination bodies.
- Prepare inputs for CARE situation reports and internal updates, including relevant climate risks, seasonal trends, environmental conditions and progress against adaptation objectives.

Assessment, planning and design:

- Coordinate and participate in conducting food security, livelihoods, market, climate-risk and vulnerability assessments with partners and CARE field teams.Map and analyze market systems, value chains, key stakeholders, climate hazards, exposure and vulnerability to inform targeting and programme design.
- Coordinate partner inputs to develop and maintain detailed project plans and implementation schedules, including the creation of climate-sensitive assessment tools and questionnaires.
- Coordinate partner inputs to support inclusive project planning and detailed designs, ensuring that proposed interventions are technically appropriate to identified climate risks and local adaptation priorities.
- Ensure all assessments, targeting, site selection, and implementation processes are gender-sensitive, inclusive, conflict-sensitive and climate risk-informed, with meaningful participation of women and girls in decision-making and feedback mechanisms.
- Liaise with Procurement and Supply Chain teams to resolve delivery challenges and ensure timely implementation, including the development and review of technical specifications for climate-adaptation technologies, equipment and services.

Implementation oversight:

- Coordinate day-to-day implementation with CARE field teams, partners, and vendors to ensure the smooth delivery of cash, voucher, agricultural, livelihood-support and climate-adaptation activities.
- Ensure market monitoring, post-distribution monitoring (PDM), climate and seasonal monitoring, and feedback mechanisms are in place, actively used, and regularly reviewed to inform programme adaptation and align with MEAL and activity plans.
- Coordinate with MEAL and Risk teams to triangulate monitoring data, climate and early-warning information, address implementation challenges, and ensure compliance with CARE’s accountability framework.Facilitate regular biweekly progress meetings with partners, vendors, and field teams to review work plans, budgets, technical quality and climate-adaptation measures; address challenges and bottlenecks; and escalate delays when necessary.
- Conduct regular site and vendor visits for technical supervision and quality monitoring, including verification of climate-resilient designs, environmental safeguards and the functionality of adaptation technologies, documenting findings and follow-up actions.
- Provide coordination and logistical support to field teams for the smooth delivery of climate-related interventions.
- Provide technical support on early recovery and FSL programming, including climate-smart agriculture and livestock production, sustainable water and natural-resource management, ecosystem-based adaptation, climate information services, and climate-adapted VSLA interventions, ensuring teams and partners follow approved standards, tools and processes.
- Strengthen the Area-Based Approach (ABA) to promote integrated, multisectoral responses in targeted locations based on local climate-risk profiles, environmental pressures and community adaptation priorities.

Line Management (if applicable):

- The position currently has no staff directly reporting to it.
- If Program Officers are recruited in the future, the Coordinator will provide supervision, set objectives, offer coaching and mentoring, and conduct performance reviews.
- Ensure compliance with CARE’s safeguarding, PSEA, code of conduct, and safety and security procedures.

1. **Financial & Grant Compliance:**

- Lead the development and modification of SGA packages with partners, and review financial payment requests (including partner payments, field consultants, and technical advisors) in coordination with the Finance Team.
- For CARE awards and partner subgrants, monitor and update burn rates and expenditure projections, including expenditure against climate-specific activities, adaptation measures and environmental commitments, under/overspending conditions with partners and support teams.
- Prepare and update project-level pipelines and spending projections for each grant; update monthly with the Finance Team.
- Flag and resolve under/overspending in coordination with partners, ensuring that required climate-related technical activities and quality standards are adequately resourced.
- Review partner financial reports for accuracy and coherence with activity progress; flag issues for follow-up with Finance.
- Ensure correct coding and eligibility for all activities, including accurate allocation and tracking of climate-related expenditure where required by the donor. Maintain full, auditable grant documentation at the hub level and support donor or internal audits and spot checks.
- Support the preparation and review of budgets for climate adaptation, climate-resilient livelihoods and environmental activities, ensuring that technical specifications and associated costs are realistic and appropriately justified.

1. **Monitoring & Reporting:**

- Support the drafting of donor narrative reports and ensure timely submission of partner inputs.
- Maintain a well-structured and regularly updated archiving system for all program documents, reports, and supporting materials, in alignment with CARE’s documentation standards.
- Contribute to the monitoring review reports for partners
- Follow up with partners and field teams on MEAL findings and corrective action plans to ensure accountability and program improvement.

1. **Program Development, Learning & Representation:**

- Organize and facilitate trainings for partners, vendors, and staff on FSL standards, market-based programming, and inclusion, as well as climate-risk screening, locally led adaptation, climate-smart agriculture, environmental sustainability and the application of climate information.
- Lead learning and reflection sessions during and after implementation and document lessons learned.
- Organize end-of-project partner debriefs to capture key achievements and learning.
- Facilitate partner co-creation and design workshops for new proposals, ensuring learning and evidence from current implementation are incorporated into new project concepts.
- Lead or contribute to broader hub-level needs assessments, gender analysis, market assessments, post-implementation reviews or thematic studies that inform future program design, sector strategies, and proposal development, including climate vulnerability and capacity assessments, environmental analysis, value-chain climate-risk assessments and feasibility studies for adaptation technologies.
- Provide hub-level inputs to new proposals, concept notes and budgets, ensuring gender-responsive and market-based approaches are reflected, and that proposed interventions are aligned with identified climate risks, adaptation priorities and relevant national climate frameworks.
- Represent CARE, as delegated by the Programme Manager, in coordination with relevant ministries and technical authorities, as well as climate change, environment, agriculture, food security and livelihoods, early recovery, cash, and disaster-risk reduction sector coordination mechanisms and technical working groups.
- Contribute technical inputs to climate-focused and climate-finance opportunities and support engagement with government institutions, research organizations and technical partners on climate adaptation and resilience.

**Required Qualifications, Skills and Experience**

- Bachelor’s degree in Climate Change, Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, Agriculture, Agricultural Engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience in climate adaptation and resilience programming.
- 4–5 years of experience coordinating humanitarian or early recovery programs, climate adaptation, environmental or resilience programmes in complex or insecure environments.
- Training or certification in climate change adaptation, Climate Vulnerability and Capacity Analysis (CVCA), climate-smart agriculture, ecosystem-based adaptation or disaster-risk reduction.
- At least 3 years of experience managing or coordinating FSL, climate adaptation, climate-resilient FSL, food security, agriculture, natural-resource management, cash/voucher or livelihoods projects.
- Proven experience working with and through local implementing partners, vendors and financial service provider, technical institutions and relevant government authorities.
- Experience with grant and budget monitoring, burn-rate tracking, variance analysis and donor compliance in multi-donor programs, as well as climate hazards, vulnerability, adaptive capacity and their effects on food and livelihood systems.
- Strong understanding of market systems, value chains and basic economic principles in crisis-affected contexts.
- Demonstrated technical experience in one or more relevant areas, such as climate-smart agriculture and livestock production, sustainable water and natural-resource management, climate information services, ecosystem-based adaptation, renewable energy or environmental safeguards.
- Advanced written and spoken English; Arabic language skills essential.
- Strong computer skills (Microsoft Office: Word, Excel, Outlook, plus familiarity with Kobo or similar data collection platforms).
- Good communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively under stress in emergency settings.

Desired:

- Additional training or professional certification in climate change adaptation, climate-risk and vulnerability assessment, climate-smart agriculture, ecosystem-based adaptation, disaster-risk reduction, environmental safeguards, climate finance, or geographic information systems and climate-data analysis.
- Experience working with CARE or similar international NGOs.
- Master’s degree or additional professional training in Climate Change, Environmental Management, Climate Adaptation, Climate-Smart Agriculture, Natural Resource Management, Disaster Risk Reduction, Climate Finance, GIS, or climate-data analysis.

**Safeguarding Commitments**

The organization has a zero-tolerance approach toward sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, and child abuse. We will carefully examine allegations and investigate, and take appropriate disciplinary action where this is needed, taking into consideration the rights and interests of the survivor, consistent with the organization’s survivor-centred approach. We make very clear that sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, and child abuse in any form, perpetrated by our staff, partners or other related personnel, towards anyone, will not be tolerated.

We provide equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, handicap, disability, or marital status.

jobs.title: TOR: SUPPLY, INSTALLATION AND COMMISSIONING OF MILK COOLING AND PROCESSING EQUIPMENT IN TANZANIA FORSolidaridad East and Central Africa
jobs.description:
## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

[Solidaridad Network ](https://www.solidaridadnetwork.org/)is an international solution-oriented civil society organisation working through eight regional expertise centres to transform markets to make them more sustainable and inclusive. Our eight regional expertise centres include Asia, Eastern and Central Africa, Europe, Latin America, North America, Southern Africa, South America, West Africa and our global Secretariat in the Netherlands. Solidaridad Eastern and Central Africa, one of the regional centres, headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya with country offices and programmes in Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, Tanzania and Uganda. We bring together supply chain players and engage them with innovative solutions to improve production, ensuring the transition to a sustainable and inclusive economy that maximises the benefit for all. We facilitate strengthening of local capacity in developing countries, support the creation of enabling environments for economies to thrive, and improve market access. Solidaridad embraces the public-private and people partnerships (PPPP) in order to test innovations, speed up change, and take success to scale. Globally, Solidaridad works around Coffee and other 12 commodities/sectors ([http://www.solidaridadnetwork.org](http://www.solidaridadnetwork.org/))

## 2.0 The Pathways to Prosperity Coffee Project in Tanzania Summary

The Pathways to Prosperity (P2P) Coffee Project is a 7-year project funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs supporting smallholder coffee farmers through 3 pathways: (i) creating viable and resilient production systems ii) catalysing inclusive service delivery systems, and iii) championing inclusive markets. The programme will co-create and implement tailored interventions to facilitate transformation in the coffee sector, contributing to increased sustainable production (productivity and quality) and incomes, enhancing resilience to the impacts of climate change and other shocks, and the creation of decent jobs and inclusive supply chains.

The P2P project aims to build the capacity of 101,500 smallholder coffee farmers (30% women and 15% youth) in Songwe, Mbeya and Ruvuma regions\*\*.\*\* Also, strengthen the leadership and governance of Coffee Cooperative Societies within the project regions and provide a platform for cooperatives to link & interact with over 500 service providers in their respective regions to establish long-term relations that serve the interests of both.

The intended long-term impact is that small- holder coffee farmers thrive by participating in the supply chain that is economically viable, socially responsible and environmentally sound by 2029. Smallholder coffee farmers will have an opportunity to participate in economically viable value chains by increasing their productivity through adoption of Good Agricultural Practices (GAP’s) for increased incomes. It prioritises the inclusion of women and youth. Environmental conservation is a key element focusing on adoption of climate resilient practices, implementing carbon projects as well as adopting agroforestry.

**3.0 Background**

Coffee remains the main cash crop for many smallholder households in Tanzania’s Southern highland regions, yet most farmers depend on a single harvest cycle that generates income only once or twice a year. This seasonal pattern creates long periods of limited cash flow, during which households often struggle to meet basic needs or invest consistently in essential farm management practices such as fertiliser application, pruning, pest control, and labour. Diversification into complementary farm enterprises is therefore critical to stabilising household income and to sustaining investment in coffee production throughout the year.

Dairy farming is one of the most practical diversification options available in coffee-growing areas. The target regions have favourable conditions for dairy production, including moderate temperatures, adequate rainfall, and access to crop residues and fodder resources. In addition, livestock keeping is already part of many coffee-based farming systems, though often at a small scale and with limited access to structured markets. Dairy integrates well with coffee farming and strengthens the overall farm system. Manure from dairy animals provides an accessible source of organic fertiliser for coffee farms, improving soil fertility and soil organic matter while reducing dependence on costly external inputs. Crop residues from coffee farms and fodder grown along farm boundaries can be used for livestock feeding, creating a circular relationship where each enterprise supports the other.

Unlike coffee, dairy generates regular income through daily or weekly milk sales. This predictable cash flow enables households to meet routine expenses and finance ongoing farm operations without relying on premature coffee sales or expensive credit. Strengthening dairy farming within coffee-growing communities therefore offers a sound pathway to improve income stability while reinforcing the productivity and sustainability of coffee systems.

As a result, Solidaridad through the Pathways to Prosperity, Coffee Programme seeks to acquire high-quality stainless steel Bulk Milk Cooling Tanks capable of rapidly cooling raw milk, a standby generator, display refrigerators, and an automated bottle filling machine to maintaining milk quality, increasing market reach while complying with applicable dairy industry standards.

## 4.0 Scope of Work

The successful bidder shall be responsible for:

i) Supply of brand-new Bulk Milk Cooling Tanks of 3,000 Litres with Solidaridad's branding before or after installation.

ii) Supply of complete refrigeration systems including compressors, condensers, and refrigerant gas.

iii) Supply of control panels and all standard accessories.

iv) Supply of a standby generator

v) Supply of automated bottle filling machines for both cups and bottles

vi) Supply of display refrigerators

vii) Delivery of equipment to site.

viii) Mechanical, electrical, and refrigeration installation.

ix) Testing and commissioning of the complete system.

x) Demonstration of cooling performance.

xi) Training of client personnel.

xii) Provision of documentation, warranty, and after-sales support.

xiii) Provide capacity-building training for cooperative and factory staff on the proper operation, routine maintenance, and management of the cooling facility, filling machine, and standby generator to ensure efficiency, product quality, and equipment durability.

## 4.1 Technical Specifications

1. 1 Bulk Milk Cooler (BMC) – 3,000 Litres
2. 1 Standby Generator – 30 kVA
3. **Automated Filling Machine for Bottles and Cups – 1 Unit**

- Food-contact parts manufactured from **food-grade stainless steel**
- Suitable for yoghurt and other liquid/semi-liquid dairy products
- Filling range: approximately **250 ml to 1,000 ml**
- Compatible with both **bottles and cups**
- Automated filling and dosing system with adjustable filling volumes
- Designed to improve filling accuracy, hygiene, production efficiency, and reduce product losses

1. **Display Refrigerators – 3 Units**

- Brand/model: **BOSS or equivalent**
- Capacity: approximately **200 litres per unit**
- Upright commercial display refrigerator with transparent/glass door
- Adjustable temperature control suitable for chilled dairy products
- Internal shelving for product display
- Energy-efficient cooling system
- Suitable for installation at retail outlets for storage and display of yoghurt and other dairy products.

**4.1.1 Milk Tank Specifications for the 3,000Litre BMC**

**Item and Specification**

**Working Capacity**

3,000 Litres

**Gross Capacity**

3,300 Litres

**Tank Design**

Open, Cylindrical Horizontal

**Material**

Stainless Steel AISI 304 (Food Grade)

**Inner Sheet Thickness**

**Outer Sheet Thickness**

**Insulation**

**Insulation Thickness**

**Insulation Standard**

ISO 5708 2A II or equivalent

**Volume Measurement**

**Supports**

Adjustable stainless steel feet

**4.1.2** **Refrigeration System for the 3,000 Litre BMC**

**Item and Specification**

**No. of Compressors**

**Condenser**

35°C

≤ 3.0 hrs (1st milking), ≤ 1.25 hrs (2nd milking)

**Power Supply**

415V, 3 Phase

**4.1.3** **Generator**

- Rated capacity: **30 kVA**
- Suitable for supporting dairy cooling and processing equipment during power interruptions
- Automatic voltage regulation
- Fuel-efficient diesel engine
- Complete with control panel and relevant safety protection features

**4.1.3** **3 BOSS company - 200L display single door refrigerators**

- Brand/model: **BOSS or equivalent**

- Upright commercial display refrigerator with transparent/glass door
- Adjustable temperature control suitable for chilled dairy products
- Internal shelving for product display
- Energy-efficient cooling system
- Suitable for installation at retail outlets for storage and display of yoghurt and other dairy products.

**4.1.4 Specifications for automated bottle filling machine - 1 Unit**

**Item and Specifications**

**Filling range**

250 ml to 1000 ml within +-0.5% to +-1%

**Production capacity**

4 nozzles

**Bottle compatibility**

**Material standard**

Food-grade stainless steel SS316L for all product contact parts, SS304 frame; non-toxic, food-grade silicone seals and gaskets

**Hygiene**

Clean-In-Place (CIP) automated cleaning loop compatibility

**5.0 Common Accessories**

1. **Refrigeration Control Panel** with auto/manual operation, overload protection, and digital temperature display.
2. **CIP (Clean-in-Place) System**, including:
1. CIP spray ball
2. Stainless steel piping (approx. 38 mm)
3. Food-grade hose pipe – minimum 10 m
4. Stainless steel dump/balance tank – approx. 200 L with sieve
3. **Milk Pump & Offloading System**:
1. Centrifugal milk pump, approx. 1 HP
2. SS 304 construction
3. Product offloading hose – approx. 38 mm, 10 Mtrs.
4. **Earthing**:
1. Pipe-type earthing
2. Minimum four (4) earthing points

**6.0** **Electrical & Power Requirements**

**Item and Specification**

**Power Supply**

415V ±10%, 3 Phase, 50 Hz

**Generator Compatibility**

Approx. 30 kVA

**Servo Stabilizer**

Approx. 18 kVA, 3 Phase (350–500 V range)

**7.0 Installation, Testing & Commissioning**

The supplier shall install the equipment on a foundation prepared by the client, complete all mechanical, electrical, and refrigeration connections, test the system for performance and safety, commission the equipment, and train designated client personnel.

**8.0 Recommended Spare Parts (To Be Quoted Separately)**

The bidder shall provide pricing and availability for the following recommended spares:

1. Temperature sensor / probe
2. Digital temperature controller
3. Agitator motor
4. Agitator shaft seal
5. Solenoid valve
6. Expansion valve
7. Contactor and overload relay
8. Milk pump mechanical seal
9. Condenser fan motor
10. Refrigerant gas (top-up quantity)

*Note: Spare parts are not covered under warranty.*

**9.0 Warranty & After-Sales Support**

- Warranty Period:
- Two (2) years warranty on main equipment parts, including tank structure, compressors, evaporator, condenser, agitator assembly, and control panel.
- Consumables and spare parts are excluded from warranty, including seals, gaskets, sensors, refrigerant gas, hoses, and electrical consumables.
- Technical support shall be provided during the warranty period.

**10.0 Delivery Timeline**

The Bulk Milk Cooling Tanks are ex-stock and delivery shall be immediate upon receipt of a confirmed purchase order. The delivery, installation and testing should be finalised in 120 days maximum after signing of the contract.

**11.0 Tender Compliance**

Bidders shall:

- Be manufacturers or authorized suppliers of Bulk Milk Coolers
- Submit separate price for 3,000L units
- Submit separate price for a 200L display refrigerators
- Submit a separate price for a 30kv standby generator
- Submit a separate price for an automated food-graded bottle filling machine 250ml to 1000ml
- Include supply of refrigerant gas, installation, testing, and commissioning
- Confirm full compliance with this Terms of Reference.

**12.0 Acceptance**

Final acceptance shall be subject to successful installation, testing, commissioning, and written approval by the Solidaridad ECA.

**Location:** Kenya

**Employment Type:** Full-time

**Department:** Mission Impact

**Position Summary:**

We are seeking an exceptional, strategic and mission-driven executive leader to join our organisation as **Vice President Mission Impact Africa**.The successful candidate will provide strategic, programmatic and operational leadership across our African portfolio, translating Feed the Children's enterprise Mission Impact Strategy into locally relevant country strategies, high-quality programmes, measurable outcomes, effective operations and sustainable partnerships.

- Finance
- People & Culture
- Supply Chain and Procurement

- Operational judgement and accountability
- Strategic partnership development
- Financial stewardship
- Adaptive leadership and change management

- Demonstrated commitment to ethical leadership, safeguarding, accountability, dignity and respect.

**Our Commitment to Safeguarding, Diversity and Inclusion**

Feed the Children is committed to safeguarding children and communities and preventing exploitation, abuse, harassment and neglect.

We are committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, respectful and safe working environment where all individuals are treated fairly and with dignity.

Pacific Australia Skills is a significant Australian investment which stands to make a major contribution to supporting social and economic growth in the region through strengthening the skills and training sector across the Pacific and Timor-Leste. Pacific Australia Skills builds on the achievements of 17 years of Australian Government support for skills and training in the Pacific.

**About DT Global Asia Pacific**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [www.dt-global.com](http://www.dt-global.com/)

The Country Safeguards Manager is responsible for leading the implementation, coordination and continuous improvement of safeguarding systems across the Paciﬁc Australia Skills Solomon Islands program. The role provides strategic and technical leadership to ensure safeguarding is effectively integrated into program planning, procurement, partnership management, activity implementation and organisational operations. The position is accountable for ensuring compliance with DFAT safeguarding requirements, DT Global safeguarding policies, procedures and Paciﬁc Australia Skills safeguarding strategy through the delivery of safeguarding risk management, due diligence, incident management, monitoring, compliance and capacity strengthening activities. The Country Safeguards Manager also supports the development of a strong safeguarding culture by promoting accountability, prevention, respectful behaviours and continuous organisational learning.

**Reporting Relationship**

The Country Director provides overall leadership, operational oversight and performance management of the position, ensuring safeguarding is integrated into country operations and strategic priorities. The Regional Safeguards Manager provides specialist technical advice, professional supervision and quality assurance to ensure consistent implementation of safeguarding policies, procedures and standards across Pacific Australia Skills.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

## 1. **Strategic Safeguarding Leadership**

- Lead the implementation of the Pacific Australia Skills Safeguarding Strategy and annual country safeguarding workplan, ensuring safeguarding is embedded across all aspects of program delivery in Solomon Islands.
- Provide strategic and technical advice to the Country Director and Country Leadership Team on safeguarding risks, compliance obligations, emerging issues and continuous improvement initiatives.
- Champion a culture of safeguarding, accountability and respectful behaviours by promoting awareness, prevention and shared responsibility across the program.
- Ensure safeguarding considerations are integrated into program planning, activity design, procurement, partnership development and operational decision-making.
- Contribute to regional safeguarding priorities and support the consistent application of safeguarding standards across Pacific Australia Skills.

## 2. **Safeguarding Risk Management and Due Diligence**

- Lead the implementation of safeguarding due diligence processes for implementing partners, contractors, service providers and other stakeholders in accordance with DFAT and DT Global safeguarding requirements and procedures.
- Conduct Safeguards Risk and Capacity Assessments and develop practical safeguarding plans to strengthen organisational capability and compliance.
- Review and provide technical quality assurance of Activity Safeguards Risk Assessments, ensuring risks are appropriately identified, mitigated, monitored and documented.
- Monitor implementation of safeguarding mitigation measures and partner action plans, providing technical support to address identified gaps and strengthen safeguarding systems.
- Work collaboratively with procurement, partnerships and program teams to ensure safeguarding considerations are appropriately incorporated throughout the partnership lifecycle.

## 3. **Incident Management and Case Coordination**

- Ensure safeguarding incidents are reported, managed and escalated within required timeframes while maintaining confidentiality and appropriate information management.
- Coordinate survivor-centred and child-centred responses, including referrals to appropriate support services and monitoring implementation of agreed actions.
- Provide technical advice and support to managers and staff in responding to safeguarding concerns and implementing appropriate risk mitigation measures.

## 4. **Capacity Development and Technical Support**

- Coordinate and deliver safeguarding induction, briefings, awareness and capacity strengthening initiatives for Pacific Australia Skills staff, implementing partners, government stakeholders, contractors and service providers.
- Build safeguarding capability through coaching, mentoring and ongoing technical support to Safeguards Focal Points and key stakeholders.
- Support partners to strengthen safeguarding governance, policies, procedures, reporting mechanisms and organisational practices aligned with DFAT safeguarding requirements.
- Promote continuous learning by identifying emerging safeguarding issues, lessons learned and opportunities to strengthen organisational capability.

## 5. **Monitoring, Compliance and Quality Assurance**

- Monitor safeguarding implementation through regular field visits, compliance reviews, partner engagement and activity monitoring to assess the effectiveness of safeguarding measures.
- Track implementation of safeguarding action plans, recommendations and corrective actions, ensuring timely follow-up and continuous improvement.
- Prepare high-quality safeguarding reports, dashboards, risk analyses, briefing papers and technical updates for the Country Director, Regional Safeguards Manager and other stakeholders as required.
- Monitor compliance with DT Global safeguarding policies, Codes of Conduct, DFAT safeguarding requirements and contractual safeguarding obligations.
- Contribute to internal audits, assurance processes and organisational reporting to demonstrate safeguarding compliance and program performance.

## 6. **Stakeholder Engagement and Partnerships**

- Develop and maintain effective working relationships with government agencies, TVET institutions, employers, civil society organisations, implementing partners, contractors and development partners to strengthen safeguarding outcomes.
- Provide trusted technical advice to internal and external stakeholders on safeguarding policy, risk management and good practice.
- Work closely with Rural Training Centres (RTCs) in Solomon Islands to strengthen safeguarding practices through tailored assessments, training and technical support, with follow-up on agreed improvement actions that reflect their local contexts and training environments.
- Represent Pacific Australia Skills in safeguarding-related meetings, working groups, technical forums and partner consultations as delegated by the Country Director.
- Foster collaborative partnerships that strengthen safeguarding capability, promote organisational learning and support sustainable safeguarding systems across the program.

## 7. **Other Responsibilities**

- Contribute to regional safeguarding initiatives, Communities of Practice, cross-country learning and the continuous improvement of safeguarding systems across Pacific Australia Skills.
- Support the development, review and continuous improvement of safeguarding policies, guidance materials, tools, templates and training resources.
- Participate in organisational planning, learning and knowledge management activities to strengthen safeguarding practice across the program.
- Maintain professional knowledge of emerging safeguarding legislation, DFAT policies, international standards and best practice to ensure continuous improvement in safeguarding approaches.
- Undertake other duties consistent with the responsibilities, classification and level of the position, as reasonably directed by the Lead.
- This TOR may be revised or updated in the future as required.
