jobs.title: Venezuela: Oficial de Manejo de Información (Caracas)
jobs.description:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humanitaria cuyo mandato es salvar vidas y mejorar las condiciones de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad. Como parte del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja, brinda asistencia oportuna en emergencias, desastres y contextos de necesidad humanitaria.

Guiada por sus Principios Fundamentales -Humanidad, Imparcialidad, Neutralidad, Independencia, Voluntariado, Unidad y Universalidad- la CRV actúa como auxiliar de los poderes públicos en el ámbito humanitario, trabajando para reducir el sufrimiento humano sin distinción de raza, género, religión o ideología. Su labor abarca la atención médica de emergencia, el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia comunitaria, la capacitación en primeros auxilios, la respuesta a desastres y la promoción de la salud y el bienestar.

A través de una red de voluntarios altamente comprometidos, la CRV moviliza recursos de manera eficiente y eficaz para estar presente donde más se necesita, cuando más se necesita. Su labor se fundamenta en la solidaridad, el respeto a la dignidad humana y el compromiso con la protección de la vida en todas sus formas.

**Compromiso con la Salvaguarda**

La Cruz Roja Venezolana está comprometida con la creación y mantenimiento de entornos seguros y respetuosos para las comunidades, el personal y el voluntariado y con la prevención de la explotación, el abuso y el acoso sexual.

Las personas seleccionadas deberán cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas y estándares de Salvaguarda aplicables. Como parte de su proceso de contratación segura, la CRV podrá realizar verificaciones de referencias profesionales y solicitar información pertinente sobre antecedentes de conducta profesional y Salvaguarda, de acuerdo con sus procedimientos y la normativa aplicable.

**Responsabilidad general de Salvaguarda**

La persona titular del puesto deberá promover y respetar los estándares de Salvaguarda de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas aplicables, mantener límites profesionales apropiados, contribuir a prevenir daños y reportar de forma inmediata cualquier preocupación de Salvaguarda a través de los mecanismos establecidos.

**Adición para puestos de riesgo elevado**

Debido a la naturaleza de sus funciones, la persona deberá identificar y mitigar activamente riesgos de Salvaguarda asociados a sus actividades, mantener estándares reforzados de conducta y límites profesionales y asegurar que su interacción con comunidades y personas en situación de vulnerabilidad se desarrolle de forma segura, digna, inclusiva y respetuosa.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

Por favor verifique que cumpla con todos o la mayoría de los requisitos para aplicar.

**¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia? Funciones claves / Responsabilidades**

El/la Oficial de Manejo de Información será responsable de brindar apoyo técnico al Oficial de Planificación, Monitoreo, Evaluación y Reporte (PMER) en la recolección, organización, procesamiento, análisis y visualización de la información institucional y operativa de la Cruz Roja Venezolana.

Su trabajo contribuirá al seguimiento del Plan Estratégico 2026–2030, los planes operativos anuales y las operaciones de emergencia, con especial atención a la respuesta institucional ante el terremoto.

La persona contribuirá a que el Oficial PMER y la Dirección de Programas dispongan de información oportuna, confiable, desagregada y presentada de manera comprensible para el seguimiento institucional, la elaboración de reportes y la toma de decisiones.

**Funciones y responsabilidades**

1\. Recolección, consolidación y calidad de los datos

- Apoyar al Oficial PMER en la consolidación de información proveniente de direcciones nacionales, programas, proyectos, filiales y equipos desplegados en terreno.
- Organizar y actualizar las bases de datos, matrices de seguimiento y repositorios de información institucional y operativa.
- Realizar la revisión, limpieza y validación de los datos, identificando inconsistencias, duplicaciones, omisiones y valores atípicos.
- Dar seguimiento a la recepción oportuna de información, de acuerdo con los calendarios y flujos de reporte establecidos.
- Verificar la aplicación de las desagregaciones, definiciones operativas y criterios de calidad definidos por PMER.
- Mantener organizados los medios de verificación y las evidencias relacionadas con los indicadores y resultados reportados.

2\. Herramientas y sistemas de información

- Apoyar el diseño y actualización de formularios digitales, bases de datos, matrices y otras herramientas para la recolección y gestión de información.
- Configurar y administrar herramientas de recolección digital, como KoboToolbox, Microsoft Forms u otras plataformas utilizadas por la institución.
- Apoyar la estandarización de formatos, variables, catálogos y procedimientos para el registro y almacenamiento de datos.
- Desarrollar y actualizar tableros de seguimiento y otros productos de visualización de información.
- Documentar las herramientas, procedimientos y flujos de información para facilitar su uso y sostenibilidad.
- Proponer mejoras técnicas para optimizar la integración, organización y accesibilidad de la información.

3\. Análisis y productos de información

- Preparar tablas, gráficos, mapas, resúmenes estadísticos y otros productos requeridos
- Apoyar la actualización de indicadores, metas, cobertura geográfica, población alcanzada y servicios prestados.
- Elaborar insumos para informes institucionales, reportes de situación, informes operacionales y reportes para socios y donantes.
- Apoyar la identificación de brechas, retrasos, duplicaciones y desviaciones a partir del análisis de los datos.
- Desarrollar tableros, fichas y visualizaciones que faciliten la comprensión de los avances y resultados.
- Adaptar la información técnica para que sea comprensible y útil para equipos programáticos y responsables de la toma de decisiones.

4\. Acompañamiento técnico y protección de datos

- Brindar asistencia técnica al personal y voluntariado en el uso de formularios, matrices, bases de datos y herramientas de visualización.
- Elaborar orientaciones sencillas y materiales de apoyo para el registro y reporte de información.
- Coordinar con las áreas programáticas y operativas para resolver dudas o inconsistencias relacionadas con los datos.
- Garantizar el manejo seguro de los datos personales y sensibles, de acuerdo con los principios de confidencialidad, protección de datos y no hacer daño.
- Realizar otras funciones relacionadas con el cargo que sean asignadas por su supervisor inmediato.

**Resultados esperados del cargo**

- Bases de datos y matrices de seguimiento actualizadas, organizadas y validadas.
- Información institucional y operativa consolidada y disponible oportunamente.
- Herramientas digitales de recolección y gestión de datos implementadas y documentadas.
- Tableros, gráficos, mapas y productos de información actualizados.
- Insumos para reportes institucionales y de emergencia preparados dentro de los plazos establecidos.
- Inconsistencias, vacíos y duplicaciones de información identificados y comunicados oportunamente.

**Reporte**

El/la Oficial de Manejo de Información reportará a la Dirección de Programas y trabajará bajo la supervisión técnica y coordinación directa del/de la Oficial de Planificación, Monitoreo, Evaluación y Reporte (PMER).

**Lugar de trabajo y viajes**

El lugar de trabajo será Caracas, en la sede central de la Cruz Roja Venezolana. La persona deberá tener disponibilidad para realizar desplazamientos a las zonas de intervención cuando sea requerido.

**Requisitos del perfil**

Para contribuir al fortalecimiento del sistema humanitario venezolano, la persona deberá cumplir con los siguientes requisitos:

- Título universitario en estadística, ingeniería, sistemas, informática, ciencias sociales, geografía, salud pública, administración u otras áreas afines.
- Experiencia mínima de dos años en manejo de información, análisis de datos, monitoreo de proyectos o funciones similares en contextos humanitarios, sociales o de desarrollo.
- Manejo avanzado de Excel, DAX y Power Bi
- Experiencia en el uso de herramientas digitales de recolección de datos, como KoboToolbox, ODK, Microsoft Forms u otras plataformas similares.
- Experiencia en limpieza, validación, consolidación y estructuración de información proveniente de distintas fuentes.
- Conocimientos básicos de planificación, monitoreo, evaluación y reporte, gestión basada en resultados e indicadores.
- Capacidad para elaborar tablas, gráficos, mapas, resúmenes estadísticos y productos de información.
- Habilidades analíticas, pensamiento lógico y alta atención al detalle.
- Capacidad para traducir datos técnicos en información clara y comprensible para equipos no especializados.
- Buenas habilidades de comunicación oral y escrita.
- Capacidad para trabajar de manera autónoma y en coordinación con equipos multidisciplinarios.
- Capacidad para manejar información personal, sensible y confidencial de manera segura.
- Compromiso con los Principios Fundamentales del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y de la Media Luna Roja.
- Disponibilidad para realizar desplazamientos a las zonas de intervención.

**Se valorará**

- Experiencia previa en organizaciones humanitarias, ONG o con el Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y de la Media Luna Roja.
- Experiencia en gestión de información durante emergencias o desastres.
- Manejo de sistemas de información geográfica o herramientas de elaboración de mapas.
- Conocimiento de sectores como salud, gestión del riesgo de desastres, protección o WASH.
- Conocimiento funcional del idioma inglés.

jobs.title: Director for Movement Building and Partnerships
jobs.description:
ILGA World seeks a Director of Movement Building and Partnerships to manage, develop, and grow ILGA World’s work in movement building and partnerships.

The Director of Movement Building and Partnerships (DMP) provides strategic and programmatic leadership for ILGA World’s work under Strategic Objective 3 on movement building, including cross-movement partnerships, regranting, and some aspects of our monitoring, evaluation and learning work.

This is a new role within ILGA World, and a core part of the role is to develop and grow this area of work in keeping with movement-building best practice, ensuring robust monitoring, evaluation and learning.

The DMP is part of the executive leadership of the organisation (Team of Directors) and reports directly to the Executive Director. They will hold relationships with ILGA World’s membership, cross-movement leaders, and supervise — initially — a small staff team with expertise in cross-movement and partnerships work, movement building, regranting and MEL work.

The Movement Building and Partnerships team is being created at a pivotal moment for ILGA World and builds on several years of work across various aligned movements and established relationships with key actors in feminist, SRHR and broader human rights movements.

ILGA World´s work is highly collaborative, interconnected and intersectional. In our work, we seek to connect SOGIESC and feminist issues, empower LGBTI activists and organisations, and convene our communities to strengthen their voice in global human rights advocacy and debates.

A core part of this role will be to lead the organisation’s development of a substantive regranting program to support LGBTI organisations across the globe in an environment of extremely restricted resources. This will include developing a re-granting strategy that aligns with our organisational strategy, best practice policies and working methods for subgrant eligibility criteria, due diligence, risk assessment, programme and financial accountabilities and MEL. This role collaborates closely with both the finance and programmes teams at ILGA to ensure best practice and alignment with advocacy priorities.

The successful candidate must be able to skilfully navigate the global LGBTI activist community and feminist, SRHR, and broader human rights movements and partnership spaces. They will be a respected (feminist) leader in our communities, a strategic thinker with a proven ability to develop partnerships and in movement building. They will have demonstrated management and staff supervision experience, an understanding of MEL and on practices and principles of regranting.

Ideally, the candidate will start working in **March 2027**.

[Follow this link to learn more about responsibilities; requirements; performance of duties, remuneration, and benefits.](https://ilga.org/vacancies/job-opportunity-director-movement-building-partnerships/)

jobs.title: Expert en biostatistique et gestion des données
jobs.description:
**Contexte**

SDI Inc., organisme spécialisé dans les études socio-économiques en Afrique, recherche avec ses partenaires un(e) Expert(e) en biostatistique et gestion des données pour une évaluation de la qualité sanitaire et nutritionnelle de la spiruline (dihé) produite dans les ouadis du Lac et du Kanem, au Tchad. Cette évaluation comprend deux campagnes de prélèvement dans une trentaine de sites, des enquêtes auprès des cueilleuses, des analyses en laboratoire, une base de données et une cartographie des risques et des profils de qualité. Le recrutement est soumis à l'attribution du contrat.

**Rôle et tâches**

L'Expert(e) en biostatistique encadre les méthodes d'analyse statistique.

- Assurer la qualité des données
- Analyser les réplicas et la variabilité spatiale et temporelle
- Comparer les résultats entre campagnes
- Contribuer au classement des sites selon le risque sanitaire et la qualité nutritionnelle

**Durée et lieu**

La mission s'étend sur environ dix (10) mois. Le travail s'effectue à N'Djaména et en partie à distance.

**Qualifications exigées**

- Formation en statistique, biostatistique, science des données, épidémiologie ou discipline connexe
- Au moins trois (3) ans d'expérience en traitement et en analyse de données
- Maîtrise d'un logiciel d'analyse statistique (R, Stata)
- Maîtrise du français, à l'écrit et à l'oral

**Atouts**

- Cinq ans d'expérience ou plus
- Expérience des données de laboratoire ou de surveillance sanitaire
- Expérience en zone isolée ou en contexte communautaire au Tchad

**Conditions**

Contrat de consultant. Les honoraires sont négociés selon le profil et l'expérience.

jobs.title: Project Associate [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Moldova is part of the EU’s European Neighborhood Policy (ENP) and in the Eastern Partnership framework, which aims at strengthening individual and regional relationships between the EU and countries in its neighborhood. Moldova is also part of the Energy Community Treaty since 2010 and has signed the Association Agreement with EU in June 2014, including the DCFTA which entered into force in 2016. As a follow-up, Moldova is required to ensure transposition of the EU acquis Communautaire, which underpins the EU energy legislation on electricity, gas, oil, renewables, energy efficiency and environment. The country has synchronized its electricity network with the ENTSO-E to connect to European electricity market.

Considering the ongoing energy crisis, the energy sector is one of the top priorities for the Government and it is addressed in Government’s Plans and a number of policy documents, laws and regulations which outlined the need to undertake more actions towards a green and just energy transition of the Republic of Moldova.

In accordance to the existing strategic planning documents, one of main priorities of the Government is to diversify the energy mix with more renewable energy, which is also fully in line with commitments under the EU Clean Energy for all Europeans package. Achieving this goal will require significant investment in the medium and long term, but also the country’s ability to attract and absorb the funds. The development of renewables, such as wind and solar, will also depend on improving the balancing capabilities of the Moldovan power system and its integration with neighboring countries.

In this regard the EU and Moldova stressed the importance of resilience against any potential efforts by third parties to use energy as a geopolitical level. The EU has urged Moldova to ensure that the energy sector reform demonstrates full respect of the Energy Community acquis and is in line with the EU Third Energy Package. The EU side confirmed its support to the objective of Moldova for integration into the EU energy system and market, an important step being the recent synchronization of its electricity network with the Continental European Network (CEN).

Recognizing the importance of a just and green energy transition in addressing the root causes of the ongoing crisis, the "Accelerating a Just Energy Transition in the Republic of Moldova" portfolio of interventions has emerged - co-designed with the Government and other representatives of the energy system to ensure its relevance and effectiveness.

Through this Portfolio of interventions, the Government of Moldova will be further assisted to tackle the current energy crisis and energy poverty, and addressing prioritized systemic elements in the energy sector to cope with potential future energy crisis.

The Accelerating a Just Energy Transition in Republic of Moldova has the following five key areas of intervention:

- Accelerate Energy Diversification and Efficiency: By supporting the modernization of infrastructure, buildings, and the grid, the Project aims to increase access to renewable energy sources, promote energy efficiency, and encourage investment in renewable energy and innovative technologies.

- Decarbonizing Industries and Economic Sectors: The Project seeks to drive the decarbonization of various economic sectors such as construction, transportation, agriculture, and the private sector. It aims to promote sustainable practices, share green business models, and develop vocational skills for the green energy sector to create equitable employment opportunities and support the transition to a low-carbon economy.

- Foster Sustainable Consumption Patterns: Through comprehensive public awareness campaigns and educational materials, the Project aims to deepen understanding of energy efficiency and renewable energy among community members, business leaders, and government agencies. It strives to promote behaviour change towards sustainable energy practices, particularly among vulnerable populations.

- Strengthen Inclusive Energy Governance: The Project recognizes the importance of inclusive energy governance at both the national and local levels. It aims to strengthen the capacity of relevant institutions and stakeholders to effectively govern and manage the energy sector. By promoting transparency, accountability, and participation, the Project seeks to ensure that decision-making processes related to energy transition are inclusive, empowering all segments of society, including marginalized groups.

- Addressing Energy Vulnerability and Promoting Resilience: One of the Project 's primary focus is to address energy vulnerability and promote resilience among households and businesses. It will provide further support to the Government in improving and implementing compensation mechanisms, including the established an on-bill compensation mechanism targeting the households by level of vulnerability. This intervention aims to provide immediate relief to energy-poor households and the private sector, while also fostering long-term energy resilience and efficiency. The Project places a strong emphasis on meeting the energy needs of vulnerable groups, prioritizing affordability, reliability, and sustainability. To this end, it will explore conceptualisation of decentralized energy solutions, off-grid options, and harness the role of energy access in conflict and disaster recovery efforts, livelihoods, and social inclusion.

Implementation period: 2023-2027.

Duties and Responsibilities

The specific duties and responsibilities of the Project Associate during the assignment will include, but not be limited to, the following:

Assist in efficient delivery of the projects, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Undertake administrative, logistical, travel, procurement, financial and asset management tasks in full compliance with UNDP rules, regulations and policies;

- Provide support to procure goods and services required by the projects, in liaison with the relevant staff and units of UNDP Country Office;

- Provide administrative support in arranging Projects related meetings when needed.

- Participate in the preparation of work plans, operation plans and procurement plans and periodical reviews thereof;

- Provide support in quality control of Projects activities, including assessing impact and effectiveness, tracking outputs and results, and ensure timely and efficient delivery;

- Maintain an appropriate filing system and documenting the implementation to enable further operational and financial closure of the projects;

- Provide support in regular monitoring and data collection of Projects activities in accordance with work plan and procurement plan;

- Provide general secretarial and administrative assistance to the projects in close liaison with UNDP teams, other UN agencies.

Ensure administration and implementation of operational strategies, adapt processes and procedures focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Full compliance with respective UNDP and donor rules, regulations, and policies of financial activities, financial recording/reporting system and follow-up on audit recommendations;

- Implementation of effective internal controls, proper functioning of a client-oriented financial resources management system.

- Personal initiative to perform daily work timely, efficiently, and in compliance with established rules and plans;

Provide financial support to the Projects, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Assist Projects team in drafting Project progress reports with financial data;

- Assist projects management in performing budget cycle: planning, preparation, revisions, and budget execution;

- Provide assistance to partner agencies involved in Projects activities, performing and monitoring financial aspects to ensure compliance with budgeted costs in line with established policies and procedures;

- Monitor Projects expenditures, ensuring that no expenditure is incurred before it has been authorized;

- Perform preparatory work for mandatory and general budget revisions, annual physical inventory, auditing; and assist external evaluators in fulfilling their mission;

- Ensure that all Projects financial activities are carried out on schedule and within budget to achieve the project outputs;

- Ensure timely submission of financial reports to the UNDP Country Office to verify the accuracy of such reports for the national partner or donor;

- Perform all other financial related duties, upon request.

- Participate in the preparation of work plans, operation plans and procurement plans and periodical reviews thereof;

- Provides support in the creation of projects in ERP, draft/entry of project budgets, draft required budget revisions, revision of project award and project status, determination of unutilized funds, support with operational and financial closure of projects, if necessary;

Provide operations support to the Project, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Ensure that UNDP procurement rules are followed during procurement activities that are carried out by the project and maintain responsibility for the inventory of the project assets;

- Organization of procurement processes including preparation of RFQs, ITBs or RFPs documents, receipt of quotations, bids or proposals, their preliminary evaluation, note-to-files and justifications in cooperation with the UNDP Operations Unit.

- Coordination of surveys, DSA, travel agencies, organization of common services and other administrative surveys;

- Prepare and timely submit travel documents in accordance with UNDP requirements;

- Support with protocol matters, registration of staff, coordination with national partners on space and other administrative matters;

- Compile, organize and file information and documents for reference and use by team members.

- Preparation of documents set for vendor creation;

- Ensure proper control of the supporting documents for payments;

- Prepare and timely submit payment requests with proper support documentation to the UNDP Country Office;

- Provide financial monitoring over Project commitments and expenditures and assist the Project Manager in assuring proper Project delivery;

- Keep regular contact with Project experts and consultants to inform them about the Joint Project details and changes;

- Control the usage and proper accounting of non-expendable equipment (record keeping, drawing up regular inventories), inventories and materials;

- Provide necessary administrative, financial and logistical support to the Project events, including among other workshops, seminars, working meetings and visits of national and international delegations (visa support, transportation, hotel accommodation etc.);

- Keep files of Project documents and expert reports and ensure general circulation of documents for knowledge management and sharing;

- Act on telephone inquiries, fax, post and e-mail transmissions, and co-ordinate appointments;

- Provide translation of documents for/to English/Russian/Belarusian as required;

- Draft Project correspondence and documents; finalize correspondence of administrative and financial nature; edit reports and other documents for correctness of form and content as required;

- Provides support to the Project Manager in preparing and reviewing the Project’s procurement reports;

- Coordinates with relevant UNDP units issuance of Purchase orders and contracts as well as supplier profile creation in ERP, prepares requisitions and follows the Purchase order processing;

- Preparation of inventory reports, if any;

- Assist in collection, preparation and submission of support documents for NPSA contracts extensions.

Facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing within the Project, related to POPP application:

- Participates in trainings for the operations/projects staff on HR, Finance, Programme and Operations, Policies and Procedures, and organizes briefings for the project staff where necessary on new internal procedures;

- When necessary, provides guidance to project staff in business processes, administrative and other requirements, and procedures;

- Sound contribution to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

- Synthesis of lessons learnt and best practices in projects.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Background

The United Nations (UN) has been working in Nepal for several decades, supporting the Government and people of Nepal in advancing sustainable development, promoting human rights, strengthening governance, and addressing humanitarian and development challenges. The UN Country Team in Nepal brings together various UN agencies, funds and programmes, each contributing its expertise and mandate towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and supporting Nepal's national development priorities.

Recognizing the importance of working together and strengthening operational efficiency, UN agencies in Nepal have come together to establish a common Driver Roster. This is a joint recruitment initiative of the United Nations agencies in Nepal to establish a common roster of qualified and suitable candidates for Driver positions. Candidates placed on the roster may be considered for future Driver vacancies across participating UN agencies in Nepal, based on their respective operational requirements and recruitment procedures.

The roster will provide participating agencies with access to a shared pool of pre-assessed candidates, while ensuring that recruitment remains transparent, competitive and based on merit.

Interested and qualified candidates are therefore invited to apply for inclusion in the common Driver Roster. Inclusion in the roster does not guarantee employment, and candidates may be considered for relevant vacancies as and when opportunities arise, subject to the specific requirements and recruitment procedures of the respective UN agencies. The selected candidate can be placed anywhere within Nepal as per the requirement.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of Project Manager / Admin and Finance Focal Point, the Driver will perform following responsibilities to support the project / country office:

1. Ensures provision of reliable and secure driving services by;

b. travel to different field locations with project staff.

c. receiving official personnel and visitors at the airport; and

d. arrangement of visa and customs formalities when required.

2. Ensures cost-savings through proper use of vehicle through accurate maintenance of daily vehicle logs, provision of inputs to preparation of the vehicle maintenance plans and reports.

3. Ensures proper day-to-day maintenance of the assigned vehicle through timely minor repairs, arrangements for major repairs, timely changes of oil, check of tires, brakes, car washing, etc.

jobs.title: Programme Analyst, RBM (Open to Tier 0, 1 & 2 applicants only)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background & orgnaizational context

The UN Volunteers programme promotes volunteerism globally and mobilizes volunteers at scale across the UN system, with a broad global presence and partnerships across UN entities, contributing to the UN’s three key mandates: peace and security, development, and humanitarian assistance.

Six UNV Regional Offices serve as the institutional anchors for representing, leading and overseeing the mobilization of UN Volunteers at country level, while also supporting volunteerism promotion and the broader objectives of the UNV Strategic Framework. Under the overall leadership of a Regional Manager, each Regional Office is accountable for generating demand for UN Volunteers, developing partnerships, and growing UNV’s portfolio across its geographical area, mobilizing UN Volunteers for UN agencies, funds and programmes in response to peace, development and humanitarian priorities.

Onsite and online volunteering are integral parts of UNV’s offer. Regional Offices provide oversight and strategic guidance to UNV Field Units, as well as to countries with non-Field Unit presence, within their respective regions. Across the six regions, and in collaboration with relevant headquarters sections, Regional Offices also generate and share knowledge, promote good practices, and strengthen cross-regional learning on volunteer mobilization and partnerships, contributing to stronger and more coherent global results.

To fulfil these functions, the Regional Offices combine a common base of leadership, portfolio management and administrative capacity with specialist expertise in volunteer mobilization, talent acquisition, results-based management and communications. They also lead the scoping and delivery of UNV’s advisory services on volunteer infrastructure. Management support and knowledge-sharing responsibilities are embedded across roles, strengthening accountability, financial sustainability, organizational effectiveness and cross-regional learning.

Position Purpose

Reporting to the Regional Manager, with technical oversight and support for global coherence from HQ/Executive Office, the Programme Analyst, RBM is responsible for providing technical support on evidence-based monitoring and planning. She/he contributes to the strategic planning process through qualitative and quantitative data analysis and integration for the purposes of UNV programming, planning, monitoring, and reporting. Moreover, she/he contributes to providing analytical content to the progress monitoring of the UNV Strategic Framework performance indicators by providing regional input to the Integrated Results and Resources Framework. She/he provides inputs to capacity development initiatives for strengthening strategic and results-focused volunteer mobilization in the region by promoting analytical approaches and the use of data and analytics through its network of Field Units, in alignment with UNV’s evolving role and new challenges. She/he strengthens management support to the Regional Office through data analytics to inform regional decision-making and performance management.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Management support, analytics and technical support to UNV’s corporate planning and reporting

- Support the Regional Manager with data and analytics, dashboards and evidence to inform decision-making, and performance measurement across the region and countries covered.

- Conduct regional intelligence and forecasting and performance analysis, monitor trends, and provide evidence-based insights to support planning and decision-making.

- In focus areas defined by the Regional Manager, conduct basic research on country context, country portfolios and sub-regions and/or synthesize country inputs to facilitate proper planning, monitoring and reporting.

- Collect, classify and analyze statistical information for the region through data identification and compilation from various relevant sources; contribute to corporate global and regional planning processes and the establishment of annual targets aligned to UNV’s Strategic Framework and regional volunteer mobilization targets.

- Ensure data quality assurance and results data integrity across regional monitoring and reporting processes, including indicator validation, verification of baselines and targets, monitoring framework and KPIs tracking and reporting, as well as periodic quality reviews of performance data submitted by Field Units.

- In close consultation with the Deputy Regional Manager, Portfolio Specialists/Analysts, and overall guidance from the Executive Office, propose critical parameters to facilitate the overall regional and country analysis, and the establishment of related planning and monitoring tools.

- Contribute to the regional planning exercise by ensuring adequate linkages of the region’s priorities with UNV’s Annual Business Plan and verifying they are duly reflected in applicable systems.

- Provide technical support to the regional planning exercise by ensuring that agreed regional priorities are appropriately aligned with UNV’s Annual Business Plan and reflected in the relevant results frameworks, indicators, targets and corporate planning systems. Make analytical observations for possible course correction and/or performance enhancement as guided by the Regional Manager.

- Support risk management and manage assigned risks; undertake analysis using UNV/UNDP’s enterprise risk framework, update RO workplan risk matrix, advise RO management on possible risk mitigation and response measures.

- Monitor regional and country performance on cost recovery and contribute to the analysis of budget utilization and financial performance, if needed, in coordination with the Administrative Associate who has primary responsibility for supporting the Regional Manager in RO budget preparation, oversight, and maintenance, including allocations to Field Units.

- Support the elaboration of the overall/regional results-oriented annual reports and other relevant materials, contributing to the visibility of key substantive results aligned with the Strategic Framework outcomes and outputs.

2. Provide capacity development and technical support to evidence-based monitoring

- Strengthen regional analytics by developing and maintaining dashboards and data visualizations that translate monitoring data into actionable insights for management;

- In consultation with the regional manager, disseminate data and analytical reports to stimulate evidence-based planning of mobilization efforts at all levels.

- Contribute to the production of high-quality briefs and other analytical notes to inform portfolio decision making, high-level engagements, and missions.

- Under the guidance of RO leadership and as required, develop a plan to improve skills and capacity for basic results-based planning, data collection and survey methods.

- Provide technical support for the collection of accurate, reliable and coherent data, achieving the right balance of qualitative and quantitative evidence.

- Guide Field Units in the proper utilization of RBM tools and technical support data integration and consolidation, and support the interpretation and use to data and evidence assess corporate results.

- Promote innovative data collection solutions, where relevant, drawing from regional/national statistics data, coordinating with other UN agency partners, and staying abreast of emerging digital/analytical methods for processing and visualizing data and evidence.

- Provide technical support to the Field Units in the region for country level reporting compliance and contribute to the maintenance of a regional data-base.

- Participate in communities of practice on data, analytics, digital approaches to RBM and monitoring, and other internal or external networks to stimulate learning and to inform further advancement of the function.

3. Contribute to performance-driven knowledge management in UNV

- Support the continuing and evolving effort of defining ‘success’ in UNV, by contributing meaningfully to the analytical process, based on indicators such as impact for the client results of volunteers deployed, effectiveness of mobilization activities, quality of pipeline, inclusive volunteerism, diversification of partnerships, etc.

- Support the regional management in scanning the regional portfolio(s) that meet established success criteria and the identification of successful practices, specifically ensuring the collection and analysis of data and evidence.

- Support the regional management in scanning practices from other regions that could help the region to address performance weaknesses or improve results achievement;

- Support the monitoring of results, pipelines, and performance related to the partnerships with UN entities in the region, and make observations that can contribute to strengthen performance in partnerships.

- Collaborate with colleagues in the RO, FUs, and HQ to promote knowledge management, as well as strengthening cross regional learning and comparative analysis.

- Contribute to the documentation of key lessons learned and provide recommendations for replication or other follow up action, where relevant.

- Collaborate with the regional communications personnel in supporting the dissemination of best practices on relevant internal knowledge networks, by monitoring or coordinating that such submissions are made by the RO.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization, as well as contributes to corporate initiatives and provides management support as required.

Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results

- Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively

- Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously

- Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility

- Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination

- Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner

- Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationship

Enable Diversity and Inclusion

- Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Project Management

- Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals

Portfolio management

- Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity.

- Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management

Working with Evidence and Data

- Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making

Developmental evaluation

- Learning and adaptation focused: ability to promote and facilitate ongoing reflection and adaptation; aimed at informing learning and portfolio related decision making.

- Being comfortable with unknown unknowns, uncertainty and understand the traits and value of working with emergence. Being able to give direction rather than destination: monitor and learn about how we understand the present and our direction towards something better (general intent) – not measuring progress and milestones towards a specific predefined goal

- Being able to carry out evaluation thinking in complex systems and adapting evaluation strategies to changing realities.

- Being inclusive, collaborative and co-creative: being able to design and implement evaluation frameworks with the variety of stakeholders and beneficiaries involved.

- Being flexible and able to use of a mix of methods, having a high tolerance for ambiguity and can draw on a variety of qualitative and quantitative evidence, is open to unorthodox types of evidence.

- Ability to set up the structures, conditions, rituals to create a culture for curiosity, reflection and learning and promote evaluation results and insights from a learning perspective.

- Understand key principles of systems and complexity theory.

Data collection

- Being skilled in Data Sorting, Data Cleaning, Survey Administration, Presentation and Reporting including collection of Real-Time Data (e.g. mobile data, satellite data, sensor data)

Solutions mapping

- Ability to engage and build rapport with vulnerable communities and get consent, facilitate participatory processes and navigate intricate power relations and cultural dynamics.

- Having the sensitivity and ability to identify grassroots solutions, capacities, assets, coping strategies that impacted communities have developed or used to address (emerging) development challenges.

- Being able to understand these solutions from a people's perspective and learn about the conditions that enable or prevent communities from developing such grassroots solutions or coping mechanisms.

- Understand how solutions and needs are paired, and how grassroots solutions can be used as an entry point to identify unaddressed or unmet development challenges and how to use these insights to inform policy design.

- Ability to reverse engineer solutions, understanding what aspects (artefactual, principles, conditions, configuration) can be scaled and how, being able to assess their potential to be transferred to other domains, regions or contexts and build a case for that.

- Ability to appreciate and integrate various sources of knowledge (academic, experiential, observational, traditional, indigenous) in problem solving processes. Set up structures and processes to collect ideas, solutions and facilitate matchmaking between supply and demand of solutions.

System Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced degree in social sciences, in economics, business administration, statistics, social sciences or related fields.

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

- Professional certificates in M&E or RBM is an asset

Experience:

- A minimum of 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant professional experience in in data analysis and monitoring, statistical methods, and programme management and implementation.

- Experience in working with monitoring and evaluation of projects/programmes, including lessons learned.

- Technical knowledge and application of results-based management

- Experience in reviewing or drafting project reports or supporting evaluations is desirable

- Experience in developing and operationalizing RBM and programme quality assurance procedures and systems is desirable.

- Demonstrated experience in data analysis and statistical methods, including proficiency in various data monitoring and/or statistical software is desired.

- Working experience in the United Nations is an asset

Language

Fluency in English and Arabic

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background and Organizational Context

UNDP has been a key development partner of the Surinamese Government and its people since 1994. UNDP has a strong track record and comparative advantage to support the achievement of national priorities and United Nations Multi-Country Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNMSDCF). It is one of the leading United Nations agencies present in Suriname in terms of programmatic scope, partnerships and financial footprint. The advantage of UNDP is illustrated by the achievements during the program cycle 2022-2026, which supported the priorities around democratic governance, sustainable development and climate action. The Country Program 2027-2031 will focus on supporting Suriname around two strategic programme areas: (a) democratic governance for inclusive transformation; and (b) resilience and environmental protection.

UNDP’s support to the Democratic Governance for Inclusive Transformation will include four interlinked priorities: a) electoral support; b) decentralization and local governance; c) revenue governance and public financial management; and d) digitalization and innovation. In addition, UNDP Suriname will continue as the funding recipient of the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM) Suriname and facilitates the CCM Secretariat. Other programmatic priorities may be included in consultation with the development partners and stakeholders in Suriname. In its interventions, UNDP prioritizes participation of all, including women, youth, and ITPs as a way to increase institutional effectiveness and improve transparency, accountability, and inclusion in public decision-making.

Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative/Head of Office, the Programme Analyst (Effective Governance and Inclusive Transformation) is responsible for managing and further expanding the programme portfolio and creating synergies, complementarities and linkages with the resilience and environment protection work of UNDP, applying a portfolio approach.

Specifically, the role includes executing and expanding current projects, building a pipeline of new initiatives that are aligned with Suriname’s national priorities, and UNDP’s policies, programmatic and operational offer globally and in the region. Importantly, the incumbent will be responsible for maintaining and expanding UNDP’s partnerships with the Government, bilateral donors, UN agencies, vertical funds (GEF, GCF, others), the EU, IFIs and other partner organizations.

The incumbent will support the senior management of the UNDP Suriname in the design and execution of thematic and sectoral strategies, knowledge management, partnerships, and support the implementation of other strategic initiatives.

The Programme Programme Analyst (Effective Governance and Inclusive Transformation) will supervise the Programme Associate and be a part of a multidisciplinary team working closely with other thematic portfolio and the Operations team at UNDP Suriname, the Regional Bureau for LAC, the Regional Hub in Panama and the technical and operational teams across UNDP.

Position Purpose

Under the guidance and direct supervision of the Resident Representative (RR), Deputy Resident Representative (DRR) the Programme Analyst is responsible for management of UNDP programme within the thematic/sectoral areas assigned. The Programme Analyst analyzes political, social and economic trends; leads formulation, management and evaluation of programme activities within his/her portfolio; and provides policy advice services.

The Programme Analyst supervises and leads the Programme Associate and coordinates activities of the project’s staff. The Programme Analyst works in close collaboration with the Programme and Operations teams in the CO, programme staff in other UN Agencies, UNDP staff in HQs and Regional Hubs, technical advisors/experts, external specialists, government officials and partners, donors, and civil society to ensure successful implementation of the UNDP programme.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Key Duties and Accountabilities

1. Contribute to formulation and Implementation of UNDP Programme Strategies and policies

- Analyze socio-political, governance, and social development trends and identify areas for UNDP support.

- Lead the development and execution of thematic strategies on governance, poverty reduction, social services, and SDG integration.

- Provide technical input to national planning processes (e.g., CCA, UNMSDCF, CPD).

- Promote inclusive and gender-sensitive approaches in programme design and delivery.

2. Ensure effective management of the CO programme within the assigned thematic/sector areas focusing on quality assurance and risk management from formulation to implementation of the country programme

- Design and formulate programme/project proposals, ensuring alignment with national development goals and UNDP priorities.

- Apply RBM tools and manage project implementation, financials, and reporting.

- Ensure programme results and indicators are met in a timely and efficient manner.

- Organize and support evaluations, audits, and strategic reviews.

3. Build strategic partnerships and resource mobilization

- Develop and strengthen partnerships with government, UN agencies, donors, NGOs, civil society, and the private sector.

- Identify funding opportunities and contribute to the office’s resource mobilization strategy.

- Contribute to joint programming and inter-agency collaboration, especially around social development and governance reform.

4. Policy Advisory Services and Knowledge Management

- Provide policy advice to government counterparts in governance, poverty alleviation, and inclusive development, with a particular focus on the Indigenous and Tribal communities, youth, women and other groups.

- Facilitate the development of evidence-based policies and institutional reforms related to governance and inclusive transformation.

- Document and disseminate best practices, lessons learned, and knowledge products.

- Foster internal and external knowledge sharing and innovation, including through UNDP Communities of Practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Supervise and manage Programme Associate

Requirements:

Education

Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Economics, Public Administration, Business Administration, Law, Political, Social Sciences, Environmental or Development Studies, or any other related field is required. Or

A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience, Knowledge, and Skills

- A minimum of 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in programme management, policy analysis, and stakeholder engagement is required.

- Experience working with government institutions, civil society, vulnerable groups, including Indigenous and Tribal Peoples (ITPs) and People with Disabilities (PWDs), and international development partners is required.

- Demonstrated experience in Democratic Governance and Inclusive Transformation related focus area is required.

- Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc), database packages, and web-based management systems such as ERP is required.

- Experience of leading and supervising multidisciplinary teams is required.

- Experience in programme management and policy development is desired.

- Experience in design, implementation and/or evaluation of development projects is desired.

- Experience and knowledge of UN/DP’s programming, including CPDs, CCAs, MSDCF, and various UN funding mechanisms is desired.

- Familiarity with UN/UNDP systems, procedures, and programming frameworks is an asset.

- Experience in working with multidisciplinary issues such as Governance, Climate Change, Local Development, Social Inclusion, Economic Transformation, Gender, Youth, Digitalization (is desired) or other development related field is a strong asset.

- Working experience with UNDP or other UN or other regional/global organization is desired.

Language requirement

- Fluency in Dutch and English is required

- In close cooperation with the Talent Acquisition Analyst, support the roll out of talent acquisition actions, as designated.

- In close cooperation with the RBM Analyst, propose actions in response to Volunteer Reporting Application (VRA) analysis and keep track of their implementation in the assigned countries, as needed.

- Support facilitation training and capacity development events for UN Volunteers in the assigned countries, as needed.

- Support the mobilization of UN Volunteers across all modalities, including in Field Unit countries with high volumes, as needed.

- Act as focal point for the RO to strategically coordinate fully funded calls for volunteer assignment proposals in the region, as designated.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The UNDP Peace and Stabilization Programme Team, through the recently concluded camp transformation project, conducted consultations with various stakeholders including the Joint Peace Mechanisms, particularly the Task Force on Decommissioned Combatants and their Communities (TFDCC), and has identified the following needs for future programming: (a) need for a consolidated database and management system to inform, manage and document socio-economic services for DCs and their communities; (b) need to align case management work and service delivery within the mechanisms and timeline of the CAB; and (c) support delivery of socio-economic interventions for DCs, their families and communities.

To ensure continuity in the efforts and programmes implemented in the past years, the UNDP has collaborated with The World Bank (WB) to co-develop the Project “Unifying Pathways, Linkages and Inclusive Facilitation of Transformative Services for Decommissioned Combatants (UPLIFT DC),” a project to support the government’s initiatives to help transition the former combatants in BARMM. The Project will be funded by the multi-donor trust fund, the Bangsamoro Normalization Trust Fund, managed by The World Bank. The project objectives are as follows: (a) to strengthen information and case management for the decommissioning of MILF combatants, to enable more coordinated service provision and better monitoring and (b) to strengthen the livelihoods and wellbeing of Decommissioned Combatants (DCs) and their families through the provision of targeted services and support.

There will be three (3) components of the project namely:

- Component 1: Establishment and operationalization of an Information, Advisory, and Referral Services (IARS) System

- Component 2: Strengthening of social case management system and capacity building for social workers and parasocial workers

- Component 3: Delivery of socio-economic services to selected male and female Decommissioned Combatants

To ensure that the interventions are appropriate, UNDP is now seeking to recruit an IT Analyst who is qualified to support the Project Manager and the Peace and Stabilization Programme Team to operationalise the Information, Advisory and Referral Services (IARS) system by localising, configuring, deploying, and administering the Decommissioning, Reintegration and Assistance Management (DREAM) platform, which will be customized and deployed for Project UPLIFT. This will serve as a central mechanism for case management, service coordination, and monitoring of support to decommissioned combatants.

The IT Analyst is expected to report to the Project Manager. The position holder also demonstrates a client- oriented approach, tact, and ability to work with people of different national and cultural backgrounds. Moreover, the IT Analyst works closely with other project colleagues from the Peace & Stabilization Programme Team and with representatives from other UN Agencies, government officials, technical advisors and experts, multilateral and bilateral donors, and civil society to successfully implement the activities.

Duties and Responsibilities

The IT Analyst will be directly responsible for completing the following set of tasks within allotted, agreed-upon time frames:

- Operationalize the IARS by localizing, configuring, deploying, and administering DREAM- Management Information System (DREAM-MIS). DREAM supports the registration and profiling of participants, issuance of ID cards, service mapping, need–opportunity matching, monitoring of reintegration support (including financial disbursements and training), and robust reporting.

- Ensure compliance with data privacy and safeguards and build counterpart capacities for sustained handover and maintenance beyond the project period.

System localization, Configuration, and Deployment (IARS via DREAM‑MIS)

- Ensure DREAM-MIS meets the agreed case management workflows and referral pathways (modules, forms, user roles, dashboards).

- Support further data migration protocols from DSWD/TFDCC sources and ensure appropriate separation of biometrics and other sensitive data in line with data‑sharing agreements.

- Maintain and ensure reporting dashboards are aligned to the Project Results Framework and partner reporting requirements.

- Provide technical assistance in usability testing and roll out phase of DREAM-MIS to ensure platform readiness.

- Ensure hardware and software platforms meet the UNDP corporate standards and the key business processes.

- Deliver technical advisory services on ICT asset lifecycle management, including maintenance planning, performance optimization, and hardware acquisition in accordance with organizational standards and specifications”.

- Ensure that asset management responsibilities are clearly covered within the scope.

- Coordinate implementation of corporate UNDP systems.

Ensure System Administration, Security, and Quality Assurance

- Contribute to the user manuals and training materials for DREAM-MIS and conduct training and provide post-training technical support.

- Administer role‑based access (including decentralized permissions), manage user provisioning and deprovisioning, and maintain audit logs.

- Oversee the service desk process, including ticket intake, classification, prioritization, and updates. Coordinate with the vendor or technical support team for issue resolution and required adjustments, provide replication steps, and validate fixes as needed.

- Maintain technical documentation (configuration notes, SOPs, admin runbooks, data dictionaries, Application Programming Interface specifications.

- Ensure interoperability with national systems such as those of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) and BARMM institutions.

- Establish UNDP and counterpart’s data protection protocols access controls, and system documentation to ensure long-term sustainability.

- Support the gradual transfer of ownership and technical capacity to relevant national agencies, enabling full handover and independent management of the system post-project.

- Conduct regular audits to identify areas for improvement and ensure the systems are up-to-date with the latest security patches and features.

- Develop long-term sustainability and maintenance plans to ensure the continued operation and improvement of the systems.

Ensures efficient networks administration, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Monitoring of the computing resources to provide a stable and responsive environment.

- Operation of network utility procedures defining network users and security attributes establishing directories, menus and drive-mappings, configuring network printers and providing user access.

- Monitoring of backup and restoration procedures for both server and local drives.

- Monitoring of network traffic, including LAN and internet connectivity, to ensure alignment with UNDP requirement.

- Provision of technical advice on network administration to other agencies as required.

Ensures facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing in the CO focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Organization and facilitation of trainings for the programme, project personnel;

- Synthesis of Lessons Learnt and Best Practices;

- Sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the overall guidance of the Team Leader of the Peace and Stabilization Programme Team and/or his designated deputy as well as with the Head of the Cotabato Office, and under the direct supervision of the Project Manager of UPLIFT DC, the IT Analyst will be tasked to deliver distinct outputs of the project, to ensure quality implementation. The IT Analyst will work closely with the project team, the Peace and Stabilization Programme Team, and UNDP CO teams and project stakeholders, particularly the Joint Peace Mechanisms and local authorities within the BARMM and its adjacent provinces, particularly Lanao.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction and Strategy

- Systems Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business management

- Digital Awareness and Literacy Ability and inclination to rapidly adopt new technologies, either through skillfully grasping their usage or through understanding their impact and empowering others to use them as needed. Knowledge of the usage of digital technologies and emerging trends.

- Working with Evidence and Data Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making.

- Risk Management Identify and organize action around mitigating and proactively managing risks.

- Customer Satisfaction/Client Management Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs. Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Administration & Operations

- Events management (including retreats, meetings, workshops) Ability to manage events, including identification of venue, accommodation, logistics, catering, transportation, and cash disbursements, etc.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering, or other related field is required. OR;

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) the areas mentioned above in combination with additional two (2) years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Applicants with a Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.

- Applicants with a Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of relevant professional experience in IT management and web-based information management.

Desirable skills:

- At least 2 years working experience, including development and implementation of ICT strategies, management of ICT services, hardware and software platforms, telecommunications facilities.

- At least 2 years network and administration experience.

- At least 2 years of relevant work experience in system administration, configuration, and user support for multi‑stakeholder platforms; familiarity with role‑based access and data privacy controls.

- At least 2 years experience in web based management information system.

- Experience using standard software applications Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook.

- At least 2 years experience with Government or Social Sector MIS.

- At least 2 years of experience in working with the joint peace mechanisms and other key stakeholders involved in the peace processes in the BARMM.

- Previous experience in International Organizations, such as the UN.

- At least 2 years of experience of working with national/local government agencies, development partners and civil society.

Required language(s):

- Fluency in English and Filipino is required.

Professional Certificates

- Cisco Certified Network Engineer (CCNE) and Microsoft Certified Systems.

- Engineer (MCSE) would be an asset.

- Certificate in any of the following cybersecurity, data protection/privacy, cloud systems (Azure/AWS), database administration would be an asset

Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality,

and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. Learn more at undp.org or follow at @UNDP.

Indonesia showed strong preparedness in rolling out its COVID-19 vaccination programme, and this experience helped it take an active role globally. During the rollout, the Ministry of Health (MoH) adopted a “One Health Data” (Satu Data Kesehatan) approach to monitor and digitise the vaccination process. It worked with the Ministry of Communication and Informatics (now Komdigi) on registration (PeduliLindungi, now SATUSEHAT Mobile), with UNDP on supply chain management of vaccines and related logistics (SMILE), and with BPJS Kesehatan, the National Health Insurance Agency, on the individual registry of vaccinated people (P-Care). As of 1 February 2023, the MoH had managed distribution data for 454.4 million doses of COVID-19 vaccine, from the provincial level down to more than 12,000 health facilities.

Building on this experience, the Directorate of Immunization applied the same integrated approach to routine immunization by linking SMILE with the ASIK system. Several MoH directorates now work closely with UNDP to improve data visibility between vaccine logistics and immunization beneficiaries. To date, more than one billion vaccine doses have been distributed and tracked through SMILE.

Reliable medical and laboratory logistics are also critical for timely disease detection and treatment, hence supply chain management for non-vaccine health products has become a priority of the MoH’s health transformation agenda. Under Minister of Health Decree No. HK.01.07/MENKES/1568/2024, SMILE was formally established as part of the SATUSEHAT Platform, operating as SATUSEHAT Logistik–SMILE. It has since expanded to track commodities for tuberculosis, malaria, HIV and rabies (including anti-rabies vaccine and serum), as well as to support medical waste management. In 2026, SMILE is being extended to non-ATM essential medicines and now supports the national Free Medical Check-up Programme (Cek Kesehatan Gratis/CKG), in which health offices record their stock of medical consumables and laboratory reagents (BMHP) in SMILE. SMILE’s integration with the programme information systems for HIV (SIHA), tuberculosis (SITB) and malaria (SISMAL) was launched in August 2025 and completed in 2026. Through SMILE, UNDP has helped the MoH plan distribution, anticipate stock-outs, reduce drug and vaccine wastage from expiry, and track the disposal of drugs and vaccines transparently and in real time at every level. However, gaps in health logistics and inequities between regions remain.

Under the overall guidance of the Project Analyst the Project Associate for Regional Papua, Papua Barat, Maluku & Maluku Utara provides project support services in ensuring regional coordinator under his/her supervision prepare regular data reporting on supply-chain management for medical commodities especially commodities for HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria (ATM) programmes, vaccines and health care waste and apply the monitoring framework as set up in the project document, in line with prevailing internal monitoring guidelines and ensure reporting arrangements are in place and are being implemented to ensure that the reporting requirements are met in a timely manner.
