Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP is the leading United Nations organization fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. The Fiji multi-country office covers ten countries including Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, Kiribati, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Nauru, Palau, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu as well as provides support to regional initiatives.

UNDP in the Pacific has developed its multi-country programme document (MCPD, 2023-2027) to guide its interventions in the next five years in full alignment and directly to contribute to the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF, 2023–27). The Office covers 10 countries in the Pacific with an extensive portfolio which has grown over time. The UNSDCF and UNDP MCPD are designed in full alignment with the 2030 agenda, Samoa Pathway, and 2050 Blue Content Strategy, which is endorsed by the Pacific Island Countries (PICs) among others. The UNDP Pacific Office next five-year plan strategic priorities are encapsulated under three outcome areas: (i) Planet, (ii) Prosperity, and (iii) Peace. Following a strategic review process which was completed in June 2022, UNDP Pacific office structure is aligned to the emerging priorities of the office. In this regard, the programme portfolio will include mutually reinforcing work streams crafted around two clusters (i) Resilience and Climate Change; and ii) Inclusive growth and Effective governance, supported by a policy and innovation team, Operations team, Management and Oversight team that provides strategic guidance on results Management and compliance entrusted with the corporate alignment, programme finance management and quality assurance, and strategic communications team that provides knowledge management and communication support to all programme interventions.

Within the Pacific Office Multi-Country Office (MCO), the Operations Team provides programme with backbone support and services related to finance, procurement, human resources, digital services, travel, and logistics, as well as common services and CO transactions support. The team further provides demand driven Common services to the UN agencies (per agreed procedures). In addition, the team will provide administrative support to UNDP Staff including project personnel on areas such as protocol, visa facilitation, travel, and others.

In Tonga, the MCO has several projects for which the Area Programme Specialist provides programmatic leadership and liaison to the projects and the partners in the country, including the Government of Tonga. There is a Joint Presence Office (JPO) which is collectively occupied by UN Agencies/Entities in Tonga. Administrative management of the JPO will be led by UNDP.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of the Area Programme Specialist, the Administrative and Common Premises Associate will provide day-to-day administrative support to the Area Programme Specialist and support with the management, financial oversight, and coordination of common premises and services in Tonga, ensuring effective and compliant operations across participating UN agencies. The scope of work is outlined below:

1) Provide appropriate and required administrative and logistical services to the Country Office.

- Serve as custodian for management of office stationery supplies, including maintenance of stock list of stationery, distribution of stationery as required by staff, and keeping a log of distribution.

- Serve as the custodian for pre-positioned emergency items ensuring that all pre-positioned items are accessible, secured, and within expiry dates.

- Provide support to procurement processes, including preparation of micro canvassing documents, and market research, receiving goods.

- Organize shipments and customs clearance arrangements.

- Prepare documents/documentation for UNDP shipments (received/sent) and follow-up actions.

- Arrange travel and hotel reservations and prepare travel authorizations.

- Provide support to staff members and their dependents by processing requests for visas, identity cards, and other documents in accordance with requirements of the United Nations and national government. When requested, collect information for DSA, travel agencies, and other administrative surveys.

- Arrange vehicle transportation, regular vehicle maintenance, and insurance for corporate visitors.

- Follow up on deadlines, commitments made, actions taken, and coordination of collection and submission of the reports to Area Programme Specialist.

- Maintain contacts with visitors and staff, arrange appointments and meetings, and when needed, take minutes, act as an interpreter and/or translate simple correspondence.

- Support in compiling and preparing briefing and presentation materials, speeches, background information and documentation for meetings and missions.

2) Provide support for assets management.

- Maintain records on attractive items, assets and ensure tagging is in place.

- Regular checks on attractive items and assets, including that insurance was in place.

3) Provide support for effective administrative and financial control in the Tonga Office.

- Support research and compilation of statistical data from internal and external sources.

- Prepare statistical charts, tables, and reports as requested.

- Review and support travel authorizations, documentation, and payments.

4) Management of Common Premises and Services.

- Ensure effective and efficient provision of administrative support services of the Tonga JPO, focusing on achievement of the following results.

- Support the overall day-to-day management of the premises and services for a functional, safe and hygienic work environment to ensure non-interruptible working condition for all personnel located in UN House.

- Coordinate services including utilities and maintenance; cleaning and security; office space allocation.

- Manage cost-sharing and agency billing.

- Act as focal point for facility management and service providers.

- Maintain SOPs for common premises operations.

- Alert Area Programme Specialist and Operations Manager in advance on potential problems.

5) Support knowledge building and sharing.

- Help organize and participate in training for the operations/projects staff on administration and common premises.

- Provide sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangements

- The Admin and Common Premises Associate will report to the Area Programme Specialist.

- The Admin and Common Premises Associate will work in close collaboration with the Operations team of the UNDP Pacific Office in Fiji, as well as the UN Agencies/Enties in Tonga and the UNDP projects based in Tonga.

- The Admin and Common Premises Associate will provide secretariat services to the local Tonga OMT.

Provide inputs into the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach / Approche Tiers

Conformément à l'engagement pris de préserver les capacités et de soutenir le personnel déjà en poste au sein de l'Organisation, la majorité des postes vacants au PNUD, au FENU et au programme VNU sont publiés selon un processus de candidature à plusieurs niveaux, dans le cadre duquel :

- Niveau 0 : Personnel international du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA), dont les postes seront supprimés, ou dont les contrats seront résiliés ou non renouvelés en 2026

- Niveau 1 : Autre personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA)

- Niveau 2 : Personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat temporaire (TA), personnel sous contrat PSA régulier, et Volontaires des Nations Unies Experts et Spécialistes

- Niveau 3 ou aucun niveau indiqué : Tous les autres types de contrat du PNUD/FENU/VNU et d'autres agences, ainsi que les candidats externes

Veuillez prendre note du ou des niveaux indiqués dans l'intitulé du poste vacant, le cas échéant, et vous assurer que vous remplissez les conditions requises pour postuler.

Background

Le Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement (PNUD) est le réseau mondial de développement des Nations Unies, qui milite pour le changement et connecte les pays aux connaissances, à l'expérience et aux ressources pour aider les gens à construire une vie meilleure. Nous sommes sur le terrain dans 170 pays et territoires, travaillant avec les gouvernements et les citoyens sur leurs propres solutions aux défis de développement mondiaux et nationaux pour aider à autonomiser des vies et à construire des nations résilientes.

Au Burundi, le PNUD a été identifié comme Récipiendaire principal (RP) intérimaire pour les programmes du Fonds mondial de lutte contre le sida, la tuberculose et le paludisme (FM) à partir du 1er janvier 2021. Depuis lors, le PNUD, en collaboration avec le ministère de la Santé (MSP) et ses partenaires, a géré trois subventions, dont la subvention actuelle, Cycle de subvention 7 (CS) qui prendra fin le 31 décembre 2026. Une nouvelle subvention, CS8, de trois ans débutera en 2027. Les volets pris en charge par le PNUD couvrent le VIH, la tuberculose et le paludisme, ainsi que des interventions prioritaires visant le renforcement des systèmes de santé et communautaires et la préparation et la réponse aux pandémies. Le PNUD collabore également avec l'Unité de gestion et d’appui au développement sanitaire (UGADS) au ministère de la Santé — l'autre RP— pour mener des interventions conjointes de renforcement des systèmes de santé et communautaires.

Pour gérer ses projets financés par le FM, le PNUD Burundi a mis en place une unité de gestion de programme (UGP), dirigée par un Coordinateur de programme. Cette structure comprend une Spécialiste Programme/MEAL supervisant les volets intégrés VIH, tuberculose et paludisme. Afin de garantir une mise en œuvre techniquement rigoureuse et de qualité du volet paludisme, le PNUD Burundi a créé le poste de Specialiste de Programme Paludisme. Le paludisme demeurant l'une des premières causes de morbidité et de mortalité au Burundi, ce poste s'inscrit dans le cadre du plan stratégique national de lutte contre le paludisme et de la stratégie d'intégration du système de santé, et répond aux évolutions stratégiques de la gestion des subventions du FM, qui privilégient l'intégration entre les composantes de lutte contre les maladies.

Duties and Responsibilities

Le/La Specialiste de Programme Paludisme exerce ses fonctions sous la supervision de la Spécialiste Programme/MEAL, conformément aux règles, politiques et procédures du PNUD, aux accords de subvention et aux accords de siège avec le FM. Le poste apporte à l'UGP un leadership technique et programmatique national dédié à la composante paludisme de la subvention GC8 du Fonds mondial pour le Burundi. Le/la titulaire traduit les orientations stratégiques en plans opérationnels cohérents, veille à l'intégration et à la complémentarité avec les composantes VIH et TB, anticipe les goulots d'étranglement – notamment liés aux campagnes de masse, à la disponibilité des intrants et aux épidémies – et organise la réponse collective de l'équipe de projet. Il/elle constitue un point de convergence entre la direction de l'UGP, les fonctions Programme/MEAL, GAS, Finances, Achats et Logistique, et les partenaires nationaux et techniques. Il/elle renforce la cohérence des interventions, la qualité de la planification, la maîtrise des interdépendances programme–approvisionnement–finance–données, l'alerte précoce sur les risques et la redevabilité envers le FM, le Gouvernement, l'Instance de coordination nationale (ICN) et les populations bénéficiaires.

Le PNUD adopte une approche de portefeuille afin de répondre à l’évolution des besoins de l’organisation et de tirer parti des liens entre les interventions pour atteindre ses objectifs stratégiques. En conséquence, le personnel du PNUD est appelé à travailler de manière transversale entre les unités, fonctions, équipes et projets, au sein d’équipes multidisciplinaires, afin de renforcer et de faciliter la collaboration horizontale.

IV. Principales fonctions et responsabilités

Sous la supervision directe de la Spécialiste Programme/MEAL, et en étroite collaboration avec le Coordinateur du programme, le/la titulaire exerce les responsabilités suivantes :

4.1) Assure la gestion efficace et le contrôle qualité du programme de lutte contre le paludisme financé par le Fonds mondial :

 Assurer la gestion opérationnelle de la composante paludisme de la subvention – planification, lancement et suivi des activités – conformément aux règles et procédures du PNUD et aux exigences du FM ;

 Assurer le suivi programmatique et financier des activités, en collaboration avec les équipes Finances, Achats et Suivi-Évaluation, et appuyer la Spécialiste Programme/MEAL dans l'identification de solutions aux goulots d'étranglement programmatiques et financiers ;

 Coordonner la mise en œuvre de la subvention paludisme avec les acteurs concernés, notamment les sous-récipiendaires (SR), les agences des Nations Unies et les autres partenaires de la lutte contre le paludisme ;

 Consolider, en coordination avec les équipes Finances et Achats, les rapports trimestriels, semestriels et annuels destinés au FM (dont les rapports PU/DR) et veiller à la qualité des données programmatiques ;

 Appuyer le ministère de la Santé dans l'opérationnalisation de la plateforme DHIS2 et la qualité des données paludisme, en étroite collaboration avec le/la Specialiste de Programme Intégré VIH/TB ;

 Effectuer des missions de supervision et de vérification sur le terrain afin de contrôler la qualité des services et la conformité des activités mises en œuvre par les SR ;

 Veiller à la mise à jour trimestrielle du module de gestion de programme dans Quantum.

4.2) Assure le leadership programmatique et l'orientation stratégique du programme paludisme :

 Diriger la traduction des orientations de la subvention GC8 paludisme en stratégies opérationnelles, plans de travail, budgets, calendriers, cadres de résultats et dispositifs de suivi cohérents ;

 Conseiller la direction de l'UGP sur les choix programmatiques, les priorités, les arbitrages et les mesures correctives nécessaires à l'atteinte des cibles de la subvention, à travers des notes stratégiques et dossiers de décision ;

 Analyser les politiques, stratégies, directives techniques et données épidémiologiques nationales relatives au paludisme, et proposer leur prise en compte dans la programmation du PNUD ;

 Appuyer la planification et le suivi des interventions clés : prévention par les moustiquaires imprégnées (campagnes de masse et distribution de routine), pulvérisation intradomiciliaire, traitement préventif intermittent chez la femme enceinte, diagnostic et traitement des cas aux niveaux des formations sanitaires et communautaire, surveillance et riposte aux épidémies ;

 Veiller à l'alignement des interventions sur le plan stratégique national de lutte contre le paludisme, les normes du ministère de la Santé, les engagements de la subvention et les principes de gestion axée sur les résultats, ainsi qu'à leur complémentarité avec les composantes VIH et TB ;

 Assurer l'intégration transversale des droits humains et du genre dans la conception, la mise en œuvre et le suivi du programme, en tenant compte des besoins spécifiques des populations vulnérables (femmes enceintes, enfants de moins de cinq ans, populations déplacées et réfugiées).

4.3) Assure la coordination interfonctionnelle Programme, MEAL, GAS, Finances, Achats et Logistique :

:  Animer la coordination interfonctionnelle nécessaire à la réussite de la composante paludisme, et s'assurer que les dépendances critiques, notamment pour les campagnes de masse, sont identifiées et suivies ;

 Travailler avec les équipes GAS, Achats et Logistique sur les quantifications, prévisions, achats, assurance qualité, stockage, distribution et suivi des consommations des produits de santé (moustiquaires, tests de diagnostic rapide, antipaludiques, insecticides) aux niveaux central et des formations sanitaires ;

 Collaborer avec l'équipe Finances pour assurer la qualité des prévisions, le suivi budgétaire, l'analyse de l'absorption et le traitement rapide des écarts ;

 Collaborer avec les fonctions MEAL et données pour définir les besoins d'information, valider les analyses, suivre les résultats et orienter les décisions programmatiques ;

 Déclencher les alertes appropriées lorsque des retards, ruptures de stock, insuffisances de données, écarts financiers, situations épidémiques ou risques opérationnels menacent l'atteinte des résultats, et veiller à la traçabilité et au suivi des décisions convenues.

4.4) Assure la gestion des risques, la conformité et la redevabilité du portefeuille paludisme :

 Tenir à jour, avec les fonctions concernées, le registre des risques programmatiques, opérationnels, fiduciaires, de chaîne d'approvisionnement, de données, de sauvegardes sociales et environnementales et de fraude du portefeuille paludisme ;

 Définir et suivre les mesures de mitigation, les indicateurs d'alerte précoce, les responsables et les échéances, et escalader les risques majeurs à la direction de l'UGP ;

 Veiller au respect des accords de subvention, des politiques et procédures du PNUD, des exigences du FM et des dispositions de prévention de l'exploitation, des abus et du harcèlement sexuels ;

 Sous la direction de la Spécialiste Programme/MEAL, préparer les réponses programmatiques aux demandes du FM, du LFA, des auditeurs et des missions d'assurance, dans les délais requis ;

 Appuyer la conduite des audits, spot-checks et évaluations du programme paludisme et assurer le suivi de la mise en œuvre des recommandations, en collaboration avec le point focal audit du Bureau pays et le/la Specialiste de Programme Intégré VIH/TB.

4.5) Conseille et contribue au renforcement des capacités du PNLP et des sous-récipiendaires, et à la gestion des connaissances :

 Identifier, avec le PNLP, les SR et les équipes de l'UGP, les besoins prioritaires en renforcement des capacités, et appuyer la mise en œuvre et le suivi d'un plan de formation et de développement des capacités ;

 Appuyer les SR dans l'élaboration des plans opérationnels annuels et trimestriels et dans la mise en œuvre du plan national de suivi-évaluation du paludisme, en collaboration avec les analystes Suivi-Évaluation ;

 Appuyer le PNLP dans la décentralisation progressive de la prise en charge du paludisme dans les structures de santé publiques et parapubliques et au niveau communautaire, ainsi que dans l'élaboration des modules, manuels, guides et outils de mise en œuvre ;

 Appuyer le PNLP dans la conduite des formations, ateliers, supervisions, revues et conférences nationales ;

 Fournir un appui technique aux SR pour l'élaboration des TdR, protocoles d'études, enquêtes (dont la surveillance de l'efficacité thérapeutique et de la résistance aux insecticides) et activités de recherche opérationnelle, et en assurer le suivi ;

 Documenter et partager les leçons apprises et bonnes pratiques avec le ministère de la Santé, les SR, l'UGP et les réseaux de connaissances du PNUD, et contribuer aux rapports nationaux et régionaux sur le paludisme.

Le titulaire du poste accomplit d'autres tâches relevant de son profil fonctionnel, jugées nécessaires au bon fonctionnement du Bureau et de l'Organisation

Responsabilités de supervision et de gestion : N/A

Competencies

Noyau

Obtenir des résultats

Penser de manière innovante

Apprendre en continu

NIVEAU 3 : Créer et saisir des opportunités pour élargir ses horizons, diversifier ses expériences

Adaptez-vous avec agilité

NIVEAU 3 : Initier et promouvoir le changement de manière proactive, gérer plusieurs demandes concurrentes

Agir avec détermination NIVEAU 3 : Voir au-delà des tâches immédiates et des obstacles, et agir pour obtenir de meilleurs résultats

NIVEAU 3 : Faire preuve de sens politique, évoluer dans un environnement complexe, promouvoir la collaboration interinstitutionnelle

Compétences transversales et techniques

Domaine thématique Nom Définition

Direction et stratégie d'entreprise Pensée systémique Capacité à comprendre comment des éléments interdépendants coexistent dans un système et à apprécier l’effet d’une modification sur les autres composantes.

Numérique et innovation Analyse et visualisation des données Capacité à extraire, analyser et présenter les données pour produire des informations utiles et soutenir la décision en temps utile.

Programme 2030 : Engagement et efficacité Paludisme et systèmes de santé Connaissance des politiques, stratégies et interventions de lutte contre le paludisme (prévention, diagnostic, traitement, surveillance et riposte aux épidémies) et de renforcement des systèmes de santé résilients et pérennes.

Gestion des risques Assurance, conformité et contrôle interne Capacité à identifier, apprécier et suivre les risques ; proposer des mesures de mitigation ; préserver la traçabilité et soutenir les dispositifs d’assurance.

Gestion des affaires Gestion de portefeuille Capacité à sélectionner, hiérarchiser et piloter les programmes et projets de l’organisation, conformément à ses objectifs stratégiques et à ses capacités ; capacité à trouver un équilibre entre la mise en œuvre d’initiatives de changement et le maintien des activités courantes, tout en optimisant le retour sur investissement.

Connaissance et compréhension des principes clés de la gestion de projets, de programmes et de portefeuilles

 •

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Diplôme universitaire avancé (Master ou équivalent) en santé publique, médecine, épidémiologie, sciences de la santé, gestion de programmes/projets, politiques de santé, développement international ou domaine connexe. OU

Un diplôme universitaire de premier cycle (Licence) dans les domaines susmentionnes combiné à deux années supplémentaires d’expérience qualifiante sera dûment pris en considération en lieu et place du diplôme avancé.

Une certification en gestion de projet, suivi-évaluation, santé publique, droits humain, genre, gestion des risques ou domaine connexe constitue un atout.

Experience:

Minimum cinq (5) années d’expérience pertinente (avec un Master) ou sept (7) années (avec une Licence) dans la gestion, la coordination ou le suivi de programmes de santé publique de grande envergure est requise.

Compétences et expériences requises

Expérience en planification, suivi de la performance, coordination multipartite, analyse de données et gestion des risques ;

Capacité démontrée à produire des rapports et notes décisionnelles de haute qualité ; maîtrise des outils bureautiques et de gestion de données.

Connaissances prouvees en matière de réduction des obstacles liés aux droits humains et au genre ; connaissance du système de santé du Burundi et de son fonctionnement aux niveaux central et décentralisé ;

Expérience avec le PNLP, des sous-récipiendaires, la société civile ou des agences internationales ; connaissance de DHIS2 et d'outils numériques de suivi ; expérience des défis programmatiques dans des contextes fragiles/humanitaires ;

Connaissance prouvee des règles et procédures du PNUD ou du système des Nations Unies.

Droit de sélectionner plusieurs candidats

Le PNUD se réserve le droit de sélectionner un ou plusieurs candidats à partir de cette annonce de vacance de poste. Nous pouvons également retenir les candidatures et prendre en considération les candidats qui postulent à ce poste pour d'autres postes similaires au PNUD, au même niveau et avec une description de poste, une expérience et des exigences éducationnelles similaires.

jobs.title: Security Analysis and Operations Intern
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

- Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

CORPORATE BACKGROUND:

UNDP works in about 170 countries and territories, helping to achieve the eradication of poverty, and the reduction of inequalities and exclusion. We help countries to develop policies, leadership skills, partnering abilities, institutional capabilities and build resilience in order to sustain development results.

UNDP is working to strengthen new frameworks for development, disaster risk reduction and climate change. We support countries' efforts to achieve the new Sustainable Development Goals, which will guide global development priorities through 2030. The key 2030 Agenda principle of leaving no one behind and stamping out inequality is at the core of everything we do.

UNDP focuses on helping countries build and share solutions in three main areas:

• Sustainable development

• Democratic governance and peacebuilding

• Climate and disaster resilience

In all our activities, we encourage the protection of human rights and the empowerment of women, minorities and the poorest and most vulnerable.

INTERNSHIP OFFICE BACKGROUND:

The Bureau for Management Services (BMS) is the UNDP’s central Bureau tasked with the development of corporate strategies, policies, tools and systems in key cross-cutting management areas. The BMS supports the achievement of development results through management advice, innovative business solutions, and other corporate services. The Service Delivery Model adopted by BMS aims to provide more integrated, effective, and customer-focused services; delivering improved management services in the areas of Legal Support, Procurement Oversight, Information Management and Technology, Consolidated Transactions, Sourcing and Operations, and Security.

The UNDP Security Office (SO) is a client-oriented Centre of Excellence for Security Risk Management, focusing on high-quality, timely and effective support and advisory services, helping clients to assure an environment for safe programme delivery. The Security Office is responsible for providing effective Security Risk Management advice and support at all levels (HQ, Regional, Country Office and Project), within the overall UN Security Management System, thereby enabling security of UNDP operations, programmes, and personnel globally.

Recognizing the importance of gender equality and the empowerment of women, the disparity in access women have to career development opportunities, networks and mentors in the field of International Security, and aiming to contribute to the UNDP’s Strategy for Gender Parity, the UNDP Security Office and the Regional Security Advisor for Latin America and the Caribbean (RSA-RBLAC) team are committed to promote female talent to continuing substantial learning and professional development in a sector traditionally dominated by men.

The Security Office Intern – Security Analysis and Operations – will work within the structure of the UNDP Regional Security Advisor for Latin America and the Caribbean team, assisting in researching, monitoring and analysing the security situation in the region, contributing to maintaining security information awareness of aspects which could potentially affect the safety and security of the UNDP personnel and operations in field environments.

The UNDP RSA RBLAC internship provides an exciting opportunity for candidates interested in enhancing their understanding of: i) mandates and operations of the United Nations Development Programme in its efforts to provide support for achieving SDGs; ii) Corporate Security Risk Management Systems, specifically the UN Security Management System; iii) processes of security analysis, threat and risk identification and security management strategies in complex environments; iv) planning and implementing strategic processes and security policy.

Duties and Responsibilities

The intern will work under the overall supervision of the Regional Security Advisor in supporting the management of open source information relevant to security and assisting in the management of operations-related activities. Duties may include, but are not limited to the following:

1 Knowledge Management and Research:

• Assist in performing unclassified research of online media and other open sources of information, daily situation reports, incident reports, its collation, analysis, drafting advisories.

• Support maintaining up-to-date knowledge of events relating to the security environment;

• Assist in the coordination with UNV online volunteers, the research and collation of open media sources information, and processes for developing media monitoring and security reports and advisories for corporate clients in the Latin America and the Caribbean Region;

2 Security Operations Management:

• Assist in monitoring international security frameworks;

• Support adjusting developed information on threats and trends of security incidents to changes in the operational security environment;

• Support Emergency Response and Crisis Management situations;

• Support drafting situation and operational reports, lessons-learnt reports;

3 Security Coordination:

• Supports liaison and coordination activities with partner organisations and counterparts;

• Assist attending conferences and meetings where relevant, providing meeting minutes, outcome notes, briefings and profiles;

• Support team events and training workshop;

• Assist in performing other related duties as assigned.

Competencies

• Interest and motivation in working in an international organisation;

• Good analytical skills in gathering and consolidating data and research for practical implementation;

• Outgoing and initiative-taking person with a goal-oriented mindset;

• Communicates effectively when working in teams and independently;

• Good in organising and structuring various tasks and responsibilities;

• Displays cultural, gender, religion, race, nationality and age sensitivity and adaptability;

• Responds positively to feedback and differing points of view;

• Consistently approaches work with energy and a positive, constructive attitude;

• Attention to details;

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

• (a) Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme (such as a master’s programme, or higher) in Social Sciences, Latin American or Caribbean Studies, International Political Economy, Politics and International Relations, International Relations, Peace and Security, International Security Studies, Strategic Studies, Geopolitical Studies, Interdisciplinary studies, Military studies, Police studies, or any equivalent studies;

• (b) Be enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree programme (such as bachelor’s degree or equivalent); in Social Sciences, Latin American or Caribbean Studies, International Political Economy, Politics and International Relations, International Relations, Peace and Security, International Security Studies, Strategic Studies, Geopolitical Studies, Interdisciplinary studies, Military studies, Police studies, or any equivalent studies;

• (c) Have recently graduated with a university degree in Social Sciences, Latin American or Caribbean Studies, International Political Economy, Politics and International Relations, International Relations, Peace and Security, International Security Studies, Strategic Studies, Geopolitical Studies, Interdisciplinary studies, Military studies, Police studies, or any equivalent studies; (as defined in (a) and (b) above) and, if selected, must start the internship within one- year of graduation;

• Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional traineeship program and undertake the internship as part of this program.

Experience:

• Experience in data collection and analysis in the field of social sciences is an asset;• Proficient writing and communication skills, for a range of different audiences and media;

• Experience working collaboratively in a team structure in a multicultural environment is an asset.

IT skills:

• Knowledge and a proficient user of Microsoft Office productivity tools, including Excel;

• Knowledge of mapping, information and GIS systems and information management data bases, AI, python programming is an asset.

Language skills:

• Good communication skills, and writing capabilities in English and Spanish,

• Speaks and writes clearly, concisely and effectively;

• Knowledge of French or other UN languages is an advantage.

INTERNSHIP CONDITIONS

• Internships within the UNDP are subject to conditions the applicant must get familiar with before signing his/her internship agreement.

• Starting from January 2020 interns will receive stipends according to UNDP rules and regulations.

• Any further costs associated with the internship must be borne by the nominating institution, related institution or government, which may provide the required financial assistance to its students; or by the student, who will have to obtain financing for subsistence and make his or her arrangements for travel, accommodation and other costs.

APPLICATION PROCEDURE

The application should contain:

• Brief Cover Letter (in English) stating interest in and qualifications for the post;

• Current and complete CV in English or Spanish.

• Please group all your documents into one (1) single PDF document as the system only allows to upload maximum one document.

Candidates who are selected must submit the following documents:

• Official letter from the University confirming enrolment in a graduate-level degree programme;

• Proof of medical and life/accident insurance valid for the location in which the internship will be carried out. Selected intern must have medical and life insurance.

• UNDP only accepts interns for a minimum of 6 weeks and a maximum of 6 months.

• UNDP accepts no responsibility for costs arising from accidents and/or illness or death incurred during the internship.

• Interns are not staff members and may not represent UNDP in any official capacity.

• It is important to note that interns are responsible to arrange for their own visa and residence documents and need to plan for these well in advance.

Subsequent Employment:

The purpose of the Internship Programme is not to lead to further employment with UNDP but to complement an intern’s studies.

Therefore, there should be no expectation of employment at the end of an internship.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

Please click here to view UNDP Data Privacy Statement

jobs.title: Investigations Specialist (Investigator) (Open to all applicants).
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Office of Audit and Investigations (OAI) reports to the Administrator and is responsible for internal audit and investigations services to UNDP and its affiliated entities. It is comprised of the Audit Section and the Investigations Section. The Investigations Section (OAI/IS) is charged with conducting misconduct investigations and with compliance review of UNDP’s social and environmental policies and procedures and has sole responsibility for the conduct of all investigations within UNDP.

In its performance of misconduct investigations, OAI/IS addresses allegations of misconduct, such as fraud, theft and embezzlement, corruption, abuse of privileges and immunities, sexual exploitation and sexual abuse, workplace harassment and abuse of authority, retaliation, or other acts or omissions in conflict with the general obligations and policies that govern the conduct of UNDP staff and other personnel. OAI also investigates allegations of fraud and other financial irregularities committed by contractors, implementing partners and other third parties, deemed to be detrimental to UNDP. OAI’s capacity includes specialized SEAH, IT forensics, Artificial Intelligence (AI), data analytics, and proactive investigations units and resources.

As the provider of a professional, secure and reliable mechanism that responds to and addresses reports of possible misconduct or fraud, OAI is the sole and centralized custodian of a unique dataset of information regarding possible irregularities across UNDP’s operations. As such, OAI has a role to play in providing real-time and data-supported advice to management on wrongdoing risks, controls, lessons and mitigation strategies, and to use this information to develop intelligence-led detection, diversion and proactive investigation strategies that prevent and deter wrongdoing without relying solely on received reports.

OAI conducts misconduct investigations in accordance with the Uniform Principles and Guidelines for Investigations endorsed by the 10th Conference of International Investigators, with the UNDP Legal Framework for Addressing Non-Compliance with the United Nations Standards of Conduct, and with the OAI Investigation Guidelines.

OAI’s Investigations Section has established Units, under the supervision of Investigation Chiefs, that are comprised of (a) functionally specialized teams and (b) regionally focused misconduct investigation teams. This structure facilitates the accessibility of specialized functions to the entirety of the Investigations Section under the guidance and leadership of a manager and ensures close and rigorous oversight of investigation matters, also under the appropriate level of leadership.

The Investigation Specialist functionally reports to the Investigations Team Lead East and Southern Africa (ESA), on investigation issues, under the overall supervision of the Chief, Investigations, Unit 2.

Position Purpose

Under the supervision of the Investigations Team Lead (ESA), the primary role of the Investigation Specialist is to conduct investigations into alleged wrongdoing that falls within OAI’s mandate, as outlined in ‘Organizational Context’ above, and that relates to the East and Southern Africa region.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1.) Provision of Effective Investigations Management

· Conducts case assessments and/or investigations into allegations in accordance with UNDP policies and procedures and the OAI investigation guidelines.

· Plans investigations to ensure that all appropriate lines of inquiry are identified and investigation resources are used effectively and efficiently to factually determine the issues relevant to an investigation.

· Identifies, collects and analyses information, demonstrating an understanding of information security and confidentiality issues relevant to investigation.

· Collects, records and handles appropriate evidence, ensuring chain of custody and demonstrating knowledge of handling considerations for different types of evidence.

· Uses specialist investigation services as and when appropriate (for example, handwriting analysis, document examination and computer forensics).

· Uses investigative technologies including case management systems, analytical software, open-source intelligence tools and artificial intelligence enabled solutions to enhance investigative efficiency, accuracy and timeliness.

· Interviews witnesses showing appropriate communications skills, accurate recording and verification of testimony through the use of interpreters as required.

· Interviews subjects/suspects in accordance with generally accepted best practice procedures (in order to obtain reliable information, while affording due process).

· Undertakes frequent, and at times extended, missions to UNDP offices worldwide, including areas with hazardous working conditions.

· Ensures that case records, databases, and documentation for matters under the Investigator’s responsibility are accurate, complete, and up to date, supporting institutional accountability and auditability.

· Formulates and recommends case closure decisions, including assessments of evidentiary sufficiency and proportionality, for review and approval by the Team Lead.

· Proposes action to close matters where appropriate.

· Drafts investigation reports of a high standard, providing an objective and factual summary of the investigation, with soundly based conclusions and recommendations.

2.) Ensure Efficient Client Services

· Under the direction of the Investigations Team Lead ESA, liaises with the Office of Legal Services (OLS), the Ethics Office, the Procurement Support Office, the Social and Environmental Compliance Unit, and other relevant offices in UNDP.

· Under the direction of the Investigations Team Lead ESA, liaises with the investigation sections of other international organizations and with national anti-corruption and law enforcement agencies as appropriate.

3.) Facilitate knowledge management and other tasks

• Contributes to the ongoing development of professional practices within OAI.

• Assesses the potential for fraud and corruption in UNDP offices and operations.

• Contributes to risk assessment planning.

• Participates in the implementation of his/her personal learning and training development plan.

• Keeps him/herself abreast of the jurisprudence of the United Nations Dispute Tribunal (UNDT) and United Nations Appeals Tribunal (UNAT).

• Performs other assignments or tasks as determined by the Deputy Director and/or the Chief, Investigations, Unit 2.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: No Managerial Responsibilities

Competencies

- Core Competencies:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

The UN Volunteers programme promotes volunteerism globally and mobilizes volunteers at scale across the UN system, with a broad global presence and partnerships across UN entities, contributing to the UN’s three key mandates: peace and security, development, and humanitarian assistance.

Six UNV Regional Offices serve as the institutional anchors for representing, leading and overseeing the mobilization of UN Volunteers at country level, while also supporting volunteerism promotion and the broader objectives of the UNV Strategic Framework. Under the overall leadership of a Regional Manager, each Regional Office is accountable for generating demand for UN Volunteers, developing partnerships, and growing UNV’s portfolio across its geographical area, mobilizing UN Volunteers for UN agencies, funds and programmes in response to peace, development and humanitarian priorities.

Onsite and online volunteering are integral parts of UNV’s offer. Regional Offices provide oversight and strategic guidance to UNV Field Units, as well as to countries with non-Field Unit presence, within their respective regions. Across the six regions, and in collaboration with relevant headquarters sections, Regional Offices also generate and share knowledge, promote good practices, and strengthen cross-regional learning on volunteer mobilization and partnerships, contributing to stronger and more coherent global results.

To fulfil these functions, the Regional Offices combine a common base of leadership, portfolio management and administrative capacity with specialist expertise in volunteer mobilization, talent acquisition, results-based management and communications. They also lead the scoping and delivery of UNV’s advisory services on volunteer infrastructure. Management support and knowledge-sharing responsibilities are embedded across roles, strengthening accountability, financial sustainability, organizational effectiveness and cross-regional learning.

Scope of Work

- Support to regional partnerships building and promotion of volunteerism within the UN System

- Support in developing and implementing joint initiatives with different entities at the regional level and/or in the assigned portfolio of countries, as per respective RO workplan.

- Collect data, evidence, and examples of success on UNV’s work for use in partnership meetings and external presentations, drawing also on content from other regions.

- As guided by the supervisor, support design and drafting of UNV offer and mobilization proposals.

- In collaboration with RO colleagues (communication, RBM) engage in design and drafting of substantive and partner specific outreach materials (fact sheets, best practice, value add collection, etc.).

- Contribute to UNV’s engagement with key regional bodies for joint advocacy and visibility events/initiatives by drafting of programme and concept notes, other key communication to partners, and engage in event coordination on behalf of the RO, as needed.

- In close cooperation with the communications team, support coordination of the joint celebration of UN Thematic days with UN entities, including regional IVD (International Volunteer Day) and country level IVD, as needed.

- Support other activities that promote volunteerism in the country, as designated by the Regional Manager.

2. Support to mobilization and volunteer satisfaction across the region, including online volunteering

- Support the preparation/compilation of data/materials on the UNV offer for outreach to UN partners.

- Keep track on UN partners’ trends in the assigned countries and provide inputs for volunteer mobilization planning and outreach.

- Administer and promote online volunteering and ensure the integration of online volunteering in assigned portfolio countries and with key partners as well taking necessary operational actions as per standard operational procedures.

- Provide guidance support and inputs to Host Entities in the design and matching of OV assignments, including in the design of campaigns and supporting a positive online volunteer experience, as needed at the regional/Country level.

- In close cooperation with the Talent Acquisition Analyst, support the roll out of talent acquisition actions, as designated.

- In close cooperation with the RBM Analyst, propose actions in response to Volunteer Reporting Application (VRA) analysis and keep track of their implementation in the assigned countries, as needed.

- Support facilitation training and capacity development events for UN Volunteers in the assigned countries, as needed.

- Support the mobilization of UN Volunteers across all modalities, including in Field Unit countries with high volumes, as needed.

3. Support to Regional Office coordination and management

- Support the Regional Manager, regional management team, and portfolio managers in the coordination and implementation of regional partnership and portfolio initiatives by facilitating partner engagement, preparing proposals, briefs, correspondence, and other UNV documentation, supporting high-level meetings and missions, and contributing to planning, reporting, and information-sharing processes across the Regional Office.

- Act as focal point for the RO to strategically coordinate fully funded calls for volunteer assignment proposals in the region, as designated.

- Provide support for the preparation of missions in the region, by preparing and reviewing briefing documents and background materials, as per mission SOPs and objectives.

- Provide support and coordinate the implementation of mission follow up actions, as per mission reports.

- Support in meeting preparation with regional partners and entities and coordinate timely implementation of follow up actions. Participate on behalf of UNV in external meetings, as required.

- Coordinate procurement of goods/services for regional partnership events, as designated;

- Support external communication and internal dissemination of good practices and lessons learned, including through UNV knowledge networks, where relevant and required.

- Perform other portfolio support functions, including support to non-Field Units as well as Field Units with high volumes of candidate registration and/or UN Volunteers, as may be required.

- Assist the Portfolio Specialist/Analyst in the duty of care for volunteers, particularly in the countries without a UNV Field Unit, and with a focus on security and positive volunteer experiences.

- In the absence of the Administrative Associate, support the coordination and preparation of internal and external meetings, preparation of workplans, meeting minutes, information dissemination, mission planning, etc., as designated.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization, as well as contribution to corporate initiatives as required.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the overall guidance of the Regional Manager (RM) and the day-to-day supervision by a designated staff in the Regional Office, the Portfolio Associate supports outreach for partnership building, partnership initiatives and mobilization of volunteers, and plays a key role in coordination and management support within the Regional Office. He/she provides support to the RO outreach to field units and non-field unit countries, the mobilization of both onsite and online volunteers, and activities that generate and facilitate volunteer mobilization. The Portfolio Associate also supports the implementation of partnerships related to Online Volunteering, working closely with UN Host Entities. He/she supports the development and implementation of special programme initiatives, joint

initiatives with UN entities, and other partnerships, and contributes to UNV’s engagement with regional bodies for advocacy and visibility, as well as coordination for the implementation of joint regional events. The Portfolio Associate supports and backstops the RO portfolio management in the implementation of the RO priorities and regional work plan, while actively building and nurturing relationships with regional partners, host entities, volunteers, and other key stakeholders to enhance UNV impact for the UN System.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results

- Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

- Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

- Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

- Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

- Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

- Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

- Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Systems Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Digital Awareness and Literacy

- Ability and inclination to rapidly adopt new technologies, either through skillfully grasping their usage or through understanding their impact and empowering others to use them as needed.

Customer satisfaction/ client management

- Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs;

- Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy; Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests;

- Ability to anticipate clients' upcoming needs and concerns.

Communication

- Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience;

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Relationship management

- Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding.

Procurement management

- The ability to acquire goods, services or works from an outside external source.

Knowledge Generation

- Ability to research and turn information into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Secondary education with technical training in administration, business administration or related areas;

- University degree in business, or public administration, or related areas is desirable but is not a requirement.

Experience:

- A minimum of 6 years (with secondary education) or 3 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant work experience in administration, project support, personnel and/or business management.

Required skills:

- Experience in MS Office 365.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section:

- Experience working in web-based management/CRM systems would be an asset.

- Experience working with Salesforce Service Cloud would be an asset.

- Experience in an international or non-profit context would be an asset.

- Experience working with volunteers would be an asset.

Required Language(s):

- Fluency in English and in the local language of the duty station (Arabic).

- Proficiency in another UN official language and/or other dominant language in the region would be an asset.

Disclaimer

- Only short-listed applicants will be contacted.

- The successful candidate will hold a UNDP NPSA Contract.

jobs.description:
Enfoque por niveles

En línea con el compromiso de salvaguardar la capacidad y apoyar al personal ya existente en la Organización, la mayoría de las vacantes de PNUD/UNCDF/UNV se publican utilizando un proceso de postulación por niveles, mediante el cual:

• Nivel 0: Personal internacional del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA), cuyos puestos séran abolidos, o cuyos contratos serán rescindidos o no renovados durante el año 2026

• Nivel 1: Otro personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA)

• Nivel 2: Personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos temporales (TA), personal con contratos PSA regulares y Voluntarios Expertos y Especialistas de las Naciones Unidas

• Nivel 3 o sin nivel indicado: Todos los demás tipos de contratos del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU y de otros organismos, y demás candidatos externos

Por favor, tome nota del(los) nivel(es) indicado(s) en el título de la vacante, si corresponde, y asegúrese de cumplir con los requisitos de elegibilidad para postular.

Descripción Oficina/Unidad/Proyecto

El Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD) es el principal organismo de las Naciones Unidas dedicado a poner fin a la injusticia de la pobreza, la desigualdad y el cambio climático. El PNUD en México, apoya al gobierno para integrar el enfoque de la agenda 2030 en sus procesos y promueve la inclusión y la igualdad en el país.

El Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD) en México se encuentra en una posición estratégica para abordar los desafíos climáticos y ambientales complejos que enfrenta México. El cambio climático, la pérdida de la biodiversidad y la contaminación son las tres grandes crisis planetarias que afectan el desarrollo y el bienestar de las personas, el PNUD ofrece apoyo y asistencia técnica a los países para desarrollar, implementar y armonizar sus prioridades, planes de acción y estrategias nacionales con los compromisos y metas internacionales en temas de clima, biodiversidad, energía, químicos y residuos y la agenda oceánica.

La agenda comprende, entre otros temas, gobernanza oceánica, conservación y uso sostenible de los ecosistemas marinos y costeros, financiamiento azul, cambio climático y océanos, biodiversidad marina, contaminación, pesca sostenible, observaciones oceánicas y cooperación internacional.

El PNUD implementa el proyecto Construcción de capacidades financieras para la conservación de ecosistemas costeros y la resiliencia pesquera a nivel subnacional y nacional con el apoyo financiero de la Walton Family Foundation.

Esta posición tendrá como objetivo fortalecer la capacidad técnica, estratégica y operativa de la Dirección de la Agenda Oceánica perteneciente a la Dirección General para Temas Globales de la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores en la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores (SER), apoyando la coordinación y seguimiento de la ejecución del proyecto y su adecuada alineación institucional, esto incluye la elaboración de posiciones e insumos de alto nivel, la articulación interinstitucional y la identificación y desarrollo de oportunidades de cooperación y financiamiento. Una responsabilidad prioritaria será acompañar el proceso de elaboración e implementación de la Estrategia de Financiamiento para el Plan Oceánico Sostenible de México, en coordinación con el PNUD, la SHCP y otros actores relevantes.

Alcance del Trabajo

1.Proporcionar asistencia técnica que contribuya al diseño, desarrollo y seguimiento de proyectos e iniciativas estratégicas de la agenda oceánica

- Colaborar transformando prioridades y oportunidades de cooperación en propuestas concretas, hojas de ruta, planes de trabajo y resultados susceptibles de implementación

- Dar seguimiento al desarrollo de la Estrategia de Financiamiento para el Plan Oceánico Sostenible de México, incluyendo la coordinación con PNUD, SHCP y otros socios; la identificación de brechas y oportunidades de financiamiento; y el seguimiento de productos y acuerdos.

- Participar en la elaboración y revisión notas conceptuales, fichas técnicas, documentos de trabajo, proyectos de declaración, intervenciones, fichas ejecutivas e insumos de alto nivel sobre temas de la agenda oceánica internacional, garantizando calidad técnica, claridad, consistencia y atención al detalle.

- Apoyar a la Dirección de la Agenda Oceánica en la preparación, organización y sistematización reuniones técnicas, talleres, seminarios, eventos y grupos de trabajo, cuando sea requerido, dando seguimiento posterior a los resultados alcanzados y el seguimiento sustantivo y oportuno a los compromisos, acuerdos e iniciativas derivadas de foros.

2. Contribuir al establecimiento y fortalecimiento de alianzas estratégicas:

- Contribuir al establecimiento y fortalecimiento de alianzas estratégicas con gobiernos, organismos internacionales, instituciones financieras, fundaciones, academia y sociedad civil, particularmente aquellas que puedan traducirse en cooperación técnica, fortalecimiento de capacidades o movilización de recursos para las prioridades oceánicas, relacionadas con los objetivos y alcances del proyecto.

- Promover la vinculación del proyecto y otras iniciativas impulsadas por la SRE en la agenda oceánica, identificando oportunidades para traducir compromisos, buenas prácticas y mecanismos internacionales en acciones e iniciativas concretas.

3. Apoyar la comunicación estratégica y visibilidad de las iniciativas de la agenda oceánica

- Elaborar información clara y de alta calidad, adaptando los mensajes a distintas audiencias nacionales e internacionales.

- Preparar y proporcionar materiales de comunicación estratégica, como informes ejecutivos, presentaciones y notas de resultados, orientados a tomadores de decisión.

- Apoyar el análisis del posicionamiento institucional del proyecto entre actores estratégicos, generando insumos para fortalecer la estrategia de comunicación y difusión de resultados.

4. Apoyar la generación y el intercambio de conocimientos, así como el fortalecimiento de capacidades en el marco del proyecto.

- Participar en actividades de capacitación y organizar sesiones informativas sobre procedimientos internos para el personal del proyecto. Brindar apoyo a otras iniciativas de fortalecimiento de capacidades, incluyendo el diseño y la elaboración de herramientas, materiales para talleres o plataformas que aprovechen la inteligencia colectiva y movilicen la acción.

- Apoyar la difusión y el intercambio de datos relevantes y lecciones aprendidas, tanto a nivel de la oficina de país como a escala regional. Mantenerse al tanto de las mejores prácticas emergentes —a nivel nacional, regional e internacional— relacionadas con la labor del proyecto.

- Realizar aportes valiosos a redes de conocimiento y comunidades de práctica. Apoyar la recopilación y sistematización de los conocimientos, productos y herramientas del proyecto, así como su amplia difusión entre los socios.

Desempeñar otras funciones relacionadas con su perfil que sean necesarias para el cumplimiento de los objetivos del proyecto.

Acuerdo Institucional

El/la Asociado técnico de Gobernanza Oceánica en México estará bajo la supervisión directa del Oficial de Nacional de Ambiente, Energía y Resiliencia del PNUD México, y apoyará a la Dirección de la Agenda Oceánica. de la Dirección General para Temas Globales quien evaluará su desempeño y plan de trabajo. Estará basado/a en la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores (SRE) en la Ciudad de México.

En el cumplimiento de sus tareas y responsabilidades, la persona seleccionada deberá observar los principios de calidad de servicio del PNUD: compromiso estratégico, contenido sólido y administración impecable.
