jobs.title: Project Manager - EW4ALL Project [Open to Tier 1 & 2 applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background- Office/Unit/Project Description

Ethiopia is one of the African countries most vulnerable to climate-related hazards, including droughts, floods, landslides, heatwaves, and wildfires. These hazards significantly affect agriculture, infrastructure, health, and livelihoods. Vulnerability is heightened by poverty, gender inequality, rapid population growth, and displacement due to conflict or environmental shocks. The lack of timely, reliable, and integrated early warning information has historically hindered effective disaster preparedness and response, particularly at the sub-national and community levels.

The GCF Early Warning for All (EW4All) project aims to establish a Multi-Hazard Impact-Based Early Warning and Early Action System (MH-IB-EWEAS) in Ethiopia. The project aligns with the Climate Resilient Green Economy (CRGE) strategy, national disaster risk management policies, and Ethiopia’s commitment to global climate adaptation priorities. It seeks to improve national and sub-national capacities in disaster risk knowledge, hydro-meteorological observation, impact-based forecasting, and anticipatory action, ensuring that early warning information leads to timely and coordinated responses.

The project operates through a national Project Management Unit (PMU) within UNDP Ethiopia Country Office, supported by Responsible Parties (EDRMC, EMI, ENA, ECA, ERCS, ITU, IFRC), sub-national agencies, and community-level stakeholders. It is guided by a national EW4All Coordination Platform, chaired by EDRMC, which integrates the input of technical working groups, provincial focal points, and capacity-building programs.

Project Outputs: - Output 1: Strengthened disaster risk knowledge and data management, including a national Digital Risk Data Hub and Woreda-level risk profiling. - Output 2: Improved hydro-meteorological observation and impact-based forecasting capacities at national and sub-national levels. - Output 3: Enhanced disaster risk communication, anticipatory action, and preparedness for national, sub-national, and community stakeholders.

The project’s goal is to reduce vulnerability, increase resilience, and ensure that Ethiopia’s early warning and early action systems are robust, inclusive, and sustainable.

The Project Manager (PM) will oversee the overall planning, procurement, execution, and management of all activities related to Risk Knowledge; monitoring and forecasting; risk communication and dissemination; and disaster preparedness and response capabilities. S/he will directly work with the Responsible Parties and Stakeholders and ensures that project pillar leads are delivering their commitments.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Manager is responsible for:

Project Leadership and Oversight

- Ensure successful delivery of project outputs and results, in line with GCF and UNDP standards.

- Lead the national PMU and ensure alignment with project objectives, timelines, and budgets. Supervise and guide PMU staff, including Administrative & Finance Associate and M&E Specialist. Establish performance objectives and standards, and ensure timely and appropriate feedback, guidance and support.

- Draft and review terms of references and work specifications for all contractors’ work; monitor the work of consultants for local contractual management in coordination with the Procurement Office and Admin/Finance Officer.

Project Coordination

- Coordinate with Responsible Parties (RPs), Pillar Leads, the National EW4All Steering Committee, government agencies, and community stakeholders to ensure proper and timely implementation of activities and reporting.

- Maintain regular communications with RPs and national partners and about progress, future plans and issues of the Project. Prepare ad hoc communication materials to inform the progress of the Project, organize formal or informal briefing sessions, to inform relevant stakeholders of progress or changes in the implementation plan, emerging risks, needs for adaptive management.

- Provide inputs from the EW4All GCF initiative to relevant UN, government and multi-stakeholders coordination platforms (relevant to Climate Adaptation, Resilience, Disaster Risk Reduction, Anticipatory-Action, and humanitarian action), participate in meetings, as requested.

Project Planning and Management

- Organize and support regular Project Board meetings, ensuring timely preparation of agendas, reports, and minutes.

- Monitor project risks and technical, financial, political, operational and management situations on the ground, identify implementation bottlenecks, identify risk mitigation measures and solutions in consultation with the UNDP CO and Project Board.

- Ensure adherence to the Environmental and Social Management Plan, the Gender Action Plan, and Safeguards in project implementation.

- Develop and implement Annual Work Plans (AWPs) and monitor progress against targets.

- Oversee project budgeting, financial reporting, and compliance with UNDP and GCF procedures.

Technical Guidance and Knowledge Management

- Seek guidance from the Project Support team, and ensure technical quality of outputs and provide strategic guidance to PMU staff and implementing partners.

- Support knowledge sharing, capacity building, and national and international visibility of project outcomes.

- Ensure capturing and disseminations of lessons learnt during project implementation. Support the development of communication materials and knowledge products for national and international audiences, in close collaboration with the UNDP Communications Specialist.

- Ensure that the Project systematically builds capacities of the Government through introduction of innovation and best practices, access to knowledge and expertise and promote their application to project implementation.

- Facilitate the Project’s representation and/or participation in international knowledge networks to draw on and share best practice and lessons learned.

Monitoring, Reporting, and Adaptive Management

- Oversee project monitoring and evaluation procedures and systems throughout project activities in close collaboration with the PMU and implementing partners, ensuring accurate, timely, and high-quality outputs.

- Oversee annual progress reporting in line with UNDP and GCF requirements.

- Coordinate and prepare ad hoc thematic and substantive reports/analysis/briefs;

- Coordinate the collection and analysis of project data and ensure integration of lessons learned into project adaptation.

- Provide inputs to audit management responses; implement audit recommendations for the project.

Community Engagement and Communication

- Facilitate engagement with local communities to ensure participatory planning and implementation. Act as a window for any environmental or social grievances from local communities.

- Serve as the primary liaison for communicating project progress, emerging risks, and adaptive measures.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Concrete Output

The Project Manager will be responsible for the timely delivery of the following concrete outputs:

- Annual Work Plans and Reports: Develop, submit, and ensure implementation of the Annual Work Plan, including objectives, activities, and budgets. Prepare and submit semi-annual and annual progress reports to UNDP CO and the Project Board.

- Project Board Support: Organize at least 1-2 Project Board meetings annually; prepare agenda, background documents, presentations, and minutes. Ensure follow-up on Board decisions and action items.

- Safeguards and Compliance: Ensure compliance with UNDP Social and Environmental Standards, Gender Action Plans, and other safeguard measures. Provide inputs to audit management responses and implement recommendations for corrective actions.

- Financial and Administrative Deliverables: Oversee the preparation of quarterly financial reports, expenditure tracking, and ensure compliance with UNDP and GCF procedures. Ensure proper contractual management and timely disbursement to Responsible Parties.

- Monitoring and Evaluation: Ensure effective implementation of the project M&E plan, including tracking of indicators in the Results Framework. Support mid-term, terminal evaluations, and audits, ensuring quality data collection and participation of national and community stakeholders.

- Technical Outputs and Knowledge Products: Ensure quality delivery of all technical outputs under project Outputs 1–3, including development of the Digital Risk Data Hub, improved hydro-meteorological observation systems, and impact-based forecasts. Facilitate production of technical briefs, case studies, and lessons learned for national and international dissemination.

- Capacity Building and Knowledge Sharing: Organize at least 10 national-level workshops and technical trainings to build technical capacities across the four EW4All pillars. Support the annual inter-pillar national GCF EW4All Conference to review progress and share lessons learned.

- Community Engagement: Ensure integration of community feedback into project implementation and adaptive management processes. Act as the focal point for grievances or social/environmental issues arising during project implementation.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the supervision of the UNDP Country Office and the Project Board, and under the overall guidance of the Team Leader for the Climate Resilience and Environmental Sustainability Unit, with direct reporting responsibility to the DRM Programme Specialist, and in close collaboration with the project's Responsible Parties (EDRMC, EMI, ENA, ECA, ERCS, ITU, and IFRC) and the National EW4All Steering Committee, while receiving technical advisory support from the Project Support Team, the National Project Manager will be responsible for the overall management, coordination, and implementation of the GCF EW4All Project in Ethiopia.

The Project Manager will work closely with the Programme Management Unit, comprising an Administrative and Finance Associate and a Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Specialist. S/he will oversee the day-to-day implementation of the project, provide strategic and operational direction to ensure the timely delivery of project activities, and achieve planned outputs, targets, and results. S/he will also liaise closely with the UNDP Country Office Programme and Operations Teams and maintain effective working relationships with project donors, government.

Competencies

Core competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Development

- Knowledge Facilitation Ability to animate individuals and groups, internally and externally, and to design and facilitate activities, to share and exchange knowledge, information and ideas. Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation, contribution, and exchange.

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Partnership Management

- Relationship Management Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding

Business Management

- Project Management Ability to plan, organize, priority and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

- Communication Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

- Resource Management Ability to allocate and use resources in a strategic or tactical way in line with principles of accountability and integrity

- Results-based Management Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in disaster risk management, climate science, development studies, environmental management, meteorology or related field. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional two (2) years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree

Experience:

- Minimum 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience at the national or international level in project development, management and coordination, including results-based management, monitoring and evaluation related to early warnings, climate change, disaster risk reduction, meteorology, atmospheric science, or related fields at national and international level is required.

Required skills and competencies

- Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and web-based management systems, and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages.

Desired additional skills

- Demonstrate technical expertise and knowledge in early warning systems, risk knowledge, preparedness, and/or weather forecasting and monitoring is required.

- Proven working experience in managing complex multi-stakeholder projects.

- Ability to administer budgets, lead a team, train and work effectively with counterpart staff at all levels, and interact effectively with all teams involved in the project is required.

- Strong knowledge and familiarity with the national road map for multi-hazard early warning and early action.

- Strong writing, presentation and reporting skills is required.

- Familiarity with GCF or similar donor-funded projects.

- Experience working with UN agencies, international NGOs, or donor-funded projects.

- Proven experience in procurement, logistics, contract management, and stakeholder coordination in the context of project management.

Required Language(s) (at working level)

- Fluency in English as well as in Amharic or Tingrinia) of the duty station is required.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

jobs.title: Auxiliar Operativo de Proyecto en Conservación de ANP - Monterrey
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

El objetivo general del proyecto Sinergia+ es generar procesos de gestión que fortalezcan a la CONANP y que le permitan convertirse en una institución que planea con base en resultados, con finanzas fuertes y mecanismos de gobernanza y alianzas estratégicas eficaces, que contribuyan a incrementar la conectividad entre ecosistemas

representativos para salvaguardar su biodiversidad y equilibrio ecológico.

El proyecto Sinergia+ tiene seis resultados estratégicos: 1) Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP; 2) Gobernanza y fortalecimiento de redes de colaboración; 3) Enfoque de género y fortalecimiento de la participación ciudadana; 4) Incremento de superficie de conservación con enfoque de conectividad ecológica; 5) Conservación y recuperación de especies en riesgo; 6) Proyectos Estratégicos.

En el marco del Proyecto Sinergia+, la persona a contratar contribuirá al fortalecimiento de las acciones de conservación y manejo efectivo del Área Natural Protegida, mediante el apoyo operativo y técnico a las actividades de protección, monitoreo y restauración de los ecosistemas, así como a la atención de contingencias ambientales,

favoreciendo la conservación de los recursos naturales del ANP.

Este puesto contribuye al logro de metas del Resultado 1 “Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP”.

Alcance de Trabajo:

- Coadyubar en la atención de problemas de sanidad forestal

- Realizar recorridos de vigilancia para la detección temprana de ilícitos, incendios y enfermedades forestales, así como seguimiento a proyectos en materia de restauración forestal.

- Realizar actividades de monitoreo biológico en apoyo a la conservación.

- Realizar actividades de evaluación y monitoreo de predios con trabajos de restauración.

- Apoyo en la atención a contingencias por incendios forestales.

Acuerdo Institucional:

El o la persona contratada trabajará bajo la supervisión técnica directa de la Dirección del Parque Nacional Cumbres de Monterrey, de la Dirección Regional Noreste y Sierra Madre Oriental, así como de la Coordinación General del Proyecto Sinergia+.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos Mínimos:

- Certificado de preparatoria/Bachillerato, es requisito.

- Estudios Universitarios concluidos de primer nivel Licenciatura en: Biología, Agronomía, Ing. Ambiental, Derecho o carrera a fin, no es requisito, pero se dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Para candidatos/as con Certificado de Preparatoria (Bachillerato), se requieren 4 años de experiencia comprobable en: Proyectos de conservación y manejo de Recursos Naturales.

- Para candidatos/as con Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura, se requiere 1 año de experiencia en los temas antes mencionados.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia en elaboración de Informes técnicos.

Habilidades Deseadas:

• Conocimiento y/o experiencia en contingencias por incendios forestales.

• Conocimiento y/o experiencia en problemática de plagas y enfermedades forestales

• Conocimiento y/o experiencia en monitoreo Biológico

• Conocimiento y/o experiencia en proyectos de Restauración Forestal.

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar

jobs.title: Country Economist [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Organizational Context

UNDP has been working in India since 1951 in almost all areas of human development. Together with the Government of India and development partners, we have worked towards eradicating poverty, reducing inequalities, strengthening local governance, enhancing community resilience, protecting the environment, supporting policy initiatives and institutional reforms, and accelerating sustainable development for all.

With projects and programmes in every state and union territory in India, UNDP works with national and subnational government, and diverse development actors to deliver people-centric results, particularly for the most vulnerable and marginalized communities. As the integrator for collective action on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) within the UN system, we are committed to supporting the Government of India’s national development vision and priorities and accelerating the achievement of the SDGs for the people and the planet.

UNDP India’s new Country Programme (2023-2027) builds on our prior work and aims to provide an integrated approach to development solutions in three strategic portfolios:

- Strong, accountable and evidence-led institutions for accelerated achievement of the SDGs.

- Enhanced economic opportunities and social protection to reduce inequality, with a focus on the marginalized.

- Climate-smart solutions, sustainable ecosystems and resilient development for reduced vulnerability.

South-South cooperation, gender equality and social inclusion are promoted across the pillars. The programme is supported by a framework of renewed partnerships and blended finance solutions, strategic innovation and accelerator labs, and data and digital architecture.

Office/Unit/Project Description

The Policy Unit leads UNDP India’s research and advocacy on Global Goals and the national development agenda, with a special focus on environment and climate change, skill development, inclusive growth and strengthening systems for SDG localization.

The Economist Network of the Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific (RBAP) is one of the region’s most valuable initiatives to enhance policy support and capacity. The Country Economist plays an important role at the country but also regional and global levels in contributing to renewed development momentum in an era of turbulence and uncertainty.

Main Purpose:

The Country Economist works under the direct guidance of the Resident Representative and Deputy Resident Representative in the Country Office India, in close collaboration with programme and operations teams, and has a dotted line to the RBAP Chief Economist.

The Country Economist integrates the activities UNDP delivers in the region and ensures these contribute the greatest development impact possible. S/he makes a difference by being keenly aware of the changing development landscape, embedding a sharp strategic focus on the development interventions that matter the most, and connecting diagnostics and solutions to the politics of change and the art of delivery.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

In this respect, the Country Economist works closely with colleagues of RBAP as well as the Global Policy Network (GPN). S/he develops and maintains a professional network across development partner agencies, government institutions, the private sector, and civil society at the country level.

Summary of key functions:

- Policy support and strategic positioning at the country level particularly in preparation for the country office analysis for CPD and the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF).

- Development of at least four thematic briefs aligned with the new strategic plan.

- Advise and provide analysis to UNDP Country Office management and programme teams to strengthen foresight analytics, systems thinking and portfolio design.

- Provide technical expertise and global best practice to national and sub-national government counterparts and other partners, especially in support of the 2030 Agenda and (sub-) national development priorities, with regard to sustainable and inclusive economic policies.

- Advocate and engage with partners to support UNDP’s role and advance its mandate, when directed by the Resident Representative.

- Contribute to UNDP’s work across the Asia-Pacific region, including collaboration with RBAP’s Economist Network, sub-regional and other Country Offices, and analytical work on priority regional thematic areas.

Duties and Responsibilities:

1- Advise and provide analysis to UNDP Country Office management and programme teams to strengthen foresight and portfolio design

- Provide analysis to UNDP Country Office management with the preparation and implementation of country programmes and strategies, including the development of country programme document (CPD) and related analyses.

- Advise and support UNDP Country Office teams to develop and manage relevant thematic portfolios, such as activities to support inclusive growth and progress towards the SDGs and (sub-) national development priorities.

- Lead UNDP Country Office efforts to conceptualize and implement the Development Finance Assessment (DFA) and accompanying process and use existing financial resources more effectively and efficiently to achieve the SDGs.

- Provide analysis, research and foresight in priority thematic areas at the country level, including publication of policy briefs (and state briefs) or other analytical outputs.

- Provide analysis of economic, social and political developments at national and sub-national level.

- Support the preparation of policy briefs, background notes, speeches, talking points, presentation materials, etc., on critical development issues within the SDG framework for senior management at the country and regional levels.

- Lead the development of the National Human Development Report (HDR) at national and sub-national level and ensure that it provides added value in terms of development economic analysis, updated data, and information for policy formulation; Compile data and perform statistical analysis as required to support innovative knowledge work country strategies and activities.

- Collaborate across UNDP teams, especially to ensure linkages to the work emerging from the network of acceleration labs.

- Advise on systems thinking and support the creation of large-scale development solutions to help address complex development challenges.

- Support expansion of Country Office service offers on financing for development, including innovative financing models and country specific/sector specific studies.

2- Provide policy advice and technical expertise to (sub-) national government counterparts and other partners, especially in support of the 2030 Agenda and (sub-) national development priorities, with regard to sustainable and inclusive economic policies;

- Advise and facilitate dialogue on sustainable development issues with government officials, development partners, civil society, and the private sector, providing and sharing global experience and policy

- Provide the best global practice, policy and programming advice and support for development planning and policy formulation at the national, sub-national, and local levels, including on data for development, systems thinking and foresight exercises. Advise and support the identification and analysis of interventions that can impact multiple development goals and targets at the same time.

- Advise and support monitoring and reporting of progress related to SDGs and other national development frameworks, including to help strengthen national and local level data collection and statistical capacity.

- Guide to leverage UNDP’s regional and global programmes, to provide holistic and effective support to the country.

- Leverage support and expertise from the UNDP’s global/regional Economist networks to strengthen UNDP’s support on economic analysis and policy development for the Government and the UN Country Team.

3- Advocate and engage with partners, including to support UNDP’s role and advance its mandate, when directed by the Resident Representative and facilitate knowledge sharing

- Contribute, in close collaboration with senior management, to the development and/or strengthening of partnerships with UN agencies, IFIs, bilateral development agencies, private sector entities, and civil society.

- When delegated, represent the UNDP Country Office in relevant forums, conferences, or workshops, including presenting research or programmatic results.

- Facilitate the Resident Representative in resource mobilization and future growth strategies and contribute to the design of large-scale programme and development solutions.

- Contribute to national, regional, and global knowledge networks and communities of practice.

4- Contribute to UNDP’s work across the Asia-Pacific region, including collaboration with RBAP’s Economist Network, sub-regional and other Country Offices, and analytical work on priority regional thematic areas.

- Substantively contribute as possible to UNDP regional knowledge products and development of programming offers in regional priority areas (e.g., inequality, future of work, innovative financing, development strategies, economic governance, political economy).

- Participate actively in the Economist Network of RBAP by attending regional meetings (in-person and/or virtual), sharing relevant experiences, and conducting peer reviews.

- Collaborate and contribute to regional and sub-regional publications, practice notes, and Regional Human Development Reports.

- Stay informed about broader developments, contribute to cross-border and cross-GPN initiatives, and support the economist network through common analyses, frameworks, and templates.

- Enhance UNDP’s understanding and design of new approaches to sustainable development across the region by acting as a regional thematic lead where possible.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

jobs.title: Team Lead - Programme Specialist (Open to Internal and External Applicants)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP’s Rule of Law Programme in Pakistan is working to strengthen the rule of law and to ensure equal access to justice and security services, particularly for women and marginalized groups across Pakistan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) including the merged districts (MDs), Balochistan, and Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT). In close collaboration with a range of government, rule of law and justice sector institutions, the overall Programme aims to enhance and sustain peace and stability for the longer-term in Pakistan.

The Programme activities and interventions therefore directly correspond with the Government of Pakistan’s strategies and commitments to rule of law and justice reforms, as well as improving the efficiency and effectiveness of institutions to deliver accountable and affordable security and justice services to the public.

The Rule of Law Programme implementation is guided by the following four strategic objectives:

- Policy, legal and regulatory frameworks strengthened to warrant people-centered, equitable, timely, affordable justice and security delivery to all people with an emphasis on women, marginalized and vulnerable groups, and digital technologies.

- Capacity of justice and security stakeholders (duty bearers) enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible services to all people with an emphasis on women and digital technologies.

- Capacity of women, and the most vulnerable and marginalized (rights holders) strengthened to access referral pathways to justice and security.

- Justice and security sector institutional facilities enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible justice and security services, through women friendly and gender-responsive infrastructure development support with an emphasis on flood resilience and green energy.

Against this backdrop, UNDP actions and interventions are aimed at restoring public confidence and service delivery in the formal justice and rule of law sectors through a range of initiatives i.e. policy development and reform, fostering justice and security sector governance, as well as oversight and accountability at an institutional level with emphasis on inclusive and gender-responsive programming. The overall engagement strategy, therefore, involves both federal and local levels. The Programme is implemented in partnership with the Judiciary, Police, Prosecution, Prisons, Probation and Reclamation, Bar Associations, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and academia both at federal and provincial levels.

The Team Lead /Programme Specialist will support the Chief Technical Advisor (CTA) in the implementation and achievement of programme results, liaising closely with key government and rule of law counterparts at federal and provincial levels, donor agencies, UN agencies and other international organizations. The Team Lead /Programme Specialist will provide technical leadership and advisory support to government counterparts and rule of law, security and justice-sector institutions and will supervise designated Rule of Law Programme personnel in accordance with the approved organigramme.

The incumbent will support the CTA in the strategic positioning of UNDP Rule of Law activities and provide policy and programme-management advice on rule of law, security and justice-sector issues. S/he will support donor coordination and resource-mobilization efforts, contribute to programme formulation, strategic direction and evaluation, and serve as a key technical focal point for major national and international stakeholders.

Duties and Responsibilities

The incumbent will report directly to the Chief Technical Advisor (CTA). S/he will provide day-to-day technical leadership and coordination for the Rule of Law Programme, support programme management and oversight, and provide substantive advice on rule of law, law enforcement, security-sector and institutional reform.

The role entails supervision of designated programme personnel and short-term consultants, in accordance with the approved organigramme and applicable UNDP policies and procedures. The incumbent will support the CTA in programme development, implementation, quality assurance and achievement of results.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

Provide technical leadership and advisory support on rule of law, law enforcement, security-sector and institutional reform.

- Provide day-to-day technical leadership, coordination, and advisory support to ensure effective implementation of programme interventions relating to security-sector and criminal justice reform, access to justice, and institutional strengthening

- Provide specialised technical advice to relevant institutions on institutional reform priorities affecting police, prosecution, prisons, probation and other security and criminal justice institutions, including institutional governance, operational effectiveness, accountability, coordination and service-delivery systems.

- Lead and coordinate institutional assessments and diagnostics to identify systemic gaps and recommend tailored solutions.

- Provide technical guidance on strengthening investigation and prosecution practices, institutional coordination, fair-trial safeguards, lawful and accountable service delivery, victim/survivor referral mechanisms and other priority criminal justice functions.

- Guide technical interventions aimed at strengthening citizen-responsive, accessible, inclusive and gender-sensitive law-enforcement and security services, including institutional systems and practices that improve services for women and vulnerable populations.

- Offer technical guidance to provincial and federal justice institutions on case management, investigation standards, and fair trial guarantees.

- Assist in the rollout of case management systems, and integrated data platforms.

- Provide substantive oversight and coordination for interventions involving law-enforcement and correctional institutions, ensuring coherence across institutional reform, capacity development, digital transformation, infrastructure and service-delivery initiatives.

- Coordinate communication and sharing knowledge with other regional Rule of Law Programmes.

- Provide advice to CTA on scaling up and sustainability of the Rule of Law Programme.

Provide technical leadership for gender-responsive institutional reform and women’s advancement across law-enforcement, security and criminal justice institutions.

- Provide technical leadership and advice on integrating gender equality, non-discrimination, accessibility and survivor-centred approaches into law-enforcement, security and criminal justice institutional reforms, policies, procedures and service-delivery systems.

- Guide diagnostics and institutional analysis of barriers affecting the recruitment, retention, participation, leadership and career progression of women within police, prosecution, prisons, probation and other relevant institutions.

- Support development and implementation of evidence-based institutional reform measures addressing gender-responsive human-resource policies, career progression pathways, safe and inclusive workplace standards and appropriate mechanisms for addressing harassment and discrimination.

- Provide substantive technical guidance on gender-responsive and survivor-centred institutional responses to gender-based violence and other cases involving vulnerable groups, including victim identification, trauma-informed approaches, referral pathways, confidentiality, informed consent and inter-institutional coordination.

- Guide the integration of gender-responsive approaches into law-enforcement and security-sector training systems, operational procedures, institutional policies, digital systems, facilities and service-delivery models.

- Support professional development, mentorship, leadership and pipeline-development approaches aimed at increasing the participation and advancement of women within law-enforcement, prosecution, correctional and other relevant institutions.

- Coordinate on reforms involving the judiciary, ADR, legal profession and access-to-justice institutions to ensure coherent gender-responsive programming while maintaining clear technical responsibilities.

Ensure programme management and oversight.

- Prepare annual and quarterly workplans aligned with programme outcomes, ensuring sequencing of interventions and resource allocation.

- Provide substantive and strategic support to the Rule of Law Programme, including supervision of programme team and several short- term consultants.

- Facilitate and manage Rule of Law Programme activities, and measure performance and report on project results and outcomes for CTA to present to the Project Review Board (PRB) and other forums, ensure reporting to donors is timely and maintains required standards.

- Support the establishment and functioning of the Rule of Law team and manage the recruitment of team and local consultants, as well as identifying short-term local experts as necessary.

- Coordinate and supervise the activities of the Rule of Law personnel , experts and consultants working as part oof the technical assistance team.

- Contribute toward Rule of Law work plans, progress reports, and terminal reports.

- Be responsible for the timely preparation and quality control of all substantive technical outputs, briefs and required documents, ensuring timely production and submission of outputs and reports by all members of the Rule of Law, contractors and partners.

- Support to organize PRB, donor coordination and project review meetings. Prepare background. documents, briefs, issues papers, and progress reports for the PRB meetings and for donor reporting. Follow-up on the implementation of PRB decisions and recommendations.

- Support process for the selection of suppliers, contractors, and partners. Supervise procurement of goods and services including preparation of equipment specifications, Terms of Reference (TORs) and Request for Proposals (RFPs) according to approved UNDP procedures.

- Conduct field visits to supervise, coordinate and monitor field-level activities of the Rule of Law Programme.

- Supervise outsourced research and dissemination of research findings.

- Provide support to the Rule of Law Programme’s infrastructure development projects.

- Conduct day-to-day meetings with Rule of Law personnel , providing feedback on performance and advice on way forward.

Strengthen coordination, partnerships and institutional engagement.

- Support CTA in coordination with UNDP country office, donors, government, and all other partners including other UN agencies for successful implementation of the Rule of Law Programme.

- Organize and document regular Criminal Justice Coordination Committee sessions at provincial and district levels to align police, prosecution, judiciary, and corrections.

- Develop and update SOPs for case referrals, evidence sharing, and victim/survivor support across institutions

- Link judicial academies, police training schools, and prosecution departments to harmonize curricula and embed reforms

- Facilitate structured dialogue with CSOs, bar associations, and academia to strengthen accountability and inclusion.

- Assist the CTA in building relationships with key government counterparts for achievement of results consistent with government priorities.

- Support in the delivery of the communications and visibility strategy, making use of a variety of technologies and information platforms;

Contribute to the results-based management, monitoring, reporting and knowledge management.

- Work closely with the designated team members to ensure that technical implementation is aligned with the programme results framework, indicators, baselines, targets and reporting requirements.

- Provide substantive inputs to progress reports, donor reports, programme reviews, briefing notes and other results-based documentation, ensuring that reported achievements accurately reflect implementation progress and institutional change.

- Support systematic use of evidence, monitoring findings, assessments and evaluation results to inform technical decision-making and programme adaptation.

- Capture lessons learned, promising practices and knowledge generated through programme implementation and support their dissemination and application across relevant institutions and programme locations.

- Contribute to quality assurance of research, assessments, diagnostics and knowledge products commissioned under the programme.

- Document programme achievements, challenges, and corrective actions, aligned with EU reporting requirements.

Facilitate Cross Cutting initiatives

- Mainstream gender equality, disability inclusion, and survivor-centred approaches across programme activities .

- Track participation of women and persons with disabilities in justice institutions and measure accessibility improvements.

- Integrate gender-sensitive approaches into all programme outputs, including survivor-centred justice for GBV cases and recruitment of women into justice institutions.

- Support ADR mechanism tailored to ethnic and religious minorities in remote areas.

- Expand digital case management systems with user-friendly interfaces for marginalized groups.

- Incorporate environmental crime awareness and enforcement into justice sector training, linking to SDG 16.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The incumbent will be based in the UNDP Pakistan Country Office in Islamabad, with travel to programme implementation locations, particularly Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, as required.

The incumbent will report directly to the Chief Technical Advisor (CTA) and will support the CTA in the overall technical leadership, programme management, strategic positioning, quality assurance and achievement of results of the Rule of Law Programme.

The incumbent will supervise designated programme personnel and consultants in accordance with the approved organigramme and will maintain effective working relationships with relevant government institutions, justice and security-sector stakeholders, development partners, UN entities, civil society and other partners. S/he will coordinate with designated other team members and relevant Country Office colleagues to ensure coherent and effective programme implementation.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

- UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site .

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Management

- Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

- Partnerships Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

- Communication: Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. . Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

2030 Agenda: Peace

- Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights Access to Justice Rule of Law

2030 Agenda: People

- Gender Gender Equality and Institutional Transformation

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Law, International Peace and Conflict Resolution, Political Science or a related thematic area is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of seven (7) years (with master’s degree) or nine (9) years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant professional experience in rule of law, security, justice, conflict resolution, peacebuilding, governance or a related technical field, with demonstrated project/programme management experience, is required.

Desired Skills

- Specific experience facilitating multi-stakeholder consensus, preferably in post-crisis or complex settings, is an asset.

- Demonstrated experience providing policy advice and preparing high-quality technical, policy and programme reports at national and/or international level is desired.

- Demonstrated programme/project management experience in complex operating environments is desired.

- Experience providing technical leadership on rule of law, law enforcement, security-sector, criminal justice or institutional reform is desirable.

- Experience working with government institutions, justice and security-sector actors, development partners and other diverse stakeholders is desirable.

- Experience supervising multidisciplinary teams, consultants or technical experts is desired.

- Experience in gender-responsive institutional reform, survivor-centred approaches and women’s advancement within justice or security institutions is desired.

- Experience in results-based management, donor reporting, research/assessment oversight and knowledge management is desirable.

- Previous work experience with UNDP, UN agencies or international development organizations would be an advantage.

- Basic computer skills, including MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint, are required.

Language Requirements :

- Fluency in English and Urdu is required.

jobs.title: Auxiliar de Atracción de Inversión
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

Fruto del Acuerdo de Colaboración firmado por el Gobierno de México y el Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD), se diseña el proyecto: “Fortalecimiento de las Capacidades para el Impulso Económico y la Implementación de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible”, que tiene como objetivo colaborar con la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores en el fortalecimiento de sus capacidades para posicionar los intereses de México en el escenario internacional mediante el cumplimiento de sus funciones en materia económica.

En seguimiento a estos objetivos, se impulsan acciones orientadas al fortalecimiento de la diplomacia económica de México, incluyendo la atracción de inversión, la promoción comercial, la interlocución con actores estratégicos y la articulación con Representaciones de México en el Exterior, dependencias federales, gobiernos estatales y organismos empresariales. En este marco, se implementa el Plan Integral de Promoción Económica, mediante misiones comerciales de México al exterior y misiones extranjeras hacia México, la participación de México en ferias internacionales, la canalización de oportunidades de proveeduría e inversión, así como la organización de seminarios de inversión y exportación.

En un contexto internacional marcado por la reconfiguración económica global, se llevarán a cabo las acciones previstas para la presente vacante, mismas que contribuirán a robustecer las capacidades de la SRE en materia de fortalecimiento de alianzas institucionales y apoyo a las prioridades estratégicas de México en el ámbito económico internacional.

Alcance de Trabajo:

- Asistir en las tareas de coordinación de las acciones de las representaciones de México en el exterior orientadas a fomentar la atracción de inversiones, dando seguimiento operativo a las instrucciones de la Dirección y a las políticas que definan las autoridades competentes.

- Asistir en el seguimiento a la vinculación con entidades del sector público competentes en materia económica, particularmente de inversiones, apoyando en la preparación de los insumos y materiales necesarios para el desahogo de los asuntos que deriven de la conducción de la política exterior.

- Asistir en la vinculación con el sector privado y las autoridades competentes en materia económica, particularmente de inversiones, mediante el apoyo en la elaboración de perfiles de empresas, tarjetas de apoyo y materiales de preparación para reuniones con inversionistas.

- Asistir en la identificación y el seguimiento de los obstáculos en materia de atracción de inversiones que enfrentan las empresas, en apoyo a la coordinación con las representaciones de México en el exterior y la Secretaría de Economía.

- Apoyar en las tareas de elaboración de análisis, reportes y materiales de inteligencia económica que sustenten la atracción de inversión, así como asistir en el seguimiento al programa de capacitación económica para las representaciones diplomáticas de México.

Acuerdo Institucional:

La presente vacante estará bajo supervisión directa de la Subsecretaría para América del Norte y la coordinación del proyecto Fortalecimiento de las Capacidades para el Impulso Económico y la Implementación de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible, quienes evaluarán el desempeño del contratista al término del contrato.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos:

- Certificado de bachillerato es requerido, licenciatura concluida en finanzas, economía, ciencia política, relaciones internacionales, políticas públicas, negocios internacionales o carreras afines, no es requisito, pero se le dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Para candidatos con preparatoria 4 años de experiencia; para candidatos con licenciatura concluida, 1 año de experiencia. Áreas de experiencia: evaluación de proyectos, atracción de inversión, comercio exterior, desarrollo del sector privado, innovación o temas afines.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia en comunicación efectiva, excelentes habilidades de comunicación oral y escrita.

- Experiencia o conocimiento en habilidades de negociación.

- Experiencia o conocimiento en gestión equipos y de tiempo. Experiencia o conocimiento en gestión de relaciones institucionales.

Habilidades Deseadas:

- Experiencia o conocimiento en economía internacional, desarrollo del sector privado, comercio exterior o diplomacia.

- Experiencia o conocimiento en desarrollo de alianzas estratégicas o habilidades afines.

- Experiencia o conocimiento en la Administración Pública Federal o en Organismos Internacionales.

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar

jobs.title: Operations Manager [Open to Internal & External Applicants]
Monitoring & Evaluation Specialist [Open to internal and external applicants]
Energy Finance Specialist [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Program (UNDP) is the leading UN organization advancing sustainable development globally and in Ethiopia. As a key integrator within the UN system, UNDP plays a central role in helping countries achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP operates at global, regional, and country levels, combining international expertise with local knowledge to deliver practical solutions and impactful advocacy.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Program Support (BPPS) have the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working.  BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data driven including in its program support efforts.

As per UNDP’s new Strategic Plan 2026-2029, four strategic objectives – prosperity for all, effective governance, crisis resilience and healthy planet – define the organization’s strategic direction, powered by three accelerators: digital and artificial intelligence (AI) transformation; gender equality; and sustainable finance.

The central purpose of the Rome Centre is to ensure the effective implementation and further development of the strategic partnership between UNDP and the government of Italy across the objectives of sustainable development and in doing so advancing the broader partnership between UNDP and G7 and G20 countries.

The Rome Centre focuses on the critical policy areas of youth engagement in climate action, energy for development and climate finance.

At the core of UNDP’s work is the Global Policy Network (GPN), which mobilizes world-class technical expertise to support six signature solutions: energy, poverty alleviation, democratic governance, resilience, environmental sustainability, and gender equality. These solutions are aligned to foster structural transformation, promote inclusion, and build resilience in Ethiopia and beyond.

Energy is a critical enabler of most countries’ development agenda and is one of UNDP’s flagship areas of intervention. UNDP’s energy work aligns with Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7), focusing on:

- Expanding access to affordable, reliable, and modern energy services.

- Improving energy efficiency across sectors.

- Increasing the share of renewable energy in the national energy mix.

In Ethiopia, the government has set bold energy access and transition goals, including through Mission 300, which aims for universal electricity access by 2030, with a target of 65% on-grid and 35% off-grid connections. Achieving these ambitions will require substantial and sustained investment, robust planning, and strengthened public-private collaboration.

A key initiative supporting this agenda is "Energy for Growth in Africa", which aims to identify and support clean energy projects across the continent that face difficulties accessing finance. The initiative, launched in the context of the Italian G7 Presidency and promoted by the Italian Ministry of Environment and Energy Security (MASE) in collaboration with UNDP, provides technical assistance, risk mitigation tools, and access to concessional finance to improve project viability and attract private sector investment. Operated through UNDP Country Offices, the initiative works with governments to ensure alignment with national energy priorities and to help scale up investment-ready projects.

Currently active in twelve African countries, the initiative focuses on markets with limited access to commercial finance, working in close coordination with multilateral efforts to streamline support and enhance the delivery of sustainable energy solutions.

Scope of Work

The UNDP Rome Centre for Climate Action and Energy Transition is seeking an Energy Finance Specialist to support the implementation of the “Energy for Growth in Africa” program in Ethiopia. The Specialist will work in close coordination with the UNDP Country Office in Ethiopia and under the technical guidance of the Rome Centre’s Energy for Growth in Africa Team to accelerate clean energy investments aligned with national priorities and UNDP’s global and regional energy strategy.

The primary objective of this role is to identify, develop, and support energy initiatives that unlock financing and contribute to a just, inclusive, and sustainable energy transition in Ethiopia. The Energy Finance Specialist will provide strategic insights and technical expertise to ensure that interventions respond to national development goals while advancing regional and global objectives under SDG 7.

The Energy Finance Specialist will serve as the focal point for the UNDP Rome Centre’s “Energy for Growth in Africa” initiative in Ethiopia. The Specialist will provide technical expertise, strategic advice, and stakeholder coordination to accelerate clean energy investments that contribute to Ethiopia’s sustainable energy and climate goals, in alignment with CPD for Ethiopia (2025-2030), UNSCDF for Ethiopia (2025 – 2030) UNDP’s regional and global energy strategy. The key responsibilities include:

Ensure Project Identification and Origination

- Ensure the Implementation of the project origination framework established centrally by the Energy for Growth in Africa initiative;

- Ensure project identification is aligned with Ethiopia’s national energy priorities, in particular with the recently developed National Energy Compact.

Build Strategic Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination

- Map relevant stakeholders in Ethiopia energy landscape and maintain active communication to ensure inclusive and coordinated engagement;

- Engage and coordinate with key energy stakeholders—government entities, private investors, development institutions (including G7 partners and the Italian Cooperation System), and financial actors—to facilitate partnerships and co-investment opportunities;

- Organize and contribute to technical meetings, stakeholder roundtables, and outreach events to promote the Energy for Growth in Africa initiative and related energy access and transition programs;

- Engage directly and, if requested by the Government counterparts, support the Compact Delivery and Monitoring Unit that will be formed to deliver on the Mission 300 Compact.

Ensure Project Risk Mitigation and Investment Facilitation

- Liaise with financial institutions, investors, and multilateral partners to coordinate the deployment of financial instruments and appropriate risk mitigation tools for the successful completion of the projects;

- Identify opportunities for clean energy projects to generate carbon credits under voluntary or compliance carbon markets (e.g., Article 6 of the Paris Agreement), and support the integration of carbon revenue streams into project financing structures.

Provide Technical Assistance, Capacity Building, and Knowledge Sharing

- Offer technical inputs to clean energy project developers on feasibility studies, business models, power purchase agreements, and compliance with environmental and social safeguards;

- Advise and support clean energy project developers in structuring project financing by drawing on public and private, national and international climate finance sources, including those provided by multilateral development banks (e.g. WB, AfDB), vertical climate funds (e.g. GCF, GEF) and bilateral funds from G7 countries and Italy (e.g. Italian Climate Fund) - and support the submission of funding applications to these instruments. Facilitate the exchange of lessons learned and best practices with other participating countries under the Energy for Growth in Africa initiative.

Reporting, Monitoring, and Impact Assessment

- Prepare quarterly progress reports detailing project identification, pipeline development, risk mitigation efforts, and stakeholder engagement outcomes;

- Provide regular updates on cooperation with development partners, particularly G7 entities, including challenges, opportunities, and strategic recommendations;

- Develop and apply monitoring tools to track project outcomes related to energy access, investment mobilization, and sustainable development impact;

- Capture and share insights to improve program design, execution, and overall contribution to Ethiopia’s energy transition.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangements:

jobs.title: Auxiliar de Información y Documentación de Proyectos de Cooperación Sur Sur
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

La implementación de los proyectos de “Sembrando Vida” y “Juntos por el Bienestar” en Centroamérica y el Caribe, forma parte de los compromisos adquiridos por la Presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo en el marco de la IX Cumbre de la Comunidad de Estados Latinoamericanos y Caribeños (CELAC) celebrada el 08 y 09 de abril del 2025 en Tegucigalpa, República de Honduras.

En ese marco, México reafirmó su voluntad de profundizar la cooperación regional a través de programas y/o proyectos de desarrollo inclusivo, priorizando el bienestar de las comunidades rurales y la promoción de la autosuficiencia alimentaria como motores de una prosperidad compartida.

Estos proyectos se apegan al principio de Prosperidad Compartida instruido por la Presidenta de México. La prosperidad compartida, que México proyecta en materia de cooperación internacional se refiere al beneficio mutuo de los países a nivel bilateral, regional y triangular, a través de la cooperación y el intercambio de experiencias, buenas prácticas y recursos. Este principio implica que los países colaboren entre sí para contribuir a erradicar el hambre y la pobreza, así como potenciar la sostenibilidad a través de acciones específicas para combatir el cambio climático y salvaguardar el medio ambiente.

Además, la ejecución de estos proyectos en Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Belice y Cuba, es parte de los compromisos que la Presidenta de México ha asumido con sus homólogos de esos países, a fin de promover las condiciones necesarias para el bienestar y desarrollo integral de la población, de manera inclusiva y participativa.

El objetivo de “Sembrando Vida” es contribuir a la seguridad alimentaria y al incremento de productividad de productores agrícolas que se encuentran en situación de retorno, o que sean residentes en departamentos y distritos con altos índices de migración, fomentando la implementación de sistemas de producción agrícola que incentiven el autoconsumo y la comercialización de excedentes mediante el acompañamiento y capacitación y reducir sus intenciones de migrar.

El objetivo de “Juntos por el Bienestar” es brindar oportunidades de capacitación laboral a personas de entre 18 y 55 años de edad, que no estudian y no trabajan, que se encuentren en situación de retorno, o que sean residentes de municipios con altos índices de migración, vulnerabilidad y desempleo. Las personas podrán realizar su capacitación en el sector privado, gubernamental o con Organizaciones de la Sociedad Civil.

La posición de Auxiliar en revisión de registros y sistema tiene como objetivo general, apoyar al proceso de revisión de los registros recibidos para los proyectos de Sembrando Vida y Juntos por el Bienestar, así como al mantenimiento del archivo de la Dirección General de Proyectos de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo, Convenios y Becas en El Salvador, Honduras, Guatemala, Belice y Cuba.

Alcance del Trabajo:

1.Verificación y depuración de información de aspirantes

a.Validar que la información solicitada en los registros esté completa y sin inconsistencias.

b.Detección de errores y duplicidades, así como de registros incompletos, inconsistentes o duplicados para su corrección o descarte.

c.Ajustar o solicitar la rectificación de datos conforme a estándares definidos.

2.Validación de elegibilidad conforme a lineamientos

a.Revisar cada registro contra los requisitos establecidos en los lineamientos de operación de Sembrando Vida.

b.Determinar de manera preliminar el estatus de la solicitud, según cumplimiento de criterios.

c.Registrar evidencias para asegurar trazabilidad y transparencia.

3.Compilar la información de la población beneficiaria registrada

a.Organizar la información validada en sistemas, incluyendo la identificación de edad, género, ubicación u otras variables determinadas por la coordinación del proyecto.

b.Apoyar las actividades de descarga masiva de información del sistema correspondiente.

El titular desempeña otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y la Organización.

Acuerdo Institucional:

El Auxiliar de Información y Documentación de Proyectos de Cooperación fromará parte de la estructura operativa de la Dirección General de Ejeccución de Proyectos, Especialies de Cooperación Internacional, AMEXCID.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar de Forma Innovadora: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende delos errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos Mínimos:

- Certificado de educación preparatoria, es requisito.

- Título de Licenciatura en Ciencias Sociales, Administración, Contabilidad o afines, no es requisito, pero se le dará la debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Relevante:

- Para candidato/as con certificado de preparatoria: 3 años de experiencia en temas relacionados apoyo administrativo, revisión documental, registro de información, seguimiento operativo de procesos y proyectos.

- Para candidato/as con título de licenciatura: no se requiere experiencia.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia en revisión, cotejo, captura o sistematización de información y documentos administrativos.

- Manejo de herramientas de oficina, en particular procesador de textos y hojas de cálculo para controles y listados.

- Experiencia en organización de expedientes y seguimiento de solicitudes o pendientes documentales.

Habilidades Deseadas:

- Experiencia de apoyo administrativo en proyectos sociales, de desarrollo, de cooperación o en instituciones públicas.

- Experiencia en revisión de registros de actividades, listas de participantes y documentación de respaldo de programas o proyectos.

- Conocimiento de prácticas de gestión documental, manejo de bases de datos y coordinación de información entre equipos o contrapartes.

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar
