jobs.description:
Background

The position is located in the Crisis Response Division (CRD), Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). OCHA is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA also ensures there is a framework within which each actor can contribute to the overall response efforts. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate for the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention; and facilitate sustainable solutions.

This multiple-duty-station temporary job opening is being advertised for the position of Monitoring and Reporting Officer and is located across a number of OCHA Humanitarian Financing Units Kenya. Under the overall supervision of the Head of Office, the incumbent reports to the Head of Humanitarian Financing Unit/Fund Manager.

The Humanitarian Fund Units in OCHA Regional and Country Offices manage multi-donor country-based pooled funds under the leadership of the Humanitarian Coordinator/Resident Coordinator.

These funds receive unearmarked contributions from donors. The funds are allocated to humanitarian actors for ongoing humanitarian operations and to respond to new emergencies.

Under the supervision of the regional humanitarian pooled fund manager, the Monitoring and Reporting Officer will play a central role in strengthening accountability, effectiveness, and learning within the Humanitarian Funding Unit (HFU). The position is responsible for leading the implementation of monitoring, evaluation, and accountability frameworks that ensure compliance with established standards, promote transparency, and deliver measurable impact among partners and stakeholders.

The Monitoring and Reporting Officer will support evidence-based decision-making by developing and piloting innovative monitoring approaches, documenting best practices, and generating insights on the operationalization of localization strategies. Through active engagement with coordination forums and close collaboration with humanitarian partners, including local and national NGOs, the role facilitates inclusive participation, capacity strengthening, and knowledge sharing across the humanitarian system.

The position will also contribute to the planning and execution of monitoring missions, provide technical guidance to partners, and ensure systematic documentation and dissemination of results, lessons learned, and success stories. By maintaining strong coordination with field offices and stakeholders, the M&E Officer enhances program quality, promotes risk-sharing initiatives, and supports continuous improvement in fund management and delivery.

Overall, the role aims to ensure that the HFU operates in a results-oriented, accountable, and collaborative manner, while advancing localization and strengthening the effectiveness of humanitarian response efforts.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the supervision of the Head of Humanitarian Financing Unit/Fund Manager, the Monitoring and Reporting Officer will be responsible for the following duties:

1.) Strengthen accountability, coordination, and monitoring effectiveness of the Humanitarian Funding Unit (HFU).

- Provide strategic leadership in advancing the HFU’s commitment to accountability, impact, and compliance by ensuring the robust and consistent application of the Accountability and Integrity Tool (AIT). This includes promoting transparency, reinforcing adherence to established operational standards, and fostering a culture of results-oriented performance among implementing partners and stakeholders.

- Represent the HFU in a broad range of coordination mechanisms, including Working Groups, area-based coordination platforms, sector-specific forums, and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) structures. Actively contribute to discussions, influence decision-making processes, and ensure that HFU priorities and perspectives are effectively integrated into inter-agency coordination efforts.

- Identify, conceptualize, and pilot innovative and context-appropriate monitoring models and approaches aimed at strengthening oversight, improving data quality, and enhancing the overall effectiveness and efficiency of Country Fund interventions.

- Work in close collaboration with Resident Coordinator’s Office (RCO) area offices, UNHCR, and implementing partners to strategically plan and execute monitoring missions. Provide hands-on technical assistance during these missions to ensure compliance, strengthen partner capacity, and enhance programme delivery on the ground.

- Maintain continuous and proactive engagement with the broader humanitarian community by participating in joint field missions alongside HFU and OCHA field staff, fostering collaboration, information sharing, and coordinated responses to emerging humanitarian needs.

2.) Enhance knowledge management, reporting, and localization efforts within the HFU framework.

- Design, coordinate, and facilitate webinars and other knowledge-sharing platforms aimed at strengthening the technical and operational capacities of partners, while promoting the exchange of experiences, expertise, and innovative practices across the humanitarian ecosystem.

- Systematically identify, compile, and analyze localization models and best practices implemented by other humanitarian funds, agencies, and organizations. Ensure that these insights are effectively documented and disseminated to inform strategic decision-making and continuous improvement within the HFU.

- Generate, synthesize, and disseminate evidence on the operationalization of the Uganda Humanitarian Fund’s localization approach by documenting both successful implementation models and key challenges or bottlenecks encountered in practice.

- Develop high-quality analytical products, including case studies, success stories, and practical examples, to effectively communicate lessons learned and showcase impact to the Fund’s Advisory Board and other strategic stakeholders.

- Contribute substantively to the preparation of a wide range of knowledge and communication products, including annual reports, policy and guidance documents, briefing notes, presentations, social media content, and official correspondence, ensuring accuracy, clarity, and alignment with organizational standards.

3.) Provide technical support, foster partnerships, and promote collaborative engagement.

- Deliver tailored, context-sensitive technical guidance and capacity-building support to Local and National NGOs through structured one-on-one consultations, group training sessions, and ongoing advisory support, with the aim of strengthening their operational effectiveness and compliance capacity.

- Support the design, development, and implementation of risk-sharing initiatives with Local and National partners, ensuring that such approaches are aligned with broader programmatic goals while promoting equitable partnerships and sustainable localization outcomes.

- Actively promote and sustain a high level of team cohesion and synergy within the HFU by encouraging collaborative, complementary, and cross-functional approaches to programme implementation and problem-solving.

- Establish and maintain strong, trust-based partnerships and communication channels with a wide range of stakeholders, including UN agencies, NGOs, and government counterparts, to facilitate coordinated, efficient, and impactful programme delivery.

- Undertake additional responsibilities and assignments as required by the HFU Manager, contributing flexibly and proactively to broader OCHA priorities and responding effectively to evolving operational demands and emerging humanitarian contexts.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies

Business Direction & Strategy - Systems Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management - Portfolio Management

- Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization’s programs and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimizing return on investment.

Business Management - Monitoring

- Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback on the consistency or discrepancy between planned and actual activities and program performance and results

Business Management - Evaluation

- Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns

Business Development - Knowledge Generation

- Ability to research and turn information into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need

Partnership Management - Relationship Management

- Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding

2030 Agenda: Engagement & Effectiveness

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in political science, economics, sociology, law, international relations or related field is required, or

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of 2 years (with Master’s degree) or 4 years (with Bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience at the national or international level in monitoring, reporting or relevant related field is required

- Excellent interpersonal communication skills/experience is required

- Proven experience in report writing is required

- Experience in the use of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.). and advanced knowledge of web-based management systems such as ERP is required.

- Proven availability for travel in-country is desired

- Proven ability to work with moderate supervision with efficiency, competence, and integrity with people of different backgrounds is desired.

jobs.title: Policy Analyst [Open to Tier 1 & 2 applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Aligned with UNDP’s mission to end of poverty, reduce inequalities and exclusion, promote effective governance, and enhance sustainable environmental governance, UNDP Uganda has been collaborating with the Government, Stakeholders and the People to contribute to Uganda’s Sustainable Development. Supporting Uganda’s priorities in this regard is advanced in line with Uganda’s Vision 2040, the Tenfold Growth Strategy and the National Development Plan IV (NDP IV – 2025/26 – 2029/30).

Uganda is pursuing an ambitious transformation agenda under Vision 2040, NDP IV and the Ten-Fold Growth Strategy, while operating in a rapidly changing development financing environment. Rising financing needs, constrained fiscal space, declining and increasingly fragmented ODA, climate vulnerabilities, demographic pressures and changing development-partner priorities require new approaches to mobilising, deploying and managing development finance.

Accelerating Uganda’s development ambitions will require not only additional resources, but also better use of existing financing, stronger project preparation and implementation, innovative financing, improved public investment management, stronger domestic resource mobilisation, and more effective partnerships with the private sector and international financial institutions.

UNDP supports Government through policy advice, institutional strengthening, development financing, resource mobilisation and strategic partnerships. Its Government Development Financing (GDF) offer helps strengthen the financing-to-results chain—from strategic prioritisation and project preparation, through financing mobilisation and implementation, to measurable development outcomes.

Against this background, UNDP Uganda seeks to engage a Policy Analyst to provide advice and strengthen engagement with key Government counterparts, particularly Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development (MoFPED), Office of the Prime Minister (OPM), National Planning Authority (NPA) and other relevant institutions. The Analyst will also support UNDP in its integrator role within the UN.

The Analyst will enhance UNDP’s position as a strategic partner of choice on development financing, implementation and economic transformation, while strengthening partnerships with development partners, IFIs, private investors, foundations and other sources of development finance.

Duties and Responsibilities

Provide advice and support to UNDP management, programmes and projects focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Advise the Resident Representative and senior management on development priorities, economic transformation, development finance and emerging policy issues.

- Support engagement with MoFPED, OPM, NPA and other key Government institutions.

- Advise on development financing, domestic resource mobilisation, public investment management, climate and innovative finance, blended finance and development cooperation.

- Identify priority policy and financing issues where UNDP can provide high-value advice.

- Prepare policy briefs, talking points, investment propositions and analyses.

- Support high-level policy dialogue among Government, UNDP, development partners and other stakeholders.

- Compilation, analysis and interpretation of economic and statistical data, thorough research of the economic and development issues in the country and preparation of top-quality analysis and reports;

- Provision of top-quality analysis and substantive inputs to strategic documents of UNDP and the UN system, including but not limited to the UNDP Country Programme, UN Common Country Assessment, UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework;

- Leadership in the production, launch and popularization of the Country office knowledge products such as National Human Development Reports, annual reports;

- Contribution to sub-regional, regional and inter-agency initiatives related to development issues;

- Participate in different working groups, within the UN system, Development partner community and government.

Support to Partnership/Network Building and Resource Mobilization:

- Development of partnerships with the UN Agencies, International Financial Institutions (IFI’s), government institutions, bilateral and multi-lateral donors, private sector, civil society in areas based on strategic goals of UNDP, country needs and donors' priorities.

- Analysis and research of information on donors, preparation of substantive briefs on possible areas of cooperation and resource mobilization.

- Provide support to programme team in mobilizing financial resources for effective implementation of their programmes.

Support to the Office’s Advocacy and Outreach Activities:

- Support the organization of events, meetings, conferences, etc., including preparation of concept notes and presentations, proposing agenda topics, identifying participants, etc.

- Support to public and policy advocacy of the Country Office for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), pro-poor and equitable economic growth by participating in relevant forums, conferences, and trainings.

- Support to monitoring progress and formulation of strategies towards the achievement of the SDGs.

Provision of technical support to UNDP Programmes and Policies for effective implementation:

- Compilation, analysis and interpretation of economic and statistical data, thorough research of the economic and development issues in the country and preparation of top-quality analysis and reports.

- Review and provide detail technical feedback and inputs to the various analytical products produced by UNDP or Government with support from UNDP.

- Provide support and analytical inputs to UNDP Senior Officials in negotiating, formulating and reviewing UNDP technical assistance programmes and projects.

- Advice on possible areas for UNDP support and adjustment of on-going programmes to ensure that UNDP programmes are in line with national policies and priorities.

Provision of technical backstopping and policy advice support to Government counterparts and other Partners:

- Provide technical backstopping support to National Planning Agency in the formulation and implementation of the National Development Plans;

- Advise and facilitate dialogue on sustainable development issues with government officials, development partners, civil society, and the private sector;

- Provide policy and programming advice and support for development planning and policy formulation at the national, sub-national and local levels;

- Support monitoring and reporting of progress related to SDGs and other national development frameworks, including to help strengthen national and local level data collection and statistical capacity;

- Support to leverage UNDP’s regional and global programmes, to provide holistic and effective support to the country;

UN System and Development Partner Engagement

- Support UNDP’s integrator role within the UN Country Team and Cooperation Framework on development financing, economic transformation and partnerships.

- Support the identification of opportunities for greater UN coherence in supporting Government financing priorities.

- Support development-partner coordination mechanisms and relevant technical groups.

- Support the strengthening of engagements with the World Bank, IMF, AfDB and other IFIs on financing and implementation

Facilitate knowledge building on economic and development issues.

- Contribute to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

- Provide capacity building support to CO personnel on economic issues

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Policy Analyst will report on a regular basis directly to the Deputy Resident Representative.

Competencies

Core Competencies

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Este processo seletivo busca contratar um(a) profissional para atuar de forma compartilhada no apoio técnico e operacional de duas iniciativas estratégicas desenvolvidas no âmbito da parceria de cooperação técnica internacional entre o Programa das Nações Unidas para o Desenvolvimento (PNUD) e o Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ):

- Justiça 4.0 : o Programa, iniciado em 2020, visa desenvolver e aprimorar soluções tecnológicas para tornar os serviços oferecidos pela Justiça brasileira mais eficientes, eficazes e acessíveis à população, além de otimizar a gestão processual para magistrados(as), servidores(as), advogados(as) e demais atores do sistema de Justiça. O Justiça 4.0 é um dos maiores programas de transformação digital do Poder Judiciário e também dialoga com os Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável e com a Agenda 2030 da ONU.

- Justiça [+Segura] : firmado em 2025, o Programa foca no fortalecimento da segurança cibernética no Poder Judiciário. O Justiça [+Segura] desenvolve e implementa ferramentas e estratégias para o fortalecimento da segurança cibernética, da preservação digital e da integridade da informação, ampliando a proteção dos sistemas e dos usuários do Judiciário. A iniciativa fortalece a segurança institucional e promove a transparência, a boa governança e a eficiência dos processos judiciais, contribuindo para a economia de recursos e para uma atuação mais ágil da Justiça em benefício dos cidadãos e da sociedade.

Nesse cenário, o(a) profissional integrará a equipe compartilhada dos programas, atuando sob a supervisão direta da Unidade de Gestão de Projetos do PNUD e em estreita articulação com as coordenações técnicas do CNJ, com o propósito de garantir a excelência operacional, a sinergia entre as ações e o alcance dos resultados pactuados.

A posição será exercida em regime remoto, sendo requisito que o(a) candidato(a) tenha residência no Brasil. Quando houver necessidade de cobertura presencial de eventos, poderão ser realizadas viagens nacionais, com as despesas correspondentes custeadas pelo projeto.

Duties and Responsibilities

O(a) Assistente de Áudio e Vídeo trabalhará de forma remota, prestando suporte à criação e finalização de soluções de design e comunicação para os projetos, em estreita articulação com as equipes do CNJ e do PNUD.

Sob supervisão direta da Analista de Gestão em Educação Institucional e Comunicação, e com base em diretrizes de comunicação pré-estabelecidas, a missão do(a) profissional selecionado será apoiar as rotinas de produção gráfica e audiovisual, auxiliando na organização do fluxo de trabalho e na manutenção da identidade visual dos projetos em diferentes mídias.

Em seu dia a dia, desempenhará as seguintes atividades:

1. Apoio à produção e edição audiovisual

- Editar e finalizar vídeos institucionais e de curta duração para redes sociais: cortes, ajustes de cor, tratamento e mixagem básica de áudio, inserção de trilhas, vinhetas e letterings;

- Criar animações simples e motion graphics para vídeos e peças digitais; c. Adaptar vídeos para diferentes formatos e plataformas (redes sociais, YouTube, eventos, apresentações).

2. Suporte à acessibilidade em conteúdos audiovisuais

- Produzir legendas e transcrições dos vídeos;

- Apoiar a inclusão de recursos de acessibilidade, como janela de Libras e audiodescrição, em articulação com fornecedores.

3. Apoio na captação e cobertura de eventos, quando necessário

- Apoiar a captação de vídeo, áudio e fotografia em gravações e eventos, inclusive presenciais, com possibilidade de deslocamentos eventuais;

- Apoiar operacionalmente transmissões ao vivo, webinars e eventos híbridos;

- Produzir conteúdo rápido para redes sociais durante e após os eventos.

4. Apoio à produção de peças gráficas e digitais

- Criar e adaptar peças de apoio aos conteúdos audiovisuais e digitais (thumbnails, cards, posts, banners, apresentações), seguindo a identidade visual dos projetos.

5. Gestão de acervo e conformidade visual

- Organizar e catalogar material bruto e finalizado, banco de imagens e logomarcas;

- Verificar a conformidade de produtos audiovisuais e gráficos de parceiros com a identidade visual dos projetos.

6. Apoiar a construção e o compartilhamento de conhecimentos relevantes para o projeto.

- Participar de treinamentos sobre procedimentos internos voltados à equipe do projeto e oferecer suporte à organização de capacitações e outras atividades de desenvolvimento de competências, conforme necessário.

- Contribuir de forma consistente para redes de conhecimento e comunidades de prática.

- Manter registros organizados de dados do projeto, atividades de campo, estudos de caso, relatos de experiências humanas, fotografias e outros documentos pertinentes que possam subsidiar o compartilhamento de conhecimento e ações de defesa de causas (advocacy).

O(a) titular desempenha outras funções dentro do seu perfil funcional que considere necessárias ao bom funcionamento do projeto.

Arranjo institucional

O(a) contratado(a) será supervisionado(a) pelo(a) Analista de Gestão em Educação Institucional e Comunicação de projetos do PNUD.

Competencies

- Pensar de forma Inovadora - NÍVEL 1: Aberto a ideias criativas e riscos conhecidos, é um solucionador de problemas prático e faz melhorias.

- Adaptar com Agilidade - NÍVEL 1: Adapta-se às mudanças, lida de forma construtiva com ambiguidades e incertezas, e é flexível.

- Agir com Determinação - NÍVEL 1: Demonstra determinação e motivação, mantém a calma diante da adversidade e tem confiança.

- Engajar e fazer Parcerias - NÍVEL 1: Demonstra compaixão e compreensão em relação aos outros, formando relacionamentos positivos.

- Promover a Diversidade e Inclusão - NÍVEL 1: Valoriza e respeita as diferenças, está consciente de vieses inconscientes e enfrenta a discriminação.

Desenvolver estratégias eficazes e planos prioritários alinhados com a missão e os objetivos do PNUD, baseando-se em uma análise sistêmica de desafios, oportunidades e riscos potenciais; conectar a visão geral à realidade no campo para criar soluções tangíveis e direcionadas; aprender a partir de diversas fontes para antecipar e responder de forma eficaz às tendências atuais e futuras; demonstrar capacidade de previsão.

Capacidade de compreender e lidar com situações de negócios de forma a alcançar bons resultados. Habilidade para tomar boas decisões e fazer julgamentos rápidos dentro de tais contextos. Conhecimento e compreensão dos marcos operacionais da organização

jobs.location: Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

La mise en œuvre du Programme d’actions du Gouvernement de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) exige une coordination soutenue entre les ministères, les agences d’exécution et les partenaires pour traduire les priorités gouvernementales en résultats vérifiables.

Rattachée à la Primature, la Delivery Unit (DU) suit les projets et réformes prioritaires, signale les retards et facilite la coordination et le traitement des blocages. Elle consolide les informations sur le portefeuille, prépare les arbitrages et suit les mesures correctives avec les ministères et agences responsables de l’exécution.

L’assistance technique du PNUD a permis de structurer et de prioriser les portefeuilles sectoriels, de définir des cadres de performance, de standardiser les outils et de développer la plateforme numérique. Ces travaux couvrent notamment l’énergie, l’emploi et l’entrepreneuriat, les infrastructures et la connectivité, l’eau et l’assainissement, ainsi que la santé.

La nouvelle phase vise à mettre ces outils en service dans les routines de pilotage. Les données vérifiées alimentent les tableaux de bord et les revues de performance, qui débouchent sur des décisions et des mesures correctives. Les missions de terrain servent à vérifier les progrès déclarés.

L’appui de la Banque africaine de développement (BAD), mis en œuvre avec le PNUD, soutient la digitalisation, le pilotage, la structuration des projets et le renforcement des capacités. Le portefeuille sera élargi progressivement, selon la maturité des projets, la disponibilité des données et la capacité de suivi des équipes.

Le projet recrute un Coordonnateur ou une Coordonnatrice pour assurer sa gestion quotidienne et coordonner l’intervention des parties prenantes.

Duties and Responsibilities

Le Coordonnateur ou la Coordonnatrice assure la coordination globale du projet d’appui à la Delivery Unit, veille à la cohérence de sa stratégie et pilote l’exécution du plan de travail selon une approche axée sur les résultats.

1. Assurer la coordination technique et programmatique du projet

- Définir les orientations de mise en œuvre et superviser l’exécution du plan de travail et du budget.

- Élaborer le plan de travail annuel, le plan de suivi-évaluation et le calendrier des rencontres avec les partenaires.

- Préparer les termes de référence nécessaires à l’acquisition de biens et services et à la réalisation des activités.

- Coordonner les partenaires d’exécution et les partenaires nationaux, dont les ministères provinciaux. Assurer la concertation avec les institutions publiques, le bailleur, les agences partenaires et la société civile.

2. Traiter les blocages et vérifier les progrès sur le terrain

- Organiser un suivi rapproché, tenir un tableau de bord des alertes et qualifier les blocages avec les responsables sectoriels.=

- Faciliter les ateliers de résolution de problèmes et convenir de mesures correctives assorties d’un responsable, d’un délai et d’un critère de vérification.

- Programmer des missions ciblées pour comparer l’avancement déclaré aux réalisations observées et réunir les preuves disponibles.

- Produire des notes de terrain et vérifier les suites données aux mesures correctives.

3. Coordonner et suivre l’appui BAD–PNUD

- Harmoniser les cadres de résultats avec les outils de la DU et élaborer un plan de travail et budget annuel commun assorti de jalons trimestriels.

- Organiser des points techniques mensuels avec la DU, la BAD, le PNUD et les ministères concernés. Désigner un point focal pour le suivi de cet appui au sein de la DU.

- Vérifier les livrables et leurs pièces justificatives sur la plateforme. Suivre les délais de décaissement, les avis de non-objection et les étapes de passation des marchés.

- Associer les équipes nationales à la préparation des rapports et aux revues conjointes. Leur transférer la mise à jour des données et l’utilisation des outils de pilotage.

4. Assurer le rapportage, le suivi-évaluation et la gestion des risques

- Préparer les rapports trimestriels d’avancement, le rapport annuel des activités et les notes de situation sur le portefeuille à l’intention du PNUD et du Comité de pilotage. Communiquer les résultats du projet.

- Organiser des missions de suivi et des réunions régulières avec les partenaires. Faciliter la participation des agences et des bénéficiaires aux comités de pilotage et technique. Appuyer la revue annuelle et proposer, selon les résultats, la clôture ou la restructuration des projets durablement bloqués et la réaffectation des ressources.

- Superviser la préparation des audits du projet et des partenaires d’exécution. Mettre en œuvre les mesures de gestion des risques et les adapter à l’évolution du contexte politique et sécuritaire.

- Documenter les leçons apprises et conduire l’évaluation du projet en collaboration avec l’UPAQ.

5. Faciliter le renforcement des connaissances et des capacités, le partage des connaissances et les actions de plaidoyer

- Identifier les besoins et les opportunités en matière de renforcement des capacités. Veiller à ce que des formations, des ateliers de projet et d’autres activités pertinentes soient organisés et mis en œuvre de manière concertée, en associant des experts techniques et des parties prenantes,

- Veiller à ce que les rapports de projet rendent compte des résultats, des enseignements tirés et des bonnes pratiques en vue d’une application plus large.

- Participer aux réseaux de connaissances et aux communautés de pratique sur les questions liées au développement et aux projets, et veiller à y apporter des contributions de qualité.

Le titulaire du poste accomplit d'autres tâches relevant de son profil fonctionnel, jugées nécessaires au bon fonctionnement du Bureau et de l'Organisation.

Arrangement institutionnel

Le Coordonnateur ou la Coordonnatrice exerce ses fonctions sous l’autorité du Représentant résident adjoint chargé du Programme du PNUD et sous la supervision du responsable du Pilier Gouvernance efficace et résilience aux crises.

Le poste travaille en lien avec la Delivery Unit de la Primature, les institutions nationales et provinciales, les partenaires d’exécution, les équipes du PNUD, la BAD et les organisations de la société civile concernées.

Competencies

Core

Obtenez des Résultats :

NIVEAU 3 : Fixer et aligner des objectifs ambitieux et atteignables pour plusieurs projets, avoir un impact durable.

Pensez de Manière Innovante :

NIVEAU 3 : Atténuer de manière proactive les risques potentiels, développer de nouvelles idées pour résoudre des problèmes complexes.

Apprentissage Continu :

NIVEAU 3 : Créer et exploiter les opportunités pour élargir les horizons, diversifier les expériences.

S'Adapter avec Agilité :

NIVEAU 3 : Initier et défendre le changement de manière

Agir avec Détermination :

NIVEAU 3 : Pensez au-delà des tâches/obstacles immédiats et agissez pour obtenir de meilleurs résultats.

S’Engager et s’Associer :

NIVEAU 3 : Connaissances politiques, capacité à naviguer dans un environnement complexe, capacité à promouvoir la collaboration interinstitutionnelle.

Favoriser la Diversité et l’Inclusion :

NIVEAU 3 : Apprécier les avantages d’une main-d’œuvre diversifiée et défendre l’inclusion

Compétences transversales et techniques

Domaine thématique

Nom

Définition

Gestion d'entreprise

Planification et gestion de projet

- Capacité à traduire la stratégie en plans de travail, calendriers et livrables, puis à en suivre l’exécution.

Orientation et stratégie de l’organisation

Réflexion sur le système

- Maîtriser l’analyse objective des problèmes et savoir faire preuve de discernement pour comprendre comment des éléments interdépendants coexistent au sein d’un processus ou d’un système global. Déterminer en quoi la modification d’un élément peut influer sur d’autres parties du système.

Gestion d'entreprise

Coordination institutionnelle et partenariale

- Capacité à conseiller les autorités publiques, à faciliter la coordination interministérielle et à assurer la concertation avec les partenaires techniques et financiers.

Gestion d'entreprise

Communication et qualité de service

- Capacité à rédiger et synthétiser avec clarté, à communiquer à l’oral et à fournir un service adapté aux interlocuteurs internes et externes.

Gestion d'entreprise

Suivi de la performance

- Capacité à fournir régulièrement aux managers et aux parties prenantes clés un retour d'information sur la cohérence ou l'écart entre les activités planifiées et réelles ainsi que la performance et les résultats du programme.

Technique - Finance

Gestion budgétaire

- Capacité à élaborer et à suivre le budget du projet et à coordonner son exécution avec les équipes concernées.

Gestion de programme

Gestion des risques

- Capacité à identifier les risques d’exécution et à suivre les mesures correctives avec les responsables concernés.

Required Skills and Experience

Formation:

- Un diplôme universitaire supérieur (Master’s ou équivalent) en sciences sociales, notamment en droit, économie ou sciences politiques, en gestion de projets, en administration des affaires ou administration publique, en relations internationales, en finances ou dans une discipline connexe est requis, OU

- Un diplôme universitaire de premier cycle (Licence) dans les domaines sus mentionnes associé à 2 années supplémentaires d'expérience qualifiante sera dûment pris en considération à la place du diplôme universitaire supérieur

Expérience professionnelle pertinente

- Minimum 5 ans (avec le Master) ou 7 ans (avec la Licence) d'expérience professionnelle en gestion de projets ou de programmes, dont au moins quatre ans dans l’administration publique ou le développement public est requise.

Compétences requises

- Expérience de la gestion de projets et de ressources humaines dans le cadre d’un fonds commun multidonateurs.

- Bonne connaissance prouvée des enjeux du développement national et du contexte social, politique et institutionnel congolais.

- Expérience du travail avec la Primature, la fonction publique, les ministères, les entreprises publiques, les partenaires au développement, les organisations de la société civile et les structures communautaires.

- Très bonne connaissance prouvée du droit pénal national et international, des procédures pénales et des instruments internationaux pertinents.

- Deux expériences similaires en priorisation de projets et en gestion de projets ou de programmes.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Description du bureau/unité/projet

Le Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement (PNUD) est une organisation internationale avec plus de 17 000 employés travaillant dans environ 170 bureaux dans le monde pour aider les gouvernements à développer des politiques, des institutions et des partenariats solides pour atteindre le Programme de développement durable et ses 17 objectifs de développement durable à l’horizon 2030. Dans le cadre de son mandat, le PNUD contribue aux efforts des pays dans le renforcement de leurs capacités de résilience face aux effets du changement climatique et à la gestion durable des ressources naturelles.

Afin de concrétiser et de renforcer son engagement en faveur de la conservation et de la gestion durable des forêts algériennes, le PNUD met en œuvre une initiative en partenariat avec la Direction Générale des Forêts (DGF) et le soutien du Fonds pour l’Environnement Mondial (GEF), visant à promouvoir la restauration et la gestion forestière durable de l’écosystème de Pin d’Alep en Algérie. L’écosystème de Pin d’Alep, qui s’étend sur plus d’un million d’hectares dans les Hauts Plateaux, est soumis à des pressions croissantes liées à la dégradation des terres, aux effets du changement climatique (sécheresse, incendies, attaques parasitaires) et aux activités anthropiques non durables. Face à cette situation, le PNUD Algérie soutient la Direction Générale des Forêts afin de mettre en œuvre une série d’actions visant à restaurer les paysages forestiers dégradés, renforcer les capacités de gestion durable des forêts et contribuer au développement des économies locales dans les wilayas ciblées.

À la lumière de ce qui précède, le bureau du PNUD à Alger prévoit de recruter un/e Coordinateur/trice de projet pour soutenir l’exécution et la mise en œuvre de l’initiative « Restauration et Gestion Forestière Durable de l’Écosystème de Pin d’Alep en Algérie ». Le/la coordinateur/trice devra travailler en collaboration avec l’équipe programme Nature, Climat et Énergie et avec la Direction Générale du Projet, et devra prévoir des déplacements fréquents dans les wilayas d’intervention.

Portée des travaux

En étroite collaboration directe du Directeur National du projet et la supervision directe du Directeur National du projet et du chef d'équipe du portefeuille Nature, climat et énergie du PNUD, l'objectif principal de la mission est de coordonner et de gérer les activités prévues dans le cadre de l’initiative d’appui à la DGF.

Le/la Coordinateur/trice du projet travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le Directeur National du Projet, l’associé(e) administratif (ve) et financier (e) et Team Leader du portefeuille Nature, Climat et Énergie du Bureau Pays du PNUD ainsi qu'avec les diverses parties prenantes parmi lesquelles, principalement, la Direction Générale des Forêts et le Ministère de l’Agriculture et du Développement Rural et de la Pêche.

Résumé des fonctions:

- Gestion de projet : Assurer la gestion administrative et financière du projet selon les règles et procédures du PNUD, et veiller à la réalisation des activités et l’atteinte des résultats du projet dans les délais fixés via un plan de travail détaillé ; superviser le travail des coordinateurs(trices) locaux(les) déployées dans les 3 wilayas ciblées par le projet

- Appui et conseil technique : Veiller à la qualité des produits techniques et à la coordination des travaux techniques, au besoin ;

- Appuyer le développement de réseaux/partenariats : Appuyer la communication des résultats, le développement du réseau de parties prenantes à impliquer dans le projet, et assurer la circulation de l’information et bâtir des relations en vue de maximiser l’engagement des acteurs dans le processus de mise en œuvre du projet

Axe 1 – Gestion administrative, financière et opérationnelle du projet

Le/la Coordinateur/trice assure la gestion quotidienne du projet conformément aux règles, procédures et politiques du PNUD (POPP), notamment :

- Coordonner et superviser le travail des coordinateurs(trices) locaux(les) déployées dans les 3 wilayas ciblées par le projet

- Coordonner le travail de l’équipe chargée de préparer et réviser les plans de travail et les programmes financiers, veiller à la soumission dans les délais des rapports financiers et des rapports d’avancement trimestriels, du rapport annuel du projet et autres rapports ;

- Élaborer et mettre à jour les plans de travail annuels (PTA) et pluriannuels du projet, en coordination avec la DGF et l'équipe NCE du PNUD, et en assurer le suivi continu

- Gérer le cycle de vie du projet : planification, mise en œuvre, suivi, ajustements et clôture

- Assurer la liaison permanente entre les consultants, l'UGP, la partie nationale (DGF/MADR) et le bureau de pays du PNUD

- Planifier et coordonner les activités de terrain sur les trois sites du projet (Telagh, Beni Imloul, Senalba) et y effectuer des missions régulières de supervision

- Identifier, suivre et atténuer les risques liés à la mise en œuvre du projet

- Organiser les réunions périodiques du Comité de Pilotage (Board de Projet) et en assurer le secrétariat et le suivi des décisions

- Préparer les rapports d'avancement : rapports mensuels d'activités, rapports trimestriels, Rapports annuels de mise en œuvre (PIR) destinés au GEF, et rapport de fin de projet

- Assurer le suivi des décaissements et des dépenses par rapport aux budgets approuvés, en coordination avec l'assistant(e) administratif(ve) et financier(ère)

- Préparer et soumettre les rapports financiers trimestriels au PNUD

- Mettre à jour régulièrement les Indicateurs de Base du GEF (Core Indicators 3, 4, 6 et 11) pour les rapports d'étape et les évaluations (MTR et TE)

Axe 2 – Supervision technique et assurance qualité des livrables du projet

Le/la Coordinateur/trice veille à la qualité scientifique et technique des produits du projet :

- Rédiger et valider les Termes de Référence pour le recrutement de consultants, d'experts et de prestataires (experts en SFM/FLR, spécialistes en PSE, experts genre, M&E, etc.) recrutés par le PNUD

- Superviser, orienter et évaluer les travaux des consultants recrutés par le PNUD, et valider leurs livrables en coordination avec la DGF, le DNP, le PNUD et les parties prenantes concernées.

- Veiller à l'intégration transversale des questions de genre et d'inclusion sociale dans tous les livrables et activités du projet (marqueur genre GEN 2)

- Suivre la mise en œuvre des outils de sauvegarde environnementale et sociale (ESMF, SESP) et veiller au respect des normes environnementales et sociales du PNUD

- Contribuer aux apports techniques permettant d'aligner les produits du projet avec la Loi 23-21 sur les forêts et des stratégies nationales de développement forestier

- Apporter un appui à la sélection des experts et consultants/prestataires du projet, et prendre part au processus de sélection en cas de besoin ;

Axe 3 – Communication, partenariats et gestion des connaissances

Le/la Coordinateur/trice est responsable de la visibilité du projet et de la mobilisation des parties prenantes :

- Entretenir des relations de travail constructives avec l'ensemble des parties prenantes du projet

- Appuyer l'élaboration et la mise en œuvre de la stratégie de communication du projet, en lien avec le/la chargé(e) de communication de la DGF et du PNUD

- Fournir les éléments nécessaires à la production d'articles, notes d'information, messages-clés et supports de communication relatifs aux résultats et enseignements du projet

- Assurer une veille active sur les initiatives complémentaires (FAO, IFAD, GEF SGP, programmes gouvernementaux) pertinentes pour les thématiques du projet

- Promouvoir le partage des bonnes pratiques, des enseignements tirés et des innovations du projet au sein des réseaux nationaux et internationaux pertinents

- Assurer les formations et le partage des connaissances

Le titulaire du poste accomplit d'autres tâches relevant de son profil fonctionnel, jugées nécessaires au bon fonctionnement du Bureau et de l'Organisation.

- Résultats attendus :

Sur la base de la description détaillée des tâches qui précède, les résultats attendus du/de la coordinateur/tric du projet, seront principalement :

- Mise en œuvre efficace et dans les délais du Plan de Travail Annuel du projet

- Qualité et conformité de tous les livrables techniques du projet aux standards du PNUD et du GEF

- Rapports financiers et programmatiques soumis dans les délais impartis

- Comité de Pilotage du Projet fonctionnel et réuni au moins deux fois par an

- Intégration effective du genre et des sauvegardes dans tous les aspects du projet

- Mobilisation active et constructive des parties prenantes à tous les niveaux

- Promouvoir le plaidoyer sur les tendances du développement et les opportunités de collaboration, en coordination avec les partenaires du projet, les parties prenantes et le personnel de communication du PNUD.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Dispositif institutionnel

Le/la coordonnateur/trice travaillera en étroite collaboration directe du Directeur National du projet et sera sous la supervision Directe du Directeur National du projet et du chef d'équipe du portefeuille Nature, climat et énergie du PNUD, l'objectif principal de la mission est de coordonner et de gérer les activités prévues dans le cadre de l’initiative d’appui à la DGF. Le/la coordonnateur/trice assurera la supervision de l’équipe des coordinateurs(trices) locaux(les) composée de trois (3) personnes déployées dans les trois wilayas visées par le projet.

Compétences :

Essentielles

Atteindre des Résultats

Niveau 2 : Faire monter en échelle les solutions et simplifier les processus, tout en équilibrant rapidité et précision dans l’exécution du travail.

Pensée Innovante

Niveau 2 : Proposer de nouvelles idées / être ouvert à de nouvelles approches, démontrer une pensée systémique et intégrée.

Apprendre en Continue

Niveau 2 : Sortir de sa zone de confort, apprendre des autres et soutenir leur apprentissage.

Adapter avec Agilité

Niveau 2 : Adapter les processus et approches à de nouvelles situations, impliquer les autres dans le processus de changement.

Agir avec Détermination

Niveau 2 : Être capable de persévérer et de gérer simultanément plusieurs sources de pression.

Engager et Partenaires

Niveau 2 : Être facilitateur/intégrateur, rassembler les personnes, construire et maintenir des coalitions/partenariats.

Permettre la Diversité et l’Inclusion

Niveau 2 : Faciliter les conversations pour rapprocher les points de vue et tenir compte de la diversité dans la prise de décision.

Gestion du personnel

Les compétences du PNUD en matière de gestion du personnel sont disponibles sur le site dédié.

Compétences transversales et techniques

Intitulé

Capacité à élaborer des stratégies efficaces et à fixer des priorités en cohérence avec les objectifs du PNUD, sur la base d’une analyse systémique des défis, des risques et des opportunités clés ; capacité à articuler la vision avec la réalité du terrain et à créer des synergies.

Pensée systémique

Capacité à utiliser une analyse et un jugement objectifs pour comprendre comment des éléments interreliés coexistent dans un processus ou un système global, et à considérer comment l’alternance d’un élément peut avoir un impact sur d’autres parties du système.

Gestion opérationnelle

Capacité à planifier, organiser, hiérarchiser et contrôler les ressources, les procédures et les protocoles afin d’atteindre des objectifs spécifiques.

Capacité à gérer des programmes et des projets en mettant l’accent sur l’amélioration de la performance et des résultats démontrables.

jobs.title: Intern - Green Transition (2 positions)
jobs.description:
BACKGROUND

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

CORPORATE BACKGROUND

As the United Nations lead agency on international development, UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. We help countries to develop policies, leadership skills, partnering abilities, institutional capabilities, and to build resilience to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals. Our work is concentrated in three focus areas; sustainable development, democratic governance and peace building, and climate and disaster resilience.

INTERNSHIP OFFICE BACKGROUND

The UNDP Seoul Policy Centre (USPC), established in 2011, represents UNDP in the Republic of Korea (ROK), works with the ROK on international development priorities, and shares development experience and technical expertise of the ROK with other countries. As one of UNDP’s global policy centres, USPC works as a facilitator of innovative development cooperation for the achievement of the SDGs in four thematic areas of i) digital and AI, ii) governance and gender, iii) green transition, and iv) private sector engagement and development.

Building on the unique development experience of the ROK and UNDP’s wide Global Policy Network, USPC facilitates knowledge exchanges of SDG-enabling development solutions in the above-mentioned thematic areas through its signature ‘SDG Partnership’ country-support programme and other initiatives, and brokers partnerships between the ROK and other countries to help tackle development challenges.

USPC offers a small group of outstanding final year undergraduate, and graduate students, the opportunity to acquire direct exposure to UNDP’s work and gain technical knowledge and experience in international development and multilateral cooperation.

USPC work on environmental issues started in 2017. Since then, it has evolved to encompass different processes, workstreams and partnerships. USPC has worked on projects related to waste management, wastewater management and sustainable energy. Currently, the Green Transition team is implementing sustainable forestry projects (including both community-based forestry and forest fire prevention) with SDG Partnership programme in Ecuador, El Salvador, Namibia, and Zambia. The Green Transition portfolio is also expanding to new thematic areas such as circular economy (solid waste management, plastics, wastewater), carbon markets and energy. Two pilot projects are currently being implemented: one with Mongolia and the Korea Environment Corporation (K-eco) on Carbon Market and Emissions Trading System (ETS), and the other on circular economy and plastic waste management with Costa Rica.

You are invited to join a small, but vibrant team. Whereas the focus of your assignment will be on the tasks outlined in this Terms of Reference, you need to expect considerable amount of multi-tasking and supporting other members of the team.

For more information on USPC’s work, please visit the website: https://www.undp.org/policy-centre/seoul.

DUTIES

The intern will assist in the following duties and responsibilities:

Assist and Support to Green Recovery and Transition Activities (90%):

Policy Research, Analysis and Translation

- Conducting research and producing publications on various issues related to international development cooperation, including the Sustainable Development Goals and the ROK’s development experiences (e.g., sustainable forestry, environment & green economy topics such as circular economy, energy, carbon pricing (Paris Agreement Article 6 and ETS), sustainable/climate finance, and digital transition);

- Documenting and packaging the ROK’s development experiences and lessons learned from an international perspective as a basis of knowledge exchange and triangular cooperation;

- Translating publications, papers, web content, and other materials from English to Korean and vice-versa.

Project Management & Event Organization

- Providing support in the organization of meetings and events, including international conferences, workshops, webinars and study visits, including through drafting concept notes, coordinating with co-organizers in the ROK and abroad, supporting logistical & travel arrangements, assisting with substantive preparations, note-taking, photo documentation, and providing technical support for webinars;

- Supporting the design and implementation of pilot projects and partnership activities to share the ROK’s specific experiences with developing countries;

- Liaising with partners – at the UNDP HQ, Regional hubs, and UNDP Country Offices as well as various governments, non-governmental organizations and academia on various aspects of programme implementation.

Communication, Administrative and Operations Support

- Supporting communications and advocacy infrastructure (website, social media channels, media presence, public outreach) to ensure effective advocacy on USPC’s key focus areas related to Green Transition;

- Providing holistic support across all aspects of office operations and staff support including key tasks such as the high-level visits from UNDP headquarters and partner countries;

- Supporting administrative and communication tasks as necessary for the day-to-day operation of the office.

Other (10%):

- Supporting other/ad hoc activities as seen relevant and needed.

COMPETENCIES

General:

- Takes initiative and works independently with minimum supervision.

- Upholds highest standards of integrity, discretion, and loyalty.

- Shows excellent organizational, interpersonal, communication, and administrative skills.

- Able to multitask, balance multiple responsibilities, and meet deadlines.

- Shows commitment to UNDP’s vision, mission, and strategic goals.

- Able to work in a multicultural environment and be aware of political sensitivities.

Communication Skills:

- Speaks and writes clearly and effectively.

- Listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others, and responds appropriately.

- Asks questions to receive further clarity on requests and exhibits interest in having two-way communication.

- Tailors language, tone, style, and format to match the audience.

Teamwork:

- Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational and unit goals.

- Solicits input by genuinely valuing others' ideas and expertise and willingness to learn from others.

REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS

Education:

Applicants to the UNDP internship programme must at the time of application meet one of the following requirements:

- Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme (such as a master’s programme, or higher);

- Be enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree programme (such as a bachelor’s degree or equivalent);

- Have recently graduated with a university degree and, if selected, must start the internship within one year of graduation;

- Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional traineeship program and undertake the internship as part of this program.

Field of study: environmental policy/env. science/env. engineering, geography, natural resource economics, economics, climate science, energy, international studies or related area.

Experience:

- Prior experience on environmental and climate projects and /or policy research is desirable;

- Familiarity with basic aspects of project management is desirable;

- Familiarity with issues related to green transition, development and digitalization is desirable;

- Experience writing analytical pieces on relevant issues is desirable;

- Prior experience in Korean-English translations would be an asset;

- Proficiency or prior experience in using Zoom and other digital tools would be preferable.

IT skills:

- Knowledge of/proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office productivity tools;

- Proficient in hosting Zoom and other web-based meetings and seminars;

Language skills:

- Fluency in oral and written English is required;

- Fluency in oral and written Korean is a major asset;

- Knowledge of another UN language is also an asset.

APPLICATION

To apply please include in your application one pdf file that includes:

- Your resume in a format of your choosing;

- Cover letter (max. 1 page) including information about:

1. Your interest to apply for an internship with UNDP / UNDP Seoul Policy Centre.

2. Your general interest in issues related to the topic of Green Transition.

VISA

Interns are responsible for obtaining necessary visas and arranging travel to and from the duty station where the internship will be performed. The internship opportunities are exclusively available to individuals who possess the legal right to reside and work in the Republic of Korea (ROK). Any applicant would need to have legal permission to carry out an internship in ROK and, for non-Korean applicants, would need to fulfill the visa requirements as set by ROK.

INTERNSHIP CONDITIONS

- UNDP will not pay interns for the internship but will provide a monthly stipend in accordance with the provisions of the UNDP internship policy (as reference, the stipend for 2026 is set at KRW 1,169,728 per month;the stipend amount for 2027 is subject to change); all other expenses connected with the internship will be borne by the intern or the sponsoring government or institution;

- UNDP accepts no responsibility for costs arising from accidents and/or illness or death incurred during the internship;

- Interns are responsible for obtaining necessary visas and arranging travel to and from the duty station where the internship will be performed;

- Interns are not eligible to apply for, or be appointed to, any post in UNDP during the period of the internship;

- Interns must provide proof of enrolment in health insurance plan;

- Interns are not staff members and may not represent UNDP in any official capacity;

- Interns are expected to work full time but flexibility can be allowed for education programmes;

- Interns need to obtain financing for subsistence and make own arrangements for internship, travel, VISA, accommodation, etc.

- Interns will accrue leaves at a rate of 1.5 days per month and will be granted off-days on official UN holidays for the Republic of Korea. If exceptional leave arrangements are necessary, requests must be submitted to and approved by the supervisors in advance to ensure adequate office arrangements.

Disclaimer

Non-discrimination

UNDP has a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and misconduct, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles.

UNDP is an equal opportunity and inclusive employer that does not discriminate based on race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, and culture. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization in fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. Learn more at undp.org or follow at @UNDP

The project supports the Republic of Suriname to prepare and submit its First Biennial Transparency Report (BTR1) and the combined Fourth National Communication and Second Biennial Transparency Report (NC4/BTR2) under the UNFCCC and Paris Agreement. The project is implemented at national level under the NIM modality, with the Ministry of Oil, Gas and Environment (OGM) as Implementing Partner. It is financed by a GEF grant of USD 1,233,000 administered by UNDP and has a planned duration of 52 months, from 22 December 2026 to 22 April 2031. The Project Management Unit (PMU) will be located in OGM, if physical office space is available. The PMU comprises the Project Coordinator and the Project Associate. The technical preparation of BTR1 and NC4/BTR2, including the greenhouse gas inventory, the electronic reporting tables and the report chapters, is carried out by a technical team and consultants recruited under separate terms of reference. The project focuses on strengthening national capacity for transparent and consistent greenhouse gas inventories, reliable climate data and MRV systems, tracking mitigation and adaptation action, and stakeholder engagement, awareness and outreach. BTR1 is planned for submission by December 2027 and the combined NC4/BTR2 by December 2029.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Support the project team to ensure effective project planning and implementation.

- Assist the Project Coordinator in day-to-day management and oversight of BTR1 and NC4/BTR2 project activities, including administrative, operational and monitoring tasks, in accordance with the Project Document, approved annual work plans and UNDP POPP/SOP requirements.

- Compile, organize and summarize project information and data to support annual and quarterly work planning, budget preparation, procurement planning, implementation arrangements and management decisions.

- Support coordination of consultants, contractors and responsible partners and monitor delivery of agreed outputs, escalating delays, quality issues or implementation bottlenecks to the Project Coordinator.

- Support compliance of project business processes with UNDP Project Operational Policies and Procedures (POPP), Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), the Project Document and applicable agreements with responsible partners.

- Maintain complete and accessible hard-copy and electronic project records, including progress reports, technical reports, contracts, correspondence, meeting minutes, work plans, financial documentation and monitoring evidence.

- Support mainstreaming of gender equality and social inclusion in project implementation, data collection and reporting, including compilation of sex-disaggregated information and gender-related project results.

- Provide administrative and logistical support for project meetings, workshops, consultations, field missions, study visits, roundtables, Project Board meetings and other project events.

2. Support partnerships and stakeholder coordination.

- Maintain and regularly update stakeholder and partner databases, contact lists, engagement records and coordination trackers.

- Support regular communication with government counterparts, consultants, technical experts, responsible partners and beneficiaries, ensuring timely follow-up on actions and feedback.

- Support stakeholder consultations and participatory processes required for development and validation of BTR1 and NC4/BTR2, including engagement of women, Indigenous and tribal peoples civil society and other relevant stakeholders,.

- Support project visibility and communication activities and the dissemination of project outputs, lessons learned and relevant climate transparency information.

3. Provide support to monitoring, evaluation, financial monitoring and reporting.

- Assist implementation of the project Monitoring and Evaluation framework and maintain systematic records of indicators, targets, milestones, deliverables and results for Components 1–3.

- Collect, compile, quality-check and present information for monitoring project implementation against approved results, work plans and targets, including information required for audit and Project Board review.

- Support preparation of project progress reports, annual status information, financial and narrative inputs, combined delivery reporting and the End of Project Report, ensuring consistency with donor and UNDP reporting requirements.

- Support the Project Coordinator in assembling the documentation for the project milestones and deliverables set out in the Project Coordinator’s terms of reference, including the inception package, quarterly progress reports, Project Board dossiers, annual Project Implementation Review inputs, and evidence files for the mid-term review and terminal evaluation.

- Maintain records of project funds, expenditures and commitments; monitor expenditures against the approved project budget and work plans; identify variances and provide timely information to the Project Coordinator for corrective action.

- Prepare draft FACE forms, Itemized Cost Estimates and supporting expenditure documentation for review by the Project Coordinator and certification by the authorized official of OGM, in accordance with UNDP HACT procedures.

- Maintain the project asset register and support preparation for NIM audits and spot checks, including compilation of supporting documentation and follow-up of agreed recommendations.

- Support project risk management by maintaining risk and issue trackers, monitoring emerging risks and following up on agreed mitigation measures.

- Assist with monitoring missions and site visits, including preparation of agendas, documentation, logistics and follow-up actions, and support validation of reported progress.

4. Support procurement, contracting and operational processes.

- Support procurement and contracting processes for individual consultants, companies and other service providers in accordance with UNDP procurement procedures and the approved project procurement plan.

- Support preparation and processing of Terms of Reference, requests for quotations/proposals, contracts, purchase orders, travel arrangements and other operational documentation, as assigned.

- Track procurement and contracting actions, deliverables and payment milestones and maintain complete supporting records.

- Coordinate with UNDP Country Office operations and finance teams on recruitment, contracting, procurement, travel and payment processing for project implementation.

- Support cost-effective and timely delivery of project activities and communicate operational bottlenecks and proposed solutions to the Project Coordinator.

5. Support knowledge building, knowledge sharing and capacity development.

- Assist in organizing training, briefings and capacity-building activities.

- Support compilation and systematization of lessons learned, good practices, project knowledge products, tools, datasets and other resources generated through the BTR1 and NC4/BTR2 processes.

- Support dissemination of relevant data, lessons learned and good practices within UNDP, nationally and through regional/international knowledge networks and communities of practice.

- Maintain an organized repository of project knowledge resources,and support timely sharing of approved materials with OGM, UNDP, project partners and other stakeholders.

6. Support data and digital information management.

- Compile, clean, organize and maintain project administrative, financial, monitoring and stakeholder data to support evidence-based project management and reporting.

- Support use of digital tools, databases, spreadsheets and web-based systems for project tracking, documentation, monitoring and information sharing.

- Support quality control of project data and documentation and flag inconsistencies, gaps or missing information for follow-up with relevant counterparts.

- Support the use of appropriate digital platforms for reporting, data sharing, stakeholder engagement and project monitoring, consistent with the Project Document.

7. Support knowledge building, knowledge sharing and capacity building relevant to the project.

- Participate in training and organize briefings on internal procedures for the project staff. Provide support to other capacity building activities, including to the design and delivery of tools, materials for workshops, or platforms that tap into the collective intelligence of communities and mobilize action.

- Provide support in the dissemination and sharing of relevant data and lessons learned within the CO and regionally. Keep pulse on emerging best practices nationally, regionally, and internationally that relate to the work of the project.

- Make sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice. Support compiling and systematizing project knowledge, products and tools as well as their wide distribution to partners.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Required skills: Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and web-based management systems, and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

- Experience in preparation of financial reports and overviews

- Experience in monitoring and evaluation tools

- Experience in procurement procedures of national / international organizations

- Experience with UNDP/GEF or other donor-funded projects

Required language: Fluency in English and Dutch is required
