jobs.title: PBF Secretariat M&E and Communications Analyst [Open to internal and external applicants]
Chargé (e) des Affaires Humanitaires Associé (e) / Chef(fe) de Sous-Bureau (Nationaux uniquement)
jobs.location: Kalemie, Democratic Republic of the Congo
jobs.description:
Conexte

Le Bureau des Nations Unies pour la coordination des affaires humanitaires (OCHA) fait partie du Secrétariat des Nations Unies et relève du Secrétaire général adjoint aux affaires humanitaires et Coordonnateur des secours d’urgence.

En République démocratique du Congo (RDC), OCHA appuie le Coordonnateur humanitaire dans la coordination de la réponse humanitaire, en facilitant une action collective, cohérente et fondée sur les besoins des populations affectées. Son mandat comprend notamment la coordination inter organisations, l'analyse et la gestion de l'information humanitaire, le plaidoyer, la facilitation de l'accès humanitaire et l'appui à la mobilisation des ressources.

Pour assurer sa présence opérationnelle et une coordination de proximité, OCHA RDC dispose de sous-bureaux et d'antennes sur le terrain, dont le Sous-Bureau de Kalemie, auquel le présent poste est rattaché. Selon les besoins opérationnels, le/la titulaire du poste pourrait être réaffecté(e) dans une autre localité de la RDC.

Sous la supervision directe du Chef de Bureau adjoint et la supervision générale du Chef de Bureau d'OCHA RDC, le/la Chargé(e) associé(e) des affaires humanitaires – Chef(fe) de Sous-Bureau de Kalemie assure la représentation d'OCHA et la coordination des activités du sous-bureau dans sa zone de responsabilité.

À ce titre, il/elle facilite les mécanismes de coordination humanitaire, contribue à la planification et au suivi de la réponse, coordonne les évaluations et missions inter organisations et assure une veille régulière de l'évolution du contexte humanitaire, sécuritaire et opérationnel. Il/elle veille également à la collecte, à l'analyse et à la diffusion des informations nécessaires à la prise de décision et à l'identification des priorités humanitaires.

Dans l'exercice de ses fonctions, il/elle entretient un dialogue régulier avec les autorités provinciales et locales, les agences des Nations Unies, les ONG nationales et internationales, le Mouvement international de la Croix-Rouge et du Croissant-Rouge et les autres partenaires concernés. Il/elle assure également une collaboration étroite avec les autres bureaux de terrain et les unités techniques d'OCHA afin de garantir la cohérence des interventions et la circulation efficace de l'information.

Tâches et Responsabilités

1. Représentation et coordination humanitaire:

- Représenter OCHA auprès des autorités provinciales et locales, des agences des Nations Unies, des ONG, du Mouvement de la Croix-Rouge et des autres partenaires pertinents.

- Assurer la coordination humanitaire au niveau provincial, faciliter les mécanismes inter organisations et inter clusters et promouvoir une réponse collective, cohérente et fondée sur les besoins prioritaires.

- Faciliter le dialogue entre les autorités et les partenaires humanitaires, en veillant à la participation effective des acteurs locaux et nationaux.

2. Accès humanitaire, plaidoyer et protection :

- Contribuer à l'amélioration de l'accès humanitaire en identifiant les contraintes opérationnelles, en facilitant le dialogue avec les parties concernées et en soutenant les initiatives de plaidoyer collectif.

- Identifier, analyser et rapporter les principales préoccupations humanitaires, notamment en matière de protection des civils, de déplacements de populations et de sécurité des acteurs humanitaires.

3. Analyse et gestion de l’information :

- Assurer le suivi et l'analyse de l'évolution du contexte humanitaire, sécuritaire et opérationnel, notamment dans les zones à risque, et produire des rapports et notes d'analyse pour appuyer la prise de décision.

- Faciliter la collecte, la consolidation et l'analyse des données relatives aux besoins, aux interventions et aux lacunes de la réponse, en collaboration avec les clusters et les partenaires.

4. Planification, suivi de la réponse et préparation aux urgences :

- Coordonner les évaluations conjointes des besoins humanitaires et contribuer à la définition des priorités de réponse en faveur des populations les plus vulnérables.

- Appuyer les processus de planification humanitaire, notamment l'élaboration et le suivi du Plan de réponse humanitaire, en collaboration avec les clusters et les partenaires.

- Faciliter l'identification des priorités et des lacunes de financement, ainsi que les processus de coordination liés aux allocations du Fonds humanitaire dans la zone de responsabilités.

- Coordonner l'élaboration, l'actualisation et le suivi des plans de contingence inter organisations et contribuer à la préparation et à la réponse aux urgences.

5. Partenariats et complémentarité des interventions :

- Renforcer les partenariats avec les ONG nationales et internationales et promouvoir leur participation aux mécanismes de coordination et de planification humanitaire.

- Favoriser les complémentarités entre les interventions humanitaires, de développement et de paix, dans le respect des principes humanitaires.

- Assurer une collaboration étroite avec les unités techniques d'OCHA pour garantir la cohérence des interventions et la circulation efficace de l'information.

6. Gestion du sous-bureau:

- Assurer la gestion quotidienne du sous-bureau, notamment la supervision du personnel, la planification des activités et le suivi des performances.

- Veiller à la gestion efficace des ressources du bureau, au respect des procédures administratives et à la mise en œuvre des priorités opérationnelles d'OCHA.

- Accomplir toute autre tâche confiée par son supérieur hiérarchique.

Compétences

Professionnalisme : Connaissance et compréhension des questions d'assistance humanitaire, de secours d'urgence et des questions de droits de l'homme connexes. Aptitude à travailler dans des circonstances contraignantes dans un cadre stressant ; persévérer face aux obstacles et aux difficultés ; savoir rester serein et efficace dans des situations difficiles. Encourager l’égale participation des femmes et des hommes dans toutes les activités. Aptitude à tenir les délais impartis, à respecter le budget convenu et à se tenir aux normes ; se conformer aux règles et procédures de l’Organisation.

Aptitude à la communication : Savoir bien s’exprimer oralement et par écrit ; aptitude à écouter les autres, à bien les comprendre et à donner suite comme il convient ; savoir poser des questions aux fins de clarification et à favoriser le dialogue ; aptitude à adapter le langage, le ton, le style et la présentation au public auquel on s’adresse ; aptitude à partager l’information avec tous ceux qu’elle intéresse et tenir chacun au courant. Capacité à rédiger des rapports. La capacité de mener une planification stratégique, une gestion basée sur les résultats ainsi que la rédaction des rapports.

Planification et organisation : Développe des objectifs clairs qui sont cohérents avec les stratégies convenues ; identifie les activités et les missions prioritaires ; ajuste les priorités si nécessaire ; alloue le temps et les ressources nécessaires à l'accomplissement du travail ; prévoit les risques et les éventualités lors de la planification ; contrôle et ajuste les plans et les actions si nécessaire ; utilise le temps de manière efficace.

Souci du client: Aptitude à voir des « clients » en tous les destinataires de services et chercher à voir les choses de leur point de vue; aptitude à établir et entretenir des partenariats productifs avec les clients en gagnant leur confiance et leur respect; aptitude à discerner les besoins des clients et y répondre; aptitude à suivre l'évolution de la situation des clients, sur les plans tant intérieur qu'extérieur, afin d'anticiper les problèmes; aptitude à tenir les clients informés de l'avancement des projets; aptitude à tenir les délais de livraison des produits ou de prestation des services.

QUALIFICATIONS ET EXPERIENCE

Education:

- Un diplôme universitaire de deuxième cycle (Licence/Master ou équivalent : BAC+5) en sciences sociales, sciences politiques, relations internationales, études du développement, action humanitaire ou dans tout autre domaine pertinent est requis.

- Un diplôme universitaire de premier cycle (Graduat/ Bachelor ou équivalent : BAC+3) dans l’un des domaines susmentionnés, assorti d’au moins quatre (4) années d’expérience professionnelle pertinente supplémentaires, peut être accepté en lieu et place du diplôme de deuxième cycle.

Expérience:

- Un minimum de deux (2) années d'expérience professionnelle avec un diplôme universitaire de deuxième cycle (Licence/Master ou équivalent : BAC+5) ou 4 années avec un diplôme universitaire de premier cycle (Graduat/ Bachelor ou équivalent : BAC+3) à des niveaux de responsabilité croissants dans les affaires humanitaires, la coordination interorganisations, la gestion des urgences ou un domaine connexe est requis.

- Une expérience d’au moins trois ans dans la coordination humanitaire sur le terrain, notamment dans des contextes d'urgence complexes, ainsi que dans la collaboration avec les autorités et les partenaires humanitaires, est souhaitable.

- Une expérience d’au moins trois ans en matière d'accès humanitaire, de plaidoyer et de négociation avec différentes parties prenantes est un atout.

- Une expérience d’au moins trois ans dans la supervision d'équipes, la gestion d'un bureau ou la coordination d'opérations humanitaires sur le terrain est souhaitable.

- La connaissance du lieu d’affectation est un atout.

- Maîtrise des outils informatiques standards avec une excellente connaissance des logiciels Word, Excel et PowerPoint est un atout;

- Un engagement et loyauté envers les idéaux des Nations Unies et le mandat d’OCHA est un atout;

- Une excellente communication parlée et écrite, y compris la capacité de transmettre des concepts complexes au personnel à tous les niveaux, dans un style clair et concis ; bonne présentation personnelle est un atout;

- Esprit d’initiative, tact, capacité de négociation, d’analyse et de communication est un atout;

- Usage éprouvé de bonnes relations interpersonnelles et communicationnelles est un atout;

- Autonomie, capacité de travail efficace dans un environnement difficile et multiculturel est un atout;

- Aptitude à travailler de manière productive sous pression et à respecter les délais impartis est un atout.

Langues:

- L’anglais et le français sont les langues de travail du Secrétariat des Nations Unies. Pour le poste publié, la maîtrise du français, à l’oral comme à l’écrit, est requise.

- La connaissance de l’anglais et/ou d’une autre langue officielle des Nations Unies et d’au moins une langue locale constitue un avantage.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNOCHA values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNOCHA is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNOCHA does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Probation

For all new UNOCHA fixed term appointments (FTA), including for staff members being transferred or seconded to UNOCHA under the Inter-Organization Agreement concerning Transfer, Secondment or Loan of Staff, on an appointment of more than one year, continuation of the appointment beyond the initial 12 months is contingent upon the successful completion of a probationary period.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNOCHA reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNOCHA at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

With a total gross domestic product (GDP) of over USD 450 billion, Bangladesh is the second-largest economy in South Asia. Between 2000 and 2019, Bangladesh’s economy registered high GDP growth, averaging around 6% per annum. During this period, there were several notable improvements across different socioeconomic indicators, putting the country on track for a formal graduation from the group of least developed countries (LDCs). Bangladesh’s score on the human development index (HDI) increased from 0.49 in 2000 to 0.68, placing it among countries categorized as medium human development. The national poverty rate fell from over 48% in 2000 to less than 19% in 2022.

Despite the progress, Bangladesh faces several development challenges, and with the current trend, the country is unlikely to meet several Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Bangladesh has been grappling with high inflation. GDP growth is slowing down, and according to the latest estimates, GDP grew by 3.5% in fiscal year 2024-25. Without an uptick in private investment, the economy cannot diversify, a necessary condition for creating decent jobs. With low social spending and weak capacities, the government is constrained from providing quality services to the people. Moreover, Bangladesh is one of the most vulnerable countries to climate change and prone to natural hazards, including climate-induced disasters.

As the UN’s development agency, UNDP has been in Bangladesh since 1972, promoting democratic governance, climate adaptation, environmental protection and inclusive growth, and helping the country to achieve equitable and sustainable development. UNDP has been a close partner of Bangladesh in co-designing policy solutions, building national capacities, and promoting innovations to help meet its developmental aspirations. This entails high-quality policy and technical advice, implementation support, helping Bangladesh to mobilize development financing, and promoting knowledge sharing. The programme portfolio of UNDP Bangladesh is organized in two Programme Clusters: a) Democratic Governance; and b) Resilient and Inclusive Growth (RIG). The Programme Clusters support the achievement of strategic objectives articulated in UNDP’s Country Programme Document (CPD) and the UN’s Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF).

UNDP Bangladesh’s Democratic Governance programming aims to accelerate effective governance so that all citizens can openly and peacefully contribute to Bangladesh’s development story. It focuses on making the country inclusive, capable, rule-based accountable, and transparent by 1) strengthening effective and accountable governance that responds to the need of people in addressing equitable and improved access to justice and rule of law, 2) strengthening civil society and promoting participatory governance to ensure that the voice of all citizens are heard, and 3) enhancing civic, political and economic empowerment of women and youth.

In response to a formal request from the Bangladesh Election Commission (BEC) and a UN Needs Assessment Mission, UNDP Bangladesh developed the BALLOT project to support the electoral process. Following the 13th Parliamentary Election held in February 2026, the BALLOT project is now supporting the BEC in preparing for the upcoming local government elections.

The BALLOT is a three-year initiative designed to strengthen the institutional, technical, and operational capacities of the BEC; create an enabling electoral environment; and promote long-term governance resilience and reform. The project aligns with national priorities, the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF), and UNDP’s Country Programme Document (CPD) Outcome 3.

The project is structured in two phases. Phase I (Jan 2025 – Jun 2026) focused on immediate election support through voter registration updates, civic education, strategic communication, and capacity-building for BEC staff and stakeholders. It also included combating election-related misinformation and gender-based violence. Phase II (Jul 2026 – Dec 2027) aims to institutionalize reforms and strengthen governance mechanisms by expanding regional voter education centers, formalizing stakeholder dialogues, and consolidating support to conduct local body elections.

The BALLOT places strong emphasis on inclusion, gender equality, youth engagement, and digital innovation. Key tools like the iParticipate and eMonitor+ platforms will support voter education and disinformation management. The project also promotes South-South cooperation, sustainable policy reform, and long-term civic engagement through the Electoral Training Institute (ETI) and the Women’s Leadership Academy.

By fostering inclusive, transparent, and peaceful electoral processes, the BALLOT will contribute to building a more accountable, participatory, and resilient democratic system in Bangladesh

Scope of work

Under the overall guidance and direct supervision of the Chief Technical Adviser, and in close coordination with the UNDP Gender Analyst and Programme Analyst, Governance, the Project Analyst (Gender) will provide technical support to the BALLOT project and the BEC to mainstream gender equality and women’s participation across the electoral cycle, including civic and voter education, campaigns and candidate nomination. The Project Analyst will promote women’s meaningful participation, representation, and leadership in electoral and local governance processes. The incumbent will conduct gender analysis and identify barriers to women’s political and electoral participation, support capacity-building and communication initiatives, contribute to the collection and analysis of sex-disaggregated data, and prepare reports, knowledge products and evidence-based recommendations to advance women’s participation in the pre-election, election and post-election periods, in close collaboration with relevant stakeholders.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Analyst will perform the following duties and responsibilities in collaboration with the UNDP and BEC:

- Technical Support

- Capacity Building & Knowledge Management

- Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement

- Reporting, Documentation and Monitoring

1- Technical Support:

jobs.description:

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

2. Office/Unit/Project Description

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience and resources to help people build a better life. We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations.

As a trusted, long-term partner of The Global Fund (GF), UNDP’s value proposition lies in providing an integrated package of development solutions to strengthen institutions to deliver health services. Through its contributions as interim Principal Recipient (PR) and provider of technical assistance in over 53 countries since 2003, UNDP’s provision of integrated policy, implementation and capacity development support to countries has yielded significant health and development results in challenging operating environments. Proactive risk management and investing in sustainability are the cornerstones of UNDP’s portfolio management approach and providing technical assistance to national counterparts during all phases of implementation, strengthening legislation, policies and regulatory frameworks, and building capacities across key functional areas, including programme and financial management, integrated health information systems, procurement and supply chain management.

In Zimbabwe, UNDP is the Principal Recipient (PR) for the Global Fund GC8 HIV grant and is also providing Support Services (Fund Administration) to the Ministry of Health and Childcare (MOHCC) as the continuing Global Fund PR for the Tuberculosis (TB), Malaria and Resilient and Sustainable Systems for Health (RSSH) grants. Additionally, UNDP has been designated the ‘CCM Funding Recipient’ responsible for receiving and managing CCM funding on its behalf. The HIV grant for 2027-2029 aims to contribute towards the achievement of the vision and goals of Zimbabwe National HIV Strategic Plan, 2026-2030.

UNDP Zimbabwe manages Global Fund grants through a dedicated Programme Management Unit (PMU), which provides overall programme oversight, coordination, and operational management to ensure effective, compliant, and results-driven implementation. The PMU oversees financial management, risk management, procurement and supply chain operations, monitoring and evaluation, health information systems, integrated capacity development and reporting in line with Global Fund and UNDP policies and procedures.

Working in close partnership with the Ministry of Health and Child Care (MoHCC), National AIDS Council (NAC), national disease programmes, NatPharm, MCAZ, civil society and community organizations, technical partners, donors, UN agencies, the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM), LFA and the Global Fund, the UNDP’s PMU strengthens national health systems and ensures the uninterrupted delivery of quality health commodities and services. This contributes to improved prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and health outcomes for HIV, tuberculosis, malaria, and broader health system resilience.

3. Scope of Work

Under the direct supervision of the Health Products Management Specialist (NPSA-11), the Health Products Management Specialist (Pharmaceuticals) will provide technical support to the Ministry of Health and Child Care (MoHCC), NatPharm, National Disease Programmes, and other stakeholders to strengthen pharmaceutical commodity management systems. The incumbent will support forecasting and quantification, supply planning, inventory management, procurement monitoring, pharmaceutical logistics information systems, data analytics, and health commodity security for HIV, TB, Malaria, and other public health pharmaceutical commodities.

1. Ensures effective forecasting, quantification, and supply planning for pharmaceutical commodities

• Support national forecasting, quantification, and supply planning exercises for pharmaceutical commodities in collaboration with MoHCC, NatPharm, and National Disease Programmes.

• Analyse pharmaceutical consumption, morbidity, service delivery, stock status, and pipeline data to inform forecasting and supply planning decisions.

• Monitor supply plans and pipeline performance and identify risks of stock-outs, overstocks, expiries, and supply disruptions.

• Prepare and disseminate stock status, pipeline, and commodity security reports for management and stakeholders.

• Support maintenance and continuous improvement of quantification tools, forecasting models, and supply planning systems.

• Monitor implementation of Health Products Management Team (HPMT) forecasts, supply planning assumptions, and agreed actions.

2. Ensures effective pharmaceutical inventory management and commodity security

• Monitor stock status and inventory performance at central, provincial, district, and facility levels.

• Analyse stock-on-hand levels, months of stock, inventory trends, stock variances, and consumption patterns.

• Support implementation of stock redistribution and inventory optimization measures to prevent stock-outs, overstocking, wastage, and expiries.

• Monitor compliance with FEFO (First Expiry First Out) principles and expiry management procedures.

• Review inventory reconciliation reports and recommend corrective actions to improve stock accuracy and accountability.

• Contribute to strengthening inventory management practices and pharmaceutical commodity security across the supply chain.

3. Ensures effective monitoring of procurement plans and supply chain performance

• Monitor implementation of pharmaceutical procurement plans and supply schedules.

• Track purchase orders, shipments, delivery timelines, and supplier performance to ensure uninterrupted availability of health commodities.

• Support procurement implementation reviews and monitor progress against approved procurement plans.

• Prepare procurement tracking reports, expenditure analyses, and implementation status updates.

• Identify and escalate procurement delays, bottlenecks, and supply risks affecting commodity availability.

• Support coordination between procurement, programme, and supply chain stakeholders to facilitate timely resolution of implementation challenges.

4. Ensures effective management of pharmaceutical supply chain information systems and analytics

• Support implementation, utilization, and optimization of eLMIS, ERP, and pharmaceutical inventory management systems.

• Analyse pharmaceutical supply chain data and develop routine dashboards, reports, and performance indicators.

• Monitor data quality, completeness, consistency, and timeliness within pharmaceutical information systems.

• Develop analytical tools and management reports to improve visibility of commodity performance and support evidence-based decision-making.

• Support digitization and automation initiatives that strengthen pharmaceutical supply chain management and reporting.

• Contribute to continuous improvement of supply chain data management processes and systems.

5. Ensures capacity development, systems strengthening, and technical support

• Provide mentoring, coaching, and on-the-job training in forecasting, quantification, supply planning, inventory management, and pharmaceutical logistics.

• Support development and implementation of SOPs, guidelines, job aids, training materials, and knowledge products.

• Participate in HPMT meetings, pharmaceutical technical working groups, quantification committees, and other relevant coordination forums.

• Support implementation of pharmaceutical supply chain strengthening and performance improvement initiatives.

• Provide technical support and guidance to MoHCC, NatPharm, National Disease Programmes, and implementing partners on pharmaceutical commodity management.

• Promote knowledge sharing, documentation of lessons learned, and adoption of best practices in pharmaceutical supply chain management.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

4. Institutional Arrangement

The Health Products Management Specialist (Pharmaceuticals) will work under the direct supervision of the Health Products Management Specialist (NPSA-11).

The Specialist will provide technical support for the management of pharmaceutical commodities, including forecasting and quantification, supply planning, inventory management, procurement monitoring, stock status analysis, and supply chain performance monitoring. The position will work closely with the MoHCC, NatPharm, National Disease Programmes, and other stakeholders to strengthen pharmaceutical supply chain systems and support uninterrupted availability of HIV, TB, malaria, and other essential medicines.

To support national ownership and sustainable capacity development, the Specialist is expected to spend approximately 70% of his/her level of effort embedded within MoHCC and NatPharm, working closely with the Health Products Management Team (HPMT), pharmaceutical logistics, warehousing, and supply chain counterparts to strengthen pharmaceutical commodity management systems, data visibility, and health commodity security.

5. Competencies

Core

Achieve Results - LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively - LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously - LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility - LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination - LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner - LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion - LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Thematic Area Name Definition

Business Management - Results-Based Management: Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools.

Business Management - Risk Management: Identify, assess, monitor, and mitigate supply chain and health products management risks, including stock-outs, overstocks, expiries, and supply disruptions.

Partnership Management - Relationship Management: Ability to establish, maintain, and strengthen strategic relationships with MoHCC, NatPharm, National Disease Programmes, development partners, and other stakeholders.

Business Direction and Strategy - System Thinking: Ability to understand and strengthen complex health products and supply chain systems and identify interdependencies across forecasting, supply planning, warehousing, distribution, and information systems.

Business Development - Knowledge Facilitation: Ability to animate individuals and groups, internally and externally, and to design and facilitate activities, to share and exchange knowledge, information and ideas. Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation, contribution, and exchange.

2030 Agenda - People: Health Support to Global Fund and other Health Programmes

Digital - Supply Chain Information Systems and Analytics: Ability to support implementation and optimization of eLMIS, ERP, dashboards, analytics, and data-driven decision-making for health products management.

6. Minimum Qualifications of the Successful NPSA

Min. Education requirements: Advanced University Degree (Master's Degree or equivalent) in Pharmacy, Supply Chain Management, Public Health, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or related field is required,

OR

University degree (Bachelor's Degree) in the above mentioned fields in combination with an additional two (2) years of relevant experience will be given due consideration in lieu of advanced university degree.

Min. years of relevant work experience

• Minimum 5 years (with master´s degree) or 7 years (with bachelor´s degree) of relevant experience in:

o Pharmaceutical supply chain management.

o Forecasting and quantification.

o Inventory management.

o Pharmaceutical commodity security.

o eLMIS/ERP systems.

o Procurement monitoring and supply planning.

Required skills

• Demonstrated experience in health products management, including forecasting, quantification, supply planning, inventory management, and health commodity security.

• Proven experience analysing stock status, consumption trends, pipeline performance, inventory levels, and supply chain risks to inform decision-making and prevent stock-outs, overstocks, and expiries.

• Demonstrated experience supporting or managing logistics and supply chain information systems, including eLMIS, ERP, warehouse management systems, or related digital supply chain platforms.

• Strong experience in warehouse operations, inventory control, stock reconciliation, cycle counting, FEFO implementation, and inventory performance monitoring.

• Demonstrated experience preparing and reviewing quantification reports, stock status reports, pipeline analyses, supply plans, procurement implementation reports, and supply chain performance reports.

• Experience monitoring implementation of health products management workplans, procurement plans, budgets, purchase orders, and supplier delivery performance.

• Demonstrated experience developing and monitoring supply chain performance indicators, dashboards, analytics, and management information systems.

• Proven experience in capacity building, mentoring, and institutional strengthening of government and partner staff in health products and supply chain management.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

• Experience supporting Global Fund, PEPFAR, USAID, WHO, UNICEF, or other donor-funded health supply chain programmes.

• Experience participating in national forecasting, quantification, supply planning, Health Products Management Team (HPMT), or supply chain technical working groups.

• Experience managing HIV, TB, malaria, laboratory, pharmaceutical, or other public health commodity supply chains.

• Experience working with MoHCC, NatPharm, National Disease Programmes, or similar public health institutions.

• Experience with Zimbabwe's health products management and supply chain systems.

Required Language(s) Fluency in English and national language (Shona and/or Ndebele) is required.

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Working in close partnership with the Ministry of Health and Child Care (MoHCC), National AIDS Council (NAC), national disease programmes, NatPharm, MCAZ, civil society and community organizations, technical partners, donors, UN agencies, the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM), LFA and the Global Fund, the UNDP’s PMU strengthens national health systems and ensures the uninterrupted delivery of quality health commodities and services. This contributes to improved prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and health outcomes for HIV, tuberculosis, malaria, and broader health system resilience.

Scope of Work

Under the overall guidance of the Global Fund Programme Manager and direct supervision of the Head of Programmes, the Digital Health Information Systems Specialist (DHIS2/EHR) will provide strategic, technical and operational support to strengthen Zimbabwe's digital health ecosystem in support of the Global Fund HIV Programme. The incumbent will lead efforts to enhance the design, interoperability, governance, performance and sustainability of DHIS2, Electronic Health Records (EHR), and other digital health platforms to ensure the availability and use of high-quality data for programme implementation, monitoring, reporting and decision-making.

The Specialist will work closely with the Ministry of Health and Child Care (MoHCC), National AIDS Council (NAC), implementing partners and other stakeholders to strengthen digital health systems, information management, interoperability, data governance and institutional capacities. The position will contribute to a national digital health ecosystem that generates reliable and timely data, supports evidence-based decision-making, enables seamless exchange of information across systems, strengthens health programme performance, and promotes long-term sustainability and national ownership of digital health solutions.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Lead Digital Health Systems Strategy, Architecture and Governance

- Provide strategic and technical leadership to strengthen digital health systems architecture supporting HIV programme implementation, monitoring, reporting and achievement of national and Global Fund objectives.

- Support the development, review and implementation of digital health strategies, enterprise architecture, standards, policies, technical specifications and implementation roadmaps aligned with national priorities and Global Fund requirements.

- Conduct assessments of health information systems, business processes, workflows and data flows to identify opportunities for optimization, integration, automation and improved system performance.

- Provide technical guidance on system architecture, database management, metadata governance, interoperability standards and digital health best practices.

- Strengthen governance frameworks, standards, SOPs and policies related to data management, information security, access control, confidentiality and data protection.

2. Strengthen DHIS2, EHR and Health Information Systems Interoperability

- Lead the design, implementation and optimization of interoperability between DHIS2, EHR and other national health information systems to ensure secure and seamless data exchange.

- Support the development and maintenance of APIs, integration frameworks, interfaces and data exchange mechanisms in line with national and international standards.

- Strengthen harmonization of indicators, metadata, registries, organizational structures, facility codes and reporting standards across systems.

- Coordinate system integration testing, user acceptance testing, deployment and troubleshooting activities to ensure functionality, reliability and data integrity.

- Monitor system performance and interoperability effectiveness and recommend continuous improvement measures.

3. Strengthen Strategic Information Management, Data Quality and Analytics

- Strengthen data quality assurance systems, including validation, verification, reconciliation and data quality review processes.

- Monitor and analyse data quality, completeness, timeliness, consistency and accuracy, and support implementation of corrective actions.

- Develop and enhance dashboards, scorecards, data visualizations and analytics tools to support programme monitoring and management decision-making.

- Promote routine analysis and use of data for performance management, forecasting, strategic planning and achievement of national and Global Fund targets.

- Support the generation of strategic information products and reports for stakeholders, management and donors.

4. Ensure Information Security, System Quality Assurance and Sustainability

- Strengthen information security controls, user access management, audit mechanisms and privacy safeguards across digital health systems.

- Support implementation of risk management, business continuity, backup and disaster recovery measures to safeguard data and system functionality.

- Ensure availability and maintenance of system documentation, technical specifications, configuration records, user guides and change management documentation.

- Establish and monitor quality assurance processes to ensure reliability, consistency and sustainability of digital health solutions.

- Promote adoption of sustainable approaches for long-term operation, maintenance and institutionalization of digital health systems.

5. Lead Capacity Building and Institutional Strengthening

- Assess capacity needs and develop capacity-building initiatives for MoHCC, NAC and implementing partners in DHIS2, EHR, interoperability, systems administration and data analytics.

- Deliver training, coaching, mentoring and knowledge transfer programmes to strengthen national technical capacity.

- Develop and maintain training materials, SOPs, user manuals and other knowledge products to facilitate effective system utilization.

- Support progressive transfer of system administration and technical support functions to national institutions to strengthen country ownership and sustainability.

6. Provide Programme Support, Innovation and Stakeholder Coordination

- Provide technical support to Global Fund grant planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, reporting, grant revisions and funding request processes.

- Coordinate with MoHCC, NAC, implementing partners, technical working groups and digital health coordination platforms to ensure alignment of digital health investments and interventions.

- Identify and promote innovative digital health solutions, emerging technologies and best practices to improve programme effectiveness and system performance.

- Contribute to the preparation of technical reports, concept notes, investment cases, operational plans and other strategic programme documents.

- Represent UNDP in relevant technical forums and provide expert advice on digital health priorities, innovations and sustainability initiatives.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Digital Health Information Systems Specialist (DHIS2/EHR & Interoperability) will work under the direct supervision of the Head of Programmes.

The Specialist will serve as the focal point for strengthening DHIS2, EHR, interoperability, digital health governance, data quality, analytics, and strategic information management across the MoHCC, NAC, and other key stakeholders. The position will support a strengthened national digital health ecosystem that delivers high-quality data, improves programme performance and decision-making, and builds sustainable national capacity in digital health systems management and use.

To promote national ownership and capacity transfer, the Specialist is expected to spend approximately 70% of his/her level of effort embedded within MoHCC, working closely with Health Information Systems, Health Informatics, Digital Health, and M&E counterparts.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Digital/Data governance: Knowledge of data science, skills to develop data management tools, organize and maintain databases and operate data visualization

technologies

Business Direction & Strategy/System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Digital/Data strategy and management: Knowledge to draft or execute a data strategy or a data management framework

Information Management & Technology/ Solutions Architecture: Ability to design and manage the Information system architecture supporting corporate business processes. Design integration strategies and approaches to integrate of one or more applications or services to maintain a coherent and effective

IT architecture. Knowledge of ISO 20000 and IT operations. The Open Group TOGAF9 or Open CA, ITIL Master certification, or DevOps or UNDP | People for 2030 – Competency Framework – Technical Competencies (2024)similar certification desirable;

Digital/Data collection: Being skilled in Data Sorting, Data Cleaning, Survey Administration, Presentation and Reporting including collection of Real-Time Data (e.g. mobile data, satellite data, sensor data)

Business Management/Risk Management: Identify and organize action around reducing, mitigating and proactively managing risks

Business Development/Knowledge Generation: Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Advanced University Degree (Master's Degree or equivalent) in Health Informatics, Digital Health, Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Biomedical Informatics, Data Science, Health Information Systems, Public Health with specialization in Health Information Systems, or a related field.

OR

A first-level university degree (Bachelor's Degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional two (2) years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of an advanced university degree

Experience:

-Minimum of 5 years (with master’s degree) or 7 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience at the national or international level in digital health, health information systems, DHIS2, Electronic Health Records (EHR), health systems interoperability, health informatics, strategic information management, health data analytics, or related areas.

Required skills

-Demonstrated experience in the design, implementation, administration, optimization, and support of national or large-scale health information systems, including DHIS2 and/or Electronic Health Records (EHR) platforms.

-Demonstrated experience in strengthening Health Management Information Systems (HMIS), including configuration and management of indicators, metadata, datasets, tracker programs, validation rules, analytics, dashboards, and reporting tools.

jobs.title: Monitoring & Reporting Officer (National Only)
jobs.description:
Background and organization context

Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention and facilitate sustainable solutions.

The position is located in the Crisis Response Division (CRD), Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). OCHA is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA also ensures there is a framework within which each actor can contribute to the overall response efforts. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate for the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention; and facilitate sustainable solutions.

This multiple-duty-station temporary job opening is being advertised for the position of Monitoring and Reporting Officer and is located across a number of OCHA Humanitarian Financing Units (in Uganda, kenya and Mozambique). Under the overall supervision of the Head of Office, the incumbent reports to the Head of Humanitarian Financing Unit/Fund Manager.

The Humanitarian Fund Units in OCHA Regional and Country Offices manage multi-donor country-based pooled funds under the leadership of the Humanitarian Coordinator/Resident Coordinator.

These funds receive unearmarked contributions from donors. The funds are allocated to humanitarian actors for ongoing humanitarian operations and to respond to new emergencies.

Position Purpose

Under the supervision of the pooled fund manager in Mozambique, the Monitoring and Reporting Officer will play a central role in strengthening accountability, effectiveness, and learning within the Humanitarian Funding Unit (HFU). The position is responsible for leading the implementation of monitoring, evaluation, and accountability frameworks that ensure compliance with established standards, promote transparency, and deliver measurable impact among partners and stakeholders.

The Monitoring and Reporting Officer will support evidence-based decision-making by developing and piloting innovative monitoring approaches, documenting best practices, and generating insights on the operationalization of localization strategies. Through active engagement with coordination forums and close collaboration with humanitarian partners, including local and national NGOs, the role facilitates inclusive participation, capacity strengthening, and knowledge sharing across the humanitarian system.

The role will also contribute to strengthening the visibility and strategic communication of humanitarian outcomes by capturing lessons learned, success stories, and good practices; supporting the development of communication and advocacy products; and helping translate monitoring and operational findings into accessible content for donors, partners, and affected communities. In doing so, the position will help raise awareness of the impact of humanitarian action, localization efforts, and pooled fund investments while fostering greater transparency and accountability.

The position will also contribute to the planning and execution of monitoring missions, provide technical guidance to partners, and ensure systematic documentation and dissemination of results, lessons learned, and success stories. By maintaining strong coordination with field offices and stakeholders, the M&E Officer enhances program quality, promotes risk-sharing initiatives, and supports continuous improvement in fund management and delivery.

Overall, the role aims to ensure that the HFU operates in a results-oriented, accountable, and collaborative manner, while advancing localization and strengthening the effectiveness of humanitarian response efforts.

Key Duties and Accountabilities

Under the supervision of the Head of Humanitarian Financing Unit/Fund Manager, the Monitoring and Reporting Officer will be responsible for the following duties:

1.) Strengthening accountability, coordination, monitoring effectiveness and visibility of the Humanitarian Funding Unit (HFU):

- Provide strategic leadership in advancing the HFU’s commitment to accountability, impact, and compliance by ensuring the robust and consistent application of the Accountability and Integrity Tool (AIT). This includes promoting transparency, reinforcing adherence to established operational standards, and fostering a culture of results-oriented performance among implementing partners and stakeholders.

- Represent the HFU in a broad range of coordination mechanisms, including Working Groups, area-based coordination platforms, sector-specific forums, and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) structures. Actively contribute to discussions, influence decision-making processes, and ensure that HFU priorities and perspectives are effectively integrated into inter-agency coordination efforts.

- Identify, conceptualize, and pilot innovative and context-appropriate monitoring models and approaches aimed at strengthening oversight, improving data quality, and enhancing the overall effectiveness and efficiency of Country Fund interventions.

- Work in close collaboration with Resident Coordinator’s Office (RCO) area offices, UNHCR, and implementing partners to strategically plan and execute monitoring missions. Provide hands-on technical assistance during these missions to ensure compliance, strengthen partner capacity, and enhance programme delivery on the ground.

- Maintain continuous and proactive engagement with the broader humanitarian community by participating in joint field missions alongside HFU and OCHA field staff, fostering collaboration, information sharing, and coordinated responses to emerging humanitarian needs.

- Contribute to accountability and transparency by supporting the communication of programme outcomes, funding allocations, and impact to stakeholders.

- Collect, analyse and package monitoring findings into accessible communication products tailored to different audiences, including donors, partners, government counterparts, and affected communities.

2.) Enhance knowledge management, reporting, communication and localization efforts within the HFU framework:

- Design, coordinate, and facilitate webinars and other knowledge-sharing platforms aimed at strengthening the technical and operational capacities of partners, while promoting the exchange of experiences, expertise, and innovative practices across the humanitarian ecosystem.

- Systematically identify, compile, and analyze localization models and best practices implemented by other humanitarian funds, agencies, and organizations. Ensure that these insights are effectively documented and disseminated to inform strategic decision-making and continuous improvement within the HFU.

- Generate, synthesize, and disseminate evidence on the operationalization of the Kenya Humanitarian Fund’s localization approach by documenting both successful implementation models and key challenges or bottlenecks encountered in practice.

- Develop high-quality analytical products, including case studies, success stories, and practical examples, to effectively communicate lessons learned and showcase impact to the Fund’s Advisory Board and other strategic stakeholders.

- Contribute substantively to the preparation of a wide range of knowledge and communication products, including annual reports, policy and guidance documents, briefing notes, presentations, social media content, and official correspondence, ensuring accuracy, clarity, and alignment with organizational standards.

- Support the production of communication and visibility materials, including factsheets, newsletters, briefing notes, presentations, web content, social media content, and donor updates.

- Develop and disseminate human-interest stories, success stories, case studies, and lessons learned from humanitarian programmes and pooled fund investments.

- Contribute to accountability and transparency by supporting the communication of programme outcomes, funding allocations, and impact to stakeholders.

3.) Provide technical support, foster partnerships, and promote collaborative engagement.

- Deliver tailored, context-sensitive technical guidance and capacity-building support to Local and National NGOs through structured one-on-one consultations, group training sessions, and ongoing advisory support, with the aim of strengthening their operational effectiveness and compliance capacity.

- Support the design, development, and implementation of risk-sharing initiatives with Local and National partners, ensuring that such approaches are aligned with broader programmatic goals while promoting equitable partnerships and sustainable localization outcomes.

- Actively promote and sustain a high level of team cohesion and synergy within the HFU by encouraging collaborative, complementary, and cross-functional approaches to programme implementation and problem-solving.

- Establish and maintain strong, trust-based partnerships and communication channels with a wide range of stakeholders, including UN agencies, NGOs, and government counterparts, to facilitate coordinated, efficient, and impactful programme delivery.

- Undertake additional responsibilities and assignments as required by the HFU Manager, contributing flexibly and proactively to broader OCHA priorities and responding effectively to evolving operational demands and emerging humanitarian contexts.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Expected Demonstration of Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity. Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

Monitoring and Evaluation

Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results.

Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming.

Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Required Education, Experience, Skills and Competencies

Minimum Education requirements

Minimum of 2 years (with Master´s Degree) or 4 years (with Bachelor´s degree) of experience in project monitoring, evaluation and reporting is required.

jobs.title: Auxiliar Operativo de Proyecto para el Establecimiento de Áreas Naturales Protegidas
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

El objetivo general del proyecto Sinergia+ es generar procesos de gestión que fortalezcan a la CONANP y que le permitan convertirse en una institución que planea con base en resultados, con finanzas fuertes y mecanismos de gobernanza y alianzas estratégicas eficaces, que contribuyan a incrementar la conectividad entre ecosistemas representativos para salvaguardar su biodiversidad y equilibrio ecológico.

El proyecto Sinergia+ tiene seis resultados estratégicos: 1) Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP; 2) Gobernanza y fortalecimiento de redes de colaboración; 3) Enfoque de género y fortalecimiento de la participación ciudadana; 4) Incremento de superficie de conservación con enfoque de conectividad ecológica; 5) Conservación y recuperación de especies en riesgo; 6) Proyectos Estratégicos.

En el marco del Proyecto Sinergia+, la persona a contratar contribuirá al fortalecimiento de actividades en apoyo a la Dirección General de Conservación para elaborar las AIR (Análisis de Impacto Regulatorio) de las Declaratorias de las ANP y Programas de Manejo.

Este puesto contribuye al logro de las metas del Resultado 4) Incremento de superficie de conservación con enfoque de conectividad ecológica.

Alcance de Trabajo:

- Recopilar, sistematizar y analizar la información documental para la integración de estudios previos justificativos para establecer áreas naturales protegidas.

- Elaborar y mantener actualizadas bases de datos y tablas de seguimiento sobre los procesos de establecimiento o modificación de áreas naturales protegidas.

- Integrar y resguardar los expedientes de los procesos de establecimiento de áreas naturales protegidas que se asignen.

- Apoyar en la elaboración de respuestas de solicitudes de información, competencia de la Dirección.

- Apoyar en la preparación de reuniones de trabajo y en el seguimiento de los acuerdos que se tomen en ellas.

- Apoyo en la elaboración de informes que le soliciten a la Dirección sobre los proyectos de establecimiento de nuevas establecer áreas naturales protegidas.

- Elaborar las propuestas de presentaciones relacionadas con el establecimiento de áreas naturales protegidas.

Acuerdo Institucional:

El o la persona contratada trabajará bajo la supervisión técnica directa de la Dirección General de Conservación, así como de la Coordinación General del Proyecto Sinergia+.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: NIVEL 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: NIVEL 1 Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructive, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: NIVEL 1 Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: NIVEL 1 Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacía los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: NIVEL 1 Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

- Certificado de Preparatoria(Bachillerato), es requisito.

- Para candidatos/as con Certificado de Preparatoria (Bachillerato), se requieren de al menos 4 años de experiencia comprobable Normatividad ambiental, Áreas Naturales Protegidas, Administración pública,

- Para candidatos/as con Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura, se requiere de al menos 1 año de experiencia en los temas antes mencionados.

- Se dará ventaja si cuenta con Licenciatura en: Ciencias Biológicas, Ciencias Ambientales, Ecología, Recursos Naturales, Geografía o afines; Conocimiento en el Sistema Nacional de Áreas Naturales Protegidas.

jobs.title: Asociado(a) de Gestión de Información Estratégica
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

Fruto del Acuerdo de Colaboración firmado por el Gobierno de México y el Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD), se diseña el proyecto: “Fortalecimiento de las capacidades para el Impulso Económico y la implementación de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible”, que tiene como objetivo colaborar con la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores en el fortalecimiento de sus capacidades para posicionar los intereses de México en el escenario internacional mediante el cumplimiento de sus funciones en materia económica.

En seguimiento a estos objetivos, se impulsan acciones orientadas al fortalecimiento de la diplomacia económica de México, incluyendo la atracción de inversión, la promoción comercial, la interlocución con actores estratégicos y la articulación con Representaciones de México en el Exterior, dependencias federales, gobiernos estatales y organismos empresariales. En este marco, se implementa el Plan Integral de Promoción Económica, mediante misiones comerciales de México al exterior y misiones extranjeras hacia México, la participación de México en ferias internacionales, la canalización de oportunidades de proveeduría e inversión, así como la organización de seminarios de inversión y exportación.

En un contexto internacional marcado por la reconfiguración económica global, se llevarán a cabo las acciones previstas para la presente vacante, mismas que contribuirán a robustecer las capacidades de la SRE en materia de fortalecimiento de alianzas institucionales y apoyo a las prioridades estratégicas de México en el ámbito económico internacional.

Alcance del Trabajo

1.Gestionar la recopilación, integración y sistematización de información estratégica proveniente de distintas áreas de la Cancillería, dependencias gubernamentales y otros actores relevantes, para apoyar las prioridades de diplomacia económica de México.

2.Monitorear la elaboración e integración de documentos de análisis, informes, reportes e insumos institucionales que contribuyan a la toma de decisiones y a la atención de requerimientos estratégicos.

3.Gestionar el monitoreo y seguimiento de indicadores de gestión y resultados, así como la integración de información sobre los avances y actividades de la Unidad.

4.Organizar y monitorear la preparación y actualización de carpetas de trabajo, documentos informativos, presentaciones y materiales de apoyo para reuniones, eventos y actividades institucionales.

5.Administrar y dar seguimiento a proyectos, actividades y compromisos prioritarios de la agenda de diplomacia económica, mediante herramientas de gestión que permitan identificar avances, pendientes y áreas de atención.

6.Gestionar la elaboración de reportes de avance y mecanismos de seguimiento que faciliten la evaluación de resultados, el cumplimiento de objetivos y la atención oportuna de los compromisos institucionales.

Acuerdo Institucional:

La presente vacante estará bajo supervisión directa de la Subsecretaría para América del Norte y la coordinación del proyecto Fortalecimiento de las capacidades para el Impulso Económico y la implementación de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible, quienes evaluarán el desempeño del contratista al término del contrato.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos:

- Certificado de bachillerato es requerido o licenciatura concluida en Relaciones Internacionales, Economía, Ciencia Política, Administración Pública, Políticas Públicas o áreas afines.

- Maestría no es requisito, pero se le dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Al menos 3 años de experiencia para candidatos con licenciatura concluida, en los temas antes mencionados.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Capacidad para atender múltiples requerimientos en plazos cortos.

- Experiencia en comunicación efectiva, excelentes habilidades de comunicación oral y escrita.

Habilidades Deseadas:
