jobs.title: Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist [Open to affected staff and personnel of the PMU, UNDP ZIMBABWE]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience and resources to help people build a better life. We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations.

As a trusted, long-term partner of The Global Fund (GF), UNDP’s value proposition lies in providing an integrated package of development solutions to strengthen institutions to deliver health services. Through its contributions as interim Principal Recipient (PR) and provider of technical assistance in over 53 countries since 2003, UNDP’s provision of integrated policy, implementation and capacity development support to countries has yielded significant health and development results in challenging operating environments. Proactive risk management and investing in sustainability are the cornerstones of UNDP’s portfolio management approach and providing technical assistance to national counterparts during all phases of implementation, strengthening legislation, policies and regulatory frameworks, and building capacities across key functional areas, including programme and financial management, integrated health information systems, procurement and supply chain management.

In Zimbabwe, UNDP is the Principal Recipient (PR) for the Global Fund GC8 HIV grant and is also providing Support Services (Fund Administration) to the Ministry of Health and Childcare (MOHCC) as the continuing Global Fund PR for the Tuberculosis (TB), Malaria and Resilient and Sustainable Systems for Health (RSSH) grants. Additionally, UNDP has been designated the ‘CCM Funding Recipient’ responsible for receiving and managing CCM funding on its behalf. The HIV grant for 2027-2029 aims to contribute towards the achievement of the vision and goals of Zimbabwe National HIV Strategic Plan, 2026-2030.

UNDP Zimbabwe manages Global Fund grants through a dedicated Programme Management Unit (PMU), which provides overall programme oversight, coordination, and operational management to ensure effective, compliant, and results-driven implementation. The PMU oversees financial management, risk management, procurement and supply chain operations, monitoring and evaluation, health information systems, integrated capacity development and reporting in line with Global Fund and UNDP policies and procedures.

Working in close partnership with the Ministry of Health and Child Care (MoHCC), National AIDS Council (NAC), national disease programmes, NatPharm, MCAZ, civil society and community organizations, technical partners, donors, UN agencies, the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM), LFA and the Global Fund, the UNDP’s PMU strengthens national health systems and ensures the uninterrupted delivery of quality health commodities and services. This contributes to improved prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and health outcomes for HIV, tuberculosis, malaria, and broader health system resilience.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the overall guidance of the Global Fund Programme Manager and direct supervision of the Head of Programmes, the Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) Specialist will provide technical leadership and oversight for monitoring, evaluation, strategic information, and performance management of Global Fund-supported programmes. The role will strengthened M&E ecosystem across the PR, MoHCC, NAC, and SRs that delivers complete, timely, and high-quality data; proactively identifies performance gaps; improves achievement of Global Fund indicators and targets; supports evidence-based decision-making; and builds sustainable national capacity for monitoring, evaluation, and strategic information management, focusing on the job descriptions below .

1. Strategic M&E Systems Strengthening and Capacity Development

- Strengthen national and grant M&E systems, tools, frameworks, and reporting mechanisms in alignment with Global Fund, UNDP, and national requirements.

- Support effective use of HMIS/DHIS2, surveillance systems, and other strategic information platforms to improve data availability, completeness, and utilization.

- Provide technical assistance, mentoring, and capacity development to MoHCC, NAC, SRs, and implementing partners on data collection, analysis, reporting, and use of information for programme management.

- Support development and implementation of disease-specific and health systems M&E plans, indicators, guidelines, and reporting tools.

2. Performance Monitoring, Data Analysis and Quality Assurance

- Monitor grant performance against approved targets, workplans, and Global Fund indicators, identifying implementation bottlenecks, emerging risks, and underperforming indicators.

- Conduct routine data verification, data quality assessments (DQAs), on-site data verification (OSDV), and field monitoring visits to improve data accuracy, completeness, consistency, and reliability.

- Analyse epidemiological, programmatic, financial, procurement, and health systems data to assess programme effectiveness and support evidence-based decision-making.

- Provide regular performance alerts, corrective actions, and strategic recommendations to management and stakeholders.

3. Grant Reporting and Performance Management

- Lead compilation, validation, analysis, and timely submission of all Global Fund and UNDP programmatic reports, including quarterly, semi-annual, annual, and ad hoc reports.

- Ensure quality assurance of SR reports and provide timely feedback on reporting gaps, data issues, and corrective actions.

- Coordinate grant performance reviews, management responses, and follow-up on recommendations from the Global Fund, LFA, audits, evaluations, and other assurance activities.

- Develop dashboards, analytical briefs, presentations, and performance reports to support management oversight and donor reporting.

4. Provide Strategic Information, Surveillance and Evaluations

- Coordinate collection, analysis, interpretation, and dissemination of epidemiological, surveillance, survey, and programme data for HIV, TB, Malaria, RSSH, and other grant-supported interventions.

- Support the planning, implementation, and utilization of evaluations, assessments, surveys, operational research, and studies.

- Ensure systematic use of evidence, lessons learned, and best practices to improve programme performance and strengthen national systems.

5. Promote Partnership Coordination and Facilitate Knowledge Management

- Maintain effective collaboration with MoHCC, NAC, SRs, Global Fund, LFA, technical partners, civil society, and other stakeholders on M&E and strategic information matters.

- Facilitate joint monitoring missions, programme reviews, and technical working groups.

- Promote knowledge sharing, documentation of best practices, and continuous improvement of M&E systems and capacities across implementing partners.

6. Perform Other Duties

- The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation

Institutional Arrangement

The Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) Specialist will work under the direct supervision of the Head of Programmes.

The Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) Specialist promotes a collaborative, client-focused, quality and results-oriented approach across grant sub-recipients and stakeholders. S/he works in close collaboration with the PMU functional team, procurement and supply chain management, and finance and admin staff within the UNDP-PMU and the colleagues within the UNDP Country Office and other implementing partners.

The Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) Specialist serves as the focal point for strengthened M&E ecosystem across the PR, MoHCC, NAC, and SRs that delivers complete, timely, and high-quality data; proactively identifies performance gaps; improves achievement of Global Fund indicators and targets; supports evidence-based decision-making; and builds sustainable national capacity for monitoring, evaluation, and strategic information management, and is expected to spend 50% of his/her level of efforts working directly with counterparts

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy /Systems Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Management/Monitoring & Evaluation: Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results. Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Business Management /Results-based Management: Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools.

Digital/ Data governance: Knowledge of data science, skills to develop data management tools, organize and maintain databases and operate data visualization technologies

Business Development/Knowledge Facilitation: Ability to animate individuals and groups, internally and externally, and to design and facilitate activities, to share and exchange knowledge, information and ideas. Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation, contribution, and exchange.

Business Management/Working with Evidence and Data: Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making

2030 Agenda: People/Health: Support to Global Fund and other Health Programmes

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Public Health, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Monitoring and Evaluation, Health Informatics, Demography, Population Studies, Medicine, Health Sciences, or a related field is required. Or

A first-level university degree (Bachelor's degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional two (2) years of relevant experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced degree.

Experience:

Minimum 5 years (with master’s degree) or 7 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible experience in monitoring and evaluation, strategic information, epidemiology, health information systems, public health programmes, or Global Fund/donor-funded health programmes is required.

Required skills

- Demonstrated experience in designing, implementing, and managing comprehensive M&E systems for large-scale health or development programmes.

- Proven experience in monitoring performance against results frameworks, targets, indicators, and workplans, and providing evidence-based recommendations for programme improvement.

- Strong technical expertise in health information and strategic information systems, including DHIS2, HMIS, EHRs, surveillance systems, and routine programme monitoring platforms.

- Demonstrated experience conducting data quality assessments (DQAs), on-site data verification (OSDV), data audits, and data quality improvement initiatives.

- Strong analytical skills with experience in collecting, analysing, interpreting, and presenting epidemiological, programmatic, and performance data.

- Proven experience in preparing high-quality donor reports, performance reviews, dashboards, and analytical products.

- Advanced proficiency in data management, statistical analysis, and visualization tools such as Power BI, Tableau, SPSS, STATA, R, or similar software.

- Demonstrated experience facilitating capacity development, mentorship, and institutional strengthening of government entities, implementing partners, and sub-recipients.

- Strong stakeholder coordination skills and experience working with government institutions, development partners, civil society organizations, and implementing partners.

- Experience preparing or reviewing Performance Update/Disbursement Requests (PU/DRs), Funding Requests, Grant Making documents, Performance Frameworks, and Grant Closure Reports.

- Experience supporting HIV, TB, Malaria, RSSH, or broader public health programmes.

- Experience coordinating evaluations, surveys, surveillance activities, operational research, or epidemiological studies.

- Experience working with UNDP, UN agencies, multilateral organizations, or international donor-funded programmes.

- Demonstrated knowledge of Zimbabwe's health sector, national HMIS architecture, and HIV response.

- Experience developing data visualization products, executive dashboards, and management performance reports.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

Fluency in English and national language (Shona and/or Ndebele) is required

jobs.title: Auxiliar Técnico de Proyecto en Manejo Efectivo de Áreas Naturales Protegidas - Oaxaca
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

El objetivo general del proyecto Sinergia+ es generar procesos de gestión que fortalezcan a la CONANP y que le permitan convertirse en una institución que planea con base en resultados, con finanzas fuertes y mecanismos de gobernanza y alianzas estratégicas eficaces, que contribuyan a incrementar la conectividad entre ecosistemas representativos para salvaguardar su biodiversidad y equilibrio ecológico.

El proyecto Sinergia+ tiene seis resultados estratégicos: 1) Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP; 2) Gobernanza y fortalecimiento de redes de colaboración; 3) Enfoque de género y fortalecimiento de la participación ciudadana; 4) Incremento de superficie de conservación con enfoque de conectividad ecológica; 5) Conservación y recuperación de especies en riesgo; 6) Proyectos Estratégicos

En el marco del Proyecto Sinergia+, la persona a contratar contribuirá al fortalecimiento del ANP mediante la planeación, coordinación, seguimiento y evaluación de acciones de prevención, detección, control y atención de incendios forestales a la Dirección del Área Natural Protegida para el desarrollo y seguimiento de reuniones, recorridos, actividades de campo, coordinación interinstitucional, atención a comunidades y demás acciones necesarias para el cumplimiento de los objetivos institucionales y de conservación del ANP.

Este puesto contribuye al logro de metas del Resultado 1) Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP.

Alcance de Trabajo:

- Asistir en la elaboración de diagnósticos e informes finales de las brigadas de contingencia ambiental.

- Asistir en el seguimiento de la operación y ejecución de los programas de subsidios PROREST y PROCODES, mediante la asesoría, verificación, integración y revisión de expedientes en apego a las reglas de operación y lineamientos de los programas.

- Atender recorridos de vigilancia, inspección y monitoreo biológico de especies y hábitats en el ÁNP.

- Apoyar en la construcción de las metas del Programa Operativo Anual (POA.) de ANP.

- Asistir en actividades de Restauración de ecosistemas.

- Atender actividades de educación y participación comunitaria para el cumplimiento de los objetivos del Plan de Manejo de ANP.

Acuerdo institucional:

El candidato/a contratada trabajará bajo la supervisión técnica directa de la Dirección Regional Frontera Sur, Istmo y Pacífico Sur, así como del/la Coordinador(a) General del Proyecto.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requsitos Académicos Mínimos:

- Certificado de preparatoria/Bachillerato, es requisito.

- Estudios de primer nivel liceciatura en: Biología, Ecología, Agronomía, Ing Ambiental o carrera a fin no es requisito, pero se dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Para candidatos/as con certificado de preparatoria/bachillerato se requieren 3 años de experiencia comprobable en: Acciones de protección y conservación de los recursos naturales.

- Para candidatos/as con Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura en: Biología, Ecología, agronomía, Ing. Ambiental o carrera a fin, No se requiere experiencia.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia en: Elaboración de informes de calidad.

- Experiencia en: Manejo de recursos naturales.

Habilidades Deseadas:

- Conocimiento / Experiencia en: Restauración

- Conocimiento / Experiencia en: Uso y aprovechamiento sustentable

- Conocimiento / Experiencia en: Trabajo en campo y con comunidades,

- Conocimiento / Experiencia en: Educación ambiental e Impartición de talleres y platicas

- Conocimiento / Experiencia en: Proyectos productivos y Programas de Subsidio

- Se dará ventaja si cuenta con Licenciatura en: Biología, Ecología, agronomía, Ing. Ambiental o ca-rrera a fin; Conocimiento en Áreas Naturales Protegidas; monitoreo básico de flora y fauna.

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar

jobs.title: Project Analyst, Conscious Food Systems Alliance (CoFSA) Community Engagement and Alliance Development (Home-Based) (Open to Tier 0,1 & 2)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organisation for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP's policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

UNDP’s 2026–2029 Strategic Plan reaffirms our continued commitment to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals by accelerating structural transformations that advance poverty eradication, reduce inequalities, strengthen resilience, and drive sustainable, climate-aligned development.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policies and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices; advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government, and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas.

As part of GPN in BPPS, the Planet Hub promotes and scales up an integrated approach to deliver UNDP’s environment portfolio across nature, climate, energy, and chemicals and waste, supporting countries in advancing implementation of the Paris Agreement, the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and related multilateral environmental agreements. It coordinates UNDP’s flagship offers—Nature Pledge, Climate Promise, and Energy Moonshot, and Cooling, Circularity and Pollution Prevention initiatives—to meet strong country demand across more than 140 countries. The Hub enables joined-up policy, programming, and financing solutions that accelerate low-emission, nature-positive, and pollution-free development, while strengthening resilience and advancing sustainable, inclusive growth in line with the Strategic Plan.

As part of its Food Systems Strategy, UNDP has established the Conscious Food Systems Alliance (CoFSA), a global movement convened by UNDP that brings together food, agriculture, and consciousness practitioners to cultivate the inner capacities that enable systemic change and regeneration. Publicly launched in 2022 following a two-year incubation phase, CoFSA has since developed a global community, leadership programmes, a resource library, and the Conscious Food Incubator. In 2025–2026, this work reached a major milestone with the announcement of the first Global Conscious Food Systems Summit, to be hosted in partnership with the Royal Government of Bhutan, marking the recognition of conscious food systems as an important dimension of the global food systems agenda.

Scope of Work

The Food Systems Team is looking to engage a Project Analyst for CoFSA Community Engagement and Alliance Development to perform the following tasks:

Coordinate the implementation of CoFSA’s community engagement strategy

- Coordinate and implement CoFSA's community engagement activities, including online and in-person events, webinars, workshops, and learning sessions.

- Develop and strengthen engagement mechanisms that foster active participation, collaboration, and knowledge exchange across the Alliance.

- Coordinate outreach and onboarding of new members and strategic partners.

- Support the decentralization of CoFSA, including the development of regional, thematic, or other community-led hubs and spaces for collaboration.

- Build and maintain strong relationships with members, ensuring regular communication and meaningful engagement opportunities.

Enhancing Digital Infrastructure of the Alliance

- Oversee the maintenance and continuous improvement of CoFSA's membership database and relationship management systems.

- Coordinate the collection, organization, and dissemination of knowledge products, resources, and learning materials to support the growth of the Alliance.

Monitor community engagement and learning

- Design and coordinate community surveys, feedback mechanisms, and engagement tracking to assess participation, identify emerging needs, and inform continuous improvement.

- Prepare analytical summaries and recommendations to strengthen community engagement and Alliance development.

Support strategic post-summit activities within the community

- Support the planning, coordination, and delivery of CoFSA’s post-Summit engagement activities and initiatives.

- Support the development and implementation of CoFSA’s governance system, supporting inclusive participation, transparent decision-making, coordination, and accountability across the Alliance.

Facilitate knowledge sharing and other responsibilities

- Support recruitment processes for Secretariat personnel, including preparing written assessments, participating in interview panels, and contributing to candidate evaluations and selection processes.

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

- Perform other related duties as required to support the effective implementation of the Food Systems Team and CoFSA work programme.

Institutional Arrangement

- The incumbent will work remotely from his/her home-base;

- The incumbent will be supervised by the CoFSA Lead Technical Advisor.

- The incumbent will be given access to relevant information necessary for execution of the tasks under this assignment;

- The incumbent will be responsible for providing her/his own workstation (i.e. laptop, internet, phone, scanner/printer, etc.) and must have access to a reliable internet connection;

- Given the global consultations to be undertaken during this assignment, the incumbent is expected to be reasonably flexible with his/her availability for such consultations taking into consideration different time zones.

Competencies Core

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Development-Knowledge Facilitation

- Ability to animate individuals and groups, internally and externally, and to design and facilitate activities, to share and exchange knowledge, information and ideas.

- Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation, contribution, and exchange.

Business Management-Partnerships Management

- Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and Policies.

Business Management-Communication

- Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

2030 Agenda: Planet-Nature

- Ecosystems and Biodiversity: Green commodities

Business Direction and Strategy-Systems Thinking

Minimum Qualifications of the Successful IPSA

Min. Academic Education

- An advanced university degree (Master´s degree or equivalent) in Economics, International Studies, Agriculture, Development Studies, Environmental Science, or other related fields is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above fields, with two additional years of relevant experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. years of relevant Work experience

- Minimum 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of professional work experience in sustainable development project management support-related functions (planning, communications, reporting, research) is required.

Required skills and competencies

- Experience in supporting projects and initiatives related to food systems and/or agricultural commodities will be an advantage.

jobs.title: ICT Analyst - Cloud Services (Open to all applicants)
jobs.description:
Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Office of Information Technology and Management (ITM) is the organization’s primary provider of high-quality products of ICT systems and Green Energy services to a global network of 155+ country offices and UNDP partners worldwide. Within ITM, the mission of the ITM Smart Infrastructure Services (SIS) is to “Create Smart Facilities, build local Capacity and Inspire and Movement”, which guarantees efficient, innovative, and sustainable management of technologies for UN facilities, and consistency with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The Smart Facility solutions include Green Energy services, Connectivity, Security and IoT, and Cloud Infrastructure Services. ITM offers a framework of best practices to deliver resilient, highly available and sustainable business solutions that flourishing innovation throughout the organization.

The mission of the Cloud Infrastructure Services unit is to offer state of the art Cloud based solutions to the Organization, including Cloud platforms such as Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, Amazon Web Services, as well as cloud-based services such as Mobile Device Management and Cloud Printing service. We do this to maintain organizational productivity using technology, improve stakeholders well-being, optimize financial efficiency, and serve as a showcase for development at local level.

Under the overall guidance of the Cloud Infrastructure Services unit manager, Cloud Services Analyst is to provide technical support for Cloud-based services for the UNDP offices and business units across the globe. The incumbent is required to follow UNDP standard operating procedures for information technology service deliveries.

Duties and Responsibilities

Scope of Work:

Contribute to the performance of UNDP Cloud platform(s):

- Attend to incidents and service catalog requests for the Cloud platform

- Periodically review and keep internal records on the Cloud platform up-to-date

- Update Cloud platform to reflect changes in internal records

Support implementation of Cloud Platform(s) oversight controls:

- Ensure that all Cloud resources have required oversight controls applied

- Monitor and troubleshoot oversight controls assignments

- Review and advise on remediation actions for oversight controls non-compliances

- Assist with implementation of remediation actions

Monitor Cloud Platform(s) costs and update budgets:

- Monitor and update technical controls for cost management

- Escalate and follow up on budget exceptions

- Recommend actions based on consumption forecasts

Monitor Cloud Platform(s) updates and health notifications:

- Monitor Cloud platform’s service health, changes and updates

- Notify and follow up Cloud platform users about health events and upcoming platform changes

Guide and support with audits and assessments of Cloud Platform(s):

- Perform periodic automated assessments of Cloud services

- Assist in complying with audit and assessment requests

Report on compliance status of Cloud Platform(s) resources:

- Provide periodic reports on compliance status of Cloud platform resources and services

- Participate in periodic service review meeting with vendors and suppliers

Facilitate in conducting the training and communications with stakeholders on compliance requirements and updates:

- Facilitate with periodic trainings and workshops on Cloud platform compliance to UNDP ICT community

- Recommend updates to UNDP ICT Policies, Standards and Procedures as it relates to Cloud Platform(s)

- Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement:

- On the day-to-day basis, the Cloud Services ICT Analyst will be working with and directly reporting to the Manager of Cloud Infrastructure Services unit

- The Global ICT Advisor/Chief of SIS has the overall responsibility to guide the team

Competencies

Core:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1:

- Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1:

- Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1:

- Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1:

- Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1:

- Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1:

- Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1:

- Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical:

Background

Job Purpose and Organizational Context

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The UNDP Strategic Plan underscores the organization’s dual imperative to deliver development results with greater efficiency and value for money, while leading by example on sustainability, climate action, and responsible resource use.

Within this context, UNDP has committed to continuously improving the efficiency, effectiveness, and environmental performance of its operations, recognizing that internal operational practices directly affect institutional credibility, partner trust, and staff engagement. The Strategic Plan highlights the need to modernize management practices, strengthen data-driven decision-making, reduce waste and inefficiencies, and align operational systems with UNDP’s broader climate and environmental ambitions.

The Greening Moonshot Initiative, hosted by Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) in collaboration with the Bureau for Management Services (BMS), is UNDP’s flagship, inward-facing transformation effort to reduce the environmental footprint of corporate operations. Through the Greening Moonshot, UNDP has committed to significantly reducing greenhouse gas emissions, improving resource efficiency, and adopting best practices across energy use, procurement, mobility, buildings, and waste management. The initiative is overseen by the Moonshot Task Force and supported by a dedicated Moonshot Secretariat.

Waste management is a highly visible and material component of UNDP’s operational sustainability agenda. As a leading development actor working extensively on waste, circular economy, chemicals, and pollution issues at the country level, UNDP is expected to “walk the talk” by applying the same principles internally. At the same time, sound waste management and resource efficiency practices are increasingly recognized as cost‑reduction and efficiency levers.

The Waste Management Specialist position is associated with the Greening Moonshot team and is designed to strengthen UNDP’s capacity to provide coherent corporate guidance, practical tools, monitoring approaches, and strategic recommendations that support offices worldwide in improving waste management performance in a cost‑effective, context‑sensitive manner.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Waste Management Specialist will support the design, rollout, and continuous improvement of UNDP’s corporate approach to waste management and resource efficiency. The assignment balances technical rigor, operational practicality, and cost‑effectiveness, in line with UNDP’s Strategic Plan and Greening Moonshot commitments.

- Develop and improve corporate waste management guidance and tools Continuously improve and maintain waste management guidance for UNDP offices, covering both non‑hazardous and hazardous waste streams, process to limit waste generation and to assist in designing office-specific strategies. Guidance should reflect sectoral best practices, regional feasibility constraints, and life‑cycle cost considerations, and support offices in making efficient, defensible operational decisions. Tools to be developed by the Waste Management Specialist should leverage advancements in automation, AI and digital solutions to maximize the availability, ease of use and impact of advice and guidance generated for UNDP.

2. Monitoring, data quality, and efficiency improvements

- Guide and support the integration of waste management considerations into UNDP’s environmental monitoring and reporting systems, including the Environmental Management Tool (EMT).

- Develop training materials, deliver webinars, and provide targeted support to focal points to improve data quality, consistency, and usability for management decision‑making.

- Provide on-going support to monitoring and reporting efforts by facilities and COs, assist in developing, testing and maintaining assumptions and calculations to generate valuable Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

- In the context of UNDP’s Scope 3 Strategy, develop assessment methodologies, coordinate EMT programming and support data collection for project end-of-life waste impacts and support development of subsequent management guidance.

3. Provision of corporate recommendations and strategic alignment

- Based on EMT data, consultations with Country Offices, and engagement with technical networks, develop evidence‑based recommendations for corporate‑level actions that improve waste management outcomes while reducing operational inefficiencies and avoidable costs.

- Prepare briefing materials to support senior management endorsement and strategic decision‑making. Support the development and change management aspects of the Waste Management and Resource Efficiency Strategy.

4. Promote staff engagement

- Guide and support the organization‑wide roll‑out of waste management initiatives through clear communications, consultations with Country Offices, and documentation of lessons learned.

- Practical implementation, peer learning, and solutions that balance ambition with feasibility.

- Organize and lead regular webinars and technical-level discussions. Provide bilateral helpdesk support to Country Offices, Regional Hubs and Headquarters as needed.

5. Support to the greening moonshot secretariat

- Contribute to other Greening Moonshot activities as required, including coordination with procurement, facilities, IT, and programme teams to ensure alignment between operational sustainability objectives, efficiency gains, and UNDP’s broader climate and development commitments.

- Apply a pragmatic, solutions‑oriented approach that strengthens UNDP’s leadership on sustainable operations while recognizing the diversity of operational contexts across regions and offices.

6. Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing

- Identify capacity building needs and opportunities.

- Ensure appropriate training, project workshops and other relevant activities are organized and implemented in a consultative manner, involving technical experts and stakeholders that may include the government, private sector, NGOs, donors, and/or academia.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Waste Management Specialist will work under the guidance of the BMS and BPPS Moonshot Secretariat Managers and report directly to the Moonshot Secretariat Coordinator. The candidate will be responsible for the fulfilment of the duties and responsibilities specified above.

The incumbent will work from home and will be given access to relevant information necessary for execution of the tasks under this assignment. The incumbent will be responsible for providing his/her own working station (i.e., laptop, internet, phone, scanner/printer, etc.) and must have reliable internet connection. Given the global scope of the work undertaken during this assignment, the incumbent is expected to be reasonably flexible with his/her availability taking into consideration different time zones.

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

BACKGROUND

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the leading organization for sustainable development within the UN system and acts as the key integrator for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP operates across headquarters, regional, and country levels, leveraging local expertise alongside global insights to deliver effective advocacy and solutions. For six decades, UNDP has worked with partners to lift millions out of poverty and expand opportunities for all.

UNDP’s Strategic Plan 2026–2029 is grounded in the determination to eradicate poverty—the greatest global challenge and a prerequisite for achieving the 2030 Agenda. Through the Strategic Plan, UNDP will continue supporting countries in advancing high human development while protecting the planet. Four strategic objectives—prosperity for all, effective governance, crisis resilience, and a healthy planet—guide its direction, powered by three accelerators: digital and artificial intelligence (AI) transformation, gender equality, and sustainable finance. All efforts are underpinned by a strong commitment to human rights and to leaving no one behind.

Within UNDP, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) brings together world-class policy expertise, flagship global programmes, and collaborative innovation and learning networks. BPPS ensures that UNDP is not only ready for the future but actively helps shape it with governments and partners. Working closely with the Crisis Bureau (CB), BPPS supports countries in navigating complex development and crisis contexts, integrating risk considerations into programming, and strengthening results-based management, innovation, and data-driven approaches.

The Global Policy Network (GPN) is central to this effort, mobilizing technical expertise to advance UNDP’s strategic objectives and signature solutions. Within the GPN, BPPS is responsible for developing policy and guidance, providing technical advice to Country Offices, representing UNDP in multi-stakeholder fora, and supporting UN inter-agency coordination across thematic areas.

The position of Partnership Analyst is located within the UNDP Rome Centre for Climate Action and Energy Transition (the “UNDP Rome Centre”). The central purpose of the Rome Centre is to ensure the effective implementation and further development of the strategic partnership between UNDP and the Government of Italy, while advancing broader collaboration with G7 and G20 countries in support of sustainable development.

The Rome Centre focuses on three priority areas: the Platform for Investment Support and Technical Assistance (PISTA), Youth Engagement in Climate Action, and Energy for Development.

PISTA aims to mobilize finance for climate, energy, and environment by originating projects that support decarbonization and climate-resilient transitions in developing economies, while catalyzing international financial resources. Matching impactful projects with investors goes hand in hand with engagement with financial institutions—both institutional and private—at Italian and global levels.

Energy for Growth promotes access to sustainable energy in developing countries, contributing to SDG7. It supports partner countries in unlocking finance to scale up clean energy solutions, expand energy access, and accelerate the energy transition. By connecting UNDP’s country presence and technical capacity with the public-private ecosystem of Italy and other G7 countries, the initiative helps mobilize capital aligned with the international energy and SDG agenda.

Youth4Climate advances youth engagement in climate action, contributing to SDG13. It supports youth-led and youth-inclusive solutions through financing and capacity development, while providing young climate leaders worldwide with a platform to engage with policymakers and global decision-makers.

The Rome Centre also holds a broader mandate to engage the Italian ecosystem, working closely with key public and private sector actors to mobilize financial resources for development objectives. To ensure effective implementation of the Centre’s workplan and its long-term strategic impact, the Rome Centre will continue to expand strategic partnerships and reinforce collaboration with Italy and other key partners.

The initiative aligns with UNDP’s goals on inclusive climate governance, energy transition, and intergenerational equity, linking global policy to local implementation.

DUTIES & RESPONSABILITIES

The Partnership Analyst provides coordination and partnership management support and technical support to the Partnerships and Strategy Unit of the UNDP Rome Centre, with primary responsibility for managing non-financial partnership agreements and related processes across the partnership lifecycle. Working closely with programme management and operations colleagues, the incumbent helps ensure that partnership instruments (e.g. Statements of Intent and Memoranda of Understanding) are aligned with UNDP internal governance, implementation modalities and risk requirements. Under the guidance of the Team Leader, the incumbent supports the development, review, and finalization of partnership instruments—such as Memoranda of Understanding, Statements of Intent, and other collaboration frameworks—ensuring compliance with UNDP legal, risk, branding, and due diligence requirements.

The position focuses on the operationalization of partnership engagements by coordinating internal clearance processes, liaising with legal, risk, and communications units, and supporting counterparts in headquarters, regional hubs, and country offices. The Partnership Analyst contributes to translating strategic partnership opportunities into structured, compliant, and implementable agreements that enable effective collaboration with institutional donors, private sector actors, foundations, and academic partners.

In addition, the incumbent supports stakeholder mapping, partner due diligence, and the documentation of partnership processes and workflows, contributing to institutional knowledge management and continuous improvement of partnership practices within the Rome Centre. Through this operational role, the position ensures efficiency, consistency, and risk-informed management of partnerships in support of UNDP’s programmatic priorities in areas such as climate action, energy transition, and innovation.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration

Ensure partnership agreement development and management

- Support coordinating the preparation, review, and finalization of partnership agreements, including Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs), Statements of Intent (SoIs), and other collaboration instruments, in line with UNDP policies and procedures.

- Contribute to managing internal clearance processes by liaising with legal, risk, procurement, and communications units to ensure timely and compliant approval of partnership documents.

- Maintain accurate records and tracking of partnership agreements, including status updates, validity periods, and required follow-up actions.

Provide operational support to partnership processes and compliance

- Support due diligence, risk assessment, and partner screening processes for institutional and private sector partners, in coordination with relevant UNDP units.

- Ensure partnership engagements comply with UNDP legal, branding, and visibility guidelines, including coordination on co-branding and communications requirements.

- Contribute to the identification and mitigation of operational and reputational risks associated with partnership engagements.

Ensure stakeholder coordination and internal collaboration

- Act as a focal point for partnership coordination with internal stakeholders across UNDP headquarters, regional hubs, and country offices on partnership-related matters.

- Support communication and information exchange with external partners during the agreement development and implementation phases.

- Facilitate alignment between partnership agreements and programmatic priorities by coordinating inputs from technical and policy colleagues.

Support partnership-related initiatives and events

- Provide coordination support to the planning and delivery of partnership-related meetings, consultations, and high-level outreach events.

- Prepare background materials, briefing notes, presentations, and supporting documentation for partnership discussions and negotiations.

- Ensure systematic follow-up on partnership meetings and events, including documentation of outcomes and next steps.

Facilitate knowledge management and process improvement

- Document partnership workflows, standard operating procedures, and lessons learned to strengthen institutional knowledge and consistency of practice.

- Support data collection and reporting on partnership activities, agreements, and engagement pipelines for internal monitoring and decision-making.

- Contribute to continuous improvement of partnership processes by identifying operational bottlenecks and proposing practical solutions.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: May supervise, Consultants, PSA holders and UNVs

COMPETENCIES

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

- Learn Continuously LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making

People Management

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

CROSS-FUNCTIONAL & TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking : Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Management

- Portfolio Management : Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity. Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfoliomanagement

- Partnership Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies

- Communication: Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. .Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

Finance

- Due Diligence Management: Ability to conduct a comprehensive appraisal of an organization or opportunity to be undertaken by a prospective investor or partner, especially to establish its assets and liabilities, as well as evaluate the potential opportunity and its related risks; knowledge of respective methodology and tools.

Partnership management

- Private sector engagement: Ability to identify, conduct outreach, and manage relationships with the private sector

- Private sector resources mobilization: Ability to identify, develop and manage partnerships that leverage private sector technical expertise and resources

REQUIRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in International Relations, International Development, Law, Political Science, Public Administration, Humanities or other relevant Social Sciences is required OR

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience at the national and/or international level in partnership management and advisory services is required.

- Experience and ability to support and manage end-to-end partnership processes, including the preparation, coordination, and follow-up of formal partnership instruments (e.g. MoUs, Statements of Intent), with proven attention to procedural accuracy, compliance, and timelines is required.

- Experience and proven capacity to conduct stakeholder analysis, synthesize complex information, and produce high-quality written outputs such as briefing notes, concept notes, partnership documentation, and internal coordination materials in English is required.

- Experience to work effectively in multicultural and multi-actor environments, liaising with internal colleagues and external counterparts, and facilitating clear communication across institutional, linguistic, and cultural contexts is required.

- Experience in managing evolving institutional requirements, and ability to acquire and apply new knowledge related to partnership policies, procedures, and tools in a dynamic operational environment is required.

- Direct experience supporting partnership processes within UN, particularly within a Partnerships and Strategy context, with familiarity with internal workflows and corporate systems is desired.

- Practical exposure to partnership due diligence, risk assessment, and compliance procedures, especially in engagements involving private sector and institutional partners is desired.

- Experience in legal research and confidentiality-sensitive documentation processes, contributing to risk mitigation and procedural robustness in partnership engagements is desired.

- Experience coordinating across multiple UNDP internal stakeholders, including headquarters units, thematic teams, and communications/branding functions, ensuring alignment with corporate visibility and positioning standards is desired.

Background

The UNDP Country Office success in its delivery of UNDP programmes is dependent on ensuring an adequate security framework is in place. The Host Government has primary responsibility for the security and protection of personnel employed by United Nations Security Management System organizations, their eligible family members, and property.

The UN House Security Team provides security coverage for UN House personnel, visitors, premises and assets, including 24/7 coverage of designated security posts and daytime coverage during UN House working hours.

Position Purpose

This position serves a dual function, supporting both the UN House/Common Services security arrangements, while also supporting UNDP's broader operational and programmatic objectives.

Under the guidance and supervision of the UNDP Operations Manager, the UNDP- UN House Security Associate supports the activity of the UN House Security Team and provides reliable security services for UN House Agencies. The assignment will include supporting the security arrangement with an outsourced security service, including preparation of technical requirements, technical support to related procurement process and monitoring of contractor performance. Further to support UNDP as required in the implementation of security and safety management in Moldova

The incumbent will work in close coordination with the UN House Management Committee, UNDP Procurement and other relevant functions for the outsourced security services transition and contract implementation. He/she will also work in close coordination with the UNDSS Security Associate for technical security guidance on UN House related matters as well as with UNDP Security Office, through the RSA/SRSS for technical guidance on UNDP related security matters.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

Performance monitoring of the security company (Guards team):

- Monitor and coordinate the outsourced security services, aimed at ensuring uninterrupted security coverage of UN House.

- Support induction and briefing of the selected company’s deployed personnel on UN House security procedures, access control arrangements, control-center functions, CCTV and access-control systems, fire and emergency procedures, incident reporting requirements, confidentiality and standards of conduct.

- Draft and/or coordinate post instructions, relevant SOPs, logbooks, access arrangements and operational information required for the UN House security service.

- Check, against contractual requirements, that deployed contractor personnel meet the required qualifications, training and documentation requirements and that the contractor has the required staffing/replacement arrangements in place.

- Monitor service delivery against the contract, technical specifications and agreed KPIs, including staffing levels, attendance, post coverage, response to incidents, reporting, replacement arrangements and compliance with UN House security procedures.

- Maintain regular operational communication with the contractor’s designated supervisor/team leader and promptly escalate performance gaps, security incidents or non-compliance with the UNDP Operations Manager, with technical coordination with UNDSS as appropriate.

- Monitor the performance and conduct of Security Guards and ensure compliance with applicable SOPs and security instructions and support follow-up on corrective actions and prepare periodic performance observations/reports as required.

- Support verification that the contractor operates in accordance with applicable Moldovan legislation and contractual obligations, while referring legal or contractual compliance issues to the responsible UNDP functions for determination.

Monitor the Access Control and Control Center:

- Control admission of authorized personnel and movement of United Nations property into and out of the premises.

- Ensure that unauthorized personnel and prohibited items do not gain access to UN House facilities.

- Conduct patrols and physical security checks of the compound, offices, perimeter and parking areas, and report irregularities.

- Use relevant technical screening and access-control equipment and maintain control of the emergency key system and related records.

- Maintain and/or supervise operation of the security control center.

- Prepare, print, issue, activate/deactivate and replace UN House access cards for personnel, as required, and maintain accurate records of cards issued, returned, lost, damaged or cancelled.

- Monitor and control, as applicable, the UN House Emergency Line and Panic Button, video surveillance system, fire safety and suppression system, electronic door locking/access-control system and VHF working channel.

- Ensure familiarity with and compliance with established procedures for operation of security systems.

Assist in supporting CO in Emergency Response:

- Act as a support response during emergencies or security incidents and promptly report to the designated supervisors.

- Be familiar with emergency procedures, Security Standard Operating Procedures and contingency plans and support their implementation.

- Know how to use firefighting equipment and support emergency response measures on the premises.

- Respond to emergencies affecting the safety and security of UN House personnel, visitors, assets and facilities in accordance with authorized procedures.

Overall security support to UNDP management and personnel:

- Provide support in keeping UNDP management informed of security matters affecting UNDP programmes and its personnel.

- Assist in implementing the Country Security Plan, Contingency Plans, and Business Continuity Management.

- Provide support to the UNDP Operations Manager on implementation of relevant security arrangements, including Warden System support, maps, security routes and related documents, as requested.

- Gather information for inclusion in Country Office security reports;

- Respond to and assist in reporting safety and security incidents affecting UNDP personnel and eligible dependents by gathering and verifying security information relevant to analyzing the situation;

- Maintain information of UNDP security contact details;

- Assist UNDP OM with the preparation and updating security aspects of procedures for dealing with emergencies involving UNDP staff and operations;

- Provide support in organizing training courses on security awareness and preparedness for UNDP personnel and provide security briefings to newly recruited employees;

- Assist UNDP OM during emergencies, incidents and security-related events;

- Monitoring news/information with potential impact on the security environment through different external and internal sources and providing information to OM on possible effects to UNDP personnel, programs and assets;

Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.
