jobs.title: Programme Specialist - Inclusive Growth [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Viet Nam is entering a new phase of accelerated development, building on more than three decades of sustained economic growth and improvements in human development. The country aspires to achieve high-income status by 2045 and net-zero emissions by 2050, while accelerating modernization, digital transformation and innovation-led growth. Viet Nam’s Human Development Index reached 0.766 in 2023, placing the country in the high human development category, while multidimensional poverty declined from 4.4 per cent in 2021 to 1.3 per cent in 2025.

Despite this progress, structural and spatial inequalities persist. Ethnic minorities, older persons, persons with disabilities, unregistered internal migrants, women and young people continue to face unequal access to services, productive assets, decent work, finance and economic opportunities. Women remain disproportionately represented in informal and vulnerable employment, while youth unemployment is more than three times the national rate. Rapid population ageing, evolving labour-market demands and uneven access to digital skills create additional challenges for inclusive transformation.

Private-sector development is central to Viet Nam’s future growth. The private sector generates 82 per cent of jobs and contributes approximately half of gross domestic product. More than 97 per cent of the country’s active enterprises are small and medium enterprises, but productivity and competitiveness are constrained by limited technology adoption and transfer, restricted access to capital, land and skilled labour, and an uneven capacity to adopt responsible, low-carbon and circular business practices.

The UNDP Country Programme Document for Viet Nam, 2027–2031, responds to these challenges through an integrated, issue-based and portfolio approach linking economic transformation, human development, climate resilience and governance. Under the economic and digital transformation outcome, UNDP will support private-sector competitiveness, responsible business, innovation and technology adoption; expand access to sustainable finance, particularly for small and medium enterprises led by or benefiting women and young people; strengthen resilient livelihoods and shock-responsive social-protection systems; and connect policy reform with investment and implementation at national and subnational levels. Digital and artificial intelligence transformation, gender equality and sustainable finance will serve as cross-cutting accelerators of systemic change.

Within this framework, the Inclusive Growth Unit leads UNDP Viet Nam’s portfolio on inclusive economic and digital transformation. Its work encompasses private-sector development, responsible and sustainable business, small and medium enterprise competitiveness and finance, youth economic empowerment and skills, innovation ecosystems, sustainable and innovative finance, resilient livelihoods, adaptive and shock-responsive social protection, and economic opportunities for groups at risk of being left behind. The Unit works across the Country Office and in partnership with government institutions, provincial authorities, United Nations entities, international financial institutions, development partners, the private sector, social organizations, academia and research institutions to support the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The Unit places particular emphasis on connecting inclusive economic transformation with emerging financing opportunities, supporting the development of integrated programmes that translate policy priorities, private-sector innovation and sustainable finance into tangible development results.

Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative and the overall guidance of the Resident Representative, the Programme Specialist - Inclusive Growth serves as a senior policy and programme adviser to Country Office management and provides strategic, technical and managerial leadership for UNDP Viet Nam’s Inclusive Growth portfolio.

The incumbent leads the strategic development, implementation and adaptation of an integrated Inclusive Growth portfolio, contributing principally to the Country Programme outcome on economic and digital transformation while building substantive linkages with climate and environmental sustainability, governance and inclusive human development. The portfolio encompasses inclusive private-sector development, responsible business, innovation and digital transformation, sustainable and innovative finance, resilient livelihoods, adaptive social protection and expanded economic opportunities for groups at risk of being left behind.

The incumbent works closely with the Country Office's Economic and Sustainable Finance Specialist to integrate economic and financing perspectives into programme development, identify opportunities for cross-portfolio collaboration and translate emerging policy and financing opportunities into strategic initiatives, partnerships and programme proposals.

The Programme Specialist ensures that UNDP’s policy advice, programmes, partnerships and financing instruments are coherent, evidence-based, gender-responsive, digitally informed and capable of generating scalable and sustainable development results. The incumbent identifies emerging development challenges and opportunities and translates them into strategic initiatives, partnerships and investable programme pipelines.

The Programme Specialist manages and supervises Inclusive Growth Unit personnel and relevant project staff, ensuring strategic prioritization, results-based management, programme quality, financial stewardship, appropriate risk management and compliance with UNDP policies and procedures. The incumbent promotes a collaborative, inclusive and accountable team culture, encourages learning and innovation, and ensures effective cooperation with other programme and operations teams.

The incumbent reports directly to the Deputy Resident Representative and retains accountability for the strategic direction, management, performance and results of the Inclusive Growth Unit. The incumbent works in close technical collaboration with the Economic and Sustainable Finance Specialist, drawing on specialized analytical and financing expertise while maintaining clear managerial and programme accountabilities.

The incumbent works closely with government institutions, provincial authorities, United Nations entities, international financial institutions, bilateral and multilateral partners, the private sector, social organizations, academia and UNDP technical and policy networks. The Programme Specialist represents UNDP in relevant policy dialogues, technical forums and partnership platforms, within the authority formally delegated by the Resident Representative.

The incumbent contributes to the Country Office management team and provides senior management with timely advice on programme performance, substantive and operational risks, financing and partnership opportunities, emerging policy priorities and measures required to maintain the strategic relevance and effectiveness of the portfolio.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to respond to changing development and business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. UNDP personnel are therefore expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary arrangements that enable horizontal collaboration and integrated solutions.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Programme Specialist - Inclusive Growth supervises Inclusive Growth Unit personnel and designated project personnel.

Provide strategic and analytical leadership, policy advice and direction for the Inclusive Growth portfolio

- Analyze economic, social and institutional developments, national policy priorities and emerging trends to identify challenges and opportunities for inclusive and sustainable economic transformation.

- Lead the strategic direction and development of an integrated Inclusive Growth portfolio, ensuring alignment with national priorities, the UNSDCF and the UNDP Country Programme.

- Identify and develop strategic programme opportunities in inclusive private-sector development, SME competitiveness, responsible business, innovation and digital transformation, sustainable finance, resilient livelihoods and adaptive social protection.

- Promote synergies within the Inclusive Growth portfolio and across Country Office programmes, working closely with the Economic and Sustainable Finance Specialist to integrate economic and financing perspectives into programme strategy.

- Provide evidence-based policy and strategic advice to government counterparts, development partners and Country Office management on inclusive economic transformation, emerging priorities and opportunities, and measures to strengthen development impact.

- Ensure that portfolio design systematically integrates gender equality, disability inclusion, youth empowerment, human rights, environmental sustainability and the principle of leaving no one behind.

Ensure effective portfolio management, programme quality, risk management and team performance

- Lead and supervise the Inclusive Growth Unit, establishing clear workplans, responsibilities and performance expectations, managing staff performance, and promoting professional development, collaboration and accountability.

- Oversee the full programme cycle, ensuring effective planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and closure of programmes and projects in accordance with UNDP policies and procedures.

- Ensure rigorous substantive and operational quality assurance of programme and project documents, implementation arrangements and results frameworks, including the identification, assessment and mitigation of programmatic, fiduciary, environmental, social and reputational risks, in accordance with UNDP standards.

- Oversee portfolio financial performance, delivery, resource utilization and appropriate cost recovery, ensuring timely corrective action to address implementation bottlenecks, underperformance and financial or operational constraints.

- Ensure effective results-based management, including credible indicators, baselines and monitoring systems; high-quality corporate and donor reporting; timely implementation of audit and evaluation recommendations; and systematic use of lessons learned to improve programme performance.

Lead strategic partnerships, private sector engagement and resource mobilization

- Develop and maintain strategic partnerships with national and international partners (government institutions, bi-lateral and multi-lateral donors, IFIs, private sector, civil society), to advance inclusive economic transformation and strengthen UNDP’s positioning and comparative advantage.

- Identify and develop new programme opportunities, translating national development priorities, policy reforms and emerging financing opportunities into integrated, scalable programmes and partnerships, including in private-sector development, innovation, sustainable finance and resilient livelihoods.

- Lead resource mobilization and the development of a forward-looking programme pipeline, overseeing the preparation of high-quality concept notes, project documents, funding proposals and partnership arrangements.

- Engage with national and provincial authorities to identify opportunities for Government Development Financing opportunities in line with national priorities and UNDP comparative advantage.

- Lead the Unit's engagement in relevant partnerships, policy platforms and UN joint programming initiatives, ensuring effective coordination and representation of UNDP within delegated authority.

Promote institutional capacity development, knowledge exchange and learning

- Identify and support institutional capacity-development needs of national and subnational counterparts in areas relevant to inclusive economic transformation, private-sector development, innovation, sustainable finance and social protection.

- Facilitate knowledge exchange, South-South and triangular cooperation, and access to UNDP regional and global expertise to support the adaptation and application of international good practices in Viet Nam.

- Oversee the development and dissemination of knowledge products, lessons learned and practical guidance, drawing on programme experience and partnerships with research institutions, academia and technical networks.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-functional & technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking : Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

- Business Acumen : Ability to understand and deal with a business situation in a manner that is likely to lead to a good outcome. Ability to make good judgments and quick decisions within such frameworks. Knowledge and understanding of the operational frameworks in the organization

2030 Agenda: Prosperity

- Inclusive Growth: Growth strategies

Business Management

- Resource Management: Allocate and use resources in a strategic or tactical way in line with business needs and priorities and principles of accountability and integrity

- Communication: Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience; Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

- Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity. Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management

- Partnerships Management : Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in International Development, Economics, Social Sciences, Public Administration, Public Policy Business Administration, Finance or other relevant field is required.

- A first-level university degree (bachelor´s degree) in one of the above fields, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 5 years (with master’s degree) or 7 (with bachelor’s degree) of progressive experience at the national or international level in programme and portfolio management, policy advice and development programming in one or more areas relevant to inclusive growth, poverty reduction, private sector development, economic value chains, or finance for development is required.

- Demonstrated experience in providing substantive policy and programmatic advice to government institutions or other development partners on inclusive economic transformation, private-sector development, innovation, sustainable finance, social protection or related areas is required.

- Proven experience in resource mobilization, programme-pipeline development and the preparation of high-quality concept notes, project documents or funding proposals is required.

- Demonstrated experience in managing complex development programmes or portfolios, including programme planning, results-based management, financial oversight, quality assurance and risk management is required.

- Demonstrated experience in managing teams and staff performance is required. Having experience with supervision of multidisciplinary international teams is desired.

- Experience with Viet Nam’s institutional, economic and policy context is required. Experience in other developing country context is desirable .

- Experience working with UNDP, another United Nations entity, government institutions or an international organization working on development issues is desired.

- Demonstrated experience working with financial institutions, banking institutions or the private sector to leverage development financing is desirable.

- Experience in the use of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.), and experience using web-based management systems such as ERP is desirable.

Required Languages:

- Fluency in English and Vietnamese is required.

- Knowledge of another UN language is desirable.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

jobs.title: Auxiliar en Diseño y Comunicación Visual
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

Fruto del Acuerdo de Colaboración firmado por el Gobierno de México y el Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD), se diseña el proyecto: “Fortalecimiento de las capacidades para el Impulso Económico y la implementación de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible”, que tiene como objetivo colaborar con la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores en el fortalecimiento de sus capacidades para posicionar los intereses de México en el escenario internacional mediante el cumplimiento de sus funciones en materia económica.

En seguimiento a estos objetivos, se impulsan acciones orientadas al fortalecimiento de la diplomacia económica de México, incluyendo la atracción de inversión, la promoción comercial, la interlocución con actores estratégicos y la articulación con Representaciones de México en el Exterior, dependencias federales, gobiernos estatales y organismos empresariales. En este marco, se implementa el Plan Integral de Promoción Económica, mediante misiones comerciales de México al exterior y misiones extranjeras hacia México, la participación de México en ferias internacionales, la canalización de oportunidades de proveeduría e inversión, así como la organización de seminarios de inversión y exportación.

En un contexto internacional marcado por la reconfiguración económica global, se llevarán a cabo las acciones previstas para la presente vacante, mismas que contribuirán a robustecer las capacidades de la SRE en materia de fortalecimiento de alianzas institucionales y apoyo a las prioridades estratégicas de México en el ámbito económico internacional.

Alcance de Trabajo:

1. Diseñar y elaborar materiales gráficos, incluyendo infografías, mapas, fichas informativas y otros insumos visuales para reuniones, eventos y actividades institucionales de la Unidad de Diplomacia Económica.

2. Desarrollar visualizaciones de datos económicos y estadísticos que permitan comunicar información técnica de manera clara, precisa y accesible.

3. Elaborar y adaptar presentaciones ejecutivas para el titular de la Unidad y sus distintas áreas, de acuerdo con los objetivos y requerimientos de cada actividad.

4. Desarrollar y actualizar plantillas, formatos y elementos de identidad gráfica para garantizar la uniformidad y consistencia visual de los materiales institucionales.

5. Realizar el diseño editorial, diagramación y adecuación visual de documentos, reportes y otros materiales de trabajo.

6. Seleccionar, editar y adaptar imágenes, fotografías e iconografía para su incorporación en materiales institucionales.

7. Organizar y mantener actualizados los archivos editables y recursos gráficos de la Unidad para facilitar su consulta, actualización y reutilización.

Acuerdo Institucional:

La presente vacante estará bajo supervisión directa de la Subsecretaría para América del Norte y la coordinación del proyecto “Fortalecimiento de las capacidades para el Impulso Económico y la implementación de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible”, quienes evaluarán el desempeño del contratista al término del contrato.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agildad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos:

- Certificado de Bachillerato (Preparatoria) es requerido y/o Licenciatura concluida en diseño gráfico, comunicación visual, diseño de información, diseño digital o carreras afines.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Para candidatos con Bachillerato (Preparatoria) de al menos 4 años de experiencia en diseño gráfico, comunicación visual, diseño de información, diseño digital, economía internacional, visualización de datos, análisis estadístico o temas afines.

- Para candidatos con licenciatura al menos 1 año de experiencia en los temas antes mencionados.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia o conocimiento en diseño gráfico y comunicación visual, como presentaciones ejecutivas, infografías y materiales institucionales

- Experiencia o conocimiento de PowerPoint. Capacidad para diseñar gráficas, infografías y representar información cuantitativa de manera clara y precisa.

- Experiencia o conocimiento de composición visual, tipografía, jerarquía de información y diseño editorial.

- Capacidad de organización, atención al detalle y cumplimiento de plazos de entrega.

- Capacidad para adaptar materiales gráficos a distintos formatos, contenidos y audiencias.

- Capacidad de comunicación efectiva y trabajo en equipo.

- Capacidad de creatividad y proactividad para proponer soluciones visuales.

Habilidades Deseadas:

- Experiencia o conocimiento en manejo técnico de programas de diseño y edición.

- Experiencia o conocimiento en manejo de herramientas de visualización de datos.

- Experiencia o conocimiento en tratamiento gráfico de datos e información económica y estadística.

- Experiencia o conocimiento en desarrollo de productos gráficos institucionales y materiales editoriales .

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar

jobs.title: Asociado(a) de Proyecto en Procesos de Capacitación y Comunicación Estratégica
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

El objetivo general del proyecto Sinergia+ es generar procesos de gestión que fortalezcan a la CONANP y que le permitan convertirse en una institución que planea con base en resultados, con finanzas fuertes y mecanismos de gobernanza y alianzas estratégicas eficaces, que contribuyan a incrementar la conectividad entre ecosistemas representativos para salvaguardar su biodiversidad y equilibrio ecológico.

El proyecto Sinergia+ tiene seis resultados estratégicos: 1) Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP; 2) Gobernanza y fortalecimiento de redes de colaboración; 3) Enfoque de género y fortalecimiento de la participación ciudadana; 4) Incremento de superficie de conservación con enfoque de conectividad ecológica; 5) Conservación y recuperación de especies en riesgo; 6) Proyectos Estratégicos.

En el marco del Proyecto Sinergia+, la persona a contratar contribuirá al fortalecimiento de la Coordinación del Proyecto Sinergia+ para fortificar la coordinación y gestión de los procesos de capacitación y comunicación estratégica del proyecto, mediante la identificación de necesidades formativas, la planeación, implementación y evaluación de acciones de fortalecimiento de capacidades, así como la coordinación y difusión de contenidos institucionales, asegurando la articulación entre el PNUD y la contraparte, así como en congruencia con los objetivos y las estrategias del Proyecto.

Este puesto contribuye al logro de metas del Resultado 6 “Proyectos Estratégicos”.

Alcance de Trabajo:

- Coordinar y dar seguimiento a las acciones en temas de capacitación obligatorias del PNUD, así como a aquellos solicitados por el proyecto o la contraparte.

- Implementar acciones de coordinación con RH para detectar y documentar las necesidades de capacitación de los colaboradores.

jobs.title: Auxiliar Enlace de Mecanismos Económicos Regionales - 4 posiciones
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

Fruto del Acuerdo de Colaboración firmado por el Gobierno de México y el Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD), se diseña el proyecto: “Fortalecimiento de las capacidades para el Impulso Económico y la implementación de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible”, que tiene como objetivo colaborar con la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores en el fortalecimiento de sus capacidades para posicionar los intereses de México en el escenario internacional mediante el cumplimiento de sus funciones en materia económica.

En seguimiento a estos objetivos, se impulsan acciones orientadas al fortalecimiento de la diplomacia económica de México, incluyendo la atracción de inversión, la promoción comercial, la interlocución con actores estratégicos y la articulación con Representaciones de México en el Exterior, dependencias federales, gobiernos estatales y organismos empresariales. En este marco, se implementa el Plan Integral de Promoción Económica, mediante misiones comerciales de México al exterior y misiones extranjeras hacia México, la participación de México en ferias internacionales, la canalización de oportunidades de proveeduría e inversión, así como la organización de seminarios de inversión y exportación.

En un contexto internacional marcado por la reconfiguración económica global, se llevarán a cabo las acciones previstas para la presente vacante, mismas que contribuirán a robustecer las capacidades de la SRE en materia de fortalecimiento de alianzas institucionales y apoyo a las prioridades estratégicas de México en el ámbito económico internacional.

Alcance de Trabajo:

2. Apoyar en recopilar, analizar y sistematizar información económica y comercial sobre países, regiones y sectores estratégicos, incluyendo datos de comercio, inversión y cooperación económica internacional.

3. Colaborar en la elaboración y actualización de documentos institucionales, tales como tarjetas informativas, fichas país, perfiles de empresas, notas de referencia, antecedentes y otros insumos de apoyo para las actividades del área.

4. Auxiliar en la preparación y seguimiento de reuniones, encuentros y actividades de diplomacia económica, mediante la integración de carpetas de trabajo, recopilación de información, elaboración de minutas y registro de acuerdos.

5. Mantener actualizadas las bases de datos, directorios, archivos y herramientas de seguimiento del área, para facilitar la organización, consulta y disponibilidad de información relevante.

6. Apoyar en actividades de investigación, apoyo documental y seguimiento operativo relacionadas con los proyectos, iniciativas y prioridades de diplomacia económica que le sean encomendados.

La presente vacante estará bajo supervisión directa de la Subsecretaría para América del Norte y la coordinación del proyecto “Fortalecimiento de las capacidades para el Impulso Económico y la implementación de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible”, quienes evaluarán el desempeño del contratista al término del contrato.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

jobs.title: Asociado(a) en Gestión Operativa y Atención Institucional de Proyectos de Cooperación
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

Vigente desde 2013, el Programa de Cooperación AMEXCID-PNUD (PROCAP) contribuye al fortalecimiento del Sistema Mexicano de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo y a la implementación del Objetivo de Desarrollo Sostenible 17, relativo a las alianzas para el desarrollo sostenible.

El Programa apoya los esfuerzos de la Agencia Mexicana de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo (AMEXCID) para fortalecer sus capacidades institucionales y de gestión de la cooperación internacional para el desarrollo (CID), considerando el carácter de México como país oferente y receptor de cooperación.

En este marco, se promueve el fortalecimiento de procesos y capacidades para la planeación, ejecución, seguimiento y sistematización de proyectos e iniciativas de cooperación; la articulación con actores públicos y otros socios; y el intercambio de conocimientos y buenas prácticas.

El trabajo se desarrolla en coordinación con las áreas competentes de la AMEXCID y del PNUD, con apego a la normatividad institucional y a los objetivos del Programa de Cooperación.

El objetivo general del Programa de Cooperación AMEXCID-PNUD (PROCAP) es la consolidación institucional de la AMEXCID para fortalecer la Cooperación Sur-Sur en México, a través de cuatro resultados:

1. Desarrollo de capacidades institucionales para la gestión de la CID;

2.Fortalecimiento de la política mexicana de CID, en sus modalidades de recepción y oferta;

3.Promoción de alianzas estratégicas para el desarrollo;

4.Apoyo a la implementación del Plan de Desarrollo Integral.

Alcance de Trabajo:

1. Coordinar el registro, canalización y seguimiento de solicitudes, trámites y asuntos administrativos relacionados con actividades de los proyectos de cooperación, brindando atención y orientación inicial a las personas e instituciones involucradas conforme a los procedimientos establecidos.

2. Organizar y dar seguimiento a los procesos de integración, revisión, actualización y resguardo de expedientes, oficios, constancias, notificaciones y demás documentación operativa, procurando la trazabilidad y disponibilidad de la información.

3. Facilitar la coordinación operativa con autoridades locales, áreas institucionales y actores territoriales que participen en iniciativas de cooperación, dando seguimiento a gestiones, acuerdos, requerimientos y plazos de atención.

4. Apoyar la organización y ejecución de actividades territoriales, reuniones de trabajo y acciones de vinculación comunitaria relacionadas con proyectos de cooperación, incluyendo convocatoria, registros de participación y documentación de resultados.

5. Dar seguimiento a verificaciones documentales, comunicaciones y trámites derivados de los procesos administrativos del área; identificar pendientes y elaborar matrices, listados y reportes periódicos para facilitar su atención oportuna.

6. Contribuir a la mejora de los procedimientos de atención, notificación, seguimiento de asuntos y gestión documental, sistematizando incidencias y proponiendo ajustes operativos en coordinación con las unidades responsables.

Acuerdo institucional:

El/la Asociado/a en Gestión Operativa y Atención Institucional de Proyectos de Cooperación formará parte de la estructura operativa de la Dirección Ejecutiva de la AMEXCID o de la dirección general en la que se asigne. Desarrollará funciones de apoyo especializado en procesos de atención, gestión documental, seguimiento de trámites y coordinación operativa con las áreas y contrapartes participantes, conforme a los procedimientos y responsabilidades institucionales aplicables.

jobs.title: Procurement Specialist (Roster - Multiple Locations) [Open to Tier 0, 1 & 2 applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Across Asia and the Pacific, UNDP helps countries build and share their own solutions to urgent development challenges, supporting coalitions for change and connecting individuals and institutions so they can share knowledge, experience and resources. As countries develop local capacity, they draw on the people of UNDP and our wide range of regional and global partners.

The Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific (RBAP) concentrates its efforts on developing the region’s capacity to promote and accelerate action on its progress towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It implements the UNDP Strategic Plan in Asia and the Pacific and delivers on UNDP’s partnerships within the region and with development actors in the region. In this context, RBAP is making conscious efforts to provide enhanced support to the COs within the region to accelerate programme delivery. To this end, a roster of Procurement Specialists (IPSA-10) is being developed to select candidates who can independently lead highly complex, strategic procurement and manage the unit in any UNDP Office in the Asia-Pacific region, offering timely guidance and appropriate support for short- or long-term assignments as may be required in each particular case.

Under the supervision of the Hiring Office, and in close coordination with the Regional Procurement Team in RBAP, the Procurement Specialist may lead or support procurement implementation in the Office, such as guiding on and processing of procurement transactions, or perform oversight functions such as carrying out quality assurance on all aspects of Country Office procurement actions in the region in assigned areas of responsibility, and flags issues of concern requiring senior management attention in a timely manner.

Placement on the roster does not guarantee an assignment.

Deployment under this roster may be for regular or shorter-duration assignments, depending on the needs of the requesting Country Office, provided the assignment is at the same level and within the same job function.

The Procurement Specialist will be deployed in UNDP Offices in the Asia and Pacific region and will provide on-site or remote procurement support as required by the assignment.

The roster has a validity of three years from the date of endorsement by Management (2027-2029) and is maintained by the COSQA, RBAP.

UNDP is striving to ensure its procurement function and practices are an integral part of UNDP’s competitive advantage as a development partner of choice. This requires placing more attention on strategically integrating procurement at the project design stage, stimulating innovation in specifications and technologies, and adopting more sustainable production and consumption practices that align with UNDPs sustainable development goals. Sustainable procurement means making sure products, services, and purchases are as sustainable as possible with the lowest environmental impact and most positive social results. In implementing UNDP strategic procurement priorities, Country offices will strive to use flexible methods for high-value/low-risk and timely delivery that meet the needs of its clients and key stakeholders.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Procurement Specialist will work under the strategic guidance and direct supervision of the DRR, OM or (Head of Procurement, as per the structure of the office) and is responsible for managing the Country Office Procurement unit with a large procurement volume.

The Procurement Specialist ensures efficiency and integrity in procurement management and provides solutions to a wide spectrum of complex issues related to procurement. The Procurement Specialist promotes a collaborative, client-focused, quality, strategic, and results oriented approach to all tasks; and works in close collaboration with Operations, Programme and project teams in the Country Office, Region, and UNDP HQ as well as with vendors and Government officials to successfully deliver procurement services, provide solutions to complex procurement issues, and provide advisory support. S/he may supervise Procurement Analyst and support staff in Procurement Unit.

Elaborate and manage implementation of innovative and sustainable procurement strategies and policies that are in alignment with principles of fairness, integrity and transparency to achieve best value for money.

- Ensure full compliance of procurement activities with UNDP rules, regulations, policies, and strategic priorities through effective internal controls and properly used client–oriented procurement management system.

- Elaborate/establish internal public sector procurement Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), mapped CO procurement business processes, and harmonized workflows within the Procurement unit and the broader CO.

- Discuss procurement strategies and plans with projects and other stakeholders and donors to ensure mutual alignment.

- Conceptualize, elaborate and implement strategic procurement in the CO including sourcing strategy, supplier selection and evaluation, quality contract management, contract administration, contractor appraisal, cost reduction strategies, customer relationship management, e-procurement, and performance measurement.

Efficiently manage procurement processes for CO, projects and other UN Agencies.

- Ensure timely and proper preparation of procurement plans for the office and projects, including establishment of the deadlines and monitoring of their implementation.

- Establish and manage implementation of proper monitoring systems, mechanisms and controls for procurement processes that cover RFQ, ITB or RFP, receipt and evaluation of quotations, bids or proposals, negotiation of certain conditions of contracts in full compliance with UNDP rules and regulations.

- Review and certify submission of documents to internal procurement review committees (CAP, RACP and ACP).

- Ensure management of procurement contracts and perform delegated responsibilities in e-procurement for Purchase Orders approval. Elaborate and implement internal control system, which ensures purchase orders are duly prepared, dispatched, and corrected on a timely basis when there are errors or other problems.

- Supervise implementation of harmonized procurement services and expansion of these services for joint procurement for UN agencies in line with the UN reform.

Elaborate, introduce and implement strategic sourcing strategy and e-procurement tools to find best values in marketplace and align purchasing strategy to project and CO goals.

- Develop and manage rosters of suppliers.

- Elaborate supplier selection and evaluation, and quality and performance measurement mechanisms.

- Review and provide input on the Term of Reference for establishment of Long-Term Agreements/Framework Agreements for more efficient category management.

- Ensure proper management and implementation of e-procurement system in CO.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Bureau for Management Services’ Office of Financial Resources Management (BMS/OFRM) supports the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in the implementation of the 2030 agenda and UNDP’s Strategic Plan. It achieves this by developing and making fully operational a dynamic and harmonized integrated resource management framework based on comprehensive analysis that enhances UNDP’s financial and administrative performance, as well as facilitating UN reform and coherence. The primary role of BMS/ OFRM is to maintain the financial integrity of UNDP through providing functional leadership, supporting the efficient and effective management of its financial resources, promoting financial sustainability and responsible resource allocation. This is accomplished by the development and implementation of sound financial policies and practices, oversight of corporate financial management performance, and flexible scalable support to resource allocation. BMS/OFRM serves as a business partner to Bureaux and Country Offices, providing sound financial management, advisory and analytical services, with a view to continuously improve the financial management performance of business units and support Bureaux in the exercising of their oversight functions.

Within OFRM, the Financial Performance Management & Reporting (FPMR) team is responsible for oversight of financial reporting, the preparation and integrity of UNDP’s financial statements, and providing timely and accurate financial information in accordance with international accounting standards. FPMR fosters trust and accountability through leadership in financial policy, robust internal financial controls, and close engagement with auditors to support an unqualified audit opinion, while also delivering expert accounting and financial advisory support, addressing complex and non-routine financial issues, and overseeing financial risk related to implementing partners, enabling informed senior decision-making and sustained audit assurance.

Within FPMR, there are four units:

- Corporate Financial Reporting (CFR): Responsible for promoting clear accountability for financial transactions and for producing UNDP’s corporate financial statements.

- Financial Performance Management (FPM): Responsible for managing aspects of financial performance, including the administration of the Annual Representation exercise and the Statement of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting; monitoring of financial risks related to financial statement integrity; and management of the implementing partners policy framework, including the agency-wide Harmonized Approach to Cash Transfers (HACT) framework.

- Payroll Finance Oversight (PFO): Responsible for the financial oversight of payroll accounting functions, as well as the reporting of employee benefits and liabilities for all UNDP personnel.

- Internal Advisory and Decision Support (IADS): provides expert, structured financial analysis to resolve complex, non-routine issues and enhance the quality and timeliness of senior decision-making.

Position Purpose

The Corporate Financial Reporting (CFR) function is responsible for the preparation of the organization’s financial statements, ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant financial reporting in line with international accounting standards. The team delivers reliable accounting and reporting execution, internal control assurance, and audit support through disciplined efficient close processes, strong data governance, and consistent application of financial policies.

Finance Associates in FPMR play a substantive technical role in the application of IPSAS and, where relevant, maintenance of the policy framework for the Harmonized Approach to Cash Transfers (HACT). They contribute to the integrity, reliability, and consistency of UNDP’s financial data, oversee and support the preparation of UNDP’s financial statements and other statutory reports, and undertake monitoring and analytical activities in support of OFM’s corporate oversight responsibilities. Finance Associates provide technical accounting and reporting and HACT-related guidance to relevant stakeholders and contribute to the articulation and defense of management positions during the external audit process, applying professional judgment and a sound understanding of accounting standards, internal controls, and audit assertions.

Note that UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. This is a recognition of interconnected nature of development risks & crises that the world is facing and that call for assembling of multidisciplinary teams for an integrated & systemic response. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Provides substantive support and leads aspects in the preparation of statutory and corporate financial reports, including financial statements, donor reports, executive board reports, and other financial reporting outputs:

- Leads the planning and execution of data collection and preparation of financial statements and notes, applying sound professional judgment in the interpretation and application of IPSAS standards.

- Prepares donor financial reports on revenue, expenditures, and related information, and proactively follows up with relevant UNDP units to resolve financial or programme-related issues and respond to donor queries.

- Prepares financial highlights, interim financial reports, and audit-related information, and performs analytical work and data analysis to support financial reporting and global process owners.

- Performs detailed analytical reviews of financial data and reports to identify, investigate, and resolve anomalies, ensuring accuracy and consistency of reported information.

2. Ensures data integrity within the UNDP financial systems while assisting with the preparation and review of the general ledger and other related financial modules:

- Regularly monitors the financial dashboards and other financial reports to identify data errors, analyze Month on Month/Quarter on Quarter/Year on Year movement and collaborate with the respective Bureaux or business units or for follow-up and clearance to instill a strong internal control environment.

- Performs GL reconciliations and performs monthly/quarterly analysis of balance sheet accounts, ensuring significant issues are identified, resolved or escalated as needed.

- Maintains core accounting information (account, fund and donor), financial statement mapping, IPSAS trees and accounting templates and other master data as needed.

- Supports regular financial closure processes including module closure per schedule, data analytics relating to the financial statements, among others.

3. Monitors compliance with financial procedures:

- Follows-up, reviews and monitors bureaus/Country Office submissions and account analyses and other financial information and summarized and prepares plan for resolving issues systematically.

- Liaises and communicates with GSSC teams, country offices, Regional Bureaus, HQ units and/or client Agencies (as appropriate) on corrective actions.

- Performs oversight support of assigned financial processes and accounts, reviewing the work of other units, as appropriate. For example, review cost recovery balances, including transactions and exceptions, monitoring performance, coordinating issue resolution with other teams (including IT department) to ultimately support reporting to Offices and the Executive Board, ensuring appropriate GMS levels are charged, collected, and reported.

- Performs finance business processes mapping and elaboration of the content of policies and prepares/updates Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) in Finance in consultation with FPMR management, proposing changes as required to enhance efficiency and effectiveness.

- Assists in the development of system tools, reports, dashboards, and testing and user guides and training materials.

4. Provides substantive accounting and transaction support across the finance function, contributing to accurate financial recording, reconciliations, and reporting in accordance with IPSAS and established policies and procedures:

- Manages accounting, billing, and reconciliation activities for assigned financial areas, including balance sheet and income statement accounts (e.g. MIP billing, investment accounting, GMS accounting), ensuring accuracy and timely resolution of issues.

- Prepares, validates, and reconciles financial data and supporting schedules for financial reporting, audit, actuarial, and management purposes, applying sound professional judgment within established frameworks.

- Proactively coordinates with shared services, country offices, policy units, and external service providers to investigate and resolve accounting queries and transaction issues, escalating complex matters as appropriate.

5. Audit support:

- Leads assigned internal and external audit activities by preparing documentation, data, and explanations, and responding to audit requests in a timely and accurate manner.

- Supports follow-up on audit observations by tracking actions, supporting remediation activities, and maintaining appropriate audit trails.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: None

LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

- Monitoring & evaluation Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively. Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback on the consistency or discrepancy between planned and actual activities and programme performance and results. Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Business Development

Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Finance

- Audit risk management Ability to address risks and audit issues raised in the course of an audit and propose solutions in order to ensure true and fair audit opinion is achieved.

- Financial risk management Ensures financial resilience through proactive assessment of risk, implementation of controls and taking mitigating action. Understands risk and reward in relation to collaborative and commercial projects. Ensures a culture of positive risk management.

- Finance business partnering Able to support business units and add value by innovating and providing solutions to financial issues/queries, including through FAQs, financial tools, advisory, etc. Influences and appropriately challenges non-finance colleagues for whom the service is being provided. Understands the operations opportunities and challenges of the organization. Holds a commercial outlook, demonstrating accountability towards organizational goals.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Completion of Secondary Education is required with specialized certification in accounting and/or Finance is required. University degree in Finance or Accounting is desirable.

- A professional accounting qualification (Fully Qualified) from an internationally accredited institute of accountancy is required.

Experience:

- Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, with ability to work in and across teams.

- Experience with ERP systems and Excel, preferably Oracle Cloud ERP, is required.

- Collaborative team player with flexibility to work across global time zones.

Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

jobs.title: Compliance Specialist (Open to All Applicants)
jobs.description:
Background

The Office of Audit and Investigations (OAI) reports to the Administrator and is responsible for internal audit and investigations services to UNDP and its affiliated entities. OAI has the sole responsibility for the conduct of all investigations within UNDP.

The Investigations Section of OAI conducts assessments and investigations into allegations of misconduct, such as fraud, theft and embezzlement, corruption, abuse of privileges and immunities, sexual exploitation and sexual abuse, workplace harassment and abuse of authority, retaliation on whistleblowers, or other acts or omissions in conflict with the general obligations that involve UNDP staff and other personnel.

OAI also investigates allegations of fraud and other financial irregularities committed by contractors, implementing partners and other third parties, deemed to be detrimental to UNDP.

OAI operates separate mechanisms for the reporting of alleged non-compliance with UNDP’s social and environmental policies and procedures. OAI established the Social and Environmental Compliance Unit (SECU) to respond to complaints that UNDP may not be meeting its social and environmental commitments. The SECU became operational on 1 January 2015. The assessment, investigation and reporting of alleged non-compliance with UNDP’s social and environmental policies and procedures is conducted by the SECU as a compliance review in accordance with generally accepted international processes. The purpose of a compliance review is to investigate alleged violations of UNDP’s social and environmental policies and procedures, and to identify approaches to bring the project into compliance.

In that regard, SECU operates a complaint mechanism for communities and public stakeholders and assesses such complaints to determine whether an investigation is required or whether the issue raised is more appropriately dealt with through a separate Grievance Resolution process. Where the assessment determines that an investigation is warranted, SECU will investigate allegations of non-compliance with UNDP’s social and environmental policies and procedures. Based on the evidence collected during the investigation, SECU will recommend action to bring a project into compliance.

See -

https://www.undp.org/content/undp/en/home/accountability/audit/secu-srm/social-and-environmental-compliance-unit.html

The Compliance Specialist functionally reports to the Head SECU (P4), while he/she works closely under the technical guidance of the Lead Compliance Officer, SECU.

- Demonstrates a strong understanding of information security and confidentiality issues relevant to SECU’s work.

2.) Ensure Effective Client Services

jobs.title: Associate Finance Officer - UNOCHA (Nationals Only)
jobs.description:
Background

The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) coordinates effective and principled humanitarian response and ensures that relief assistance reaches the people in need in a timely manner. OCHA-managed Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) is a multi-donor country-based pooled mechanism created in 2010 to allocate funding for the most urgent life-saving interventions in Somalia. Combining flexibility and strategic focus, the Fund ensures timely allocation and disbursement of resources, enables effective humanitarian action, and strengthens coordination.

The Associate Finance Officer - communication, under the guidance of the Head, Humanitarian Financing Unit (HFU), and direct supervision of the SHF Finance Officer, participates in the overall implementation of the SHF Accountability Framework and works in close collaboration with the HFU and other OCHA Somalia staff, as well as cluster coordination staff. He/she is expected to travel extensively to the SHF project locations within Somalia to assist with the implementation of the SHF Accountability Framework as well as provide support in communications and external relations activities of the SHF.

Duties and Responsibilities

- Provide support in the allocation and financial management processes of the Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF)

- Review and advise on the clearance of the project budgets and grant agreements;

- Review and advise on budget amendments or no-cost extension requests;

- Regular follow-up with IP to obtain financial reports;

- Review of interim and final financial reports and supporting documents to ensure compliance with the signed SHF agreements, budgets and guidelines;

- Follow up on disbursement of funds and refund of balances from partners;

- Review of grant agreements and supporting documents to ensure accuracy, consistency, reasonableness, compliance with the United Nations Financial Rules and Regulations (UNFRR) and the Country-based Pooled Funds (CBPF) Guidelines;

- Receipt & review of audit reports from contractors and ensure projects records are updated as necessary.

2) Provide support in implementing the financial aspects of the SHF Accountability Framework

- Conduct financial spot-checks in line with the SHF operational modalities;

- Facilitate and provide support during audits, at the project and fund level, as requested, including assistance with vendor contracting, supporting the planning process and assisting in the follow-up of critical audit findings;

- Liaise with partners, SHF/HFU staff and other third parties in verifying expenditure supporting documents during spot-checks, review of financial reports, capacity assessments and audits;

- Assist with the submission and return of Partners’ financial documentation for spot-checks in OCHA field offices.

3) Provide support to the implementation of the monitoring pillar of the SHF accountability framework.

- Contribute to the development and implementation of monitoring plans in line with allocation funding modalities;

- Participate in planning and actual field project monitoring together with other HFU/OCHA field staff;

- Participate in the request and review of partner due diligence information/document submissions and corresponding status update in Grant Management System (GMS);

- Assist with updating the project monitoring timelines, results and recommendations in the GMS.

4) Facilitate knowledge-building and knowledge-sharing on finance, monitoring & evaluation within OCHA Somalia, clusters and the SHF implementing partners

- Identify and synthesize finance, monitoring and evaluation best practices, lessons learned and recommendations to be integrated into fund management efforts and channeled into decision-making processes;

- Promote of awareness on SHF guidelines, operational manuals, clauses in partner agreements, UNFRR and best practices;

- Plan and participate in trainings to implementing partners and other stakeholders.

5) Provide support in communication and external relations activities

- Supports implementation of SHF communications activities, prepares public information and donor materials, and maintains the SHF website and social media.

- Serves as a focal point for the preparation of public information materials that feature information related to the implementation and impact of SHF-funded projects and interventions, including human interest stories that feature audio visual materials, text etc. across multiple platforms (website, bulletins and reports, social media). This includes proactive outreach to SHF Implementing Partners, cluster coordinators, OCHA communications teams locally and globally, HFU and other humanitarian stakeholders.

- Utilizes and analyses SHF monitoring data from SHF accountability mechanisms (OCHA field monitoring, third-party and call monitoring, cluster monitoring tools) as basis for SHF communications deliverables, including verification with partners and beneficiaries, to demonstrate impact and accountability to affected people.

- Supports with the preparation of donor communications materials, including briefing materials, presentations and info graphics on SHF and other humanitarian financing issues (HRP funding status etc.)

- Supports with the coordination of regular and ad hoc SHF donor meetings, including preparing relevant communications and briefing materials, drafting minutes and ensuring follow up on any action items.

- Supports with the production of the SHF annual and interim reports (development of the outline, drafting, data collection etc.).

- Supports with the regular update and management of the SHF section of OCHA Somalia website and OCHA Somalia social media presence

Competencies

- Professionalism: Knowledge of different aspects of humanitarian response, public information and communication. Ability to address a range of issues in the context of political developments, public attitudes and local conditions. Ability to conceptualize, design and implement major information campaigns. Ability to rapidly analyze and integrate diverse information from varied sources. Ability to diplomatically handle sensitive situations with target audiences and cultivate productive relationships. Ability to produce a variety of written communications products in a clear, concise style. Ability to deliver oral presentations to various audiences. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work.

- Communication : Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed.

- Creativity: Actively seeks to improve programmes or services; offers new and different options to solve problems or meet client needs; promotes and persuades others to consider new ideas; takes calculated risks on new and unusual ideas; thinks "outside the box"; takes an interest in new ideas and new ways of doing things; is not bound by current thinking or traditional approaches.

- Accountability: Takes ownership for all responsibilities and honours commitments. Delivers outputs for which one has responsibility within prescribed time, cost and quality standards. Operates in compliance with organizational regulations and rules. Supports subordinates, provides oversight and takes responsibility for delegated assignments. Takes personal responsibility for his/her own shortcomings and those of the work unit, where applicable.

- Planning & Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies. Identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required. Allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work. Foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning. Monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary. Uses time efficiently.

- Teamwork : Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced (Masters) University Degree in Finance/Accounting, Business Administration, Public Administration, Law, Communications or a related field.

- A first level university degree with relevant academic qualifications with a combination of two (2) years of relevant work experience may exceptionally be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

- Diploma/Certificate of Professional or vocational training in the fields of Accounting, Financial Management, financial controls or auditing (Certified Public Accountant, Certified Internal Auditor, Certified Fraud Examiner, Chartered Accountant or equivalent) is desirable and will be considered an asset.

Experience:

- Applicants with Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.

- Minimum 2 years of relevant experience with Bachelor degree at the national or international level in providing management advisory services and hands-on experience in finance, accounting or auditing is required.

- Good knowledge of internal control systems and experience with accounting and auditing tools is desirable.

- Experience communicating financial information to donors, implementing partners, management or non-finance stakeholders, including preparation of financial and narrative reports, is desirable.

- Experience in the use of computers, accounting information systems, Microsoft Office software packages and web-based management systems is required.

Language:

- Fluency in oral and written English is required.

- Fluency in Somali language is required.
